f.name: RemoveChildrenByStatus
f.ap: Status - the current status of the child objects you wish to delete
f.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
Instead, use the DeleteDCOChildWithStatus action in the ApplicationObjects action library.
This action, when placed on an object, will check the status of all child objects and delete the ones
from the current parent. Note:if you delete pages, the images will still exist in the batch directory, but
the reference to them will be removed from the page file.
RemoveChildrenByStatus(75)
f.g:
'Your VBScript code goes here.
RemoveChildrenByStatus = TRUE 'Actions must always return a TRUE or FALSE.
for i = CurrentObj.NumOfChildren -1 to 0 step - 1
if cLng(CurrentObj.GetChild(i).Status) = cLng(ChildStatus) then
Writelog("Deleting: " & CurrentObj.GetChild(i).Type)
CurrentObj.DeleteChild(i)
end if
next 'i

f.name: MoveBatchPageToPreviousDocument
f.qi: Take a batche's child pages and move them to a document structure
f.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
Instead, use the MoveBatchPageToPreviousDocument action in the ApplicationObjects action library.
This action, when placed on a page that is a child of the batch level object,
will move it in to the previous document structure, or create a new document structure if no previous document exists
MoveBatchPageToPreviousDocument(OtherDoc)
f.lvl: Page Level, but will execute only if the page's parent is the batch level object.
f.g:
'Your VBScript code goes here.
Dim oNewDoc
MoveBatchPageToPreviousDocument = TRUE 'Actions must always return a TRUE or FALSE.
if CurrentObj.ObjectType <> 2 then
Writelog("This action is to be placed on page objects only. Exiting")
Exit Function
end if
If currentObj.Parent.ObjectType <> 0 then
Writelog("This action will only execute on pages that are not already assigned to a document. Exiting")
Exit Function
end if
CurrentBatchIndex = CurrentObj.Parent.FindChildIndex(CurrentObj.ID)
Writelog("CurrentBatchIndex: " & cStr(CurrentBatchIndex) )
if CurrentBatchIndex = 0 then
Writelog("Page was first child. Creating a document at the start of the batch")
Set oNewDoc = DCO.AddChild(1,Pilot.BatchID & ".added",0)
Call CurrentObj.MoveIn(oNewDoc,0)
oNewDoc.Type = NewDocumentType
oNewDoc.Status = 0
Exit Function
end if
CurrentBatchIndex = CurrentBatchIndex -1
While CurrentBatchIndex > -1
if DCO.GetChild(CurrentBatchIndex).ObjectType = 1 then
Writelog("Detected a document at index: " & cStr(CurrentBatchIndex) )
Call CurrentObj.MoveIn(DCO.GetChild(CurrentBatchIndex),-1)
Exit Function
end if
CurrentBatchIndex = CurrentBatchIndex -1
wend
if CurrentBatchIndex = 0 then
Writelog("Page was first child. Creating a document at the start of the batch")
Set oNewDoc = DCO.AddChild(1,Pilot.BatchID & ".added",0)
Call CurrentObj.MoveIn(oNewDoc,0)
oNewDoc.Type = NewDocumentType
Exit Function
end if

com.qi: : Actions that create and manipulate DCO objects.
com.h:
Datacap applications all contain a hierarchy of Datacap Application Objects,
which is more commonly called the application's DCO hierarchy.
The DCO defines the structure of the objects of the application. At the top level is the Batch object.
There is only one batch object. All
objects are off of this main root node. The other objects are Document, Page and Field. A typical structure
would look something like this:
Batch
- Document
- - Page
- - - Field
A Batch node can have a child Document, Page or Field.
Documents can also have child Documents, Pages and Fields. Pages can only have child Pages, and Fields.
Fields can only have child fields.
Page objects are usually a child of a Document and are named and arranged in a way that is
meaningful for a specific application. One exception is the page type "Other". "Other" is a common
page type in Datacap applications. As documents are ingested to create a batch, they are assigned the
initial type of "Other". This type is used as a starting point for processing documents.
Unlike other page types, the Other page is directly attached to the Batch node. Other application specific
page types are typically attached to a Document object to group one or more pages or page types together
in a meaningful way.
After files are ingested and assigned a type of Other, the next step is to identify and process the files.
The "Other" pages are typically processed then assigned new page
types that define a more detailed hierarchy that groups
pages together under a Document.
Each page type can have a unique set of fields that indicate
areas on the page where data will be extracted. A page typically defines the kind of page, such as
an "Invoice", the fields define the type of data expected on a page such as Date, Vendor Name,
Address, Invoice number, and other data expected on an Invoice.
It is also possible for a page to have different
locations of data based on the document although the same page type is used. For example, this is commonly
performed in the APT application where invoices are processed, while each invoice has the same types of
data such as names, addresses, dates, line items, the location of this data can be different based
on the fingerprint of the page. For example, in one invoice the date may be on the top left,
another invoice may have the date in the top right, and still another
may place the date somewhere else on the page.
This allows an application to process the same type of page
consistently although the pages and location of data on each page is different.
While there is only one Batch node, there can be multiple nodes of all of the other types.
An application specific hierarchy can consist of any combination of these objects that
defines the documents, pages and fields required to process a set of files as defined
by specific use cases.
Here is one example:
For illustration (B=Batch, D=Document, P=Page, F=Field)
B MyApplication
- P Other
- D Invoice
- - P MainPage
- - - - F Date
- - - - F Invoice Number
- - - - F Invoice Amount
- - - - F Line Items
- - - - - F Quantity
- - - - - F Description
- - - - - F Price
- - P TrailingPage
- D Mortgage
- - P Agreement
- - - F Signature
- - - F Date
While this is a very simple example, it shows a typical structure used in applications. Each of these nodes is
a DCO node and each are used to represent the current state of the application as well as
providing a way to attach processing rules and actions that will be acted upon each node within the
application that process the data.
Each DCO node can have a "property" / "variable" that holds metadata about the node. These are defined
directly on the node. For example, a page
will have a variable that contains the name of the file associated with the page. There are some sets of variables
that are standard however any number of additional user required variables can be created at any time.
A DCO node can contain any number of variables or children. While objects typically have a specific type of child,
there are some exceptions. For example, a Page or a Field can be attached directly to a Batch node. Likewise,
a Field node can in turn have additional children fields, as is required for line item processing.
Each application has a "Setup DCO" and a "Runtime DCO". A Setup DCO is the static hierarchy that defines the object layout
of the application. It is called the "Setup DCO" because it is defined at application setup / design time. It
defines one of all of the possible types of nodes that will be processed.
The setup DCO is also used to define the relationship of each application object
to the application rules that will be run on each object. For example rules can be attached to the "MainPage" object that will
run on each object that has been identified as a MainPage. The same rules or different
sets of rules can run on the TrailingPage.
The Runtime DCO is the dynamic version of the object hierarchy that directly reflects a specific batch that is being
processed and contains all of the currently instantiated objects.
For example, if there are 10 pages in the batch, there will be 10 page objects existing in the Runtime DCO.
The types of these pages may be mixed. Perhaps there are 3 MainPages, 9 TrailingPages, all children of a set of 3 Invoice document objects
and 1 Agreement page under a Mortgage document object. The runtime DCO will contain the values of each of the variables
contained in each object node. At runtime, DCO nodes are created for the pages, documents and fields within the batch
to reflect the unique files and data within the batch.
The primary focus of the Application Object action library is on manipulation of these DCO nodes. Every action library
will read, act on, and can also update an object.
The Application Object library is more general for updating, organizing and deleting DCO nodes themselves.
Access of variables and nodes is case sensitive but it is not recommended to use names and types
for objects that differ only in case.
User variables can be configured in the setup DCO. Any object that has a variable preconfigured will automatically
have that value unless it is changed at runtime. For example, a DCO node may be configured with a
variable value so all objects of that type, will initially have the value set in the setup DCO, then specific
nodes can have that variable updated at runtime, as required by specific application use cases.
Predefined DCO Variables
The following is a list of common variables and attributes that are used to process an application:
ID
: The unique identifier for the object.
TYPE
: The type of the object which corresponds to the setup DCO.
STATUS
: The status has many meanings and refers to the current state of the object.
IMAGEFILE
: The file associated with a page node. Typically this is a TIFF, but it can be any type of file.
PageName
: Often used to hold the original file name without the extension.
ScanSrcPath
: The path and name of the source file.
DATAFILE
: The name of the runtime dco for the fields. This file must only be manipulated using actions.
TemplateID
: The ID of the fingerprint associated with the page.
CCOFILE
: The name of the CCO file associated with the page.
These common predefined variables can be read and written by any application.
While an application can freely read these variables, care should be taken to update these variable using provided actions.
If a variable is updated incorrectly, it can cause problems at runtime. If there is a need to update these variables,
there are often predefined actions to update the variables. For example, the TemplateID can be updated using the SetPageFingerprintID
or the status can be updated using SetDCOStatus or SetDCOType to update the type. The ID of a node is assigned when it is created
and should not be changed once created. For example, a new child node can be added at runtime using AddChildDCONode and the
ID for that child is specified as a parameter.
Once created, the ID of a node should not be changed or results can be unpredictable.
DCO Status
Each DCO has a status property. The status indicates if the data associated with the node is valid, invalid
or indicates a particular state or problem. Verify panels are the primary place the status is used
although actions may set the status or make logic decisions based on the status of an object.
The status is updated at run time depending on the object type and the rules and actions of the task.
Some actions may update the status of a DCO object. It is also possible for a failed ruleset
to automatically change the status of an object to fail, if the Status Preserve option is disabled.
Some common status values are shown in this table with their conventional meanings. Commonly used
status values are -1, 0, 1, 2, 49. Other status status are less common and may or may not be used
as listed depending on the configuration and uses cases for the application.
If you are using an uncommon value for status, it is recommended that the listed values are used
instead of making up a new status value,
if they apply to your application. If a status is required by an application that is not
listed in the predefined values, a new unique value can be used in the
application, however it will be unique for your application and may be updated
by an action that updates the status. Actions can be used to look for the unique status
and control the logic flow of rules based on that status value.
-1 Hidden / Ignore. The object should be ignored. If set on a field, the field is not displayed in the verify panel.
0 OK / Passed. An object with no known issue or has had a problem corrected so it is now valid. This status may be used
at any DCO level.
1 Error / Problem. A verify panel and actions can take specific actions for failed pages. This status may be used at any DCO level.
2 Overridden. Used for pages that fail validation but are overridden by the operator.
3 InvalidType. Set by document creation if a page type is invalid.
48 RecogDoneOK. Indicates a page that has been successfully processed by the Recognition task and is ready for Verification.
This status does not mean that data in all fields on the page is complete and accurate.
49 ScanOK. Scan tasks will typically uses this as an initial page status.
50 ScanBad. Indicates that unsuccessful scanning has resulted in a problem page.
51 CannotFindAnchor. Indicates that the workflow’s Recognition task has failed to identify the anchor fields of the page.
A batch containing a page with this status usually must be reviewed by a user in a "FixUp" panel.
52 DontNeedVerification. Verification can be skipped. Typically a status of 0 would be used instead.
65 Indicates that although Recognition successfully identified the anchors on the page, a processing error prevented further steps.
Pages with this status should be treated as problems.
66 Verification Done. Indicates that a page has been successfully processed by a "FixUp" task operating in the Verify mode.
70 RescanPage. Identifies the page as needing to be scanned again.
71 VerificationFailed
72 PageOnHold. Suspends the processing of a page, often when a page requires special attention, and places its document on Hold as well.
If any page remains on Hold after the task processes the other pages in a batch, Taskmaster automatically assigns a Hold status to the batch itself.
73 PageOverridden
74 NoData. Ensures that none of the data on the page will be forwarded to an Export task – in effect, deleting the page.
The assignment of this status to a page, usually by an operator or supervisor, results in a Pending status for the document.
75 DeletedPage. Marks a page and its parent document for deletion and removes their association with the sponsoring batch.
This status does not, however, directly affect the corresponding Image file which can still exist in the batch.
76 Export completed. Indicates that the entire workflow has successfully processed a page.
77 DeleteApproved. Indicates that an operator or supervisor has approved the deletion of the page and document.
78 Removed. “Removes” the page from the workflow and its data from further consideration.
It also removes the document containing the page. In most cases, a page with this status is beyond repair.
79 ReviewPage. Branches a page to a child job for review and possible repair.
128 DeletedDoc. Indicates that an authorized operator or Supervisor has removed a document from the internal organization of the batch.
129 Rescan. Indicates that the document needs to be scanned again.
145 ReviewDoc. Marks the document for review by a remedial FixUp task.
147 IncompleteDoc. Denotes a document with the wrong number or types of pages.
DCO Type and Page Identification
Images and files are ingested using the scan or virtual scan task. During the ingestion, the pages are initially
assigned the page type of "Other". This is a special page type that does not have any document structure and
uses the batch as a parent. This is the starting point for processing of ingested files.
The next goal is to change the page type from "Other" to another meaningful page type.
A DCO type cannot contain double quotes. Once assigned
a meaningful type, the pages can be processed and manipulated based on the use cases for
the application. While page identification is
the next goal, it is not necessarily the next direct processing step. The next step can vary from application
to application.
For example, if images are ingested as PDFs, word documents, emails or other types of formats, one of the
use cases may be to recognize these pages so the text within them can be analyzed, verified and stored.
In this situation, before performing page ID, these kinds of documents are typically converted into TIFF
images. The final result is that the original source file, such as a PDF, is still in the batch, but now
there are individual images for each page from within the parent file. Similar work is typically performed
on emails or other types of documents that become a parent for multiple images, one new image
for each page.
Another common step prior to page ID is to perform image enhancements on all or some of the images.
If recognition is going to be performed and the image source isn't a nice clean document, such as
a Word document, then the image may need some image adjustments. While leaving out many
details from this description, typically operations like deskew, automatic rotation, line removal
and other enhancements are performed to create clean images to provide to recognition.
The result would be a clean document that has proper orientation and is not skewed.
It is also sometimes useful to remove any lines from the document in this step.
The actual page ID process can be performed in a number of ways and varies based on
specific use cases. One approach would be to perform fingerprinting after image enhancement.
Fingerprint matching directly assigns a type ID to the page, changing it from "Other" to
the correct type. The fingerprinting actions will look at a page, and the known
fingerprints and match the page to the correct fingerprint, so now the page type
is determined along with the locations of any fields on the page.
Using barcodes or patch codes are another technique for determining the type of a page and
then assigning the page type with the SetPageType action. This could be a barcode
directly on the page to identify, or a separator page that is scanned before the current
page that that indicates the page type of the following page.
Other types of identification can include performing recognition and identifying a page
by specific text within the page that the application knows belongs to a specific type type
and then directly assigning the page type. If a page is blank, that may be assigned a different
page type or possibly deleted or used as a separator.
Datacap provides a number of different kinds of actions that can be used to identify
the page type and then assign it. Again, what is appropriate depends on the
application use cases. Custom actions could even be used to use specific logic
to figure out a page type and then assign it to the page. A page could also be
provided to a classification engine, which will determine the correct page
type and fingerprint.
Some applications use manual page identification with the Flex ID panel to have operators
set page types by reviewing the document,
or may simply supplement manual identification only for a smaller set of pages that could not
be automatically identified. The actions are the tools to perform the
identification process, how to arrange them to achieve the
required page identification use cases is specific to an application.
Most applications use some common
techniques as described.
Once the Page ID rules have set new page types for each of the "Other" pages, then the "Create Documents"
ruleset can be called which will automatically organize all of the pages into the appropriate
page hierarchy, grouping pages together under a document node, or multiple document nodes, as
defined by the application. Once page identification is done and the new document structure has
been created, then processing of the batch can continue, but now that the page types are
identified, then specific rules, and different rules, can be run on each object based on
the DCO node level and the type.
After creating documents, the CreateFields action in the ApplicationObjects library will
generate the field objects for a page. Initially these fields exist with no position
information. The position information is then determined by loading the zones
for the associated fingerprint or using actions to dynamically find zone locations
using rules at runtime.
Once all the pages are identified and documents created, subsequent actions that
have been defined on the objects will run to perform the specific
operations required for each type of object within the DCO hierarchy.
Field Confidence
A field represents a specific type of data from a field. While it is not required,
a field usually also has position information that identifies the location
on the associated parent page object where the data exists. This position information
is a representation of the pixel area on the page from where the text
was recognized in a format of: left, top, right, bottom.
Field objects have the ability to store recognized text that is associated
with the field. For example, if the field represents a date, the position would
indicate the location of the text and the field's value would be the date, such as
"01/01/2020".
Each character within the field's value also has an associated confidence level.
The confidence level represents if the recognition engine thinks the value that
was read is accurate or could have been misread. The confidence level is
represented as a number between 1 to 10, where 1 means the engine is very unsure
that the character is correct and 10 means the engine is very sure the number is
correct. Typically a confidence value of 8, 9 or 10 are considered "high" confidence
and that the engine was probably correct in reading the text. This default
value is adjustable. If adjusted, it could be dropped to 7 or 6. It is rarely raised
to 9 or 10.
Each of the characters has this confidence level. If any one of the characters
has a confidence lower than the minimum confidence, it is highlighted to the
verification operator when viewing the fields in the verify panel. The operator
can visually confirm or correct any misread values.
There are other ways to confirm characters are correct, including mechanisms
to automatically lower or raise confidence values based on one or more conditions.
The ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library is one action library that
can perform automatic verification. Other mechanisms such as pattern matching
or voting can also automatically adjust the confidence of characters
within a field.
In some situations, a character's confidence may be represented
in a range from 0-9. Be sure to understand the correct range when
working with confidence values.
A field's confidence value can be returned as a string using the field property "CONFIDENCESTRING".
For example, if the action rrCompare("@P\Field1.CONFIDENCESTRING","99999") is called on a page
that has a field name "Field1", it will return true if the field contains 5 characters and
confidence of the field is "99999".
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
For example, "@X" is notation for accessing the current object. "@P" accesses the page object, which
could be the current object, or a parent object. Being evaluated at runtime, allows recognized data
or other batch specific data to be passed to actions or stored as metadata. A smart parameter such
as @DATE could be used to name export files based on the current date. Similar smart parameters
will retrieve the current batch ID, current batch directory, current operator ID, and more.
Smart parameters are a very powerful mechanism of getting data from other areas of the application and copying
it into a new location or passing it as a parameter to an action. It is recommended that the smart parameter
documentation is reviewed to understand the full capabilities available. The top-level help of the
ValidationAndTextAdjustments action library also has information about smart parameters. Some characters such
as +, \ and . also have special smart parameter meaning and may be interpreted as a smart parameter. This
can be controlled using smart parameter syntax.

method.name: AddChildDCONode
method.qi: : Adds new Node (Document, Page or Field) to the Runtime DCO
method.ap:
ObjectType:
The new DCO node object type: 3=Field, 2=Page, 1=Document.
ID:
The Node's ID. This value must be unique. If blank, a unique ID will be assigned.
Type:
The Node's Type.
Status:
The Node's Numeric Status. Optional, Defaults to 0.
Index:
The Node's Zero based Index. Optional, Defaults to add to the end of the children (-1).
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Creates a child DCO node of the type indicated by the first argument (A Field, Page or Document).
The new node is a child to the current DCO node.
If a node of the same type and ID exists no new node will be created and the action will return True.
Restrictions: Documents can only have child Documents, Pages and Fields. Pages can only have child Pages, and Fields.
Fields can only have child fields.
The new child node is added to the runtime DCO hierarchy. The new node will now function just like all existing
nodes meaning that any rules defined for that object type in the setup DCO will now run in subsequent rules.
For example, if a page is added to a document, subsequent page level rules associated with that object type
will be run on this new node.
A page level node must have a unique ID but typically has common types. For example, the ID of a page could
be "TM000005" and the type could be "Main_Page". It is common for fields to have a field ID that is the same
as the field type, however the ID must be unique.
AddChildDCONode("3","NewField","NewField","0","-1")
This example adds a new field DCO node to the current object.
The new field is added to the end of the collection of children
and has an initial status of 0.
AddChildDCONode("@X.MyLevel", "@X.MyID", "@P\TM000001\TYPE", "@X.MyStatus", "@X.MyPosition")
This example illustrates obtaining the parameter values at runtime. If the parameters
are static, then they can simply be hard coded in the parameter as in first example.
Here the intent is to show that values can be obtained from other locations
as necessary. The object created is determined by the value of "MyLevel" on the current node.
Likewise, the ID is determined by the value of the variable MyID on the current node.
Assuming this action is called on a document node, the type obtained is the same type
of the page with ID "TM000001" and that page's type is passed as a parameter to create
a sibling page of the same type. The last two parameters in this example are also
obtained from variables on the current object.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for a list of status values.

method.name: AddChildDCONodeToBatch
method.qi: : Adds new Node (Document, Page or Field) to the Runtime DCO on the batch level
method.ap:
ObjectType:
The new DCO node object type: 3=Field, 2=Page, 1=Document.
If the parameter provided is invalid, this value will default to "3" (Field).
ID:
The Node's ID. This value must be unique. If blank, a unique ID will be assigned.
Type:
The Node's Type.
Status:
The Node's Numeric Status. Optional, Defaults to 0.
Index:
The Node's Zero based Index. Optional, Defaults to add to the end of the children (-1).
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Creates a child DCO node of the type indicated by the first argument (A Field, Page or Document).
The new node is a child to the batch top-level DCO node. The child will always be added to
the batch object regardless of the calling object's level.
If a node of the same type and ID exists no new node will be created and the action will return True.
Restrictions: Documents can only have child Documents, Pages and Fields. Pages can only have child Pages, and Fields.
Fields can only have child fields.
The new child node is added to the runtime DCO hierarchy. The new node will now function just like all existing
nodes meaning that any rules defined for that object type in the setup DCO will now run in subsequent rules.
For example, if a page is added to a document, subsequent page level rules associated with that object type
will be run on this new node.
A page level node must have a unique ID but can have common types. For example, the ID of a page could
be "TM000005" and the type could be "Main_Page". It is common for fields to have a field ID that is the same
as the field type, however the ID must be unique.
AddChildDCONodeToBatch("3","NewField","NewField","0","-1")
This example adds a new field DCO node to the batch object.
The new field is added to the end of the collection of children
and has an initial status of 0.
AddChildDCONodeToBatch("@X.MyLevel", "@X.MyID", "@P\TM000001\TYPE", "@X.MyStatus", "@X.MyPosition")
This example illustrates obtaining the parameter values at runtime. If the parameters
are static, then they can simply be hard coded in the parameter as in first example.
Here the intent is to show that values can be obtained from other locations
as necessary. The object created is determined by the value of "MyLevel" on the current node.
Likewise, the ID is determined by the value of the variable MyID on the current node.
Assuming this action is called on a document node, the type obtained is the same type
of the page with ID "TM000001" and that page's type is passed as a parameter to create
a sibling page of the same type. The last two parameters in this example are also
obtained from variables on the current object.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for a list of status values.

method.name: CheckDCOStatus
method.qi: : Confirms that the status of the Document Hierarchy's current object is identical to the status entered as the parameter.
method.ap:
ExpectedStatus:
The expected status of the current DCO object.
Multiple expected status values can be provided as a comma separated list.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Confirms that the status of the Document Hierarchy's current object is identical
to any of the the status values entered as the parameter.
When only one status value is provided,
this action is equivalent to the following action:
rrCompare("expected status","@X.STATUS")
Either action will achieve the same result where "expected status" is
the same value passed in to CheckDCOStatus when a single status value
is expected. It may be still desirable to
use CheckDCOStatus for clarity of intention.
If an object needs to be checked for multiple possible status values,
then use CheckDCOStatus.
CheckDCOStatus("0")
CopyFile("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.tif", "@APPPATH(export)+\+@ID+.tif", true)
This action returns true if the current object has a
status equal to 0, and false if it does not.
This kind of action is used to control logic flow. The action after this action
will run if true is returned. If false is returned, then the next action is
skipped and control continues on the next function in the ruleset.
In this particular example, if the status of the current object is 0 then
the CopyFile action is run to and the current image file
is copied to the export directory. Any set of required
actions can follow a check like this.
CheckDCOStatus("0,2,49")
This action returns true if the current object has a
status equal to 0 or 2 or 49, and false if it does not.
rrSet("48", "@X.StatusToCheck")
CheckDCOStatus("@X.StatusToCheck")
This is similar to the above example however the expected status
is stored in a DCO variable called "StatusToCheck". In this example,
the variable was previously set to "48" so the action will check if the
current DCO object has a status of 48 and returns true if the current object has a status
equal to 48, and false if it does not.
method.see:
SetDCOStatus, CheckDCOType, rrCompare
Refer to the top level help for more information about an object's status.

method.name: CheckDCOType
method.qi: : Confirms that the status of the Document Hierarchy's current object is identical to the status entered as the parameter.
method.ap:
ExpectedType:
The expected type of the current DCO object.
Multiple expected status values can be provided as a comma separated list.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Confirms that the type of the Document Hierarchy's current object is identical
to any of the the type values entered as the parameter.
When only one type value is provided,
this action is equivalent to the following action:
rrCompare("expected type","@X.TYPE")
Either action will achieve the same result where "expected type" is
the same value passed in to CheckDCOType when a single type value
is expected. It may be still desirable to
use CheckDCOType for clarity of intention.
If an object needs to be checked for multiple possible type values,
then use CheckDCOType.
CheckDCOType("Invoice")
CopyFile("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.tif", "@APPPATH(export)+\+@ID+.tif", true)
This action returns true if the current object has a
type equal to Invoice, and false if it does not.
This kind of action is used to control logic flow. The action after this action
will run if true is returned. If false is returned, then the next action is
skipped and control continues on the next function in the ruleset.
In this particular example, if the type of the current object is Invoice then
the CopyFile action is run to and the current image file
is copied to the export directory. Any set of required
actions can follow a check like this.
CheckDCOType("Invoice,Main_Page,Trailing_Page")
This action returns true if the current object has a
type equal to Invoice or Main_Page or Trailing_Page, and false if it does not.
rrSet("Main_Page", "@X.TypeToCheck")
CheckDCOType("@X.TypeToCheck")
This is similar to the above example however the expected type
is stored in a DCO variable called "TypeToCheck". In this example,
the variable was previously set to Main_Page so the action will check if the
current DCO object has a type of Main_Page and returns true if the current object has a type
equal to Main_Page, and false if it does not.
method.see:
SetDCOStatus, CheckDCOType, rrCompare
Refer to the top level help for more information about an object's type.

method.name: CheckDocumentCount
method.qi: : Compares the number of documents to a previously set variable.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action counts the number of documents
within the batch and confirms that it matches the adjusted or expected
number of documents. A single document can contain multiple pages,
but will still be counted as one document.
The number of expected documents is usually provided by the operator of a job's Scan task.
This very handy action can compare the actual amount to the estimate at any time after a
CreateDocuments
action has assembled the documents in the batch.
The action will check the count against an "adjusted" count or an "expected" count. The
adjusted count is determined by the value of the batch level variable "AD".
If the batch level variable "AD" does not exist or is not a valid number, the actual pages
count from the batch pilot object is used. It is expected that a previous rule or task
as set the AD variable at the batch level as appropriate for the application logic.
if the adjusted count, @B.AD, is not set, or is zero, then the batch page count
is compared to the "expected" page count. The expected page count is determined
by the value of the batch level variable "ED".
If the batch level variable "ED" does not exist or is not a valid number, the expected pages
count from the batch pilot object is used.
If both the adjusted count and expected counts are non-zero, then this action will
compare the number of pages against the expected count.
Refer to the CreateDocuments action to understand how it converts the pages in a
batch to a document structure after each page has had a page type configured
in a typical Page ID task.
rrSet("10","@B.AD")
CheckPageCount()
In this example, if the actual number of documents in the batch is 10,
then the action will return true, otherwise it will return false.
It does not matter if a document has one page or many pages,
it will still be counted as one document.
rrSet("12","@B.ED")
rrSet("10","@B.AD")
CheckPageCount()
In this example,
because both ED and AD are set, the count will be checked against
the ED setting.
method.ret:
True
if the actual count is the same as the expected or adjusted count.
Otherwise,
False.

method.name: CheckFieldConfidence
method.qi: : Checks the confidence of all fields on child pages against a minimum acceptable confidence value and sets the page status.
method.ap:
MinimumConfidence:
The Numeric value of the minimum confidence required for the action to return true.
The confidence must be an integer between 1 and 10.
If a field has the variable "ReqConf" set, the value of this variable will override
the provided parameter. The "ReqConf" variable uses the range 0-9.
NewPageStatus:
The Numeric Page Status code to assign to any page that has one or
more fields with Low Confidence data: if a field's ConfidenceString property contains
a value lower than the first parameter. Child fields, line items, etc. are included.
Typically, "1" (Problem) is the value of this parameter.
PageStatusToCheck:
A comma separated list of page status to check.
If blank then only pages with a status of "0" will be checked. Pages that already
have a page status of "1" will be skipped even if it is specified as a parameter.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Checks the confidence of all field data on child pages with a status that matches the specified status.
Each field will have the confidence value of each character within the field evaluated
against a minimum acceptable confidence value.
1 is the lowest confidence level and 10 is the highest confidence.
Starting from the current DCO node, the action will check each field to confirm each character meets
the minimum confidence. If any field contain characters that have a confidence
lower than the specified minimum, the parent page status is changed
to the new status provided by the parameter. If this action is called on a page object,
then just the fields on the page object will be checked. If called on a document, then all
pages within that document node are checked. If called at the batch level, then all pages
in the entire batch are checked.
If a field object has the variable "ReqConf" set, then the value of
that variable will override the value of the MinimumConfidence parameter for the field.
A typical use for this action is to confirm that the recognized field data
is of a high enough confidence so the application can assume that the page data has been
recognized accurately. If one or more characters in any field attached to the page have a confidence
that is lower than the minimum, then the page status is changed. Typically the status is changed
to "1" so the page will be flagged for review by a verify operator in a verification panel.
During verification, the operator will review and adjust the recognized data as necessary,
raising the confidence so the page will result in a successful status allowing it to complete
the verification step.
CheckFieldConfidence("8", "1", "")
This example will confirm that all fields contain characters that have a confidence
of 8, 9 or 10. If one character of any field has a lower confidence, then the parent
page will be set to a status of "1". Only pages with a status of "0" will be checked.
rrSet("1","@X.TheNewStatus")
CheckFieldConfidence("6", "@X.TheNewStatus", "0,2,49")
This is similar to the above example. Here the action will check that
each character on a page has a confidence between 6 and 10. If a field has
a lower confidence, then the parent page will be set to the value provided
in the DCO variable "TheNewStatus", which was preset to "1". Pages with
a status of 0, 2 or 49 will be checked. If a page does not match this status,
the page's fields will not be checked.
method.ret:
True
if all fields in all source pages meet the confidence requirement.
False
if any field on any page has low confidence data, or if the parameters are not Numeric.
method.see:
CheckDCOStatus
Refer to the top level help of this action library for more information regarding confidence.

method.name: CheckIntegrity
method.qi: : Checks that the batch meets the document page count requirements.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Checks that the integrity of the batch, as detailed in the Page file
of the current task, meets the integrity requirements (min, max, order) set within the
Document Hierarchy (Setup DCO).
"Integrity" refers to the correct types and numbers of pages within each document
in the batch and the correct order of the pages in each document.
This action performs an integrity check on the entire batch regardless of the DCO level on which it is called.
Refer to the CreateDocuments action to understand how it converts the pages in a
batch to a document structure after each page has had a page type configured
in a typical Page ID task.
CheckIntegrity()
This action is typically called at a batch level after the document structure has
been created by the "Create Documents" action to confirm the objects
within the batch meet the integrity requirements.
method.lvl: Any level, but usually called at the batch level.
method.ret:
Returns
True
if no integrity problems are found. Otherwise,
False.
method.see: See the top level help for more information regarding the DCO.

method.name: CheckLastDCOType
method.qi: : Checks the type of the previous sibling object.
method.ap:
PreviousTypeToMatch:
The previous object's DCO Type to compare. The comparison is case sensitive.
LevelToCheck:
(Optional) Objects to compare:
0 - All
1 - Documents only
2 - Pages only
3 - Fields only
If this parameter is blank or invalid, it will default to 0.
IgnoreTypes:
(Optional) A comma-delimited list of Types to skip/ignore in the evaluation.
If the prior object's Type is listed
within the parameter then it will be not be evaluated and if present,
the next object prior to it will be evaluated to see if it matches the specified type.
The first previous sibling object not within this list will
be checked to see if its type matches the expected type.
If the parameter is blank, then only the previous object will be checked to see if it
matches the expected type.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action allows you to test the previous sibling DCO Type relative
to the current DCO node
so an application can take specific subsequent steps based on that type.
This previous node is also considered to be the "last" object
that was processed prior to the current DCO object that is being
processed by the rules engine.
The type of the previous sibling object is compared to the type
provided in the parameter. If the type of the previous sibling DCO node exactly matches
the specified type, then the action will return true.
The LevelToCheck parameter determines if every sibling should be checked or
if only specific sibling types should be checked. If the previous sibling level
does not match the level to check, then the action will look backwards through
the previous siblings until it finds a DCO node with the correct level to check.
For example, if there previous node is a page but the level to check
is specified as document nodes, then the page node will be skipped and
the search will continue until the first sibling node is found that
matches the expected level is found.
If one or more types to skip has been provided, the previous sibling DCO node
will not be checked to see if it is a matching type if the type is specified
in the skip parameter list. For example, if looking for objects of the level
of "page" and the previous sibling found is a page and the type of the page
is listed in the skip list, then that node will not be compared and instead
the search will continue to look at the next previous sibling.
This action only checks sibling objects that are in the DCO prior to the
currently running object. For example, if the current object
is a page level object and the previous search reaches the
first page in the current document, the search will not continue to
the previous document in the DCO hierarchy.
CheckLastDCOType("Separator", "", "")
SetPageType("Invoice")
SetPageStatus("1")
Assuming this action is called on a Page level DCO object,
this sequence checks to see if the previous sibling object was a Separator page.
If so, the type and status of the current page are set to Invoice and 1.
If the previous sibling object's type was not a "Separator", the subsequent actions will not execute.
If the previous sibling object's type is "Separator", then the SetPageType action will run next.
Note that this example does not limit checks to page level sibling objects only,
to do that it would set the second parameter to 2.
CheckLastDCOType("Separator", "", "Trailing_Page,Main_Page")
For this example, assume the batch has this document object
that contains these pages:
˂Document>
- ˂Main_Page>
- ˂Separator>
- ˂Trailing_Page>
- ˂Trailing_Page>
- ˂Invoice>
- ˂EOB>
- ˂Trailing_Page>
If the action shown is called on the "Invoice" page, then the action
would find at the first Trailing_Page and ignore it because
it is in the ignore list. It would then look at the node before
it which is another Trailing_Page and it would also be ignored.
The action would then look at the previous sibling of "Separator"
and return True because that previous sibling is not skipped and it matches
the expected type.
As another example, assume that the action is called on the
EOB object. The action would look at the previous sibling
"Invoice". This type is not ignored so the action would
see if it is the expected type "Separator". Because the
previous sibling is not "Separator", the action will return false.
method.ret:
True
if the Type property of the Document Hierarchy's previous sibling non-skipped object
matches the page type attempting to be matched. Otherwise,
False.
method.see:
SetDCOType, CheckDCOType
Refer to the top level help topic for more information about an object's type.

method.name: CheckPageCount
method.qi: : Confirms the number of pages in the batch meets the expected count.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Counts the number of pages within the batch and confirms that it matches the adjusted or expected
number of pages.
The action will check the count against an "adjusted" count or an "expected" count. The
adjusted count is determined by the value of the batch level variable "AP".
If the batch level variable "AP" does not exist or is not a valid number, the actual pages
count from the batch pilot object is used. It is expected that a previous rule or task
as set the AP variable at the batch level as appropriate for the application logic.
if the adjusted count is not set, or is zero, then the batch page count
is compared to the "expected" page count. The expected page count is determined
by the value of the batch level variable "EP".
If the batch level variable "EP" does not exist or is not a valid number, the expected pages
count from the batch pilot object is used.
If both the adjusted count and expected counts are non-zero, then this action will
compare the number of pages against the adjusted count. If the adjusted count
is zero, then this action will check the current number of pages against
the expected count.
Refer to the CreateDocuments action to understand how it converts the pages in a
batch to a document structure after each page has had a page type configured
in a typical Page ID task.
rrSet("10","@B.AP")
CheckPageCount()
In this example, if the actual number of pages in the batch is 10,
then the action will return true, otherwise it will return false.
rrSet("12","@B.EP")
rrSet("10","@B.AP")
CheckPageCount()
In this example,
because both EP and AP are set, the count will be checked against
the AP setting.
method.ret:
True
if the actual count is the same as the expected or adjusted count.
Otherwise,
False.

method.name: ClearVariableInFields
method.qi: : Copies the value of the field along with the position and confidence.
method.ap:
VariableName:
The variable to clear in all child fields.
FieldPrefix:
Optional. If provided, only fields that match this type prefix will be cleared.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action clears a specific variable in all child fields for the current page. If a FieldPrefix is provided,
then the action only clears the variable if the field type starts with the text
provided in the FieldPrefix.
ClearVariableInFields("FlexFieldType","Field")
This example clears the variable "FlexFieldType" in
all child fields that have the type "FieldXXXXXXXX".
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: CopyFieldAndChildren
method.qi: : Copies an entire field object to another page or field.
method.ap:
Target:
Specifies the parent page or field object where the new field will be added. It must
consist of smart parameter syntax that navigates to the target page / field object or it can be the name of the page
where the child field will be copied.
Source:
Specifies the field object to copy as a child to the target object. This must be a smart parameter navigation specification
for a field object.
method.h:
This action copies the source field and all of its child fields, if any, to the destination object.
The field's text values and runtime DCO variables and children are also copied.
The target object cannot be a child of the source object.
If the target object already contains a child field of the same name, the existing child field will be removed
and will be replaced by the new field and its children.
CopyFieldAndChildren("TM000002", "@X")
This example assumes the action is part of a rule called on the field that will be copied.
The current field object, specified by the smart parameter syntax "@X", and any child fields
is copied to the page with the ID "TM000002". If the current field object is called "MyField",
then "MyField", and any children field objects, will be copied to the page with ID TM000002.
rrSet("TM000002", "@P.MyTarget")
CopyFieldAndChildren("@P.MyTarget", "@X")
This example is very similar to the previous example. The difference is that the target page name
is stored within a DCO variable. In this case, the DCO variable is called "MyTarget" and
is a variable on the parent page of the field attached to this rule.
In a realistic scenario, the variable "MyTarget" would have populated in a previous rule or
task and is now being used by CopyFieldAndChildren. This example sets the variable
immediately before calling the action for illustration of how the page name can be stored
in a variable.
CopyFieldAndChildren("@D\Main_Page", "@P\MyFieldToCopy")
This example assumes the action is part of a rule called on a page that contains a field called "MyFieldToCopy"
or on a child field of that page. The example also assumes that the source page is within the same document structure
that contains a Main_Page.
The smart parameter "@P\MyFieldToCopy" instructs the action to access the field "MyFieldToCopy" from
the current page. The smart parameter "@D\Main_Page" instructs the action to locate the "Main_Page"
object which is a child of the parent document object.
The result is that the field "MyFieldToCopy" and any child fields it contains, if any,
are copied to the "Main_Page" of the current parent document.
method.lvl:
This action can be called on any level as but is typically called on the
current page object that contains the field to be copied or
on the current field to be copied.
method.ret: True if the operation succeeds. False if an error occurs.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about DCO variables.

method.name: CountPagesToVariable
method.qi: : Counts the number of pages in the document.
method.ap:
Variable:
The variable that will hold the page count. If the input is a smart parameter
syntax that specifies a variable, the value will be stored in that location. If the input
is not a smart parameter, it will be treated as the name of the variable to
use on the current DCO object.
method.h:
This action will count the number of page objects that exist on the current
DCO document object and write the result into the variable.
CountPagesToVariable("MyVarName")
This example will place the count in a variable called "MyVarName" on the current
document object. If the variable does not exist in the DCO, it will be created.
CountPagesToVariable("@B.MyVarName")
This example uses smart parameter syntax and
will place the count in a variable called "MyVarName" on the batch level
object. If the variable does not exist in the DCO, it will be created.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about DCO variables.

method.name: CreateDocuments
method.qi: : Arranges the contents of a batch into documents based on the Document Integrity rules.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action assembles all of the pages within the batch to a hierarchy of Batch->Document->Page.
Pages within the batch are grouped together based on the document integrity rules based
in the settings in the Setup DCO. The special document and page level variables/properties
"min", "max" and "order", along with the order of the pages within the batch, are
used to determine how many pages, and which pages, belong under
a single document node. The rules for how the pages become arranged can be complex
and these variables must be properly set in the Setup DCO. The result is that
the pages are arranged in the runtime DCO in the manner specified.
Initially pages are ingested to a batch with a page type of "Other", which is a page
without a document structure and each page is attached directly to the batch node.
After ingestion, images could be manipulated such as splitting single page tifs
out of a PDF or from a multi-page tif. The parent fields may then be marked as deleted
so they are no longer processed, although they can still exist in the batch for export
at the end of the process. Images may then have image enhancements applied to
clean them up and make them consistent for the page identification step.
Next page identification would occur. Rules run on each page of type "Other". These
custom rules then determine the actual page type of the document. It could be determined
by matching an image fingerprint to assign a the real type, reading a barcode on the
actual page or on the preceding page, to determine the correct type, other types of automated tests
can be performed, or pages can be manually identified with the Flex ID task. Once
the correct type for a page is determined, the page type is changed from "Other"
to the correct type. This is important as the next step will be to create the document
structure. The
CreateDocuments
action will look at these assigned page types
and generate the desired object hierarchy based on the order, page types, and the
special "min", "max" and "order" variables.
A high-level example of how this action can work would can be illustrated with
the foundation APT application. In this application, a single document can contain
one "Main_Page" type followed by any number of "Trailing_Page" types. Separators can also
be optionally used to note the start and end of documents. The order in which the
pages exist within the batch is also very important as it determines how pages are associated
with the same document. A document can consist of only 1 Main_Page and no trailing pages
or it can have any number of trailing pages. As CreateDocuments runs, it will
look at each page type, the controlling variables and organize each page under a document.
The first document may have under it 1 Main_Page and 2 Trailing_Page. This is a 3
page document. The next page type was Main_Page and since only 1 is allowed,
create documents created a new document node and put the page in the new document node
along with the trailing pages, if any. This continues until all of the pages
have been arranged.
When developing an application, the runtime DCO is written to the batch directory
for use by the next step in the workflow. This XML can be reviewed by the
application developer to confirm that the application is configured correctly so
the pages are arranged correctly under documents. While the developer can
manually review the XML file, it is only for direct use by the systems within
Datacap. Any direct manipulation by custom actions or other applications
is not supported. If writing custom actions, the supported DCO objects
and Datacap APIs can be used to manipulate the DCO and its nodes.
Batches containing existing document structures will cause this action to return False,
with no affect to the existing document structure. If it is necessary to
re-create the batch structure a second time, then the existing document structure
needs to be removed prior to calling this action. This can be performed
with the action RemoveDocumentStructure.
Note: During document creation, temporary IDs are assigned (with a different format than final Document IDs),
and if the action fails, these temporary IDs may remain.
This action is applied at the Batch level, and generally in its own Ruleset such as a CreateDocuments ruleset.
CreateDocuments()
method.ret:
True
if successful. Otherwise,
False.
This action will not create a document structure if a document structure already exists.
If there is a need to re-create the document structure, first remove the document structure
then call this action.
method.see:
RemoveDocumentStructure
Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document structure.

method.name: CreateFields
method.qi: : Creates the fields for a page and the associated runtime DCO Data file.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Creates the runtime field objects based on the field structure defined
for the page within the setup DCO. Once the fields have been created,
then the rules engine will begin running rules on fields and operations
such as recognition can be performed on the fields.
This action creates the field DCO structure. It does not load the position
information for the fields. A fields "zone" or "position" is determined by the
fingerprint that is associated with the page. A single page type can have one
or more fingerprints that are applicable to the page. For example, a page could be
an "Invoice" type. Invoices have a known set of data that is captured such as
Date, Invoice Number, Customer, Vendor, Tax, Total, etc. An invoice from vendor
"XYZ Plumbing" probably has a very different format than an invoice from "123 Donuts".
Different fingerprint templates will identify the "zone" coordinates for each field
on the different documents, allowing documents of different formats to be processed
by a single application with the same set of rules. Additional fingerprints allows
an application to ingest and validate invoices from other vendors without
having to develop new rules to process the new type of document.
When this action is run and the fields are created, they exist in the
batch as an XML datafile. The Data file for the first page
in the batch, tm000001, as an example, is tm000001.xml. While developing
an application it may be useful to look at this file to debug problems.
It is not recommended and is not supported for custom actions or external
program to directly
use or manipulate the runtime DCO XML file. The only way a custom action is allowed
to manipulate DCO nodes is through the Datacap DCO object interface.
This Data file lists all fields for the current page based on the fields listed
in the setup Document Hierarchy. Each field has an ID and
three properties with default values:
TYPE, Position, and STATUS. If this action is called but fields are not
created, then it is recommended to confirm that the action is being
called on the correct page object and that the setup DCO is correct.
Subsequent actions of various kinds such as Recognition, Locate, Zone, Validation, etc.,
can assign other values to these properties.
These actions can also add properties, also called DCO variables,
and values to the Data file, or remove properties and values.
AnalyzeImage()
SetSearchArea("0.5")
SetProblemValue("0.3")
SetDirectoryFPX("@APPPATH(fingerprint)")
FindFingerprint("True")
CreateFields()
This Invoices application sequence sets up the current page for processing,
associates the page with a fingerprint,
and finally creates the fields and associated runtime DCO with blank fields for the page.
method.see:
Refer to the top level help for this action library for information regarding application
objects, the DCO hierarchy, variables and how they can be used.

method.name: CopyFieldTextConfidenceAndPosition
method.qi: : Copies the value of the field along with the position and confidence.
method.ap:
Source:
A reference to the source field.
Target:
A reference to the target field.
Either parameter is optional. If a parameter is not specified, it will default to the text value of the
calling object.
method.h:
The action retrieves the value, confidence, zone coordinates and image reference of the source field object,
and copies them to the target field object. The target must specify a field object.
CopyFieldTextConfidenceAndPosition("@B\OPERATOR","@P\OPERATOR")
This example copies the Batch field OPERATOR values to the
OPERATOR field of the bound object of the Document Hierarchy. It implies that this action is called on a page
object and the child field OPERATOR will be the target field.
CopyFieldAndConfidence("@P\Total","@X")
This example assumes the rule is associated with a field object. The values from the sibling
field object "Total" will be copied to the current field object.
method.lvl: Any level but the parameters must reference a field using smart parameter notation.
method.ret:
False
if the action cannot retrieve the target or source object. Otherwise,
True.
If the position or confidence cannot be copied, the action will still return
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: CopyFieldAndPositionToVariable
method.qi: : Copies the value of the field and position to another variable in the same field object for all child objects.
method.ap:
TextVariable:
The name of the variable to store the text value. If blank, then the text value will not be stored.
PositionVariable:
The name of the variable to store the position. If blank, then the position will not be stored.
Smart parameters are supported for both variables.
method.h:
This action will check the current object and all children objects. If the object is a field
object, then the text value of the field will be stored in a backup variable whose name is specified by the
TextVariable parameter and the position of the field will be backed up into a variable whose name is
specified by the PositionVariable. Variables will be created using the provided name on the current field
object, if this action is called on a field, and each field child field object of the current object.
This action can be useful to back up field information on an entire page. For example, the action could
be called prior to a Verify task and then after the verification is complete, the application can check to see
if the data as changed in any the fields.
CopyFieldAndPositionToVariable("PreVerify Val", "PreVerify Pos")
Assuming this action is called on a document object, the action will check all fields on every
page within the document object. For each field on every page, the text value of the field will be duplicated
in a variable called "PreVerify Val" on the same object and the field position will be stored
in a variable called "PreVerify Pos". For example, if the document contained two pages and
each page contained three fields, then each field on each page will have the new
variable "PreVerify Val" and "PreVerify Pos" created with the data from the field.
rrSet("PreVerify Val", "@X.MyTextVarName")
rrSet("PreVerify Pos", "@X.MyPosVarName")
CopyFieldAndPositionToVariable("@X.MyTextVarName", "@X.MyPosVarName")
This second example will have the same result as the first example. This is simply an illustration
of obtaining the names of the variables at runtime using smart parameters. In an actual implementation
the names would probably have been set by some other rule or obtained from a location that was
set at runtime.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: DeleteDCOChildOfType
method.qi: : Deletes a child DCO node of the specified type.
method.ap:
Type:
The child type to remove.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Deletes all child objects of the specified type from the Document Hierarchy.
The search is only 1 level deep which will only delete immediate child objects.
Grandchildren are not evaluated but will be removed if their parent is removed.
This action must be the last action called in a ruleset. Due to the removal of objects
from the DCO, subsequent actions may not run on objects that were not deleted. Any
subsequent actions must be run in a following ruleset.
DeleteDCOChildOfType("Trailing_Page")
Assuming the application has pages of type called "Trailing_Page", when called
at on a document level object, any children of type "Trailing_Page" will
be removed from the parent object. Subsequent rules will no longer be run
on the object that was removed.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: DeleteDCOChildWithStatus
method.qi: : Deletes a child DCO node of the specified status.
method.ap:
Status:
Remove all children with the specified status.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Deletes all child objects with the specified status from the Document Hierarchy.
The search is only 1 level deep which will only delete immediate child objects.
Grandchildren are not evaluated but will be removed if their parent is removed.
This action must be the last action called in a ruleset. Due to the removal of objects
from the DCO, subsequent actions may not run on objects that were not deleted. Any
subsequent actions must be run in a following ruleset.
DeleteDCOChildWithStatus("75")
While any status can be specified, 75 typically means that the object
has been previously marked for deletion. The example
will delete any children of with a status of 75
from the parent object. Subsequent rules will no longer be run
on the object that was removed.
method.ret:
True
unless an error occurs then
False
is returned.
If no child objects are removed because none of them have a matching
status, the action will still return true.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy and an object's status.

method.name: DeleteDCOParent
method.qi: : Deletes the parent DCO node of the current node.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Deletes the parent of the document hierarchy object to which a rule with this action is bound.
This action will also delete the current object as well. This must be called as
the last action on a ruleset and that any subsequent actions
that need to run must be placed in a following ruleset.
DeleteDCOParent()
If called on a page object, this will delete the parent object, which is
usually a document node. If called on
a field node, this will delete the parent which is typically a page node.
method.lvl: Document, Page, and Field. The calling object must have a parent node and a grandparent node.
method.ret:
False
if a parent object cannot be found, the grandparent cannot be found or if the deletion
of the parent object fails. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: DeleteDCOChildrenWithVariableValue
method.qi: : Removes immediate children that contain a variable with a specific value.

p.name: VariableName
p.qi: The variable to test on the child object.

p.name: VariableValue
p.qi: The value that indicates the child is to be deleted.

method.ap: All parameters support smart parameters.
method.h:
This action removes immediate children from the batch object, such as pages that have the batch object as the parent.
The child object is removed if it contains the specified DCO variable and the variable's value matches the provided value.
One use for this action is that as objects are processed, they can have a variable set that indicates
they are no longer needed and should be removed from the DCO tree. For example, PDF or multi-page TIFF
documents that have been burst into single pages. This action does not delete any of the files
associated with the object, it only removes the object from the DCO tree so it is no longer processed.
Any files that were associated with the object will remain in the batch directory.
The action is expected to run at the batch level and will only look at the immediate children, meaning
that it does not traverse down document hierarchies to delete pages.
Therefore, this action must be called prior to calling the CreateDocuments action which creates the full
document tree structure.
It is recommended that this action is called only in the last function of a ruleset.
DeleteDCOChildrenWithVariableValue("original_source_image", "yes")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: DeleteDCOChildren
method.qi: : Deletes all child objects from the calling object of the Document Hierarchy.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Deletes all child objects such as pages or fields that are children of the bound object of the Document
Hierarchy. If called on a page object, this action will also remove the page data file (.xml),
which holds the field information, from the batch,
if it exists.
DeleteDCOChildren()
If this action were called on a document node, then all of the pages attached
to the document, and their field objects, will be removed from the DCO. If called
on a page level object, then all of the fields will be removed from the page.
If called on a field, then any children sub-fields will be removed.
method.ret:
True
if successful, otherwise
False.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: DeleteDCOChildrenAndVariables
method.qi: : Clears all variables and child objects of the current object.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Removes all DCO children and variable references from the currently bound object. All child
objects are deleted and all variables in the current DCO object are deleted, leaving the
current DCO object existing, but it will not contain any data.
Once a child object is deleted, it no longer exists in the object hierarchy and
rules will not be run on deleted objects.
While not explicitly prevented, this action is not expected to be called at the
batch level because every object and variable from within the batch will be removed.
CreateFields()
DeleteDCOChildrenAndVariables()
Applied at the Page level, the example will first add fields to the page and then remove
all of the fields and all of the variables within the current page object. While
these two actions would not typically be ordered like this in a real application,
it is intended to demonstrate that all of a page's field objects will be removed
by this action.
method.ret:
True
if all child objects and their variables are removed, otherwise
False.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: DeleteDCOVariable
method.qi: : Deletes the specified DCO variable
method.ap:
VariableName:
The name of the variable to delete.
ObjectType:
Indicates if the variable should be deleted on the current object
or on children of a specific type. If the value is invalid or blank, the current object
will be used.
0 = Current object only.
1 = Child document objects only.
2 = Child page objects only.
3 = Child field objects only.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action will delete the specified variable from the runtime DCO. If the ObjectType is set to the
current object, then the variable will be deleted for just the current object. If a document,
page or field object type is specified, then if the current object, or any of the child objects,
match the specified object type, then the specified variable will be deleted.
It is not required that the variable exists on the target object, but if it does exist it will
be deleted.
DeleteDCOVariable("MyVar","3")
This example will delete the variable "MyVar" on the current object, if it is a field,
and all child objects. If this was called on a document object, then all of the fields
on all pages within the current document would be checked and the variable would
be deleted.
rrSet("MyVar", "@X.NameOfVarToDelete")
rrSet("3", "@X.ObjectTypeToUpdate")
DeleteDCOVariable("@X.NameOfVarToDelete","@X.ObjectTypeToUpdate")
This second example has the same results as the first example. It simply illustrates that
the values can be passed using smart parameters. In an actual implementation, the variables
would like be assigned in some previous rule or task.
DeleteDCOVariable("MyVar", "0")
This example deletes the variable "MyVar", but only on the current object that is
associated with the running rule.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy.

method.name: HasDCOChildOfType
method.qi: : Returns true if the current object has a child of the specified type.
method.ap: The type to locate as a child of the current DCO node. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action checks the child objects of the current node to see if any of them
match the type that is specified. This action only checks the immediate child objects
with a one child depth and will not check the children of the child nodes.
HasDCOChildOfType("Main_Page")
If the current DCO node has a child page object of the type "Main_Page", the
action will return true. If it does not, it will return false.
rrSet("Airline", "@X.LookForMe")
HasDCOChildOfType("@X.LookForMe")
This example checks each of the child node to see if one of them
is of the type specified in the DCO variable "LookForMe". In this example,
the variable was previously set with "Airline" causing the action
to look for a child of type "Airline".
method.ret:
True
if the current object contains a child or children specified of the type
specified by the parameter. Otherwise,
False.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information about the document hierarchy and an object's type.

method.name: IsDocumentCountMoreThan
method.qi: : Counts the number of documents and returns true or false if the count is exceeded.
method.ap:
Count:
The document count to compare.
ReturnTrueIfMore:
Controls if the action returns true or false based on the comparison.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Counts all of the document objects within the batch and returns true or false based
on the provided count.
This action only counts document nodes attached to the batch level object.
Typically documents only exist off of the batch level. If an application should have
a document that is the child of another document node, the child document nodes
are not included in the total count.
IsDocumentCountMoreThan("1", "true")
This example returns true if there are more than 1 document object in the batch.
IsDocumentCountMoreThan("1", "false")
This example returns false if there are more than 1 document object in the batch.
method.ret:
if returnTrueIfMore is
true,
the action returns true if the document count exceeds the parameter, otherwise
false
is returned.
if returnTrueIfMore is
false,
the action returns false if the document count exceeds the parameter, otherwise
true
is returned.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding document objects.

method.name: IsFirstDocumentInBatch
method.qi: : Checks to see if this is the first document in the batch.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Checks to see if this is on an object in the first document in a batch. If called on
a document node, the action will return true if it is the first document in the batch.
If called at a page or field level, the action will check to see if the parent
document node is the first node in the batch.
IsFirstDocumentInBatch()
If the current node belongs to the first document, the action will return true
and the next action in the function will run. If not, the action will return false
and control will switch to the next function in the ruleset.
method.ret:
True
if on the first document, or the current object in the first document. Otherwise
False.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding document objects.

method.name: IsFirstPageInBatch
method.qi: : Checks to see if this page is the first in the batch.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Checks to see if this page is the first in the batch.
If documents have been created,
it does not matter if this has been arranged as the first page object or if other
page objects have been placed ahead of it in the DCO tree. If the page was
the first page created in the batch, it will return true.
IsFirstPageInBatch()
If the current page node is the first page in the batch, the action will return true
and the next action in the function will run. If not, the action will return false
and control will switch to the next function in the ruleset.
method.ret:
True
if it is the first page. Otherwise
False.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding page objects.

method.name: IsMultiPageDocument
method.qi: : Checks if the current document object has multiple pages.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action returns true if the current document object contains multiple child pages.
If called on a page or field object, the action will check the parent document object.
IsMultiPageDocument()
method.ret:
False,
if called at the Batch level, the document object cannot be found,
or if the document does not have more than 1 child.
Otherwise,
True.

method.name: IsSinglePageDocument
method.qi: : Checks if the current document contains a single page.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action is used to determine if the current object is a document with only 1 child page attached.
IsSinglePageDocument()
PopulateZNField()
method.ret:
False,
if called at the Batch level, the document object cannot be found,
or if the document has more than 1 child.
True,
if the document contains one page.

method.name: JoinDocumentWithPreviousDocument
method.qi: : Combines the previous document into the current document.
method.ap:
Type:
Document Type of previous document (to be joined with the current document).
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Called on a document level object, the pages from the previous document
are moved into this document. The pages from the previous document will be placed
in front of the pages in the current document.
The previous document object will be removed so the result is that the
structure of both documents are merged into a single document level object.
