If the type of the previous document does not match the type
provided in the parameter, then the documents will not be joined.
JoinDocumentToPreviousDocument("SeparatorDoc")
The current document object will be merged with the previous document object,
if the previous document type is "SeparatorDoc".
If the runtime DCO was like this before:
SeparatorDoc
- Page1
- Page2
InvoiceDoc
- Main_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Trailing_Page
After calling the join action, the structure will look like this:
InvoiceDoc
- Page1
- Page2
- Main_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Trailing_Page
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding document objects.

method.name: MoveBatchPageToPreviousDocument
method.qi: : Moves the current page without a document structure into a document object.
method.ap:
NewDocumentType:
If the current page is the batch's first child object, a new document object
will be created with the type specified.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The current page will be moved to become a child of the first document node
that is previous to the current page node. If the page is the first object
in the batch, then a new document node will be created and this page object
will be moved to the new document, becoming a child page of the new document object.
This action must be run on a page object that is directly attached to the batch level object.
The "Other" page type is an example of a page that does not have a document hierarchy and
is directly attached to the batch DCO node.
If this action is run on a page node that is already in a document structure,
the action will exit without moving the page.
MoveBatchPageToPreviousDocument("OtherDoc")
This example must be run on a page object that is directly attached to the
batch level object. This is a page that has not yet been assigned to a document
structure. The page will be moved into the previous sibling document, if it
is a document object. If there isn't a previous document object, then
a new document object will be created and assigned the provided type.
With the DCO structure like this:
Batch
- Document1
- InvoicePage
- Document2
If the action is called on "InvoicePage", then the page will be moved
to the "Document1" object.
Batch
- InvoicePage
- Document1
- Document2
If the action is called on "InvoicePage", then a new document node
of type "OtherDoc" will be created and "InvoicePage"
will be moved to the new "OtherDoc" object.
method.lvl: Page Level, but will execute only if the page's parent is the batch level object.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding page objects.

method.name: PageIDBySequenceTypes
method.qi: : Assigns a type to all pages of type 'Other' from a list of types.

p.name: SequenceTypes
p.qi: A comma separated list of page types to assign.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action processes all pages with a type of "Other", assigning them page types
as specified by the input parameter list. The action will process each page and assign each type
in order as they appear in the DCO tree.
When the end of the list is reached, assignments will start again from the start of the list.
PageIDBySequenceTypes("Front,Back")
The action will set the page types of the batch to Front, Back, Front, Back, Front, and so on.
It is assumed that the pages have all been ingested in the correct order, or that earlier
actions have determined the correct order and have either properly ordered the pages
or have created a correct list used as a parameter.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: PageIDByVariableChange
method.qi: : Assigns page types using a main and trailing page paradigm based on the value of a DCO variable.

p.name: VariableToWatch
p.qi: The name of the variable to check in each page object.

p.name: MainPageType
p.qi: The type to assign to the first page of the document.

p.name: TrailingPageType
p.qi: The type to assign to all trailing pages in the document.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action processes all pages within a batch and sets the page type according to the input parameters.
When pages are ready for PageID, a variable can be "watched" so that when it changes
a new page type will be triggered.
One use case for this action is to create the document structure from
multi-page TIFFs or PDFs that went through a VScan process and have
been split into single images.
The action will watch the DCO variable that is identified by the first parameter. The first page
in the batch will be set to the page type identified by the second parameter. The action will
then continue to look at the DCO variable for each subsequent page. If the value of the variable
does not change, each subsequent page will considered a trailing page and is assigned the page type identified by the third
parameter. Processing all of the pages in the batch, this continues until the value of the DCO variable changes. When a change is
detected, it indicates a new main page and that page type is set to the page type identified in the second parameter.
Subsequent pages are then set to the page type identified by the third parameter, until reaching
the last page of the batch, or the watched variable changes again.
While this action is attached to the batch level node,
the DCO variable identified in the first parameter is a variable that must exist on
every page level DCO object in the batch.
PageIDByVariableChange("ScanSrcPath", "Main_Page", "Trailing_Page")
In this example, the variable ScanSrcPath contains the path to the
source image. When TIF pages are split from a multiple page TIF or PDF,
the ScanSrcPath variable identifies the parent document that was split into pages.
This variable will be the same for all pages that came from the parent and will change
on pages that came from a different parent.
This action will watch the contents of the variable ScanSrcPath on each page within
the batch. When the variable changes,
the first page will be set to the page type Main_Page, and any
other pages that continue to have the same value in ScanSrcPath that immediately follow will
have the page type set to Trailing_Page.
The action will scan through each page, looking at the value of ScanSrcPath. When it changes again,
the first page will be set to the page type Main_Page and any subsequent pages with the same
value in ScanSrcPage will have the page type set to Trailing_Page. This will continue until
all pages in the batch have been set. It is also assumed that after splitting a document into
multiple pages, the parent document has been deleted from the DCO tree prior to calling this action.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: PopulateTaxType
method.qi: : Loads the search terms for the Taxes field.
method.ap: A comma separated list of types to process for creation of the tax lineitems.
method.h:
For each tax type provided, a "Tax_Type" and "Tax_Value" lineitem field is created.
The current field must not contain children.
This action is for APT and not intended for general use.
PopulateTaxType("Sales,VAT,GST")
method.lvl: Field Level. The Taxes/TaxLineitem/Tax_Value field in APT.
method.ret:
Always
TRUE.

method.name: PromotePageToDocument
method.qi: : Converts a page object to a document object.
method.ap:
NewDocumentType:
The new document type for this page node.
NewDocumentID:
The new document ID for this page node. If a parameter is provided
this ID must be unique within the batch.
Leave this field blank to have the action create a unique ID.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action converts the current page object to a document level object. This action is useful for situations
where file has been ingested as a page level node and it is desired to change the page node to a document node,
so the file associated with the node is now a document level object.
This is achieved by creating a new document node of the type specified in the parameter.
The variables from the current page node, such as IMAGEFILE and other variables will be copied
over to the new document node. If the page has associated data files, they will now be
associated with the current document using the same variable names.
The ID of the new document object will be unique, it will not duplicate the ID from the original page object.
Once the new document object is created, the existing page DCO node will have its status changed
to "75", indicating that it is in "Deleted" state. This action does not delete the page from the object hierarchy.
To fully remove the page object from the batch, use an action like DeleteDCOChildWithStatus("75") to remove
pages that have been marked for deletion.
The current page node must be a direct child of the batch. The new document node will be a child of the batch.
Any child fields of the current page will not be moved to the document object.
Any child fields and associated data will be deleted when the page node is deleted.
After this action is called, it is recommended that no further rules are run on the page object as it will be removed.
Additionally, any rules which will be run on the new document object should be in a
following ruleset, not the same ruleset as this action.
Ruleset1
- Rule1 (Attached to a page DCO)
- - Function1
- - -
PromotePageToDocument(“Invoice”,“”)
- Rule2 (Attached to batch close)
- - Function2
- - - DeleteDCOChildWithStatus("75")
Ruleset2
- Rule3 (Attached to a document level “Invoice” DCO)
- - Function3
- - - SetNamePattern(“2”)
- - - rrSet(“1”,”@X.convPdfIgnoreContent”)
- - - rrSet(“0”,”@X.y_createLayout”)
- - - PDFFREDocumentToImage(“300”,”18”,”33”,”32”,”.bw.tif”,”col.tif”,”gray.tif”,”0”,”False”,100”)
This example assumes that Rule1 is attached to a page level object that needs to be promoted to a document
object, Rule2 is attached to the batch close event and
Rule3 is attached to an “Invoice” document object. The action PromotePageToDocument
will convert the current page object to a new document object of type “Invoice”. The original
page is marked with status 75 to indicate it is deleted.
Rule2 runs at the batch level and deletes all children that have a status of 75. This action
must be the last action in a ruleset. Any subsequent actions must be in a separate ruleset.
If desired, DeleteDCOChildWithStatus could be in its own ruleset as long as the ruleset
does not contain additional actions. Any subsequent actions must be in a new ruleset.
Ruleset1 will complete and then the next ruleset2 will run on the new document node,
converting the associated PDF file into multiple TIF images.
A new page object will be created for each TIF and each page will be a child of the Invoice document.
method.lvl: Page level only. The page must be a direct child of the batch object.
method.ret:
Returns
false
if the NewDocumentType parameter is blank or if an error occurs, otherwise
true
.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding field objects.

method.name: RefreshFields
method.qi: : Updates the Data file for a page in a batch with new fields and also preserves the data for previously created fields.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Updates the runtime field data file for a page
with new fields and also preserves the data for previously created fields. If additional fields have been
created after a previous call to CreateFields, this action will create the required
child DCO field objects for the current page for the newly created fields.
This action is similar to CreateFields except that if there is already a Data file for a page then it will not
erase the previously created fields and will just add new fields to the page.
Existing fields will remain unchanged.
SetPageType("Main_Page")
RefreshFields()
This sequence of actions assigns the page type "Main_Page" to the current
page, then will initialize any new fields that belong to "Main_Page"
that do not already exist on the current page.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding field objects.

method.name: RemoveDocumentStructure
method.qi: : Removes the document hierarchy from the batch.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action will flatten the document - page hierarchy from the batch. If the batch consists of multiple documents,
each with a set of pages, the document level is removed and all of the pages become a flat structure.
Once complete, there is no distinction of sets of pages within a document.
It is recommended that this action is called as the last action within a ruleset.
Place any following actions into a follow on ruleset.
RemoveDocumentStructure()
If a batch has a document structure like this:
Batch
- Invoice
- - Main_Page
- - Trailing_Page
- - Trailing_Page
- Invoice
- - Main_Page
- - Trailing_Page
- Invoice
- - Main_Page
- - Trailing_Page
- - Trailing_Page
- - Trailing_Page
After this action completes, the DCO structure will be:
Batch
- Main_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Main_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Main_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Trailing_Page
- Trailing_Page
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding the DCO hierarchy.

method.name: SetDCOStatus
method.qi: : Assigns a value to the Status property of the current object of the Document Hierarchy.
method.ap:
An Integer representing the new status.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Assigns a value to the Status property of the current object of the Document Hierarchy.
The status indicates various states of the object. It may indicate the last step
that was performed on the object or it can convey that the object is in an error
state.
CheckDCOType("Invoice")
SetDCOStatus("1")
This sequence checks to see if the current object of the Document Hierarchy is a
an Invoice. If so, the value of the object's Status property is set to "1".
Function1 Test Date Range
- IsFieldDateEqualOrBefore("@DATE()")
- IsFieldDateWithinXDays("7")
-
SetDCOStatus("0")
Function2 Date Outside Range
-
SetDCOStatus("1")
Assuming this is called on a field object node, these actions first validate that the
current field contains a valid date that is equal to or before the current date.
The next action then confirms that the date is within 7 days of today's date.
If both of these tests pass the status of the field is set to "0"
indicating that it does not have any errors.
If either "IsField..." action fails, then control passes
to the following function which sets the object status to "1"
which indicates it has a failure.
method.ret:
False
if the input parameter is not an integer, otherwise
True.
method.see:
SetDCOType, SetPageType
Refer to the top level help of this action library for information regarding DCO types and status.

method.name: SetDCOType
method.qi: : Assigns a value to the Type property of the current object of the Document Hierarchy.
method.ap:
Type:
The new value to assign to the current DCO node's Type property.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Assigns a value to the Type property of the current object of the Document Hierarchy.
When changing the type of the current node, the status value of the node
is left unchanged.
This action can set the type of a page similar to the action SetPageType. SetPageType
also has some slightly different features refer to that action for details.
The batch type defaults to the name of the application. While this action allows the
batch type to be changed, it is not recommended as it could cause unintended results.
This action allows field types to be changed. Typically the field type and field ID are
the same value.
An object's type value may not contain a double quote. If a double quote is provided,
it will be changed to a single quote.
CheckLastDCOType("Separator")
SetDCOType("Invoice")
This sequence checks to see if the previous sibling object of the application's
document hierarchy was a Separator page. If so, it
sets Invoice as the Type property of the current object.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetDCOStatus, SetPageStatus, SetDocumentType
Refer to the top level help of this action library for information regarding DCO types and status.

method.name: SetDocumentStatus
method.qi: : The action assigns a status to the current document node or parent document node.
method.ap:
Type:
An integer representing the new status.
method.h:
Similar to the SetDCOStatus action, but works at the Document, Page or Field level. If called at the
page or field level, the status is set for the parent document object and the status of the current
child object will not be changed.
CheckDCOType("Invoice")
SetDCOStatus("1")
This sequence checks to see if the current object of the Document Hierarchy is a
an Invoice. If so, the value of the object's Status property is set to "1".
Function1 Test Date Range
- IsFieldDateEqualOrBefore("@DATE()")
- IsFieldDateWithinXDays("7")
-
SetDCOStatus("0")
Function2 Date Outside Range
-
SetDCOStatus("1")
Assuming this is called on a field object node, these actions first validate that the
current field contains a valid date that is equal to or before the current date.
The next action then confirms that the date is within 7 days of today's date.
If both of these tests pass the status of the field is set to "0"
indicating that it does not have any errors.
If either "IsField..." action fails, then control passes
to the following function which sets the object status to "1"
which indicates it has a failure.
method.ret:
False
if the input parameter is not an integer, otherwise
True.
method.see:
SetPageType, SetDCOStatus, SetDCOType, SetDCOStatus
Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding an object's status.

method.name: SetDocumentType
method.qi: : The action assigns a type to the current document or parent document object of the Document Hierarchy.
method.ap:
Type:
The new value to assign to the Document DCO node's Type property.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Similar to the SetDCOType action, but works at the Document, Page or Field level to set the
document object type. If called at the page or
field level, the type is still set for the parent document object and the type of the current
object will not be changed.
When changing the type of a page node, the status value of the node
is left unchanged.
An object's type value may not contain a double quote. If a double quote is provided,
it will be changed to a single quote.
The application's scan task typically assigns Other as the Page Type and 49 as the default
Page Status for every successfully scanned image in the batch.
The sequence below is an example of a rule that changes the type of the current page to Invoice and assigns a page new status:
SetPageType("Invoice")
SetPageStatus("1")
This combination sets the page as an Invoices page, and gives it a status of 1.
This means that the page has not yet been validated and must be processed by a
task which applies Validation rules.
method.ret:
False
if the current DCO node is not a page or a field or if the provided field does not have a parent object.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
SetPageStatus, SetDCOStatus, SetDCOType
Refer to the top level help of this action library for information regarding DCO types and status.

method.name: SetFieldConfidence
method.qi: : Sets the confidence for all characters in a field to the same value.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a DCO field node.
NewConfidence:
The confidence value (1-10) to be assigned to the field's characters.
If the parameter is invalid or out of range, it will default to 10, which is the
highest confidence.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action unconditionally sets the confidence values for every character within a field to a specific value.
This action can help change confidence levels when the preceding actions are all successful
and it is desired to update the field confidence automatically to show that all characters are valid.
Conversely, it is possible to set all of the characters to a low confidence value to ensure
that the characters are all reviewed in a follow on process or in a verification panel.
If a field has text such as "Hello Datacap" and the characters were recognized
in order with these confidences, "8,8,8,8,4,4,8,8,8,3,9,9", calling this
action with a confidence value of 8 will set the confidence for each character
in the field to a value of 8, regardless of its current value.
For example, if a set of calculations involving one or more fields is
successful, this may indicate that the confidence level of those fields' values should be forced
to a high confidence - regardless of the
confidence set by the recognition engine. After the success of the calculation, the rules
can call
SetFieldConfidence("@P\MyField","10")
to unconditionally re-set
the confidence values of the fields to the highest possible confidence.
The examples below show how the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action
CalculateFields could be used to automatically validate the results
of field recognition. Applications can have other kinds of use cases that
would allow a field to be automatically validated and set to a high
confidence without requiring operator interaction. Another example
could be a database look-up of a recognized name, or other automatic type
of confirmation that one or more fields are believed to be recognized
correctly even if the recognition engine is unsure of some of the characters.
When viewing the confidence directly in the field level XML, values are actually
0 - 9 to permit one character to reflect the value of each character within
the xml. This illustrates that to the user the range is exposed as 1 - 10
but internally it is sometimes treated as 0-9. When developing and debugging
an application, be aware of this potential situation.
SetFieldConfidence("@P\GrossSalary", "10")
This example sets all characters in the field "GrossSalary" to a confidence of 10.
The action could be called on a page level DCO node or on a sibling field level
DCO node and the smart parameter would resolve correctly as first it would
resolve to the current page and then to the child DCO node called "GrossSalary".
SetFieldConfidence("@P\AdjustedPay" , "1")
Similar to the previous example, this one will lower the confidence of each
character in the field "AdjustedPay" to a low confidence of 1.
If called on a page level node, it will navigate from the current page to find
the child "AdjustedPay". If called on a field level node, it will navigate up
to the parent page, then look for the sibling field "AdjustedPay".
SetFieldConfidence("@X", "1")
Similar to the previous action, however this one would be expected to
be called directly on a field level DCO node and the current field's confidence
would be adjusted.
This next example shows using SetFieldConfidence in the context
of a test run before setting the confidence.
CalculateFields("@STRING('1TotalWages' + '2TaxableInterest' + "3Unemployment' = '4AdjustedGross')")
SetFldConfidence("@P\1totalWages", "10")
SetFldConfidence("@P\2TaxableInterest", "10")
SetFldConfidence("@P\3Unemployment", "10")
SetFldConfidence("@P\4AdjustedGross", "10")
If the calculation works, the application can assume that all of the characters are read
correctly because all of the fields summed up to the correct value
and
SetFieldConfidence
can adjust the fields to high confidence.
Note, in this example it would be a good practice to also add a check
that the values are all non-zero to eliminate a completely "bad read".
method.ret:
Always
True.
If the target input parameter is invalid, no confidence levels
are changed and a message is logged.
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic for more information regarding a field's confidence.

method.name: SetObjectID
method.qi: : Renames the target dco node with a new object ID.
method.ap:
NewID:
The value that will be used as the new Target ID. If this parameter is blank, the
text property of the current object will be used.
TargetObject:
A smart parameter referencing a target which is receiving the new ID.
If this parameter is blank, then the current object will be the target.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Allows an object's ID to be changed at runtime. An object's ID should be unique.
An object's ID is set by Datacap actions and clients when new objects are created.
The assigned ID usually does not need to be manually set or changed. Changing an object's
ID can change how rules are run. An object's ID should not be manually changed unless it
is absolutely necessary as it can produce unintended results. If this action must
be used, it is recommended that this be run in the last rule of a
ruleset so any subsequent rules are run in a new ruleset.
SetObjectID("@F.MySourceVar","@P")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, new ID value is obtained from
the variable called "MySourceVar". The value is then assigned to
of the calling object's Parent page object.
SetObjectID("","")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, new ID value is obtained from
the text value of the current field. The value is then assigned to the ID
of the current field.
method.see: Refer to the top level help of this action library for information regarding DCO types and status.

com.qi: : Identifies pages and assigns types and fingerprints through fingerprint matching.
com.h:
When ingesting and processing documents in a Datacap application, typically documents and pages are classified to identify the data within
the document or to control how the page should processed. Fingerprints are a classification mechanism that matches images
based on the geometry of the image. It is typical for a Datacap application to use fingerprints to classify pages
within the workflow. It is allowed for other types of classification techniques to be used in addition to fingerprints.
The rules within an application are flexible to allow exclusive use of fingerprints for classification or mixing fingerprinting
with other types of classification, including techniques that may be custom for an application.
Classification can be configured uniquely for any Datacap application. With that said, there are some typical types of classification
that are performed and are briefly described here. The intent is to provide basic understanding of fingerprints, how they can be used
as a starting point that can be used in an application which are then changed or expanded as required by a specific application's
use cases.
One approach to classification is by using separator sheets. These are typically sheets with a barcode and are used to separate
different pages that are scanned. The presence of a new separator sheet, denotes the start of a new document. Fingerprints
can classify documents in addition to or instead of separator sheets. To fingerprint a page, the page needs to be analyzed,
using the AnalyzeImage action, to create a CCO file that is a geometric representation of the page. This representation will then
be matched using the FindFingerprint action against known formats. When match, the page type is then determined. Additionally
a fingerprint template is assigned to the page, the fingerprint template defines zones / fields on the page that contain
the data that will be extracted or verified by an operator. While classification can be performed without using fields,
it is a typical scenario where fields are also used.
Using the APT application as an example, a page may be identified as a "MainPage" which is the first page of
an invoice. This causes different processing for that type of page, opposed to other types such as separator
pages which may be ignored or deleted. An application may process invoices from 1000s of different vendors.
One invoice may be from "ABC Plumbing" and another may be from "XYZ Car Rental". Because they are provided by different
vendors, each will have their own format and layout to the invoice that was received. However, there are some common properties
of an invoice that the application needs to process such as date, vendor name, address, tax, total and line items for items
covered by the invoice. While each page is identified as a "MainPage", the matched fingerprint template for each page will
be unique. For example, ABC Plumbing may have the date in the top left corner of the page while XYZ Car Rental puts the
date at the bottom of the page. The matched template contains the location of the desired data so the application can
correctly obtain the data from the invoice. APT has additional abilities where it can ingest invoices that have not
been previously processed and dynamically determine the locations of these values and then save a fingerprint so the
locations are known the next time an invoice is received from the same vendor.
That is one example of how fingerprints can assign page types and field zone templates for pages. Datacap has the ability
to run unique rules for each object type within an application. Perhaps pages defined as invoices need one set of operations
and documents identified as bank statements need a different set of processing steps. The page types determined by fingerprinting
will then control the pages as the continue through the workflow.
Prior to fingerprinting, images are typically pre-processed to ensure the greatest accuracy when processed. For example,
images are typically straightened, de-speckled and have blobs and lines removed prior to fingerprinting. This will help
detection by applying a uniform look to pages prior to identification. It is quite possible that it may not be desired to
show these processed forms to the user, or more likely, it is desired to save the original documents as they came in and
not the versions that have been adjusted for fingerprinting or recognition. The Datacap actions always save the original
version of the image prior to performing image adjustments. This original version of the image can always be used or stored
as required in later steps of the workflow.
Local Fingerprints
By default fingerprints are stored and used "locally" on the machine that is running rules and are held within
the client or process. For example, fingerprints are typically used in a "Page Identification" task.
When this process is performed, the AutomaticDocumentFingerprint actions will load the fingerprints
defined for the application, then perform fingerprint matching and creation. It is all local on the
current machine. This process occurs for each batch that is run. The benefit of using fingerprints
locally is that no additional setup is required beyond adding the required fingerprint actions to a
Datacap application. A draw back of local fingerprints are that the fingerprints will be loaded for
each batch. If there are a large number of fingerprints, this could be several minutes. It also will\
consume memory within the process that is running the batch. For better performance, the
fingerprint service is the recommended mechanism for using fingerprints.
Fingerprint Service
The Datacap Fingerprint Service, in combination with actions from this action library, supports the ability to cache and
use the fingerprints from one or multiple Datacap applications simultaneously. The Fingerprint Service overcomes
the time-consuming process of loading all the fingerprints of an application each time a batch is run.
The solution involves reading all the fingerprints into the system memory cache of the Fingerprint Server when the
first fingerprint match is requested. As a further optimization of this process, only the identification portion
of the fingerprint is loaded into memory. The fingerprints remain in system memory for the life of the Fingerprint
Service process. The result is the elimination of the fingerprint load time for all but the first batch that
is processed by an application. Large-scale implementations, where large numbers of fingerprints
(typically over 1000 fingerprints) are required for document identification, use of the Fingerprint Service is recommended.
Other than identifying the location of the fingerprint service with the SetFingerprintWebServiceURL, the actions
within this action library will transparently use the fingerprint service vs the local service. The important step is to
first call the
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL
action to specify the location of the service, then subsequent actions,
in the same profile, will automatically use the service instead of using local fingerprinting operations.
The fingerprint service requires IIS and can be configured on a machine which can be shared
by multiple applications. Refer to the fingerprint service configuration documentation
"Installing and configuring the Datacap Fingerprint Service" for more information.
The first time that a match is requested by an application, the Fingerprint Service loads the fingerprints (all *cco files)
for that application. When more than one application is set up to use a single Fingerprint Service,
the first time each application requests fingerprint matching, the fingerprints for that application are loaded into memory.
The greater the number of Fingerprints to read into memory, the longer the service takes to begin fingerprint processing;
which can be from a few seconds to many minutes for large fingerprint deployments. Subsequent requests for matching
work with the fingerprints in the cache in memory. When a matching fingerprint is not found and the
application creates a new fingerprint, that new fingerprint is loaded into the cache.
The Datacap Fingerprint Service is a web service that is based on Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS).
The service can service multiple client requests simultaneously. The service can service multiple client requests simultaneously.
The Datacap Fingerprint Service cache is shared by all rulerunners or clients running the application.
Therefore, the single load of fingerprints into the cache for an application is all that is required even when multiple threads are running.
If the fingerprint service is enabled and an action that uses the fingerprint service is called, such as FindFingerprint,
and if the fingerprints are not yet loaded, or if the load is in progress due to it being initiated by another batch,
by default the action will wait up to 20 minutes for the fingerprint load to complete. The default time is long enough for most installations.
Should more time be required due to a significantly large amount of fingerprints, set the DCO variable
FingerprintServiceWait_Seconds
to
the maximum number of seconds that the action should wait for the fingerprints to load on the service. This variable would be set on the
same DCO node where FindFingerprint is called. In other words, if one batch is loading fingerprints and another batch calls FindFingerprint,
it will wait up to the 20 minute default time for the load to finish. If the load is not finished, the FindFingerprint action will not perform
a fingerprint match and will return false. Increasing the timeout will avoid this problem during long fingerprint load times at the service.
Once the fingerprints are loaded by the services, they
will remain loaded for subsequent calls to FindFingerprint and will not need to be reloaded. If the service is recycled, then on the next
call to the service, the fingerprints will be reloaded.
XML Fingerprints
XML fingerprints are preferred over traditional/legacy fingerprints. Fingerprints consist of two types of metadata. The first type is a
CCO file that contains the fingerprint geometry information used when matching fingerprints. The second type of metadata are
the zone locations on the fingerprint. Each zone identifies the location of text that is captured by an application.
For example, typical areas of an invoice page would include a date, invoice number, customer name, etc. The zone location
identifies each of these and the coordinates where the text exists on a page.
The key difference between these two types of fingerprints is how the zone information is stored.
Traditional fingerprints store the zone information within the Setup DCO of an application. The XML fingerprints
store the zone information externally as associated files in the fingerprint directory.
The advantage of XML fingerprints becomes apparent as the number of application fingerprints increases.
When the application's Setup DCO contains a large number of fingerprints, it can slow the processing
of an application, even when not performing fingerprint operations. The issue does not occur when using XML fingerprints.
If 'Enable FPXML' setting is checked in the application settings 'Main' tab within the Taskmaster Application Manager,
when zoning fingerprints in Datacap Studio, the application will place field zone information into a fingerprint XML file instead of placing the zone
information into the applications setup DCO. One XML file is created per fingerprint.
If the application is using fingerprint XML files, then use the action XMLReadZones to load the field zone coordinates.
Additional Information
It is recommended to review the best practices guide for recognition for tips on how to improve
image quality prior to fingerprint matching and recognition.
Fingerprints rely on the creation of a CCO for the image that is associated
with the DCO page. The CCO is typically created by the AnalyzeImage
action and/or with a recognition action. More information about the CCO can be found in the top level
help of the "SharedRecognitionTools" action library.
The top-level help topic of the ApplicationObjects action library discusses the Datacap Object Hierarchy (DCO)
including the different object levels and object variables. It is recommended that the DCO is well
understood when writing a Datacap application.
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
The complete smart parameter reference is available in the top-level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library.

method.name: CalculateOffset
method.qi: Sets the standard Offset value to be used when matching source pages to fingerprints.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Calculates the offset, in pixels, between the CCO for the current page and the fingerprint that
it matches. The fingerprint template must have already been set from a previous call to FindFingerprint,
SetFingerprint or some other method to associate the correct template with the current page.
The result of the calculation is stored in the current page object in a variable called "Image_Offset"
in the form "x,y", where the value x is the pixel difference on the x-axis and y is the
pixel difference on the y-axis.
The confidence of the match is stored in the current DCO variable called "Confidence".
FindFingerprint("False","")
CalculateOffset()
This example will compare the CCO for the current image with the matched fingerprint and store the difference
in the variable "Image_Offset". For example, "-24,-16"

method.name: AddAndSetFingerprint
method.qi: Creates a fingerprint for the current source page with a specified class type.
method.ap:
FingerprintClass:
The fingerprint class name to assign to the new fingerprint. If this parameter is
blank, then the global name '˂New˃' will be assigned. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Unconditionally adds the current fingerprint for the current source page to the fingerprint
directory for future fingerprint matching and allows the host fingerprint class to be specified.
The current page must have an existing, black and white, image file (.tif) and its fingerprint processing file (.cco).
These files are given a unique fingerprint template ID and added to the fingerprint database.
The TIF image and the CCO file will be added to the fingerprint directory.
Upon successful completion of the action, the following variables will be created in the
current page DCO:
"Confidence" are created with a value of "1".
"TemplateID" are set with the new ID associated with the fingerprint.
"Fingerprint Created" are set to "Yes".
The resulting fingerprint will consist of two files: the page's Image file (.tif) and its Processing file (.cco).
SetFingerprintDirectory must have been called before this action. If using the fingerprint service, then
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL must also have been previously called.
SetFingerprintDirectory("@APPPATH(fingerprint)")
AnalyzeImage()
AddAndSetFingerprint("Invoice")
This example configures the fingerprint directory then calls AnalyzeImage to create a fingerprint for the
current page based on the page's associated TIF image. The fingerprint is then added to the
current collection of fingerprints. Note that while SetFingerprintDirectory is shown in this example,
it is typically called on a batch level so it is set only once.
For more information, see SetFingerprintDirectory.
method.ret:
False
if the rule with this action is not bound to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy;
if the current page does not have an Image file; if a CCO fingerprint file has not been
created or if the fingerprint's two files cannot be created in the fingerprint directory.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
SetFingerprintDir, SetFingerprintWebServiceURL
Refer to the top-level help for more information on using fingerprints and the fingerprint service.

method.name: AddFingerprint
method.qi: Creates a fingerprint for the current source page.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Unconditionally adds the current fingerprint for the current source page to the fingerprint
directory for future fingerprint matching.
The fingerprint will be associated with the global host fingerprint class ID.
If the new fingerprint must be associated with a specific fingerprint class, then use the
AddAndSetFingerprint action.
The current page must have an existing Image file (.tif) and its fingerprint processing file (.cco).
These files will be given a unique fingerprint template ID and added to the fingerprint database.
The TIF image and the CCO file will be added to the fingerprint directory.
Upon successful completion of the action, the following variables will be created in the
current page DCO:
"Confidence" will be created with a value of "1".
"TemplateID" will be set with the new ID associated with the fingerprint.
"Fingerprint Created" will be set to "Yes".
The resulting fingerprint will consist of two files: the page's Image file (.tif) and its Processing file (.cco).
SetFingerprintDirectory must have been called prior to this action. If using the fingerprint service, then
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL must also have been previously called.
SetFingerprintDirectory("@APPPATH(fingerprint)")
AnalyzeImage()
AddFingerprint()
This example configures the fingerprint directory then calls AnalyzeImage to create a fingerprint for the
current page based on the page's associated TIF image. The fingerprint is then added to the
current collection of fingerprints. Note that while SetFingerprintDirectory is shown in this example,
it is typically called on a batch level so it is set only once. Refer to SetFingerprintDirectory
for more information.
method.ret:
False
if the rule with this action is not bound to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy;
if the current page does not have an Image file; if a CCO fingerprint file has not been
created or if the fingerprint's two files cannot be created in the fingerprint directory.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
SetFingerprintDir, SetFingerprintWebServiceURL
Refer to the top-level help for more information on using fingerprints and the fingerprint service.

method.name: DeleteFingerprint
method.qi: Deletes the current page's fingerprint.
method.ap: None.
method.ret:
Always returns
True.
Under certain conditions the action will be unable to delete the fingerprint
but will still return True. For example if the action is not applied at the Page level or if the
current page does not have an fingerprint template set.
Please review the action log file if DeleteFingerprint does not perform as expected.
method.h:
Removes a fingerprint from the application and fingerprint database.
Deletes the image file (.tif) and fingerprint file (.cco) of the current page's fingerprint from the
application's fingerprint directory, and its record from the Fingerprint database.
The current page must have an associated fingerprint template from a previous
action such as FindFingerprint or nothing will be deleted.
SetFingerprintDirectory action must be called prior to this action.
If the fingerprint service is in use, the fingerprint will not be unloaded. Instead
it will simply not be loaded the next time the service loads fingerprints.
SetFingerprintDirectory("C:\ParentDirectory\Application\fingerprint")
DeleteFingerprint()
This example will set the fingerprint directory and then delete the fingerprint template
that is associated with this page. It is assumed that FindFingerprint, SetFingerprint
or similar action has been previously run to find the fingerprint that is associated with
the page. Note that while SetFingerprintDirectory is shown in this example,
it is typically called on a batch level so it is set only once. Refer to SetFingerprintDirectory
for more information.
method.see:
SetFingerprintDirectory, AddFingerprint
Refer to the top-level help for general information about this action library.

method.name: CheckForStickyFingerprint
method.qi: Checks if a new fingerprint applies to a follow on page in the same batch.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
For new fingerprints this action checks to see if there another matching fingerprint
within the same batch that has already been verified, where it can
use it to obtain zone information. An example is when a batch contains two similar
invoices, which have never been processed by the system before. Once the first
invoice is zoned during verify, the same new fingerprint can be used
on the second invoice. This is only needed on new matching fingerprints within the same batch
because a fingerprints zones are saved at export time and are available for subsequent batches.
This action has a requirement that the line items parent is called "Details".
CheckForStickyFingerprint()
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: FindBlackFingerprint
method.qi: Attempts to match black forms to fingerprints in the fingerprints directory of an application.
method.ap:
AddFingerprintIfNotFound:
If an existing fingerprint is not matched for the
current page, a value of "True" will cause a new fingerprint to be created based
on the current page. The new fingerprint will match this page on future
calls to this action. The value "False" will cause the action to return false
if the page does not match an existing fingerprint and a new fingerprint will not be created.
PageType:
If parameter "AddFingerprintIfNotFound" is "True", then the provided
page type is assigned to the new fingerprint. The parameter is option. If it is blank
and a new fingerprint is created, then the type assigned to the new fingerprint
will be the same as the current page.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action is similar to FindFingerprint and attempts to match black forms to an existing fingerprint.
A "black" form is a page that contains a dense amount of lines that have not been removed and can provide
better matching on these kinds of pages than FindFingerprint. An example of a black form is a typical
medical claim form which has been faxed making all of the lines black instead of a typical medical form
that uses a drop out color that allows a scanner to remove a specific color, leaving just the text on the image.
The action can optionally create a new fingerprint that matches the current page if none of the existing fingerprints
match the current image.
A CCO file must be associated with the current page prior to calling this action. The CCO file is typically
created using the action AnalyzeImage to create a geometric representation of the image that is used
to match with existing fingerprints.
It is typically recommended to use image enhancement features, such as deskew to first adjust the image prior
to creating the fingerprint. This will improve the matching quality of the fingerprints and
will also improve subsequent recognition, if it will also be performed on the image.
A fingerprint match will occur if the current fingerprint matches an existing fingerprint
with a confidence higher than the value configured with the action SetMinimumMatchingTolerance.
If multiple fingerprints match with a tolerance greater than the configured tolerance,
then the fingerprint that has the best match is returned as the matching fingerprint.
If multiple fingerprints have a the highest confidence match of "1", then the first fingerprint
that matches at the highest confidence will be considered the best match.
This action library has other actions that can be used to adjust how fingerprints are matched, such
as: SetFilterClassName, SetFilterPageType, SetFingerprintWebServiceFailureThreshold, SetMaximumMatchingOffset,
SetFingerprintDirectory which must be used prior to using this action.
RotateImage()
AnalyzeImage()
RecognizePageOCR_A()
SetFingerprintSearchArea("0.0","0.5")
SetMinimumMatchingTolerance("0.7")
SetFingerprintDirectory("@APPPATH(fingerprint)")
FindBlackFingerprint("True","Invoice_Page")
In this sequence, the FindBlackFingerprint action will only use the top 50% of the current page to
search for a match. However, it will accept a match with a confidence of 0.7 or higher. If no match is found,
the sequence will create a new fingerprint and store it in the location specified by the
SetFingerprintDirectory action. If the parameter has been set to False, a new fingerprint
will not be created in case there is no match.
For illustration, this example shows a number of settings such as SetMinimumMatchingTolerance,
SetFingerprintSearchArea and SetFingerprintDirectory on the page object that is calling FindFingerprint.
These actions only need to be called once and they will remain in effect for the rest of the
task profile. They could be called once at the batch level. If implemented exactly as shown,
then these actions will be called over and over for each page of this type, which is
not required and will use some amount of unnecessary processing time.
If fingerprints are used again in a later task profile, any global settings
such as the fingerprint directory, the fingerprint service URL, search area, etc.
must again be configured before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
If the parameter is instead been set to False, no fingerprint will be created if a match is not found.
method.ret:
False
if the action is not applied at the Page level or if the first parameter is
False
and
a fingerprint match does not occur. Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
SetFingerprintDirectory
Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about fingerprints and the fingerprint service.

method.name: FindFingerprint
method.qi: Attempts to match the current page to a fingerprint and creates a new fingerprint if a match does not occur.
method.ap:
AddFingerprintIfNotFound:
If an existing fingerprint is not matched for the
current page, a value of "True" will cause a new fingerprint to be created based
on the current page. The new fingerprint will match this page on future
calls to this action. The value "False" will cause the action to return false
if the page does not match an existing fingerprint and a new fingerprint will not be created.
PageType:
If parameter "AddFingerprintIfNotFound" is "True", then the provided
page type is assigned to the new fingerprint. The parameter is option. If it is blank
and a new fingerprint is created, then the type assigned to the new fingerprint
will be the same as the current page.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action will use fingerprint web service if fingerprint web URL is set by SetFingerprintWebServiceURL and if the
service is available. If the fingerprint web service is not available, then it will default to local fingerprint service.
This action attempts to match the image associated with the current page to an existing fingerprint.
The action can optionally create a new fingerprint that matches the current page if none of the existing fingerprints
match the current image.
A CCO file must be associated with the current page prior to calling this action. The CCO file is typically
created using the action AnalyzeImage to create a geometric representation of the image that is used
to match with existing fingerprints.
It is typically recommended to use image enhancement features, such as deskew and line removal to first adjust the image prior
to creating the fingerprint. This will improve the matching quality of the fingerprints and
will also improve subsequent recognition, if it will also be performed on the image.
A fingerprint match will occur if the current fingerprint matches an existing fingerprint
with a confidence higher than the value configured with the action SetMinimumMatchingTolerance.
If multiple fingerprints match with a tolerance greater than the configured tolerance,
then the fingerprint that has the best match is returned as the matching fingerprint.
If multiple fingerprints have a the highest confidence match of "1", then the first fingerprint
that matches at the highest confidence will be considered the best match.
This action library has other actions that can be used to adjust how fingerprints are matched, such
as: SetFilterClassName, SetFilterPageType, SetFingerprintWebServiceFailureThreshold, SetMaximumMatchingOffset,
as: SetFilterClassName, SetFilterPageType, SetFingerprintWebServiceFailureThreshold,
SetFingerprintDirectory must be used prior to using this action.
If required by Datacap Support, additional logging can be enabled by setting the batch level
variable "EnableCCOLogging" to "1". The logging will provide additional log details
during fingerprint matching. This setting is only applicable to local fingerprints. It has no effect
if the fingerprint service is in use. Enable this logging only when required by Datacap Support.
RotateImage()
AnalyzeImage()
RecognizePageOCR_A()
SetFingerprintSearchArea("0.0","0.5")
SetMinimumMatchingTolerance("0.7")
SetFingerprintDirectory("@APPPATH(fingerprint)")
FindFingerprint("True","Invoice_Page")
In this sequence, the FindFingerprint action will only use the top 50% of the current page to
search for a match. However, it will accept a match with a confidence of 0.7 or higher. If no match is found,
the sequence will create a new fingerprint and store it in the location specified by the
SetFingerprintDirectory action. If the parameter has been set to False, a new fingerprint
will not be created in case there is no match.
For illustration, this example shows a number of settings such as SetMinimumMatchingTolerance,
SetFingerprintSearchARea and SetFingerprintDirectory on the page object that is calling FindFingerprint.
These actions only need to be called once and they will remain in effect for the rest of the
task profile. They could be called once at the batch level. If implemented exactly as shown,
then these actions will be called over and over for each page of this type, which is
not required and will use some amount of unnecessary processing time.
If the parameter is instead been set to False, no fingerprint will be created if a match is not found.
method.ret:
False
if the action is not applied at the Page level, or if the parameter is False and a
fingerprint match does not occur. Otherwise, True. If a new Fingerprint cannot be added, the
action still returns
True.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using
fingerprints and the fingerprint service.

method.name: IdentifyBlankPagesBySize
method.qi: Uses the Image file's size to determine if the file represents a 'blank' page.
method.ap:
MaximumSize:
Numeric value (0 to 2147483647) indicating the maximum size in bytes that qualifies a page as a blank page.
PageType:
If the page is determined to be blank, the specified page type will be assigned to the page. This parameter cannot be blank.
PageToEvaluate:
Numeric value (0, 1 or 2) to designate which pages in a multi-page dco are to be evaluated.
If this value is blank or invalid, then the value "0" will be used.
Values 0, 1 and 2 mean the following:
0 : Every page under the current DCO object will be evaluated.
1 : Only "odd" dco page objects will be evaluated within the DCO. The first child, then the third child, the 5th child, etc.
2 : Only "even" dco page objects will be evaluated within the DCO. The second child, then the fourth child, the 6th child, etc.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.ret:
False
if the MaximumSize or PageType parameter is invalid, the rule with this action is bound to a Field object of the Document Hierarchy
or if an error occurs.
Returns
true
if one or more child pages are identified as a "blank" page because the file size is smaller than the specified size.
method.h:
Uses a page object's image file's size to determine if the file represents a 'blank' page.
The action looks exclusively at the physical file size to determine if the image is blank.
It does not look at the pixels of the image to determine if the page is blank.
The compression of a file will affect the size of a file and the ability of this action to accurately
detect blank pages. A file using a compression such as fax or LZW compression, will likely be very small
if there are a small number of black pixels on an image. A file that is uncompressed, will be the same
size on disk regardless of the number of black or white pixels on the image, making this action ineffective.
The intent of this action is to identify pages that are likely to be blank because they are using
file compression and the physical file size is very small.
Any page or child page with an image file smaller than the size parameter (in bytes) will be
assigned the Page Type value provided as a parameter.
The PageToEvalute parameter will determine if all child pages will be evaluated or if only
alternating pages within the DCO structure are evaluated.
IdentifyBlankPagesBySize("1000","Blank_Page","")
This example will evaluate the current object and the child objects. If called on
a page object, then just the page object will be evaluated. If called on a document object
then all of the document's pages will be evaluated. If called at the batch level, then all
pages in the batch will be evaluated.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.
A similar action, IsBlankPage, in the SharedRecognitionTools action library counts the number of words
in a page's CCO, and if the count is smaller than the provided size, it is considered to be blank.

method.name: IsFingerprintClass
method.qi: Test that the fingerprint belongs to the specified class.

p.name: FingerprintDatabase
p.qi: The connection to the fingerprint database.

p.name: ClassName
p.qi: Test for the fingerprint class name.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action connects to the fingerprint database and verifies that the
specified fingerprint class name contains the
fingerprint ID loaded for the current page.
CheckDCOStatus("75")
IsFingerPrintClass("@APPVAR(*/fingerprintconn:cs)", "Invoice")
DeleteFingerprint()
IncrementVariable("@X.DeletedNewFingerprint", "1")
A parameter of "Invoice" checks to see if the current fingerprint exists in the class called "Invoice",
and if it does, the action returns true and follow on actions can perform further processing in the same function.
method.ret:
False,
if there is an error or if the
current page's fingerprint ID does not exist in the specified class.

method.name: MergeCCOsByType
method.qi: Merges the Fingerprint files (.cco) associated with Page objects of the Document Hierarchy.
method.ap:
TypesToMerge:
Comma-separated string values indicating the Page Types of the Document Hierarchy objects to be merged.
At least one page type must be provided for CCO files to be merged.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
False
if a Fingerprint file (.cco) for one of the Page Types is not available or if an error occurs
while merging. Otherwise,
True.
If none of the pages match the specified page type,
the action will still return
True.
method.h:
Merges the Fingerprint files (.cco) associated with Page objects of the Document Hierarchy.
The CCO for each page under the document node are merged with the CCO for the first page
within the document. The final result will be that the CCO for the first page has been updated
to contain the CCOs for each following page merged into the first page CCO.
Only the CCO for a page that has an associated TIF image can be merged. If a page does
not have a CCO or if the associated page image is not a TIF image, then it will not
be merged.
If called on a page or field level, then the current DCO node must have a parent document
object. The CCOs for each page under the parent document DCO node will be merged
together. For example, if called on a page, the pages under the current document will have
their CCO's merged together. If the page does not have a parent document, such as the page type
"Other" which has a batch as a parent, then this action will not merge the CCOs.
Created DCO Variables:
This action creates several DCO variables in the first page node that
has been merged with the rest of he pages. The variables that contain the information about the merge.
CCOBlock
: The DCO variable "CCOBlock" will be set with the name of the merged CCO file.
id.CCO_n
: The name of this variable is comprised of the ID of the page that contains a merged CCO
followed by ".CCO_" and then suffixed by the index of the page within the CCO. The value
of this variable is the name of the image file that was appended to the CCO. For example
"TM000002.CCO_2" with a value of "TM000003.tif" indicates the primary page is TM000002
and the second CCO that merged corresponds to image file "TM000003.tif". One of these entries
is created for each page that is merged.
mergedimagefile
: This variable is created based on the previous variable. The
value of the variable is the height of the merged image.
For example, the value of the variable is "TM000003.TIF" the value could be 4800. That means
the height of the merged CCO was 4800 pixels. One entry is created for each page merged.
MergeCCOsByType("Invoice_Page,Invoice_Cont")
The
MergeCCOsByType
example above will merged all page types that are of "Invoice_Page"
and "Invoice_Cont" into a single CCO. The CCO for the first page that matches
either of these types will become the primary CCO with all of the merged
pages. All of the pages under the current document will be merged together.
If pages of the same type exist in the batch, but they are associated with a
different document object, they will not be included in the merged CCO.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about fingerprints and CCO files.
Refer to the top-level help topic for the "SharedRecognitionTools" action library
for additional information regarding the CCO file.
The action AdjustMergedCCOPositions in the ZonesAndLineItems action library will
adjust the positions in the merged CCO.

method.name: MergeLayoutByType
method.qi: Merges the layout files (*layout.xml) associated with Page objects of the Document Hierarchy.
method.ap:
Comma-separated string values indicating the Page Types of the Document Hierarchy objects to be merged.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
False
if a layout file (*layout.xml) for one of the Page Types is not available or if the merged layout
cannot be created. Otherwise,
True.
method.h:
Merges the layout files (layout.xml) associated with Page objects of the Document Hierarchy.
The layout.xml for the first page merged will become the new merged layout.xml.
The merged layout.xml can be then loaded to create a merged CCO for the merged pages.
The layout file for the first merged page will be updated to contain
the recognition results from the layout block information for all of the merged pages.
Only pages contained in the current document object will be merged. A layout file must
exist for each of the pages to be merged. Only page types indicated by the parameter
will be included in the merged file.
This action can only be attached to a document node so a document structure must exist.
The document node's child pages will be merged if the page type matches one of the types
provided as a parameter.
MergeLayoutByType("Main_Page,Trailing_Page")
The
MergeLayoutByType
action above combines all of the text of the pages in the current DCO document
of type Main_Page and Trailing_Page into
a single, searchable layout file.

method.name: SetFilterClassName
method.qi: Sets the Fingerprint Class filter for the identification (matching) algorithm.
method.ap:
ClassName:
The name Fingerprint Class you want to use as the filter. Smart Parameters are supported.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.h:
Sets the Fingerprint Class filter for the identification (matching) algorithm.
The filter will force the fingerprint-matching algorithm to use only fingerprints
associated with the specified Fingerprint Class. This can improve accuracy and
performance by limiting the search of fingerprints to smaller subset of fingerprints
within the application.
To disable this filter, call with an empty string as the parameter. If this action is not called then
this filter is not enabled.
Once set, this setting will be in effect for the length of the current task profile or until it is change.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the setting before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
SetFilterClassName("MyFingerprintClass")
FindFingerprint("False","")
This example configures the fingerprint class prior to calling find fingerprint. Only fingerprints
associated with the specified class will be matched. This example shows the filter is set just prior to
FindFingerprint for illustration. As long as this action has been called by a prior rule, the configured
filter will be in effect for the length of the current profile, or until SetFilterClassName is called
again with a different parameter.
method.see: Refer to the top-level action help topic for more information about fingerprints and this action library.

method.name: SetFilterPageType
method.qi: Sets the Page Type filter for the identification (matching) algorithm.
method.ap:
PageType:
The Page Type you want to use as the filter. Smart parameters are supported.
method.lvl: All levels, but generally at the Page level.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.h:
Sets the Page Type Filter For the identification (matching) algorithm.
The filter will force the fingerprint-matching algorithm to use only fingerprints
associated with the specified fingerprint type. This can improve accuracy and
performance by limiting the search of fingerprints to smaller subset of fingerprints
within the application.
A single page type is allowed to have multiple fingerprints. For example, a page type could
be an invoice. While an invoice will typically always have the same kind of data such as
dates, invoice numbers, vendor, shipping information, line item information, etc., the location
of the text on the page can be different on invoice from vendor "A" compared to the location
of data on an invoice from vendor "B". The fingerprint will define the location of the data
based on the specific fingerprint that was matched.
To disable this filter, call with an empty string as the parameter. If this action is not called then
this filter is not enabled.
Once set, this setting will be in effect for the length of the current task profile, unless it is changed.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the setting before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
SetFilterPageType("Invoice_Page")
FindFingerprint("False","")
This example configures the fingerprint class prior to calling find fingerprint. Only fingerprints
associated with the specified class will be matched. This example shows the filter is set just prior to
FindFingerprint for illustration. As long as this action has been called by a prior rule, the configured
filter will be in effect for the length of the current profile, or until SetFilterPageType is called
again with a different parameter.
method.see: Refer to the top-level action help topic for more information about fingerprints and this action library.

method.name: SetFingerprint
method.qi: Sets a newly created fingerprint's Fingerprint Class and Fingerprint Class ID values.
method.ap:
FingerprintClass:
The Fingerprint Class value.
FingerprintID:
(optional) The Fingerprint ID value. All fingerprints must have a unique ID.
If left blank, a unique ID will be assigned automatically. It is recommended to allow the
fingerprint ID to be assigned automatically.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
After using the action AddFingerprint to add a new fingerprint to the set of
fingerprints for the application, use this action to set the newly created fingerprint's Fingerprint Class
and Fingerprint Class ID values.
The fingerprint class and ID are added to the Host table of the
application's Fingerprint database - as RefName and RefID values.
The combination of the actions AddFingerprint() followed by SetFingerprint() may only be used
when the fingerprint service is not enabled. If the fingerprint service is enabled,
and a fingerprint host class ID must also be set for the fingerprint,
then you must use the AddAndSetFingerprint() action instead of the combination of
AddFingerprint and SetFingerprint().
AddFingerprint()
SetFingerprint("@P\VendorName","@P\VendorID")
In this example, smart parameter notation obtains the values at runtime from the field text of the
fields VendorName and VendorID and the text values of those fields
will populate the Host table of the application's Fingerprint Database.
Use this action combination only when the fingerprint
service is not enabled. If the fingerprint service is enabled, use AddAndSetFingerprint.
method.see: AddAndSetFingerprint

method.name: SetFingerprintDirectory
method.qi: Sets the Fingerprint directory of your application.
method.ap:
Directory:
the path to the directory where the fingerprints (.cco files) are stored for the application. Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
Returns
True,
if successful. Otherwise,
False
and sets the batch to an abort state.
method.h:
Sets the Fingerprint directory of your application. This directory contains the application's fingerprints.
This action must be called prior to creating or finding fingerprints.
This action must be called if using local fingerprints or if the fingerprint service is used.
When using the application service, call SetFingerprintWebServiceURL prior to this action.
This action only needs to be called once within a task profile. It can be called at any level but is generally
called on a batch level object on a batch open event. If this is placed on a lower level object, it may then
be called multiple times, which is unnecessary. The setting is in effect for the length of the task profile.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the fingerprint directory before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
SetFingerprintDirectory("C:\ParentDirectory\Application\Fingerprint")
The action above identifies the location and path of an application's Fingerprint directory.
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL(@APPVAR(FPServiceURL)
SetFingerprintDirectory(@APPPATH(fingerprint))
This example is similar to the previous example. The difference is that the values of the parameters
are obtained from the application manager settings using smart parameter notation. Storing values in the application manager allows
a single location to place application settings. Commonly settings that could be different between
production and test systems are stored here. This allows an application to be deployed without any
changes to the rules it would simply be the application manager configuration settings that
contain the correct values for the test environment or the production environment.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about fingerprints.

method.name: SetFingerprintSearchArea
method.qi: Controls the portion of the current page that will be used to find a matching fingerprint.
method.ap:
MatchStart:
A decimal value from 0.01 (1%) to 1.00 (all) to indicate how much of the page is to be matched.
If the second parameter is empty the first parameter represents the bottom of the area for matching, starting from the top of the page.
If the second parameter is not empty, the first parameter is the top or start of the area for matching.
For example, a single parameter of 0.5 indicates that fingerprint matching will be limited to the first half of the page (0 to 50%).
Decimal separators must be appropriate for the current locale.
In applications which might be used in locales with different decimal separators, use percentage notation.
MatchEnd:
Optional: A decimal value from 0.01 (1%) to 1.0 (all) to indicate the end point on the page to be
used for fingerprint matching. If this parameter is supplied, the fist parameter is the starting point.
For example: if the first parameter is 0.6, and the second parameter is 1.0,
the last 40% of the page will be used for fingerprint matching (60-100%).
Both parameters allow either a decimal value or a percentage. The decimal values must match the decimal format for the current locale.
To indicate the value is a "Percentage" the action can use a number followed by "p" - 50p, for example - to represent 50%.
When using the percentage values, the number must be a whole number, and cannot contain a decimal separator.
Decimal separators must be appropriate for the current locale.
In applications which might be used in locales with different decimal separators, use percentage notation.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action uses the numeric value(s) you supply to determine the portion of the current page
that will be used to find a matching fingerprint.
This setting will be in effect for the length of the task profile that is running the rules.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the search area before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
SetFingerprintSearchArea("0.5","")
The example above compares lines and words in the upper 50% of the current page to the lines and
words in the same portion of each fingerprint. Notice the second parameter has been left blank.
SetFingerprintSearchArea("0.5","1.0")
This example compares lines and words in the lower 50% of the current page to the lines and
words in the same portion of each fingerprint. Remember: you can replace a parameter's decimal
value with a percentage(p) or metric(m) number.
method.lvl: All levels, but generally at the Page level.
method.ret:
False
if the first parameter is missing or is not numeric. Also returns
False
if the second parameter is not numeric. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for more information regarding fingerprints and this action library.

method.name: SetFingerprintWebServiceApplicationID
method.qi: Use this action to specify unique application ID.
method.ap:
ApplicationID:
A unique Application ID. This value used to retrieve correct list of fingerprints loaded to the server.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
By specifying an application ID, it will cause the fingerprint service to segregate the fingerprints
from this calling application from other applications. This will prevent fingerprints from another
application being matched with images from this application. It will also limit the fingerprint
matching to the fingerprints within this application only.
Unless there is a specific need to match fingerprints across different applications, then
each application that uses the fingerprint service should use its own unique application ID
to separate its fingerprints and fingerprint matching from other applications.
Once this action is called, it remains in effect for the life of the current task profile.
It is typically called on a batch open event and does not need to be called over and
over on each page when FindFingerprint or other fingerprint actions are called.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the application ID before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
If this action is not called, then the default application name "datacap.ccodb" will
be used. To configure the use of an application name, this action must be called
immediately before or immediately after SetFingerprintWebServiceURL.
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL("http://'FPSERVERNAME'/fpservice/Service.asmx?WSDL")
SetFingerprintWebServiceApplicationID("1040ez")
This example enables the application service by setting the URL, causing subsequent actions
to be handled by the fingerprint service. The action SetFingerprintWebServiceApplicationID
configures all of the subsequent operations from this application to be processed using
the application ID "1040ez".
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for more information regarding fingerprints and the fingerprint service.

method.name: SetFingerprintWebServiceFailureThreshold
method.qi: Uses this action to specify percentage of fingerprint upload failures to ignore.
method.ap:
IgnorePercent:
An integer that represents percent threshold of fingerprint upload failures to ignore.
The batch will abort if the percentage of fingerprints that are failed to load exceeds this value.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
Returns
False
when:
The fingerprint service is not configured using action SetFingerprintWebServiceURL().
Returns
False
and aborts the batch when:
The input parameter is not an integer value from 0 to 100.
If the percentage of fingerprints that failed to load is greater than the threshold.
If no fingerprints have been loaded and at least one has failed to load.
Otherwise,
True.
method.h:
Uses this action to set the maximum number of fingerprint upload failures to ignore.
If the application has been set using the action SetFingerprintWebServiceApplicationID, then the threshold
will be set for that specific application only.
This action is only used with the fingerprint service and SetFingerprintWebServiceURL must
be called prior to this action.
If some fingerprints are not able to be loaded, that may or may not be a problem, depending
on the application. This action will configure the threshold that will determine if too many missing
fingerprints needs to be considered an error. Once this threshold is reached, it will likely cause
all subsequent batches to fail as the fingerprint service will be considered to be non-operational
until the fingerprint issue is resolved.
The fingerprint service will load fingerprints only when an action that requires searching
of fingerprints is called, such as FindFingerprint or FindBlackFingerprint.
If the fingerprint service has not previously been called by an earlier batch using the
same application ID, or if the current batch has not yet called an action that loads
the fingerprints for the specified application, then the service will report that no
fingerprints have been loaded and this action will still return true.
This action typically only needs to be called once per batch. Calling it multiple times
