is allowed but is unnecessary and will take some amount of processing time. Configure your rules
so this action is called once after the fingerprints are loaded and not so it is called
over and over within a single batch. The setting will exist for the length of the
current task profile that is running rules.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure this setting again before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL("http://127.0.0.1/fpservice/Service.asmx?WSDL")
SetFingerprintDirectory(@APPPATH(fingerprint))
FindFingerprint("False","")
SetFingerprintFailureThreshold("10")
This example enables the use of the fingerprint service by configuring the URL for the service,
configures the fingerprint directory for the application, finds the fingerprint
for the current page and then checks to see if the number of failed fingerprints
exceeds the allowed percentage. If it does exceed the maximum, the action returns
false and the batch will be set to abort.

method.name: SetFingerprintWebServiceURL
method.qi: Provides the Uniform Resource Locator (URL) that is a link to a pre-established Fingerprint Service.
method.ap:
URL:
The URL that is the link to the Fingerprint Web Service. Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.h:
This action configures the URL for the fingerprint service. If using the fingerprint service, this action must
be called prior to an action that communicates with the service, such as FindFingerprint and FindBlackFingerprint.
Once connected, then the fingerprint service will be used for all subsequent calls. The action SetFingerprintDirectory
must also be configured prior to using the fingerprint service. When using the fingerprint service,
SetFingerprintWebService should be called within the task profile from this action library.
This action will use fingerprint web service if fingerprint web URL is set by SetFingerprintWebServiceURL and if the
service is available. If the fingerprint web service is not available, then it will default to local fingerprint service.
>
This action should not be called if the application is using "local" fingerprints only. The top-level help topic
for this action provides more information about the fingerprint service and the situations where the fingerprint
service should be used instead of local fingerprints. The fingerprint service must be configured and running
prior to running an application that uses the service.
This action only needs to be called once within a task profile. It can be called at any level but is generally
called on a batch level object on a batch open event. If this is placed on a lower level object, it may then
be called multiple times, which is unnecessary. The setting is in effect for the length of the task profile.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the fingerprint service URL before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
SetFingerprintWebServiceApplicationID("MyApplication")
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL("http://'FPSERVERNAME'/fpservice/Service.asmx?WSDL")
SetFingerprintDirectory("\ParentDirectory\Application\Fingerprint")
This example sets the application name for the fingerprint service and then configures
the web service URL and also sets the fingerprint directory. This example
would typically be called on a batch level object.
SetFingerprintWebServiceURL(@APPVAR(FPServiceURL)
SetFingerprintDirectory(@APPPATH(fingerprint))
This example is similar to the previous example. The difference is that the values of the parameters
are obtained from the application manager settings using smart parameter notation. Storing values in the application manager allows
a single location to place application settings. Commonly settings that could be different between
production and test systems are stored here. This allows an application to be deployed without any
changes to the rules it would simply be the application manager configuration settings that
contain the correct values for the test environment or the production environment.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about fingerprints and the fingerprint service.

method.name: SetMaximumMatchingOffset
method.qi: Sets the Maximum Offset value while matching source pages to fingerprints.
method.ap:
MaximumOffset:
Integer value between 1 and 255. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets the Maximum Offset value while matching source pages to fingerprints.
The actual shift is four times the maximum offset value in pixels (4 * MaxOffset).
Increasing this value improves but slows the matching process.
If this action is not called, the default value is 6: 4 * 6 = 24 pixels.
This action has no effect when used with the Fingerprint Service
Once set, this setting will be in effect for the length of the current task profile.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the setting before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
SetMaximumMatchingOffset("12")
This example results in a Maximum Offset value of 48 pixels, well above the 24 pixel default.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about fingerprints.

method.name: SetMinimumMatchingTolerance
method.qi: Uses the decimal value you supply as a parameter to set a minimum Matching Tolerance Rating.

p.name: Minimum
p.qi: The minimum matching tolerance level.

method.ap:
Minimum:
A decimal value from 0.00 (Lowest Tolerance) to 0.99 (Highest Tolerance).
The decimal separator must be appropriate for the locale. Smart parameters are supported.
method.lvl: All, but generally at the Page level.
method.h:
This action sets the minimum confidence matching tolerance rating to determine if a fingerprint is a match.
If none of the existing fingerprints match with the specified tolerance or greater, then it is
considered that none of the existing fingerprints correctly match the
fingerprint for the current page.
A non-matching fingerprint is not necessarily an error. For some applications, all of the expected types
of pages are known. Maybe there are 10 known page types or perhaps there are 10,000 known page types, but they
are all known when the application goes into production so it is expected that the FindFingerprint action
should match one of the predetermined fingerprints. If it does not match, then the page may have been
ingested as an error, or perhaps needs other handling to be correctly processed.
For other applications, such as APT, they may be deployed with a set of known fingerprints, but can also
learn new fingerprints as the application is used. For example, a new vendor starts sending a new kind
of document. Fingerprint matching would also fail in that case, however, for APT, it would cause
alternate processing which will define the fingerprint at runtime during the course of processing the
new document. Once the document has been fully processed, a new fingerprint will be generated, allowing
a successful fingerprint match the next time that new page format is ingested.
A lower tolerance rating will allow greater chance for a match of a fingerprint, but also a greater chance for a
False
match.
It is recommended to adjust the tolerance against the set of fingerprints for an application to allow for poor quality documents
to successfully match the fingerprint, but not so low that fingerprints match incorrectly.
Once set, this setting will be in effect for the length of the current task profile.
If fingerprint actions are used again in a later task profile, then this action must be called again
to configure the setting before using subsequent fingerprint actions.
AnalyzeImage()
RotateImage()
RecognizePageOCR_S()
SetSearchArea("0.0","0.5")
SetMinimumMatchingTolerance("0.70")
FindFingerprint("True","")
In this sequence, the fingerprint is created for the current page to create the CCO and the recognition results are also
placed into the CCO. The search area is configured to the top 50% of the page and the matching tolerance is set to ".7".
The FindFingerprint action then attempts to match the fingerprint for the current page to the existing set
of fingerprints. If a fingerprint does not match the minimum tolerance, then the fingerprint for the
new page is added to the set of existing fingerprints.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about fingerprints.

method.name: SetPageFingerprintID
method.qi: Assigns a value to the FingerprintID property of the selected Page object of the Document Hierarchy.

p.name: FingerprintID
p.qi: The fingerprint ID to associate with the page.

method.ap:
FingerprintID:
The fingerprint ID, sometimes called the template ID, to assign to this page.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Assigns a value to the FingerprintID property of the selected Page object of the Document Hierarchy.
This links a specific fingerprint template ID with the page. The fingerprint template identifies the
zone locations for each field within the page, associating an area of the image to
the location of the text represented by the field.
Typically fingerprint templates are automatically assigned with the action FindFingerprint which will
automatically identify the fingerprint template that matches the document. However,
there are times when alternate techniques can be used to match a page to a specific fingerprint
template. This action assigns a specific fingerprint template ID to the page.
A common use for this action is to first determine what it is about that page that
determines which fingerprint should be associated with the page. One typical mechanism is
determining the fingerprint by some unique text on the page. Other methods are possible
such as the name of the source file or other attributes that can be detected about the page.
Once the use case is understood, then rules can be written to determine which fingerprint
template ID should be assigned. Once determined by the rules, then this action can be
used to assign a specific fingerprint template ID to the page. Once assigned, then
the zones can be loaded to assign the position locations to the page's fields.
The
SetPageFingerprintID
action
will create a fingerprint ID property/variable "TemplateID" of the
current Page object if it does not already exist.
This action is functionally equivalent to the following generic action:
rrSet("1010","@X.TemplateID")
However, using SetPageFingerprintID can add additional context to the intention
of setting the fingerprint.
RecognizePageOCR_A()
WordFind("MQSW")
SetPageFingerprintID("1010")
In this sequence, the page is recognized then the recognized text
is searched to see if it contains "MQSQ", which is an example of some
kind of unique text that identifies the page.
If the WordFind action locates "MQSW" on the current page,
the SetPageFingerprintID action assigns "1010" as the page's
Fingerprint ID. This links the page to a fingerprint with a Fingerprint ID of "1010"
as was setup in the Zones tab of Datacap Studio.
method.see:
FindFingerprint, ReadZones, ReadZonesFPX
Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about fingerprints.

method.name: UpdateFingerprintStatistics
method.qi: Updates the Fingerprint hit statistics.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Fingerprint information is stored in the Fingerprint Database. One piece of information is a count
of the number of times a fingerprint is matched. This information can be useful for in
some instances. Use this action to increment the count for the current page and update the fingerprint statistics
in the fingerprint database.
FindFingerprint("False","")
UpdateFingerprintStatistics()
This example calls UpdateFingerprintStatistics after matching the fingerprint to increment the count for the
number of times the specific fingerprint associated with the current page is matched.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about fingerprints.

method.name: XMLReadZones
method.qi: Loads position information for current fingerprint.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action reads the field zone information from the fingerprint XML file associated with the fingerprint for
the current page object and sets the zone coordinates for the fields from the zoned fingerprint.
This action is similar to the ReadZones action in the ZonesAndLineItems library.
The primary difference is that ReadZones reads the zone information stored in the setup DCO from legacy
fingerprints and XMLReadZones
reads the zone information from the associated fingerprint XML file.
Typically this action will be called after the CreateFields action but before field recognition.
XMLReadZones loads position information for each field in the calling object and it's children. If available, it adjusts
these values based on offset information stored in the 'Image_Offset' variable at any node level.
The offset value is applied to all child objects of a node where an 'Image_Offset' variable is found;
unless overwritten by a child node also having an Image_Offset value to apply.
Position information is based on the Fingerprint XML position for the parent page's fingerprint ID.
If 'Enable FPXML' setting is checked in the application settings 'Main' tab within the Taskmaster Application Manager,
when zoning fingerprints Datacap Studio will place field zone information into a fingerprint XML file instead of placing the zone
information into the applications setup DCO. One XML file is created per fingerprint.
Depending on application needs, using fingerprint XML files may have
advantages over legacy fingerprints.
If the application is using fingerprint XML files, then use this action to load the zones instead of the ReadZones action.
SetFingerprintDirectory("@APPPATH(*/fingerprint)")
XMLReadZones()
method.ret:
False,
if the fingerprint xml cannot be loaded or if SetFingerprintDirectory has not
been called to set the location of the fingerprint XML files. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: The top-level help of this action library contains an explanation of XML fingerprints.

method.name: XMLSetDetailsAndLineitemPair
method.qi: Sets the type of the special Details and Lineitem fields.

p.name: DetailFieldType
p.qi: The type for the current page's detail field, if one exists.

p.name: LineitemFieldType
p.qi: The type for the current page's line item field, if one exists.

method.ap:
Two comma separated parameters:
Detail field type:
type of the field that is the parent to the line item field, often called "Details".
LineItem field type:
type of the line item field which is the parent of the fields to be captured, often called "Lineitem".
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Use this action if your page contains "Details" and "Lineitems" fields.
The action sets the type of the special Details and Lineitem fields. These fields, unlike other field types,
are handled by the XMLReadZones and XMLWriteZones actions in a special way that is compatible
with the Locate actions framework.
If your page has Details and Lineitems, then this action is required to identify the types
so the position information will be properly saved.
Using SetDetailsAndLineitemPairFPX prior to calling XMLWriteZones will cause XMLWriteZones to save line
item field positions to the fingerprint file. The second parameter is the type of the line item
field which is the parent of the fields to be captured and is often called "Lineitem".
If your page contains Detail and Lineitem fields, this action also needs to be used prior
to calling XMLReadZones.
Details are the parent object of the line item fields. Details are a collection of lineitems
and each line item has a collection of fields. For example, in a typical invoice
application a single lineitem can contain the fields: quantity, item number, description, unit price, and total.
This setting will stay in effect until the current task profile completes.
XMLSetDetailsAndLineitemPair("Details","Lineitem")
XMLReadZones()
In this example, the details field is called "Details" and the line items are called "Lineitem".
An example DCO hierarchy may look something like this:
- Details
--- Lineitem
------- Qty
------- ItemID
------- ItemDesc
------- Price
------- LineTotal
method.see: The top-level help of this action library contains an explanation of XML fingerprints.

method.name: XMLWriteZones
method.qi: Writes position information for all fields of the page.

p.name: FingerprintHostName
p.qi: Target fingerprint class name.

p.name: FingerprintHostID
p.qi: Target fingerprint host ID.

p.name: FingerprintPageType
p.qi: Target fingerprint page type.

method.ap:
Fingerprint host name:
This is the fingerprint class name and can be seen in the zones tab of Datacap Studio.
It is used to group or classify fingerprints.
If this value is not provided, then a blank class name will be used.
Fingerprint host id:
This is an internal numeric value that is associated with the fingerprint class name.
If a value is not provided, a blank value will be used.
Fingerprint page type:
This is the page type that corresponds to the fingerprint for the page.
If this value is not provided, it uses the page type of the current page.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters. All parameters are optional.
method.h:
This action will write out all of the field positions for the current page to the fingerprint XML file.
Typically this action is used for applications that are using fingerprint XML files and new pages
are dynamically zoned at runtime. After the zoning of the page has been completed, then this action
is used to write out the zone information to the FPXML file, allowing subsequent pages of this
type to be processed using the saved zone information. If pages are not being zoned by a verify operator
at runtime, then it is not necessary to use this action.
If the fingerprint directory that had been previously specified using SetFingerprintDirectory does not exist, it will be created,
providing that the parent directory already exists.
Fields with empty positions are not written to the fingerprint XML file.
SetFingerprintDirectory("@APPPATH(*/fingerprint)")
XMLWriteZones("MyFPClass,,MyPageType")
This example writes out the zones for the current page and sets the fingerprint class to "MyFPClass" and
the page type to "MyPageType".
SetFingerprintDirectory("@APPPATH(*/fingerprint)")
XMLWriteZones("MyFPClass,,@P.MyType")
This example writes out the zones for the current page and sets the fingerprint class to "MyFPClass" and
the page type to the value contained by the page variable "MyType".
method.ret:
False,
if there is a problem saving to fingerprint XML file or if not called at the page level,
if the page does not have a fingerprint assigned, or a fingerprint directory has not been set. Otherwise
True.
method.see: The top-level help of this action library contains an explanation of XML fingerprints.

com.qi: : Reads barcodes from a page or field.
com.h:
The Barcode action library performs recognition of barcodes on pages or in a field. The page can
contain a single barcode or multiple barcodes. The value of a barcode is stored and can
be used by subsequent actions. The value of a barcode can of course be stored with
a page as part of it's data. Barcodes can also be used for controlling the logic
flow of Datacap rules, as an separator page indicator or a mechanism to assign
a page type.
The page must be a single page TIF, PNG, BMP or JPEG image. Other types of images or documents
are not supported. Document types such as PDF, DOC, multi-page TIF, etc., can be converted
to a TIF image using the Convert action library. It is recommended that the best
practices guide is reviewed to understand what kind of images work well for recognition.
Action Summary
GetAllBarcodes : Reads all of the barcodes on the page and returns them in a delimited string.
GetBarcode : Reads the first barcode on a page.
GetDataMatrixBarcode : Reads the first Data Matrix barcode on a page.
GetPDF2DBarcode : Reads a the first PDF-417 barcode on a page.
IdentifyPageByBarcode : Sets page types based on a barcode value.
MatchAnyBarcode : Compares an expected value with all of the barcodes on the page.
MatchBarcodePrefix : Compares an expected prefix value with all of the barcodes on the page.
MatchFirstBarcode : Compares the first barcode read on the page with a value.
SetBarcodeMinimumConfidence : Sets the minimum tolerance required to except a barcode read as accurate.
Setting The Expected Barcode Type
By default, the barcode engine will consider the barcode type to be unknown. Unknown will automatically
attempt to detect 1D barcodes. The following barcode types must be specifically set to be
detected: PatchCodeBarcode, PostNetBarcode, GS1 DataBar, IntelligentMail, Royal Post Mail 4-State,
Australian Post 4-State, QR Code, PDF417Barcode, Aztec and DataMatrixBarcode.
It may still be necessary to set the expected barcode type for the engine to find and recognize the barcode.
If a barcode is not being detected, set the proper barcode type to aid the barcode detection.
Multiple barcode types can be set. It is recommended that the expected barcode types are specifically
configured.
The expected barcode types can be easily set using the "BAR/P" tab property within the "Zones" tab of Datacap Studio.
This property can be set by selecting the target DCO node page or field that will have an associated
rule that calls barcode recognition, locking the DCO and selecting
the expected barcode types. This will automatically calculate the correct value based on all of the selected types
and set the bp_tp variable for your application in the Setup DCO. For best results, keep the expected types to a minimum.
When you use this property approach to setting the expected barcode type, it is not
necessary to separately set the bp_tp variable manually within the setup DCO or at runtime using actions.
Alternatively, the expected barcode type can be set at runtime on the target field/page being recognized
by setting the variable
bp_tp
. If the "bp_tp" variable is empty or does not exist,
the engine defaults to "Unknown".
The bp_tp variable sets the expected barcode type, or types, which will provide better recognition results.
If multiple barcode types are expected, the value of this variable must be a combination of the barcode types shown below.
Multiple types can be read by adding the values of their codes together. Always set the expected type to the minimum
possible types. This variable can be set using rrSet prior to calling a barcode recognition action.
For example: rrSet("256","@X.bp_tp") for reading a Code 39 barcode.
Valid barcode types:
0 : Unknown. Detects most 1D barcode types automatically.
1 : INDUSTRY 2 OF 5
2 : INTERLEAVED 2 OF 5
4 : IATA 2 OF 5
8 : DATALOGIC 2 OF 5
16 : INVERT 2 OF 5
32 : BCD MATRIX
64 : MATRIX 2 OF 5
128 : CODE 32
256 : CODE 39
512 : CODABAR 2
1024 : CODE 93
2048 : CODE 128
4096 : EAN-13
8192 : EAN-8
16384 : UPC-A
32768 : UPC-E
65536 : ADD 5
131072 : ADD 2
262144 : UCC128/EAN-128
524288 : Patch Code
1048576 : PostNet
2097152 : PDF417
4194304 : DataMatrix
8388608 : Code 39 Extended
16777216 : Code 93 Extended
33554432 : QRCode
67108864 : IntelligentMail
134217728 : Royal Mail (RM4SCC)
268435456 : Australian Post 4-State Code
536870912 : Aztec
1073741824: GS1DataBar
Variable Length Royal Mail Barcodes
The Royal Mail barcode is a fixed length barcode. Some countries use a variable a variable length
variation of the Royal Mail barcode, such as the Postal Services of Portugal. To allow reading of a variable
length Royal Mail barcode for Portuguese CTT, in addition to selecting the Royal Mail barcode type, the variable
length setting must be enabled. Setting the DCO variable "RoyalMailVariableLength" to "1" will allow detection
of variable length Royal Mail barcodes.
It is allowed to enable variable length for fixed length Royal Mail barcodes, if the length
restriction does not need to be enforced.
This example sets the barcode type to variable length Royal Mail:
rrSet("1", "@P.RoyalMailVariableLength")
rrSet("134217728", "@P.bp_tp")
GetBarcode()
Minimum and Maximum Expected Barcodes Settings
Multiple barcodes can exist and be recognized on a single page. The DCO variable
bp_su
controls the maximum number
of barcodes that will attempt to be read on a single page. If not specified, the default maximum is 10.
The minimum number of expected barcodes can be specified using the DCO variable
bp_minExpected.
This setting will control when image enhancement takes place. Unless specified, the minimum expected barcodes will
default to the same value as the maximum number of barcodes setting.
The engine uses these variables to determine how many barcodes are expected on the page
and will cause the engine to stop looking once the threshold has been met. If the expected
number of barcodes is not met, the engine can perform internal image adjustments to the image
and read it again looking for the expected number of barcodes. If your pages will only have
one expected barcode, then set the minimum and maximum expected barcode
variables to 1 for best results.
Barcode Detection Steps
The barcode actions will detect using the following steps.
- Recognize barcodes on the page / field.
- Stop if minimum expected is detected.
- If minimum not reached and image enhancement is enabled then
- - Use each of the enabled image enhancement features and read the barcode.
- - Stop if minimum expected is detected.
- - Continue performing each enabled image enhancement feature to detect the minimum expected barcodes.
If the number of recognized barcodes
is equal to or more than the specified minimum, image enhancement will be skipped.
If the minimum number of barcodes has not been reached, and if image enhancement is enabled,
then barcode recognition will be performed a second time using the configured type of
image enhancement in an attempt to read the barcode.
For example, if the configured minimum barcodes is 1 and the maximum is 10, first barcode
recognition will be performed without any image enhancement and attempt to read up to 10
barcodes. If at least 1 barcode is read,
the action will complete. If 0 barcodes are read, the action will perform the specified image
enhancement and attempt once more to recognize the barcodes on the page.
If 0 barcodes are read and no image enhancement is configured, the action will complete
without a second attempt at recognition.
Another example is if two barcodes are expected with the minimum set to 2. If 2 or more barcodes
are read, then recognition will stop. If less than two are read and if image enhancement
is enabled, the barcode action will perform the configured image enhancement type and
attempt to read the barcode again. It will do this for each type of enabled image enhancement.
Image Enhancements
Barcodes are more tolerant to image deterioration than traditional recognition.
Damaged barcodes can often still be recognized. The fault tolerance can vary
based on the specific barcode type, as a whole, they are more resilient
than traditional character recognition.
Barcodes are also generally more tolerant to skew and rotation problems.
It is still possible that barcodes can have problems being read if the image
is of poor quality. For example, if it has been poorly scanned, copied several
times, or has other visible issues, a barcode may still not be read correctly.
The barcode action library has built in image enhancement mechanisms
to internally adjust the image when the barcode cannot be read.
Image enhancement may be necessary in order to help read damaged or poorly scanned barcodes.
Depending on the problem with the barcode, different types of enhancements may make the barcode readable.
The barcode actions offer a way to enhance the image while reading the barcode. To enable this
feature, set the variable
bp_enhance
to "1". When set to "1", the engine will
first try to recognize the barcode without image enhancement.
If the minimum number of barcodes has
not been read, then the action will try again using the specified image enhancement.
If the minimum number of barcodes has been read, then the image enhancement will be skipped.
If your barcode images are such that they will always require image enhancement, set
bp_enhance
to "2", which will skip the first recognition step that attempts to recognize without image enhancement.
Enabling image enhancement for barcodes will only alter the image
during barcode recognition, the original image in the batch will be left unchanged.
The image enhancements are not cumulative, enable only one type of image enhancement that is needed.
If sometimes one image enhancement helps, for example binarize,
and other times a different image enhancement helps, such as smooth zoom,
then both can be enabled, however, the minimum and maximum also need to be set. The engine will
try each image enhancement that is enabled until the minimum number of expected
barcodes is read. It is not possible to control the order in which the engine tries
multiple enhancements. For best performance, enable the minimum number of enhancements
that help your images.
Image Enhancement Types
Smooth Zoom:
bp_zoom
- Scales the image larger to help improve recognition for small barcodes.
Blur:
bp_blur
- Blurs the image which can help jagged lines.
Dilate:
bp_dilate
- Expands pixels making lines thicker.
Erode:
bp_erode
- Removes pixels along line edges.
Flip:
bp_flip
- It is usually not necessary to flip the image for an upside-down barcode to recognize.
Resize:
bp_resize
- Enlarges the image which could help small barcodes, similar to zoom.
Binarize:
bp_binarize
- Converts 24 and 8 bit images to 1 bit. A 1 bit image can
improve recognition for barcodes where the contrast between the barcode lines and the background is low or when
there is light shading preventing recognition.
These enhancements are temporary and will not change the image within the batch.
Enabling Image Enhancement
To activate automatic image enhancement, set the DCO variable
bp_enhance
to "1" prior to calling a barcode action
on the DCO page or field node that will be recognized.
For example: rrSet("1","@X.bp_enhance")
Each specific image enhancement can be enabled by setting the associated DCO variable to "1" or disabled by setting it to "0".
By default, "Smooth Zoom" is always enabled and all other image enhancements are disabled.
For example, if "Smooth Zoom" is the desired enhancement, simply enabling image enhancement by setting bp_enhance to "1" will
enable image enhancement for Smooth Zoom.
If only Binarize is required, then using this sequence prior to calling a barcode action will enable only the Binarize feature.
rrSet("1","@X.bp_enhance")
rrSet("0","@X.bp_zoom")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_binarize")
The above example, and other examples in this library, show how to set DCO variables using
rrSet. This action will set variables at runtime. Alternatively these variables can be set
in the Setup DCO from within Datacap Studio. Setting the variables within the Setup DCO
can be more efficient. For example, assume that the above three rrSet actions are called
on page type "Other". Assuming the batch ingests 100 pages, then these three actions will
be called on every page, resulting in 300 calls to the rrSet action. Alternatively,
these three variables can be created and set in the DCO from within Datacap Studio
on the "Other" DCO object. When set in the Setup DCO, the variables will
automatically exist on every "Other" object and rrSet will not need to be called
within the rules to create these variables on every object within the batch.
Enabling Multiple Enhancements
Multiple enhancements can be enabled if you find that you consistently receive documents that require different types
of enhancements. For example, some documents always work the first time, other documents only detect if binarize is used
and others work only if blur is used. If multiple enhancements are enabled, the action will attempt to recognize using
each of the enabled enhancement types until the minimum expected have been read.
For example, to always use Binarize and Blur to recognize the barcode, set the following prior to recognizing the barcode:
rrSet("1","@X.bp_enhance")
rrSet("0","@X.bp_zoom")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_binarize")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_blur")
The action will then use the blur and binarize enhancements until the minimum number is read. If bp_enhance is set to "1"
the action will always first try to recognize without any enhancements and only if the minimum is not reached, will it continue.
Each additional enhancement type enabled will be attempted until the minimum are read or all enabled enhancements have been attempted.
For best performance, always set the minimum number of barcodes
expected or the action may perform unnecessary enhancements.
The order in which the enhancements are attempted by
the barcode action cannot be controlled.
Barcode Orientation
Barcode orientation defaults to both horizontal and vertical.
Specifying the orientation may help in detection of barcodes. For example, if the barcodes
will always be horizontal, then detection and recognition can be improved by setting the orientation
to Horizontal only.
If necessary, the orientation can be configured by setting the DCO variable
bp_or.
0 = Horizontal and Vertical.
1 = Horizontal.
2 = Vertical.
3 = Horizontal, Vertical and Diagonal.
Again, the bp_or variable can be set on the object within the SetupDCO or can be set
at runtime using the rrSet action.
Note:
Diagonal barcodes can be detected along with Vertical barcodes i.e by setting bp_or=0 or bp_or=2 or bp_or=3.
Barcode Byte Mode:
Some specific barcode types, such as PDF-417, allow null characters within the data stream.
If this occurs, the full length of the barcode can be truncated returning only the characters up to the first null character.
This is typically observable by noting that the read barcode data
is shorter than expected. For example, if the
barcode should be a 40 character ID but it returns truncated text.
To treat a barcode as byte data, set the DCO variable
BarcodeUseByte
to "1".
This setting will treat the stream as bytes and also convert any null characters to spaces so the entire string can then be
utilized in other parts of the application. By default, this parameter is off.
When in byte mode, the default replacement character of a space can be set to a different replacement character
by setting the DCO variable
BarcodeReplacementChar
to the desired replacement character.
For example, rrSet("-","@X.BarcodeReplacementChar") sets the variable "BarcodeReplacementChar"
on the current DCO object to "-" which will change the replacement
character from a space to a dash when byte mode is enabled.
NOTE:
Unicode characters are not supported when using byte mode.
Patch Codes
Patch codes can be recognized in addition to barcodes. Patch codes
are very similar to barcodes but can be less reliable. If all pages
are checked for patch codes it is possible for lines on a page
that resemble patch codes can be mistaken for patch codes. While this
is somewhat rare, but can happen. If you have a choice between creating
separator sheets that use patch codes or barcodes, a barcode is the
reliable option.
When the barcode type is set to
Patch Code
, the following string
values may be returned by the engine (the string value depends on the type of Patch Code
that is found):
Patch 1:
1100
Patch 2:
1001
Patch 3:
1010
Patch 4 / Toggle Patch:
0110
Patch 6:
0011
Patch T / Transfer patch:
0101
When recognizing PatchCodes, the barcode type must be set explicitly to PatchCode.
The default barcode type setting of "Unknown" will not detect PatchCodes.
Barcode Results Stored In DCO Variables
The results of barcode recognition will be stored in field data, in DCO variables
or both. When barcode recognition is performed on a field, the results of the
barcode read are stored in the field's text value. When recognized on a page,
results can be stored in variables such as GetBarCodeList and GetBarCode.
Storing and retrieving data from DCO variables is a common task for actions
and Datacap applications. Refer to the action help for names of variables
that are created from barcode recognition.
The top-level help topic of the ApplicationObjects action library discusses the Datacap Object Hierarchy (DCO)
including the different object levels and object variables. It is recommended that the DCO is well
understood when writing a Datacap application.
Using Barcode Recognition Results
When the barcode is read, the following variables are created on the current DCO object:
GetBarCode : The recognized value of the barcode.
CodeName : The barcode type.
Confidence : The barcode confidence.
Height : The height of the barcode in pixels.
Width : The width of the barcode in pixels.
Left : The left coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Top : The top coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Position : Four separated values which are the coordinates of the
barcode in pixels: left, top, right, bottom.
The data is provided for an application to use as needed. The variables can be read by other actions, including custom actions.
How this data is used is dependent on the use case. For many applications, barcodes will be read within a field, and the
recognized value will be used by accessing the field's value. Similarly, a barcode could be read that the page level, and again the
recognized value can be accessed by accessing the "GetBarCode" variable.
This example shows a simple example of setting page types based on the barcode value.
OtherRule
- Function1
- - rrCompare("Inv","@X.GetBarCode")
- - SetPageType("Invoice")
- Function2
- - rrCompare("1234","@X.GetBarCode")
- - SetPageType("Claim")
- Function3:Default
- - SetPageType("Trailing_Page")
The example first tests the barcode value to see if it is "Inv", if so, then it sets the
type of the current page to "Invoice". If the barcode is "1234", then it sets the page type
to "Claim". If it is not any of those, or if the barcode does not exist, then the page is set
to "Trailing_Page". This kind of example would require the barcode to exist on the page
being assigned the page type. If barcodes are used on separator pages, then the barcode
would indicate the grouping of the documents and the rules logic would be different.
To illustrate how other data can be used, there could be a use case to only recognize barcodes
that appear at the bottom of the page and ignore any barcodes at the top of the page. This use
case could be solved in a few ways. One solution would be to create a generic field that
spans the entire lower half of the page. This field could exist for a single page type, and
each page could be set to that page type, the fingerprint template ID set,
and then the field zones loaded. Once the field is ready, barcode recognition can be run on the
field object. If the barcode exists in the lower half of the page, it would be recognized.
If the barcode does not exist on the page, or if it exits only at the top of the page, then the
barcode would not be recognized.
An alternate way of satisfying the same use case could be done by calling GetBarcode
on the entire page. The results of the barcode can then be examined to determine if the barcode
is in the bottom half of the page or the top half of the page by using rules to
determine if the barcode coordinates are within a particular range. Here is an example ruleset.
rrSet("No","@X.BarcodeIsAtTheBottom")
GetBarcode()
SplitTextIntoVariables("@X.Position0", "BarcodeSplitPos",",")
rrCompareNumeric("@X.BarcodeSplitPos_1",>,"1600")
rrSet("Yes", "@X.BarcodeIsAtTheBottom")
This ruleset first sets a variable called "BarcodeIsAtTheBottom" and sets the value to "No". The barcode is
then read. The position variable contains the barcode coordinates in a "left,top,right,bottom" format. SplitTextIntoVariables
will take this comma separated list and break it into unique variables. The second variable BarcodeSplitPos_1, which is the top,
is checked to see if the value is greater than 1600 pages, which is about half way down a 300 dpi 8.5"x11" page. If the value
is greater than that, then the variable "BarcodeIsAtTheBottom" is changed to "Yes". Now any following rule can check
the value of this variable to see if there is a barcode at the bottom of the page.
The example shows an alternate way of solving the use case and illustrates some alternative ways
the barcode data could be used within an application.
The action SplitTextIntoVariables is in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
For example, "@X" is notation for accessing the current object. "@P" accesses the page object, which
could be the current object, or a parent object. Being evaluated at runtime, allows recognized data
or other batch specific data to be passed to actions or stored as metadata. A smart parameter such
as @DATE could be used to name export files based on the current date. Similar smart parameters
will retrieve the current batch ID, current batch directory, current operator ID, and more.
Smart parameters are a very powerful mechanism of getting data from other areas of the application and copying
it into a new location or passing it as a parameter to an action. It is recommended that the smart parameter
documentation is reviewed to understand the full capabilities available. The top-level help of the
ValidationAndTextAdjustments action library also has information about smart parameters. Some characters such
as +, \ and . also have special smart parameter meaning and may be interpreted as a smart parameter. This
can be controlled using smart parameter syntax.

method.name: GetAllBarcodes
method.qi: : Searches all the barcodes on the current page and writes them to the calling object's GetBarCodeList variable.
method.ap:
The separator to use when storing multiple barcodes. If not provided, the default separator is a comma.
If barcodes might contain a comma within the data, then the separator should be changed to a unique character.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Recognizes all of the barcodes on the current page, provided they meet the type that has
been previously configured.
All of the recognized barcodes will be stored in the current DCO object in a variable named "GetBarCodeList".
Each barcode value is separated using the string separator value entered as a parameter.
If the engine does not detect any barcodes, then the variable GetBarCodeList is not populated nor created.
The variable "NumBarcodes" will be created in the current DCO object containing the number of
barcodes that have been recognized.
For each barcode recognized, a unique set of DCO variables will be created using the following
naming convention. X is the index of the barcode starting at 0. For example, if 4 barcodes have been recognized
then GetBarCode0, GetBarCode1, GetBarCode2 and GetBarCode3 will be created along with all of the other variables
using the same naming technique.
GetBarCodeX : The recognized value of the barcode.
CodeNameX : The barcode type.
ConfidenceX : The barcode confidence.
HeightX : The hight of the barcode in pixels.
WidthX : The width of the barcode in pixels.
LeftX : The left coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
TopX : The top coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
PositionX : Four separated values which are the coordinates of the
barcode in pixels: left, top, right, bottom.
rrSet("33554432","@Xbp_tp")
GetAllBarcodes(",")
This example configures the engine to detect QR codes and then detects all of the
QA codes on the page. For each barcode detected, the results will be stored
in the variables specified and the variable GetBarcodeList will
contain a CSV list of all recognized barcode values. Instead of calling
rrSet, the expected barcode types can be selected in the Bar/P properties
tab within the Zones tab of Datacap Studio.
rrSet("3", "@X.bp_minExpected")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_enhance")
rrSet("0","@X.bp_zoom")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_binarize")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_blur")
GetBarcode()
This example assumes the barcode type has previously been configured in Datacap Studio
in the Bar/P tab of the Zones tab to configure the bp_tp on all objects of the current type.
It also enables the binarize image enhancement to run. The minimum
number of barcodes expected is 3. If 3 or more barcodes are read, then the barcode
action will stop successfully. If 2 or less barcodes are read, the action will
enable the "binarize" image enhancement and try to read the barcode again.
If still only 2 or less barcodes are read, the engine will try blurring the image
and reading the barcodes again.
The image enhancements are only in effect for the length of the action and does
not change the source image within the batch. The image enhancements
are not cumulative and the order they are used cannot be controlled.
method.ret:
True
if the action is called at the page level or field level. Otherwise,
False.
In addition the calling object's value and variable "GetBarCode" will be filled with the bar code value. This action also
stores barcode information such as confidence, coordinates, code name, and size. If the object's barcode settings are set to read more than
one barcode, and more than one barcode is found, barcodes are also stored in the variable "GetBarCodeX" where "X" is the index of
the barcode found.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: GetBarcode
method.qi: : Recognizes arbitrary 1D or 2D codes.
method.ap: None.
method.ret:
True
if the action is called at the page level or field level. Otherwise,
False.
In addition the calling object's value and variable "GetBarCode" will be filled with the bar code value. This action also
stores barcode information such as confidence, coordinates, code name, and size. If the object's barcode settings are set to read more than
one barcode, and more than one barcode is found, barcodes are also stored in the variable "GetBarCodeX" where "X" is the index of
the barcode found.
method.h:
Use this action to read the first barcode found on a page if the page has 1D or 2D barcodes.
If recognizing on a field
object, the field must have a Position assigned that corresponds to the area on the image containing the barcode
when bar code reading is performed.
For example, to load zone coordinates after a fingerprint has been assigned to the page,
the application would invoke the CreateFields action, which creates the fields in the DCO.
Then the application would call the ReadZones action to load the position coordinates from the fingerprint template associated with the page.
When this is complete, the field is ready for field level barcode reading and the GetBarcode action can be called on the fields
where a barcode is expected.
If anchors or fingerprint matching are used,
ReadZones or other registration may be required to align the fields correctly to the fingerprint template zones.
When the barcode is read, the following variables are created on the current DCO object:
GetBarCode : The recognized value of the barcode.
CodeName : The barcode type.
Confidence : The barcode confidence.
Height : The height of the barcode in pixels.
Width : The width of the barcode in pixels.
Left : The left coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Top : The top coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Position : Four separated values which are the coordinates of the
barcode in pixels: left, top, right, bottom.
If called on a field object, the barcode value will also be stored in
the field's text property.
rrSet("1", "@X.bp_minExpected")
rrSet("2048", "@X.bp_tp")
GetBarcode()
This example configures the reader to expect 1 Code-128 barcode on the page and
sets the barcode type in rules prior to calling the barcode action.
rrSet("1", "@X.bp_minExpected")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_enhance")
rrSet("0","@X.bp_zoom")
rrSet("1","@X.bp_binarize")
GetBarcode()
This example assumes the barcode type has previously been configured in Datacap Studio
in the Bar/P tab of the Zones tab to configure the bp_tp on all objects of the current type.
It also enables the binarize image enhancement to run. The minimum
number of barcodes expected is 1. If 1 barcode is read, then the barcode
action will stop successfully. If 0 barcodes are read, the action will
enable the "binarize" image enhancement and try to read the barcode again.
This image enhancement is only in effect for the length of the action and does
not change the source image within the batch.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: GetDataMatrixBarcode
method.qi: : Recognizes Data Matrix codes
method.ap: None.
method.ret:
True
if the action is called at the page level or field level. Otherwise,
False.
In addition the calling object's value and variable "GetBarCode" will be filled with the bar code value. This action also
stores barcode information such as confidence, coordinates, code name, and size. If the object's barcode settings are set to read more than
one barcode, and more than one barcode is found, barcodes are also stored in the variable "GetBarCodeX" where "X" is the index of
the barcode found.
method.h:
Use this action if your page or field has Data Matrix codes.
This action is very similar to the GetBarcode action.
The difference is that the barcode type for Data Matrix barcodes will be set automatically.
It is not necessary to set the barcode type. If the barcode type is set, it will be ignored.
When the barcode is read, the following variables are created on the current DCO object:
GetBarCode : The recognized value of the barcode.
CodeName : The barcode type.
Confidence : The barcode confidence.
Height : The height of the barcode in pixels.
Width : The width of the barcode in pixels.
Left : The left coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Top : The top coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Position : Four separated values which are the coordinates of the
barcode in pixels: left, top, right, bottom.
If called on a field object, the barcode value will also be stored in
the field's text property.
GetDataMatrixBarcode()
This action automatically configures the engine to read Data Matrix barcodes
and will return the save the first occurance in the GetBarCode variable
when called at the page level. When called at the field level, the value will
also be stored in the field text.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: GetPDF2DBarcode
method.qi: : Recognizes PDF-417 codes.
method.ap: None.
method.ret:
True
if the action is called at the page level or field level. Otherwise,
False.
In addition the calling object's value and variable "GetBarCode" will be filled with the bar code value. This action also
stores barcode information such as confidence, coordinates, code name, and size. If the object's barcode settings are set to read more than
one barcode, and more than one barcode is found, barcodes are also stored in the variable "GetBarCodeX" where "X" is the index of
the barcode found.
method.h:
Use this action if your page has PDF-417 codes.
This action is very similar to the GetBarcode action.
The difference is that the barcode type for PDF-417 barcodes will be set automatically.
It is not necessary to set the barcode type. If the barcode type is set, it will be ignored.
When the barcode is read, the following variables are created on the current DCO object:
GetBarCode : The recognized value of the barcode.
CodeName : The barcode type.
Confidence : The barcode confidence.
Height : The height of the barcode in pixels.
Width : The width of the barcode in pixels.
Left : The left coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Top : The top coordinate of the barcode in pixels.
Position : Four separated values which are the coordinates of the
barcode in pixels: left, top, right, bottom.
If called on a field object, the barcode value will also be stored in
the field's text property.
If the barcode data contains nulls, it is possible to enable byte mode.
Refer to the top-level help for this action library for more information.
GetPDF2DBarcode()
This example reads a PDF-417 barcode on the page.
rrSet("1","@X.BarcodeUseByte")
rrSet("~","@X.BarcodeReplacementChar")
GetPDF2DBarcode()
This example reads a PDF-417 barcode in byte mode and changes the default null replacement character with a tilde.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: IdentifyOtherPagesByBarcode
method.qi: : Updates the current page type if a barcode match is found.
method.ap:
BarcodePageMappings:
A delimited list of barcode value-page type mappings that are
evaluated to determine whether matching barcodes exist on the current page.
LastPageMappings:
A delimited list of page types value-page type mappings that are
evaluated to determine the page type to assign pages without a barcode match.
MappingsDelimiter:
(Optional) Delimiter separating mappings. A single character used to separate
multiple barcode and multiple last page mapping groups. Default: comma (,).
KeyValueSeparator:
(Optional) Delimiter used to separate the barcode mappings and last page mappings in an a key value pair.
Default: equals sign (=).
CaseSensitive:
(Optional) True, enforces case sensitivity when evaluating the list of barcodes found on the page. Default: False.
DefaultPageType:
The page type to assign when no matches are found.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action processes all pages with a type of "Other", looking for barcodes that match the
input page type, indicating the start of a document. If a barcode value is found,
this action updates the type of the current page by using the corresponding input mapping.
This action would be used to identify pages when separator sheets, containing a barcode value,
are used between each document. These separator sheets are added during the scan process to
signal the start of each document.
For example, if a batch contains a document consists of two a single pages, then
the scan sequence would be: separator page, document page, separator page, document page.
If the input sequence consists of a 3 page, a 1 page document, and a 2 page document,
then the scan sequence would be: separator page, page, page, page, separator page, page,
separator page, page, page.
The action does not require a document separator in the batch when each document is a single
page, until a multipage document is encountered. This allows all single page documents to be
placed first in the scan job without a separator and the multi-page document at the end,
separated with a barcode separator sheet.
For example, if a scan job consists of 3 single page documents and then two - 2 page documents,
the scan job only needs two separator sheets to be added like this:
page, page, page, separator, page, page, separator, page, page. This sequence would create
a batch of 5 documents.
Mapping Specification
The input for parameter BarcodePageMappings must take the following
form:
˂BarcodeValue>˂KeyValueSeparator>˂NewPageType>˂MappingsDelimiter>
For example: "1234=Main_Page,56789=Trailing_Page"
The LastPageTypeMappings use a similar format as the barcode mappings:
˂LastPageTypeValue>˂KeyValueSeparator>˂NewPageType>˂MappingsDelimiter>
If the barcode on the page is "1234", then the current page
will be assigned the page type "Main_Page". If the barcode value
is "56789", then the current page will be assigned the type
"Trailing_Page".
If a barcode is not found on the page, and if no previous barcodes have been read,
then the page will be assigned the type specified in "DefaultPageType".
If a barcode is not found on the page, and a barcode has been read on a previous page,
then the LastPageMappings will be used to assign the pagetype.
If multiple barcode values are found, the first barcode will be used for matching the barcode mapping specification.
It is allowed to have multiple key-value pairs that map different
barcode or last page type values to the same page type. For example:
123=Invoice,ABC=Invoice,Hello=Invoice,Separator=Separator,Sep=Separator
rrSet("ENDDOC=Document_Separator|ATTACH=Attachment_Separator","@B.Mapping")
rrSet("Document_Separator=Main_Page|Attachment_Separator=Attachment|Main_Page=Trailing_Page|Trailing_Page=Trailing_Page|Attachment=Attachment","@B.PageMapping")
rrSet("|","@B.MappingSeparator")
rrSet("=","@B.KeyValueSeparator")
rrSet("True","@B.CaseSensitive")
IdentifyOtherPagesByBarcode("@B.Mapping", "B.PageMapping", "@B.MappingSeparator","@B.KeyValueSeparator","@B.CaseSensitive", "Main_Page")
As an illustration, the action uses smart parameters to obtain the values of all parameters, except the last parameter.
Smart parameters allow values to be retrieved from other locations such as DCO locations or the application's settings file.
IdentifyOtherPagesByBarcode evaluates every page within the batch, if the page type is not "Other", then the page
is already assigned a type and will be skipped.
For each page, the action will attempt to read a barcode from the page. If a barcode is found,
it will look to see if the barcode value matches "ENDDOC" or "ATTACH". If it matches one of those,
then it will assign the page the specified type.
If the barcode type does not match, or if a barcode was not read, and if no barcodes have been read within the
batch, then the page is assigned the value in DefaultPageType.
If the barcode type does not match, or if a barcode was not read, and there previously was a barcode
found within the match, then the LastPageTypeMappings will be used to assign the page. If the previously
found page type was "Document_Separator", because a separator page was found, then the current page
will be assigned the type "Main_Page". If the previous page type was set to "Main_Page", the page will be
assigned "Trailing_Page". If the previous page was set to "Trailing_Page", then the current page will
also be set to "Trailing_Page".
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: IdentifyPageByBarcode
method.qi: : Updates the current page type if a barcode match is found.
method.ap:
BarcodePageMappings:
A delimited list of barcode value-page type mappings that are
evaluated to determine whether matching barcodes exist on the current page.
For more information, see the Details section.
If any of these mappings are regular expressions, set the batch-level variable BarcodeRegEx to "true".
If this variable is not set to true, the regular expressions are not recognized as regular expressions.
MappingsDelimiter:
(Optional) Delimiter separating mappings. A single character used to separate
multiple barcode value-page type key-value pairs. Default: comma.
KeyValueSeparator:
(Optional) Delimiter used to separate the barcode value and page type in an a key value pair.
Default: equals sign (=).
CaseSensitive:
(Optional) True enforces case sensitivity when evaluating the list of barcodes found on the page. Default: False.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action searches all of the barcodes that are found on the current page for a match from
the provided mappings by using the GetBarCodeList variable. If a barcode value is found,
this action updates the type of the current page by using the corresponding input mapping.
This action assumes that GetAllBarcodes has
previously been used to read all of the barcodes on the page.
The GetAllBarcodes action is automatically called if the GetBarCodeList variable does not exist.
If the GetAllBarcodes action was called earlier with a unique separator,
use an identical symbol for the MappingsDelimiter parameter.
Mapping Specification
The input for parameter BarcodePageMappings must take the following
form:
˂BarcodeValue>˂KeyValueSeparator>˂PageType>˂MappingsDelimiter>
For example: "1234=Main_Page,56789=Trailing_Page"
If the barcode on the page is "1234", then the current page
will be assigned the page type "Main_Page". If the barcode value
is "56789", then the current page will be assigned the type
"Trailing_Page". If the barcode on the page is not read or if
the value does not match any of the values in the specification
then no page type will be assigned and the action will return false.
Additional barcodes and page values can be listed, separated by the "MappingsDelimiter" character.
If multiple barcode values are found, the page type that is assigned is the first
corresponding value from the GetBarCodeList variable.
It is allowed to have multiple key-value pairs that map different
barcode values to the same page type. For example:
123=Invoice,ABC=Invoice,Hello=Invoice,Separator=Separator,Sep=Separator
IdentifyByBarcode("Separator=Separator_Page,Attach=Attachment_Page,Main=Main_Page","","","")
This example looks for the barcode values "Separator", "Attachment" and "Main".
The default values are used for the separators and case sensitivity.
IdentifyByBarcode("Separator=Separator_Page%Attach=Attachment_Page","%","","")
This example looks for barcodes "Separator" and "Attach". The separator % is
used to denote each key-value pair.
rrSet("Separator|Separator_Page%Attach|Attachment_Page","@B.Mapping")
rrSet("%","@B.MappingSeparator")
rrSet("|","@B.KeyValueSeparator")
rrSet("True","@B.CaseSensitive")
IdentifyByBarcode("@B.Mapping","@B.MappingSeparator","@B.KeyValueSeparator","@B.CaseSensitive")
This example changes the default values for the separators and also performs a case sensitive match
of the barcode values. It demonstrates the use of smart parameters. This example is obtaining
the input values from batch level variables. In this example the values were set just prior
to calling the action. In a real life example, the batch level variables could be set by
previous rules or tasks.
rrSet("True","@B.BarcodeRegEx)
IdentifyByBarcode("C.A=Invoice,I...=Invoice","","","")
This example sets the batch level variable BarcodeRegEx to "True", enabling
regular expression matching. A barcode that matches the regular expression "C.A" or "I..."
will be assigned the page type "Invoice".
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: MatchAnyBarcode
method.qi: : Searches all the barcodes on the current page and checks if one matches the value you enter as a parameter.
method.ap:
The value of the barcode to match.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Recognizes and evaluates all the barcodes on the current page or current field and checks
if one of the barcodes matches the parameter value.
If running at field level and the field does not have a zone defined, then recognition will run for the whole page.
If a match occurs, the barcode's value is placed into a page level variable called 'GetBarCode'.
If running at the field level, the matched value is also stored in the text property.
The expected barcode types must be set prior to calling this action. See the top-level help
for more information.
MatchAnyBarcode("FAX")
This example will look for an barcode with the value "FAX"
and will return true if one is found.
method.ret:
True
if the action is called at the page level or field level and one of the barcode values on the page
matches the parameter value (parameter value must not be empty). Otherwise,
False.
In addition the calling object's value and variable "GetBarCode" will be filled with the bar code value. This action also
stores barcode information such as confidence, coordinates, code name, and size. If the object's barcode settings are set to read more than
one barcode, and more than one barcode is found, barcodes are also stored in the variable "GetBarCodeX" where "X" is the index of
the barcode found.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: MatchBarcodePrefix
method.qi: : Searches all the barcodes on the current page and checks if one matches the value you enter as a parameter.
method.ap:
The value of the barcode to match.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Recognizes and evaluates all the barcodes on the current page or current field
and checks if one of the barcodes starts with the parameter value.
If running at the field level and the field does not have a zone defined, then recognition will run for the whole page.
If a match occurs, the barcode's value is placed into a page level variable called 'GetBarCode'.
If running at the field level, the matched value is also stored in the text property.
MatchBarcodePrefix("ATM")
If one of the barcode matches the prefix provided, the
action will return true. "ATM", "ATM123", "ATMPAGE"
are all examples of barcode values that will return true.
method.ret:
True
if the action is called at the page level or field level and one of the barcode values on the page
matches the parameter value (parameter value must not be empty). Otherwise,
False.
In addition the calling object's value and variable "GetBarCode" will be filled with the bar code value. This action also
stores barcode information such as confidence, coordinates, code name, and size. If the object's barcode settings are set to read more than
one barcode, and more than one barcode is found, barcodes are also stored in the variable "GetBarCodeX" where "X" is the index of
the barcode found.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: MatchFirstBarcode
method.qi: : Tests the first barcode found with the value specified by the parameter.
method.ap:
A value of the barcode to match.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Checks if the current page contains a barcode with the value specified by the parameter.
This action uses the first barcode that is successfully read.
One possible use of this action is to identify a document's Separator page.
The action will return true if the first barcode matches allowing the
next action after this action to run.
Refer to top-level help in this action library for information regarding barcode configuration in Datacap Studio.
MatchFirstBarcode("Separator")
SetPageType("Separator")
This example looks for a barcode with the value "Separator". If found, the second action,
an ApplicationObjects action, establishes the page as a Separator page.
method.ret:
True
if the first barcode on the page has a value that matches the parameter.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.

method.name: SetBarcodeMinimumConfidence
method.qi: : Changes the default confidence for successful barcode recognition.
method.ap:
An integer value representing the minimum confidence required for barcodes read by the engine to be accepted.
Valid values are in the range of 1-10. The default value, when this action is not used, is 3.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.lvl: Page or Field level only. Must be set on the object that calls the action to read the barcode.
method.ret:
False
if the confidence value cannot be set either because it is invalid or an error
occurs or if the action is called at a level other than page or field. Otherwise,
True
method.h:
Sets the minimum confidence required for barcodes read by the engine to be accepted.
Barcodes are generally reliable, even when the confidence is lower than a
typical character recognition. It is suggested that an application be tested with
numerous real input pages to determine the lowest confidence that is
still providing accurate results.
SetBarcodeMinimumConfidence(5)
GetBarcode()
This example sets the minimum confidence to 5. Any value in the range of 5-10 will
be considered a successful read of the barcode.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help topic of this action library for more information about using barcodes, including
how to specify the barcode type and how to enable automatic image enhancements to read barcodes
that have poor scan quality.
