method.name: FindFingerprintCC
method.qi: This action should not be used, as it is scheduled to be removed in future versions. It has been replaced by ClassifyCC.
method.h:
This Action has been marked for Deprecation and will removed in a future release. It has been replaced with Action
ClassifyCC
.

method.name: ClassifyCC
method.qi: Finds the closest matching document type and assigns the page type to the page.
method.h:
This action identifies a page using the IBM Content Classification technology. This technology analyzes the full text of pages and attempts to find match within
the Knowledge Base specified in the SetKnowledgeBaseCC action. If a match is found, the Page type is populated with the ID of the category that was matched.
If a match is not
found, the page type is set to "Other".
When classification is complete, a list of matches and their confidence values are stored in the
"MatchingCategoryX"
and
"MatchingCategoryConfX"
variables. The number of matches is stored in the variable
"MatchingCategoriesCount"
.
To run classification without updating the page type, set the variable "UpdateDCOType" to "0" prior to calling this action. In this case classification will not update the page type, but the variables mentioned aboved will still be populated.
Because the matching relies on a page's full text, a full page recognition action must be called prior to using the ClassifyCC action.
Note:
Starting in Taskmaster 9.0.1, this action supports classification of text located layout files generated by the
Recognize
actions in the
RecognitionOCRA
and
OCR_SR
action libraries.
If a layout file is present, the action will automatically load it as the source of the text to be classified.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetLanguageCC("English")
SetKnowledgeBaseCC("Mortgage")
SetProblemValueCC(0.9)
Recognize()
ClassifyCC()

method.name: SetKnowledgeBaseCC
method.qi: Sets the name of the Content Classication Knowledge Base to use to classify documents.

p.name: KnowledgeBaseName
p.qi: The name of the IBM Content Classification Knowledge Base. This parameter is required and cannot be empty. Smart parameters are supported.

method.h:
Sets the name of the IBM Content Classification Knowledge Base to use to classify documents in an application.
This action must be called after the SetListenerURLCC action.
This action must be called before the actions SetProblemValueCC and UpdateKnowledgeBaseCC.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetKnowledgeBaseCC("Mortgage")
UpdateKnowledgeBaseCC()
method.ret:
False
, if the parameter is empty. Otherwise,
True.

method.name: SetProblemValueCC
method.qi: Sets the minimum score for fingerprint matching.

p.name: MinScore
p.qi: Minimum score for fingerprint matching. Valid values are fractional values between zero and one (for example: 0.0 and 1.0)

method.h:
When ClassifyCC searches for a fingerprint match, a score between zero (no match) and one (a
positive match) is calculated. This action sets the minimum score that a match must have
to be considered a match. Any matches with a score less than the value specified is rejected.
With this action, you can control the tolerance for documents matching an existing example.
When setting up the parameter in your application, use the decimal character from the system locale defined
for the application in the Taskmaster Application Manager. For example, when the decimal character is
a period, use a value from 0.0 to 1.0. When the decimal character is a comma, use a value from 0,0 to 1,0.
This action must be called before the FindFingerprintCC action.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetProblemValueCC(0.9)
ClassifyCC()
method.ret:
True
if the parameter value is between the valid range of zero to one (0.0 and 1.0) Otherwise,
False
.

method.name: SetLanguageCC
method.qi: Sets the language used in the specified Knowledge Base.

p.name: LanguageName
p.qi: The name of the language used in the specified Knowledge Base

method.h:
This action sets the language of the specified Knowledge Base or Decision Plan.
This action must be called before the ClassifyCC action.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetLanguageCC("English")
SetKnowledgeBaseCC("Mortgage")
SetProblemValueCC(0.9)
ClassifyCC()
method.ret:
Always
True
.

method.name: SetListenerURLCC
method.qi: Sets the URL of the CC Listener that will be used for classification.

p.name: URL
p.qi: The URL of the CC Listener that will be used for classification. Smart parameters are supported.

method.h:
This action configures the URL of the IBM Content Classification Listener that will be used for classification, and opens the connection to the IBM Content Classification Listener.
This action must be called before the actions FindFingerprintCC, SetKnowledgeBaseCC, and UpdateKnowledgeBaseCC.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetKnowledgeBaseCC("Mortgage")
SetProblemValueCC(0.9)
ClassifyCC()
method.ret:
True,
if the service URL is successfully set. Otherwise,
False.
Note that
this action does not test that the CC Listener exists and is running.

method.name: SetDecisionPlanCC
method.qi: Sets the name of the Content Classification Decision Plan to use to classify text.

p.name: DecisionPlanName
p.qi: Sets he name of the IBM Content Classification Decision Plan. This parameter is required and cannot be empty.

method.h:
Sets the name of the IBM Content Classification Decision Plan to use to classify text.
This action must be called after the SetListenerURLCC action.
This action must be called before the actions RunDecisionPlanCC, RunDecisionPlanForBlocksCC, and RunDecisionPlanForTextCC.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetDecisionPlanCC("Mortgage")
method.ret:
False
, if the parameter is empty. Otherwise,
True.

method.name: SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC
method.qi: Sets the Decision Plan fields separated by comma

p.name: DPFields
p.qi: Comma separated list of content field names to be extracted from the content classification decision plan. This parameter is required and cannot be empty.

method.h:
Sets the fields returned by Content Classification that are to be saved as DCO variables on the calling object.
This action must be called before the actions RunDecisionPlanCC, RunDecisionPlanForBlocksCC, and RunDecisionPlanForTextCC.
SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC("Title,Loan,Loan Type")
method.ret:
False
, if the parameter is empty. Otherwise,
True.

method.name: ClassifyTextCC
method.qi: Classifies blocks on the page

dlentry.dd: Text to be classified. Smart parameters supported.

method.h:
Classifies text using knowledge base
This action must be called after the SetListenerURLCC, SetKnowledgeBaseICM actions.
When classification is complete, a list of matches and their confidence values are stored in the
"MatchingCategoryX"
and
"MatchingCategoryConfX"
variables. The number of matches is stored in the variable
"MatchingCategoriesCount"
.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetLanguageCC("English")
SetKnowledgeBaseCC("Mortgage")
SetProblemValueCC(0.9)
ClassifyTextCC("Place Text to classify here")

method.name: RunDecisionPlanForBlocksCC
method.qi: Runs a previously set decision plan on selected block types of a layout xml file.

p.name: blockTypes
p.qi: Comma separated values of block types to send to decision plan. Supported block types are Block, Table, Header , Footer, Title, H1, H2, H3, and Barcode. Smart parameters are supported.

method.h:
Sends the specified block types in the layout XML to Content Classification so that Content Classification can choose which block types to compare text to a KB and which to use in DP rules. For example only comparing paragraph text to a KB may produce a better match by excluding text not specific to the category.
The layout xml file can be created by the Recognize action in the
OCR_SR
or
RecognitionOCRA
action libraries.
This action
must
be called after the SetListenerURLCC, SetDecisionPlanCC, SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC actions.
To run the decision plan without updating the page type, set the variable "UpdateDCOType" to "0" prior to calling this action. In this case classification will not update the page type, but the variables mentioned aboved will still be populated.
When the action is complete, the Decision Plan field results are stored as variables in the calling object. The variables created are named after the names of the fields specified in SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC, if this action is used. If the decision plan uses a KB and returns a matched category, a variable
MatchingCategory
will be created as well. Under this same scenario, the type of the calling object will be set to the name of the matching category, unless the variable "UpdateDCOType" is set to "0" prior to calling this action.
Field mapping
When block xml data is passed to a decision plan, corresponding fields and the extracted text are created in the decicion plan. Below is a list of the fields created for each block type:
Block Type = Field Name in Decision Plan
--------------------------------------------
Barcode = Barcode
Block = Block
Footer = Footer
H1 = Heading1
H2 = Heading2
H3 = Heading3
Header = Header
Para = Body
Table = Table (single value field containing all the text in the table), and Cell (multivalue field containing all cells of the table)
To take advantage of these fields in a decision plan you must add input fields to your ICC solution. See ICC documentation for adding input fields and mapping XML nodes to them. Input fields can then be used in a decision plan rule or to include when performing a statistical comparison to a Knowledge Base.
Important!
Depending on the version of Content Classification installed, manual changes to the docFilterManager.xml file may be required in order to ensure proper data parsing of the blocks xml on the Content Classification server side.
To determine if manual changes are required:
1. Open the file %ContentClassificationInstallDir%\Filters\docFilterManager.xml in an xml or text editor.
2. Perform a search for the string "XPATH-DATACAP". If the string is present, there are no further steps to perform. If the string is not present, please follow the instructions under "Content Classification Configuration" below to manually add the necessary configuration to this file.
Content Classification configuration
In order for Content Classification to successfully parse the block data sent by the action RunDecisionPlanForBlocksCC, it is necessary to make manual changes to the docFilterManager.xml file is installed by Content Classification. The steps for this manual process are listed below.
1. Make a backup copy of the existing docFilterManager.xml file. Typically, this file is located in the %ContentClassificationInstallDir%\Filters directory, for example C:\IBM\ContentClassification\Filters.
2. Open docFilterManager.xml in a xml or text editor.
3. Locate the xml element
AllFilters
.
4. Add the following
Filter
element to the
AllFilters
node.
Note
make sure to replace
«
and
»
with the corresponding less than and greater than symbols.
«Filter»
«FilterName»XPATH-DATACAP«/FilterName»
«Timeout»30«/Timeout»
«NvpMapping»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Block/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Block«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Header/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Header«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Footer/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Footer«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Title/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Title«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/H1/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Heading1«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/H2/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Heading2«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/H3/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Heading3«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Barcode/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Barcode«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Table//«/PropName»
«NvpName»Table«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Table/Row/Cell«/PropName»
«NvpName»Cell«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«Property»
«PropName»/P/Para/«/PropName»
«NvpName»Body«/NvpName»
«/Property»
«/NvpMapping»
«/Filter»
5. Locate the xml element
AllWorkflows
.
6. Add the following
Workflows
element to the
AllWorkflows
node.
«WorkFlows»
«AllMetaData»
«TP_Extension»xmldc«/TP_Extension»
«/AllMetaData»
«FilterName»XPATH-DATACAP«/FilterName»
«/WorkFlows»
7. Save and close the docFilterManager.xml file.
Recognize()
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetDecisionPlanCC("Mortage")
SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC("Title,Loan,Loan Type")
RunDecisionPlanForBlocksCC("Table,Block")

method.name: RunDecisionPlanForTextCC
method.qi: Classifies blocks on the page

p.name: TextToClassify
p.qi: Text to be classified. Smart parameters supported.

method.h:
Classifies text using decision plans
This action must be called after the SetListenerURLCC, SetKnowledgeBaseICMCC, SetDecisionPlanCC, SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC, actions.
To run the decicion plan without updating the page type, set the variable "UpdateDCOType" to "0" prior to calling this action. In this case classification will not update the page type, but the variables mentioned aboved will still be populated.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetDecisionPlanCC("Mortgage")
SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC("Title,Loan,Loan Type")
RunDecisionPlanForTextCC(@F)

method.name: RunDecisionPlanCC
method.qi: Runs decision plan on top of the page
method.h:
Used to run the current page against the content classification decision plan specified in the
SetDecisionPlanCC
action, and
extract the content fields specified in the
SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC
action. This action uses the recognition data located in layout xml, cco, or txt files associated to the calling dco page object.
This action must be called after the SetListenerURLCC, SetDecisionPlanCC, SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC actions.
To run the decision plan without updating the page type, set the variable "UpdateDCOType" to "0" prior to calling this action. In this case classification will not update the page type, but the variables mentioned aboved will still be populated.
Because the matching relies on a page's full text, a full page recognition action must be called
prior to using the RunDecisionPlanCC action.
Recognize()
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
SetDecisionPlanCC("MortgageDp")
SetDecisionPlanFieldsCC("EmployeeId,Date")
RunDecisionPlanCC()

method.name: UpdateKnowledgeBaseCC
method.qi: Updates the CC Knowledge Base.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Provides classification feedback to the Content Clasification server.
Important:
this method is to be used to provide feedback to a previously trained knowledge base, and not to be used as the primary method for training a knowledge base from scratch.
Although training via feedback is not recommended to build the knowledge base, it is recommended that it is used to submit feedback on classification data returned on a "trained" category.
For instance, let us use a knowledge base that contains 5 categories, 4 of which have been trained. When
ClassifyCC
runs, it will either return a match or no match. When a match is found, it is recommended to provide feedback (using UpdateKnowledgeBaseCC) to the knowledge base to assert that the classification was correct.
When there is no match (no category returned) or there is a mismatch (wrong category returned), the recommended process is to export a copy of the document to a folder and train the knowledge base with these new documents via the Classification Workbench. After the new documents have been added, the knowledge based should be exported, and documents processed in Taskmaster to provide feedback. The training should be done in a non Production system, then moved to Production after testing.
Although it is recommended that this procedure is used to submit feedback on trained categories, it should be done for a period of time, and not indefinetely, since this can cause the knowledge base to grow very large.
In conclusion, this action should be used only for documents where the classification result was correct, and should only be used during a period of time until the training on the knowledge base is complete.
SetListenerURLCC("http://localhost:18087")
ClassifyCC()
UpdateKnowledgeBaseCC()

com.h:
Document Conversion
The Convert action library's primary purpose is to allow ingestion of different electronic document formats
and converts them into a format that can be processed by subsequent Datacap actions.
Common usage includes:
- PDF to TIF
- Multipage TIF to single page TIF
- Images to TIF
- Excel to PDF or TIF
- HTML to PDF or TIF
- Outlook to TIF
- DOC, RTF and TXT to PDF or TIF
- ZIP extraction
The conversions allow documents to be placed into a format that can be processed by Datacap, or a standard
desired output for export.
The PDF to TIF process optionally allows recognition to be performed in the same step. Recognition can be
performed on other document types by first converting them to separate TIF images and performing
recognition on the TIFs in a separate step.
Fingerprinting
If an application is performing fingerprinting, black and white TIF images are required.
The Convert actions allow documents to be converted to TIF, allowing the images to be processed
by subsequent actions and the images may also be used as fingerprints.
Electronic document formats are continually evolving. When upgrading
to a newer version of Datacap, and if fingerprints are used,
test that converted documents are still providing effective matching to existing fingerprints.
If document formatting changes are not allowing fingerprints to match, new fingerprints will
need to be setup with the new converted images.
Common Actions
The Convert action library "Common" actions control the operation of subsequent
Convert actions. For example, when performing an action that converts a multi-page
document to a set of single page TIF documents, the newly created TIF images have new
names that are generated at runtime. By first calling the action SetNamePattern
prior to calling a conversion action such as PDFFREDocumentToImage, or SplitMultipageTiff,
the naming convention can be adjusted. All of the common actions will adjust how
the conversion actions work when they call called prior to other convert actions.
All of the common actions work in a similar manner to control subsequent conversion actions.
This action can be called from any level and subsequent Convert library actions will use this setting.
Subsequent actions can be on different rules or rulesets, but must be within the same task profile.
Typically the common actions are called once per batch, for example on a batch open event
within the DCO hierarchy. Convert actions that create new files from documents are
typically called on the page or document node for the file to convert. This allows the common configuration
action to be called once and then the conversion action can be called for each target file. It is
allowed to call the common action on the same rule as a conversion action. If the common action
called with the same value each time then it is redundant
because the setting is already set. For greatest efficiency, set the common actions on a batch open
event for the ruleset.
When a conversion of a document fails it may be desired to continue processing files in the batch
or perhaps the batch should be stopped so the conversion problem can be reviewed and corrected
prior to continuing. The common conversion actions provide a set of actions that control
the behavior when document cannot be converted. The actions are:
ExceptionSetHandler, ExceptionSetFileTypes, ExceptionSetVariableName, and ExceptionTaskCondition.
Using these actions, the application designer can decide how the application should handle
these failures. Processing can be continue, processing logic can respond and take
action on a failure or the batch can be set to an abort state to allow the batch to be
reviewed. When using Rulerunner to process batches, Rulerunner has a configuration
setting that will stop processing subsequent batches if an abort condition is raised
or will still continue processing waiting batches. When an application is configured to
abort when a conversion fails, also confirm that the Rulerunner configurations are
set to respond as desired to an abort condition.
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
For example, "@X" is notation for accessing the current object. "@P" accesses the page object, which
could be the current object, or a parent object. Being evaluated at runtime, allows recognized data
or other batch specific data to be passed to actions or stored as metadata. A smart parameter such
as @DATE could be used to name export files based on the current date. Similar smart parameters
will retrieve the current batch ID, current batch directory, current operator ID, and more.
Smart parameters are a very powerful mechanism of getting data from other areas of the application and copying
it into a new location or passing it as a parameter to an action. It is recommended that the smart parameter
documentation is reviewed to understand the full capabilities available. The top-level help of the
RuleRunnerLogicaction library has a complete smart parameter reference.

method.name: DeleteSourceImagePages
method.qi: Removes source image dco pages.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Use this action to remove pages where the associated file has been converted using the convert library actions.
All child DCO objects that have the DCO variable "original_source_image" set to "yes" will be
deleted from the DCO hierarchy.
This action will evaluate all page objects that are children of the batch folder. It will delete any
pages that have generated new pages as a result of the convert actions. Document objects
are note removed. If fields are attached to the page, then the fields are removed
with the parent page object.
Note: Pages are only deleted from the DCO but not the batch directory.
This action must be called as the last action in the ruleset. Any subsequent
actions must be in a subsequent ruleset.
DeleteSourceImagePages()
This example removes the pages that have the variable original_source_image variable set to
"yes". Do not call any additional actions in this rule or ruleset. Subsequent actions
must be in a following ruleset.
method.ret:
True,
if the action is successful.
False,
if an error is encountered.
method.see:
The ApplicationObjects action library contains similar actions that provide additional conditions
for deleting child objects: DeleteDCOChildOfType, DeleteDCOChildren, DeleteChildrenAndVariables, and DeleteDCOChildWithStatus.
The actions will remove the DCO object so no further rules will run on the object. The associated file may not
be removed, refer to the action help for more information.
Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

method.name: SetChildPageType
method.qi: Allows the configuration of created child pages when a document is split.

p.name: Type
p.qi: The type that will be assigned to child pages created from a conversion action. Smart parameters are supported.

method.h:
When a new page is split from a multi-page document, such as a PDF, this is the default type that
will be assigned to the new DCO page. To take effect, this action must be called before calling a
subsequent convert action that creates single pages from a multi-page document.
If this action is not called and pages are split from a multi-page file associated
with a DCO page object, then the default page type will be the same as the original page.
If this action is not called and pages are split from a multi-page file associated
with a DCO document object, the default page type will be "Other".
Typically when performing a split of a multi-page document into individual files, the desired initial
page type is “Other”. This is the standard initial page type that is then used to classify pages into
appropriate types so pages are processed appropriately in later workflow stages. In some cases, when
splitting a multi-page document, the expected page type may already be known and this action can
reduce the steps required to set the types on all newly created pages.
Call this action with an empty parameter to reset to the default settings.
This action can be called from any level and subsequent Convert library actions will use this setting.
Subsequent actions can be on different rules or rulesets, but must be within the same task profile.
SetNamePattern(“2”)
SetChildPageType(“Mortgage”)
rrSet(“1”,”@X.convPdfIgnoreContent”)
rrSet(“0”,”@X.y_createLayout”)
PDFFREDocumentToImage("300","18","33","32",".bw.tif","col.tif","gray.tif","0","False","100")
This example assumes the current object has an associated PDF. This will create a new DCO page for
each TIF image created from each page of the PDF. Each new page will be assigned the page type “Mortgage”.
While this action shows SetNamePattern and SetChildPageType called directly before the conversion action,
as long as the "Set" actions are called prior to the action that performs the conversion, the settings
will be in effect. For example, it is more efficient to place the "Set" actions on a rule
attached to the batch "open" event so the actions run just once, instead of placing them on a page
object where the actions will be run over and over for each page.
method.ret:
Always
true.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

method.name: SetNamePattern
method.qi: Changes default naming pattern for converted files.

p.name: PatternType
p.qi: A single positive numeric value.

method.ap:
Value of '1' or '2'.
1: Uses default AlphaDecimal pattern, consisting of four pairs or two characters from 01 to ZZ.
2: Uses TMxxxxxx pattern where xxxxxx is a number from 000001 to 999999.
method.h:
When a conversion action creates single page TIF images from a multi-page file, each new TIF
will be created within the batch directory, given a unique name and will have a new DCO page object
created in the DCO hierarchy. Each file must have a unique name. This action will control the naming
convention used when the new TIF image is created.
If this action is not called, then the default mode "1" will be used. This uses a pattern with sets
of digits that correspond to the parentage of the file. The pattern used is in this form:
01010000.tif
01020000.tif
01030000.tif
01040000.tif
The form uses pairs of numbers that are alpha-numeric, ranging from "01" to "ZZ". While the naming
convention illustrates the level from which the file was created, it also limits a single
level to 1296 unique names. If a single source document has more than 1296 pages, then it will fail
and mode "2" must be used to extract all of the pages within the document.
Mode "2" uses the "traditional" Datacap file naming scheme where files are named in the form
"TMxxxxxx" where "x" is an increasing decimal value. The pattern takes this form:
TM000001.tif
TM000002.tif
TM000003.tif
TM000004.tif
This action can be called from any level and subsequent Convert library actions will use this setting.
Subsequent actions can be on different rules or rulesets, but must be within the same task profile.
SetNamePattern(2)
SplitMultipageTiff()
This example sets the name pattern prior to splitting a multi-page TIF into
single page TIFs. While this action shows SetNamePattern called directly before the conversion action,
as long as the action SetNamePattern is called prior to an action that performs the conversion, the setting
will be in effect. For example, it is more efficient to place the SetNamePattern action on a rule
attached to the batch "open" event so the actions run just once, instead of placing them on a page
object where the action will be run over and over for each page.
method.ret:
True,
if the setting is successful.
False,
if the setting is rejected.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

method.name: SetNamePatternFileCheck
method.qi: Configures file checking behavior in naming pattern for converted files.
method.ap:
True
- Enable file checking, naming pattern will increment count if preexisting files are found
(Default).
False
- Disable file checking, preexisting files may be overwritten.
method.h:
This action only applies to the AlphaDecimal naming pattern.
Use this action to avoiding appending files to the batch directory. When file checking is enabled, newer output
files
will not overwrite preexisting files in cases like batch reprocessing, leading to increased disk consumption.
SetNamePatternFileCheck(False)
method.ret:
Always
True
.
method.see:
SetNamePattern
Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

method.name: ExceptionSetHandler
method.qi: Sets the type of exception handling to be used during batch processing failure.

p.name: handler
p.qi: Exception handler type.

method.ap:
0
– Abort the batch (Default).
1
– Increment a variable in the runtime hierarchy, skip abort.
2
– Raise a task condition, skip abort.
method.h:
Use this action to change or reset the abort behavior caused by conversion failures.
Avoiding aborts may be desirable when an external workflow handling process is already in place.
This action can be called from any level and subsequent Convert library actions will use this setting.
Subsequent actions can be on different rules or rulesets, but must be within the same task profile.
ExceptionSetHandler(0)
method.ret:
True,
if a valid parameter is specified. Otherwise,
False
.
method.see:
ExceptionSetFileTypes
ExceptionSetVariableName
ExceptionTaskCondition
Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

method.name: ExceptionSetFileTypes
method.qi: Sets the file types to be monitored for exception handling.

p.name: types
p.qi: List of file extensions to monitor, comma delimited.

method.h:
Sets one or more file types to be monitored for special exception handling.
Unspecified file types encountering processing failures will cause abort without any further action.
If this action is not called, or the parameter is blank, then all file types will be monitored.
This action can be called from any level and subsequent Convert library actions will use this setting.
Subsequent actions can be on different rules or rulesets, but must be within the same task profile.
ExceptionSetHandler(1)
ExceptionSetFileTypes(.pdf,.doc,.docx,xls,xlsx,.txt)
method.ret:
Always
True
.
method.see:
ExceptionSetHandler
Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

method.name: ExceptionSetVariableName
method.qi: Sets the runtime document hierarchy variable to be incremented upon exception.

p.name: varName
p.qi: Variable to be incremented. Smart Parameters are supported.

method.h:
Sets the variable to be incremented upon exception.
Default is '@B.ConvertExceptions' when exception handler is set to flag variable.
This action can be called from any level and subsequent Convert library actions will use this setting.
Subsequent actions can be on different rules or rulesets, but must be within the same task profile.
ExceptionSetHandler(1)
ExceptionFlagVariable(@B.PDFConvertExceptions)
method.ret:
Always
True
.
method.see:
ExceptionSetHandler
Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

method.name: ExceptionSetTaskCondition
method.qi: Sets the task condition to be raised upon exception.

p.name: taskCondition
p.qi: Zero-based task condition index.

method.h:
Sets the task condition, defined in workflow administration, to be raised upon exception.
Batch splitting is unsupported in this action, please see the
Split
action library for information on how to
setup splitting a batch using rules.
This action can be called from any level and subsequent Convert library actions will use this setting.
Subsequent actions can be on different rules or rulesets, but must be within the same task profile.
ExceptionSetHandler(2)
ExceptionTaskCondition(0)
method.ret:
Always
True
.
method.see:
ExceptionSetHandler
Refer to the top level help for general information about the common conversion actions.

com.h:
Word Overview
The Word conversion will convert electronic DOC and DOCX documents to a TIF file. One possible use of the TIF
files is to perform recognition and subsequent rules processing on them. Use the available Word
conversion actions to set the conversion as desired, then use the WordDocumentToImage to convert
the images that have been input to the batch.
If you are converting to TIF images so recognition can be performed, it is suggested that
the output TIF format be one bit black and white, fax group 4 compressed images.
Images of this specification work best for recognition.
Conversion Limits
When using the conversion actions, the maximum number of initial input files in a single batch
using the default Alphadecimal file name pattern is 1296. These files can then expand into more files within the
batch, creating a batch with far more than 1296 total documents in the end.
For example, an input batch of a word document containing 6 pages will result
in a batch of 7 files, the initial DOC file and then the resulting 6 TIFFs that were generated from the pages.
For each file that is to be converted within the batch, there is a maximum of 1296 output pages.
For example, a word document consisting of 2000 pages will only have the first
1296 pages converted to TIFF. Likewise, a single ZIP file has a maximum of 1296
files within it and a msg file has a maximum of 1296 attachments.
The 1296 limit exists on each input file, not a total limit for all files combined.
When using the convert actions, there is a 3 level limit for embedded files.
For example a MSG file can contain a ZIP file which can contain a PDF file.
At the end of the conversion, all files will be extracted and all of the pages
in the PDF will be converted to a TIFF. An example that isn’t allowed is a
MSG file that contains a ZIP file that contains another ZIP file that contains a PDF because.
this has a 4 level hierarchy, which is not permitted.
To scan more than 1296 files into a single batch requires using the
SetNamePattern
action with
the parameter '2' which selects the alternate file naming pattern of TMxxxxxx. In this use case
all files scanned or expanded from an original scanned file will be assigned the next available
TMxxxxxx pattern where xxxxxx is a range from 1 to 999999; allowing upto a total of 999999 files
in a single batch after all scanned files have been expanded.
The Rules
Because rules are flexible, there are multiple ways that your applications can
use the electronic document conversion actions. The following is one recommended way of using the actions
within your Application.
Perform the electron virtual scanning in its own task profile, to create the batch of
input documents to be processed. Use the electronic document conversion actions in their own task
task profile.
In a single ruleset, you can perform all of the actions to convert your
electronic documents to TIF files prior to recognition. Create a function for each type
of electronic document that you expect to convert with the electronic document conversion actions.
For example, one function to operate on ZIP files, another to operate on Word files, etc., for
as many different types as you need. If the default values are not adequate, use the actions
to configure your output format, then use the action to convert the document to
a TIF file for each page within the document. If the page is not of the expected type,
the action will return false and proceed to the next type and attempt to convert again.
This operation will continue until all of the desired types have been converted.
Types that are not expected, will be ignored by this process.
You can setup additional rules to handle them,
if required by your specific application.
Example Ruleset
The following shows a specific example ruleset and functions configured to process
PDF, Word and Excel documents using the convert actions. You can add more functions to process other
file formats supported by convert, such as splitting tiff files, zip files, etc.
Execution runs through each of the functions until a function completes
successfully. The page status is first checked and then it attempts to convert the page.
If the page is converted successfully, the page status is set to 75, meaning it is deleted.
The function completes and no further processing is performed on the ruleset.
If the document cannot be converted because the type doesn't match,
then control passes to the next function and again attempts to convert the page.
Ruleset Convert Files
- Function Process PDF
- - ChkDCOStatus("49")
- - PDFDocumentToImage()
- - SetDCOStatus("75")
- Function Process Word
- - ChkDCOStatus("49")
- - WordDocumentToImage()
- - SetDCOStatus("75")
- Function Process Excel
- - ChkDCOStatus("49")
- - ExcelWorkbookToImage()
- - SetDCOStatus("75")
Setting the page to a deleted status allows that page to be skipped by subsequent processing.
For example, if you use virtual scan create a batch containing a PDF document, then convert the PDF to a
series of image files using the convert actions, it is likely that you no longer need to perform any further
processing
on the input PDF file. An application could skip processing of these pages, as needed, by first calling
ChkDCOStatus("49")
and the following actions in the function will only be run on pages that have that status.
As a general rule, subsequent processing and recognition
is performed on the TIFF files that were created at run time, such as the TIFF created from DOC file, not the parent
DOC file.
Note that setting the page to deleted does not remove the page reference
from the DCO and it does not delete the file from the batch directory. Because the original
file still exists, at export time it is possible to include the original document when exporting
to an external repository.
Variables Created During Conversion
The conversion actions will store data in variables that may be useful. These are the variables
created:
"IMAGEFILE" : The name of the TIF file that is associated with the converted page.
The value would typically look like this "01010000.tif".
This variable is on the page level.
"ParentImage" : The name of the document that was used to create this page. If the TIF was created by
the conversion of a WORD file, then the value would typically look like "02000000.doc".
This variable is on the page level. If the page has multiple parents, such as when it was extracted
from a ZIP file that was inside a ZIP file, then the parents will be separated by a colon.
For example, TM000001.zip:01020000.zip.

method.name: WordDocumentToImage
method.qi: Converts a page with *.doc or *.docx file to a page or pages in TIFF format.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
If the current page is a Word Document, the file will be converted to multiple TIFF files,
one TIFF file for each page within the Document, based on the settings of the other
Word actions that configure the conversion settings.
Each new TIFF will also have a new page created within the application environment
which can be processed by subsequent rules. The original file name from which the page was
extracted will be stored in the ParentImage variable, for possible future reference within
your application.
If the configured output image format and compression
only supports black and white, such as CCITT4, colored text is
exported as black.
WordPrintQuality(200)
WordTiffCompression("CCITT4")
WordDocumentToImage()
This example configures the DPI and compression for the Word document to TIF conversion.
Then the WordDocumentToImage action converts the file associated with the current DCO object to multiple TIF images, one
image for each page. New DCO page objects are created for each page and subsequent rules
can be run on these pages to perform other tasks such as fingerprinting,
classification, recognition and export.
method.lvl:
Page or Document level.
If called on a page level object, then each new single page TIF file created from the source
Word document will be associated with a new DCO page object that is at the same level as the parent DCO page
from which the page was created.
If called on a document level object, then each new single page TIF file will be associated
with a new DCO page object that is a child page of the parent document object.
For example, if the file is associated with a page object, then the DCO structure
will be created like this example:
˂page "Other"˃ TM000001.doc (source page object)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000002.tif (new page object, page 1 of TM000001.doc)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000003.tif (new page object, page 2 of TM000001.doc)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000004.tif (new page object, page 3 of TM000001.doc)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000005.tif (new page object, page 4 of TM000001.doc)
If the file is associated with a document object, then the DCO structure would
be created like this example:
˂Document "Invoice"˃ TM000001.tif (source document object)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000002.tif (new page object, page 1 of TM000001.doc)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000003.tif (new page object, page 2 of TM000001.doc)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000004.tif (new page object, page 3 of TM000001.doc)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000005.tif (new page object, page 4 of TM000001.doc)
method.ret:
True,
if the file is successfully converted to a TIFF document.
False,
if the current page is not a Word Document or if there is a failure in the conversion.
If the number of input files/pages exceeds the maximum allowed or
if there is a failure in the conversion, the batch will be set to abort.
method.see: Read the top level help topic for more information on this action library.

method.name: WordDocumentToPdf
method.qi: Converts *.doc or *.docx files to PDF document format.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
If the current page is a Word Document, this action will create a searchable PDF file using the text from the original document.
Unlike the standard conversion to image actions, this action does not create a new page object in the dco. It only updates the IMAGEFILE variable to point to the newly created PDF file.
By default the produced PDF documents are compliant with the Pdf15 standard.
To create PDF documents compliant with the PdfA1a standard, set the variable "targetPdfCompliance" to "1".
To create PDF documents compliant with PdfA1b standard, set the variable "targetPdfCompliance" to "2".
Note:
The "targetPdfCompliance" variable must to be set to the desired value prior to calling the conversion
action, on the same DCO object level, in order for the setting to take effect.
WordDocumentToPdf()
method.ret:
True,
if the file is successfully converted to a PDF document.
False,
if the current page is not a Word Document or if there is a failure in the conversion.
If the number of input files/pages exceeds the maximum allowed or
if there is a failure in the conversion, the batch will be set to abort.
method.see:
Read the top level help topic for more information on this action library.
PDFFREDocumentToImage will convert a PDF to an image file.

method.name: WordPrintQuality
method.qi: Adjusts the resolution of the image output by WordDocumentToImage.
method.ap: dpi : A single positive numeric value for the dots per inch (dpi) of the output image."
method.h:
Sets the resolution of the output image for WordDocumentToImage.

com.h:
Excel Overview
The Excel conversion will convert electronic XLS and XLSX documents to a TIF file. One possible use of the TIF
files is to perform recognition and subsequent rules processing on them. Use the available Excel
conversion actions to set the conversion as desired, then use the ExcelWorkbookToImage to convert
the images that have been input to the batch.
If you are converting to TIF images so recognition can be performed, it is suggested that
the output TIF format be one bit black and white, fax group 4 compressed images.
Images of this specification work best for recognition.
Conversion Limits
When using the conversion actions, the maximum number of initial input files in a single batch
using the default Alpha-decimal file name pattern is 1296. These files can then expand into more files within the
batch, creating a batch with far more than 1296 total documents in the end.
For example, an input batch of a word document containing 6 pages will result
in a batch of 7 files, the initial DOC file and then the resulting 6 TIFFs that were generated from the pages.
For each file that is to be converted within the batch, there is a maximum of 1296 output pages.
For example, a word document consisting of 2000 pages will only have the first
1296 pages converted to TIFF. Likewise, a single ZIP file has a maximum of 1296
files within it and a msg file has a maximum of 1296 attachments.
The 1296 limit exists on each input file, not a total limit for all files combined.
When using the convert actions, there is a 3 level limit for embedded files.
For example a MSG file can contain a ZIP file which can contain a PDF file.
At the end of the conversion, all files will be extracted and all of the pages
in the PDF will be converted to a TIFF. An example that isn’t allowed is a
MSG file that contains a ZIP file that contains another ZIP file that contains a PDF because.
this has a 4 level hierarchy, which is not permitted.
To scan more than 1296 files into a single batch requires using the
SetNamePattern
action with
the parameter '2' which selects the alternate file naming pattern of TMxxxxxx. In this use case
all files scanned or expanded from an original scanned file will be assigned the next available
TMxxxxxx pattern where xxxxxx is a range from 1 to 999999; allowing up to a total of 999999 files
in a single batch after all scanned files have been expanded.
The Rules
Because rules are flexible, there are multiple ways that your applications can
use the electronic document conversion actions. The following is one recommended way of using the actions
within your Application.
Perform the electron virtual scanning in its own task profile, to create the batch of
input documents to be processed. Use the electronic document conversion actions in their own task
task profile.
In a single ruleset, you can perform all of the actions to convert your
electronic documents to TIF files prior to recognition. Create a function for each type
of electronic document that you expect to convert with the electronic document conversion actions.
For example, one function to operate on ZIP files, another to operate on Word files, etc., for
as many different types as you need. If the default values are not adequate, use the actions
to configure your output format, then use the action to convert the document to
a TIF file for each page within the document. If the page is not of the expected type,
the action will return false and proceed to the next type and attempt to convert again.
This operation will continue until all of the desired types have been converted.
Types that are not expected, will be ignored by this process.
You can setup additional rules to handle them,
if required by your specific application.
Example Ruleset
The following shows a specific example ruleset and functions configured to process
PDF, Word and Excel documents using the convert actions. You can add more functions to process other
file formats supported by convert, such as splitting tiff files, zip files, etc.
Execution runs through each of the functions until a function completes
successfully. The page status is first checked and then it attempts to convert the page.
If the page is converted successfully, the page status is set to 75, meaning it is deleted.
The function completes and no further processing is performed on the ruleset.
If the document cannot be converted because the type doesn't match,
then control passes to the next function and again attempts to convert the page.
Ruleset Convert Files
- Function Process PDF
- - ChkDCOStatus("49")
- - PDFDocumentToImage()
- - SetDCOStatus("75")
- Function Process Word
- - ChkDCOStatus("49")
- - WordDocumentToImage()
- - SetDCOStatus("75")
- Function Process Excel
- - ChkDCOStatus("49")
- - ExcelWorkbookToImage()
- - SetDCOStatus("75")
Setting the page to a deleted status allows that page to be skipped by subsequent processing.
For example, if you use virtual scan create a batch containing a PDF document, then convert the PDF to a
series of image files using the convert actions, it is likely that you no longer need to perform any further
processing
on the input PDF file. An application could skip processing of these pages, as needed, by first calling
ChkDCOStatus("49")
and the following actions in the function will only be run on pages that have that status.
As a general rule, subsequent processing and recognition
is performed on the TIFF files that were created at run time, such as the TIFF created from DOC file, not the parent
DOC file.
Note that setting the page to deleted does not remove the page reference
from the DCO and it does not delete the file from the batch directory. Because the original
file still exists, at export time it is possible to include the original document when exporting
to an external repository.
Variables Created During Conversion
The conversion actions will store data in variables that may be useful. These are the variables
created:
"IMAGEFILE" : The name of the TIF file that is associated with the converted page.
The value would typically look like this "01010000.tif".
This variable is on the page level.
"ParentImage" : The name of the document that was used to create this page. If the TIF was created by
the conversion of a WORD file, then the value would typically look like "02000000.doc".
This variable is on the page level. If the page has multiple parents, such as when it was extracted
from a ZIP file that was inside a ZIP file, then the parents will be separated by a colon.
For example, TM000001.zip:01020000.zip.

method.name: ExcelWorkbookToImage
method.qi: Converts a page with *.xls or *.xlsx file to a page or pages in TIFF format.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
If the current page is an Excel Workbook, the file will be converted to multiple TIFF files,
one TIFF file for each page within the Workbook, based on the settings of the other
Excel actions that configure the conversion settings.
Each new TIFF will also have a new page created within the application environment
which can be processed by subsequent rules. The original file name from which the page was
extracted will be stored in the ParentImage variable, for possible future reference within
your application.
If the configured output image format and compression
only supports black and white, such as CCITT4, colored text is
exported as black and background shading will be set to white.
ExcelPrintQuality(200)
ExcelTiffCompression(CCITT4)
ExcelWorkbookToImage()
This example configures the DPI and compression for the Excel workbook to TIF conversion.
Then the ExcelWorkbookToImage action converts the file associated with the current DCO object to multiple TIF images, one
image for each page. New DCO page objects are created for each page and subsequent rules
can be run on these pages to perform other tasks such as fingerprinting,
classification, recognition and export.
method.lvl:
Page or Document level.
If called on a page level object, then each new single page TIF file created from the source
Excel file will be associated with a new DCO page object that is at the same level as the parent DCO page
from which the page was created.
If called on a document level object, then each new single page TIF file will be associated
with a new DCO page object that is a child page of the parent document object.
For example, if the file is associated with a page object, then the DCO structure
will be created like this example:
˂page "Other"˃ TM000001.xlsx (source page object)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000002.tif (new page object, page 1 of TM000001.xlsx)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000003.tif (new page object, page 2 of TM000001.xlsx)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000004.tif (new page object, page 3 of TM000001.xlsx)
˂page "Other"˃ TM000005.tif (new page object, page 4 of TM000001.xlsx)
If the file is associated with a document object, then the DCO structure would
be created like this example:
˂Document "Invoice"˃ TM000001.xlsx (source document object)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000002.tif (new page object, page 1 of TM000001.xlsx)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000003.tif (new page object, page 2 of TM000001.xlsx)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000004.tif (new page object, page 3 of TM000001.xlsx)
- ˂page "Other"˃ TM000005.tif (new page object, page 4 of TM000001.xlsx)
method.ret:
True,
if the file is successfully converted to a TIFF document.
False,
if the current page is not an Excel Workbook or if there is a failure in the conversion.
If the number of input files/pages exceeds the maximum allowed or
if there is a failure in the conversion, the batch will be set to abort.

method.name: ExcelWorkbookToPdf
method.qi: Converts *.xls or *.xlsx files to PDF document format.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
If the current page is an Excel Workbook, this action will create a searchable PDF file using the text from the original document.
Unlike the standard conversion to image actions, this action does not create a new page object in the dco. It only updates the IMAGEFILE variable to point to the newly created PDF file.
By default the produced PDF documents are compliant with the Pdf15 standard.
To create PDF documents compliant with the PdfA1b standard, set the variable "targetPdfCompliance" to "1".
Note:
The "targetPdfCompliance" variable must to be set to the desired value prior to calling the conversion
action, on the same DCO object level, in order for the setting to take effect.
ExcelWorkbookToPdf()
method.ret:
True,
if the file is successfully converted to a PDF document.
False,
if the current page is not an Excel Document or if there is a failure in the conversion.
If the number of input files/pages exceeds the maximum allowed or
if there is a failure in the conversion, the batch will be set to abort.

method.name: ExcelPrintQuality
method.qi: Adjusts the resolution of the image output by ExcelWorkbookToImage.
method.ap: dpi : A single positive numeric value for the dots per inch (dpi) of the output image.
method.h:
Sets the resolution of the output image for ExcelWorkbookToImage.
If this action is not called, the default value of 200 dpi will be used.
Typically, input documents for recognition are 200 dpi.
ExcelPrintQuality(200)
ExcelWorkbookToImage()

method.name: ExcelTiffCompression
method.qi: Sets the compression used in the TIFF output by ExcelWorkbookToImage.
method.ap:
tiffCompression is one of the following values to set the TIFF compression:
NONE
– A color image with no compression.
LZW
– A color image using LZW compression.
CCITT4
- A black and white image with fax CCITT4 compression.
method.h:
Sets the compression of the output image from ExcelWorkbookToImage.
If this action is not called, the default value of CCITT4 will be used.
Typically, input documents for recognition are black and white with fax compression.
ExcelTiffCompression("CCITT4")
ExcelWorkbookToImage()
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment
method.qi: Converts a *.msg or *.eml file to a page or pages in TIFF format.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
If the current page is an Outlook Message, the file will be converted to multiple TIFF files,
one TIFF file for each page within the Message, based on the settings of the other
Outlook actions that configure the conversion settings.
A copy of the original MSG file without attachments is created and converted to TIFF as well.
Each new TIFF will also have a new page created within the application environment
which can be processed by subsequent rules. The original file name from which the page was
extracted will be stored in the ParentImage variable, for possible future reference within
your application.
Each attachment or embedded image within the e-mail will be removed from the e-mail and placed on disk. A new page
entry will be created for each attachment that can be processed by rules.
If the configured output image format and compression
only supports black and white, such as CCITT4, colored text is
exported as black.
OutlookPrintQuality(200)
OutlookTiffCompression("CCITT4")
OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment()
This example converts the email file associated with the current DCO object to multiple TIF images, one
image for each page. New DCO page objects are created for each page and subsequent rules
can be run on these pages to perform other tasks such as fingerprinting,
classification, recognition and export.
method.ret:
True,
if the file is successfully converted to a TIFF document.
False,
if the current page is not an Outlook Message or if there is a failure in the conversion.
If the number of input files/pages exceeds the maximum allowed or if there is a failure in the conversion, the
batch will be set to abort.
method.see: Read the top level help topic for more information on this action library.

method.name: OutlookMessageToAttachmentOnly
method.qi: Extracts attachments from *.msg or *.eml to pages without converting the MSG to a TIFF.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
If the current page is an Outlook Message, the attachments within the message
will be saved as separate files.
Each attachment or embedded image within the e-mail will be removed from the e-mail and placed on disk. A new page
entry will be created for each attachment that can be processed by subsequent rules.
The original file name from which the page was
extracted will be stored in the ParentImage variable, for possible future reference within
your application.
The saved attachments can then be further processed by running rules on the newly created objects.
For example, if attachments are PDFs, they could be converted to separate TIF images. If the attachments
are ZIP files, then a subsequent call to ZipUnPack can extract the files from the ZIP file so they can
be processed further.
OutlookMessageToAttachmentOnly()
This example converts the attachments in the current email file associated with the current DCO object to multiple files, one
image for each page. New DCO page objects are created for each page and subsequent rules
can be run on these pages to perform other tasks such as fingerprinting,
classification, recognition and export.
method.ret:
True,
if the attachments are successfully extracted from the message, or if the message contains no
attachments.
False,
if the current page is not an Outlook Message or if there is a failure in the conversion.
If the number of input files/pages exceeds the maximum allowed or
if there is a failure in the conversion, the batch will be set to abort.
method.see: OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment

method.name: OutlookPrintQuality
method.qi: Adjusts the resolution of the image output by OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment.
method.ap: dpi : A single positive numeric value for the dots per inch (dpi) of the output image.
method.h:
Sets the resolution of the output image for OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment.
If this action is not called, the default value of 200 dpi will be used.
Typically, input documents for recognition are 200 dpi.
OutlookPrintQuality(200)
OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment()

method.name: OutlookTiffCompression
method.qi: Sets the compression used in the TIFF output by OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment.
method.ap:
tiffCompression : A parameter of one of the following values to set the TIFF compression:
NONE
– A color image with no compression.
LZW
– A color image using LZW compression.
CCITT4
- A black and white image with fax CCITT4 compression.
method.h:
Sets the compression of the output image from OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment.
If this action is not called, the default value of CCITT4 will be used.
Typically, input documents for recognition are black and white with fax compression.
OutlookTiffCompression("CCITT4")
OutlookMessageToImageAndAttachment()
method.ret:
Always
True.
