: The received date stamp on the email.
Each email attachment (page) will have the following variables set:
TYPE
: Always set to "Other".
IMAGEFILE
: The name of the attachment as saved on disk.
ATTACHNAME
: The name of the attachment.
The following batch level variable is created:
EmailCount
: The number of emails scanned into the batch.
Note: If the configured Done or Problem folders do not exist, the email will be moved to the Deleted Items folder.
Waiting emails are processed in blocks. The amount of emails processed in a block will be the number of
waiting emails, or the number of emails remaining from the value set in ex_max_docs, up to a maximum of 50.
After a block of emails are processed, the wait time
is checked. If the wait time has not been reached and the maximum number of emails
has not been reached, then another block of emails are processed.
If the wait time has been reached, then no more emails are input to the batch.
It is recommended that the subject line be no longer than 78 characters as this is a
common subject line length limitation. Some systems may support even shorter lengths,
truncating the subject. Our testing has been successful with lengths up to 255 characters.
It is recommended to test your settings and use lengths appropriate for your systems.
Use ex_max_docs to configure the number of emails processed per batch. The number of items
included in the batch can be different than this amount, see ex_max_docs for more details.
Important: If any concurrently running threads might be using the same account,
your EWSMail-related tasks cannot be run in a multi-threaded configuration. Instead, use single-threaded tasks only.
For information about configuring threads in Rulerunner, see Configuring Rulerunner to run tasks.
For information about the account, see ex_login_O365_OAuth_Graph.
ex_wait_time("20")
ex_abort_time("40")
ex_max_docs("50")
ex_types("jpg, tif")
ex_scan_graph()
method.ret:
Returns
False
if the operation fails, and the action will also pause before returning based on
the configured abort time configured by ex_abort_time. Otherwise,
True.
If no selected emails were available, the action returns
True
and also pauses before returning based

method.see: ex_login_O365_OAuth_Graph, ex_wait_time, ex_max_docs

method.name: ex_logout
method.qi: Disconnect from the mail server
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Closes the connection to the mail server.
Call once for each batch after ex_login and ex_scan have completed.
ex_logout()
method.lvl: Batch level Open or Close event only.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: ex_logout_graph
method.qi: Disconnect from the mail server
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Closes the connection to the Graph server.
Call once for each batch after ex_login_O365_OAuth_Graph and ex_scan_graph have completed.
ex_logout_graph()
method.lvl: Batch level Open or Close event only.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: ex_types
method.qi: Specifies valid image attachment extensions
method.ap:
extensions : A comma-separated list of file image file attachment extensions to import,
with or without period. If a blank extension is supplied, ex_scan will import messages with no attachments.
method.h:
This action specifies the allowable email attachment types.
If this action is not called, the default value of ".pdf" will be used.
If this action is called and no attachment types are specified, all emails and any attachments are added to the batch.
If attachment types are specified and the email contains:
• Only the specified attachment types, the email and attachments will be added to the batch
• Only unspecified attachment types, or if it contains a mix of specified and unspecified attachment types, the email is moved to the Problem folder
• No attachments, the email is moved to the Problem folder.
Please Note:
ex_types() action support all the standard extension which Datacap supports listed few of them below
ex_types(pdf,png,jpeg,jpg,tif,tiff,eml,msg,doc,docx,gif,xls,zip,txt,html) and many more.
ex_wait_time("20")
ex_abort_time("40")
ex_max_docs("200")
ex_types("jpg, tif")
ex_scan()
This example will cause ex_scan() to scan/extract jpg and tif extension files from mails.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: ex_wait_time
method.qi: Specifies the maximum time to wait for input emails for a single batch.
method.ap: nSecs : The maximum number of seconds to wait.
method.h:
The maximum time to wait for input files for a single batch.
Used by the ex_scan action after the first email has been processed to determine how long to
wait for the batch to fill up.
The import of emails into the batch will stop when the
wait limit is reached or when the maximum emails per batch has been reached.
While waiting for new mail to arrive, the mailbox will be polled every two seconds to
check for waiting mail. The action will continue to include new emails into the batch
until this wait time is reached or the maximum number of emails per batch is reached.
If this action is not called, the default wait time of 5 seconds will be used.
ex_wait_time("20")
ex_scan()
This example causes the scan operation to wait for 20 seconds for additional email,
after processing the first email, before finishing the scan operation.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: ex_scan

method.name: ex_abort_time
method.qi: Specifies the delay time before returning when a batch aborts.
method.ap: nSecs : The number of seconds to wait.
method.h:
The action will wait the specified time before returning when an abort occurs.
This action can be useful to prevent a large number of aborted batches due to
an abort condition. For example, if the email server should become unavailable
for a time, the abort timeout will limit the amount of aborted batches until
the mail server becomes available again.
If this action is not called, the default value of 30 seconds will be used.
ex_wait_time("20")
ex_abort_time("60")
ex_max_docs("200")
ex_scan
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: ex_scan

method.name: ex_max_docs
method.qi: Specifies maximum number of emails to include in a single batch.

p.name: nDocs
p.qi: The maximum number of emails in a batch.

method.ap: nDocs : The maximum number of emails in a batch.
method.h:
The import of emails into the batch will stop when this email limit is reached
or when the maximum wait time has been reached. While waiting for new mail to arrive,
the configured mailbox will be polled every two seconds to check for waiting mail.
If this action is not called, the default value of 100 will be used.
The actual amount of emails included in the batch could be less than this maximum.
Note: The value indicates the number of emails with expected attachments that will be processed.
If a waiting email contains an unexpected attachment, it is not counted against the
total maximum count.
It is also possible for an email to contain more than one valid attachment type. When this happens,
it is possible for the number of items input to the batch can be greater than the number
of configured emails. For example, if ex_max_docs is set to 5 and if there are 5 waiting
emails and each email has 2 attachments, the total number of attachments that will be
included in the batch will be 10.
ex_max_docs("50")
ex_scan()
This example causes the scan operation to limit the number of emails in a
batch to a maximum of 50.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: ex_scan

method.name: ex_done_folder
method.qi: Specifies folder for successfully imported emails

p.name: folder
p.qi: Destination folder for successfully imported emails

method.ap: folder : Destination folder for successfully imported emails
method.h:
Specifies the name of the email folder into which successfully imported emails are placed.
This folder must be a subfolder of the email account's Inbox.
When an email is processed and the attachment is imported, the email is moved
to the folder name specified by this action.
If this action is not called, the default value of "Done" will be used.
ex_done_folder("Imported")
ex_problem_folder("Failed")
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: ex_scan

method.name: ex_problem_folder
method.qi: Specifies folder for problem emails

p.name: folder
p.qi: Destination folder for problem email

method.ap: folder : Destination folder for problem email
method.h:
When an email is processed and the attachment is not one of the expected types,
the email is moved to the folder name specified by this action.
This folder must be a subfolder of the email account's Inbox.
If this action is not called, the default value of "Problem" will be used.
ex_done_folder("Imported")
ex_problem_folder("Failed")
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: ex_scan

method.name: ex_EMLOption
method.qi: Creates a one page document per email containing an .eml file.

p.name: folder
p.qi: Optional - use a nonzero value to store one .eml file per email.

method.ap: folder : Optional - use a nonzero value to store one .eml file per email.
method.h:
If set, the ex_scan action creates a one page document containing the email and
attachments in an .eml file; no attachment pages are created.
When called with a non-zero parameter, the ex_scan function does
not create pages for each attachment, instead one page is created per email document,
containing an .eml file suitable for subsequent processing using eDocument Conversion actions.
When you use this action, pages for attachments are not created, and variables for those attachments are not set.
ex_EMLOption("1")
ex_scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: ex_scan

method.name: ex_AcceptMixedAttachments
method.qi: Ingest emails with selected attachment types, even if non-selected attachment types are included

p.name: bMixedOK
p.qi: A boolean value that enables ingestion of emails with both allowed and disallowed attachment types

method.ap:
True:
An email message with an attachment type not specified by ex_types will be ingested as long as it contains some desired attachment. But, only attachment type specified by ex_types will be extracted.
False:
An email message with any disallowed attachment will be rejected. This is the default process if this action is never called.
method.h:
If this action is never called, the presence of any attachment not specified by ex_types will cause ex_scan to treat that email message as a "Problem".
If this action is called with parameter True, messages with disallowed attachment types are ingested as long as they contain at least one allowed attachment. From ingested, only allowed attachment types will be processed.
If ex_types is called with a blank parameter prior to ex_scan, all emails are ingested, so this action has no effect.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: ex_AcceptNoAttachments
method.qi: Ingest emails without attachments, even if attachment types are specified

p.name: bNoAttachOK
p.qi: A boolean value that enables ingestion of emails with no attachments

method.ap:
True:
An email message with no attachments will be ingested by ex_scan.
False:
An email message no attachments will be rejected by ex_scan, unless ex_types has been called with a blank parameter. This is the default behavoir if this action is never called.
method.h:
If this action is never called, the absence of an attachment will cause ex_scan to treat that email message as a "Problem".
If this action is called with parameter True, messages with no attachments are ingested.
If ex_types is called with a blank parameter prior to ex_scan, all emails are ingested, so this action has no effect.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: ex_login_O365_OAuth
method.qi: Login to Office 365 with OAuth using EWS.
method.ap:
clientId : Application (client) ID from Azure Active Directory - App registrations
tenantId : Directory (tenant) ID from Azure Active Directory - App registrations
username : Username of Office 365 account
password : Password of Office 365 account
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
Parameters (clientId, tenantId, username, password) can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager.
To retrieve parameters that is stored in the Advanced section,
use a smart parameter for the action's parameters similar to
@APPVAR(values/adv/password) where password is the name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
To use OAuth authentication service provided by Azure Active Directory to enable EWS to access Exchange Online in Office 365, you will need to:
1) Register application with Azure Active Directory.
2) For Authentication, under "Default client type", set "Yes" to "Treat application as a public client."
3) For API permissions, add "Exchange - EWS.AccessAsUser.All" and grant consent.
ex_login_O365_OAuth("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa", "user@organization.com", "@APPVAR(values/adv/password)")
ex_scan()
ex_logout()
If more than one logins (ex_login, ex_login_O365_OAuth or ex_login_O365_OAuth_ClientSecret) are used, second action will be ignored unless authentication fails/expires or ex_logout() was used before the second action to disconnect.
method.see: ex_login

method.name: ex_login_O365_OAuth_Graph
method.qi: Login to Office 365 with OAuth using Microsoft Graph API.
method.ap:
clientId : Application (client) ID from Azure Active Directory - App registrations
tenantId : Directory (tenant) ID from Azure Active Directory - App registrations
username : Username of Office 365 account
password : Password of Office 365 account
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
Parameters (clientId, tenantId, username, password) can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager.
To retrieve parameters that is stored in the Advanced section,
use a smart parameter for the action's parameters similar to
@APPVAR(values/adv/password) where password is the name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
To use OAuth authentication service provided by Azure Active Directory to enable Microsoft Graph, you will need to:
1) Register application with Azure Active Directory.
2) For Authentication, under "Default client type", set "Yes" to "Treat application as a public client."
3) For API permissions, add a request API permission for Microsoft Graph and Grant consent for Mail.ReadWrite".
ex_login_O365_OAuth_Graph("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa", "user@organization.com", "@APPVAR(values/adv/password)")
ex_scan_graph()
ex_logout_graph()
If more than one logins (ex_login_O365_OAuth_Graph) are used, second action will be ignored unless authentication fails/expires or ex_logout_graph() was used before the second action to disconnect.
method.see: ex_login

method.name: ex_login_O365_OAuth_ClientSecret
method.qi: Login to Office 365 with OAuth with Client Secret using EWS.
method.ap:
clientId : Application (client) ID from Azure Active Directory - App registrations
tenantId : Directory (tenant) ID from Azure Active Directory - App registrations
clientSecret : Client Secret from Azure Active Directory - App registrations
impersonatedUserId : User ID of Office 365 account to impersonate
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
Parameters (clientId, tenantId, clientSecret, impersonatedUserId) can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager.
To retrieve parameters that is stored in the Advanced section,
use a smart parameter for the action's parameters similar to
@APPVAR(values/adv/clientSecret) where clientSecret is the name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
To use OAuth authentication service provided by Azure Active Directory to enable EWS to access Exchange Online in Office 365, you will need to:
1) Register application with Azure Active Directory.
2) For Certificates & secrets, under "Client secrets", click "New client secret" to "Add" and get "Value."
3) For API permissions, add "full_access_as_app" and grant consent.
ex_login_O365_OAuth_ClientSecret("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000", "aaaaaaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaa-aaaaaaaaaaaa", "@APPVAR(values/adv/clientSecret)", "user@organization.com")
ex_scan()
ex_logout()
If more than one logins (ex_login, ex_login_O365_OAuth or ex_login_O365_OAuth_ClientSecret) are used, second action will be ignored unless authentication fails/expires or ex_logout() was used before the second action to disconnect.
method.see: ex_login

method.name: ex_SetProxy
method.qi: Allows optional specification of proxy service settings.
method.ap:
proxyURL : URL or IP address of proxy service.
proxyPort : The proxy service connection port.
proxyUsername : Username for the proxy server.
proxyPassword : Password for the proxy server.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
The password can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager.
The URL and user name parameters can be stored in the General section of the Datacap Application Manager but they cannot be encrypted.
To retrieve the password that is stored in the Advanced section,
use a smart parameter for the action's password parameter similar to
@APPVAR(values/adv/mailProxyPassword) where mailProxyPassword is the name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
Optionally sets the values to a proxy service that will be used to connect to the email server.
This action does not confirm that the connection to the proxy service is successful. Connection to the
proxy service will not occur until the ex_login action is called.
If this action is used, it must be called prior to the ex_login action. If this action is not
called, then no proxy service will be used.
ex_SetProxy("https://proxyurl.com", "8080", "proxyusername", "@APPVAR(values/adv/mailProxyPassword)")
ex_login("https://mailserver.com/ews/exchange.asmx", "username@domain.com", "password")
This example sets up the parameters to use a proxy and then performs the login.
The parameter for the password is an example smart parameter that obtains the password
from an advanced value in the application service.
method.ret:
False,
if the proxyPort is not numeric, otherwise
True.
method.see: ex_login

method.qi: Allows optional specification of proxy service settings with Full URL.
method.ap:
proxyFullURL : Full URL of proxy service.
proxyUsername : Username for the proxy server.
proxyPassword : Password for the proxy server.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
The password can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager.
The URL and user name parameters can be stored in the General section of the Datacap Application Manager but they cannot be encrypted.
To retrieve the password that is stored in the Advanced section,
use a smart parameter for the action's password parameter similar to
@APPVAR(values/adv/mailProxyPassword) where mailProxyPassword is the name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
Optionally sets the values to a proxy service that will be used to connect to the email server.
This action does not confirm that the connection to the proxy service is successful. Connection to the
proxy service will not occur until the ex_login action is called.
If this action is used, it must be called prior to the ex_login action. If this action is not
called, then no proxy service will be used.
ex_SetProxy("https://proxyurl.com:8080/proxy.url", "proxyusername", "@APPVAR(values/adv/mailProxyPassword)")
ex_login("https://mailserver.com/ews/exchange.asmx", "username@domain.com", "password")
This example sets up the parameters to use a proxy and then performs the login.
The parameter for the password is an example smart parameter that obtains the password
from an advanced value in the application service.
method.ret:
False,
if proxy settings fails, otherwise
True.
method.see: ex_login

method.name: ex_SetTopFolder
method.qi: Sets the top folder where search would start

p.name: root
p.qi: A boolean value that sets the top folder to root

method.ap:
True:
Searches done/problem folder from the root of the mailbox.
False:
Searches done/problem folder from the Inbox folder.
method.h:
If this action is never called, ex_done_folder and ex_problem_folder search starts from the Inbox folder. (Default)
If this action is called with parameter True, ex_done_folder and ex_problem_folder search starts from the root of the mailbox.
ex_SetTopFolder("true")

Always

com.qi: Saves batch data into a database.
com.h:
The ExportToDatabase action library used to export the page level and field level values into a table in the Database.
Typically, exporting data to a database is the last step in a successful batch process.
The action DatabaseOpenConnection connects to a database using the connection string.
Subsequent export actions then use the open database connection for their work.
Similarly DatabaseCloseConnection will close the existing open connection.
Note:
The ExportToDatabase Action library is 64-bit action library.
Ensure the 64 bit database (db2, Microsoft Access, SQL Server, Oracle) driver is installed properly.
Microsoft Access is only supported for development in a single rulerunner environment. It is not supported for production.
The ExportToDatabase actions only support use within a single rulerunner. A profile using these actions
must only be run by one rulerunner.
SetTableName:
The action SetTableName confirms that the table name which is passed to action is present in database or not if not, then this action will return False.
This action must be called before exporting the any values into the table.
In the example below, the action checks if the Export Results table is present in the database or not.
If not, then action returns false. If present, the action returns true and then processing moves to next action.
SetTableName("Export_Results")
ExportFieldToColumn("MyDate", "db_Date")
AddRecord()
ExportToColumn:
ExportToColumn is a field-level action that exports the captured value of the current Field object from the page's Data file to a target column
within a previously designated table of an open Export database.
ExportFieldToColumn:
Action ExportFieldToColumn is a page-level action that extracts the captured value of a Field object from the Data file of the current page,
and specifies its target location within a table of the Export database.
For Example:
SetTableName("Export Results")
ExportFieldToColumn("VendorID","db_Number","2")
ExportFieldToColumn("Date","db_Date")
ExportFieldToColumn("Total","db_Total")
AddRecord()
AddRecord:
The AddRecord action inserts assembled data into the database SetTableName("Invoice")
ExportFieldToColumn("VendorID","db_Vendor")
ExportFieldToColumn("Number","db_Number")
ExportFieldToColumn("Total","db_Total")
AddRecord()
⟸ ♕ Generating Statistics ♕ ⟹
The statistics actions are used to calculate the page classification count and recognition count. The counts are stored in runtime DCO.
The statistics actions utilize the DatabaseOpenConnection and DatabaseCloseConnection actions,
but do not require the use of any of the other export actions.
There are situations where classification or recognized text changes conditionally.
For example, recognized field text can be changed by "cleaning" rulesets or
by a verification operator.
This action library identifies that values that has been changed and counts them
counted as recognition errors or page classification errors.
The page type must be set, and a recognition action must be called, and field values populated, prior to calling
any of these actions Recognize action should be called before calling any of these actions.
SaveFieldsRecognizedText must be called prior to any cleaning actions or user verification.
The saving of statistics data can be controlled in the application manager.
The check box
Save Statistics
can be checked or unchecked, which sets the application manager entry "SaveReportStatistics".
This value can be then used in the ruleset to control the call of Statistics actions.
For Example:
rrCompareCase("@APPVAR(SaveReportStatistics)", "True", "False")
SaveFieldsText("")
In the example, the application logic first checks if the application is configured
to save statistics information. If so, it then calls the statistics action.
The following are the typical logical steps performed when using the statistics actions. These
steps are not all performed in a single task:
1. Perform recognition and populate fields.
2. Call the action StatisticsSaveFieldsText.
3. The verify operator has performed verification on page types and field recognition results.
4. Call the action StatisticsCompareFieldsText.
5. Call the action DatabaseOpenDatabase.
6. Perform any necessary actions to export batch data using the ExportToDatabase actions.
7. Call the action StatisticsAddToDatabaseTotals.
8. Call the action ExportCloseDatabase.
⟸ ♕ The Datacap Document Object Hierarchy (DCO) ♕ ⟹
Applications are created with a "Setup DCO" and each batch has a unique "Runtime DCO".
The DCO is explained in the top-level help of the ApplicationObject action library.
⟸ ♕ Smart Parameters ♕ ⟹
Smart parameters are a syntactic way of specifying action parameters that are resolved at runtime,
allowing dynamic input of data to actions. The complete smart parameter reference is available
in the top-level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library.

method.name: AddRecord
method.qi: Inserts assembled data into the database table specified by a previous SetTableName action.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Inserts assembled data into the database table specified by a previous
SetTableName
action.
Important:
This action must be placed after earlier actions that open the database, gather data, and access the correct table.
SetTableName("Invoice")
ExportFieldToColumn("VendorID","db_Vendor")
ExportFieldToColumn("Number","db_Number")
ExportFieldToColumn("Total","db_Total")
AddRecord()
This ExportDB rule applies to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy.
The actions open the database and direct the rule's attention to the Invoice table.
The rule then sets up a record with three values - Vendor ID, Invoice Number and Total.
Afterwards, the AddRecord action updates the table with new information.
Note: A return of False means the record may not have been successfully exported,
and needs to be followed by a "failure check" rule that typically would call
SetTaskStatus(0), or the RuleRunnerLogic action SetTaskAbortBatch, to ensure that the batch aborts.
method.lvl: All, but generally used at the Page or Field level.
method.ret:
False
if there is no connection to the database; if an error occurs when the action
attempts to add the record to the database; or if a SetTableName action was not previously used.
Otherwise,
True
.
method.see: SetTableName, ExportFieldToColumn

method.name: DatabaseCloseConnection
method.qi: Closes an open connection to your Export database.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Closes an open connection to the previously opened Export database.
Usually, this action is placed in a ruleset that is separate from the ruleset that opens
the connection and stores the data.
For example, this action could be placed into a ruleset called ExportDBClose,
and attached to a batch level close event which executes after all data has been
exported from the batch to the specified database.
DatabaseCloseConnection()
This action closes the previously opened connection to the Export database.
This action is usually part of a separate ruleset that prevents the need to repeatedly
open the connection to the Export database. (You can open the connection once in the first
ruleset, export data from all documents and pages in the batch, then close the connection once
in the second ruleset.) The database must be opened, used and closed all within
the same task profile. You cannot open the connection in one task profile and then
expect to use the connection in a different task profile.
method.lvl: All, but generally used as part of a separate ruleset at the Batch level.
method.ret:
True,
even if the connection is already closed.
method.see: DatabaseOpenConnection

method.name: DatabaseOpenConnection
method.qi: Opens a connection to the database specified as the parameter.
method.ap:
The Connection String of the target Export database.
Use smart parameters to retrieve the connection from the application manager
to avoid clear text passwords in your application.
method.h:
Opens a connection to the database specified as the parameter.
A rule containing this action can apply to any object of the Document Hierarchy (DCO), but it is most often used at the batch level.
This action connects to the database using a 64 bit connection.
The proper 64 bit client interface must be available for the target database.
DatabaseOpenConnection("@APPVAR(*/exportdb:cs)")
Note:
This action must come before any other ExportToDatabase actions. This example
uses smart parameters to obtain the connection string from the application service
where the custom connection string key "exportdb" has been created in the "Custom Values" tab.
It provides a single location for the connection string and security for passwords.
If necessary, multiple custom variables can be created to connect to different databases.
Note:
If the action is establishing a connection with an Oracle database,
or an SQL Server database using SQL Server Authentication, be sure to expand the DSN parameter
by adding the correct Provider, user ID and Password. For example:
Access:
DatabaseOpenConnection("Provider=Microsoft.ACE.OLEDB.12.0;Data Source=C:\Datacap\TravelDocs\TravelDocsExport.mdb;Persist Security Info=False;")
Access databases are not supported in a production environment.
Oracle:
DatabaseOpenConnection("PROVIDER=OraOLEDB.Oracle;Data Source=1040Look;ID=Admin;Password=Admin;")
SQL Server:
DatabaseOpenConnection("PROVIDER=ODBCMSSQL;DSN=1040Look;CATALOG=;DBNTA=;UID=Admin;PWD=Admin;")
DB2:
Provider=IBMDADB2;Data Source=MYDB2SOURCE;UID=user;PWD=password
Note:
Although the examples show the full connection string, it is recommended that a smart
parameter is used to obtain the connection string from the application service, as shown in the first example,
to provide password security and application portability.
method.lvl: All, but generally used at the Batch level.
method.see: DatabaseCloseConnection

method.name: SetTableName
method.qi: Sets the name of the table in your database to which the data is to be exported.
method.ap:
TableName.
The name of the database table where the exported data will be inserted.
The action confirm that the supplied table name is valid. If the table name is not valid, SetTableName will return False.
Note that this value causes an extra database call so it is typically specified only during development,
not in a production system as it will increase the number of database calls and running time.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets the name of the table in your database to which the data is to be exported. This action needs to be used before the AddRecord action.
SetTableName("Export_Results")
ExportFieldToColumn("MyDate", "db_Date")
AddRecord()
method.ret:
Returns
False
only if the first parameter contains an invalid table name and a value of 1 is specified as a second parameter.
Otherwise, this action always returns
True.
method.see: AddRecord

method.name: ExportBatchIDToColumn
method.qi: Stores the current batch ID into the database.
method.ap:
Column.
The name of the database column that will hold the value.
SQLFormatValue.
Optional: Can be set to the numerical value of 1, 2, or 3.
If this parameter is not specified, quotes will be placed around the value in the SQL query to update the table.
Setting the value to 1 causes this action to return False if the Table name is invalid;
otherwise, the error will not be discovered until the action that performs the DB insert call,
such as an AddRecord action, is called. This value would typically
only be used in a development environment as it will increase processing time.
Setting this value to 2 allows NULL column values and inserts no quotes around values (for numeric) in the SQL query to update the database.
Setting the value to 3 allows NULL and if the column value is not NULL,
the column value will be surrounded in quotes in the SQL query to update the database.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Exports the current Batch ID to the database column specified by the parameter. The action also has an optional query format parameter with two values.
SetTableName("Export_Results")
ExportBatchIDToColumn("db_BatchID","1")
ExportFieldToColumn("Date","db_Date")
ExportFieldToColumn("Total","db_Total")
AddRecord()
method.lvl: All, but generally at the Page or Field level.
method.ret:
False
if the second parameter is set to "1" and the parameters do not identify a
valid database column. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: AddRecord, ExportFieldToColumn, ExportPropertyToColumn

method.ap:

Setting this value to 2 allows NULL column values and inserts no quotes around values (for numeric) in the SQL query to update the database.

method.h:

Optionally, it can assign a query format to the action.
Batch Level:

Current field:

Last Field:
AddRecord()

if:

method.h:
