method.name: StatisticsAddToDatabaseTotals
method.qi: Calculates page type classification and field recognition accuracy statistics.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Updates the application summary statistics in the reportTotal table with this batch's totals.
Once this action executes successfully it sets batch variable TotalStatsUpdated to avoid double-counting.
DatabaseOpenConnection must be called prior to using this action. ExportCloseConnection must be called after all export database
actions have completed in the current task profile. If a connection to the database has not been made,
this action will attempt to open the database using the default database connection "@APPVAR(values/dsn/exportdb:cs)"
but the action ExportCloseConnection must still be called in the same task profile,
once the database is no longer needed.
Before StatisticsAddToDatabaseTotals updates the database, it checks the DCO variable TotalStatsUpdated to confirm that statistics
have not yet been saved for the current batch.
Once this action executes successfully it sets batch variable TotalStatsUpdated to avoid double-counting within the database.
This action saves the data in Application Engine Database ReportTotal table.
The database column rt_featureCount1 and rt_TotalSizeKB are updated by this action.
The field rt_featureCount1 will be updated only when there is a change observed in the recognition of page or fields.
The rt_TotalSizeKB field will store the size of Batch Directory.
This action does not perform any updates in the reportBatch table.
StatisticsAddToDatabaseTotals()
method.ret:
False,
if the database connection does not exist or if an error occurs. Otherwise,
True.
If the database connection does not exist, the batch will be set to the "Abort" state.
method.see:
StatisticsCompareFieldsText, StatisticsSaveFieldsText.
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general information about exporting batch statistics.

method.name: StatisticsCompareFieldsText
method.qi: Calculates page type classification and field recognition accuracy statistics.

p.name: SaveStatusVariableName
p.qi: Optional. If provided, the action will also save the object status using the variable name provided.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Call this action after data verification to calculate accuracy based on the changes to data during verification.
The StatisticsSaveFieldsText action must have previously run after the recognition has been performed, but before operator verification.
If the verify operator has corrected any of the recognized fields, this action will count the number of fields that have been changed.
The saved values that were generated by StatisticsSaveFieldsText, are compared with the values that exist after operator verification,
calculating accuracy statistics.
All pages within the batch, and all fields on all pages, are processed by this action.
Batch variables are populated with accuracy values:
PageClassifiedErrors: the number of page classification errors (page type changed after auto-classification).
PageClassifiedCount: the number of pages classified in this batch.
FieldRecognitionCount: the number of fields with recognized text.
FieldRecognitionErrors: the number of fields that were incorrectly recognized (text values were changed after recognition).
FieldAccuracyPct: Field recognition accuracy percentage.
ClassifyAccuracyPct: Classification accuracy percentage.
The action processes all pages and fields to calculate the values of the listed variables but takes no further action.
This action does not
have any interaction with the database, it simply prepares data for later processing, saving results in batch level variables.
It is not necessary to open the connection to the export database before using this action.
The action compares the original page type classification with the final value after verification. Any differences that have
occurred are counted. The calculation will be done for only those pages which were classified correctly and
have a variable
ClassifiedPageType
in DCO xml added by the action SaveFieldsRecognizedText.
Following are the variables added in runtime DCO file by this action:
PageClassifiedErrors :
The variable contains the page classification errors count (page type changed after auto-classification).
It compares the saved value in ClassifiedPageType with the current type of page.
If the value of the variable and type of page is different it is assumed the page type is changed after auto-classification and the count of PageClassifiedErrors variable will be increased.
PageClassifiedCount :
The variable stores the total number of pages classified in this batch.
The count compares the saved value in ClassifiedPageType which was added by the action SaveFieldsRecognizedText.
The page type classified as Other is considered as not classified or incorrectly classified.
FieldRecognitionCount :
The variable stores the total number of fields that were recognized.
The count is based on the variable RecognizedText, that was added by a previous call to the action SaveFieldsRecognizedText.
FieldRecognitionErrors :
The variable stores the number of fields that were incorrectly recognized, meaning it was changed after recognition.
It compares the value in variable RecognizedText with the current field object text.
If values are different, it is assumed that the value of the current field object is changed after recognition and the count of the variable FieldRecognitionErrors will be increased.
FieldAccuracyPct :
Field Accuracy Percentage calculates the percentage of field recognition accuracy using the value of the variable FieldRecognitionCount and FieldRecognitionErrors.
ClassifyAccuracyPct :
Classify Accuracy Percentage calculates the percentage of page classification accuracy using the value of the variable PageClassifiedCount and PageClassifiedErrors.
This action must be called as a final step before submitting the results to the database with the action StatisticsAddToDatabaseTotals.
StatisticsCompareFieldsText("")
These are the logical steps that must be performed in previous tasks before calling StatisticsCompareFieldsText()
Perform recognition and populate fields.
Call the action StatisticsSaveFieldsText.
The verify operator has performed verification on page types and field recognition results.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: StatisticsSaveFieldsText

method.name: StatisticsSaveFieldsText
method.qi: Stores the current recognition and page classification results prior to verification.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Call this action after page classification and OCR recognition, but before verification, to save the original recognized data for statistics calculations.
Information is stored within page and field variables allowing the contents to be saved or later compared to the results after verification.
All pages within the batch, and all fields on all pages, are processed by this action.
The classification type of each page is stored in page variable "ClassifiedPageType".
The recognized text value of each field is stored in field variable "RecognizedText".
In a second step, in a later profile, these variables will be checked by the action StatisticsCompareFieldsText
and compared to the current values to determine if the verification operator has changed
any page type classifications or has updated recognized field text on each page.
This action does not
perform any interaction with the database, it simply prepares data for later processing, saving results in batch level variables.
It is not necessary to open the connection to the export database before using this action.
StatisticsSaveFieldsText()
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: StatisticsCompareFieldsText

com.qi: : Creates a plain text data file using application data
com.h:
The ExportToText action library provides actions that will export field values, DCO variables,
batch information and other text to a plain text export file. The export file can be in a UTF-8 or UTF-16
format.
The application can control the name of the export file and its location. If the export file is written
to a shared folder, then the export file name should be unique using the batch ID or other identifier that
is guaranteed to be unique so one batch does not overwrite the export file from a different batch.
Once created, the file can be moved or sent to an external repository using subsequent Datacap actions.
Alternatively, the export file can be saved in a directory that will be picked up by an external process.
If an external process is picking up the exported file, it is up to the application designer to ensure that
the external process does not try to pick up the file prior to it being completely written out to disk.
An application can create any number of export files. There can be multiple plain text files created with this
action library or other export files can be created in addition to the plain text file created by this action library.
The format of the file and the data to include in the file is up to the application designer. The text can be lines without
any specific length, the file can be created as a comma separated file, fixed length data, or any combination of these
types.
The approach to creating a text file is to first identify the name and location of the file. This information can
be provided dynamically at runtime, allowing for a file to be named with the batch ID, date stamp, time stamp, etc.
The file information is typically provided on a batch open, but can be provided at any level.
Once the file name and location has been provided, the actions can then be called to export data as needed. Data can be
exported from any type of object: batch, document, page or field, but specific actions may only support being called
on certain types of objects.
A typical operation would be to export data at field level. By using export actions on the page level node to export
the field data, or actions on the field level, as the rules engine iterates through each Datacap object within
the application, the plain text file can be built, piece by piece. For example, if CSV output is enabled, each field
can be output and as each field is placed into the output file, the actions will automatically add commas between
each exported field, with an end result of all of the fields in a line of text, separated by commas, or any desired
separator character. At the last field, the action StartNewLine can be called to indicate that when the next
action is called to write to the file, it will be placed on a new line. If there are multiple pages being exported
into the file, then it will have the result of placing the field data for page 1 on the first line, the field data
for page 2 on the next line, the field data for page 3 on the next line, etc. The placement of the actions and the
DCO nodes they are attached to will determine the format of the output file.
Even if an export action is configured to export a field, the export of that field can be configured
to be skipped at runtime based on the value of the DCO variable NOEXPORT or the status of the field.
Any fields that have a DCO variable called "NOEXPORT" set to the value of "1" will be
excluded from the export file, regardless of the field's status.
Once all of the data has been written, then the file needs to be closed with the CloseExportFile action. This
is typically called on the batch level close of the ruleset that performed the open, or could be at the batch level in
a subsequent ruleset. While actions can be split across multiple rulesets, when generating a file,
all of the actions called to create the file must be within the same task profile if the data
is to be included in the same export file.
The following is a simple ruleset to provide an overview of how the export actions can be used
within an application. Assuming that each page has three fields called Field1, Field2 and Field3,
this example will first create an export file named based on the current batch id, then export
the date at the top of the export file. The rest of the file will contain three
comma separated entries for each page. ExportText("@X") will export the text
value for each field. Once all of the fields of all of the pages are exported, the export
file will be closed.
BatchOpenRule
- Function
- - SetExportDirectory("@APPPATH(export)")
- - SetExportFileName("@BATCHID+.txt")
- - ExportText("Current Date: +@DATE()")
- - SetCSVMode("On")
PageOpenRule
- Function
- - StartNewLine()
Field1Rule
- Function
- - ExportText("@X")
Field2Rule
- Function
- - ExportText("@X")
Field3Rule
- Function
- - ExportText("@X")
BatchCloseRule
- Function
- - CloseExportFile()
If the fields contained names, the sample output file could look like this:
Current Date: 02/10/2025
Mary,Patricia,Linda
Barbara,Elizabeth,Jennifer
Maria,Susan,Margaret
It is recommended that the application developer understands how the Datacap object hierarchy, DCO, operates.
Information about the DCO can be found in the help for the ApplicationObjects action library.
In addition to the data processed within the batch, it is likely desired that other data also be included
in the export file such as the batch ID, date, time, job ID, and other environmental information
be saved within the export file. These values can be obtained using smart parameter notation
as input to actions. Refer to the smart parameter guide for more information on using these
types of parameters.

method.name: CloseExportFile
method.qi: Closes the currently opened export file.
method.ap: None.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.h:
Closes the currently opened Export file.
Once closed, it would be expected that if further calls are made to export data, that
a new file name is provided to the action library usin ghe SetExportFileName action.
If a subsequent export action is called to write to the file and the file name
has not been changed, the existing file will be overwritten with the new data.
This action usually belongs to its own batch level rule. However, it can be used at any level.
CloseExportFile()
In a typical application, this action will be placed on a batch close event, with the SetExportFileName and
SetExportDirectory actions called on a batch open event. This action will close the file.
method.see:
SetExportFileName, SetExportDirectory
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportAllPageFields
method.qi: Exports all field values on the current page, including values of Line Item Detail sub-fields - with exceptions.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action exports all field values of the current page. The value of each field is saved
in the export file on the same line. If CSV mode is enabled, then each field will be separated
by the configured separator character.
The action does not
export those values of field objects of the Document Hierarchy with:
1. The DCO variable NOEXPORT with a value of "1".
2. If the current status of the field matches the status configured with the action SetIgnoreFieldStatus.
ExportAllFields()
This action must be called on a page level DCO object. Each of the page's child fields
will have its text value placed into the export file.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportBlankCSVFields
method.qi: Inserts blank fields into the Export file, adjacent to the current field.
method.ap:
Count
A number indicating how many blank fields to add to the Export file.
method.h:
The
ExportBlankCSVFields
action adds the number of fields you specify. This action
only has an effect if CSV mode is enabled. It will create blank entries within the CSV file.
If this action is called on a field object, the text value of the field does not matter as only
blank entries will be created in the export file.
Note: Make sure you call SetCSVMode, and optionally SetCSVElementSeparator, to set the separator values as
desired for your export file. If neither of these actions are called before
this action, no empty fields will be exported because
the default separator is set to no separator.
SetCSVMode("On")
ExportBlankCSVFields("12")
This example will add 12 blank entries in the CSV file, such as ",,,,,,,,,,,".
Additionally, this example shows the action SetCSVMode called directly before the blank fields action.
This is for illustration. As long as the action is run prior to calling ExportBlankCSVFields, on any DCO
object, then the mode will be in effect for subsequent actions.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetSCVMode
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportCurrentField
method.qi: Exports the current field value to the Export file.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Exports the current field value to the Export file. The exported value will
be on the same line as the previous exported value, unless StartNewLine
has been called. If CSV mode has been enabled, then the value will be
preceded by the current CSV separator value.
ExportCurrentField()
This example would be called on a field object. The current text value of the field
will be added to the export file.
method.ret:
False if there is an error, otherwise
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportFillerCharacters
method.qi: Adds a string of filler characters to the Export.
method.ap:
Count
A number indicating the total length in characters of the filler.
CharacterToExport:
One or more characters to place into the export file.
This value can be a single character or multiple characters. If multiple characters
are provided, then the sequence will be repeated based on the provided count.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Adds a single or multiple filler characters to the export file, repeated by the number of times indicated in the
"Count" input parameter.
If called on a field object, the filler string is written to the file regardless of the data in the current field.
ExportFillerCharacters("4",":")
The action in the example fills the current field with 4 instances of the character ":" such as
"::::" to the export file.
ExportFillerCharacters("4","@B.MyVariable")
Similar to the previous example, however this obtains the filler text from
the DCO variable called "MyVariable" which is expected to be on the batch level DCO.
method.ret:
False
if the first parameter is not numeric or if there is an error.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportPageField
method.qi: Exports the specified Field object's value to the Export file.
method.ap:
FieldToExport:
The name of the child Field object whose value you want to export.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Exports the specified Field object's value to the Export file. Will only export the
first Field if multiple fields of the same field type are found.
The text will be exported on the same line as the previously exported text
unless StartNewLine was previously called. If CSV mode is enabled, then the data
will be exported with the configured separator character.
ExportFieldValue("Date")
ExportFieldValue("Number")
ExportFieldValue("Total")
This sequence exports the current values stored in the Date, Number and Total fields.
These fields must be children of the current page.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportPageFieldFixedLengthLeftJustified
method.qi: Exports a specified number of characters from a field's left end (left-justified.)
method.ap:
FieldToExport:
The field's name to export. This is the name of the corresponding field object of the Document Hierarchy.
the field must be a child object of the current page.
FixedLength:
All exported values will be adjusted to this length.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action exports the text value of the named field to the export file. The field
must be a child of the current page. The field will be right justified and adjusted to
the length provided. If the value is longer, it will be truncated.
If the field is shorter than the provided length, then
the exported value will be padded to the end using the current pad character
to make the value the exact length specified.
Calling this action will enable left justified, fixed length export for all subsequent
export actions.
ExportPageFieldFixedLengthLeftJustified("Volume","8")
This example assumes the current page has a field called "Volume". The text
value of that field will be added to the export file and adjusted to be 8 characters
long. If the text is shorter than 8 characters, it will be padded using the current
fill character.
method.ret:
False
if either parameter is invalid or if the action is called at the wrong level.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
ExportPageFieldFixedLengthRightJustified, SetFillCharacter
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportPageFieldFixedLengthRightJustified
method.qi: Exports a specified number of characters from a field's right end (right-justified.)
method.ap:
FieldToExport:
The field's name to export. This is the name of the corresponding field object of the Document Hierarchy.
the field must be a child object of the current page.
FixedLength:
All exported values will be adjusted to this length.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.ret:
False
if either parameter is invalid or if the action is called at the wrong level.
Otherwise,
True.
method.h:
This action exports the text value of the named field to the export file. The field
must be a child of the current page. The field will be right justified and adjusted to
the length provided. If the value is longer, it will be truncated.
If the field is shorter than the provided length, then
the exported value will be padded from the front using the current pad character
to make the value the exact length specified.
Calling this action will enable right justified, fixed length export for all subsequent
export actions.
ExportPageFieldFixedLengthRightJustified("Volume","8")
This example assumes the current page has a field called "Volume". The text
value of that field will be added to the export file and adjusted to be 8 characters
long. If the text is shorter than 8 characters, it will be padded using the current
fill character.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportText
method.qi: Exports a value to the Export file.
method.ap:
Text:
The value to export.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The provided text will be exported to the export file. It will be added to the same
line as the previous exported value unless the action StartNewLine has first
been called. If CSV mode or left / right justification has been enabled,
then this value will also be adjusted based on the settings prior to writing
to the text file.
Smart parameters are supported, providing a wide range of additional values
and locations from which data can be obtained for writing to the export file.
This action is similar to the action ExportTextNotJustified, the difference is
that this action will respect the current left or right justification
mode, if it is enabled.
ExportText("Hello There")
This example will write the text "Hello There" to the export file. The value will
be exported as CSV if the CSV mode is enabled. The value will also be adjusted
to be left or right justified, if justification mode has been enabled.
ExportText("@DATE")
This example uses a smart parameter to place the current date into the
export file.
ExportText("@BATCHID")
This example uses a smart parameter to place the current batch ID into the
export file.
ExportText("Current Operator: +@OPERATOR")
If the ID of the current operator is "Tom", then this will output the
text "Current Operator: Tom" in the export file.
ExportText("@P\MyField.MyVariable"
Assuming this is called on a page or field DCO, the smart parameter will navigate from the page
to the field called "MyField", obtain the value of the variable "MyVariable"
and write that value to the export file.
ExportText("@P\MyField")
This example is similar to the previous example, but it will instead
obtain the text value of the field "MyField" and save it in the export file.
ExportTExt("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)")
This example will place the path to the current batch into the exported file.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
NotJustified, SetSCVMode, SetCSVElementSeparator
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ExportTextNotJustified
method.qi: Exports an evaluated smart parameter value to the Export file.
method.ap:
Text:
The value to export.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The provided text will be exported to the export file. It will be added to the same
line as the previous exported value unless the action StartNewLine has first
been called. If CSV mode or left / right justification has been enabled,
it will have no effect on the output value.
Smart parameters are supported, providing a wide range of additional values
and locations from which data can be obtained for writing to the export file.
This action is similar to the action ExportText, the difference is
that this action will not justify the output value even if
the left or right justification
mode is enabled.
ExportTextNotJustified("Hello There")
This example will write the text "Hello There" to the export file. The value will
be exported as CSV if the CSV mode is enabled. The value will also be adjusted
to be left or right justified, if justification mode has been enabled.
ExportTextNotJustified("@DATE")
This example uses a smart parameter to place the current date into the
export file.
ExportTextNotJustified("@BATCHID")
This example uses a smart parameter to place the current batch ID into the
export file.
ExportTextNotJustified("Current Operator: +@OPERATOR")
If the ID of the current operator is "Tom", then this will output the
text "Current Operator: Tom" in the export file.
ExportTextNotJustified("@P\MyField.MyVariable"
Assuming this is called on a page or field DCO, the smart parameter will navigate from the page
to the field called "MyField", obtain the value of the variable "MyVariable"
and write that value to the export file.
ExportTextNotJustified("@P\MyField")
This example is similar to the previous example, but it will instead
obtain the text value of the field "MyField" and save it in the export file.
ExportTExtNotJustified("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)")
This example will place the path to the current batch into the exported file.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
ExportText
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: LineItemAddElement
method.qi: Includes the specified Line Item Field object as an element of a Line Item Array.
method.ap:
FieldName:
The name of the child field object of the Document Hierarchy to export.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action is used for exporting Line Item values.
This action includes the specified Line Item field object as an element of a Line Item Array.
The elements added to the line item elements are either names of fields to export, blank
export entries, or smart parameters that will be evaluated.
When LineItemExportElements is called, it will process each of the line item "elements" that have
been added. The items added by LineItemAddElement are names of line item fields that will be exported.
A Line Item Array accumulates and organizes captured line item values retrieved from the Data
file of a particular page.
Note:
A rule using this action should be applied to the
LINEITEM
fields
of the Document Hierarchy.
LineItemAddElement("Price")
LineItemExportElements()
The action above expands the Line Item Array by one field: Price.
LineItemExportElements will populate this element and other elements
of the array with the captured values it finds in a page's Data file before exporting them.
method.lvl: The parent field that contains the child Line Item field.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
LineItemExportElements, LineItemClearElements, LineItemAddBlankFields
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: LineItemAddBlankFields
method.qi: Includes the specified number of blank fields as elements of a Line Item Array.
method.ap:
Count:
The number of Blank CSV field values to export as part of the Line Item Array.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action includes the specified number of Blank Line Item fields as elements
of a Line Item Array.
A Line Item Array accumulates and organizes captured line item values retrieved
from the Data file of a particular page. This action will add "blank" values
to the collection that will be exported when LineItemExportElements is called.
Note:
A rule using this action must be applied to the
LINEITEM
fields of the Document Hierarchy.
This action is used for exporting Blank Line Item values.
LineItemAddBlankFields("6")
The action above expands the Line Item Array by six blank fields
LineItemExportElements will populate this element and other elements
of the array with the captured values it finds in a page's Data file before exporting them.
method.lvl: The parent field that contains the child Line Item field.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
LineItemExportElements, LineItemClearElements,LineItemAddElements, LineItemAddSmartParameter
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: LineItemAddSmartParameter
method.qi: Add a smart parameter algorithm as an element of a Line Item Array.
method.ap:
SmartParameter:
Smart Parameter to be evaluated during processing of the Lineitem array.
method.h:
This action permits adding a smart parameter as an element of a Line Item Array to be evaluated
during the Array processing.
A Line Item Array accumulates and organizes captured line item values retrieved
from the Data file of a particular page.
The elements added to the line item elements are either names of line item
fields to export, blank export entries, or
smart parameters that will be evaluated.
When LineItemExportElements is called, it will process each of the line item "elements" that have
been added. The "Smart Parameter" elements that have been added will be evaluated as the elements
are processed.
Important!
A rule using this action must be applied to the
LINEITEM
fields of the Document Hierarchy.
LineItemAddSmartParameter("@F\Price+@TIME(HH:MM:SS)")
LineItemExportElements()
The action above places a child field Price of the calling field node (@F)
appended with the current time in format HH:MM:SS to the export file.
LineItemExportElements will populate this element and other elements
of the array with the captured values it finds in a page's Data file before exporting them.
method.lvl: The parent field that contains the child Line Item field.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
LineItemExportElements, LineItemClearElements, LineItemAddElements, LineItemAddBlankFields
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.
Refer to the smart parameter guide for more information on available smart parameters.

method.name: LineItemClearElements
method.qi: Clears values in the Line Item Array.
method.ap: None
method.h:
This is mainly a housekeeping function you can use to be sure the array does not contain leftover values.
LineItemClearElements()
This example will clear out any previously set line item elements for export.
method.lvl:
The parent Field object of the Document Hierarchy that contains a child
Line Item field, such as you may typically find in an invoice application.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
LineItemAddElement, LineItemAddExportElements, LineItemAddBlankFields, LineItemAddSmartParameter
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: LineItemExportElements
method.qi: Exports the captured values in a page's Line Item Array that have been populated with LineItemAddElement actions.
method.ap: None.
method.lvl: The parent field that contains the child Line Item sub-fields.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.h:
Exports the captured values in a page's Line Item Array that have been populated
with LineItemAddElement actions.
LineItemAddElement("Price")
LineItemAddElement("LineTotal")
LineItemExportElements()
StartNewLine()
This example exports the values included in the Line Item Array to your Export file.
method.see:
LineItemClearElements, LineItemAddElement, LineItemAddBlankFields, LineItemAddSmartParameter
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: ResetFieldExportSettings
method.qi: Resets the variables of the bound Field object of the Document Hierarchy.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action resets some of the export settings that can be independently set by other actions.
It is provided as a quick way to reset custom export settings.
+ The default field fill character is reset to a space.
+ Field justification is reset to left and turned off.
+ Fields are no longer set to a specific length.
+ The ignore field status is reset to not ignore any fields based on the status.
ResetFieldExportSettings()
This action can be called on any level and resets the values mentioned. Alternatively,
the user could have instead called the individual actions to turn off the features.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetFixedLength, SetJustifiedExportMode, SetFillCharacter and SetIgnoreFieldStatus
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SaveExportFilePathAsVariable
method.qi: Saves the path and name of your Export file to the variable specified by the parameter.
method.ap:
VariableName:
The name of the variable name to store the full name and path of the export file.
If the variable does not exist, it will be created.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Saves the path and name of your Export file to the variable specified by the parameter. If the
variable does not exist, it will be created. The value will be placed into the current DCO
object and can be accessed by subsequent actions in the same rule, in a following rule or
in a following task. Unless it is specifically cleared, this value will exist for
the life of the batch.
SaveExportFilePathAsVariable("Export_File")
ExportText(@X.Export_File")
This example saves the path of the export file in the variable "Export_File".
The subsequent action ExportText then writes the value to the export file. This use
is just an example and the value could be used where ever required in a subsequent action
and is easily accessed using smart parameters as shown.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetCSVElementSeparator
method.qi: Ensures that all exported values are delimited by a separator designated as the parameter.
method.ap:
CustomSeparator:
Uses the provided custom character as the separator between fields when
CSV output is enabled.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Ensures that all exported values are delimited by a separator designated as the parameter.
If you wish to set your own custom separator, SetCSVMode("Custom") must be called prior to exporting fields.
If SetCSVMode("Custom") is not called, then your custom element separator will not be used for export.
SetCSVMode("Custom")
SetCSVElementSeparator("|")
This action enables CSV output using a custom separator and
uses "|" to delimit the Export file's values.
SetCSVMode("Off")
This example turns off the addition of the separator when values are
written in the export file.
SetCSVElementSeparator(" ")
This example sets the separator to a space.
SetCSVElementSeparator("@CHR(32)")
This is an alternate example of setting the separator value
to a space using smart parameter notation for a space.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetCSVMode
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetCSVMode
method.qi: Formats exported values to be delimited by a comma separator.
method.ap:
CSVMode:
must be one of these values:
ON:
Enables CSV formatted output using a comma separator.
CUSTOM:
Uses a custom separator, as set by SetElementSeparator(), between output fields.
OFF:
Causes no separator to be placed between output fields.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Ensures that all exported values are delimited by a comma separator or by
a custom separator. This output mode can be used to create a Comma Separated
Variable, CSV, output file which is a standard way of creating rows and columns
of data within a plain text file.
SetCSVMode("On")
ExportFieldValue("Date")
ExportFieldValue("Number")
ExportFieldValue("Total")
SetCSVMode("Off")
This sequence will export the captured values of the Date, Number, and Total Field
objects into your Export file. A comma will be added after each value to separate the fields.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetElementSeparator
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetExportDirectory
method.qi: Specifies the path to the Export file's location. Alternatively, you can use a Smart Parameter to identify a Paths.ini file that has a set of path parameters for your application - see the Parameters and Details sections below.
method.ap:
ExportDirectoryPath:
The complete path to the application's Export folder.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The action's parameter specifies the path to the Export file's location.
If the directory does not exist, the action will create the folder.
If it is expected that the action will create the directory,
the rights of the user ID running the rules must have the access to create
the directory. If running with Rulerunner, then it would be the ID for the
Rulerunner service. If it is a client running rules, then the ID running the
client must have access.
For this action to take effect, it must be called prior to the first action that writes a
value to the export file.
SetExportFileName("Export_+@BATCHID+.txt")
SetExportDirectory("c:\ParentDirectory\Invoice\Export")
This example uses a hard coded path to specify the output directory.
SetExportFileName("Export_+@BATCHID+.txt")
SetExportDirectory("@APPPATH(export)")
In the second example, a smart parameter is used to obtain the location of the Export Directory from the
value configured in the Application Manager. The benefit of this approach is that the
path is stored in a central location. If the application should be moved, such as from
a test environment to production, then only the path in the application manager
needs to be updated to provide the correct path. The application rules do not need to change.
SetExportDirectory("@APPPATH(export)+\+@BATCHID")
This example expands on the the above by adding a unique subdirectory
named with the ID the current batch.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetExportFileEncoding
method.ap:
Encoding:
The encoding to use for the exported text file.
The values can be "UTF8" or "UTF16".
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Determines if the Export file is created with UTF-8 or UTF-16 encoding.
If this action is not called, then the default value is UTF-8.
If this action is called with an in valid parameter, then the format will default to UTF-8.
For this action to take effect, it must be called prior to the first action that writes a
value to the export file. It is recommended to call this action immediately before or immediately
after setting the export file name and path.
SetExportFileEncoding("UTF8")
SetExportFileName("Export_+@BATCHID+.txt")
SetExportDirectory("@APPPATH(export)")
ExportAllFields()
This example will create files in UTF-8 format.
SetExportFileEncoding("UTF16")
SetExportFileName("Export_+@BATCHID+.txt")
SetExportDirectory("@APPPATH(export)")
ExportAllFields()
This example will create the file in UTF-16 format.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetExportFileName, SetExportDirectory
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetExportFileName
method.qi: Assigns a name to the current Export file.
method.ap:
ExportFileName:
The name and extension of the file to create and fill with the exported data.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Assigns a name to the current Export file. For this action to take effect, it must be called prior to the first action that writes a
value to the export file.
If the file already exists, the file will be overwritten.
Once created, the file can be moved or sent to an external repository using subsequent Datacap actions.
Alternatively, the export file can be saved in a directory that will be picked up by an external process.
If an external process is picking up the exported file, it is up to the application designer to ensure that
the external process does not try to pick up the file prior to it being completely written out to disk.
SetExportDirectory("@APPPATH(export)")
SetExportFileName("Export_+@BATCHID+.txt")
This sequence establishes a series of Export files with names such as
Export_20021231.001.txt
Export_20021231.002.txt
SetExportDirectory("@APPPATH(export)")
SetExportFileName("@BATCHID+.txt")
This example will establish a series of Export files with Batch IDs as the name:
20021231.001.txt
20021231.002.txt
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetExportDirectory
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetFillCharacter
method.qi: Sets the filler character to be used to expand the current value of a field in the export file.
method.ap:
FixedLengthFillCharacter:
A single character to be used as the filler value to adjust a value's length.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets the filler character to be used to expand the current value of a field to the length
specified by the action SetFieldLength.
If the field value is longer than this length, it will be truncated to this length.
When using SetFillCharacter, the action SetFixedLength, ExportPageFieldFixedLengthLeftJustified
or ExportPageFieldFixedLengthRightJustified must also
be used to set the maximum length of the field.
Use ResetFieldExportSettings to clear this setting.
SetFixedLength("10")
SetFillCharacter("$")
This example sets the fill character to a $. If the exported text is "Hello", then
the value will be written to the export file as "Hello$$$$$"
SetFixedLength("10")
SetJustifiedExportMode("R")
SetFillCharacter(" ")
This example uses blank spaces to pad the exported text. The padding has been set to
right justified. If the exported text is "Hello", the exported
text will be preceded by 5 spaces as in " Hello".
SetFixedLength("10")
SetJustifiedExportMode("R")
SetFillCharacter("@CHR(32)")
This is an example similar to the previous example, but uses smart parameter
notation to set the value to a space.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetFixedLength
method.qi: Uses the Numeric value you enter as a parameter to establish a fixed length of a value exported from the current field.
method.ap:
RequiredTextLength:
The required length of exported field data. All data will be padded or truncated
to this length. If set to 0, then the length of text will not be adjusted.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Uses the numeric value you enter as a parameter to establish a fixed length of a value exported from the current field.
When this value is set, subsequent export actions will have their output values adjusted to be exactly the
length specified by this action.
Any following actions are not required to be in the same rule as the rule that calls this action. However,
the actions must be in the same task profile as the rule that called this action.
Use ResetFieldExportSettings to clear this setting or set the value to 0.
SetFixedLength("10")
SetFillCharacter("$")
ExportText("Hello")
This example sets the fill character to a $. If the exported text is "Hello", then
the value will be written to the export file as "Hello$$$$$". It is not necessary
to call this action on every object that calls an export action. The length
specification will stay in effect until the task profile is complete or
until the action is called again with a new value.
SetFixedLength("10")
SetJustifiedExportMode("R")
SetFillCharacter(" ")
ExportText("Hello")
This example uses blank spaces to pad the exported text. The padding has been set to
right justified. If the exported text is "Hello", the exported
text will be preceded by 5 spaces as in " Hello".
method.see:
ResetFieldExportSettings
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetIgnoreFieldStatus
method.qi: Any field with this status will not be included in the export file.
method.ap:
StatusToIgnore:
An integer that represents the status of fields to be "ignored" by Export tasks so the value it contains will not be exported.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action establishes the status that determines if an Export task will
export a field's value. If the status of the field being exported matches this set value,
the field's value will not be exported.
Any following export actions are not required to be in the same rule as the rule that calls this action. However,
the actions must be in the same task profile as the rule that called this action.
Use ResetFieldExportSettings to clear this setting.
Any fields that have a DCO variable called "NOEXPORT" set to the value of "1" will also be
excluded from the export file, regardless of the field's status.
SetIgnoreFieldStatus("1")
ExportCurrentField()
This example ensures that runtime values for fields with a "1" status will not
be added to an Export file or update an Export database. (Typically, "1" denotes a problem field.)
This example assumes it is running on a field level object. If the status of the field
is "1", then the field's value will not be exported. For illustration, the example shows
SetIgnoreFieldStatus as being called in the same ruleset as the ExportCurrentField action.
As long as SetIgnoreFieldStatus was called prior to the export for this field, the setting
will be in effect.
method.see:
Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.
For more information about the DCO "STATUS" variable, refer to the help in the ApplicationObjects
action library.

method.name: SetJustifiedExportMode
method.qi: Right-justifies or left-justifies exported values.
method.ap:
JustifyMode:
An upper case R (right-justified) or L (left-justified) to indicate that exported
field values should be left justified or right justified.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Right-justifies or left-justifies a field's exported values according to the parameter you enter.
For this setting to take affect, the action SetFixedLength must also be used to
set the maximum length of the field. Left justification will add characters to the end
of the exported text to extend it to the full length. Right justification will add characters
to the start of the exported text to extend it to the full length.
If SetFixedLength is set to 0, then left and right
justification is disabled.
Any following export actions are not required to be in the same rule as the rule that calls this action. However,
the actions must be in the same task profile as the rule that called this action.
Use ResetFieldExportSettings to clear this setting. If this action is not called, then it defaults to
left-justified.
SetFixedLength("10")
SetJustifiedExportMode("R")
This sequence configures the export actions so that any exported text is set to 10 characters long.
If the exported text is less than 10 characters, then it will be padded to be 10 characters long
and because the justification is set to "Right", then padding characters will be added
to the front of the text.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: SetOMRSeparator
method.qi: For multi-punch OMR fields, uses the parameter's value as the separator character.
method.ap: The separator character you want to use.
method.h:
For multi-punch optical mark recognition, OMR, fields, uses the parameter's value as the separator character. When
multi-punch fields are exported, you typically do not want to use the same separator
that you are using for CSV separators as OMR values are all within a single field. This
action allows you to specify a custom separator to be used when exporting OMR values. If this
action is not called, the default value is a space.
Any following export actions are not required to be in the same rule as the rule that calls this action. However,
the actions must be in the same task profile as the rule that called this action.
SetOMRSeparator(";")
This example sets the value separator to a semicolon.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: StartNewLine
method.qi: Starts a new line in your Export file.
method.ap: None.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.h:
Starts a new line in your Export file. Each call to an export action, such as ExportText or ExportCurrentValue,
will output the value on the same line as the previous value exported. Call StartNewLine
to start a new output line in the export file.
Depending on the application needs, it may make sense to call this action just before the first value
to be placed on a new line, or after the last value written to a line.
StartNewLine()
ExportText("Export Output")
This sequence starts a new line and adds the text "Export Output" to the beginning of the line.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

method.name: WriteBlankLines
method.qi: Inserts blank lines into the Export file.
method.ap:
LineCount:
A positive integer indicating how many blank lines to add below the current line in the export file.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Inserts
n
blank lines into the Export file.
BlankLines("4")
This action inserts four empty lines, leaving the insertion point for the next output on
the following line. Additional output will begin on the fifth line.
BlankLines("@B.LinesToAdd")
This example uses the value of the batch variable "LinesToAdd" to determine how
many lines to add to the file. It is assumed that a previous action has
created this batch level variable with the proper value or that the variable
had been created in the Setup DCO in Datacap Studio and set with the number
of lines to export.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for general information about using this action library.

com.h:
ExportToXML library is used to generate the XMl File.
Xml file contains all the dco data such as document,page and field details.
To Set the file name use the action XMLSetFileName() and location of the file will be set using XMLSetExportath() action.
NewNode:
The first xmlNewNode() action in a ruleset will create the root node of the XML file using the new parent NodeID, the child NodeID must be blank.
e.g
xmlNewNode("","Batch") in this example the Batch is the root node of XML File.
xmlNewNode("Page1","Batch") in this exmple the "Page1" is child node and "Batch" Is the Parent node.
SetNodeValue:
For adding the value of the node use
XMLSetNodeValue
action which having the parameters NodeId and NodeValue
e.g
xmlNewNode("","Batch")
xmlNewNode("Page1","Batch")
XMLSetNodeValue("Page1","Mypage");
Setting attribute:
For setting the value of node the node should be available otherwise it will method will return false.
Similarly for setting the attribute use XMLSetAttributeValue action which takes parameter as Nodeid ,AttrId as attribute id and AttrValue as Attribute Value
e.g
xmlNewNode("","Batch")
xmlNewNode("Page1","Batch")
XMLSetNodeValue("Page1","Mypage");
XMLSetAttributeValue("Page1","ID","10")
Set Encoding:
There is action XMLSetFileEncodingAsASCII() which having optional parameter set the UNICODE Encoding format to the xml
If this action will not called then by default it take UTF-8 encoding.
This action should called before XMLSave() action.
XMLSetFileEncodingAsASCII("0")
XMLSave()
Smart Parameters and Common Operations
If an action supports smart parameters, it is specified in the action help. Smart parameters are very powerful
specifications for parameters that allow access of data to and from other DCO objects and allow performing
special pre-defined operations in one step.
Smart parameters can be used to dynamically obtain or create action input parameters at runtime. For example,
an action could be fed the value of a field after recognition, a parameter could pull the value from a
DCO variable that was set by a previous action, or a smart parameter could evaluate to the current date, the current
time, the current job ID, the current operator ID, the path to the current batch that is running, and more.
Smart parameter syntax can also be used to build expressions at runtime that concatenate dynamic data and
static data at runtime. Smart parameters are
a flexible way to provide a wide range of input to any action that supports smart parameters.
e.g
Suppose the BatchID having Value "20190402.000002"
XMLSetFileName("@BatchID") will generate the xmlfile with the name of 20190402.000002 i.e 20190402.000002.xml.

method.name: XMLSaveFile
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action saves XML file to disk. You must use this action
to complete the creation of the export XML file.
XMLSaveFile()

method.name: XMLSetExportPath
method.ap:
Specifies the full path to the directory that will store the export XML file.
If this action is not called, the XML file will be saved in the batch directory.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action will only set the path. You will still need to use
XMLSetFileName
to set the
name of the export file.
XMLSetExportPath("C:\Invoice\ExportXML")
XMLSetFileName("@BatchID")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: XMLSetFileName
method.ap: The name of the XML export file. Smart Parameters are supported.
method.h:
Use of this action is required to set the name of the XML Export file.
While this action can be called at any level, it is typically called at the batch level.
If the action XMLSetExportPath is not called, the file will be saved in the batch folder.
XMLSetExportPath("C:\Invoice\ExportXML")
XMLSetFileName("@BatchID")
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: XMLSaveFile

method.name: XMLNewNode
method.ap:
1. NewNodeID:
The NodeID (tag name) of a new child node.
2. ParentID:
The NodeID (tag name) of the parent node, if there is a parent.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The new NodeID followed by the parent NodeID creates a new Node in the Export XML file.
The first
xml_NewNode
action in a ruleset will create the root node of the XML file using the
new parent NodeID, the child NodeID must be blank.
XMLSetExportPath("C:\ParentDir\APT")
XMLSetFileName("@BATCHID")
XMLNewNode("","B")
XMLSetAttributeValue("B,id,@BATCHID")
The example above starts an export XML file that is named the same as the current batch ID.
It has a root node "B" whose "id" is assigned the batch ID. It is expected that additional rules
will continue to build the XML structure. The last invoked action must call XMLSaveFile to save
the export file to disk.
XMLNewNode("ClaimsData,HCFA")
Duplicated Node ID's will cause the prior node of the same ID to commit to its specific parent
node and will no longer be available for modification.
Note: Adding a second child NodeID with the same Tag name of the root node will cause the action
to return false.
method.ret:
True
if parent node exists.
False
if duplicate root node
is declared, or parent NodeID does not exist.
method.see: XMLSaveFile

method.name: XMLSetNodeValue
method.ap:
1. The NodeID.
2. The value to assign to the node.
The action defaults the current object's value.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Assigns a value to a specific node.
The example below shows how creation of an XML for invoice line items might look.
XMLNewNode("LineItem,Invoice")
XMLSetAttributeValue("LineItem,id,@ID")
XMLNewNode("ItemID,LineItem")
XMLSetNodeValue("IdemID,@F\ItemID")
XMLNewNode("ItemDesc,LineItem")
XMLSetNodeValue("ItemDesc,@F\ItemDesc")
XMLNewNode("Qty,LineItem")
XMLSetNodeValue("Qty,@F\Qty")
XMLCommitNode("LineItem")
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: XMLNewNode

method.name: XMLSetAttributeValue
method.ap:
1.
The NodeID.
2.
The attribute's name.
3.
The value to be assigned to the attribute. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets an attribute value within a specific node in the XML hierarchy.
The example below assigns the current Page's
Number
field value to the
Xpage
node's
Number
attribute.
XMLSetAttributeValue("Xpage,Number,@P\Number")
The example below shows how creation of an XML for invoice line items might look.
XMLNewNode("LineItem,Invoice")
XMLSetAttributeValue("LineItem,id,@ID")
XMLNewNode("ItemID,LineItem")
XMLSetNodeValue("IdemID,@F\ItemID")
XMLNewNode("ItemDesc,LineItem")
XMLSetNodeValue("ItemDesc,@F\ItemDesc")
XMLNewNode("Qty,LineItem")
XMLSetNodeValue("Qty,@F\Qty")
XMLCommitNode("LineItem")

method.name: XMLSetFileEncodingAsASCII
method.ap:
0. No Encoding
1. UTF-8 Encoding
2. UTF-16 Encoding
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Determines if the Export file is created with ASCII or UNICODE encoding.
A parameter value of 1 and 2 will create files with UNICODE format.
NOTE:
This action must be called before any actions that physically write to and create the Export file.If not called,
then the file will be created with UNICODE encoding UTF-8.
XMLSetFileEncodingAsASCII("0")
XMLSaveFile()
This example will create files with no encoding .
XMLSetFileEncodingAsASCII("1")
XMLSaveFile()
This example will create the file in UNICODE UTF-8 format.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: XMLCommitNode
method.ap: String value of the xml Tag. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Commits (closes) current xml node to it's parent node with the xml tag value of the parameter. Allowing a new node with the same
tag to be created at the same hierarchical level in the output xml.
XMLCommitNode("LineTotal")
Example commits (closes) the current xml node with a Tag
LineTotal
.
Remember: Use of this action can change the expected order of xml nodes as they appear in the final xml, since this action commits the current xml
to the parent xml node when it is called. Sibling xml nodes that were not committed using this action are later committed
to the parent node when the
XMLSaveFile
is called, so those xml nodes will appear after nodes previously committed using the
XMLCommitNode
action.
method.ret:
Always
True.
