com.h:
The FileIO action library provides a set of actions that are oriented to directory and file
manipulation. They allow an application to test that a directory exists, a file exists,
copy files, rename files, delete files, etc. The actions also have the ability to parse out
file names and directories from a string to allow manipulation of the file names and
the files themselves. The actions can also read values out of an INI file
and store them in DCO variables or write new values into an INI file.
The files manipulated can be within the current batch directory or external to the
batch, as long as the Windows user that is running the rules has access to the
required directories.
The actions support smart parameters that allow the value of a parameter to
be determined at runtime. For example, the batch directory name will be unique
per batch so if manipulating a file within a batch directory, smart parameters are
the mechanism to access the proper path. Many of the actions
have examples that include smart parameters accessing files within the
batch directory. It is recommended that the smart parameter
guide is reviewed to understand the capabilities and how to use them.
Common Uses
There could be many different use cases that require the application to
copy a file or rename a file. The following are some common use cases.
It is common that images from a scanned page require image enhancement.
The image enhancement may remove lines from the page, change the image
color depth, deskew the page, etc. These steps can improve accuracy of
text and barcode recognition. However, it may be a requirement to store the
original images when the batch has completed, causing a reluctance to change the
image because the original needs to be retained.
When image enhancement actions process an image, they will always save the original
version of the image under a different name. Depending on the action, the new name
may be configurable or it may not, but it typically involves keeping the same file
name but will change the file extension to something unique.
The application designer can easily use the FileIO actions to take the original
file that was saved, and rename it or move it for storage at the end of the batch.
If desired, both the manipulated image and the original image can be exported
at the end of the batch. It is up to the specific use case and how the application
designer wants to retain the final processed files.
Another similar use case is where the image required enhancement to get good quality
text or barcode recognition, but then show the unprocessed image to the user for verification.
For example, deskewing an image is a common task and is generally required for applications
that use fields. Additional enhancements like line removal can help text recognition.
When recognition is complete, the designer may rather show the deskewed image to
the user but not the image that has had lines removed. This can be achieved with the
FileIO actions by restoring the image that was created after deskew but before line removal.
In the Verify panel the verify operator will see the deskewed page with all of the fields
properly aligned, but the page will still have the lines so the page still looks as it should.
Just because removing the lines, or other enhancements improve recognition, it doesn't mean
that is the what must be shown to the user. The deskewed image can be renamed back to the
primary image name so it will be shown in the Verify panel. The image that has its lines
removed for recognition could be deleted or given a new name to back it up for safety.
When manipulating these files, it is also common to use the SplitFileName action
to get just the file name without the extension, or just parts of the file
path, store those values into DCO variables, and then use those variables
to build a new file name or file path.
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
For example, "@X" is notation for accessing the current object. "@P" accesses the page object, which
could be the current object, or a parent object. Being evaluated at runtime, allows recognized data
or other batch specific data to be passed to actions or stored as metadata. A smart parameter such
as @DATE could be used to name export files based on the current date. Similar smart parameters
will retrieve the current batch ID, current batch directory, current operator ID, and more.
Smart parameters are a very powerful mechanism of getting data from other areas of the application and copying
it into a new location or passing it as a parameter to an action. It is recommended that the smart parameter
documentation is reviewed to understand the full capabilities available. The top-level help of the
ValidationAndTextAdjustments action library also has information about smart parameters. Some characters such
as +, \ and . also have special smart parameter meaning and may be interpreted as a smart parameter. This
can be controlled using smart parameter syntax.

method.name: CCOBackup
method.qi: Makes a copy of the CCO of the first document page.
method.ap: None
method.h:
Copies the CCO file of the first document page to a file of the same name with a CC1 extension.
This can be used prior to merging CCOs, if it is necessary to restore the CCO later.
If a CCO file does not exist, no files will be copied and the action will still return true.
method.ret: Always True.
method.see: CCORestore

method.name: CCORestore
method.qi: Copies the saved CCO file over the existing CCO file for the first page of the document.
method.ap: None
method.h:
Restores the CC1 file (if it exists) of the first document page to a file of the same name with a CCO extension.
This can be used after merging CCOs, if it is necessary to restore the CCO later.
If a CCO file does not exist, no files will be copied and the action will still return true.
method.ret: Always True.
method.see: CCOBackup

method.name: CopyFile
method.qi: Copies a file.
method.ap:
sourcefile : The name and path of the file to copy. Smart parameters are supported.
targetfile : The target path and filename. Smart parameters are supported.
overwrite : if the target file exists, this determines if it should be overwritten. True will overwrite the target file.
method.h:
The file is copied from one location to the specified location. If a file of the same target name
already exists in the target directory, the overwrite parameter will determine if that file will be overwritten by the new file.
The output directory must exist for this action to succeed. You can use action IsDirectoryPresent to create
the target directory.
If target file ends with a backslash, meaning only the target directory is specified,
the same file name from the source string will be used as the target file.
Because the target file name can be different from the source file, this action
allows the copied file to be renamed in one step. If you want to perform a "move" operation,
call the DeleteFile to remove the source file.
Smart parameters are supported in the source and target file name parameters. DOS * and ? wildcards are not supported.
CopyFile("C:\MyFile.txt", "c:\temp\+@BATCHID+.txt", true)
This action will copy MyFile.txt to the temp directory and give it a new name of the current batch ID
CopyFile("@VAR(IMAGEFILE)", "c:\temp\", true)
This action will copy the file specified by the variable IMAGEFILE and copy it to the temp directory.
CopyFile("@VAR(IMAGEFILE)", "@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.backup", true)
Assuming this is called on a page node, this example will copy the current image
file associated with the current page object to a new file that has a "backup" extension.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: DeleteFile
method.qi: Deletes a file.
method.ap: filename : The name and path of the file to delete. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Deletes the specified file. DOS wildcards are permitted in the file name.
DeleteFile("C:\Temp\DeleteThis.txt")
The above example deletes the specific file.
DeleteFile("C:\Temp\*.*")
The above example deletes all of the files in the 'Temp' directory.
DeleteFile("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.backup")
The above example deletes a file within the current batch that has the file name that is
the same as the current DCO node with an extension ".backup".
DeleteFile("C:\Temp\@BATCHID+.txt")
The above example deletes the file name that matches the current batch ID and has an extension of 'TXT'.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: ReadTextFile
method.qi: Reads a text file.
method.ap:
filename
: The name and path of the text file to read. Smart parameters are supported.
target
: The DCO node to store the value of the text file.
Smart parameters are supported for each parameter.
method.h:
Reads the specified file and stores the entire contents of the file in a DCO variable. Depending on the
file, this could potentially require a significant amount of memory and when running,
Datacap will retain the all of the DCO objects and all of their variables in memory.
ReadFile("C:\Temp\ReadThis.txt","@P.text")
The above example reads the specific file and saves the value to the parent page of the calling object's to a variable labeled 'text'.
ReadFile("C:\Temp\ReadThis.xml","@P\xmltext")
The above example reads the specific file and saves the value to the parent page of the calling object to a field named 'xmltext'.
method.ret:
True
if the text file exists and was successfully read, otherwise
False
.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: DeleteDirectory
method.qi: Deletes a directory and optionally deletes subdirectories
method.ap:
Directory:
The path of the directory to delete.
Recursive:
True will delete the directory and all files and subdirectories.
False will only delete the directory and requires that the directory is empty.
FalureReturnValue:
True will cause the action to always return True, even if
the delete fails. False will cause the action to return False if the directory delete fails.
Smart parameters are supported for the directory path.
method.h:
Deletes the specified directory and can optionally delete subdirectories.
DeleteDirectory("C:\MyDir1\MyDir2",True,True)
This example will delete MyDir2 and all files and subdirectories.
If the delete fails, the action will still return true.
method.ret:
If the directory is deleted, the action always returns
True.
If a failure occurs when deleting a directory, the action will return the value of FailureReturnValue.
This allows you to determine if the action should return True or False on a directory failure.
Depending on the application, it may make sense to ignore a delete failure so this action can be set to always return true.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: CopyDirectory
method.qi: Copies a directory and its subdirectories
method.ap:
SourceDirectory:
The path of the directory to copy.
DestDirectory:
The path to the destination directory.
Recursive:
True will copy the directory files and subdirectories.
False will only copy the files in the initial directory and requires that the directory is empty.
Smart parameters are supported for the directory paths.
method.h:
Copies the source directory to the target directory. If the target directory does not exist, it will be created, however
the parent directory does need to exist.
CopyDirectory("C:\MyDir1\MyDir2","C:\MyNewDir",True)
This example will delete MyDir2 and all files and subdirectories to C:\MyNewDir.
method.ret:
If a failure occurs when coping a directory, the action will return false. If some of the files
have been copied prior to the failure, those files will remain.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: CheckFreeDiskSpace
method.qi: Checks the size of the available disk space.
method.ap:
DriveLetter:
The drive letter to test for available disk space. UNC paths are not supported.
Threshold:
Optional. The minimum amount of required disk space in bytes. If provided, this value
must be a positive integer.
TargetVariable:
Optional. The DCO variable to store the value of the available disk space.
Smart parameters are supported for each parameter.
method.h:
Checks the available amount of free disk space in bytes.
CheckFreeDiskSpace("D","1000","@P.FreeSpace")
Checks that the amount of available disk space on drive D is at least 1000 bytes.
It also stores the amount of free space in the page level runtime DCO variable "FreeSpace".
CheckFreeDiskSpace("D","@B.MyLimit","")
Only checks that the amount of available disk space on drive D is at least as much
as the value specified in the batch level variable "MyLimit".
CheckFreeDiskSpace("D","","@P.FreeSpace")
Only stores the amount of free space in the page level runtime DCO variable "FreeSpace".
method.ret:
Returns False if the threshold is specified and the amount of free disk space is less
than the specified value, if the target variable is provided but cannot be set, or
if the drive letter is invalid. Otherwise True is returned.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: GetFileSize
method.qi: Obtains the size of a file and stores it in the specified variable.
method.ap:
filename : The name and path of the file.
targetVariable : The name of the variable to store the file size. The variable level must be specified with a Smart Parameter.
Smart parameters are supported for each of the input parameters.
method.h:
The size of the specified file will be stored into the specified variable. This can be
helpful to test for problems, such as empty files. Subsequent actions can
perform tests on the stored value and act upon it.
If the specified file is not found,
the action will return
true
and a size of 0 will be stored into the variable.
If any other kind of error occurs, the action will return false and the variable
may or may not be set to 0.
GetFileSize("C:\Temp\MyFile.txt", "@B.MyVariable")
This example sets the file size in the variable 'MyVariable' at the batch level.
method.ret:
False,
if the target variable is blank.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: GetProfileString
method.qi: Reads a key value from a settings file.
method.ap:
filename : The INI file name.
section : The section within the file.
key : The key within the section.
targetVariable : The variable where to store the value. The variable level must be specified with a smart parameter.
Smart parameters are supported for each of the input parameters.
method.h:
Reads the value from a settings file, typically a .INI file, and stores it into the variable specified.
If the variable does not exist, it will be created.
If the key does not exist but the file does exist, the action will still return true
and an empty string will be stored in the variable. If you need to test for a blank
key value, you can use the IsProfilePresent action.
If you are reading Unicode characters from an INI file,
it is required that the file is in a format that supports Unicode.
If the file is not a Unicode format, the Unicode characters may appear
incorrectly when read by GetProfileString or displayed in an editor.
Most file editors will let you chose the type of file encoding.
See the help for your specific editor.
GetProfileString("C:\Settings.ini", "MySection", "MyKey", "@B.MyVariable")
The value for 'MyKey' will be placed into the variable 'MyVariable'.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: IsDirectoryPresent
method.qi: Determines if the specified directory exists and optionally creates it.
method.ap:
directoryName : The directory path to test. Smart parameters are allowed.
create : Specifies if the directory should be created. True will create the directory, if it does not exist.
testExistence : Determines if true should be returned if the directory exists or does not exist.
method.h:
Checks for the existence of a directory. Depending on the input parameters,
if the directory does not exist, the action will create the directory. The
meaning of the return value can be changed using the testExistence parameter.
This allows rules to continue if a directory exists or rules can continue if a directory does not exist.
IsDirectoryPresent("c:\temp", true, true)
This example will create the directory C:\temp, if it does not exist, and return true
if the directory exists or was created successfully.
IsDirectoryPresent("c:\temp", true, false)
This example will create the directory C:\temp, if it does not exist, and return false
if the directory exists or was created successfully.
method.ret:
If testExistence is
True
, the action will return True if the directory exists or if the
directory did not exist but was successfully created.
If testExistence is
False
, the action will return True if the directory does not exist. This allows you to perform
negative tests that will return true when a directory does not exist.
If an error occurs, the action will return false.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: IsFilePresent
method.qi: Determines if the specified file exists.
method.ap:
filename : The file name and path. Smart parameters are allowed.
testExistence : true tests that the file exists, false tests that the file does not exist.
method.h:
Checks for the existence of a file. Depending on the testExistence parameter,
the action can return true if a file exists or true if a file does not exist to
provide flexibility when creating rules.
IsFilePresent("C:\MyDir\MyFile.abc", false)
In this example, if the file does not exist, the action will return
True
and any subsequent actions will be processed.
IsFilePresent("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.bak", true)
This example is similar to the previous example. It checks for the existence
of a file in the current batch that has the same name as the current DCO node ID
with the extension "bak". If it exists, then this action will
return true and the next action could
do something with that file, such as move it or delete it.
method.ret:
If testExistence is
True,
the action will return true if the file exists.
If testExistence is
false,
the action will return true if the file does not exist.
If an error occurs, the action will return false.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: IsFileReadOnly
method.qi: Tests the read only attribute of a file.
method.ap:
filename : The file name and path of the file to test. Smart parameters are allowed.
testForReadOnly : Determines if the action should return true for read-only or read-write.
method.h:
This action will indicate if a file is set to read only.
IsFileReadOnly("c:\mydir\myfile.txt", true)
if the file "myfile.txt" is set to read only, the action will return
true
.
IsFileReadOnly("c:\mydir\myfile.txt", false)
if the file "myfile.txt" is not set to read only, the action will return
true
.
method.ret:
If testForReadOnly is
true,
the action will return true if the file is read only.
If testForReadOnly is
false,
the action will return true if the file is not read only.
If an error occurs, or if the file does not exist, the action will return false.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: IsProfilePresent
method.qi: Tests that a profile exists and that a specific section and key exists within it.
method.ap:
filename : The INI file name.
section : The section within the file.
key : The key within the section.
testExistence : true tests that the it exists, false tests that it does not exist.
The parameters "filename", "section" and "key" can accept smart parameters.
method.h:
Checks that a specific section and key exists within a settings file, typically an INI file. It does not
test the value of the key, only that a value exists.
IsProfilePresent("C:\MyDir\settings.ini", "mysection", "mykey", true)
In this example, if settings.ini exists and contains "mysection", "mykey" and if "mykey"
has a non-blank value, it will return
True.
IsProfilePresent("@PROCESSDIR+\+settings.ini", "mysection", "mykey", true)
This example is similar to the above with the change that it reads the settings INI file from the
application's process directory, such as dco_APT for the APT application.
method.ret:
True,
if testExistence is true and the section and key is found within the profile and the key has an assigned value.
True,
if testExistence is false and the section or key is not found within the profile or the key value is blank.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: RenameFile
method.qi: Renames or moves the specified file.
method.ap:
oldName : The source file name and path. Allows smart parameters.
newName : The destination file name and path. Allows smart parameters.
overwrite : Specifies if the destination file should be overwritten. True will overwrite an existing file.
method.h:
Renames the specified file to the new name. If the directories for the original
and new file names are different, the file will be moved to the new directory.
If the overwrite parameter is true, the file will overwrite an existing file.
If overwrite is false, an existing file will not be overwritten.
RenameFile("C:\MyDir\File1.txt", "C:\MyDir\File2.txt", true)
This example renames the file within the same directory, overwriting any existing file called "File2.txt".
RenameFile("C:\MyDir\File1.txt", "C:\New\File1.txt", true)
This example moves the file from MyDir to New, overwriting any existing file called "File1.txt".
RenameFile("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.bak", "@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.tif", true)
This example moves the file within the current batch directory that is the same name as the
current DCO ID with the "bak" extension to "tif".
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: RenameImagesToStandardNames
method.qi: Renames images and page objects to the standard TMxxxxxxx convention
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action names all files in the batch to the standard TMxxxxxx.tif naming convention.
The standard naming convention is the preferred way to name the files in the batch.
The action updates the associated image file on disk, the DCO ID, and the associated image file name.
This action is only to be used immediately after a convert action has created new pages using the 0001010 naming scheme.
No other use is supported.
When images and objects are renamed, the action operates on pages that are the immediate children of the batch object.
Therefore, this action must be called before the CreateDocuments action is called,
which creates the full document tree structure.
New applications are required to use SetNamePattern("2") instead of using this action to rename files.
RenameImagesToStandardNames is largely obsolete as the Convert actions are able to use the standard naming
convention when creating single page images from a multi-page document. This action is provided as
compatibility only for legacy applications that were created before the addition of the SetNamePattern("2") action.
By default, the Convert action library does not use the standard naming convention.
However, calling the action Common Convert action SetNamePattern("2") before a Convert action to separate pages,
the created images use the standard naming convention.
When SetNamePattern("2") is called before a convert action that generates files, this action is not necessary.
RenameImagesToStandardNames()
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: SetFileReadOnly
method.qi: Sets or removes the read only attribute from a file or set of files.
method.ap:
readonly : true turns on the read only attribute, false turns it off.
filename : The path and filename. Smart parameters and DOS wildcards are allowed.
method.h:
Sets a the read only attribute of a file, or a group of files. The read only attribute can
be set or cleared with this action. Standard DOS * and ? wildcards can be used to affect a change
on multiple files at once.
SetFileReadOnly(false, "C:\MyDir\*.*")
This example sets all of the files in MyDir as read-write.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: SetProfileString
method.qi: Writes a value to a profile file, typically called an INI file.
method.ap:
filename : The profile file name.
section : The section within the file.
key : specifies if the destination file should be overwritten.
value : The value to write.
Smart parameters are supported for each of the input parameters.
method.h:
Writes a value to a settings profile, typically a file with an INI
extension. The value is stored in the variable proved as a parameter.
If the variable does not exist, it will be created.
If the variable does exist, the current value will be replaced with the new value.
If the file does not exist, the file will be created.
If you are writing Unicode characters to the INI file,
it is required that the file exist and that it is in Unicode format.
If the file is not a Unicode format, the Unicode characters may appear
incorrectly when read by GetProfileString or displayed in an editor.
Most file editors will let you chose the type of file encoding.
See the help for your specific editor.
SetProfileString("C:\MyDir\config.ini","MySection","MyKey","Batch+@BATCHID")
This example will write the current batch ID to the INI file.
SetProfileString("@PROCESSDIR+\+config.ini","MySection","MyKey","Batch+@BATCHID")
This example is similar to the above example but will use the
ini file stored in the applications process directory, such as dco_APT for the APT application.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: SplitFileName
method.qi: Splits a file name into user specified variables.
method.ap:
inputFilename : The input file name to break into its three logical parts.
rootPathVariable : The name of the variable to store the root path.
pathVariable : The name of the variable to store the file path.
fileVariable : The name of the variable to store the file name without the extension.
extVariable : The name of the variable to store the file extension.
Smart parameters are supported for each of the input parameters. For each of the
parameters that accept a variable, the level must be specified with a Smart Parameter.
It is not necessary to specify a variable name for each part of the path that is split.
Only destination variables for the desired values need to be specified.
If you do not want to store a particular file name part, leave that parameter blank.
method.h:
This action will split the input file name into its root path, path, file name and the extension,
and place each of the parts into their own variables. The file does not need to exist.
If the file contains a file extension, the saved file extension will contain a preceding period.
SplitFileName("C:\Dir1\Dir2\MyFile.abc","@B.FROOT","@B.FPATH", "@B.FNAME","@B.FEXT")
This example splits the file and saves the information into 4 variables at the batch level:
FROOT = "C:\"
FPATH = "C:\Dir1\Dir2"
FNAME = "MyFile"
FEXT = ".abc"
SplitFileName("@VAR(IMAGEFILE)","","","","@B.EXT")
Assuming this is called on a page object, this example obtains
the value stored in the variable IMAGE file and only saves the file extension into a variable called EXT.
The variable will be on the batch level DCO node and if the variable does not exist, it will
be created.
SplitFileName("@VAR(IMAGEFILE)","","","@X.FileName","@X.Ext")
Assuming this is called on a page object, this example obtains
the value stored in the variable IMAGE file and saves the file name without the extension to
a variable in the current DCO node called "FileName" and the extension
will also be saved in the current DCO node the the name "Ext".
If the variables do not exist, they will be created. If the variables do exist, the current
values will be overwritten.
method.ret:
False,
if the structure of the file name or path is invalid. Otherwise,
True.
The file does not need to exist for this action to succeed.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: SwapPageImages
method.qi: Swaps two files that correspond to the current page file.

p.name: extention1
p.qi: The extension of the file to interchange.

p.name: extension2
p.qi: The extension of the file to interchange.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
During batch processing, some actions may create copies or backup of images that correspond to the current page.
If it is needed to revert the current page image, this action performs the task with one action compared to calling
the RenameFile action multiple times.
This action requires that the filename without the extension matches the current image file name.
If there is need to swap files that do not match the current image file name, then use the RenameFile action.
SwapPageImages("TIO,TIF")
This image will swap the current page file with a TIF extension with the file that has a TIO extension.
method.ret:
False,
if called at the wrong level, if the file cannot be found or if an error occurs.
True,
if the file are interchanged.

method.name: ZipOcrResults
method.qi: Creates a ZIP file containing recognition results for every page of the document.
method.h:
This action will create a ZIP file for the associated document. The Zip file name is based on the ID of the document object
in the format of DocumentID.ocr.zip.
This zip file will contain all of the files with recognition results from every page of the document.
For example- if an action is called on document with ID "20160914.000000.01" which contains two pages,
then a zip file called 20160914.000000.01.ocr.zip will be created. The contents of the ZIP will
contain all of the recognition results associated with each page similar to this:
tm000001.xml
tm000001_layout.xml
tm000001c.xml
tm000002.xml
tm000002_layout.xml
tm000002c.xml
method.ret:
True,
if the zip file is created successfully otherwise
False.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

rrx.h:
These actions are used to automate the deletion of fingerprints in your application. It is intended for applications
that create fingerprints automatically. By periodically deleting fingerprints that are not used you can decrease the time
it takes to load them when the FindFingerprint action is called.

method.name: OpenDatabase
method.qi: Opens a connection to the fingerprint database.
method.ap: Fingerprint database connection string.
method.h:
Opens a connection to the fingerprint database using the connection string provided in the parameter. A smart parameter may be used.
OpenDatabase("provider=microsoft.jet.oledb.4.0;data source=c:\datacap\apt\APTFingerprint.mdb;persist security info=false")
This example obtains the connection string set in the applicaiton manager.
OpenDatabase("@APPVAR(*/dco_*[1]/fingerprintconn:cs)")
method.ret:
True
if the connection is established.
False
if the connection is not established.

p.name: ConnectionString
p.qi: Fingerprint database connection string.

method.name: SetFingerprintFolder
method.qi: Specifies the folder containing the fingerprint files.
method.ap: Folder path where the fingerprints are located.
method.h:
Specifies the folder containing the fingerprint files. A smart parameter may be used.
SetFingerprintFolder("C:\Datacap\APT\fingerprint")
This example obtains the path set in the applicaiton manager.
SetFingerprintFolder("@APPPATH(*/fingerprint)")
method.ret:
Always
True.

p.name: Folder
p.qi: Folder containing the fingerprints.

method.name: DeleteFingerprint
method.qi: Deletes specified fingerprint.
method.ap: The ID of the fingerprint to delete.
method.h:
Deletes the CCO, TIFF and FPXML files for the specified fingerprint. Also deletes the database record and position information from the DCO. A smart parameter may be used.
DeleteFingerprint("1002")
method.ret:
Always
True.

p.name: ID
p.qi: ID of fingerprint to delete

method.name: DeleteFingerprints
method.qi: Deletes all fingerprints returned by the SQL statement in the parameter
method.ap: SQL statement used to return a recordset of fingerprints that should be deleted.
method.h:
Deletes all fingerprints returned by the query specified in the parameter. A smart parameter may be used.
Access
- DeleteFingerprints("SELECT * FROM Template WHERE tp_LastHit < dateadd("d",-30,NOW)")
SQL
- DeleteFingerprints("SELECT * FROM Template WHERE tp_LastHit < dateadd(d,-2,GETDATE())")
Oracle
- DeleteFingerprints("SELECT * FROM Template WHERE tp_LastHit < TRUNC(SYSDATE) - 30")
method.ret:
Always
True.

p.name: SQL
p.qi: SQL statement to return a recordset of fingerprints to be deleted

method.name: CloseDatabase
method.qi: Closes connection to the fingerprint database and saves the Setup DCO.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Closes the open database connection and saves the Setup DCO if position information was deleted. The Setup DCO will not be modified if FPXML files are used, or if no fingerprints were deleted.
CloseDatabase()
method.ret:
Always
True.

net.qi: : Actions that integrate Datacap applications with the IBM Content Manager repository.
net.h:
Use these actions to upload documents and index fields into an IBM Content Manager repository.
You can configure the IBM Content Manager Connector actions for the tasks like below:
1) Log in to the IBM Content Manager server.
2) Search for an item in the IBM Content Manager repository based on an attribute and value or item ID that is provided.
3) Create a IBM Content Manager document that is based on the type in the Document Hierarchy as a document or a page.
4) Add, delete, or replace pages in the IBM Content Manager document as needed.
5) Set the attribute value on the IBM Content Manager document.
6) Set the MIME type for the IBM Content Manager document that you are uploading.
7) Create an IBM Content Manager folder in the parent folder where you can upload documents.
8) Set the attribute value on the IBM Content Manager folder.
9) Set the path to the IBM Content Manager folder where you are uploading documents.
10) Upload the document, page, or directory to the IBM Content Manager server.
11) Store the item ID of the uploaded IBM Content Manager document or page in the DCO.
12) Store the ID of the most recently created IBM Content Manager folder into a variable of the Document Hierarchy.
13) Search and download the existing IBM Content Manager documents.
14) After the files are downloaded, you can process them in Datacap application to find any additional data in the content.

method.name: IBMCM_Logon
method.qi: Logs on to a IBM Content Manager server.

p.name: connectioninfo
p.qi: A comma-separated string consisting of three values: 1) the ID of the IBM Content Manager server 2) a valid Content Manager User ID 3) the user’s Password

method.ap:
A comma-separated string consisting of three values:
1) the ID of the IBM Content Manager server.
2) a valid Content Manager User ID.
3) the user’s Password.
Smart parameters are supported for each parameter.
method.h:
Performs the logon to the IBM Content Manager system. This action must be called prior to the
actions that communicate with the Content Manager repository. Connectivity, based on
the requirements of the IBM Content Manager server, needs to be
setup on the machine which is running the Datacap rules.
IBMCM_Logon("IBMCMserver,user1,password")
IBMCM_Logon("IBMCMserver,user1,+@APPVAR(values/adv/MyPassword)")
This example uses the smart parameter @APPVAR to obtain the password from the
advanced value section of the application manager. The custom value name is "MyPassword".
method.lvl: Any level. Usually used at the Batch level.
method.ret:
Action returns
True
if the log on succeeds;
False
if the log on is unsuccessful.
The log on will be unsuccessful if the action cannot find the specified server, or if the user ID or password is invalid.

method.name: IBMCM_Logoff
method.qi: Logs off from the IBM Content Manager server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Performs the logoff from the IBM Content Manager system. This action disconnects from the Content Manager datastore and destroys the reference to the datastore object.
IBMCM_Logon("IBMCMserver,user1,password")
IBMCM_Logoff()
method.ret:
Action returns
True
if the logoff succeeds;
False
if the logoff is unsuccessful.
The logoff will be unsuccessful if logon was not done and a datastore object does not exists.

method.name: IBMCM_CreateItem
method.qi: Creates a IBM CM document based on the item type.

p.name: itemtype
p.qi: Creates a IBM CM document based on the item type.

method.ap:
itemType is a string value of a valid IBM Content Manager Item Type – NOINDEX, for example.
A IBM Content Manger Item Type is equivalent to a Document Class (Index Class).
Smart parameters are supported, such as @BATCHID, @ID, @STATUS, @TYPE, @VALUE,
@JOBID, @JOBNAME, @OPERATOR, @STATION, @TASKID, @TASKNAME, etc. Please refer to
the smart parameter documentation for more information and usage.
method.h:
Creates a IBM Content Manger document based on the item type. This action needs to be called prior to the document
and page upload actions.
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will create an IBM Content Manager document based on the NOINDEX item type,
set the mime type of the uploaded document, then perform the upload.
IBMCM_CreateItem("@P.name")
This example will create an IBM Content Manager document based on the value contained inside the Smart Parameter @P.name at the page level.
Typically, there is one item for each processed document represented by a Document object of the Document Hierarchy,
or for a processed page represented by a Page object.

method.name: IBMCM_CreateChildItem
method.qi: Create a child component under the current document created using IBMCM_CreateItem

p.name: Child Item Information
p.qi: A comma-separated string consisting of two values: 1) childItemName: Create a child component. Creates a child component specified by the childItemName, under the defined object type (IBMCM_CreateItem). 2) count: The number of child component attribute values that will be set.

method.ap:
childItemName is a string value that contains the name of a valid child componet name of the item specified by IBMCM_CreateItem.
The count is the number of child component attributes values that will be set by IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue.
method.h:
This action needs to be called after IBMCM_CreateItem.
IBMCM_CreateItem("ABCInsPlc")
IBMCM_CreateChildItem("Automobiles,1")
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue("Automobiles,ABCVIN,vin123")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will create an IBM Content Manager Child Item based on the name Automobiles.

method.name: IBMCM_CreateFolder
method.qi: Creates a IBM Content Manger folder in the parent folder, based on the specified item type.

p.name: itemType
p.qi: The item type (classification) to create the IBM Content Manger folder. This parameter is required.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

p.name: hasParent
p.qi: If true then the new folder has a parent folder.

method.ap:
If hasParent is False, the new folder will be created without a parent folder and the action will ignore attribute and attributeValue.
If hasParent is true, then it is expected that this folder will be the child of an already existing
folder and that the attribute and attributeValue specify the parent.
If hasParent is true and both attribute and attributeValue are not provided then parent folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
If folder ID is used in the attributeValue parameter, leave the attribute parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported for the string type parameters.
method.ret:
True,
if the folder is successfully created. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Creates a folder in the IBM Content Manger repository. IBMCM_SetAttributeValue can be called following this action
to set attributes of the newly created folder.
Important: If the new folder is based on an item type classfication that contains attributes that are required, an application should use the IBMCM_CreateFolderEx action instead.
IBMCM_CreateFolder will create and save the folder immediately to the repository
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "", False)
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The new folder has no parent and will be placed in the root directory.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215", True)
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The folder will be placed inside the parent folder with ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
IBMCM_CreateFolder(@B.MyItemtye, @B.MyAttribute, @B.MyAttributeValue, True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,@BATCHID")
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType and
will be a child of the folder identified by values from
the batch level Smart Parameters @B.MyAttribute and @B.MyAttributeValue.
IBMCM_CreateFolder(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", False)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder1")
IBMCM_CreateFolder(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder2")
This example will create folder "MyFolder1" and folder "MyFolder2" based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType.
The folder "MyFolder1" folder has no parent. The parent of folder "MyFolder2" is folder "MyFolder1".

method.name: IBMCM_CreateFolderEx
method.qi: Creates a IBM Content Manger folder in the parent folder, based on the specified item type.

p.name: itemType
p.qi: The item type (classification) to create the IBM Content Manager folder. This parameter is required.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

p.name: hasParent
p.qi: If true then the new folder has a parent folder.

method.ap:
If hasParent is False, the new folder will be created without a parent folder and the action will ignore attribute and attributeValue.
If hasParent is true, then it is expected that this folder will be the child of an already existing
folder and that the attribute and attributeValue specify the parent.
If hasParent is true and both attribute and attributeValue are not provided then parent folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
If folder ID is used in the attributeValue parameter, leave the attribute parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported for the string type parameters.
Important: Use this action when the new folder is based on an item type classfication that contains attributes that are required.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx will create the folder in memory and the folder will be saved to the repository once the IBMCM_SaveFolder action has been called
method.ret:
True,
if the folder is successfully created. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Creates a folder in the IBM Content Manger repository. IBMCM_SetAttributeValue can be called following this action
to set attributes of the newly created folder.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx("NOINDEX", "", "", False)
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The new folder has no parent and will be placed in the root directory.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx("NOINDEX", "", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215", True)
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The folder will be placed inside the parent folder with ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx(@B.MyItemtye, @B.MyAttribute, @B.MyAttributeValue, True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,@BATCHID")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType and
will be a child of the folder identified by values from
the batch level Smart Parameters @B.MyAttribute and @B.MyAttributeValue.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", False)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder1")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder2")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create folder "MyFolder1" and folder "MyFolder2" based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType.
The folder "MyFolder1" folder has no parent. The parent of folder "MyFolder2" is folder "MyFolder1".

method.name: IBMCM_SaveFolder
method.qi: Saves folder data from memory to IBM Content Manager.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
IBMCM_SaveFolder is used to save folder creation data to IBM Content Manager that was produced by the call to the IBMCM_CreateFolderEx action.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx("XYZ_ClaimFolder, "", "", False)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("XYZ_ClaimNumber, 12345")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
The sequence creates a folder, assigns that folder with an attribute value of 12345 to the XYZ_ClaimNumber attribute
method.ret:
True,
If the action successfully saves the folder
False
if the action is unable to save the folder.

method.name: IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder
method.qi: Set the destination folder for uploading image files to IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

method.ap:
If both parameters are not provided then destination folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
If folder ID is used in the second parameter, leave the first parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
True,
if the destination folder is successfully set. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Sets the upload destination folder in IBM Content Manger repository. To set the destination to a newly created
folder, first create the folder using IBMCM_CreateFolder and then call IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder
with empty ("") paramters.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder("Department", "Human Resource")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the folder with attribute Department="Human Resource" to upload images to it.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the folder with folder ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215 to upload images to it.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215", true)
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder("", "")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the most recently created folder to upload images to it.

method.name: IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx
method.qi: Set the destination folder for uploading image files to IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: itemType
p.qi: The item type.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

method.ap: If all parameters are not provided then destination folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
method.ret:
True,
if the destination folder is successfully set. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Sets the upload destination folder in IBM Content Manger repository. To set the destination to a newly created
folder, first create the folder using IBMCM_CreateFolder and then call IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx
with empty ("") paramters.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx allows the application to specify an Attribute, Attribute value combination associated with a specific item type, whereas IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder only
allowed an application to specify only an Attribute and Attribute value combination.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx does not support specifying just an item ID, use IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder instead.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx("NOINDEX","SOURCE","Human Resource")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the folder with attribute Department="Human Resource" to upload images to it.

method.name: IBMCM_SetAttributeValue
method.qi: Sets the attribute value on an IBM Content Manager document or IBM Content Manager folder.

p.name: attributesvalues
p.qi: Sets the attribute value on an IBM Content Manager document or IBM Content Manager folder.

method.ap:
attributesvalues is a string value of two comma separated variables.
Name :
The name of the attribute to set.
Value :
The value of the attribute.
An IBM Content Manager Item Type is equivalent to a Document Class (Index Class).
Smart parameters are supported, such as @BATCHID, @ID, @STATUS, @TYPE, @VALUE,
@JOBID, @JOBNAME, @OPERATOR, @STATION, @TASKID, @TASKNAME, etc. Please refer to
the smart parameter documentation for more information and usage.
method.h:
Sets the attribute value on an IBM Content Manager document or folder. The specified attribute must already
be defined on the IBM Content Manager server. The attribute can be applied to a document or to a folder.
This action must follow a previous action that created or identified a folder or document.
This action can be called multiple times to set multiple attributes of the same document or folder.
After the last call to this action, you must call IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC, IBMCM_UploadDCO_Page, or IBMCM_Update actions
to persist the changes to the document item in the Content Manager server.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("MyFolderItemType")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,@BATCHID")
This example will create an IBM Content Manager folder and then set the "Name"
property of the folder to the ID of the current batch.
IBMCM_CreateItem("@B.name")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Author,@D.TheAuthor")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Date,@DATE")
Assuming this is running on the document level, this will create a new document using the batch
level value stored in the DCO variable "name" and set the "Author" attribute to the value stored
in the DCO document level variable named "TheAuthor", then it stores the current date in the
"Date" property.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "3F1234D")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("FirstName,Thomas")
This example will search the IBM Content Manager repository for an existing IBM Content Manager document with EmployeeID=3F1234D.
If the existing IBM Content Manager document is found then its attribute "FirstName" will be set to "Thomas".
To set a DATE attribute, make sure the date value is in one of the date formats accepted by IBM Content Manager.
The valid date formats include:
"yyyy-MM-dd"
"yyyy/MM/dd"
"MM-dd-yyyy"
"MM/dd/yyyy"
You can reformat a date field by calling Validations.IsFieldDateWithReformat on the current field.
Note that the smart parameter @DATE defaults to using the "MM/dd/yyyy" format and does not need to be reformatted.
IsFieldDateWithReformat("yyyy/MM/dd")

method.name: IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue
method.qi: Assigns a child attribute value for a child item. (child component attribute value)

p.name: Child Attribute Information
p.qi: A comma-separated string consisting of three values: 1) childItemName: Create a child component. Creates a child component specified by the childItemName, under the defined object type (IBMCM_CreateItem). 2) attributeName: The attribute name of the child 3) attributeValue: The attribute value

method.ap:
IBMCM_CreateChildItem must be called prior.
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue must be called the same number of times that is specified in IBMCM_CreateChildItem otherwise the child attributes will not be saved
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action needs to be called after IBMCM_CreateItem.
IBMCM_CreateItem("ABCInsPlc")
IBMCM_CreateChildItem("Automobiles,2")
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue("Automobiles,ABCVIN,vin123")
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue("Automobiles,ABCLicensePlate,carlic123")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will create an IBM Content Manager Child Item based on the name Automobiles and assigns two attributes

method.name: IBMCM_UploadDCO_Page
method.qi: Uploads Image files associated with the current Page object of the Document Hierarchy to IBM Content Manager.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Uploads the Image file associated with current Page object of the Document Hierarchy to the IBM Content Manager server.
Additionally, all attributes set using IBMCM_SetAttributeValue will also be persisted.
IBMCM_Logon("cmserver,adminPWD,adminUID")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("USERID, @OPERATOR")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_Page()
This sequence uploads Image files associated with the current Page object of the Document Hierarchy
to IBM Content Manager, and assigns the name of the object – the value of its Type property.
method.ret:
True,
If the action successfully sends the image to the server;
False
if the action is unable to save the image.

method.name: IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC
method.qi: Uploads the set of Images files associated with the current document object of the Document Hierarchy to the IBM Content Manager server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Uploads the Image file(s) associated with current Document object of the Document Hierarchy to IBM Content Manager server.
IBMCM_Logon("cmserver,adminPWD,adminUID")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("USERID, @OPERATOR")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This sequence uploads the set of Images files associated with the current document object
of the Document Hierarchy to the IBM Content Manager server.
Additionally, all attributes set using IBMCM_SetAttributeValue will also be persisted.

method.name: IBMCM_Update
method.qi: Updates the current document object to the IBM Content Manager server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Updates the current document object and its attributes to IBM Content Manager server.
All attributes set using IBMCM_SetAttributeValue will be persisted into the latest version of the document item.
If the document item type has enabled versioning to 'always create new version', then a new version will be create with the changes.
The document item was checked out by the
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue
, and will be checked in by this action.
IBMCM_Logon("cmserver,adminPWD,adminUID")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("USERID, @OPERATOR")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("SOURCE, DATACAP")
IBMCM_Update()
method.lvl: Page level or the field level.

method.name: IBMCM_StoreItemIDinDCO
method.qi: Stores the Item ID of the most recently created folder or most recently uploaded IBM Content Manager item into a variable of the current object of the Document Hierarchy.

p.name: itemID
p.qi: Sets the attribute value on a CM document or folder.

method.h:
Stores the Item ID of the most recently created folder or most recently uploaded
IBM Content Manager document into a variable of the current object of the DCO Hierarchy.
If the variable does not exist, it will be created on the current DCO Hierarchy object.
It may be useful to store the item ID if the object needs to be referenced in following action,
such as setting the upload destination directory.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "", False)
IBMCM_StoreItemIDinDCO("ItemID")
The action above stores the ID of the new IBM Content Manger folder in a variable called “ItemID” in the current object of the DCO Hierarchy.
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
IBMCM_StoreItemIDinDCO("ItemID")
The action above stores the ID of the new IBM Content Manger document in a variable called “ItemID” in the current object of the DCO Hierarchy.
method.ret:
True,
if the Item ID is returned successfully, otherwise
False.

method.name: IBMCM_SearchItem
method.qi: Search for the existing item in IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or item ID.

method.ap:
Both attribute and attributeValue are required parameters.
If item ID is used in the second parameter, leave the first parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Searches for the existing item in IBM Content Manger repository that matches the specified attribute and value.
If an item is found, the current item will be set to it. Otherwise the current item will be set to NULL.
See
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems
action to specify whether to search for folder items only.
By default,
IBMCM_SearchItem
searches only folder items.
IBMCM_SearchItem is used to retrieve a existing IBM Content Manger item before calling other actions to update its attributes
or its content such as IBMCM_AddPages, IBMCM_DeletePages, IBMCM_ReplacePage, IBMCM_SetAttributeValue....
IBMCM_SearchItem("Department", "Human Resource")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Department", "Operations")
This example will search for a folder item with attribute Department="Human Resource" and change to "Operations".
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems("False")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
This example will search for a folder item or a non-folder item with the item ID: A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems("True")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "@P.PageName")
This example will search only for a folder item with item ID derived from a predefined smart parameter, @P.PageName.
The
VScan.Scan
action populates
@P.PageName
to be the filename of the image file without the file extension.
For example, the image file A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.tif will have a PageName of "A1001001A17E08B00210C00000".
This smart parameter can be used to identify the CM8 item ID if the image file name conforms to the convention.

method.name: IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
method.qi: Search and download item content from IBM Content Manger repository.
method.ret:
False,
if any error occurred during parameter validation or searching or downloading.
Otherwise,
True
.
method.h:
Searches for items in IBM Content Manger repository that matches the specified search criteria from the
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria
action.
For each matching item found, if the corresponding ICMBase parts have content,
the content file will be written to the directory set from
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory
.
The output file name will be the CM8 item ID, and the file extension will be the same as the original file extension.
If the original file did not have a file extension, the default extension will be ".tif".
If the file already exists, it will be overwritten.
To limit the number of downloads for each IBMCM_SearchAndDownload action, you can set a limit with
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum
action. The default maximum is 1000.
To add sorting, call
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort
.
To update a download status attribute for the downloaded item, call
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute
action.
After
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
has downloaded the CM8 content files,
scan()
action can be called
to read the files from the same directory.
Important:
to prevent downloading duplicate item content, the task that calls IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownload action should not
be run in a multi-threaded configuration. Instead, use single-threaded tasks.
For information about configuring threads in Rulerunner, see Configuring Rulerunner to run tasks.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT",,,,)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("100")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort("True","Date","ASCENDING")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute("DCStatus")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
SetSourceDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
Scan()
This example will search and download up to 100 APT CM items' content to the directory, C:\datacap\APT\images\input.
The CM query syntax is "/APT [ICMPARTS AND (@DCStatus IS NULL OR @DCStatus=0)] SORTBY(@Date ASCENDING)".
Each item content will have the item ID as the file name. For example, A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.tif.
When the scan() action runs, it will see the populated image directory and process as usual.
method.see:
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute
Scan

method.name: IBMCM_AddPages
method.qi: Add new page(s) to the existing document in IBM Content Manger repository. The new page(s) will be appended to the existing page(s) in the IBM Content Manger document.

p.name: newPage
p.qi: The new page to add.

method.ap:
newPage is required when calling the action at document level.
If newPage = 0, all new pages in the runtime DCO will be added to the existing IBM Content Manger document.
If newPage > 0, only the new page specified by newPage is added.
method.h:
Need to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document from IBM Content Manger repository before calling this action to add new page(s) to it.
The IBMCM_SearchItem action can be used to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
IBMCM_AddPages("2")
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will add the second page (TM000002) in the runtime Document DCO to the existing IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_AddPages("0")
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will add all new pages in the runtime Document DCO to the existing IBM Content Manger document.

method.name: IBMCM_DeletePages
method.qi: Delete page(s) from an existing document in IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: existingPage
p.qi: The existing page to be deleted. This parameter is required.

method.ap:
existingPage is required when calling the action at document level.
If existingPage = 0, all existing pages in the IBM Content Manger document will be deleted. Otherwise, only the existing page specified by existingPage will be deleted.
method.h:
Need to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document from IBM Content Manger repository before calling this action to delete page(s) from it.
The IBMCM_SearchItem action can be used to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document.
Important Notes:
Be careful with this destructive action. It should be used at the batch level to make sure it will be executed once per batch.
If you need to use it at the document or page level, make sure you set filters/conditions to avoid this action being called repeatly.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_DeletePages("2")
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will delete the second page from the IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_DeletePages("0")
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will delete all existing pages from the IBM Content Manger document.

method.name: IBMCM_ReplacePage
method.qi: Replace an existing page in the IBM Content Manger document with a new page in the runtime DCO hierarchy.

p.name: existingPage
p.qi: The existing page in IBM Content Manger document.

p.name: newPage
p.qi: The new page in runtime DCO hierarchy.

method.ap:
When calling at document level, both existingPage and newPage parameter are required.
When calling at page level, the newPage parameter is ignored.
method.h:
Need to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document from IBM Content Manger repository before calling this action.
The IBMCM_SearchItem action can be used to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_ReplacePage("2","3")
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will replace the second page in the existing IBM Content Manger document with the third page (TM000003) in the runtime Document DCO.

method.name: IBMCM_SetMimeType
method.qi: Set mime type for upload document.

p.name: mimeType
p.qi: Mime type.

method.ap: Smart parameter is supported.
method.h:
Set the mime type for upload document. This action is needed when uploading non-tiff files.
When calling at batch/document level, the same mime type will be applied to all files in the batch/document DCO.
This action needs to be called prior to the document and page upload actions.
