com.qi: : Actions that adjust and convert images.
com.h:
The ImageUtilities action library provides actions that can be used at any stage of
a Datacap application to adjust images. If needed, the these actions can be used
at multiple stages in the workflow.
Images can be adjusted for downstream actions or external processes. Adjusting an image
can be useful or necessary for best results. Many work flows have a requirement to archive the
original version of the image. This kind of requirement does not need to limit what can be
done to an image within an application. When an image is altered, the original version the image is
always maintained. The original version can always be retrieved, allowing the original,
and if desired the altered version, to be sent on to final archiving of the batch results.
In some use cases, it may be best to adjust an image to get better recognition, but show the user the original
image or something more presentable. This is possible as well. For example, some image adjustments are
always recommended for recognition and presenting to the user, such as automatic rotation, image deskew
and image equalization. These adjustments create a correctly aligned image for recognition, viewing and click-n-key in a verification panel.
If performing recognition on the image, it may be useful to perform other adjustments, such as conversion
to black and white, or other changes that could improve recognition but make it less pleasing to
a Verify operator. These types of changes can be performed in stages as desired or required. Meaning
that an image could be deskewed and then converted to black and white in separate steps, recognition then processes the deskewed
black and white image, but it is the deskewed color image is presented to the user for verification.
Because the deskew was performed in both versions of the image, it allows recognize text to correctly
align in the Verify panel, allowing click-n-key functionality. After this, the original, unchanged,
image still exists within the batch and can be accessed for archiving or wherever it may be needed.
If the application can ingest fax images, or other non-isotropic images, then it is always a best
first step to use the EqualizeUnbalancedImage action to first correct the image DPI immediately after virtual scan. A non-isotropic
image will have an X dpi that is different from the Y dpi. This difference can cause zones to be incorrect,
it can cause incorrect click-n-key operation in a Verify panel and can prevent correct fingerprint matching.
Using the EqualizeUnbalancedImage will alter only the images that need adjustment, assuring that all
images are isotropic in the rest of the workflow. The action would typically be used
immediately after virtual scanning and before Page Identification or fingerprinting.
If the image is already isotropic, then EqualizeUnbalanceImage will simply leave the original image as-is,
allowing an application to process all images after ingestion to ensure they are correct.
If images are going to under go adjustments such as equalization, rotation, deskew or any other
kind of operation that would require the image to be saved, it is recommended to first
use the SaveAsImage action to save any JPEG images or TIFF images with JPEG compression
to a lossless format. This is strongly recommended if recognition will be performed after
processing because JPEG compression softens character lines, reducing the quality of
recognition. LZW compression is a good general compression that is lossless and works on
any color depth. This compression is recommended if the application will be processing
color images. Fax compression is an excellent compression but it only supports black and white
images which will convert any color image to black and white.
The action SaveImageInformation can be called on each image to determine the compression
within the image, and if it is lossless, then the rules can be configured to save the
image in a lossless format to prevent further quality loss by subsequent actions.
Similarly image rotation and deskew would be performed before Page Identification, while this action
library does not directly perform these actions, there are several actions within Datacap that
perform this image adjustment such as the Image Enhancement ruleset and recognition actions.
Also note that by default, recognition actions can rotate and deskew an image. If an image
has already been deskewed and rotated, then it is recommended to turn off these adjustments
when performing recognition to avoid unnecessary work. See the action help for the recognition
action for instructions on how to disable default image adjustments.
This action library can adjust the dpi and physical size of the image. If the source image
is a photograph, adjusting the dpi can be key to getting recognition results. Recognition engines
will typically perform better if a photo, which typically has a 72 or 96 dpi, is converted to a 200 or 300
dpi. An image that has a designated dpi of 72 or 96 dpi may not recognize even if the X and Y
pixel size is large enough to allow for good quality recognition. Photographs can have enough x and y pixels
for successful recognition but the image dpi is too low and should be adjusted to a higher dpi
to obtain the best recognition results.
Action Overview
A brief overview of each action within this action library:
AppendAllDocumentImages:
Appends all images in the current document into a single, long image.
AppendAllDocumentImagesByType:
Similar to AppendAllDocumentImages but limits the append to only include images with a specific page type.
AppendImageSetAsFirst:
Allows appending of specific images as defined by custom rules within the application. This action
identifies a new first page that will be used the base to which all other pages will be appended.
AppendImageToFirst:
Appends the current image to the image identified by the action ApppendImageSetAsFirst.
ClipFieldToNewImage:
Creates a new page. The image for the new page is determined by the zone coordinates
of the current field, which identify the area of the parent page object image to use as the new image.
The result is a new DCO page object that has a portion of the original page image.
EqualizeUnbalancedImage:
Used to convert a non-isotropic image into an isotropic image.
An isotropic image has identical values for the X and Y DPI. Some actions and
Datacap features will not correctly find the area of an image if the image is non-isotropic.
Typically, fax images are non-isotropic. If the image is already correct, this action
will leave the image unchanged.
IsSupportedImageFile:
Determines if the image associated with the current page file
is a supported type. It can determine this using a simple check of the image type
or attempt to load the image to confirm it will load, uses supported types and compressions
and is not damaged. While all action libraries do not necessarily support every image type
validated by this action, if this action can load it, then the SaveImageAs action
can be used to convert the image to a different format that can then be
processed by an action with a more limited image type support.
RescaleImage:
Can change or correct the DPI of an image and conditionally
scale the image at the same time. When performing recognition on an image
the results may be poor or no recognition may occur if the DPI is less than 150.
SaveImageAs:
Converts and image from one type to another,
changes the color depth of an image, or changes the compression
of an image to a different compression. Useful to change an image
with a format that has limited to client and action support, to
a format that is supported by actions, change an image from a
lossy compression to a loss-less compression to help retain
image quality, etc.
SaveImageAsSettingsJPEG:
Changes the default values used when SaveImageAs
saves an image to JPEG format.
SaveAsSettingsTIFF:
Changes the default values used when SaveImageAs
saves an image to TIFF.
SaveImageInformation:
Obtains one or more image attributes and saves them
in a DCO variable. These include x/y pixels, x/y dpi, x/y physical size,
color depth and compression type. This action is useful to allow application
rules to make decisions based on image attributes. For example, if the
dpi of an image is too low, rules can decide to call an action to adjust the image;
if the image has lossy compression, then the rules can call SaveImageAs to convert
the image to a loss-less compression to prevent further quality loss; if the
image has a particular color depth, the rules could decide to change the color depth
or different sets of image enhancements or adjustments on an image based on the color depth.
SetImageDPIByWidth:
Useful to ensure an image dpi and physical size is correct by adjusting the
image based on the expected width of the image. In some cases, recognition will be poor
or will not recognize at all if the image dpi is too low or if the physical size is incorrect.
Correcting Image DPI and Physical Size
The physical size of an image is determined by the number of pixels in the image multiplied by the
dots per inch (DPI). Some processes rely on accurate image information to perform correctly.
For example, when creating a PDF, the PDF page size is dependent on the calculated physical
size of the image. Recognition quality is also dependent on a correct physical size.
If the correct physical size of the image is known, then it can be corrected, and should be corrected,
if the image information is invalid.
If image sizes vary and the image information is incorrect, a "best guess" will often
be enough to produce good results when creating a PDF or performing recognition.
Correcting Information When The Page Size Is Known:
If all images within a batch or at least all images of a specific page type,
have an expected size, such as a 8.5"x11" page, then the image can be corrected
using the SetImageDPIByWidth action. This action will adjust the images so
that the dimensions are as per the expected size.
For example, all pages that are expected to be of the size 8.5"x11",
can call the action SetImageDPIByWidth by passing a page width of "8.5".
The action will correct the physical size to 8.5", while proportionally correcting the physical height.
For example consider a bank check, if pages are expected to be a 5" long,
then this action can be used to correct the physical width of the check to be 5".
And the height will be adjusted proportionally. Application specific logic
can be used to call the action on specific page types or use other conditions
that determine when the action is to be called to adjust a page size.
If the image is believed to have the correct
size but only the DPI is incorrect, then just the DPI information can be adjusted. The action
also allows the image to be rescaled to the correct size, fixing the image information
at the same time.
This example could be run on every image to adjust it to a page that is 8.5" wide at 300 dpi.
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "300", "True")
This example will adjust an image to 8.5" wide and retain the original DPI value. First
it obtains the original DPI of the image and then passes it to the SetImageDPIByWidth
to adjust the image to the correct physical width while maintaining the original DPI.
SaveImageInformation("", "", "@X.ImgDPI", "", "", "", "", "")
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "@X.ImgDPI", "True")
Another similar example, but only adjusts the image if the DPI is very low.
Adjusting images only when it is determined they are out of a "good" range, is often
a best approach. An application could use multiple tests to determine when
to adjust an image.
SaveImageInformation("", "", "@X.ImgDPI", "", "", "", "", "")
rrCompareNumeric("@.ImgDPI", "˂", 150)
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "@X.ImgDPI", "True")
Other conditions could be performed if there is a chance of other problems with
ingested images. For example, if the pixel dimensions are very large or very small,
the image can be scaled to a typical size. Scaling up a small image to have more pixels
doesn't necessarily make the image sharper, but it can improve recognition and it can
help subsequent image enhancement functionality work better.
Other use cases could adjust the image if the reported physical size is incorrect.
The RescaleImage action will adjust image information and rescale the image.
SaveImageInformation("", "", "", "", "@X.PhysicalWidth", "", "", "")
rrCompareNumeric("@X.PhysicalWidth", "˂", 7)
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "300", "True")
Correcting Image Information When The Page Size Is Not Known:
In a case where all of the pages are expected to be portrait images, as would be ingested
from a scanner, including landscape pages that have not yet been rotated, the following
would adjust an image:
RescaleImage("3300", "2550", "300")
Another similar example, but only adjusts the image if the DPI is very low,
forcing it to rescale to a 300 DPI image.
SaveImageInformation("", "", "@X.ImgDPI", "", "", "", "", "")
rrCompareNumeric("@.ImgDPI", "˂", "150")
RescaleImage("3300", "2550", "300")
This example would retain the same X and Y pixels of the image, while adjusting
the image to a fixed DPI. This also has a test to adjust the image, only
if the DPI is low. Of course, the test could be changed to test other
image attributes, or multiple image attributes.
SaveImageInformation("@X.PixelX", "@X.PixelY", "@X.ImgDPI", "", "", "", "", "")
rrCompareNumeric("@.ImgDPI", "˂", "150")
RescaleImage("@X.PixelY", "@X.PixelX", "300")
Other conditions could be performed if there is a chance of other problems with
ingested images. For example, if the pixel dimensions are vey large or very small,
the image can be scaled to a typical size. Scaling up a small image to have more pixels
doesn't necessarily make the image sharper, but it can improve recognition and it can
help subsequent image enhancement functionality work better.
If the X pixel dimension is wider than the y pixel dimension, then it could be assumed
that the image is a landscape image and could be adjusted using a different
set of actions.
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
For example, "@X" is notation for accessing the current object. "@P" accesses the page object, which
could be the current object, or a parent object. Being evaluated at runtime, allows recognized data
or other batch specific data to be passed to actions or stored as metadata. A smart parameter such
as @DATE could be used to name export files based on the current date. Similar smart parameters
will retrieve the current batch ID, current batch directory, current operator ID, and more.
Smart parameters are a very powerful mechanism of getting data from other areas of the application and copying
it into a new location or passing it as a parameter to an action. It is recommended that the smart parameter
documentation is reviewed to understand the full capabilities available. The top-level help of the
ValidationAndTextAdjustments action library also has information about smart parameters. Some characters such
as +, \ and . also have special smart parameter meaning and may be interpreted as a smart parameter. This
can be controlled using smart parameter syntax.
Refer to the top-level action help for RuleRunnerLogic for the Smart Parameter reference guide.

method.name: AnnotateImage
method.qi: : Places text onto an image, starting at a specified coordinate..
method.ap:
DisplayText:
The text to place onto the current page image.
xCoordinate:
The X coordinate for the starting position of the text on the image.
yCoordinate:
The Y coordinate for the starting position of the text on the image.
FontName:
Optional. Allows specification of the font for the text. The default value is "Times New Roman".
FontSize:
Optional. The font name to use for the annotation text. The default value is 12.
Opaque:
Optional. 0 = Black text. 1 = White text. The default value is 0.
WidthAdjustment:
Optional. Allows adjustment to the width of the text. The default value is 30.
All parameters support smart parameters.
method.h:
Imprints the text you specify onto the current page's image file with a maximum color depth of 24 bits.
By default, this action does not save a backup of the original image. If desired, it is possible to save a copy of the original image.
To retain a backup of the original image, on the current page DCO object set the variable "KeepOriginalImage" to a value of "1".
The backup file appends "_Annotate" to the file name.
AnnotateImage("@BATCHID+ Page:+@ID","5","10", "Arial", "10", "", "100")
This example will place the Batch ID followed by ' Page:' and the calling object ID at the top of the image using the 'Arial' font
with a point size of 10 and a width of 100.
method.see:
This action requires the source image to be 24 bits or less. Refer to the action "SaveImageAs"
in the ImageUtilities action library for an example set of actions that will reduce the color depth for 32 bit images.
Refer to the top level help of the ApplicationObjects action help for an overview of the DCO.
Refer to the top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library for a reference guide for smart parameters.

method.name: AppendAllDocumentImages
method.qi: : Appends all of the images in the document to the first page.
method.ap: None.
method.ret:
True,
if all of the TIFF images within the document have been appended to the end of the first TIFF image.
Otherwise,
False.
This action can fail if too many images are appended together. It is recommended
that the number of images appended are kept to a limited number of images.
method.h:
This action will append (concatenate) all of the images within the document to the first image of the document, creating one long image.
The result of the action will modify the first image in the document to become a single continuous image like this:
Page 1
Page 2
Page 3
If images are appended prior to recognition, the entire page area will be recognized and
click-n-key enabled.
It is highly recommended that this action be used only documents that have a small number of pages, such as
two or three pages per document. The size of the
final composite image can quickly become larger than can be handled by some image viewers and subsequent
actions or verification panels. To keep memory usage to a minimum, it is also recommended that 1-bit Black and White images are used.
Note:
This action only operates on TIFF images.
If it is desired to also concatenate the CCO, then the action MergeCCOsByType in the
AutomaticDocumentFingerprinting action library can be used.
AppendAllImages()
This action will append all images belonging to the current document DCO node.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: AppendAllDocumentImagesByType
method.qi: : Appends all of the images of a specific type within a document.
method.ap: The type of page to merge together. Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
True,
if all of the TIFF images that match the specified type within the document have
been appended to the end of the first matching TIFF image.
Otherwise,
False.
This action can fail if too many images are appended together. It is recommended
that the number of images appended are kept to a limited number of images.
method.h:
This action will append (concatenate) all of the images, that are of the type
specified by the input parameter, that are all within the same document to the first image of that type, creating one long image.
Images are not appended across documents.
Assuming you have a document where the first three pages are all the same matching type,
the result of the action will modify the first image in the document to become a single continuous image like this:
Page 1
Page 2
Page 3
If images are appended prior to recognition, the entire page area will be recognized and
click-n-key enabled.
It is highly recommended that this action be used only documents that have a small number of pages, such as
two or three pages per document. The size of the
final composite image can quickly become larger than can be handled by some image viewers and by subsequent
actions or verification panels. To keep memory usage to a minimum, it is also recommended that 1-bit Black and White images are used.
Note:
This action only operates on TIFF images.
If it is desired to also concatenate the CCO, then the action MergeCCOsByType in the
AutomaticDocumentFingerprinting action library can be used.
AppendAllDocumentImagesByType("PO")
This example will append all of the images within a document that have a page type of 'PO'.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: AppendImageSetAsFirst
method.qi: : Sets the current page as the first page for a concatenated file.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Sets the current page as the start of a new concatenated image. This action is used
in conjunction with AppendImageToFirst to create a single image created by concatenating images to
the bottom of the first image. AppendImageSetAsFirst identifies the first page
and AppendImageToFirst identifies all subsequent pages that will be appended to this page.
The result of the action will modify the first image in the document to become a single continuous image like this:
Page 1
Page 2
Page 3
If images are appended prior to recognition, the entire page area will be recognized and
click-n-key enabled.
It is highly recommended that this action be used only documents that have a small number of pages, such as
two or three pages per document. The size of the
final composite image can quickly become larger than can be handled by some image viewers and possibly subsequent
actions. To keep memory usage to a minimum, it is also recommended that 1-bit Black and White images are used.
Note:
This action only operates on TIFF images.
AppendImage_StartAsNew()
This action would be attached to the first DCO page object that will be
the start of the appended image.
AppendImageToFirst()
This action would be in a rule attached to subsequent page objects
that will be appended to the first image.
method.see:
AppendImageToFirst
Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: AppendImageToFirst
method.qi: : Concatenates the current image to the bottom of an existing image.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action will concatenate the image for the current page to the bottom of the previous
image processed by a call to AppendImageSetAsFirst or AppendImageToFirst. If AppendImageSetAsFirst
has not been called, then the first image encountered will be treated as the starting image.
If images are appended prior to recognition, the entire page area will be recognized and
click-n-key enabled.
The image must be a TIFF.
See AppendImageSetAsFirst for details.
AppendImage_StartAsNew()
This action would be attached to the first DCO page object that will be
the start of the appended image.
AppendImageToFirst()
This action would be in a rule attached to subsequent page objects
that will be appended to the first image.
method.see:
AppendImageSetAsFirst
Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: ClipFieldToNewImage
method.qi: : Clips the field on the Image file to a separate Image file containing only the image from field's coordinates.
method.ap:
NewImagePageType:
The Page Type that is to be assigned to the Image file containing the clipped field and its value.
This should be a page type that is meaningful within the application.
NewImageStatus:
The Page Status to be assigned to the new DCO page object that is created.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action will create a new DCO page object. The image associated with the new page object
is determined by the zone coordinates of the current field object,
clipping the source page image to contain only the section defined by the current field's zone coordinates.
The new DCO page object will be added to the
end of the current parent document object for the page that contains the field that is clipped.
This action does not make any changes to the current field; It simply uses the field zone coordinates to define the boundaries
for the new page.
The new page object that is created from the image segment
will be assigned the initial page type and status that are provided as parameters to this action.
The name of the new image file is based on the name of the source image file by adding a two character suffix to the file name.
"_01" is the suffix of the first new page. For example, if the source page image name is TM000001.tif, the
name of the first new page will be "TM000001_01.tif".
The suffix is then incremented using an alpha-numeric pattern of 0-9 and a-z as additional fields from that same
page are clipped.
The suffix will increment "_02", "_03", etc., until "_09" is reached. From that point, alphabetic characters will be added
such as "_0a", "_0b", with the final suffix of "_zz". If more fields are clipped from the current page than be supported by
the naming pattern, the subsequent pages will not be created and this action will return false.
The new page object will have these DCO property variables created:
SourcePage: The ID of the source page.
SourceImage: The path to the parent image that was clipped for this page's image segment.
SourceField: The ID of the field that was used to determine the boundaries of the image.
SourceValue: The text value, if any, of the source field.
A DCO variable will be created on the parent document object called "ClipPage", containing the ID
of the newly created page. If a parent document object does not exist, then the variable will be created
on the parent page object. This variable will be overwritten if another child field calls this action
to create a new page. If required, the value can be saved before being overwritten, using an action like rrSet after the
call to this action has completed, to copy the value to another location.
If the current field does not have valid zone coordinates, then a new page will not be created. The field's zone
values must be loaded with an action like ReadZonesFPX or ReadZones prior to using this action.
The source page type can be TIFF, PNG, BMP or JPEG. If recognition will be performed on the image, it is recommended
to avoid using a lossy compression, such as JPEG, which can reduce the quality of text recognition. The new image
that is associated with the new page, will be of the same type and compression of the source page. Actions such as
"SaveImageAs" can change type of an image and the compression used within an image.
The following example will create a new page that is a child of the parent document
object. The type of the new page will be "Trailing_Page" and will have an initial status
of "0", which means "OK" or "No Error".
ClipFieldToNewImage("Trailing_Page", "0")
The following example uses smart parameters to get the type and status for the new page.
In this case, the new page will have the same type and status of the parent page
for the current field.
ClipFieldToNewImage("@P.TYPE", @P.STATUS)
method.ret:
False
if either parameter is invalid or if the new page cannot be created. Otherwise
True.
method.see:
ClipFieldToNewImageFileOnly, SaveImageAs
Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.
Refer to the top-level help of the ApplicationObjects action library for information
on the Datacap Object Hierarchy and common object status values.

method.name: ClipFieldToNewImageFileOnly
method.qi: : Clips the field on the Image file to a separate Image file containing only the image sized from a field's zone with a user determined file name.
method.ap:
FieldName:
If called at the page level, specify the name of the child field
whose zone will be used to denote the boundary of the new image, creating a snip of just the field area.
If the action is called on a field, the parameter is ignored.
FileName:
The name of the new clipped image. The full file path must be provided.
to create a snip in the batch directory, use the @PILOT(BATCHDIR) parameter, as shown
in the example.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.lvl: Page or field level. If called on a field, the field must have a parent page object.
method.h:
Creates a new file using a field to clip the current page image. Only the output file is created;
no other objects are created within the batch.
Supported page image types are TIF, PNG, JPG and BMP with a color depth of 24 bits or less. The output file is a TIF file.
The field must have zone coordinates loaded. For example, ReadZones or ReadZonesFPX need to be
used to load the zone position prior to calling this action.
The field must have a parent page object. For example, this action cannot be used on a batch-level field
that has the batch object as the parent.
ClipFieldToNewImageFileOnly("Total", "@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+-Total")
Called on a page object for page TM000001, the above example will find the field called "Total" and create a new
file in the batch directory called "TM000001-Total.tif". The image will be a snip of the page image using the
zoned area of the "Total" field.
ClipFieldToNewImageFileOnly("", "@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@P.ID+-Amount")
Called on a field object for page TM000001, the above example will create a file in the batch directory called
"TM000001-Amount.tif". The image will be a snip of the page image using the zoned area of the current field.
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, else
False
if an error occurred.
method.see: ClipFieldToNewImage

method.name: EqualizeUnbalancedImage
method.qi: : Adjusts a non-isotropic image into an isotropic image.
method.ap:
Integer value which determines the cut-off point for the resolution which should be equalized. The
value must be between 0 - 99.
EqualizeUnbalancedImage(0)
, for example, specifies that there is no cut-off point:
all images will be subject to equalization. Any image that already has
an X and Y DPI that are identical will not be adjusted.
EqualizeUnbalancedImage(20)
establishes a cut-off point of 200(x)/180(y). This
means that the action will equalize all images with this resolution ratio and more (200/180,
200/160 etc.) - but will ignore all images with balance ratios less than 200/180 (in this example.)
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
False
if the parameter is not numeric or if the rule containing the action is not bound
to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy. Otherwise,
True.
method.h:
Resolves differences in the dpi (dots per inch) resolutions along the horizontal (X) and
vertical (Y) planes of the current page image so the x dpi and y dpi are identical.
Images processed by Datacap work best when the x dpi and y dpi of the image
are identical, making the image an isotropic image.
The image is adjusted so the smaller dpi value of the image is scaled to match the larger
dpi value. For example, if an image is 200x180 dpi, and this action is used with
a parameter of 0 to adjust all images that are non-isotropic, the image will be adjusted to
200x200 dpi, scaling the image on only the smaller axis to make the image isotropic.
If the x and y dpi values of an image
are different, then some actions and clients may not operate as
expected. For example, using click-n-key in a client may not correctly
identify the location of the text on the page. Locations of fields
could also be incorrect when mapped to an image.
Images electronically ingested through fax servers are typically a non-isotropic
images, although the problem is not necessarily limited to images created from
faxing. If a batch could potentially ingest images are non-isotropic, then
this action should be used to inspect and adjust each image within the batch.
If the image associated with the current page is isotropic, then the action
will not perform any adjustments to the image.
Standard Mode fax resolution in Dots per Inch (DPI) is 204/98; Fine Mode fax
resolution is 204/196.
If fingerprinting is used in the application, this action must be used
to correct the image dpi prior to matching fingerprints or creating
new fingerprints. Images must be isotropic prior to being added as a fingerprint. Likewise, images
must be isotropic when searching for a matching fingerprint.
This action should be used prior to performing
recognition or other image manipulation. A typical place this action
would be used is the first actions that
are run after a scan or virtual scan ruleset. If using rules to perform virtual scan,
then a second ruleset can be added to the VScan task to equalize all images of
page type "Other". Alternatively, the action could be run in a first rule
of the next task, which is typically a "PageID" task.
EqualizeUnbalancedImage("0")
This example would be run on a rule that is attached to a page object.
If it was attached to the "Other" page type, then after VScan,
each of the newly ingested images will be examined by EqualizeUnbalancedImage
and if the x and y dpi do not match, the image will be adjusted.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: IsSupportedImageFile
method.qi: : Checks the current page file extension to determine if it is a supported format.
method.ap:
LoadImage:
A Boolean that determines the type of test to perform.
True: Tests the validity of the image by attempting to load the image.
False: Only a file extension check is performed to determine if it is a supported file type.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action tests a file to determine if the file format is supported. The extension is checked to
determine if it denotes a supported image type. If True is passed as a parameter, it also attempts to load
the image.
Using False as a parameter will greatly improve the speed of this action. A parameter of True will
slow down the processing, especially if the images are very large, but it will add an extra confirmation
that the file is not corrupted and confirm that any subformat of the file type, such as compression type,
is also supported.
This action can help an application determine if the image is a valid image and control the subsequent
flow of the rules based on this action returning true or false. For example, if the image is not
support, the page could be marked with a "Deleted" status or other steps could be taken based
on the use case.
Some actions support only specific file formats or color depths. If this action can load an image, it does not
mean every action and client support the image. For example,
this action can load an image with a 32 bit color depth (BPP : Bits Per Pixel). Most actions and clients do not support
32 bit color. This action will return true if it successfully loads a 32 bit color image, such as a TIFF or JPEG.
If the parameter is "True" and the image is successfully loaded, then the action will save the color depth in the
current DCO with the variable name "ImageBPP". If desired, this variable could be tested with an action such as rrCompareNumeric
to determine if the color depth is 24 bits or less. If the color depth is 32, then it is recommended to use
the SaveImageAs action to reduce the color depth of the image. The Image Enhancement ruleset also has the ability
to reduce the color depth.
If the image can be loaded by this action, then the SaveImageAs action can also be used to convert the image
to a type or color depth supported by subsequent actions. Refer to the guide "Datacap supported image types"
in the Datacap Knowledge base documentation.
The action SaveImageInformation will load an image and save a number of properties to the DCO. This
information can be used by an application to store the information or perform specific actions
based on the saved data.
IsSupportedImageFile("True")
This example will load the image associated with the current page object and return
true if the image was loaded successfully.
method.ret:
True,
if parameter is valid, the action is called at the page level and the page's IMAGEFILE variable
(set at scan time by the scan tasks) points to a file whose format
is supported (can be displayed) by the Image view control.
Otherwise
False.
method.see:
SaveImageAs, SaveImageInformation
Refer to the top-level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: OverlayCurrentImageOnBackgroundImage
method.qi: : Combines the current image with the image file specified by the SetBackgroundImage action into a new image replacing the current image. This action is used to reinstate a form background that was 'dropped out' during scanning.
method.ap:
BackgroundImageFileName:
The full path to the file that will be used as the background image for the current page image.
Halo:
True or false. True adds white pixels to the current image where they would otherwise touch pixels from the
background. This provides a white area around existing pixels.
All parameters support smart parameters.
method.h:
This action overlays the current image onto the background image. A typical use for this action is when
an application processes a form, but the current page contains only the data without the form lines.
For example, the form may be a dropout form where scanning has removed the form lines, leaving only the
text on the current page image. This action will overlay the current image over a blank form
to present an image to the user that resembles the original form.
The action requires the dpi and relative pixel size of the background image and current page image
to be identical. The current image and the background image must be 1 bit, black and white, images.
The action requires that a field called "Image_Offset" exists on the current page and that field
contains two comma separated integers that represent the x and y offset of the current page
relative to the background form image. For example, a value of 0,0 would overlay the page on the form
without any adjustment. A value of 3,-10 would move the current page right 3 pixels and up 10 pixels.
The offset value must exist, even if no adjustment is required.
The current image becomes the new merged image. If it is necessary to retain the original image,
the CopyFile action in the FileIO action library can be used to first save a copy of the file.
CopyFile("@X.IMAGEFILE", "@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.Original.tif")
OverlayCurrentImageOnBackgroundImage("c:\ParentDir\mclaims\process\hcfa\hcfa.tif", "False")
This example first uses CopyFile to backup the original image, then applies the overlay.
It is not necessary to first backup the original image. It is shown here as an example of how
it can be done, should it be necessary in an application.
method.ret:
False
if the action is not applied to a
Page
object, if it cannot locate
the Background Image file, or if the action encounters an error.
Otherwise,
True.

method.name: RedactCoordinates
method.qi: : Redacts the current page image at specific coordinates or on a field, allowing optional text on the redacted area.
method.ap:
FillColor:
The fill color to use for the redaction. Specified values must be either "White" or "Black".
NewText:
Optional. The text to include in the redaction area.
TopLeftX:
The top left X coordinate in pixels.
TopLeftY:
The top left Y coordinate in pixels.
BottomRightX:
The bottom right X coordinate in pixels.
BottomRightY:
The bottom right Y coordinate in pixels.
BackupFileNameSuffix:
Optional. If specified, the current image will be first copied to
a new file name, adding the provided text as a suffix to the file name. For example:
a value of "-BeforeRedaction" will create a backup file named "TM000001-BeforeRedaction.tif".
The provided coordinates are used when called on a page object.
When called on a field object, the coordinates are ignored, and the field’s zone coordinates are used.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action overlays a black, or white rectangle on the image. A default text value may optionally be applied to the overlay.
The action does not guarantee that the text fits into the redaction area. It is up to the application developer to
confirm that the area is large enough to contain the specified text.
If run on the field level, the entire field will be redacted and the last four X/Y parameters will be ignored.
If run on the page level the last four parameters to specify the location must be provided.
The image can have a maximum bit depth of 24 bits.
RedactCoordinates("black","","0","0","100","100", "-BeforeRedaction")
Called at the page level, this will apply a black square overlay on the top left of the image.
If the current page file is TM000001.tif, the original image will be copied to a
file called "TM000001-BeforeRedaction.tif".
RedactCoordinates("White","Hello","","","","","")
Called at the field level, this will apply a white square overlay on the coordinates for the current field,
and imprint the word "Hello". A backup file will not be created. Because it is called on a field
object, the coordinates are not used. The field must have zone coordinates set.

method.name: RedactField
method.qi: : Redacts the area on the page based on the zone position of the current field.
method.ap:
FieldName: If called at the page level, specify the name of the child field to redact.
If the action is called on a field, the parameter is ignored.
Color: The color to paint the redaction area. Valid values are 'White' or 'Black'. If not specified,
or if the value is invalid, white is the default.
BackupPostFileName: The text to append to the file name to create a backup file before performing
the redaction. For example, if the value is "-BeforeRedact" and the current page file is "TM000001.tif",
the name of the backup file will be "TM000001-BeforeRedact.tif". The new file will be created
in the batch directory. If this parameter is blank,
a backup file will not be created. If the file already exists, it will be overwritten.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
The area on the current page image will be redacted, colored over, in the zone area identified by the
specified field. If called on a page object, the name of the field needs to be specified. If called
on a field, the current field zone will be used regardless of the name specified.
The zone area can be redacted in White or Black.
The action will optionally create a backup file prior to performing the redaction. One use could be
to redact the image so it can be shown to a user with a redaction, but still maintain the original image.
Supported page image types are TIF, PNG, JPG and BMP with a color depth of 24 bits or less.
The field must have zone coordinates loaded. For example, ReadZones or ReadZonesFPX need to be
used to load the zone position prior to calling this action.
The field must have a parent page object. For example, this action cannot be used on a batch-level field
that has the batch object as the parent.
RedactField("SSN", "Black", "")
When called on a page objet, the above example will redact the "SSN" field using the color black. A backup file will not be created.
RedactField("", "White", "-BeforeRedaction")
When called on a field object, the area of the current field will be redacted on the page image with white.
A backup of the page image will be created before the redaction occurs. If the current page is TM000001.tif,
then the backup file name will be "TM000001-BeforeRedaction.tif".
method.lvl: Page or field level. If called on a field, the field must have a parent page object.
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, otherwise
False
if an error occurred.
method.see: ReadZones, ReadZonesFPX

method.name: RescaleImage
method.qi: : Adjusts image for the current page to the specified size.
method.ap:
ImageHeight:
Output Height of the page in pixels. If blank, defaults to 3300 pixels.
ImageWidth:
Output Width of the page in pixels. If blank, defaults to 2550 pixels.
ImageDPI:
The new DPI of the image. If blank, defaults to 300 dpi.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Scales the image and sets the DPI to the specified values.
This will force an image to be adjusted to a specific size and DPI, additionally
determining the physical size of the image, such as an 8.5" x 11" page scan.
RescaleImage(3300, 2550, 300)
This action scales the current page to a 300 dpi image that has a physical
size of 11"x8.5".
SaveImageInformation("@X.CurrentWidth","@X.CurrentHeight","","","","","","")
RescaleImage(@X.CurrentHeight, @X.CurrentWidth, 300)
If it is desired to adjust only one aspect of the image and keep the other values the same
as the source image, then SaveImageInformation could first be called to obtain the image
information and then the value can be passed as a parameter to this action.
This example keeps the pixel dimensions of the image the same but adjusts
the DPI to 300. It doesn't scale the image, just changes the DPI. If the image already
has a large pixel size but has a low resolution, as with a photograph, this can adjust the DPI.
If the image was a very small image, then it would likely be better to scale up the image
instead of just changing the DPI. That could help improve recognition, it could also help
to use a sharpening enhancement on such an image.
method.lvl: Page level only, and the page must refer to a valid single page image file
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, else
False
if any error occurred.
method.see:
EqualizeUnbalancedImage, SetImageDPIByWidth, SaveImageInformation.
Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library, including how to
correct an image with an invalid DPI.

method.name: SaveImageAs
method.qi: : Saves a new copy of the image, allowing adjustment of image type, color depth and compression.
method.ap:
NewFileType:
The file type of the new image. Supported types: TIF, JPG, BMP, PNG.
NewColorDepth:
The new color depth for the image. Values: 0, 1, 8, 24.
0: Preserve the same color depth as the source image. If blank, 0 is used as the default value. If the source
image is a 32 bit color image, then the maximum bit depth of the saved image is 24 bits per pixel.
1, 8, 24: The new bits per pixel of the saved image.
Palette:
The color palette to use for the saved image. The following values are accepted: Optimized, Fixed and Gray.
Optimized: A palette with the colors optimized for the image. If not specified, this is the default value.
Fixed: A fixed color palette.
Gray: A grayscale palette.
Dither:
The dot pattern used when reducing the color depth of an image. The following values are accepted:
Binarize1, Binarize2, FS, None, Optimized and Ordered
Binarize1: An optimized conversion to remove background information, leaving foreground information, such as dark text.
This is usually the best setting to convert an image or photo to black and white that will be used for text recognition.
No dithering is performed. This will result in a black and white image. If dither is not provided, then this
is the default method for saving 1 bit images.
Binarize2: Similar to Binarize1, but may be slightly faster. No dithering is performed. This will result in a
black and white image.
FS: Uses the Floyd-Steinberg algorithm to dither a color image into black and white. Do not use this setting
if the image will be subsequently recognized. Dither should only be used to keep a "shaded" look to the
image and when the image will not be subsequently used in a recognition step.
None: No dithering is performed. This is similar to the Binarize methods, but may not yeld results as good as Binarize1
for performing text recognition. Unlike Binarize, this setting is not limited to black and white images.
Optimized: The image engine determines how to dither the image. A dithered image will produce a black and white image
that simulates a grayscale picture, similar to a newspaper. This method is recommended to convert a photo to black
and white with the intention to retain the photographic image while converting it to a
black and white image. This is the default value if the target color depth is greater than 1.
If performing recognition on the image, instead use
Binarize1 to convert the image to black and white or use "None" when down converting
to 24 bit or 8 bits per pixel.
Ordered: An alternative method of converting a color image to a black and white dithered photo.
Again, it is not recommended to this setting if the image will be subsequently recognized.
BackupSuffix:
When the current image is saved, the original image will be retained.
If the new saved image will have the same name as the original source image, the source
image will be saved by adding a suffix to the name. By default, the suffix ".original"
will be added to the file name. For example, if the source image name is "TM000001.tif"
then the original image will be saved as "TM000001.original.tif" and the new image will
be saved as "TM000001.tif". If desired, this suffix can be changed using this parameter.
For example, passing the value ".backup" will save the original image as "TM000001.backup.tif".
If the source image is a different type, such as "TM000001.jpg" and the new image is a different
type, such as "TM000001.TIF", then the source image will not conflict with the new saved image
and the source image name will not be changed. If it is desired to change the name of
the source image in this case, then the FileIO actions can be used to rename
the original file as desired.
DeleteOriginal:
"True" or "False". If this parameter is set to "True", then
the original image will not be saved in the batch. If this parameter is set to "False",
then the original image will be retained, keeping it available for later use within
the batch, such as for archiving. If this parameter is not provided, then it will
default to "False" and the original image will be saved.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action will update the current image associated with the page object,
changing any one or all of these image attributes:
• Image Format
• Compression type
• Color depth / Bits per pixel
Input formats: BMP, DIB, EMF, GIF, JPEG, JPEG2000, PNG, TIF, WMF.
Output formats: BMP, PNG, JPEG, TIF.
The current image can be saved as the same file type, changing just the compression
or color depth of the image. For example, a TIF with JPEG compression can be resaved as
a TIF with LZW compression. The current image
can also be changed to a new file type such as converting a JPEG image
to a TIFF image.
The source image can have a color depth up to 32 bits per pixel. The image
can be saved in a color depth up to 24 bits per pixel. Some Datacap actions
have specific color depth requirements, this action can be used to adjust
the current image to different color depths as required by subsequent actions
and rulesets.
If the final image file type is the same as the source image file type,
the action will first back up the original image, giving it a unique name
by adding the suffix ".original" to the file name. For example, if the source
file name is "TM000001.tif" and the image is being saved as a TIF, then the original
file will be saved as "TM000001.orignal.tif" and the file "TM000001.tif" will be
the new updated file.
The image file associated with the current page object can be convert to one
of these file types: BMP, PNG, TIF and JPEG. Bitmap, BMP, images are always
saved without compression, which can make them large. Portable Network Graphics,
PNG, use a loss less compression that works on a 1 bit, 8 bit or 24 bit image.
The actions SaveImageSettingsTIFF and SaveImageSettingsJPEG
can be called prior to this action to adjust the file
format used to save the image when saving as a TIF or JPG image.
For example, the default file compression for TIF images is LZW.
By first calling SaveImageSettingsTIFF, the default compression can be changed for
when the SaveImageAs action saves a file as a TIFF. For example, if converting to a
black and white image, Group 3 or Group 4 can be configured as the compression
type as it is an efficient and lossless method for black and white images.
If an application is ingesting JPEG images or TIF images with JPEG compression, and these
images will be used for recognition, it is highly recommended to convert the image
to a lossless format, such as a TIF with LZW compression, immediately after images are
ingested into a batch. Subsequent actions can then operate on the new TIF image using
lossless compression. The original version of the image is always available, if necessary,
for viewing in a Verification panel or for exporting at the end of the batch.
JPEG compression is intended for photographs, not for images
that contain text to be recognized. JPEG compression will make crisp lines on letters
fuzzy, reducing the quality of the recognition. As the image is further manipulated, such as with
image enhancement, rotation, etc., and resaved again with JPEG compression,
additional quality will be lost with each save, even
if compression is set to a high quality.
It may be useful to use the action SaveImageInformation along with this action.
SaveImageInformation will read image attributes and store the values in the DCO.
Application rules can be configured to act on this information. For example,
if an image has a color depth greater than 24 bits per pixel, then the rules could
call SaveImageAs to reduce the color depth of the image.
The SaveImageInformation action can also be used to obtain the compression used
within the image. For example, rules can be arranged to check the current
image compression type and if the compression type is "Jpeg", then the rules can call
SaveImageAs only on those images to save them with a lossless compression and
if the image already has a lossless compression, then the image can be left as-is.
Example 1:
SaveImageInformation("","","","","","","","@X.ImgCompression")
rrCompareCase("Jpeg", "@X.ImgCompression", "False")
SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF("LZW")
SaveImageAs("TIF","0","","","","")
This example checks to see if the current TIFF image
is using JPEG compression. If it does have JPEG compression, the actions
configure the compression for saved TIF images to LZW using the
action SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF. The example is shown in the same rule as the
rule as SaveImageAs. If the settings are intended to be the same for all pages,
then it would be more efficient to place SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF in a rule
attached to the batch open event. That would allow the action to be called
only once instead of over and over for each page.
The SaveImageAs action will convert the current page image to a TIF using
LZW compression. It does not matter if the source image is a TIF or
a different image type, such as JPEG or PNG.
The parameter of 0 will retain the same color depth as
the original image. If the image was black and white, it will stay a
1 bit black and white image. If the source image was 24 bit color,
it will be saved as 24 bit color. This example is a good way to convert images
that may be saved using a lossy compression, such as JPEG, to a lossless
compression to limit further degradation of quality caused
by a lossless compression.
Example 2:
SaveImageAsSettingsJPEG("100","False","True")
SaveImageAs("JPEG","0","Optimized","Optimized",".Old","False")
This example converts the current image to a JPEG image. Although the color depth
parameter is set to "0", which means to retain the original color depth, JPEG
images can only be saved as 8 bit grayscale or 24 bit color. If the source image
is 1 bit, then it will be upconverted. While it will still look black and white,
it will be converted to a 24 bit color depth. This example also uses a custom
extension, ".Old", to back up the original file name, should the new file name
and the old file name evaluate to the same name.
Again, while this example shows the SaveImageAsSettingsJPEG being called
in the same rule function just prior to SaveImageAs, if all pages are going
to have the same settings, then this action can be called at the document or batch
level and the setting will stay in effect for the remainder of the current task
profile. Calling this action at a higher level will avoid unnecessarily
calling this action over and over for each
page object. If each page object may need different parameters when saved, then
calling the action with each page would be necessary.
It is recommended to save as a JPEG or a TIF with JPEG compression if processing
photos that will not be used for text recognition. If performing text recognition
on an image, or image enhancements, it is recommended to first convert to a
lossless compression and do not use the JPEG image format.
Example 3:
rrSet("Group4", "@X.Compression")
rrSet("TIF", "@X.NewFileType")
rrSet("True", "@X.DeleteOriginal")
SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF(@X.Compression)
SaveImageAs("@X,NewFileType","1","","","","@X.DeleteOriginal")
This is another example that will convert the current page image to a TIF, regardless
of the original format. It will also convert the image to a black and white image
with Group 4 fax compression, which is an efficient and lossless black and white
compression.
This example demonstrates using smart parameters to pass values to the actions.
The example illustrates how a variable, NewFileType, is passed as a smart parameter to the action at runtime.
The value of the variable "NewFileType" will be obtained and used as the input parameter. In a realistic
example, it would be likely that some earlier rule or action would have set the value
to the DCO variable "NewFileType"
prior to calling the action. For example, a value could have been previously
set in a field or be data that was recognized into a field and then the reference
to a field passed as the parameter, using the field's current runtime value as input
to the action. Another approach could have the values configured in the
setup DCO, which can be set within Datacap Studio, so they pre-exist for the object and then the actions pull the value
at runtime from a pre-configured variable.
Example 4:
SaveImageInformation("","","","","","","@P.BitDepth","")
rrCompare("@P.BitDepth", "32")
SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF("LZW")
SaveImageAs("tif", "24", "", "", ".prebitdepth", "False)
This example is run on a page object and reduces the color depth of the image
associated with the page, if the image is a 32 bit color image. It is required that the associated page file is an image.
This series of steps is useful because some actions do not support 32 bit color images. If the current image is 32 bit color,
the image is saved as a TIF image with a color depth of 24 bits and backup the original image is saved by appending ".prebitdepth" to the filename.
The LZW compression is used because it is a loss-less compression
and it supports any color depth. If the current image is 24 bits or less, then the rrCompare will return false causing the action
flow to stop in this current function and jump to the next function, if one exists. Images of 24 bits or lower are left unchanged
by this series of actions.
method.lvl: Page level only, and the page must refer to a valid single page image file
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, else
False
if any error occurred.
method.see:
SaveImageSettingsTIFF, SaveImageSettingsJPEG, and SaveImageSettingsBMP.
Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library.

method.name: SaveImageAsSettingsJPEG
method.qi: : Configures the settings used when saving an image as a JPEG image.
method.ap:
Quality:
Controls the compression of the saved JPEG. Valid values are 0-100 with 0 as the lowest quality
with the highest compression and 100 as the highest quality and the lowest amount of compression.
If this action is not called, or if the value is not provided, this value defaults to 100.
Grayscale:
"False" saves the image as color, "True" saves the image as grayscale.
If this action is not called or if the value is not provided, this value defaults to False.
Progress:
"False" the image is not saved as a Progressive image, "True" saves the image as a
progressive image.
If this action is not called or if the value is not provided, this value defaults to False.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets the JPEG file settings for the "SaveImageAs" action when
the image saved as a JPEG format and when saving a TIFF image with
JPEG compression.
JPEG compression does not support 1 bit images. The image must be color or grayscale.
If an application is ingesting JPEG images or TIF images with JPEG compression, and these
images will be used for recognition, it is highly recommended to convert the image
to a lossless format, such as a TIF with LZW compression, immediately after images are
ingested into a batch. Subsequent actions can then operate on the new TIF image using
lossless compression. The original version of the image is always available, if necessary,
for viewing in a Verify panel or for exporting at the end of the batch.
JPEG compression is intended for photographs, not for images
that contain text to be recognized. JPEG compression will make crisp lines on letters
fuzzy, reducing the quality of the recognition. As the image is further manipulated, such as with
image enhancement, rotation, etc., and resaved again with JPEG compression,
additional quality will be lost with each save, even
if compression is set to a high quality.
When this action is called, the settings are retained for the current task profile.
If SaveImageAs is used later
in a subsequent task profile, then this action must be called again to change
the default value.
SaveImageAsSettingsJPEG("100","False","True")
SaveImageAs("JPEG","0","Optimized","Optimized",".Old","False")
This example converts the current image to a JPEG image. Although the color depth
parameter is set to "0", which means to retain the original color depth, JPEG
images can only be saved as 8 bit grayscale or 24 bit color. If the source image
is 1 bit, then it will be upconverted. While it will still look black and white,
it will be converted to a 24 bit color depth. This example also uses a custom
extension, ".Old", to back up the original file name, should the new file name
and the old file name evaluate to the same name.
Again, while this example shows the SaveImageAsSettingsJPEG being called
in the same rule function just prior to SaveImageAs, if all pages are going
to have the same settings, then this action can be called at the document or batch
level and the setting will stay in effect for the remainder of the current task
profile. Calling this action at a higher level will avoid unnecessarily
calling this action over and over for each
page object. If each page object may need different parameters when saved, then
calling the action with each page would be necessary.
It is recommended to save as a JPEG or a TIF with JPEG compression if processing
photos that will not be used for text recognition. If performing text recognition
on an image, or image enhancements, it is recommended to first convert to a
lossless compression.
method.lvl: Page level only, and the page must refer to a valid single page image file
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, else
False
if any error occurred.
method.see:
This action is used in conjunction with the action "SaveImageAs".
Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library.

method.name: SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF
method.qi: : Configures the setting when saving an image as a TIFF image.
method.ap:
Compression:
The compression to use for the TIFF image.
Valid Compressions:
"None" : No compression
"RLE" : Run Length Encoding
"LZW" : Lempel-Ziv-Welch
"PackBits" : Packed bits
"Deflate" : Deflate
"Group3" : Group 3 Fax
"Group4" : Group 4 Fax
"Jpeg" : JPEG lossy compression
If this action is not called or if the value is not proved, this value defaults to LZW.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets the TIFF file settings for the "SaveImageAs" action when
the image saved as a TIFF image.
If using a black and white image, the group 3 or group 4 image compressions are recommended.
If using a grayscale or color image, then LZW compression is recommended. These
compressions are loss-less compressions. LZW is also fine for compressing black
and white images, however group 4 compression can be more efficient.
If an application is ingesting JPEG images or TIF images with JPEG compression, and these
images will be used for recognition, it is highly recommended to convert the image
to a lossless format, such as a TIF with LZW compression, immediately after images are
ingested into a batch. Subsequent actions can then operate on the new TIF image using
lossless compression. The original version of the image is always available, if necessary,
for viewing in a Verify panel or for exporting at the end of the batch.
JPEG compression is intended for photographs, not for images
that contain text to be recognized. JPEG compression will make crisp lines on letters
fuzzy, reducing the quality of the recognition. As the image is further manipulated, such as with
image enhancement, rotation, etc., and resaved again with JPEG compression,
additional quality will be lost with each save, even
if compression is set to a high quality.
When this action is called, the settings are retained for the current task profile.
If SaveImageAs is used later
in a subsequent task profile, then this action must be called again to change
the default value.
SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF("LZW")
SaveImageAs("TIF","0","","","","")
This example configures the compression for saved TIF images to LZW using the
action SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF. The example is shown in the same rule as the
rule as SaveImageAs. If the settings are intended to be the same for all pages,
then it would be more efficient to place SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF in a rule
attached to the batch open event. That would allow the action to be called
only once instead of over and over for each page.
The SaveImageAs action will convert the current page image to a TIF using
LZW compression. It does not matter if the source image is a TIF or
a different image type, such as JPEG or PNG.
The parameter of 0 will retain the same color depth as
the original image. If the image was black and white, it will stay a
1 bit black and white image. If the source image was 24 bit color,
it will be saved as 24 bit color. This example is a good way to convert images
that may be saved using a lossy compression, such as JPEG, to a lossless
compression to limit further degradation of quality caused
by a lossless compression.
method.lvl: Page level only, and the page must refer to a valid single page image file
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, else
False
if any error occurred.
method.see:
This action is used in conjunction with the action "SaveImageAs".
Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library.

method.name: SetImageDPIByWidth
method.qi: : Adjusts the dpi of the image and optionally resizes based on the expected physical size.
method.ap:
ImageWidth:
Physical width of the page in inches. If not specified, the value will default to 8.5 inches.
ImageDPI:
The target DPI for the updated image. If not specified, the value will default to 300 dpi.
Rescale:
Indicates if the image should be rescaled.
True - rescale image width and height to match the specified dpi and physical size,
False - do not rescale the page, just set the DPI.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action is useful for images that
do not have a correctly specified DPI or need to be resized based on the expected width.
This action will adjust the DPI and width of the image to the specified DPI.
The image can also be resized to the correct logical size based on the expected physical width in inches.
When the rescale parameter is true, the image size is adjusted.
The image is scaled proportionally in the horizontal and vertical directions based on the
width that has been specified for the image. The final image will have the specified DPI and the pixel width and height
will be scaled to the specified logical size.
Photos typically have a DPI of 72 or 96. While cameras often have a high pixel count, they are
unable to correctly set the DPI and physical size of an image. If a camera is used to take a
picture of a 8.5"x11" page or a 5" check, the camera cannot correctly set the image properties
that reflect the true size of the object. SetImageDPIByWidth can correct these kinds of images.
It is typically best to first deskew the image then crop the image in an attempt to retain
only the page or check that was photographed. This action will then adjust the image
to correct the DPI and physical size. This is important if recognition will be performed on the
image. If a photo has a high resolution, recognition can fail if the DPI the image is
not within the range of 200 to 300 and if the calculated physical size of the image is
incorrect.
SetImageDPIByWidth("6", "", "True")
This example is on a page level rule and sets the image width to 6 inches with
a default DPI of 300 while rescaling the image as necessary.
Typically, it is best to rescale the image.
SetImageDPIByWidth("6", "300", "False")
This example is on a page level rule and sets the image width to 6 inches without rescaling the image. This will just
change the dimensions, leaving the number of pixels unchanged within the image.
SaveImageInformation("","","@P.DPIx","","","","","")
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "@P.DPIx", "True")
This example adjust the image to 8.5" wide and keeps the original DPI of the image.
First the action SaveImageInformation obtains the current DPI of the image and
stores it in a DCO variable called DPIx. The variable name can be anything
meaningful. If the variable does not exist, it will be created. If it does exist,
the current value will be overwritten with the new value. Next the action
SetImageDPIByWidth adjusts the image to ensure it is 8.5" wide and passes
in the current DPI of the image. This will adjust the image so it is 8.5"
wide, keeping the original DPI of the image.
SaveImageInformation("","","@P.DPIx","","","","","")
rrCompareNumeric("180",>,"@P.DPIx")
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "@P.DPIx", "True")
This example is similar to the previous example.
The difference is that rrCompareNumeric is used to first check
the DPI of the image. The image will be adjusted only
if the DPI is 180 or less.
SaveImageInformation("","","","","@P.PhysicalWidth","","","")
SetImageDPIByWidth("@P.PhysicalWidth", "300", "True")
This example maintains the same physical width but adjusts the DPI of the image
to 300. The technique using SaveImageInformation and smart parameters is similar to the example above.
If the image is a low resolution image, increasing the DPI of the image
can improve recognition. While it doesn't make the image sharper
it can still help recognition and it can cause some image enhancement
operations to work better prior to performing recognition.
method.lvl: Page level only, and the page must refer to a valid single page image file
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, otherwise
False
if any error occurred.
method.see:
RescaleImage
Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library, including examples for how to correct
an image with an invalid DPI.

method.name: SaveImageInformation
method.qi: : Obtains the properties of an image and stores them in user variables within the DCO.
method.ap:
ImageWidth:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the image width in pixels. If not specified, the DCO variable is not created for width.
ImageHeight:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the image height in pixels. If not specified, the DCO variable is not created for height.
ImageDPIX:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the DPIX in dots per inch. If not specified, the DCO variable is not created for DPIX.
ImageDPIY:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the DPIY in dots per inch. If not specified, the DCO variable is not created for DPIY.
PhysicaImageWidth:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the physical width in pixels. If not specified, the DCO variable is not created for physical width.
PhysicalImageHeight:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the physical height in pixels. If not specified, the DCO variable is not created for physical height.
ColorDepth:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the color depth / bits per pixel. If not specified, the DCO object is not created for Bit Depth.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
Compression:
The input parameter is a smart parameter indicating the DCO location to store the name of the compression used in the image file.
method.h:
This action will obtain the image information, Height, Width, DPI X, DPI Y, Physical Height,
Physical Width, Color Depth and Compression type, from the current page image and
the values into the Document hierarchy. Only the desired parameters
needs to be specified. If a parameter is empty, then the value will not be saved in the DCO.
The provided smart parameters identify where to save the information using standard smart parameter
syntax. @B = batch, @D = Document, @P = Page, @F = Field, @X = current object. For example,
if on a page level node, both @P.MyVar and @X.MyVar will work identically and store the result
in a variable called "MyVar" in the page level object. If the variable exists, the value will be
overwritten. If the variable does not exist, it will be created and the value stored. Passing
the parameter "@B.MyVar" on any level node will create the variable at the top, batch-level,
node of the application runtime DCO. A batch level variable can easily be accessed by any
level DCO object by using the @B notation.
If called on a page object that has a field called "MyField", then the parameter @P\MyField.MyVar"
will store the value in the a variable called "MyVar" within the "MyField" object.
The saved information can be used as
required by the application. Perhaps there is a use case to simply save the image size when the batch is
exported. Other use cases could include the application performing specific actions based on the returned data.
For example, if the dpi of the image is below a particular value or if the width or height are not within
an expected range, the application could resize the image or take other steps based on the configured rules.
Actions that perform numeric comparisons can be used to control logic flow of rules based on the image information.
Some images and image types do not have a compression type specified.
They can appear as empty or be listed as "Naive".
Example 1:
SaveImageInformation("@P.Width","@P.Height","@P.DPIx","@P.DPIy","@P.PhysicalWidth","@P.PhysicalHeight","@P.BitDepth","@P.ImgCompression")
This example stores image information into variables specified by user at the page level.
Width = "2479"
Height = "3508"
DPIx = "300"
DPIy = "300"
PhysicalWidth = "743700"
PhysicalHeight = "1052400"
BitDepth = "1"
ImgCompression = "Lzw"
Example 2:
SaveImageInformation("","","@P.DPIx","@P.DPIy","@P.PhysicalWidth","@P.PhysicalHeight","@P.BitDepth", "")
This example stores image information DPIx, DPIy, PhysicalWidth, PhysicalHeight,BitDepth into respective variables
specified at the page level.
DPIx = "300"
DPIy = "300"
PhysicalWidth = "743700"
PhysicalHeight = "1052400"
BitDepth = "1"
Example 3:
SaveImageInformation("@P\Field1.Width","@P\Field1.Height","@P\Field1.DPIx","@P\Field1.DPIy","@P\Field1.PhysicalWidth","@P\Field1.PhysicalHeight","@P\Field1.BitDepth","")
This example stores image information into respective parameters specified by user at the field level.
Width = "2479"
Height = "3508"
DPIx = "300"
DPIy = "300"
PhysicalWidth = "743700"
PhysicalHeight = "1052400"
BitDepth = "1"
Example 4:
SaveImageInformation("","","@P.DPIx","","","","","")
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "@P.DPIx", "True")
This example adjust the image to 8.5" wide and keeps the original DPI of the image.
First the action SaveImageInformation obtains the current DPI of the image and
stores it in a DCO variable called DPIx. The variable name can be anything
meaningful. If the variable does not exist, it will be created. If it does exist,
the current value will be overwritten with the new value. Next the action
SetImageDPIByWidth adjusts the image to ensure it is 8.5" wide and passes
in the current DPI of the image. This will adjust the image so it is 8.5"
wide, keeping the original DPI of the image.
The results of SaveImageInformation can be used in similar ways
in other actions.
SaveImageInformation("","","@P.DPIx","","","","","")
rrCompareNumeric("180",>,"@P.DPIx")
SetImageDPIByWidth("8.5", "@P.DPIx", "True")
This example is similar to the previous example.
The difference is that rrCompareNumeric is used to first check
the DPI of the image. The image will be adjusted only
if the DPI is 180 or less.
Example 5:
SaveImageInformation("","","","","","","@P.BitDepth","")
rrCompare("@P.BitDepth", "32")
SaveImageAsSettingsTIFF("LZW")
SaveImageAs("tif", "24", "", "", ".prebitdepth", "False)
This example is run on a page object and reduces the color depth of the image
associated with the page, if the image is a 32 bit color image. It is required that the associated page file is an image.
This series of steps is useful because some actions do not support 32 bit color images. If the current image is 32 bit color,
the image is saved as a TIF image with a color depth of 24 bits and backup the original image is saved by appending ".prebitdepth" to the filename.
The LZW compression is used because it is a loss-less compression
and it supports any color depth. If the current image is 24 bits or less, then the rrCompare will return false causing the action
flow to stop in this current function and jump to the next function, if one exists. Images of 24 bits or lower are left unchanged
by this series of actions.
method.lvl: Page level only, and the page must refer to a valid single page image file.
method.ret:
True
if the operation is successful, else
False
if any error occurred.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library, including examples
for how to correct an invalid DPI.
Refer to the top-level help for the Application Objects action library for
information on the Datacap Hierarchy (DCO).
