com.qi: IMAP email import actions - import image attachments from email messages.
com.h:
The IMail actions are designed to scan an email Inbox for incoming mail messages,
and place selected messages into a new Batch.
It is possible to ignore all messages except those containing specific attachment types.
The actions are typically assigned to a Task that is executed by an unattended Rulerunner station.
Multiple Inboxes can be scanned by stringing together a set of
login/scan/logout actions for each Inbox, or by assigning an Inbox to each input task.
The mail account must contain an Inbox folder and separate folders for messages successfully imported (Done folder)
and messages that encountered errors (Problem folder). Processed emails will be placed into one of these folders.
Done and Problem folders must be at the same level of the folder hierarchy as the Inbox and must be manually
created prior to running your application.
The names of these folders can be changed using the im_done_folder and im_problem_folder actions.

method.name: im_login
method.qi: Specifies the IMAP mail server URL and login credentials.
method.ap:
hostname : URL or IP address of IMAP mail server. May end with colon followed by port number (:port).
username : Username for mail account.
password : Password for mail account.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters. The password can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager. The URL and user name parameters can be stored in the General section of the Datacap Application Manager but they cannot be encrypted. To retrieve the password that is stored in the Advanced section, use a smart parameter for the action's password parameter similar to @APPVAR(values/adv/mailPassword) where mailPassword is the name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
Connects to the mail server using the specified account information.
Specifies the mail server URL and login credentials.
Login credentials are for a mail server that supports the IMAP protocol (such as MS Exchange, and many others).
Call once for each batch.
To connect on an encrypted channel using SSL / HTTPS protocol, call im_useSSL(True) before login.
If a port number is not specified in the host name when using SSL, port 993 will be used.
im_login("mymailserver.com","theuser","password")
im_login("mymailserver.com:8000","theuser","password")
This example specifies the port along with the host name.
method.see: im_useSSL

method.name: im_SetProxy
method.qi: Allows optional specification of proxy service settings.
method.ap:
hostname : URL or IP address of proxy service.
proxyPort : The proxy service connection port.
proxyType : The type of proxy service: HTTP, SOCKS4, SOCKS5 or NONE.
proxyUsername : Username for the proxy server.
proxyPassword : Password for the proxy server.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
The password can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager.
The URL and user name parameters can be stored in the General section of the Datacap Application Manager but they cannot be encrypted.
To retrieve the password that is stored in the Advanced section,
use a smart parameter for the action's password parameter similar to
@APPVAR(values/adv/mailProxyPassword) where mailProxyPassword is the name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
Optionally sets the values to a proxy service that will be used to connect to the email server.
This action does not confirm that the connection to the proxy service is successful. Connection to the
proxy service will not occur until the im_login action is called.
If this action is used, it must be called prior to the im_login action. If this action is not
called, then no proxy service will be used. If proxyType is not one of the supported
types, then it will default to "none".
im_SetProxy("theHostName", "1234", "SOCKS4", "MyUser", "@APPVAR(values/adv/mailProxyPassword)")
im_login("mymailserver.com","theuser","password")
This example sets up the parameters to use a proxy and then performs the login.
The parameter for the password is an example smart parameter that obtains the password
from an advanced value in the application service.
method.ret:
False,
if the proxyPort is not numeric, otherwise
True.
method.see: im_login

method.name: im_scan
method.qi: Poll the specified mail server for incoming emails with image attachments.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Scans emails in the Inbox for specified attachments, imports selected emails with attachments into the batch.
Call once for each batch.
A connection to the email server must have previously been established using the im_login action.
Each input email will contain the following variables set in the document hierarchy:
TYPE
: Always set to "Document".
Subject
: The email subject.
Body
: The text within the email.
DateSent
: The sent date stamp on the email.
From
: The email sender.
User
: The email user specified in the im_login action.
To
: The email recipients.
Priority
: The state of the email importance flag.
Attachments are ingested as individual pages within the email document, unless im_StoreEML(true) is called before im_scan. With individual attachments, each attachment page will have the following variables set:
TYPE
: Always set to "Other".
IMAGEFILE
: The name of the attachment as saved on disk.
The following batch level variable is created:
EmailCount
: The number of emails scanned into the batch.
FailedEmailCount
: The number of emails failed to be scanned into the batch, due to the issues with email or attachments.
It is recommended that the subject line be no longer than 78 characters as this is a
common subject line length limitation. Some systems may support even shorter lengths,
truncating the subject. Our testing has been successful with lengths up to 255 characters.
It is recommended to test your settings and use lengths appropriate for your systems.
Important: If any concurrently running threads might be using the same account,
your Imail-related tasks cannot be run in a multi-threaded configuration. Instead, use single-threaded tasks only.
For information about configuring threads in Rulerunner, see Configuring Rulerunner to run tasks.
For information about the account, see im_login.
im_wait_time("20")
im_abort_time("40")
im_max_docs("200")
im_types("jpg,tif")
im_scan()
method.ret:
Returns
False
if the operation fails, and pauses before returning. Otherwise,
True.
If no selected emails were available, the action returns
True
and pauses before returning.
Action returns when timeout is reached, or the requested number of emails have been processed.
method.see: im_useSSL, im_done_folder, im_problem_folder, im_wait_time, im_abort_time, im_StoreEML, im_AcceptMixedAttachments, im_AcceptNoAttachments, im_SortByDate

method.name: im_logout
method.qi: Disconnect from the mail server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Closes the connection to the mail server.
Call once for each batch after im_login and im_scan have completed.
im_logout()
method.lvl: Batch level Open or Close event only.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_types
method.qi: Specifies valid file extensions for attachments to ingest.
method.ap:
extensions : Comma-separated list of file image file extensions to import,
with or without period. If the parameter is blank, all emails with or without attachments will be processed.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action specifies the allowable email attachment types.
If this action is not called, the default value of ".pdf" will be used.
If this action is called and no attachment types are specified, all emails and any attachments are added to the batch.
When emails without attachments are processed, this will result in documents without any "pages".
If attachment types are specified and the email contains:
• Only the specified attachment types, the email and attachments will be added to the batch
• Only unspecified attachment types, or if it contains a mix of specified and unspecified attachment types, the email is moved to the Problem folder
• No attachments, the email is moved to the Problem folder
im_wait_time("20")
im_abort_time("40")
im_max_docs("200")
im_types("jpg,tif")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_reject_types
method.qi: Specifies file extensions for attachments to reject.
method.ap:
extensions : Comma-separated list of file image file extensions to ignore,
with or without period. Use in conjunction with im_AcceptMixedAttachments(True) to reject emails with specific attachment types.
Attachments specified in im_types will be ingested, attachment types not specified in im_types or im_reject_types will be ignored.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action specifies disallowed attachment types.
im_types("jpg,tif")
im_AcceptMixedAttachments("True")
im_reject_types(".eml")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_wait_time
method.qi: Specifies the maximum time to wait for input emails for a single batch.
method.ap: nSecs : The maximum number of seconds to wait.
method.h:
The maximum time to wait for input emails for a single batch, when there is at least one pending email.
Used by the im_scan action after the first email has been processed to determine
how long to wait for the batch to fill up. If no emails are pending, the im_scan action
will not wait regardless of the wait time value.
The import of emails into the batch will stop when the wait limit is reached
or when the maximum emails per batch has been reached.
While waiting for new mail to arrive,
the configured mailbox will be polled every two seconds to check for waiting mail.
The action will continue to include new files into the batch until this wait time
is reached or the maximum number of emails per batch is reached.
If this action is not called, the default wait time of 5 seconds will be used.
im_wait_time("20")
im_abort_time("60")
im_max_docs("200")
im_types("jpg,tif")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_abort_time
method.qi: Specifies the delay time before returning when a batch aborts.
method.ap: nSecs : The number of seconds to wait.
method.h:
The action configures how long an Imail action will wait before returning when an abort occurs.
This action can be useful to prevent a large number of aborted batches due to an error condition.
For example, if the email server should become unavailable for a time, or any other error that is quickly returned from the email server.
The abort timeout will limit the number of aborted batches until the mail server becomes available again.
If this action is not called, the default abort time value of 30 seconds will be used.
When logging in or ingesting emails, a single action can make multiple communication requests to the email server.
If the server does not respond to any single communication request within a specific period of time, the request will fail and cause
the batch to abort. By default, any single communication request to the email server will wait
5 minutes for a response. Typically communication is very fast and this default time is more than enough required for a
typical request to complete.
This timeout is different from the value set by the im_abort_time action. If necessary, the maximum time to wait for an email server
response can be adjusted by setting the DCO variable "ImailResponseTimeout" to the number of seconds to wait for
a response before forcefully stopping the waiting request to the email server. The variable should be set on the same
DCO object that calls the IMail actions.
im_wait_time("20")
im_abort_time("60")
im_max_docs("200")
im_types("jpg,tif")
In this example the abort time is set to 60 seconds. If there is a failure when processing an email
that causes the action to abort, the action will delay an additional 60 seconds before
returning. This is to prevent a large number of cascade failures in a very short time as in the case
where the server may immediately reject the request for various reasons.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_max_docs
method.qi: Specifies maximum number of emails to include in a single batch.
method.ap: nDocs : The maximum number of emails in a batch.
method.h:
The import of emails into the batch will stop when this email limit is reached
or when the maximum wait time has been reached. While waiting for new mail to arrive,
the configured mailbox will be polled every two seconds to check for waiting mail.
If this action is not called, the default value of 100 will be used.
The actual amount included in the batch could be less than this maximum.
im_wait_time("20")
im_abort_time("60")
im_max_docs("50")
im_types("jpg,tif")
This example causes the scan operation to limit the number of emails in a
batch to a maximum of 50.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_done_folder
method.qi: Specifies the IMAP folder for successfully imported emails.
method.ap:
folder : Destination IMAP folder for successfully imported emails.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
When an email is processed and the attachment is imported, the email is moved to the folder name
specified by this action.
The folder is expected to be on the root level, the same level as the inbox folder in the mail account specified by the im_login action.
If the folder exists in a subfolder,
then use a forward slash to separate the folder names.
If this action is not called, the default value of "Done" will be used.
im_done_folder("Imported")
im_problem_folder("Failed")
This example changes the default names of the "Done" and "Problem" folders and also requires
the "Imported" and "Failed" folders to be on the same level as the "Inbox" folder.
im_done_folder("Inbox/Imported")
im_problem_folder("Inbox/Failed")
This example requires the folders to be a subfolder of the Inbox folder.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_problem_folder
method.qi: Specifies the IMAP folder for problem emails.
method.ap:
folder : Destination IMAP folder for problem emails.
Smart paramters are supported.
method.h:
When an email is processed and the attachment is not one of the expected types,
the email is moved to the folder specified by this action.
The folder is expected to be on the root level, the same level as the inbox folder of the mail account specified by the im_login action.
If the folder exists in a subfolder, then use a forward slash to separate the folder names.
If this action is not called, the default value of "Problem" will be used.
im_done_folder("Imported")
im_problem_folder("Failed")
This example changes the default name of the "Problem" folder to "Failed" and
requires the "Imported" and "Failed" folders to be on the same level as the "Inbox" folder.
im_done_folder("Inbox/Imported")
im_problem_folder("Inbox/Failed")
This example specifies the folder which is a subfolder of the Inbox folder.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_UseSSL
method.qi: Connect to IMAP Server via SSL encrypted channel

p.name: bUseSSL
p.qi: A boolean value that enables or disables SSL communication

method.ap:
True:
Use SSL to encrypt communication with the mail server.
False:
Communicate with the email server without encryption. This is the default method if im_UseSSL is not called.
method.h:
This action will configure the im_login action to use SSL for the login and must be called prior to im_login to have any effect.
When SSL is enabled, and no port number has been specified in the host name of the im_login action,
subsequent im_login and im_scan actions communicate with the email server via IMAPS protocol using SSL encryption via port 993.
When SSL is not in use, these actions communicate with the email server via IMAP protocol via port 143.
im_UseSSL("True")
im_login("mymailserver.com","theuser","password")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_StoreEML
method.qi: Store one .eml file per message, rather than one file per attachment

p.name: bStoreEML
p.qi: A boolean value that enables storing each email message as an .eml file

method.ap:
True:
Store each ingested email message, formatted together with all attachments, in a single .eml file and attach it as a page to the document.
False:
Add each ingested email message as a document, with associated variables, and add each attachment as a page within the document.
This is the default if im_StoreEML is not called.
method.h:
If set, the im_scan action creates a one page document containing the email and
attachments in an .eml file; no attachment pages are created and no variables are set in the document.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_AcceptMixedAttachments
method.qi: Ingest emails with selected attachment types, even if non-selected attachment types are included

p.name: bMixedOK
p.qi: A boolean value that enables ingestion of emails with both allowed and disallowed attachment types

method.ap:
True:
An email message with an attachment type not specified by im_types will be ingested as long as it contains some desired attachment.
False:
An email message with any disallowed attachment will be rejected. This is the default process if this action is never called.
method.h:
If this action is never called, the presence of any attachment not specified by im_types will cause im_scan to treat that email message as a "Problem".
If this action is called with parameter True, messages with disallowed attachment types are ingested as long as they contain at least one allowed attachment.
If im_types is called with a blank parameter prior to im_scan, all emails are ingested, so this action has no effect.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_AcceptNoAttachments
method.qi: Ingest emails without attachments, even if attachment types are specified

p.name: bNoAttachOK
p.qi: A boolean value that enables ingestion of emails with no attachments

method.ap:
True:
An email message with no attachments will be ingested by im_scan.
False:
An email message no attachments will be rejected by im_scan, unless im_types has been called with a blank parameter. This is the default behavoir if this action is never called.
method.h:
If this action is never called, the absence of an attachment will cause im_scan to treat that email message as a "Problem".
If this action is called with parameter True, messages with no attachments are ingested.
If im_types is called with a blank parameter prior to im_scan, all emails are ingested, so this action has no effect.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: im_SortByDate
method.qi: Sort emails by received date

p.name: bSort
p.qi: A boolean value that enables or disables sorting of emails before ingestion

method.ap:
True:
Causes im_scan to sort email messages by date received and ingest the oldest messages first.
This is the default behavior if im_SortByDate is never called.
False:
Disables sorting of email messages. This greatly increases performance of im_scan when many emails are pending in the inbox.
method.h: When sorting is enabled, all pending emails are sorted and the oldest is ingested first. This can take a significant amount of time for each batch. When the inbox may contain a large number of emails (e.g. more than 100), call im_SortByDate(False) to speed up the process. In this case, messages are processed in the order that the email server presents them to Taskmaster.
method.ret:
Always
True.

com.qi: : Actions that manipulates zones and assign page types
com.h:
Intellocate action library
Details:
The Intellocate action library actions focus on positions of fields and line items in a page's runtime DCO xml file.
This is in support of "Intellocate" functionality where zones positions can be assigned at runtime
to setup new page formats.
The fields zoned positions are written in App.xml file e.g. APT.XML file.
The new position will saved in XML with POS and template Id, e.g. POS 556.
The Line Item zoned position are also written to APP.xml file which
is present in the application location App\DCO_App\App.xml, the application's
setup DCO. e.g. Datacap\APT\dco_APT\APT.xml.
Usage:
It will write Position corresponding of a new fingerprint's zoned fields and line items from a page's data file(xml)
to Pos properties of the corresponding Field object and line item objects in the Document hierarchy file(App.xml).
Smart parameters:
AssignPageType supports smart parameters. Rather than passing connection string hard-coded,
you can pass as a smart parameter, e.g. @APPVAR(*/fingerprintconn:cs), it will read values from Application
.App file which is configured using the Application Service.
Smart parameters are special identifiers that are evaluated at runtime allowing action input parameters
to change based on the current state of the batch or environment.

method.name: SetZones
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Writes the position coordinates of a new fingerprint's zoned fields from a page's Data
file to the Pos properties of the corresponding Field objects in the Document Hierarchy file (.xml).
SetZones()
This will set zones of the fields in App.xml file, also known as the setup DCO.
method.ret:
False
if a fingerprint match has not occurred, or if the Document Hierarchy file
(.xml) cannot be saved. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library.

method.name: SetDetailZone
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Writes the position coordinates of a new fingerprint's Detail Line fields
from a page's Data file to the Pos properties of the corresponding Detail Line
Field objects of the application's Document Hierarchy.
SetDetailZone()
It will write Detail Position coordinates to App.xml file.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library.

method.name: AdjustZones
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Updates the zoned field position on each respective fingerprint stored in database,
for all the fields of the page in App.XML file present
under APP_DCO folder.
In the format:
Pos templateId Position
Updates fingerprint-specific position coordinates for Field objects in the
Document Hierarchy based on the locations listed for the current source page's Data file (.xml)
This action is designed to be used on existing fingerprints only. It will only update fields
that do not have position information. Existing fields will not be updated, even if the position
information for those fields has changed.
AdjustZones()
It will update the zones position of all the fields in the page in the APP.XML file as per the respective fingerprint coordinates.
e.g. Pos 1074(fingerprint) "Position".
method.ret:
False
if a fingerprint match has not occurred and a Template ID
value has not been assigned to the current page, or if the Document
Hierarchy file cannot be saved. Otherwise,
True.

method.name: IsPageDataMissing
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Checks to see that the current page data exists.
This action does not physically check for the existence of a data file. It confirms
that a valid page data is loaded into memory.
It verifies whether the current page contains children field objects.
If it has no children it will return true. i.e. Page Data is missing, otherwise it will return false.
IsPageDataMissing()
This action will check whether there are any children on the current page.
If the page doesn't have any children then it will return true.
If the page does contain children it will return false and continue with the next function
in the rule.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library.

method.name: AssignPageType
method.ap:
PageType:
The value of the page type to assign to the current page.
PageType is stored in table in fingerprint Database.
It can be numeric value, which will be stored against particular pagetype.
It can also be a alpha-numeric value, which will be stored in table and a numeric id will be automatically generated.
ConnectionString:
The ConnectionString should be passed so that Connection to fingerprint happens
and it will write the new pagetype and update template in fingerprint database
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Assigns a required Page Type value to a newly created fingerprint.
The assigned value corresponds to the values configured in the PageType table within the fingerprint database.
These values are custom defined for each application.
If the page type is non-numeric, this action will look up the corresponding numeric value within the database.
AssignPageType("2", @APPVAR(*/fingerprintconn:cs))
This example assigns a page type of 2 to the new fingerprint.
It will read the fingerprint database connection string configured in the
Application Manager.
AssignPageType("PageSeparator", @APPVAR(*/fingerprintconn:cs))
This example assigns a page type of "PageSeparator" to the new fingerprint.
It will read the fingerprint database connection string configured in the
Application Manager.
method.ret:
False
if the numeric value cannot be retrieved from the fingerprint database or if there is
no connection to the fingerprint database. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help for more information about this action library.

com.qi: : LineItemPagination Actions for Retrieval of large Number of Line Items
com.h:
LineItemPagination Actions library focuses on the LineItemPagination of line items, dividing a large set of line items into multiple smaller chunks.
By creating smaller sets of line items, data can be retrieved faster, and performance is improved for a large set of line items when performing verification.
LineItemPagination is required when there are many pages within a single document that has than 50 contiguous line items.
When the number of line items is very large, the client application may perform poorly.
To overcome this issue, LineItemPagination can be enabled to provide smaller sets of line items for verification that can be easily reviewed.
The number of line items to use for LineItemPagination is configured in the General section of the Application Manager for
the application. The maximum size of line items to display at one time is controlled by the
DetailPageSize value in Application Manager. This value would be pre-configured by the application administrator or developer.
For example, if the value of DetailPageSize is 50, and there are around 200 pages each with 50 line items.
that sums up to 10,000 line items. So, if user tries to validate all these 10,000 line items, it can cause
cause poor performance of the client application. A LineItemPagination size of 50 will cause these line items to be displayed
in sets of 50. The number is configurable. The maximum recommended size is 150 line items. It is recommended that
testing is performed to determine what number works best in your environment.
The LineItemPagination action will adjust the runtime DCO, based on the value provided by user in DetailPageSize.
The end user will see the line item grid based on the configured value. Additional functionality is available such as the
ability to move to the next set of
line items, move back to previous set of lineitems, and jump to a set of lineitems.
At runtime, LineItemPagination will create Details_TMXXXXXX pages in batch directory, and the Image.xml(Datafile) will hold only
those set of line items which are displayed in the line item grid in the client.
DetailPageSize Variable needs to be created in the General section of the Application Manager Custom Values tab.
The Value should be in range from
50 to 150 for faster retrieval of line items in the verify panel.
If the value of variable DetailPageSize is set to 0, it means LineItemPagination functionality is disabled and
the buttons on verify panel like Next Set, Previous Set and Jump To will be disabled.
For the
DetailPageSize
variable, Any value entered by User between 1 to 50 will be default to 50 and value entered greater
than 150, will be default to 150.
Ideally LineItemPagination should be implemented and executed post batch profiler(recognition) as it takes input as DataFile.
DataFile will be generated post recognition, where it will have detail information about line items of all the pages,
its values as well as positions. LineItemPagination only works with line items and with panels that support line items.
So, it is recommended where ever there are more than 500 line items till 5000 line items, where user feels the traditional
DcDesktop verify panel is too slow to retrieve line items , user can use LineItemPagination feature.
LineItemPagination should be done before Manual Verification Task.
By default the LineItemPagination feature will be turned off. If DetailPageSize Variable doesn't exist in Application Manager,
then LineItemPagination will be disabled. If there value in DetailPageSize is invalid, it will default to 50.
It is recommended to use LineItemPagination Feature in Datacap Desktop Verify Panel. If LineItemPagination actions are called other in any other
task profile it may be lead to undesirable output.

method.name: MoveDetailFilesIntoMain
method.qi: : Move all Detail files into Main file(datafile)
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action will merge all the separate Datafile_XXXX files into Main File. i.e ImageDatafile.
DivideDetailsIntoPages()
MoveDetailFilesIntoMain()
This Action will merge all the Details_TMXXXXXX pages present in batch folder in TMXXXXXX.xml(Datafile), to execute
this action user needs to divide the line items first using DivideDetailsIntoPages action.
method.ret:
True,
if the operation is successful, otherwise
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level action help for general information regarding the LineItemPagination actions along with available settings and
features.

method.name: DivideDetailsIntoPages
method.qi: : Divide Detail LineItem Section into number of pages
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action will divide the Details LineItem into a number of Pages based on variable value set in the application manager.
The number of lineitems to display is controlled by the variable DetailPageSize in the Datacap Application Manager -> Custom Variable -> General section.
Whatever value is set in DetailPageSize, that number of line items will be displayed in verify panel of the client. Refer to the top-level
help for more information.
Note: For faster retrieval of Data, it is recommended to set value of DetailPageSize in range between 50-150.
DivideDetailsIntoPages()
If DetailPageSize is set to 70 in the Application Manager Custom Values panel,
it will display 70 lineitems in detail section of verification panel.
method.ret:
True,
if the operation is successful, otherwise
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level action help for general information regarding the LineItemPagination actions along with available settings and
features.

method.name: JumpToSetOfLineitems
method.qi: : Jump to a Particular Set of Lineitems
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Post LineItemPagination, all pages whose total line items exceeds the configured value, will be divided into chunks of Datafile
depending upon value of DetailPageSize set in application manager.
If the verification user wants to see a particular set of line items, The JumpToSetOfLineitems action will move to the specified
set of line items and display them in the client. There will be a button on Verify Panel that allows the user to select the set to display. Enter a numeric value for the DataSet
the user wants to Jump to, if the value is negative or out of range then user will get a error popup.
JumpToSetOfLineitems()
In DcDesktop Verify Panel User will get a textbox, there he can specify on which page he wants to jump.
If the user entered input is out of range or negative, it will popup error msg.
This action use DetailCurrentPage Variable to get details of current page number displayed in verify panel and PageJumpNumber Variable
holds the current page number of page.
In the above example, assume there are more than 5 Datafiles(Details_TMXXXXXX pages) are created post
LineItemPagination task, and user enters 5 in JumpToSetOfLineitems textbox, so it will display the 5th Set of Lineitems
in the verify Panel Detail Section.
method.ret:
False,
if the number specified to Jump is invalid or out of range, otherwise
True.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level action help for general information regarding the LineItemPagination actions along with available settings and
features.

method.name: DeleteAllDetailPaginations
method.qi: : Delete All of the Details_TMXXXXXX pages from the Batch folder
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Deletes the additional, temporary, Datafiles created by LineItemPagination from the batch folder.
DivideDetailsIntoPages()
MoveDetailFilesIntoMain()
DeleteAllDetailPaginations()
It will delete all the Details_TMXXXXXX files created using action DivideDetailsIntoPages() from the batch folder.
method.ret:
False,
if there are No Detail pages in batch, otherwise
True.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level action help for general information regarding the LineItemPagination actions along with available settings and
features.

method.name: PreviousSetOfLineitems
method.qi: : Go To the Previous Set of Lineitems
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Post LineItemPagination in verify panel based on DetailPageSize value, Datafile will be divided into smaller chuncks
of lineitems, X/Y where X is Previous set of lineitems and Y is current set of line items.
PreviousSetOfLineitems()
The action will swap current set of line items displayed in VerifyPanel with the previous set of line items.
method.ret:
True,
if the operation is successful, otherwise
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level action help for general information regarding the LineItemPagination actions along with available settings and
features.

method.name: NextSetOfLineitems
method.qi: : Go To the Next Set of Lineitems
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Post LineItemPagination in verify panel based on DetailPageSize value, the Datafile will be divided into smaller chunks
of lineitems, X/Y where X is current set of line items and Y is next set of line items.
NextSetOfLineitems()
It will swap current set of line items displayed in Verify panel with the next set of line items.
method.ret:
True,
if the operation is successful, otherwise
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level action help for general information regarding the LineItemPagination actions along with available settings and
features.

com.h:
The mvscan action library contains actions that will control how a Datacap application will
ingest files such as images scanned as TIF images or electronic documents such as PDF, so they
can be processed.
Use these actions to create batches from files on disk, typically on a network file share.
The input files may be image files produced by a Multifunction Device (MFD) or fax, or arbitrary files dropped off for processing.
Mvscan actions can safely run in multiple threads or processes, on a single computer or on multiple computers.
These instances coordinate with each other by creating *.lock files in the input folder.
mvscan scans one or more folders within a single subtree and maintains a cached list of files for ingestion,
for performance and to reduce load on the network and file system.
In a typical situation, the mvscan actions would monitor a directory, or set of directories, looking for
files that are placed into these directories by some external process.
As the images are placed into these directories, they are ingested by the scan actions into a
batch and then processed by a Datacap application.
External processes that place files in the input folders must never overwrite an existing file.

method.name: set_folder
method.qi: : Specifies the top level folder to search for files to be ingested

p.name: folderpath
p.qi: Path to folder containing files to be ingested

method.ap:
folderpath : A string value specifying the path an input folder. Multiple input folders can be separated by vertical bar symbols (|).
The scan() action ingests selected file types from these folders, and optionally subfolders, into batches for processing.
Each ingested batch will contain files from a single folder.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action configures the folder from where the "Scan" action will look for files to ingest
into the batch. Call this action before calling the Scan action.
set_folder("@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)+@STRING(\input folder)")
scan()
The example uses a smart parameter to set the input directory. This smart parameter references
the variable vscanimagedir which is specified in the application file (*.app) and appends the additional
folder "\input folder" to the path. Because the root scan directory is read from the application
file, it makes it easy to change the source directory using the application manager to update
the root directory as necessary, without having to update the rules in the application.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: set_copy_folder
method.qi: : Optional, sets a folder to contain a copy of each ingested file

p.name: folderpath
p.qi: Path to folder to contain a copy of each ingested file

method.ap:
folderpath : A string value specifying the path of the folder where a copy of each input files will be placed,
in addition to the batch. This folder must exist or the scan() action will produce an error.
Smart Parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action designates the name of the folder where ingested files will be copied. Files are still
ingested into the batch. The files ingested into the batch will have their file names changed
to the standard Datacap naming convention of TMXXXXXX.ext. An additional copy of each ingested file
will be placed into the copy folder with the original file names. This can be useful if you
wish to retain the ingested files.
This action must be called before scan() to take effect.
For demo purposes, set the copy folder the same as the input folder.
In this case the scan action leaves ingested files in place and rescans the input folder, ignoring the cache file.
This allows a user to ingest a batch for the application and the ingested files will be placed back
into the input directory, allowing the same set of images to be ingested batch after batch. This scenario is
useful for testing or when demoing an application.
The folderpath can be specified as a relative path to the scan directory. For example, if the scan
directory is configured as "C:\Datacap\MyApp\Input" and if the copy folder is configured as "Done"
then the problem directory name will resolve as C:\Datacap\MyApp\Done. Using a relative path
for the folder can be useful when scan is configured to ingest from multiple root directories.
set_folder("@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)+@STRING(\input folder)")
set_copy_folder(@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)+@STRING(\copy folder))
scan()
The example uses a smart parameter to set the input directory. This smart parameter references
the variable vscanimagedir which is specified in the application file (*.app) and appends the additional
folder "\copy folder" to the path. Because the root scan directory is read from the application
file, it makes it easy to change the source directory using the application manager to update
the root directory as necessary, without having to update the rules in the application.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: set_problem_folder
method.qi: : Required, sets folder for any files that cannot be ingested

p.name: folderpath
p.qi: Path to folder to contain any files that cannot be ingested

method.ap:
folderpath : A string value specifying the path of the folder where files that cannot be ingested will be placed.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action must be called before scan(). If this action is not called, and scan is unable to ingest a file,
the batch will be aborted. Any files already ingested into the batch will remain in the batch.
The file which cannot be ingested may be left in a locked state. Manual intervention will be required.
The folderpath can be specified as a relative path to the scan directory. For example, if the scan
directory is configured as "C:\Datacap\MyApp\Input" and if the problem folder is configured as "Problem"
then the problem directory name will resolve as C:\Datacap\MyApp\Problem. Using a relative path
for the folder can be useful when scan is configured to ingest from multiple root directories.
set_folder("@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)+@STRING(\input folder)")
set_problem_folder(@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)+@STRING(\problem folder))
scan()
the variable vscanimagedir which is specified in the application file (*.app) and appends the additional
folder "\problem folder" to the path. Because the root scan directory is read from the application
file, it makes it easy to change the source directory using the application manager to update
the root directory as necessary, without having to update the rules in the application.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: scan
method.qi: : Poll the specified folder for files to ingest.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Scans the source folder for files with desired extensions, then ingests them into a batch.
Call this action once for each batch.
All desired options for scan must be set prior to calling this action.
If no files are present for ingestion the batch is set to pending status and the action returns immediately.
Each input file will generate one or more "pages" in the batch with the following DCO page variables set:
TYPE
: Always set to "Other".
IMAGEFILE
: The filename within the batch, e.g. "TM000002.tif".
PageName
: The original input filename without the extension, e.g. "APT0001".
ScanSrcPath
: The full path to the original file, e.g. "C:\Datacap\1040EZ\images\1040ez01.tif".
Once the files are ingested, they can then be operated on by subesquent rules and actions.
Typical next steps could be page separation of electronic documents, such as PDFs,
to convert them to single tiff images;
image enhancements or other preparations so page identification can be performed
to change the page type of "Other" to the correct page type for continued
processing by the application.
set_folder("@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)+@STRING(\mvscan folder)")
set_problem_folder(@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)+@STRING(\problem folder))
set_types("jpg,pdf,tif")
set_max_docs("2")
scan()
This example specifies the input folder, the problem folder, the types to be ingested and the maximum
number of images per batch. Scan is then called to ingest the files from the input directory.
The order of the "set" actions does not matter, they simply need to be called prior to calling
scan().
method.ret:
Returns
True.
Action returns when timeout is reached, or the requested number of files have been ingested.
If no files are ingested, the batch will remain in a pending state.
If a serious error occurs, the batch will be placed into an aborted state so the issue can be reviewed.

method.name: set_types
method.qi: : Comma-separated list of file extensions to be ingested. Can be specified with or without period. Default is TIF. Overrides set_metadata_types().

p.name: extensions
p.qi: Comma-separated list of file image file extensions to import

method.ap:
String value of extension(s) of input files that should be ingested. For multiple types, separate
each one with a comma. Any files with extensions not in this list are ignored.
A smart parameter that evaluates to a file extension or list of extensions is accepted.
It is optional to include a period before each extension. The parameter is not case-sensitive.
method.h:
Uses the value of a file extension(s) to specify the type of files the task will scan.
This is an optional action: the task will scan .tif files by default.
For this action to take effect, it must be called before the scan action.
This action overrides any previous call to set_metadata_types(), and causes files to be ingested without metadata.
set_types("tif,tiff,pdf")
Scan()
This sequence will ingest files ending with ".tif", ".tiff", and ".pdf".

method.name: set_metadata_types
method.qi: : Specifies metadata trigger file extension or comma-separated list. Overrides set_types().

p.name: extensions
p.qi: Metadata image file extension(s). If specified, XML metadata files (AKA trigger files) control ingestion of pages into batches, along with associated metadata. If specified, these extensions override any prior call to set_types()

method.ap:
String value of extension(s) of input files containing "pointers" to files to be ingested
along with metadata to be included in the batch for each file. For multiple types, separate
each one with a comma. Any files with extensions not in this list are ignored.
It is optional to include a period before each extension. The parameter is not case-sensitive.
method.h:
This action overrides any previous call to set_types(), and forces the action to read properly
formatted XML from the metadata trigger file to determine which files get ingested,
rather than ingesting individual files into the batch. Other settings such as set_min_age() are applied to the metadata files.
The XML file must follow the format below.
The tag name of the XML root node must be ᐸinputᐳ.
The ᐸitemᐳ nodes represent a group of input files or images that share metadata.
The ᐸitemᐳ nodes must contain at least one attribute, but can have a number of attributes.
In this example, the ᐸitemᐳ nodes contain the attributes name=, vendor_number=, vendor_name=, invoice_number=.
The ᐸitemᐳ attribute names are entered in the item as text following the =.
These name values are prepended with Meta_Item_ when they are written to the DCO to define
the metadata variable names that are placed on each page. The attribute values populate the variable values.
The inner most nodes must be ᐸfilenameᐳ and contain items that represent single input files.
A ᐸfilenameᐳ can be either a fully qualified path, for example \\server\folder\filename, or a partial path
relative to the location of the metadata file such as folder\filename. The number of file names in each
repeating item is only limited to the practical limit of how many files you want to ingest in a single batch.
Each file is ingested as a Page in the batch, regardless of the file type or contents.
All of the items in a metadata file are ingested into the same batch. For example, if a
metadata file contains 1 node with 50 filen ames, 50 files are ingested for that single metadata file.
If the metadata file contains 5 nodes with 50 file names in each of them, then 250 files are ingested.
The external system that creates the metafile must create all of the files to be ingested before writing the metafile that refers to them.
Here is an example of a valid XML metadata file:
ᐸinputᐳ
ᐸitem name="Invoice1" vendor_number="TS265329" vendor_name="Busy Car Repair" invoice_number="28100"ᐳ
ᐸfilenameᐳC:\Datacap\APT\images\Input\Invoice_0001S1.tifᐸ/filenameᐳ
ᐸfilenameᐳC:\Datacap\APT\images\Input\Invoice_0002S1.tifᐸ/filenameᐳ
ᐸ/itemᐳ
ᐸitem name="Invoice2" vendor_number="TS23785354" vendor_name="Trucking Co." invoice_number="876-3456"ᐳ
ᐸfilenameᐳC:\Datacap\APT\images\Input\Invoice_0003S1.tifᐸ/filenameᐳ
ᐸfilenameᐳC:\Datacap\APT\images\Input\Invoice_0004S1.tifᐸ/filenameᐳ
ᐸ/itemᐳ
ᐸ/inputᐳ
set_metadata_types("xml")
Scan()
This sequence will scan for metadata trigger files ending in ".xml".

method.name: set_sort_method
method.qi: : Selects method for sorting files for ingestion

p.name: method
p.qi: Sort method can be either DATE (default) or NAME. The parameter is not case sensitive.

method.h:
The scan action takes snapshots of the input folder, sorts the files by either date last modified
(default) or by filename, and then tries to ingest the files in that order. This action allows you to override the default sort order.
set_sort_method("NAME")
Scan()
This sequence will ingest files in alphabetical order.

method.name: set_wait_time
method.qi: : Specifies interval to wait for additional files to ingest, before finishing a batch which has not reached the specified maximum size or time limits.

p.name: nSecs
p.qi: Time to wait for files to complete a batch.

method.ap: nSecs : The maximum number of seconds to wait for files to complete a batch.
method.h:
The maximum time to wait for input files to arrive to meet the total quantity specify by the set_max_docs action.
If at least one file was ingested, no more files are available, and the batch has not reached capacity, the scan
action will wait for additional files to be placed into the directory configured by the set_folder action.
Ingestion of files into the batch will stop when the wait limit is reached
or when the maximum number of files per batch has been reached.
If no files are available during the scan() action, and this time is reached, the scan action will return and the batch status will remain "pending".
If this action is not called, the default wait time of 2 seconds will be used.
NOTE: This action can be used to group incoming files when ingesting from a single input folder. It is not effective in tree mode or for metadata XML.
When ingesting from multiple folders or in tree mode, use set_min_age instead to wait for a group of files to appear in the input folders.
See set_min_age for the special case set_wait_time(0) in tree mode.
set_wait_time("60")
scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: set_min_age

method.name: set_abort_time
method.qi: : Specifies delay time if batch aborts

p.name: nSecs
p.qi: Time to wait before continuing when a serious error occurs.

method.ap: nSecs : Time to wait before continuing when a serious error occurs.
method.h:
The scan action will wait the specified time before returning if a fatal error is detected that would cause the batch to abort.
This action can be useful to prevent a large number of aborted batches due to an abort condition.
For example, if the source folder should become unavailable for some time,
the abort timeout will limit the number of aborted batches until the folder becomes available again.
If such an even could occur, this wait time can be adjusted to slow down ingestion processing
until the source directory is available again.
If this action is not called, the default abort time value of 5 seconds will be used.
Rulerunner has settings that control how it responds to an abort situation. Review the Rulerunner settings
to ensure they are set as desired based on how it should respond should a batch abort.
set_abort_time("60")
scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: set_move_wait_time
method.qi: : Specifies time to wait for source file to be deleted after move

p.name: nSecs
p.qi: Number of seconds to wait for source file to be deleted, before failure.

method.ap: nSecs : Number of seconds to wait for source file to be deleted, before failure.
method.h:
Over a slow network, and especially with large input files, moving the file from the source
folder to the batch folder may take a significant length of time. The scan configuration action checks that the
source file has been deleted after moving it. If the source file still exists, the scan action waits for a length of time,
checking periodically if the file has been deleted. At the end of this time period, if the source file still exists,
the copy in the batch folder is renamed with an extension ".failed" and it is not included in the batch.
It is then assumed that the original source file will be ingested by another subsequent scan task.
set_move_wait_time("120")
scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: set_max_docs
method.qi: : Specifies maximum number of pages in each batch. If Metadata files are used, this is the maximum number of metadata files to import.

p.name: nDocs
p.qi: Number of documents in a batch. Default 100.

method.ap:
nDocs : An integer value which specifies the maximum number of input files to place into a batch.
If Metadata files are used, action set_metadata_types() is called instead of set_types(),
this specifies the maximum number of metadata files to ingest.
All files referenced in each metadata file are included in the batch, there is no limit on the number of pages in the batch in this case.
The default value is 100.
method.h:
This action configures the maximum number of files to be ingested into a batch. If the number of
available files is less than this number, the Scan action will wait for more files based on the
time configured with the action set_wait_time.
For this action to take effect, it must be called before the Scan action.
set_tree_mode(false)
set_max_docs("1")
scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: set_wait_time

method.name: set_tree_mode
method.qi: : Determines whether subdirectories are included in the scan for files to ingest
method.ap:
bTreeFlag : A Boolean value that enables or disables ingesting files from sub-folders within the top level scan folder.
True:
Search for files in subfolders to any depth below the scan folder.
Folder names beginning with underscore (_) are ignored. This is the default if the action is not called.
False:
Ingest files located in the scan folder only. Ignore subfolders.
method.h:
When "tree mode" is enabled, which is the default, the scan action will ingest files from an subdirectories
that are present in the configured ingestion folder.
Each batch will contain files from only one folder regardless of the tree mode setting.
If there are multiple folders, scan will only operate on one at at time.
Files from multiple folders will never be ingested into the same batch.
When tree mode is enabled, the scan action will first ingest files from the root folder directory.
When all of those files have been ingested, it will then ingest from the sub folders, one at a time.
Tree mode is true by default. For this action to take effect, it must be called before the Scan action.
set_types("tif")
set_tree_mode(false)
scan()

method.name: set_delete_empty_folders
method.qi: : Determines whether empty subdirectories will be deleted
method.ap:
bParam : A Boolean value that enables or disables deleting sub-folders if they are empty.
The root folder specified for ingestion is never deleted. Subfolders are only deleted if both this setting and tree mode are enabled.
True:
Delete subfolders of the main ingestion folder if they are empty. This is the default if the action is not called.
False:
Leave empty subfolders intact.
method.h:
set_delete_empty_folders action enables or disables deleting sub-folders, if they are empty.
The root folder specified for ingestion is never deleted. Subfolders are only deleted if they are empty and tree mode are enabled.
Note: If subfolders of the main ingestion folder has files, then the directory will not be deleted until it is empty and the next time the folders are polled.
If the folder is empty at the start of the ingestion operation, only at that point sub-folders will be deleted.
Use this action prior to calling scan to configure the deletion of empty input subdirectories.
If tree mode is not enabled, this setting has no effect.
set_types("tif")
set_min_age("10")
set_tree_mode(True)
set_delete_empty_folders(False)
scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: set_tree_mode

method.name: set_min_age
method.qi: : Specifies minimum age of file since last modified

p.name: nSecs
p.qi: Number of seconds to wait after file modified before ingesting

method.ap:
nSecs : An integer value, the number of seconds to wait after file modified before ingesting.
The default value is zero, meaning ingest files as soon as they are present.
method.h:
This setting can be used to prevent premature ingestion of a file which may be incomplete.
For example, a network scanner or multifunction device might create the image file and write contents over a period of time,
rather than all at once. In that case ingesting the file immediately could cause errors,
whereas waiting for 5 or 10 seconds would provide sufficient time for the file to be completed.
If required, the appropriate value must be determined experimentally.
If tree mode is enabled, all files in a given folder must meet the minimum age before any
file from that folder is ingested. This allows you to keep files written to a subfolder in the same batch.
To override this behavior and check the age of files individually in tree mode, set_wait_time to zero.
For this action to take effect, it must be called before the Scan action.
set_types("tif")
set_min_age("10")
scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: set_image_validation
method.qi: : Forces TIFF images to be checked before ingesting
method.ap:
bValidate : A Boolean value that enables or disables validating image files during ingestion.
True:
Check to confirm that each file ingested contains a valid TIFF or JPG image.
False:
Copy input files regardless of type or contents. This is the default if the action is not called.
method.h:
Enables testing that each file ingested is a valid image file.
If enabled, converts black and white TIF files to G4 compression.
This action should not be enabled if ingested file types are not images, such as PDFs, due to incompatibility.
For this action to take effect, it must be called before the Scan action.
set_types("tif")
set_image_validation("True")
scan()
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: set_multipage_burst
method.qi: : Forces multipage TIFF images to be split into single pages during ingestion

p.name: bBurst
p.qi: Nonzero to force bursting of TIFF image files. Default = 0, no bursting.

method.ap:
bBurst : A Boolean value that enables or disables bursting multipage image files during ingestion.
True:
Any multipage TIFF file will be separated into multiple pages in the batch, one per image.
False:
One page is output per input file. This is the default if the action is not called.
method.h:
Enables splitting or bursting multipage source image files into one image per page in the batch.
For this action to take effect, it must be called before the Scan action.
Only multi-page TIF files will be split. Other types will be ingested as-is.
set_types("tif,tiff")
set_multipage_burst(True)
scan()
If the scan action in this sequence encounters a multipage .tif file, then it will
read each one into the current batch as a separate image, thereby "bursting" the multipage
file into individual images.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: mv_retain_folders
method.qi: : Preserves the directory structure of files in the input folder tree

p.name: bRetain
p.qi: Set to True to enable this option, default is False.

method.ap:
bRetainFolders : A Boolean value that enables or disables preserving the directory structure.
True:
If and when an input file is moved to the Problem or Copy folders,
the path relative to the base input folder is reproduced within the Problem or Copy folder.
False:
Input files are placed directly in the Problem or Copy folder as appropriate.
The relative path within the input folder is only retained in the ScanSrcPath variable.
method.h:
If the option is enabled, the Problem and Copy folders are populated with subfolders to
match the path of the input files relative to the root input folder.
If retain folders is set to false, then the copied files will be placed
in the root of the copy directory, regardless of the original subfolder where
they were located in the scan directory.
Additionally, the following variables are added to the page to allow the application to
determine the path of the input file:
ScanSrcInputFolder
: The full path of the root input folder for this file. It does not include the file name. For example: c:\shared\group1
ScanSrcSubFolder
: The relative path of the ingestion folder where the file was found,
including the input root folder name but not the path leading up to it. For example: \shared\group1\batch1. If the file was ingested from the root of the source directory, this value
will be blank.
ScanSrcFileName
: The original file name without the path. For example: invoice_0001.tif
Directory Structure When Retain Is Enabled
When the folder directory is retained, the copy directory includes the source directory as the root within
the copy directory. The following illustrates a sample set of input directories and how they
will appear in the copy directory after scan has completed.
This example assumes the following actions were used:
set_folder("C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Input")
set_copy_folder("C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Done")
Files as they existed in the scan directory:
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Input\Sub1\File1.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Input\Sub1\File2.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Input\Sub1\Sub2\File3.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Input\Sub3\File4.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Input\File5.tif
Files as they exist after multiple scans to ingest all of the files:
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Done\Input\Sub1\File1.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Done\Input\Sub1\File2.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Done\Input\Sub1\Sub2\File3.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Done\Input\Sub3\File4.tif
C:\Datacap\MyApplication\Done\Input\File5.tif
set_folder(“c:\scan\group1\Input|c:\scan\group2\Input|d:\scan\group3\Input”)
set_copy_folder(“Done”)
set_problem_folder("Error")
mv_retain_folder(True)
scan()
In this example, the set_folder action specifies three input folders. The following table shows the copy and problem folders for each input folder:
Scan folder ------------- Copy folder ------------ Problem folder
c:\scan\group1\Input c:\scan\group1\Done c:\scan\group1\Error
c:\scan\group2\Input c:\scan\group2\Done c:\scan\group2\Error
d:\scan\group3\Input d:\scan\group3\Done d:\scan\group3\Error
Within the copy or problem folder, files are placed in a directory structure
that replicates the file’s original input folder except for the root input folder. The following table shows some examples:
Input file placement ------- Copy folder placement ------------ Problem folder placement
c:\scan\group1\input\f1.tif c:\scan\group1\done\input\f1.tif c:\scan\group1\error\input\f1.tif
d:\scan\group3\input\f2.tif c:\scan\group3\done\input\f2.tif d:\scan\group3\error\input\f2.tif
method.ret:
Always
True.
