af.name: SaveFieldsText
af.qi: Save recognized page types and field values after recognition, for accuracy calculations.
af.h:
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that the action is no longer used.
Instead, use the replacement action StatisticsSaveFieldsText in the application library ExportToDatabase.
Call this action after page classification and OCR recognition, but before verification, to save the original recognized data for statistics calculations.
The type of each page is stored in page variable ClassifiedPageType. The recognized value of each field is stored in field variable RecognizedText.
SaveFieldsText()
af.g:
On Error Resume Next
Call recursiveSaveRecognizedText(DCO)
if err.number<>0 then
writelog("Error " & err.number)
writelog("Error " & err.description)
err.clear
end if
SaveFieldsText = true

af.name: CompareFieldsText
af.qi: Calculates page type classification and field recognition accuracy statistics and updates database report tables.
af.h:
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that the action is no longer used.
Instead, use the replacement action StatisticsCompareFieldsText in the application library ExportToDatabase.
Call this action after data verification to calculate accuracy based on the changes to data during verification. The SaveFieldsText action must have previously run after the profiler task (recognition), and before verification.
Batch variables are populated with accuracy values. PageClassifiedErrors is the number of page classification errors (page type changed after auto-classification), PageClassifiedCount is the number of pages classified in this batch, FieldRecognitionCount is the number of fields recognized, and FieldRecognitionErrors is the number of fields that were incorrectly recognized (were changed after recognition).
CompareFieldsText()
af.g:
'Store page and field accuracy info in the runtime DCO batch level variables
DCO.Variable("PageClassifiedErrors") = "0"
DCO.Variable("PageClassifiedCount") = "0"
DCO.Variable("FieldRecognitionCount") = "0"
DCO.Variable("FieldRecognitionErrors") = "0"
DCO.Variable("FieldAccuracyPct") = "0."
DCO.Variable("ClassifyAccuracyPct") = "0."
Call recursiveCompareText(DCO) ' calculate the error info
FieldCount = CInt(DCO.Variable("FieldRecognitionCount"))
if FieldCount > 0 then
Accuracy = 100.*CDbl(FieldCount - DCO.Variable("FieldRecognitionErrors"))/FieldCount
if Accuracy > 100 then Accuracy = 100
if Accuracy < 0 then Accuracy = 0
DCO.Variable("FieldAccuracyPct") = Replace(CStr(Accuracy), ",", ".")
End If
PageCount = CInt(DCO.Variable("PageClassifiedCount"))
if PageCount > 0 then
Accuracy = 100.*CDbl(PageCount - DCO.Variable("PageClassifiedErrors"))/PageCount
if Accuracy > 100 then Accuracy = 100
if Accuracy < 0 then Accuracy = 0
DCO.Variable("ClassifyAccuracyPct") = Replace(CStr(Accuracy), ",", ".")
End If
CompareFieldsText = true

af.name: IsBatchAborted
af.qi: Reports if batch is set to abort.
af.h:
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that the action is no longer used.
Instead, use the replacement action IsBatchSetToAbort in the application library RuleRunnerLogic.
Test whether the batch has already been aborted and stop the ruleset if so.
IsBatchAborted()
af.ret: True if the batch is set to abort, else False.
af.g:
if babort then
isbatchaborted=true
else
isbatchaborted=false
end if

af.name: AddToDBTotals
af.h:
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that the action is no longer used.
Instead, use the replacement action StatisticsAddToDatabaseTotals in the application library ExportToDatabase.
Update application summary statistics in the reportTotal table with this batch's totals. Once this action executes successfully it sets batch variable TotalStatsUpdated to avoid double-counting.
ExportOpenConnection("@APPVAR(values/dsn/exportdb:cs)")
AddToDBTotals()
ExportCloseConnection()
Important.
Make sure to call the ExportOpenConnection action before calling AddToDBTotals()
af.g:
Dim sSmartParam
AddToDBTotals = true
iExported = MetaWord("@B.TotalStatsUpdated")
if iExported = "1" then
WriteLog("Statistics already updated")
exit function
End If
' for each counter in reportTotal, only update those that have changed
sParams = ""
sCounter = MetaWord("@B.CheckRecognitionCount")
if sCounter <> "" then
if CInt(sCounter) > 0 then sParams = "rt_Feature1Count" & "," & sCounter
End If
Set fso = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
dFoldersize = FSO.GetFolder(Pilot.BatchDir).Size
Set fso = nothing
sCounter = CStr(CLng((dFolderSize + 512) / 1024))
if sCounter <> "" then
if CLng(sCounter) > 0 then
if (sParams <> "") then sParams = sParams & ";"
sParams = sParams & "rt_TotalSizeKB" & "," & sCounter
DCO.Variable("SizeKB") = sCounter
End If
End If
'WriteLog(sParams)
ret = true
if sParams <> "" then
ret = AddToReportTotal(sParams)
end if
if ret = true then
WriteLog("Statistics updated OK")
DCO.variable("TotalStatsUpdated") = "1"
End If

com.qi: : Merges multiple image into a single multiple page TIFF image.
com.h:
This action library will combine images associated with a DCO page to a multiple page TIFF image.
The source images do not need to be TIFF images, the resulting file will be a TIFF image that contains
multiple images within it.
The action MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage will create a multiple page TIFF image
in a single step. Pages can be optionally included by page type. Additionally,
pages can be included or excluded by page status or by the status
of the parent document object.
The action AddCurrentpageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage will add the current page
object as the last page of a TIFF image. This action will not run as fast
as the MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage action.
A multi-page TIFF file has a maximum file size of 4GB. It is possible that files between 2GB and 4GB
will not work with some applications. Images that have very large X or Y pixel dimensions may fail
to be added to the TIFF.
Action Summary
AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage: Adds the current page as a new image of a multiple image TIFF.
MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage: Merges all pages under a document or batch object into a single multi-page TIFF.
SetMergeFileName: The name of the multiple page TIFF to create.
SetMergeOutputDirectory: Allows specification of the output directory. If not called, defaults to the batch directory.
SetPreserveCompression: If the same compression should be used in the final file.
SetStatusToIncludeOrExclude: Optionally allows inclusion or exclusion of images by document or page status.
The compression defaults to fax compression for black and white images and LZW for grayscale and color images.
LZW is preferred for images
as it is a lossless compression and will not degrade the quality of the image. The default can be changed
from LZW to JPEG compression for color and grayscale images. JPEG is a lossy compression, which can degrade
the quality of the image. If OCR is to be performed, it is recommended to use LZW compression to preserve the
image quality.
To enable JPEG compression, set the variable "MergeCompression" to "1" on the DCO object that
calls the AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage or MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage action.
Set the variable "MergeTiffJpegQuality" to configure the quality of the JPEG compression.
The value must be an integer between 0 and 100. 0 uses maximum compression, the worst image quality.
100 uses minimum compression, the best image quality.
More compression produces a smaller file size while sacrificing image quality.
For example:
rrSet("1", "@X.MergeCompression")
rrSet("80", "@X.MergeTiffJpegQuality")
Refer to the top-level action help of the Application Objects action library for more information
regarding the Datacap Object Hierarchy (DCO).
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
For example, "@X" is notation for accessing the current object. "@P" accesses the page object, which
could be the current object, or a parent object. Being evaluated at runtime, allows recognized data
or other batch specific data to be passed to actions or stored as metadata. A smart parameter such
as @DATE could be used to name export files based on the current date. Similar smart parameters
will retrieve the current batch ID, current batch directory, current operator ID, and more.
Smart parameters are a very powerful mechanism of getting data from other areas of the application and copying
it into a new location or passing it as a parameter to an action. It is recommended that the smart parameter
documentation is reviewed to understand the full capabilities available. The top-level help of the
ValidationAndTextAdjustments action library also has information about smart parameters. Some characters such
as +, \ and . also have special smart parameter meaning and may be interpreted as a smart parameter. This
can be controlled using smart parameter syntax.

method.name: AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage
method.qi: Adds each single image to the multi-Image file.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Adds the image associated withe the current page object to the multi-Image TIF file. The action SetMergeOutputDirectory and
SetMergeFileName determine the name and location of the output TIF file.
The source images can be TIFF, PNG, JPG or PNG files.
The values set in SetStatusToIncludeOrExclude are ignored by this action. The page is unconditionally added.
Use rule logic to determine if the action should or should not be called for a page.
The action MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage is more efficient than this action because a single file
is opened and all of the images are added in one step. In contrast, this action will open and close the
same file for every page. Each page within the image will lengthen the time required to
update the file. If efficiency is a concern, it is recommended to use MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage.
CheckDCOStatus("0")
AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage()
In this example, the
CheckDCOStatus
action checks that the status of the current page is “0”.
If so, the image for the current page will be added to the multi-Image file.
If the current status of this page is not “0”, the CheckDCOStatus will return false and control
will jump to the next function in the rule and the action to add the current page
to the file will not be called. This us the flow of the rule logic based
on the action's return value.
This
CheckDCOStatus
action is used as an example. You can use many other
actions to be sure the current image meets your merging criteria. Rules can be
created to determine if some criteria is met to then add the image.
It is required that first the action SetMergeFileName is called to set the
output file name. While not required,
SetMergeFileName would typically be called on a batch
or document level rule to set the file name, then multiple calls to AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage
on page level objects will add the pages to the specified file name. SetMergeFileName
must be called within the same task as the specified output file name remains in effect only
for the current task. If the action is used again in a later task, the output file
name, and optionally the output directory, will need to be set again.
method.ret:
False
if the action is not called on a rule attached to a page object or if the
corresponding image file for the current page cannot be found or is not successfully added
to the destination image. Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
SetMergeOutputDirectory, SetMergeFileName, MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage
Refer to the top-level help for this action library for general information about using these actions
and how to change the default compression.

method.name: MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage
method.qi: Merges all pages under a document or batch object into a single multi-page TIFF.
method.ap:
TypesToMerge:
A comma separated list of all page types to include in the new multi-page image.
If parameter is empty, or set to "All", then all pages under the calling object will
be added to the multi-page image.
Smart parameters are supported
method.h:
This action will add the image associated with each child page object to
a multiple page TIFF file, providing that the page object meets the
required page type or status values. The source page image can be
a TIFF, PNG, BMP or JPEG image.
If one or more page types are provided as a parameter, only those page
types will be added to the TIFF. The action SetStatusToIncludeOrExclude
can be used to place additional restrictions on what pages should be
added or excluded based on the status of the page or parent document object.
The name of the output file must have been previously set by calling
the action SetMergeFileName. By default, the output file will be created
in the batch directory. The output directory can be changed using the
action SetMergeOutputDirectory.
This action always creates a new file.
If the destination file exists, it will be replaced by the new file.
If this action is attached to a batch level rule, all of the pages within the batch,
including pages that have the batch object as the parent and pages that have parent document
objects, will be added to the multi-page TIFF.
If this action is attached to a document level rule, all of the child pages to the current
document object will be added to the multi-page TIFF.
SetMergeFileName("@BATCHID+-+@DATE(dd.mm.yyyy)")
SetMergeOutputDirectory("@APPPATH(export)")
MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage("All")
The above example will name the output file based on the current batch ID
and the current date. The file will be saved in the configured
export directory. All of the chid pages under the current
object will be added to the TIFF. Instead of specifying "All",
a blank parameter would also include all child images.
SetMergeFileName("Doc_+@ID+@DATE(dd.mm.yyyy)")
SetStatusToIncludeOrExclude("0,49","","","")
MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage("Invoice,Attachment")
The second example assumes it is called on a document object and
names the output file based on the ID of the document and current date
with a "Doc_" prefix on the file name. The action is also configured
to only add pages that have a status of 0 or 49. All other page statuses
will be excluded, even if they are of the expected type.
Finally the merge is performed, specifying that only pages of type "Invoice" and of
page type "Attachment" are added to the TIFF.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for this action library for general information about using these actions
and how to change the default compression.

method.name: SetMergeOutputDirectory
method.qi: Sets the path for the image file.
method.ap:
The output directory for the new multiple page TIFF. If this action is not called, the batch directory
will be used by default.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action allows specification of the output directory for the multi-page TIFF image that is created
by the action MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage.
If this action is not called, then the default location is the current batch directory.
If desired, the file can be created in the batch directory and then the file can be
moved or copied to another directory using the FileIO action library in a subsequent
rule, such as during an export task.
If the folder designated in the parameter does not exist,
the action will create the folder in which the TIF file will be placed. If it is expected for
the directory to be created, then ensure the account for the process running rules has permission
to create new directories.
To take affect, this action must be called before the action MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage
and must be called within the same task as the MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage action.
The setting will remain in affect for the length of the current running task.
Once the task completes, this action would need to be called again in a new task
if MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage is called again.
Can be called at any level but is usually called at the batch or document level.
SetMergeOutputDirectory("c:\ParentDir\Invoice\MultiImage")
SetMergeFileName("@BATCHID+-+@ID")
MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage("Doc_+@ID+@DATE(dd.mm.yyyy)", "All")
This example sets the output directory to the parameter provided. The file is named
based on the current batch ID and the ID of the current object.
SetMergeOutputDirectory("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)")
If SetMergeOutputDirectory is not called, then the output directory defaults to the batch
directory. It is identical to making the a call to this action with "@PILOT(BATCHDIR)".
If the default output directory has been changed to another directory, it can be
reset by using this smart parameter to set it back to the batch directory.
method.see:
SetMergeFileName
Refer to the top-level help for this action library for general information about using these actions.

method.name: SetMergeFileName
method.qi: Sets the name of the multi-Image file (.tif) to be created.
method.ap:
MultiPageFileName:
The name of the new image file to create. If the destination directory
has not been set by calling the action SetMergeOutputDirectory, then the file will be created in the
current batch directory by default.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action sets the name of the multi-Image TIFF file to be created by the action AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage
and MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage. Smart parameters can be used allowing the file name to be
a combination of text and data evaluated at runtime.
If not provided, the action automatically adds the “.tif” extension to the file.
Once set, the name is in effect for the remainder of the task, unless the action
is called again to change the output name. Once the task completes, the name will have to
be configured again in a following ruleset if more images are merged.
SetMergeFileName("Doc_+@ID+@DATE(dd.mm.yyyy)")
SetMergeOutputDirectory("c:\ParentDir\Invoice\MultiImage")
MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage("")
The example above assumes that the rules with these actions are attached to a Document object.
The names combine text values such as “Doc_” with values assigned to variables by using smart parameters
to concatenate the current document ID and current date as the name of the output file.
SetMergeFileName("MultiTif_+@ID")
This example combines "MultiTif_" with the ID of the Document Hierarchy object to which the ruleset is
associated.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
SetMergeOutputDirectory
Refer to the top-level help for this action library for general information about using these actions.

method.name: SetPreserveCompression
method.qi: Determines the output compression type for merged images.
method.ap:
True:
Preserves the original compression type of the source image.
If the image does not have the compression type then the compression
type G4 for black and white and LZW for color images will be applied.
False:
Uses G4 compression for black and white images.
LZW compression is used for color images.
The default LZW compression can be configured as described below.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret: True.
method.h:
This action will configure the output format for the new multi-page TIF file
when for the AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage action.
If this action is not called, then the default value of "FALSE" is used,
so the original image compression is not preserved and the action will
pick the optimal compression based on the color depth.
If the compression is preserved, then the action will attempt to keep the
original compression of the image. For example, if the image was uncompressed,
it will save the image in the TIFF as uncompressed. Each page in the image
can have a different compression and that compression isn't displayed in the
file properties in Windows explorer. Depending on the original compression,
it may not be supported for saving, in that case, the next best compression
that preserves the original color depth will be used.
By default, LZW compression is used for grayscale and color images. LZW is preferred for images
as it is a lossless compression and will not degrade the quality of the image. The default can be changed
from LZW to JPEG compression for color and grayscale images. JPEG is a lossy compression, which can degrade
the quality of the image. If OCR is to be performed, it is recommended to use LZW compression to preserve the
image quality.
To enable JPEG compression, set the variable "MergeCompression" to "1" on the DCO object that
calls the AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage or MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage action.
Set the variable "MergeTiffJpegQuality" to configure the quality of the JPEG compression.
The value must be an integer between 0 and 100. 0 uses maximum compression, the worst image quality.
100 uses minimum compression, the best image quality.
More compression produces a smaller file size while sacrificing image quality.
SetPreserveCompression("True")
AddCurrentPageImageToMultiplePageTIFFImage("")
This example sets the compression to preserve the original compression of
the image then merges the image.
rrSet("1", "@X.MergeCompression")
rrSet("80", "@X.MergeTiffJpegQuality")
SetPreserveCompression("False")
MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage("All")
This example configures the merge to use JPEG compression for color and grayscale images in the merged TIFF image.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help for this action library for general information about using these actions.

method.name: SetStatusToIncludeOrExclude
method.qi: Filters merged pages based on the page and document status.
method.ap:
AcceptablePageStatuses:
A CSV list of Page status values that will be merged.
DisregardPageStatuses:
A CSV list of Page status values that will not be merged.
AcceptableDocStatuses:
A CSV list of Document status value that will be merged.
DisregardDocStatuses:
A CSV list of Document status values that will not be merged.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.ret: Always True.
method.h:
This action will configure the acceptable statuses for documents and pages when calling TifMerge_MergeImages.
If this action is not called, then the status values of documents and pages will not be checked.
If multiple parameters are set, be sure they will operate as expected. It can make sense to set a document
status parameter and a page status parameter. It would probably not make sense to set both page parameters or
both document parameters as it will cause multiple exclusions.
If the AcceptablePageStatuses is set, then the status of the page object must be in the list or page image will not
be added to the merged TIFF image. This effectively disregards all other page status values.
If the AcceptableDocStatuses is set, then the status of the page's parent document object
must be in the list or the page image will not
be added to the merged TIFF image. This effectively disregards all other document status values.
If the DisregardPageStatus is set, then if the status of the page object is in the list, then the page
image will not be added to the merged TIFF image.
If the DisregardDocStatus is set, then if the status of the page's parent document object is in the list, then the page
image will not be added to the merged TIFF image.
All conditions must be met for the page to be included.
In the example below, only pages with an acceptable status of '0' or '49' will be merged. Because
the document status is also set, then if the page's document object does not have a status of "0",
the page will not be included, regardless of it's status.
Empty parameters are ignored.
SetStatusToIncludeOrExclude("0,49","","0","")
MergeToMultiplePageTIFFImage("All")
method.see: Refer to the top-level help for this action library for general information about using these actions.

com.h:
The Validations and Text Adjustments action library focus on actions that perform validation and manipulation
of recognized text within an application. When recognizing a field it is recommended to configure the field
properties for the target engine to correctly specify the type of text being recognized and limit the
field to the expected character set. For example, if a field is expected to be numeric only, then the field
should be preset to recognize only numeric values. Perhaps a field may have some other restricted character set
such as numeric values plus "A, B, C, D, E, F", then the field can be setup to allow just those characters. This
improves the recognition quality.
It isn't always possible to tell the recognition engine exactly what is expected. This action library can help
filter out invalid characters or flag fields that do not match expected patterns or expected data types. For example,
if a date does not match the expected date pattern for the locale, then the validation actions can flag the field
so it can be examined by a verification operator. Likewise, a validation check can be done for numeric formats or totals
of several numeric fields.
Upon failure of a tested condition, most of the actions in this action library will also store the
reason for the message in a standard variable called Message. This DCO variable is used by client
verification panels to display messages to verify operators so they can understand why a page
has failed a verification ruleset. If there are multiple reasons for a failure, these messages are only
displayed to the user one at a time, so the operator must fix the displayed error, rerun the validation
test and see if additional verification errors still remain. If errors still remain, the operator will
need to repeat the process until they have rectified all of the issues that are causing a page
to fail validation. Typically a the rule for a validation action is attached to the
DCO object that needs to pass the validation so the message is associated with the failed object
and typically the status of the object will be set to "1" to indicate the failure in a verification panel.
For example, one common validation is that a particular field is required to have a particular length. Perhaps
it has a minimum length, or a maximum length, or both. The validation action that checks a field's
length can be added to a validation ruleset to confirm that the length is correct. If the length is incorrect
after a recognition step, it can flag the failed field to the operator in the verify panel. Likewise, it
can revalidate a field after it has been reviewed by an operator to help confirm the field is now at
the required length before moving on to the next page. The more validations that can be placed on the
field data for an application will provide a greater assurance that the data on the page was accurately
recognized or correctly entered by an operator.
Locale Sensitive Operations
The validation actions are sensitive to the locale where it is applicable. For example, date validation and currency
validation are performed based on the current locale. If not set within the application, the locale used is the
machine's default Windows locale. The locale for the entire application can be set within the Application Manager,
which will override the windows locale, and instead use the locale configured for the entire application.
Datacap clients and actions support multiple locales within a single application and multiple locales within a single
batch. The hierarchical DCO variable hr_locale, can be specified to control the locale of the DCO object being
processed.
rrSet("en-GB", "@X.hr_locale)
This example sets the locale for the current DCO node and it's children objects to English (United Kingdom).
rrSet can be used to set the value at runtime, or the value for hr_locale can be set in the setup DCO, if needed.
When specifying locales, use standard LCIDs, and these are case sensitive.
If set at the batch level, it affects the entire application. If set on a document DCO node, then it sets the
locale for all pages and fields within that document. This can be controlled at any level. If set at the page level
then the locale will be set for the entire page and its fields, allowing each page within a document to have a unique locale.
For example, one page could have a US locale with US formatted data while the next page could have a French locale with French formatted data.
It is possible, although not usually required, to have unique locales configured for each field within
a single page.
Smart Parameters - Brief Guide
The top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library contains the complete smart parameter reference.
Here is a short set of examples.
If an action supports smart parameters, it is specified in the action help. Smart parameters are very powerful
specifications for parameters that allow access of data to and from other DCO objects and perform
special pre-defined operations in one step.
Smart parameters can be used to dynamically obtain or create action input parameters at runtime. For example,
an action could be fed the value of a field after recognition, a parameter could pull the value from a
DCO variable that was set by a previous action, or a smart parameter could evaluate to the current date, the current
time, the current job ID, the current operator ID, the path to the current batch that is running, and more.
Smart parameter syntax can also be used to build expressions at runtime that concatenate dynamic data and
static data at runtime. Smart parameters are
a flexible way to provide a wide range of input to any action that supports smart parameters.
The following are some examples of manipulation that are common for manipulating data where it may be expected
that a special action exists in the this action library but is not required. This summary is intended to
show some manipulation that is typical for validation tasks. This set of examples are by no means
the limit of how smart parameters can be used. While many of these examples show the
value being passed to the handy action rrSet, the same smart parameter can be passed to any action
that supports smart parameters as input.
Refer to the full smart parameter guide in the top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic actions
for full details on all available smart parameters and how to use them.
Append Text To A Field:
rrSet("Append This +@F","@F")
Assuming this is running on a field object, it appends the text "Append This " to the current text value of the field.
If the field originally contained "ABCD", the final value is "Append This ABCD")
rrSet("Append This +@F+ The End","@F")
Similarly, if the original field value is "ABCD", the final value of the field text is "Append This ABCD The End".
Concatenate Text From A Different Field:
rrSet("@P\AnotherField+@F","@F")
This example will grab the text value from the sibling field "AnotherField" and append the text to the front of the
text in the current DCO field.
Concatenate Text From A Different Field Variable:
rrSet("@P\AnotherField.MyVariable+@F","@F")
This example will grab the value from the sibling field "AnotherField" variable called "MyVariable" and append the text to the front of the
text in the current DCO field.
Concatenate Text From A Different Field Variable Placed Into New Variable:
rrSet("@P\AnotherField.MyVariable+@CHR(32)+@F","@F.NewVariable")
This example will grab the value from the sibling field "AnotherField" variable called "MyVariable" and append the text to the front of the
text in the current DCO field. The current value of the field object is not updated, instead the new result is placed into a variable
for the current field called "NewVariable".
Assuming that "MyVariable" contains the text "Hello" and the current field value is "Tom", the first parameter will
fully resolve to "Hello Tom" and pass that value to the rrSet action, which will then place that new string
into the variable called "NewVariable".
Assigning A Default Field Value:
rrSet("My Default Text","@P\MyField")
Assuming this action is run on a page object that contains a field called "MyField", it initialized the default value of
the field the "My Default Text". If the field was already recognized, then this new text overwrites the existing text.
If the field is later recognized, then this default text will be replaced by the recognized text.
Assigning Today's Date To A Field:
rrSet("@DATE(dd.mm.yyyy)","@X")
This example shows how to assign the current date in day, month, year format when rules are run on
a field object. If a date format is not specified, the @DATE smart parameter will default to MM/DD/YYYY.
Likewise, the smart parameter @TIME() can be used to put a time stamp into a field or as a parameter to an action
that supports smart parameters.
Assigning The Current Job ID A Field:
rrSet("@JOBID","@X")
Assuming this is called on a field level object, this example shows how to assign the current job ID to the text value of a
field object.
Is the current Job ID the expected Job ID:
rrCompare("@JOBID","MyJobID")
This compares the current Job ID with the string "MyJobID" and returns true if it matches. If needed
the hard coded "MyJobID" could reference a smart parameter that contains the value. Alternatively,
rrCompareNot can be used to return true if the current Job ID is does not match the provided string.
Other comparison actions perform case insensitive comparisons.
Clear a field's value:
rrSet("@EMPTY","@F\MyField")
This example shows how to empty the recognized value of the field "MyField" using a rule called on a page that
contains the "MyField" child.
To continue if a field is empty:
rrCompare("@EMPTY","@X)
This action would be called on the field object.
The smart parameters can reference hard coded values or obtain
values from other objects or other DCO variables.
To continue if a field is empty from page level:
rrCompare("@EMPTY","@X\MyField")
This tests to see if the page's field called "MyField" is empty. If so, the rule continues.
To continue if a field is not empty:
rrCompareNot("@EMPTY","@X")
This action would be called on the field object to check the text value of the field.
If the current field is empty, the function will continue to the next action
in the rule. If the field contains
text, then control will branch to the next function in the ruleset.
To test if a field value is greater than a specific number:
rrCompareNumeric("1234", "˂", "@X")
This action tests to see if the numeric value of the current field text is
greater than 1234. Parameters can be changed as needed. For example, if "@X" was
replaced with "@D.MyVar", the value 1234 will be compared against the
value of the parent document level variable called "MyVar".
Test if a field is hidden:
rrCompare("-1","@X.STATUS")
If a field has a STATUS of "-1", it is considered to be a hidden field or ignored and is not displayed
in a client verification panel. If rules logic needs to determine if a field is hidden,
it can be tested by checking the STATUS variable of the field to see if it is "-1".
This example assumes the action is running on the current field object whose status will
be checked. Of course, smart parameters can be used to navigate and check the status
of other DCO objects.

method.name: AddAllLineitemTaxesToTaxField
method.qi: Adds all tax values from detail structure into Tax field.
method.ap: None
method.h:
Adds all tax values from detail structure into Tax field.
This action is not for general use. It is intended for an application, like APT,
where the application has a tax detail field that contains a field lineitems of taxes
called "TaxLineitem".
The application must also have another field called "Tax", which will be updated
with the result of this action.
This action will set the position of the tax field to "0,0,0,0".
AddAllLineitemTaxesToTaxField()
method.lvl: The close event of TaxLineitem detail field in APT.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: AddPaddingCharacterToStart
method.qi: Extends a field or variable to a specified length using a specific padding character.
method.ap:
Target : A smart parameter that resolves to the target DCO object or variable to pad with characters to the start of the string.
PadCharacter : The character to pad in front of the text to extend it to the maximum length.
MaximumLength : The target path and filename.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Accepts a specification for a DCO field or DCO variable and extends the length of the text by placing
the specified character in front of the existing text until the length is at the specified maximum.
If the current text length is at, or beyond, the specified maximum length then the existing text
will not be changed.
AddPaddingCharacterToStart("@F", "0", "10")
Assuming this action is called on a feild object that contains the recognized value "2240.00",
it will be adjusted to "0002240.00"
AddPaddingCharacterToStart("@P\Total", " ", "10")
Assuming this action is called on a page object that has a child field called "Total",
this action will pad the recognized value of "Total" with leading spaces until
the length reaches 10 characters. If the field "Total" has a text
value of "Hello", it will add 5 spaces to the start of the text in
the field.
AddPaddingCharacterToStart("@X.MyVariable", "@STRING("@")", "15")
This action will pad the text stored in the object's variable called "MyVariable".
The text will pad the beginning of the text with an @ symbol until it is
15 characters in length. Because the @ symbol is a special smart parameter
it must be specified using the @STRING or @CHR smart parameter notation
to prevent it from being interpreted as a smart parameter.
If the variable "MyVariable" has the text "Jack and Jill", the final value
of "MyVariable" will be "@@Jack and Jill".
method.see: The top level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: AddPaddingCharacterToEnd
method.qi: Extends a field or variable to a specified length using a specific padding character.
method.ap:
Target : A smart parameter that resolves to the target DCO object or variable to pad with a character.
PadCharacter : The character to pad in front of the text to extend it to the maximum length.
MaximumLength : The target path and filename. Smart parameters are supported.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Accepts a specification for a DCO field or variable and extends the length of the text by placing
the specified character at the end of the existing text until the length is at the specified maximum.
If the current text length is at, or beyond, the specified maximum length then the existing text
will not be changed.
AddPaddingCharacterToEnd("@F", "0", "10")
Assuming this action is called on a feild object that contains the recognized value "2240.00",
it will be adjusted to "2240.00000"
AddPaddingCharacterToEnd("@P\Total", " ", "10")
Assuming this action is called on a page object that has a child field called "Total",
this action will pad the recognized value of "Total" with trailing spaces until
the length reaches 10 characters. If the field "Total" has a text
value of "Hello", it will add 5 spaces to the end of the text in
the field.
AddPaddingCharacterToEnd("@X.MyVariable", "@STRING("@")", "15")
This action will pad the text stored in the object's variable called "MyVariable".
The text will pad the end of the text with an @ symbol until it is
15 characters in length. Because the @ symbol is a special smart parameter
it must be specified using the @STRING or @CHR smart parameter notation
to prevent it from being interpreted as a smart parameter.
If the variable "MyVariable" has the text "Jack and Jill", the final value
of "MyVariable" will be "Jack and Jill@@".
method.see: The top level help topic for general information about this action library.

method.name: AddToErrorMessage

p.name: p1
p.qi: Error message text.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action allows for custom messages to be displayed to the verify operator when a validation fails.
The provided message is appended to any existing error message.
How the message is displayed back to user depends on the verify client used.
AddToErrorMsg("Vendor Number cannot be blank.")
method.ret:
Always
False.
method.see: ClearErrorMessage

method.name: AddToLineItemDetailErrorMessage

p.name: p1
p.qi: Error message text.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action allows for custom messages to be displayed to the verify operator when a validation fails for line items.
The provided message is appended to any existing error message.
How the message is displayed back to user depends on the verify client used.
AddToLineItemDetailErrorMessage("Description cannot be blank.")
method.lvl: Field level. Specifically, it must be a line item detail field.
method.ret:
Always
False.
method.see: ClearErrorMessage

method.name: AllowOnlyCharacters
method.qi: Filters out characters not contained in the allowed set.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to be updated.
AllowedCharacters
A value that specifies permitted characters in the current word.
An empty parameter removes all characters. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action removes all characters NOT in the parameter from the a Field's recognized value
or from a DCO variable. If the target is a field's recognized text, the confidence of the
remaining characters will not be changed by this operation.
An empty argument will remove ALL characters. The specified characters are case sensitive so
if characters should be removed regardless of case, add the upper and lower case characters to be removed.
AllowOnlyCharacters("@F", "ABCDEFG.")
Calling this action on a field DCO object, if the field value is "HELLO DOLLY." it becomes "ED."
The order of the characters in the input parameter have no affect on the result.
AllowOnlyCharacters("@X.MyVariable", "ABCDEFG.")
The action AllowOnlyCharacters" will filter the text within the DCO variable "MyVariable"
on the current DCO object.
AllowOnlyCharacters("@F", "AaBbCc+@STRING(@+)")
There are times when characters need to be passed to an action that are also special smart parameter symbols.
Because the characters + and @ are special smart parameter symbols, they must be specified
using syntax which allows them to be added without interpretation.
The @STRING specification allows the text within it to be passed to the action without smart parameter processing.
The final result from
the example is that the characters "AaBcCc@+" will be the only characters allowed in the final value.
AllowOnlyCharacters("@F", "@STRING(AaBbCc@+)")
Smart parameters are processed as tokens that can often be specified multiple ways,
producing the same final result. This example is an alternate specification of the above
example. Instead of separating parts of the character input, because the entire input
string is static, the entire input string can also be specified as a single value within
the @STRING token. This example produces the same resolved input parameter of "AaBcCc@+".
AllowOnlyCharacters("@F", "@P\Field1+@STRING(AaBbCc@+)")
Sometimes input to an action needs to come from another location, or data that is captured
at runtime. This example shows another use of smart parameters to combine dynamic text from a field
and hard coded text. The example would be called on a field object who has a sibling
field called "Field1". Assuming the text value of Field1 is "XYZ", the final parameter
passed to the action evaluates to "XYZAaBbCc@+".
method.ret:
False,
if called on the wrong level. Otherwise
True.
method.see:
The top level help topic for general information about this action library.
The top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library contains the complete smart parameter reference.

method.name: AlterDateByDay
method.qi: Adds or subtracts days from a date text.

p.name: target
p.qi: A smart parameter that specifies the target field or variable to update.

p.name: days
p.qi: The number of days to add to the date.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The action will add or subtract the specified number of days to the date text. The target text to update can be in a field
or a variable.
The action requires that the date format match that of the current locale. The hr_locale variable is respected, if set.
The action will output the
updated date in the default format for the current locale. The output date may or may not have leading zeros
for single digit dates.
The original character confidence is not changed.
rrSet("04/01/2025", "@F")
AlterDatebyDay("@F", "7")
This example adds one week to the date contained in the field. If the date crosses
over a month or year boundary, they will be adjusted appropriately.
The value 04/01/2025 is changed to 4/8/2025.
method.ret:
Always,
True.

method.name: CalculateDateDifference
method.qi: Calculates a date difference in days, months, quarters or years.
method.ap:
startDate
: The starting date.
endDate
: The ending date.
targetVariable
: The variable to hold the calculated result value.
dateProperty
: The value to calculate. 0 = days, 1 = months, 2 = quarters, 3 = years.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Calculates the number of days, months, quarters or years between two dates.
Only whole numbers are returned. Any fractional parts of the value are dropped.
Quarters are calculated simply by dividing the number of months by 3.
The order of the dates does not matter.
Note this action only supports Gregorian short dates as input and the date format must match the
default format of the current locale.
If the date requirements are met, the action returns true. If the date requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object. Typically this would be
called on a field object which needs to pass this validation test.
CalculateDateDifference("4/20/2012", "5/19/2012", "@P.Months", 1)
This example will create the page variable "Months" with a value of "0".
CalculateDateDifference("4/20/2012", "5/20/2012", "@P.Months", 1)
This example will create the page variable "Months" with a value of "1".
CalculateDateDifference("4/20/2012", "4/19/2013", "@P.Years", 3)
This example will create the page variable "Years" with a value of "0".
CalculateDateDifference("4/20/2012", "4/20/2013", "@P.Years", 3)
This example will create the page variable "Years" with a value of "1".
CalculateDateDifference(@P\MyDate1, @P\MyDate2, "@P.Days", 0)
This example will create the page variable "Days" with the number of days between the dates specified by the values in field MyDate1 and field MyDate2.
CalculateDateDifference(@P.MyDate1, @P.MyDate2, "@P.Days", 0)
This example will create the page variable "Days" with the number of days between the dates specified by page variables MyDate1 and MyDate2.
method.ret:
False,
If the format of either date is invalid. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters and the use of the current locale.

method.name: CalculateFields
method.qi: Performs numeric calculations on fields and evaluates the result.
method.ap:
Equation:
The equation that is the basis for the calculation.
You can use a Field object's name or numeric values with any arithmetic operator (+,-,*,/,^).
To use a Field object's name, or numeric value, surround it with single quotation marks (').
An empty value is treated as a "0".
DecimalDigits:
The number of decimal places to limit the logical comparison. If left blank, or invalid, the
number will default to the value for the current locale.
PreserveStatus:
Can be "True" or "False" to indicate if he status of all associated fields if the calculation fails should
be updated based on success or failure of the operation. If not provided, or invalid, the value will default to False.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Calculates the equation entered as a parameter. The equation can contain field names which will
use the field's value at runtime. The equation can contain mathematical operations +, -, *, and /.
A single equality can also be performed such as =, ˂, =˂, =>, >, and ˂>.
If the equation contains a boolean equality, the action will determine if the equation evaluates to true or false.
If the result is false, then status of the fields specified within the equation
will be set to "1", allowing them to be reviewed by a following task
such as a verification operator. The equation should be specified so that two sides of
the equation can be evaluated to determine if the entire equation is correct.
Note:
If the result does not match the equation's result, dependent fields (fields involved in the
equation) will receive a Failed status and will appear pink in the applicable field of the Client's Verification panel.
If the results of a previously failed CalculateFields call are corrected by a user, such that the calculation no longer returns false, dependent fields that
were set to status Failed by the CalculateFields action will be updated to status Pass.
It is likely that dependent fields could have their statuses updated via other rules and actions,
so it is important when configuring your application to properly stage,
and sequence your validations action logic to work in tandem with the CalculateFields action.
It is important to be aware that smart parameters are supported for all parameters. Smart parameters use special
characters such as "+". To use a "+" in an equation, it is necessary to specify the text so it is not
interpreted as a special character. This can be achieved using the @STRING or @CHR smart parameters
as shown in the example.
If the equality calculation equation is successful, the action returns true. If the equation is not satisfied, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object. Typically this would be
called on a field object which needs to pass this validation test.
If the specified equation does not contain an equality operation, then the resulting
value will be calculated and stored in the text value of the current field object.
If called on a page level object, then the calculated value will be stored in
a DCO variable called "CalculateField" and the action will return true.
CalculateFields("@STRING('SubTotal' + 'Shipping' + 'Tax' = 'Total')", "2", "False")
This example sums the "SubTotal", "Shipping" and "Tax" fields and checks to see if the total
of the three fields equals the value in the "Total" field. If they are not the same,
then the status will be changed to "1" for each of the fields.
The above example places the entire expression into the "@STRING" smart parameter keyword to
prevent any pre-processing of the expression, particularly the + signs within the expression, which
would otherwise be first interpretated as smart parameter operators, changing the evaluated expression.
CalculateFields("('SubTotal' +@CHR(43)+ 'Shipping' +@CHR(43)+ 'Tax') - '0.05' = 'Total'", "2", "False")
This example is similar to the above example, but also includes a hard coded value
within the equation. The smart parameter @CHR(43) evaluates to a plus sign. Because the parameter is
supports smart parameters, the + will be interpreted as a smart parameter and change the input string.
This technique will resolve to a + in the final equation like this:
('SubTotal' + 'Shipping' + 'Tax') - '0.05' = 'Total'
The above example takes an alternate approach by using @CHR(43) to insert the + sign into the expression.
To check for a 'tolerance' use two actions in sequence like this:
CalculateFields("@STRING(('Wages' + 'Interest' + 'Unemployment') > =('Gross'- '.05'))", "2", "False")
CalculateFields("@STRING(('Wages' + 'Interest' + 'Unemployment') < =('Gross'+ '.05'))", "2", "False")
The example will calculate fields twice and allow the range of values. If both tests pass, then they will both return
True. If either test fails, the action will return false and set the status of the field to "1" indicating there is
a problem with the field.
CalculateFields("'SubTotal' +@CHR(43)+ 'Shipping' +@CHR(43)+ 'Tax')", "0", "False")
This example will sum the values of the "SubTotal", "Shipping" and "Tax" fields and stores the result
in the text value of the current field, or if called on a page object, the value will be stored
in a variable called "CalculateFields". This calculated value can be accessed by subsequent actions.
CalculateFields("'SubTotal' * '2')", "0", "False")
This example finds the value of the SubTotal field and multiplies it by 2 and stores the result.
Some numeric operators used for field calculations are also used as smart parameter tokens. When a parameter
allows smart parameters, the parameter will always be processed for smart parameter tokens first. The
@STRING() token is a common way to pass these values without interpretation. If an action is not processing
correctly, it is likely due to a numeric symbol being processed as a smart parameter. Check the action log
to see if the evaluation statement is built as expected and adjust the action parameters as required.
method.ret:
True
if the expression evaluates to True.
False
if the expression evaluates to False or the expression is not valid (eg. a field's value is not numeric).
method.see:
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding the use of the current locale.
The top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library contains the complete smart parameter reference.

method.name: CalculateInvoiceTotal
method.qi: Determines if the Total field is within the tolerance for the data on the page.
method.ap: The floating point tolerance value that will be used to determine if the Tax, Shipping and Detail values equal the Total within the tolerance.
method.h:
Uses the Details, Tax and Shipping fields to calculate the total value and checks to see if it matches the Total field within
the specified tolerance.
This action is not for general use. It is intended for an application, like APT,
where the application has a "Tax", "Shipping" and "Details" field.
IsFieldCurrency()
CalculateInvoiceTotal("0.02")
In this example, the combined total of the Tax, Shipping and Details fields must be within .02 of the total field.
method.lvl: Must be called on the invoice total field.

method.name: CalculateLineItemQuantityAndPrice
method.qi: Determines if the LineTotal field is correct.
method.ap: The floating point tolerance value that will be used to determine if the LineTotal matches the Qty * Price within the tolerance.
method.h:
Determines if the fields "Qty * Price = LineTotal" within
the specified tolerance value.
This action is not for general use. It is intended for an application, like APT,
where the application has a lineitems field with a qty and price.
IsFieldCurrency()
CalculateLineItemQuantityAndPrice("0.02")
method.lvl: Must be called on the Invoice_Total field.
method.ret:
False
if the Qty, Price or LineTotal fields do not contain a numeric value.
True
if the Qty * Price matches the LineTotal value within the specified tolerance. Otherwise,
False.

method.name: ChangeTextToMixedCase
method.qi: Changes the text so the first letter of every word is upper-case.

p.name: Target
p.qi: A smart parameter that specifies a variable or field.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action changes text to be Title case where the first letter of
each word will be capitalized.
ChangeTextToMixedCase("@P\Field1")
If the field in this example is "hello, i MUST be going.", the text will be changed to "Hello, I Must Be Going."
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library for the smart parameters reference guide.

method.name: CheckAndSetCurrencyDecimalToPeriod
method.qi: Changes currency values to have a period decimal separator.

p.name: target
p.qi: A smart parameter that references a field or variable.

method.ap: The target location identifies the location of the text to check and update.
method.h:
The action updates the decimal separator on text that is expected to be a currency value, meaning
that the value has two decimal places, such as "xxx.xx". The action will check the location where
the decimal separator is expected. If the character is a space, or a comma, the character
will be replaced with a period. This action is not locale aware and will operate the same
regardless of the currently selected locale.
This action can be used to fix errors where the decimal is not recognized and leaves a blank in that area,
also this can be used for conversion for European numbers that use a comma to separate the whole amount from decimal
portion. For example: "$100,00" becomes "$100.00" and "$100 00" becomes "$100.00".
CheckAndSetCurrencyDecimalToPeriod("@F")
AllowOnlyCharacters("0123456789.-")
IsFieldCurrency()
This example assumes it is called on a field object.
method.ret:
False, if an error occurs. Otherwise,
True.

method.name: CheckSubFields
method.qi: Checks values in a lineitem.
method.ap:
An "expression" that specifies which LINEITEM child fields are to be checked for the presence or absence
of captured values. Within the expression, each child Field object's name needs to be surrounded
with single quotation marks ('). You can also use parentheses () in your expression. Action is placed on the
parent of the LINEITEM field. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
In an application that uses lineitems, this action validates an instance of a
parent Field object by confirming the presence (or absence) of
captured values for one or more of its child fields. (In the APT application, as an example,
child fields of the LINEITEM parent include: ItemID, ItemDesc, Quantity, Price and LineTotal.)
Invalid parent Field objects are deleted from the DCO if they do not meet this criteria.
This action should be configured to run in its own RuleSet (for example, in a Filter RuleSet)
because it can delete the DCO objects as rules are running and would be applied
to the DETAILS Field object (parent object to the LINEITEM field) in an application that uses LINEITEMs such as APT.
Example 1:
The captured values for a LINEITEM field are:
ItemID = 12345
ItemDesc =
Price = 12.00
LineTotal =
The action's parameter contains this expression:
CheckSubFields("('ItemID' OR 'ItemDesc') AND ('Price' OR 'LineTotal')")
In this example the action returns
True
and the current LINEITEM object is Valid.
Example 2:
The captured values for the LINEITEM field are:
ItemID = 12345
ItemDesc = Thank you for your order
Price =
LineTotal =
The action's parameter contains this expression:
CheckSubFields("('ItemID' OR 'ItemDesc') AND ('Price' OR 'LineTotal')")
In this example the action's equation returns is
False
and the current LINEITEM
object is Invalid. The field and the values of its child fields are deleted from the Data file.
Example 3:
The captured values for the LINEITEM field are:
ItemID = 12345
LineTotal = gonetolunch
The action's parameter contains this expression:
CheckSubFields("('ItemID') AND ('LineTotal')")
In this case, the action returns
True
and validates the LINEITEM field - despite the
presence of a nonsense entry in the LineTotal child field!
method.lvl: Field level. The parent of the LINEITEM field.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: ClearErrorMessage
method.qi: Removes any previous error messages.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action clears the current error message. Notice that the paradigm is that the error message is cleared at the start
of the function. After clearing the message, then the work will be performed, such as a validation. If the validation
passes, then the message would remain empty. If an error occurs, then the message would be set with the new message.
Status_Preserve_OFF()
ClearErrorMsg()
CaptureOpInfo()
rrCompare("@P\Routing_Instructions","None")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: ConvertFieldToCurrency
method.qi: Formats a numeric field as currency without a currency symbol.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Formats the current field's text value as a currency value without a currency symbol.
If the value does not have a decimal separator, the decimal separator will be added.
The following steps are performed on the field:
1. Removes existing currency symbols.
2. Replaces negative value characters such as parenthesis, 'NEG', 'CR' and trailing hyphen
with a leading hyphen.
3. If a decimal exists, its position is not changed.
4. If a decimal does not exist and the field contains 2 or more characters, a decimal is inserted
before the last two characters in the field.
5. If a decimal does not exist and the field contains less than 2 characters, no decimal is inserted.
This action works on the recognized text value of a field.
To convert a numeric value that is in a DCO variable, first use rrSet to copy the value into a field, then
this action can be run on the field. Once complete, the value could be copied back to the original
DCO variable.
ConvertFieldToCurrency()
A value of
1
remains
1
A value of
12
becomes
.12
A value of
105
becomes
1.05
A value of
104.009
remains
104.009
A value of
$104.009
becomes
104.009
A value of
$12345
becomes
123.45
A value of
($123.45)
becomes
-123.45
A value of
$123.45 NEG
becomes
-123.45
method.ret:
True
if the text value is numeric and greater than one character. Otherwise,
False
.
method.see: Refer to the top level help item in this action library for more information about the use of the current locale.

method.name: ConvertToLowerCase
method.qi: Converts text in a field or variable to lower case.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to be updated.
method.h:
Converts any upper case characters in a field's recognized text value, or in a DCO variable, to lower case characters.
If the target is a field's recognized text, the confidence of the characters will not be changed by this operation.
ConvertToLowerCase("@X")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, it will update the field's text value so it is all lower case.
ConvertToLowerCase("@P\MyField")
Assuming this action is called on a page object, it will update the text value for the DCO child field "MyField"
so it is all lower case.
ConvertToLowerCase("@X.MyVariable")
This example will update the DCO variable called "MyVariable" on the current DCO node so it is
all lower case.
method.ret:
Always
True.

ConvertToUpperCase

method.name: CreateGUID
method.qi: Creates a globally unique identifier
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to be updated.
method.h:
Generates a new GUID value string and stores it in the target location.
CreateGUID("@X")
Assuming this action is called on a field, it will update the field's text value with a new GUID.
CreateGUID("@P\MyField")
Assuming this action is called on a page, it will update the text value for the DCO child field "MyField"
with a new GUID.
CreateGUID("@B.MyVariable")
This example will create a batch level variable called "MyVariable" and set it with a new GUID value.
If the variable does not exist, it will be created.
CreateGUID("@X.MyVariable")
This example will update the DCO variable called "MyVariable" on the current DCO node
with a new GUID value. If the variable does not exist, it will be created.
CreateGUID("@X.MyVariable")
rrSet("This is the GUID:+@X.MyVariable", "@X.myVariable")
This example will update the DCO variable called "MyVariable" on the current DCO node
with a new GUID value. The following rrSet then makes an additional update to the variable to pre-append the string
"This is the GUID:" to the generated GUID.
method.ret:
True,
if successful, otherwise
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters and the
RuleRunnerLogic action library top level help for the complete smart parameter reference.

method.name: DeleteAllCharactersAlphabetic
method.qi: Deletes alphabetic characters from a field or variable.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to be updated.
method.h:
Deletes all alphabetic characters from the current Field object's recognized text value or a DCO variable.
Other characters such as numbers, punctuation and symbols will remain.
If the target is a field's recognized text, the confidence of the
remaining characters will not be changed by this operation.
DeleteAllCharactersAlphabetic("@F")
Assuming this action is called on a field level object, the recognized text value
"JAN2003" becomes "2003".
DeleteAllCharactersAlphabetic("@X.MyVariable")
This action will delete all alphabetic characters from the variable on the current
DCO object.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: DeleteAllCharactersMatchingExpression
method.qi: Deletes all characters in a field or variable that match a regular expression.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to be updated.
RegularExpression:
A regular expression that equates to a matching string pattern. Any characters
that match the expression will be deleted from the text. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Removes all characters with the target field text or target DCO variable that
match the provided expression. Other characters will remain.
If the target is a field's recognized text, the confidence of the
remaining characters will not be changed by this operation.
DeleteAllCharactersMatchingExpression("@F", "@STRING(\p{N}+)")
Assuming this action is called on a field level object, it will remove
all numeric characters from the text. Because the action supports smart
parameters and because the input expression has a + symbol, which is
a special smart parameter symbol, the input string needs to be specified
using a smart parameter to prevent interpretation of the +. One possible
way to do this is by using the @STRING() as shown.
DeleteAllCharactersMatchingExpression("@P\MyField", "@STRING(\p{N}+)")
Assuming this action is called on a page object, it will update the text value for the child field "MyField"
by removing all numeric characters.
DeleteAllCharactersMatchingExpression("@X.MyVariable", "STRING(\p{N}+)")
This action will delete all numeric characters from the variable "MyVariable" on the current
DCO object.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
DeleteAllCharactersAlphabetic, DeleteSelectedCharacters, DeleteAllCharactersMiscellaneous, DeleteAllCharactersPunctuation

method.name: DeleteAllCharactersSelected
method.qi: Deletes specific characters from a field text value.
method.ap:
CharactersToDelete
The character or string of characters to be deleted.
StartIndex
A number indicating the starting index within the string to start deletion. If this parameter
is blank or is not a number, the starting index value will default to the first position in the string.
Count
The number of times the character or character string is to be deleted from the
value. The default is "1" and "*" deletes all instances.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Deletes specific characters from the current Field object's recognized value.
Other characters will remain.
The confidence of the remaining characters will not be changed by this operation.
If a single character is provided as the pattern, then every occurrence of that character will
be deleted up to the amount specified by the count. If multiple characters are provided,
then that pattern must match exactly for the pattern to be deleted.
This action works on a field text value. To perform this operation on a DCO variable,
a temporary field could be used by calling rrSet to populate a field with the desired text,
run the action, then use rrSet to copy the data back to where it is needed.
As with any action that supports smart parameters, if the characters to delete include
smart parameter symbols, they must be specified as a smart parameter so they are properly processed.
DeleteAllCharactersSelected("-", "","*")
223-56-7669 becomes 223567669
DeleteAllCharactersSelected("-","5,"*")
223-86-7669 becomes 223-867669
DeleteAllCharactersSelected(",","","2")
"Hello, Roger, Tom, and Jan" becomes "Hello Roger Tom, and Jan"
DeleteSelectedChars("@STRING(@)","","*")
"Hello, @Roger, @Tom, and @Jan" becomes "Hello, Roger, Tom, and Jan"
DeleteSelectedChars("@STRING(@)+Tom,","","*")
"Hello, @Roger, @Tom, and @Jan" becomes "Hello, @Roger, , and @Jan"
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:

DeleteAllSystemCharacters("@X.MyVariable")

DCO object.

method.qi: Removes spaces from a text field value based on their confidence.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Deletes all low confidence spaces from the current field's recognized text value. By default, any spaces with a confidence of less than 9
is removed from the fields text value. The default value can be changed by configuring the Setup DCO variable "ReqConf".
This variable must be configured in the setup DCO of the object, not the runtime DCO.
DeleteLowConfidenceSpaces()
method.ret:
Always
True.
