method.name: FormatNumberToLocale
method.qi: Guesses at the current numeric format to change a numeric value to match the current locale formatting.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action evaluates the current field value for known number patterns and if a known pattern is detected,
updates the decimal and digit separators characters (if present) to match that of the current locale,
for use when processing fields with number types formatted incorrectly for the current locale. i.e. USA vs European.
Known patterns are industry standard digits with or without 3 digit group separators, and 1-2 digits following a decimal separator.
Distinct Analyzed groups:
1) Numerals with decimal point
Group Separators using comma, apostrophe or space characters.
Decimal Separator using decimal character.
2) Numerals with decimal comma
Group Separator using decimal, apostrophe or space characters.
Decimal Separator using comma character.
3) Numerals with Arabic/Persian characters
Group Separator using Arabic/Persian character.
Decimal Separator using Arabic/Persian character.
Note: Numerals with lakhs layout and decimal mark (pattern of n,nn,nn,nnn.dd) are not supported.
The target numeric format is determined by the default number format for the locale in affect for the current DCO node.
For example, the default United States format uses a period as a decimal separator.
The standard default numeric format for the current locale is always used as the target numeric format.
A Datacap application can operate in
a single local or multiple locales, depending upon the setup and rules of an application.
See the section "Locale Sensitive Operations" in the top level help of this action library.
a) Given a US number 1,234.56 to be formatted to Germany.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 1.234,56
b) Given a US number 1234.5 to be formatted to Germany.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 1234,5
c) Given a US number 1,234.567 to be formatted to Germany.
FormatNumberToLocale()
Format will remain 1,234.567 since 3 digits following the decimal are not supported.
d) Given a US number 12345678.90 to be formatted to Germany.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 12345678.90
e) Given a German number 1.234.567,89 to be formatted to US.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 1,234,567.89
f) Given a German number 0,5 to be formatted to US.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 0.5
method.see: Refer to the library top level help topic "Locale Sensitive Operations" for information regarding the use of different locales in an application.

method.name: GetSubstringOccurrenceCount
method.qi: Counts the number of times a character, or substring, occurs within the text.
method.ap:
TextToSearch:
The string to search for the character or string of characters.
Substring:
The character, or character string, to search for in the TextToSearch.
StorageVariable:
A smart parameter that resolves to the target DCO object or variable that will be used
to store the occurrence count.
CaseSensitive:
False, search is case insensitive. True, search is case sensitive. Defaults to True, if the value is blank or invalid.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
The action counts the number of times the Substring is found within the TextToSearch.
The Substring can be a single character or a string of characters.
Typically, the TextToSearch will be a smart parameter that references a variable or field.
The Substring count is stored in the specified StorageVariable location. Subsequent actions can access the variable
and use it as required.
The StorageVariable smart parameter can reference a variable or the text value of an existing field.
StorageVariable specifies a DCO variable that does not exist, it will be created. If the target
specified by StorageVariable already contains a value when this action is called, it will be overwritten by the new value.
GetSubstringOccurrenceCount("This is the test string", "t", "@X.Count", "")
The example will count the number of lower case "t" characters in the string and store the value in
a variable called "Count" on the current object.
GetSubstringOccurrenceCount("AAAaA aaAAAA", "aa", "@P\Field1", "False")
This example will perform a case insensitive compare looking for the word "aa" in "AAAAa aaAAAA"
and the count will be stored in a field attached to the current page called "Field1".
The total count will be 5, because overlaps are not counted. The matches are
"AA", "Aa", "aa", "AA" and "AA".
GetSubstringOccurrenceCount("@P\Field1", "Total", "@P\Field1.MyCount", "False")
rrCompareNumeric("@P\Field1.MyCount",">", "10")
Here the action will search the text value in the child field object called "Field1".
It will perform a case insensitive count for the word "Total" in the field. The count
total will be stored in a variable called "MyCount" on "Field1". Then rrCompareNumeric
will check the value of the count. If the occurrences are more than 10, then the action will return
True and the next action in the function will run. If there value is 10 or less, then
rrCompareNumeric will return False and skip to the next function in the rule.
method.see:
rrCompareNumeric in the RuleRunnerLogic action library.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters and the
RuleRunnerLogic action library top level help for the complete smart parameter reference.

method.name: GetTextLength
method.qi: Places the numeric length of a text string into a variable.
method.ap:
TestString:
The string to calculate the length. Smart parameters are supported.
StorageVariable:
A smart parameter that resolves to the target DCO object or variable that will be used
to store the length of the TestString.
method.h:
Determines the length of a the provided string, or of the value of the DCO variable specified by a smart parameter.
The length value is stored in the specified StorageVariable location. Subsequent actions can access the variable
and use it as required.
If the target DCO variable specified in StorageVariable does not exist, it will be created. If the target
specified by StorageVariable already contains a value when this action is called, it will be overwritten by the new value.
GetStringLength("Hello","@X.MyLength")
The example will calculate the length of the word "Hello" and store "5" in a DCO
variable on the current object called "MyLength". If this example is called on a Page DCO object,
then the Page object will have the variable called "MyLength". Likewise, if this example is called
on a Field object, then the variable "MyLength" will be created on the Field object.
GetStringLength("@X.FirstName","@X.FirstNameLength")
It is not usually useful to hard code the test string for this action, as shown in the example "Hello" above.
A typical use of this action will be to provide a "smart parameter" for the TestString parameter, allowing the input
to be a runtime variable or field. This example assumes that the application has created a variable called "FirstName"
on the current DCO node prior to calling this action. The length is then stored in a variable called "FirstNameLength"
on the same node.
GetStringLength("@P\FirstName","@X.FirstNameLength")
This example assumes that the action is called at the page level and there is a field called "FirstName"
on the current DCO page. The length of the text in the field's text value is then stored in a variable called "FirstNameLength"
on the current page node.
GetStringLength("@P\FirstName","@P\FirstName.FirstNameLength")
This example assumes that the action is called at the page level and there is a field called "FirstName"
on the current DCO page. The length of the text in the field's text value is then stored in a variable called "FirstNameLength"
on the "FirstName" field node.
GetStringLength("@X","@X.MyLength")
rrCompareNumeric("@X.MyLength",">", "10")
This example assumes that the action is called on a field node and obtains the length of the text within the field and
stores it in a field variable called "MyLength".
If the length is greater than 10 characters, the next action in the current function will be called. If this is an expected
condition, the following actions may do some work. If it is an unexpected condition, the following actions may set an error.
If the length is less than 10, rrCompareNumeric will return false and the next function in the ruleset will run.
method.see:
rrCompareNumeric in the RuleRunnerLogic action library.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters and the
RuleRunnerLogic action library top level help for the complete smart parameter reference.

method.name: GetWorkstationLocale
method.ap:
StorageVariable:
A smart parameter that resolves to the target DCO object or variable that will be used
to store the length of the TestString.
method.h:
This action determines the current locale that is in effect and writes it to a field or variable specified
in the parameter.
If the locale has been set via the locale setting in the application service, or by the application
setting the hr_locale variable, then that locale is in effect. If the locale has not been set by either
of these features, then the locale set in the machine's OS is in effect.
This action can be useful, should the application need to keep a track of the locale that is enabled.
For example, it the locale could be obtained and then could be acted upon by the application, should
the application need to perform different operations based on the current locale.
If the application has specifically set the hr_locale variable, that variable can be checked directly.
If they hr_locale variable may not be set, then this action will check both hr_locale and the
current machine locale and return the one that is in effect.
It is important to remember that if hr_locale is not set, actions will use the locale of the machine
that is running the rules. For example, if the rules are being run by rulerunner, then it will use
the locale of the machine used by rulerunner. If a web interface is used, then it will be the configuration
of the machine running the web service. If DCDesktop is used, then it will be the machine running DCDesktop.
If hr_locale is not set, then configure all of the machines to have the same base locale setting or
rules may run with different locales, depending on the machine running the rules.
GetWorkstationLocale("@X.CurrentLocale");
rrCompareNotCase("@X.CurrentLocale", "en-US", "False")
SwitchMMDD("/")
This example gets the current locale and stores it in a DCO variable called "CurrentLocale".
If the current locale is not US English, it swaps the month and day.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information about Locale Sensitive Operations.

method.name: InsertCharacters
method.qi: Inserts one or more characters into a field text value at a specific position.
method.ap:
InsertString:
The character or character string to be inserted; defaults to a space.
StartIndex:
A number indicating the target position within the captured value;
defaults to the end of the value.
Count:
The number of insertions.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Inserts a character or string of characters into the field's recognized value. The string can be
inserted one or more times. The confidence of the existing characters will not be changed.
InsertCharacters("=$","1","1")
345.67 becomes =$345.67
InsertCharacters("=$","1","2")
345.67 becomes =$=$345.67
InsertCharacters("@STRING(+$),1,1")
Because smart parameters are supported, if the characters to insert
contain a smart parameter symbol, such as '+' or '@' and it should not be interpreted as a smart parameter,
then it needs to be specified with a smart parameter to prevent interpretation as shown.
345.67 becomes +$345.67
rrSet("A","@X.MyVariable")
InsertCharacters("@X.MyVariable","3","4")
The value of "MyVariable" is inserted 4 times at position 3.
abcde becomes abAAAAcde
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: InsertDecimalPoint
method.qi: Inserts the current locale's decimal separator at a specified position in a field text value.
method.ap:
Position:
A number indicating the character position at which to place the decimal with respect
to the end of the string. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Places a decimal character in the captured value, at the character position specified as a parameter.
The parameter indicates the position of the decimal point, moving from right to left.
The decimal point inserted is the character designated for the current locale.
InsertDecimalPoint("2")
324556 becomes 3245.56
InsertDecimalPoint("2")
355 becomes 3.55
rrSet("de-DE", "@X.hr_locale")
InsertDecimalPoint("2")
This action first explicitly configures the locale for the current DCO node for Germany, then InsertDecimalPoint
inserts the correct decimal separator based on the locale, which is a comma for this locale.
355 becomes 3,55
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level action help topic for more information regarding the use of locale in this action library.

method.name: IsDocumentUsingCommaDecimalSeparators
method.qi: Returns true if the current document has numbers using commas as decimal separators.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Determines if the numeric fields in the document mostly use a comma as a decimal separator or a period as a decimal separator.
It is required that FormatNumberToLocale has been previously called on all of the numeric fields.
IsDocumentUsingCommaDecimalSeparators()
rrSet("en-GB", "@F.hr_locale")
IsFieldDate()
In this example, because most numbers are using a comma as decimal separator, it assumes that the
date format should match the UK format.
method.ret:
Returns
True
if most numerics use a comma as a decimal separator, otherwise
False
is returned.

method.name: IsFieldCurrency
method.qi: Returns true if the current field's text value is a valid currency for the current locale.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Determines if the Field's captured value meets the current locale's currency format,
including the number of decimal places, decimal and digit separator characters and
any present currency indicators. The locale formats are the standard currency symbol,
digit grouping symbol and decimal symbols as defined in windows for a specific locale.
A currency symbol is not required for the validation to pass. If a currency symbol is present,
then the currency symbol provided must be correct for the current locale or the
validation will fail. Similarly, digit
grouping symbols are not required, but if they are present, they must also be the correct symbol
for the current locale.
If the currency has a decimal value, then the decimal symbol must be the correct symbol. For example,
if validating U.S. currency, and the currency has a decimal value such as 123.56, then the decimal
separator must be the correct separator for the country. Some countries do not allow decimal
values in their currency, and if a decimal value is present, it will fail validation.
If the field appears to have a valid currency but it is not passing the validation, confirm
that the locale used by the field is correct for the currency type. For example, if
the field has a Japanese currency, then the locale must be set to Japan. This can either be
in effect for the whole application, such as the machine's locale, or it can be in effect
based on the setting of the hr_locale DCO variable.
When validating Japanese currency, in addition to using the defined locale's currency
format, it is also allowed to specify negative values using the △ symbol instead of a
minus symbol. Additionally, in place of a Yen symbol ¥ at the start of a currency,
the word 円 is allowed at the end of the currency value.
If the field matches the currency format, the action returns true. If the requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action. Typically this would be
called on a field object which needs to pass this validation test.
Example 1:
IsFieldCurrency()
$1,200 returns
False
$1,200.00 returns
True
Example 2:
rrSet("ja-JP","@X.hr_locale")
IsFieldCurrency()
This example first sets the locale for the field to Japan prior to
validating the currency. If hr_locale was already set at a higher DCO node level,
such as page, document or batch, then it is not necessary to set it again
at the field level.
method.see: Refer to the top level action help topic for more information regarding the use of locale in this action library.

method.name: IsFieldDate
method.qi: Determines if the current field's text value matches the current locale's default date format.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Checks that the value of the field has an acceptable Date format. Uses the current locale setting to determine
the valid date pattern.
This action will accept any valid date from January 1st year 1 through December 31st 9999.
If the date requirements are met, the action returns true. If the date requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsFieldDate()
In locale en-US (United States):
April 6, 1944 returns
True
04/06/44 returns
True
30.6.44 returns
False
Feb 31,2003 returns
False
method.see: Refer to the top level action help topic for more information regarding the use of locale in this action library.

method.name: IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter
method.qi: Returns true if the current field is equal to or after the specified date.
method.ap:
The parameter is the date that will be compared to the date of the current field.
The source date can be a hard coded date or it can be obtained from another field value
or a DCO variable referenced with a smart parameter.
method.h:
Checks that the Date value in the current DCO field recognized text value
is greater than or equal to the Date value in the
DCO field or value specified as the parameter.
The two dates must both conform to the date format for the current locale.
See the top level help in this action library for more information about the locale.
If the date requirements are met, the action returns true. If the date requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter("2/14/1964")
This action compares the date in the current field's text value with the hard coded date "2/14/1964".
If the date in the field is the same or after 2/14/1964, the action will return true.
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter("@DATE")
This example compares the current field's value with the current date.
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter("@P\MyCompareField")
Assuming the parent page object contains a sibling field called "MyCompareField",
this example compares the current field's value with the text value in the field
called "MyCompareField".
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter("@X.MyVariable")
This example compares the current field's value with the value of the DCO variable
"MyVariable" in the current field object.
method.ret:
False
if the date condition is not met, if the action is not applied at the Field level, or either field
does not contain a valid date. Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
IsFieldDateEqualOrBefore, IsFieldDateWithinRange
Refer to the top level action help topic for more information regarding the use of locale in this action library.

method.name: IsFieldDateEqualOrBefore
method.qi: Returns true if the current field is equal to or before the specified date.
method.ap:
The parameter is the date that will be compared to the date of the current field.
The source date can be a hard coded date or it can be obtained from another field value
or a DCO variable referenced with a smart parameter.
method.h:
Checks that the Date value in the current DCO field recognized text value
is less than or equal to the Date value in the
DCO field or value specified as the parameter.
The two dates must both conform to the date format for the current locale.
If the date requirements are met, the action returns true. If the date requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsFieldDateEqualOrBefore("2/14/1964")
This action compares the date in the current field's text value with the hard coded date "2/14/1964".
If the date in the field is the same or before 2/14/1964, the action will return true.
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter("@DATE")
This example compares the current field's value with the current date.
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter("@P\MyCompareField")
Assuming the parent page object contains a sibling field called "MyCompareField",
this example compares the current field's value with the text value in the field
called "MyCompareField".
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter("@X.MyVariable")
This example compares the current field's value with the value of the DCO variable
"MyVariable" in the current field object.
method.ret:
False
if the date condition is not met, if the action is not applied at the Field level, or either field
does not contain a valid date. Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter, IsFieldDateWithinRange
Refer to the top level action help topic for more information regarding the use of locale in this action library.

method.name: IsFieldDateWithinRange
method.qi: Returns true if the current field text value is between the specified dates.
method.ap:
StartDate:
The current field must be a validate that is the same or after this date.
EndDate:
The current field must be a validate that is the same or before this date.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Checks that the value assigned to the Text property of the current field is within the range specified by the parameters.
All of the provided dates must be in the correct format, for the current locale.
IsFieldDateWithinRange("1/1/2020", "1/31/2020")
This example tests that the current field's text value is between the 1/1/2020 and 1/31/2020.
IsFieldDateWithinRange("February 9, 1964", "January 30, 1969")
This example tests that the current field's text value is between the 2/9/1964 and 1/30/1969.
IsFieldDateWithinRange("9/12/1966", "@DATE")
This example uses the smart parameter @DATE to set the end date to the current date. If the current
field's text value is between 9/12/1966 and the current date, then the action will return true.
IsFieldDateWithinRange("@P\MyField1", "@P\MyField2")
This example assumes that the current field has two sibling fields on the same page
called "MyField1" and "MyField2". If the current field value is greater than or equal to the
date value in MyField1 and less than or equal to the field value in MyField2, the action will return true.
IsFieldDateWithinRange("@X.MyVariable1", "@P\MyField1")
This example assumes that the current field has a sibling field on the same page
called "MyField1". If the current field value is greater than or equal to the
date value in DCO variable "MyVariable" on the current field and less than or equal to the
field value in MyField1, the action will return true.
method.ret:
False
if the current field text is not a valid date;
if either parameters are not validate dates; or the Text property's Date value is not within the range
specified by the parameters. Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter, IsFieldDateEqualOrBefore
Refer to the top level action help topic for more information regarding the use of locale in this action library.

method.name: IsFieldDateWithinXDays
method.qi: Returns true if the current field text value is near the specified date within the day count limit.
method.ap:
A number that specifies how many days make up the review period from the current date.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Checks that current Field object's text value is a date that is within the number of days
of the current date as indicated
by the input parameter. The field's text value must be a date that matches the date
format for the current locale.
If the date requirements are met, the action returns true. If the date requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsFieldDateWithinXDays("30")
This sequence checks that a value is a date within 30 days of today's date.
The field date can be up to 30 days earlier or 30 days later.
IsFieldDateWithinXDays("@P.Days")
This example obtains the number of days from a DCO variable called "Days" on the
parent page object and then compares it to the date in the current field's text
value to confirm that it is with the number of days of today's date. If the variable
"Days" contained the value "45", then the action will return true if the field's value
is a date that is within 45 days of today's date.
rrSet("@P\MyField.MyVariable", "@X")
IsFieldDateWithinXDays("30")
To use this action on a variable instead of a field, rrSet can be used to first
populate a field with a date from a DCO variable and then the action can be run
on the field with the date to test. This example shows that the field
is filled with the value of the variable "MyVariable" from the sibling
field on the same page called "MyField". The current field text is
populated with the value of the variable then IsFieldDateWithinXDays
runs to perform the test. This approach can be used with virtually
any similar action that only operates on field text values.
These actions must be run on a rule attached to a DCO field object.
method.ret:
False
if the field's value is not a valid date or if the date is
out side of the number of days in the parameter; otherwise,
True.
method.see:
IsFieldDate, IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter, IsFieldDateEqualOrBefore
Refer to the top level action help topic for more information regarding the use of locale in this action library.

method.name: IsFieldDateWithReformat
method.qi: Returns true if the field is a valid date that matches the current locale date format and reformats it to a new date pattern.
method.ap:
The new date format that will be applied to the date in the current field.
mm/dd/yyyy
mm/dd/yy
dd/mm/yy
mm.dd.yy, etc.
Defaults to system short date format if no format or single '*' is used.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Reformats the date in the current field to the month, day and year format specified by the
parameter. The parameter can use the values "d", "m" and "y" to indicate the respective
portions of the date and "." or "/" can be used to separate the values.
Dates are reformatted into a short date format only.
The field's source date must be in a format that is correct for the current locale. Once the operation
is complete, the date may no longer conform to the format specified for the current locale.
d or m evaluates to the number without a leading zero, such as 1 to 31.
dd or mm evaluates to the number with a leading zero, such as 01 to 31.
ddd or mmm evaluates to the abbreviated name, such as Mon or Dec.
dddd or mmmm evaluates to the full name such as Monday or December.
yy evaluates to a two digit year with a leading zero.
yyyy evaluates to a four digit year.
If the length requirements are met, the action returns true. If the length requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsFieldDateWithReformat("*")
June 3, 2002 becomes 06/03/2002
IsFieldDateWithReformat("yyyy/mm/dd")
May 26, 1967 becomes 1967/05/26
IsFieldDateWithReformat("yyyy/mm/dd")
06/25/67 becomes 1967/05/26
IsFieldDateWithReformat("mm.dd.yy")
June 3, 2002 becomes 06.03.02
method.ret:
False
if the parameter is invalid, or the current field value is not a valid date given the specified format. Otherwise
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsFieldPercentAlphabetic
method.qi: Returns true if a field's text value has the specified percentage of alphabetic characters
method.ap:
Percentage:
An integer from 0 to 100 indicating the percentage of characters in the field's text value that must be
alphabetic. The value is the minimum percentage required for the action to return true.
The parameter must be numeric, without the percent sign. If the percentage is invalid, it will default to 100.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Determines if the characters in the current field's text value are n% alphabetic.
If the percentage requirements are met, the action returns true. If the percentage requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsFieldPercentAlpha("50")
#RPR-1421 returns
False
IsFieldPercentAlpha("30")
#RPR1421 returns
True
method.ret:
True
if the parameter's minimum requirement is met. Otherwise
False.
method.see:
IsFieldPercentNumeric, IsValueExactMatch
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsFieldPercentNonNumeric
method.qi: Returns true if a field's text value has the specified percentage of non-numeric characters
method.ap:
Percentage:
An integer from 0 to 100 indicating the percentage of characters in the field's text value that must be
non-numeric characters. The value is the minimum percentage required for the action to return true.
The parameter must be numeric, without the percent sign. If the percentage is invalid, it will default to 100.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Determines if the characters in the current field's text value are n% not numeric
characters, this includes and is not limited to valid decimal and numeric separator characters. The
action will compare the actual percentage and confirm that it is less than or equal to the percentage
provided by the parameter.
Given the current value is "1,234.56US"
(Percentage of non-numeric characters is 40%)
IsFieldPercentNonNumeric("0")
returns
True
IsFieldPercentNonNumeric("30")
returns
True
IsFieldPercentNonNumeric("40")
returns
True
IsFieldPercentNonNumeric("70")
returns
False
IsFieldPercentNonNumeric("100")
returns
False
method.ret:
True
if the parameter's minimum requirement is met. Otherwise
False.
method.see:
IsFieldPercentAlphalphabetic, IsValueExactMatch
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsFieldPercentNumeric
method.qi: Returns true if a field's text value has the specified percentage of numeric characters
method.ap:
Percentage:
An integer from 0 to 100 indicating the percentage of characters in the field's text value that must be
numeric. The value is the minimum percentage required for the action to return true.
The parameter must be numeric, without the percent sign. If the percentage is invalid, it will default to 100.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Determines if the characters in the current field's text value are n% numeric
characters. Does not include, and is not limited to, valid decimal and numeric separator characters.
Given the current field text value is "1,234.56US"
(Percentage of numeric characters is 60%)
IsFieldPercentNumeric("0")
returns
True
IsFieldPercentNumeric("50")
returns
True
IsFieldPercentNumeric("60")
returns
True
IsFieldPercentNumeric("70")
returns
False
IsFieldPercentNumeric("100")
returns
False
method.ret:
True
if the parameter's minimum requirement is met. Otherwise
False.
method.see:
IsFieldPercentAlpha, IsValueExactMatch
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsInCharacterSet
method.qi: Tests that the text only contains characters within the specified list.
method.ap:
CharacterSet:
A list of characters.
TextToText
The text to test to confirm it only contains characters from the character set.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Validates that text in a field or in a DCO variable contains only characters from within the provided character set.
Characters are case sensitive.
IsInCharacterSet("@X", "0123456789.,-$")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, it will return true if the text within the field is only contains
characters from within the provided set. If the field contains text that is not within the provided character set,
then the action will return false.

method.name: IsLocalDecimalSeparator
method.qi: Tests the current decimal separator.
method.ap: A single character to test as the decimal separator. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Tests the input decimal separator to see if it matches the default separator of the locale
of the current DCO object. Be aware that the locale for the current DCO object
can be different from the locale of other objects in the hierarchy and different from
the locale of the machine running the rules if hr_locale has been set.
IsLocalDecimalSeparator(",")
IsInCharacterSet("0123456789.,-$", "@X")
ConvertToLocalDecimal()

method.name: IsOMRCheckedMaximum
method.qi: Returns true if the current OMR field has detected selections up to the specified maximum.
method.ap:
OMRLimit:
Integer value specifying the maximum number of OMR selections that are allowed.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action confirms that the number of OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) selections
is less than or equal to the number passed as a parameter. An OMR is typically a circle or box shape
that is either filled in or not filled in. The number of selections that are filled in cannot
exceed the value provided as a parameter. If the number of filled in selections is less than
or equal to the parameter, then this action will return true. If the selected count it
greater than the parameter, this action will return false.
This action must be set on a field that is configured as an OMR field. An OMR field must have
the DCO variable "RecogType" set to "4". An OMR field must also be setup properly to be correctly
recognized and processed as an OMR field.
The OMR field has a sub-field for each OMR selection. When the OMR is recognized,
the parent OMR field will have a text value of 0's and 1's, each corresponding to the sub-fields.
A "0" indicates the OMR was not considered as filled in and a "1" considers the OMR was filled in.
This action will check the text value of the OMR field to determine if the number of 1's meets
the parameter's requirements.
If the maximum requirement is exceeded, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsOMRCheckedMaximum("1")
This action confirms that only 1 of the available OMR selections has been filled in. One
example would be a selection of the type of credit card, only one credit card should be
selected. If multiple credit cards are selected, then this can be used to flag the OMR field as an
error so a verify operator can review the selection.
IsOMRCheckedMaximum("1")
IsOMRCheckedMinimum("1")
This set of actions combines two requirements to ensure that 1 and only 1 OMR has been selected. If these
both pass, then the selection count is valid. If one of the tests fails, then it can be flagged
for a verify operator to review the problem in a verify panel.
IsOMRCheckedMaximum("@X.MaxAllowed")
This example uses a smart parameter to obtain the required maximum from a DCO variable called "MaxAllowed"
on the same DCO object that is running the action.
method.ret:
False
if the parameter you enter is not numeric, or the field is not an OMR field.
True
if the number of OMR boxes checked is less than or equal to the parameter you entered.
method.see:
IsOMRCheckedMinimum
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsOMRCheckedMinimum
method.qi: Returns true if the current OMR field has detected selections of the specified minimum value.
method.ap:
OMRLimit:
Integer value specifying the minimum number of OMR selections that are allowed.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action confirms that the number of OMR (Optical Mark Recognition) selections
is greater than or equal to the number passed as a parameter. An OMR is typically a circle or box shape
that is either filled in or not filled in. The number of selections that are filled in cannot
exceed the value provided as a parameter. If the number of filled in selections is greater than
or equal to the parameter, then this action will return true. If the selected count it
less than the parameter, this action will return false.
This action must be set on a field that is configured as an OMR field. An OMR field must have
the DCO variable "RecogType" set to "4". An OMR field must also be setup properly to be correctly
recognized and processed as an OMR field.
The OMR field has a sub-field for each OMR selection. When the OMR is recognized,
the parent OMR field will have a text value of 0's and 1's, each corresponding to the sub-fields.
A "0" indicates the OMR was not considered as filled in and a "1" considers the OMR was filled in.
This action will check the text value of the OMR field to determine if the number of 1's meets
the parameter's requirements.
If the minimum requirement is not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsOMRCheckedMinimum("1")
This action confirms that only 1 of the available OMR selections has been filled in. One
example would a form that has multiple selections and one or more selections can be chosen, but at least
one of them must be selected. This action will confirm that there is at least one OMR selected
out of the available selections.
IsOMRCheckedMinimum("1")
IsOMRCheckedMaximum("1")
This set of actions combinds two requirements to ensure that 1 and only 1 OMR has been selected. If these
both pass, then the selection count is valid. If one of the tests fails, then it can be flagged
for a verify operator to review the problem in a verify panel.
IsOMRCheckedMinimum("@X.MinAllowed")
This example uses a smart parameter to obtain the required maximum from a DCO variable called "MinAllowed"
on the same DCO object that is running the action.
method.ret:
False
if the parameter you enter is not numeric, or the field is not an OMR field.
True
if the number of OMR boxes checked is less than or equal to the parameter you entered.
method.see:
IsOMRCheckedMaximum
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsRegularExpressionPatternInValue
method.qi: Returns true if a field or variable has a pattern that matches the regular expression.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field, DCO variable or string to validate.
RegularExpression:
The expression can include any Regular Expression characters.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action validates the value Target parameter to see if it meets the requirements
of the provided regular expression.
If you are using an input boundary, ^, it must be followed by a space and then the remainder
of the search string.
If the regular expression is matched, the action returns true. If the regular expression is not matched, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object. Typically this would be
called on a field object which needs to pass this validation test.
IsRegularExpressionPatternInValue("@F", "[\^\b\s\n\r]*Inv[oO0][iItl1]ce[\b\s]*")
Assuming this action is attached to a field object,
this example searches for the word “Invoice” in the text value of the current field.
To allow for recognition errors, the search allows for common recognition
substitutions in “o” and “i” by matching “Invoice”, “InvOice”, “Inv0ice”,
“Inv01ce”, “Involce”, etc. The search will also ignore any text placed before or after the word.
IsRegularExpressionPatternInValue("@F", "@STRING([\^\b\s\n\r]*Inv[oO0][iItl1]ce[\b\s]*)")
Because the action supports smart parameters, if the regular expression contains
smart parameter identifiers like @ or +, then those parameters will need to be passed in
a way to prevent interpretation as smart parameter identifiers.
Typically the easiest way to achieve this is by encapsulating the parameter
with the smart parameter @STRING() or @CHR().
IsRegularExpressionPatternInValue("@F", "@X.MyExpression")
This example is similar to the previous examples but obtains the regular expression
pattern from a DCO variable called "MyExpression" on the current object.
method.lvl: All, but generally at the Field level.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsUSZipCode
method.qi: Checks to see if the postal code follows a US format.

p.name: PostalCode
p.qi: Smart parameters are supported.

method.ap: The zip code to test for a US zip code pattern.
method.h:
Checks to see if the postal code follows a US format. If the format of the ZIP
fits a US format, then it assumes the document is of US origin.
Allowed formats:
nnnnn
nnnnnnnnn
nnnnn-nnnn
IsUSZipCode(@P\Remittance_Zip)
rrSet("en-US", "@F.hr_locale")
IsFieldDate()
IsFieldDateWithReformat("yyyy/mm/dd")
method.ret:
Returns
True
if the test for a US ZIP code format passes, otherwise
False.

method.name: IsValuePercentFuzzy
method.qi: Returns true if the current field text value matches a pattern using common substitution characters.
method.ap:
Source:
The source field, DCO variable or string that will be tested. This is the field with a value to be compared
to see if it meets the required minimum percentage.
CompareTo:
The source field, DCO variable or string that will be used to compare against the source value.
PerformFuzzyCompare
A boolean flag determines if the comparison to the source string will be a
"fuzzy" comparison. A "fuzzy" comparison will compare text using common substitution characters
that can occur from recognition mistakes. The value "True" will enable fuzzy comparison.
MinimumPercentage
Numeric value of the percentage of required precision when matching
by word. Numbers less than
"100" permit the comparison to pass by requiring a smaller percentage of words to match. This value
must be an integer between 0 and 100. If the value is invalid, it will default to 100.
When MatchByWord is false, then the entire target string is considered a single word
and must match the compare string 100%, but still respecting the fuzzy compare setting.
MatchByWord
A boolean value of True or False which indicates if the comparison should be
a word-by-word comparison vs. a character comparison. True will enable a word by word
comparison, False compares a character comparison.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Compares an entire line of text or each word within the line, to a provided pattern. The pattern can be matched
"fuzzy" meaning that the patter can match if specific characters are interchanged with commonly substituted
recognition characters.
When ByWord is false, the entire line of text from the source field text or DCO variable will be compared to the
comparison pattern. The entire string of characters must match the comparison string. If PerformFuzzyCompare
is true, then the pattern does not need to match exactly if common substitution characters are within the source string.
The percentage parameter is not relevant when ByWord is False.
When MatchByWord is true, then the provided comparison text will be checked against each word within the source string.
A word is considered as a string of characters separated by a space. Each of these words will be compared to the
comparison parameter and must match exactly. If the PerformFuzzyCompare parameter is True, then the comparison will
allow commonly substituted characters to match, so the text does not need to be an exact match. The percentage value determines
the percentage of the words that must match the comparison string. If the source string has 10 words and 2 of the words
match the comparison pattern, then it is considered to be a 20% match.
When performing a "fuzzy" compare, the action will use common recognition substitutions to determine if the text matches the required
text. For example, when fuzzy comparisons are enabled a word like "Sam" will match "5am", or "He110" will match "Hello".
The following are common substitutions that will match when fuzzy comparisons are enabled: B8, Z2, S5, o0O and ilt1I.
Enabling the fuzzy comparison will allow these commonly substituted characters to match the provided pattern and still
be evaluated as an exact match.
If the comparison requirements are met, the action returns true. If the comparison requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action.
IsValuePercentFuzzy("@F", "Hello", "True", "100", "False")
Assuming this is attached to a DCO field, it will compare the text value
of the field with the pattern "Hello". Fuzzy matching is enabled. The following field
values will have these return values:
"Hello" = True
"He11o" = True
"He110" = True
"Hel1O" = True
"HELLO" = False
IsValuePercentFuzzy("@F", "@P\OtherField", "True", "100", "False")
Similar to the above example, however the comparison pattern will be obtained from the
text value of the sibling field "OtherField". A fuzzy comparison will be performed
using OtherField as the pattern.
IsValuePercentFuzzy("@F", "@DATE(DD\MM\YYYY)", "True", "100", "False")
This example will compare the current field to the current date and use fuzzy matching.
Assuming the current date is 01/01/2025, the following field values will have these return values:
"0l/01/20Z5" = True
"01/01/2025" = True
"01/07/2025" = False
"0l/0l/20ZS" = True
IsValuePercentFuzzy("@F", "@P.MyVariable", "True", "25", "True")
This example will compare the text value of the current field with the comparison value
that is in the parent page object variable called "MyVariable". Assuming the text
value of the current field has the text "He110 Tom and Sally" and the value of "MyVariable" is
"Hello", then the 1 of 4 words will match the pattern with the result of 25% of the
words matching and the action will return true.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsTextLength
method.qi: Returns true if the text in a field or variable satisfies a length condition.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to validate.
Length:
A numeric value to use for the length comparison. If not provided, defaults to 1.
ComparisonOperator:
The comparison operator. It must be one of the following operators: ˂, ˂=, =, ˃=, ˃
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action checks the text length to confirm if it meets a minimum or maximum length requirement.
It will determine if the text length of the "Target", typically a field value, is less than, less than or equal to,
equal to, greater than or equal to, or greater than the length specified in the length parameter.
This action is useful for validation of recognized data to confirm it meets requirements. It also
will confirm if data entered by a verify operator has entered data that meets the length requirements.
If the length requirements are met, the action returns true. If the length requirements are not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object.
The action will also store the actual length of the tested text in a DCO variable called "TextLength".
If needed, this variable can be optionally used to obtain the length of the text that was tested and used
in other actions. The variable is created regardless of the comparison test passing or failing.
It is not required to use this variable, it is provided should an application need to determine
the actual length of the text for use in a subsequent task.
Because the target specification supports smart parameters, the target can be a field's text value, a DCO variable
or hard coded text.
IsTextLength("@F", "10", "˂=")
Assuming this action is called on a rule attached to a field object, it will test the field's
text value to confirm the length of the text is less than or equal to 10 characters. The action will
return true if the test passes, otherwise the action will return false and control will pass to the next function
in the ruleset. The actual length of the string will also be stored in the current DCO variable "TextLength"
for optional use.
IsTextLength("@F", "0", "=")
Assuming this action is called on a rule attached to a field object, it will test the field's
text value to confirm the field is empty. The action will return false if the field is
not empty and set a user message.
IsTextLength("@F", "0", ">")
Assuming this action is called on a rule attached to a field object, it will test the field's
text value to confirm the field is not empty. The action will return false and set
a message if it is empty.
IsTextLength("@X.MyVariable", @X.LengthToTest, "=")
This example uses a smart parameter to test the text contained in the DCO variable "MyVariable"
on the same DCO object that is attached to the ruleset. It also uses a smart parameter
to obtain the expected length from another variable called "LengthToTest". If the
text contained in MyVariable is equal to the number of characters indicated
by the numeric value of the variable LengthToTest, then the action will return true.
method.lvl: Any level but typically at the field level.
method.ret:
True
if the comparison meets the length requirement; Otherwise
False.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsValueLessOrEqual
method.qi: Returns true if a numeric comparison on a field or variable is less than or equal to the comparison value.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field, DCO variable or string to validate.
ComparisonValue:
A numeric value to use for the comparison to the value of the "Target" parameter.
The target and the comparison value numbers must be properly formatted for the current locale.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action performs a numeric compare of the value of the "Target" parameter to the "ComparisonValue".
It will determine if the "Target", typically a field value, is less than, less than or equal to,
equal to, greater than or equal to, or greater than the comparison value.
This action is very similar to IsValueLessOrGreater. The action IsValueLessOrGreater has
greater flexibility.
This action is useful for validation of recognized data to confirm it meets requirements. It also
will confirm if data entered by a verify operator has entered data that meets the numeric requirements.
If the comparison requirement is met, the action returns true. If the comparison requirement is not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object.
IsValueLessOrEqual("@F", "10.50")
Assuming this action is called on a rule attached to a field object, it will test the field's
text value to confirm the numeric value of the text is less than or equal to 10.5. The action will
return true if the test passes, otherwise the action will return false and control will pass to the next function
in the ruleset.
method.lvl: Any level but typically at the field level.
method.ret:
True
if the two values meet the comparison requirement; Otherwise
False.
method.see:
IsValueLessOrGreater
rrCompareNumeric in the RuleRunnerLogic action library
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsValueLessOrGreater
method.qi: Returns true if a numeric comparison on a field or variable meets the condition for the comparison value.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field, DCO variable or string to validate.
ComparisonValue:
A numeric value to use for the comparison to the value of the "Target" parameter.
The target and the comparison value numbers must be properly formatted for the current locale.
ComparisonOperator:
The comparison operator. It must be one of the following operators: ˂, ˂=, =, ˃=, ˃
The comparison is applied in this format "Target" "Comparison" "Value" such as "is Target ˂= 5".
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action performs a numeric compare of the value of the "Target" parameter to the "ComparisonValue".
It will determine if the "Target", typically a field value, is less than, less than or equal to,
equal to, greater than or equal to, or greater than the comparison value.
This action is useful for validation of recognized data to confirm it meets requirements. It also
will confirm if data entered by a verify operator has entered data that meets the numeric requirements.
If the comparison requirement is met, the action returns true. If the comparison requirement is not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object.
If the goal is to perform a numeric comparison to control logic flow but the message variable
does not need to be set if the comparison fails, then consider using the rrCompareNumeric action
in the RuleRunnerLocic action library.
IsValueLessOrGreater("@F", "10.50", "˂=")
Assuming this action is called on a rule attached to a field object, it will test the field's
text value to confirm the numeric value of the text is less than or equal to 10.5. The action will
return true if the test passes, otherwise the action will return false and control will pass to the next function
in the ruleset.
IsValueLessOrGreater("@F", "0", "=")
Assuming this action is called on a rule attached to a field object, it will test the field's
text value to confirm the numeric value is zero.
IsValueLessOrGreater("@F", "0", ">")
Assuming this action is called on a rule attached to a field object, it will test the field's
text value to confirm the value is greater than zero.
IsValueLessOrGreater("@X.MyVariable", @X.ExpectedValue, "=")
This example uses a smart parameter to test the text contained in the DCO variable "MyVariable"
on the same DCO object that is attached to the ruleset. It also uses a smart parameter
to obtain the test value from another variable called "ExpectedValue". If the
numeric value of text contained in ExpectedValue is equal to the numeric value
the variable MyVariable, then the action will return true.
method.lvl: Any level but typically at the field level.
method.ret:
True
if the two values meet the comparison requirement; Otherwise
False.
method.see:
rrCompareNumeric in the RuleRunnerLogic action library
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: IsValueExactMatch
method.qi: Returns true if the field or value matches the comparison value with our without case sensitivity.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field, DCO variable or string to validate.
Value:
Text that the action is looking for in the current field.
CaseSensitive:
Determines if the comparison should be case sensitive. Use values "True" or "False".
If the parameter is left blank, it defaults to "True".
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
The action will check the text referenced by the Target parameter to validate if the text in the
Value parameter is identical to the Target's text. The Value must exactly match
the input text. If the case sensitive parameter
is true then the sub-string must also exactly match the case of the comparison text.
If the comparison requirement is met, the action returns true. If the comparison requirement is not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object.
IsValueExactMatch("@F", "NEW", "")
Assuming this action is called on a ruleset attached to a field object, it will compare the
text value of the current field with the word "NEW" to confirm if the word "NEW"
is contained in the source field.
The following are return values based on the field's text value:
Field contains: "NEW" = TRUE
Field contains: "I Love NEW YORK" = FALSE
Field contains: "Project" = FALSE
Field contains: "NEW Project" = FALSE
Field contains: "New Project" = FALSE
Field contains: "Development" = FALSE
IsValueExactMatch("@F", "@P.MyVariable", "False")
This example will compare the text value of the current DCO field with
the value of the variable "MyVariable" which is on the parent page
object. The comparison will be case insensitive.
method.lvl: All, but generally at the Field level.
method.see:
IsFieldPercentAlpha, IsFieldPercentNumeric
rrCompare, rrCompareNot, rrCompareCase, rrCompareCaseLength, rrCompareNotCase and rrCompareNotCaseLength in the RuleRunnerLogic action library.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters and in the top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library.

method.name: IsValueInText
method.qi: Returns true if the specified text is a substring text in a field or variable
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field, DCO variable or string to validate.
Value:
Text that the action is looking for in the current field.
CaseSensitive:
Determines if the comparison should be case sensitive. Use values "True" or "False".
If the parameter is left blank, it defaults to "True".
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
The action will check the text referenced by the Target parameter to validate if the text in the
Value parameter is a subset of text contained within the Target's text. The Value can exactly match
the length the input text or can be a portion of the input text. If the case sensitive parameter
is true then the substring must exactly match the case of the comparison text.
If the comparison requirement is met, the action returns true. If the comparison requirement is not met, the
action returns false and also sets a corresponding error message in the standard Message variable that
is used by clients to display in verification panels when a rule check fails. The message is set on
the DCO that is calling this action, so it is typically useful to call this action on the DCO object
that is being checked so the message is associated with the same object.
IsValueInText("@F", "NEW", "")
Assuming this action is called on a ruleset attached to a field object, it will compare the
text value of the current field with the word "NEW" to confirm if the word "NEW"
is contained in the source field.
The following are return values based on the field's text value:
Field contains: "NEW" = TRUE
Field contains: "I Love NEW YORK" = TRUE
Field contains: "Project" = FALSE
Field contains: "NEW Project" = TRUE
Field contains: "New Project" = FALSE
Field contains: "Development" = FALSE
IsValueInText("@F", "@P.MyVariable", "False")
This example will compare the text value of the current DCO field with
the value of the variable "MyVariable" which is on the parent page
object. The comparison will be case insensitive.
method.lvl: All, but generally at the Field level.
method.see:
IsFieldPercentAlpha, IsFieldPercentNumeric
