Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters and in the top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library.

method.name: ReplaceBlankFieldWithCharacter
method.qi: If the current field is blank, the specified character will be placed into the field.
method.ap:
Replacement:
A character or string that will be placed into the field if it is blank.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
If a field is empty or only contains spaces, it is replaced with the character or string that is passed in as a parameter.
If the field is replaced with the input parameter, the confidence of the new replacement text is set to a low confidence of 1.
ReplaceBlankFieldWithCharacter("~")
This example will replace the current field with the character "~", only if the field is empty or only
contains spaces.
ReplaceBlankFieldWithCharacter("@B.MyVariable")
If the field is empty or only contains spaces, it will be replaced with the text in
the batch level variable "MyVariable".
method.ret:
False
if it is called at the wrong level or if the parameter is missing, otherwise
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: ReplaceCharacters
method.qi: Replaces specific characters in a field to a replacement character.
method.ap:
Find:
The character or string of characters to be replaced; defaults to a space.
Replacement:
The character(s) of the replacement String.
Count:
The number of times replacement is to occur. The default is "1" and "*" replaces all instances.
Smart parameters supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action will update the text of the current field object by replacing the matched character
or string of characters with the replacement string. The number of
replacement occurrences is controlled by the Count parameter.
The confidence values of the characters that are not replaced will not be changed, keeping
their original confidence values. Replacement characters will be added with the default
passing confidence value.
ReplaceCharacters(".","/","*")
If the text value of the field has a starting value of
"02.09.1964", it will become "02/09/1964".
ReplaceCharacters("", "@EMPTY", "*")
If the source field contains "Remove The Spaces Here", the final result will be "RemoveTheSpacesHere".
ReplaceCharacters("@X.FindThis", "@X.Replacement", "1")
This example will look for the text indicated by the DCO variable "FindThis" and replace
the first occurrence with the value of the variable "Replacement" on the same DCO object.
If "FindThis" is set to "oo", "Replacement" is set to "a" and the starting
field value is "Moon to Moose", the final field value will be "Man to Moose".
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: ReplaceSubstringFirst
method.qi: Replaces the First occurance of a substring in a text string with a new substring.
method.ap:
TextToSearch:
A smart parameter syntax that references a DCO field or variable to search and update.
Substring:
The character, or character string, to search for in the resolved value of TextToSearch.
Replacement:
The character, or character string, to replace the Substring.
CaseSensitive:
False, search is case insensitive. True, search is case sensitive. Defaults to True, if the value is blank or invalid.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action will search the text of the field or variable referenced in the TextToSearch parameter.
The first occurrence of the specified Substring will be replaced with Replacement parameter and
the location referenced by TextToSearch will be updated.
If the smart parameter specified in TextToSearch resolves to a field's "text" value, this action
will maintain the existing confidence values of the characters that are not replaced.
The replacement characters will be set to a high confidence value. If TextToSearch
resolves to a DCO variable, then the confidence value does not apply.
The Replacement parameter is not required to be the same length as the substring.
ReplaceSubstringFirst(@F, "TOO", "Three", "True")
Because the specification is @F, this action would be run on a field to update the captured text in the field.
If the text value of the field has a value of "This Too is TOO Much Text Too", then the final value
of the field will be "This Too is Three Much Text Too", because this is a case sensitive search.
if the confidence of the field was "55555555555555555555555555555", after updating the text value
the field confidence would become "5555555555559999955555555555555".
rrSet("This Too is TOO Much Text Too", "@X.MyVariable")
ReplaceSubstringFirst(@X.MyVariable, "TOO", "Three", "false")
The example first sets a DCO variable on the current DCO object to the value "This Too is TOO Much Text Too".
This is performed as an illustration. Typically the variable would have been set earlier.
The action ReplaceSubstringFirst will update the variable "MyVariable" to
"This Three is TOO Much Text Too".
ReplaceSubstringFirst(@P\Field1, ".", ",", "False)
It is assumed that this action is running on a page object that has an existing child field called "Field1".
The action will update the text value of Field1.
If the text value of the field has a value of "1.234.56", then the final value
of the field will be "1,234.56".
if the confidence of the field was "72387279", after updating the text value
the field confidence would become "79387279".
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: ReplaceSubstringLast
method.qi: Replaces the last occurance of a substring in a text string with a new substring.
method.ap:
TextToSearch:
A smart parameter syntax that references a DCO field or variable to search and update.
Substring:
The character, or character string, to search for in the resolved value of TextToSearch.
Replacement:
The character, or character string, to replace the Substring.
CaseSensitive:
False, search is case insensitive. True, search is case sensitive. Defaults to True, if the value is blank or invalid.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action will search the text of the field or variable referenced in the TextToSearch parameter.
The last occurrence of the specified Substring will be replaced with Replacement parameter and
the location referenced by TextToSearch will be updated.
If the smart parameter specified in TextToSearch resolves to a field's "text" value, this action
will maintain the existing confidence values of the characters that are not replaced.
The replacement characters will be set to a high confidence value. If TextToSearch
resolves to a DCO variable, then the confidence value does not apply.
The Replacement parameter is not required to be the same length as the substring.
ReplaceSubstringLast(@F, "TOO", "Three", "True")
Because the specification is @F, this action would be run on a field to update the captured text in the field.
If the text value of the field has a value of "This Too is TOO Much Text Too", then the final value
of the field will be "This Too is Three Much Text Too", because this is a case sensitive search.
if the confidence of the field was "55555555555555555555555555555", after updating the text value
the field confidence would become "5555555555559999955555555555555".
rrSet("This Too is TOO Much Text Too", "@X.MyVariable")
ReplaceSubstringLast(@X.MyVariable, "TOO", "Three", "false")
The example first sets a DCO variable on the current DCO object to the value "This Too is TOO Much Text Too".
This is performed as an illustration. Typically the variable would have been set earlier.
The action ReplaceSubstringLast will update the variable "MyVariable" to
"This Too is TOO Much Text Three".
ReplaceSubstringLast(@P\Field1, ",", ".", "False)
It is assumed that this action is running on a page object that has an existing child field called "Field1".
The action will update the text value of Field1.
If the text value of the field has a value of "1,234,56", then the final value
of the field will be "1,234.56".
if the confidence of the field was "72387279", after updating the text value
the field confidence would become "72387979".
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: ReplaceValueAtPosition
method.qi: Replaces a character in a field at a specific position with a replacement character.
method.ap:
Position:
An integer identifying the position within the text that contains the value to be replaced.
Replacement:
The replacement string; if blank this parameter defaults to "" indicating a deletion.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters
method.h:
This action replaces a single character at the indicated position within the string
with a replacement value. The replacement value can be 0 or more characters. If the value is empty,
then the replacement acts as a deletion. The single character that is replaced can be replaced
with multiple characters. Only the character at the specified index is replaced.
The confidence values of the remaining characters is not changed by this action. The
added characters will be given a default passing confidence.
ReplaceValueAtPosition("3","/")
The field value "10.05.1962" becomes "10/05.1962".
ReplceValueAtPosition("5","Hello")
The field value "1234567890" becomes "1234Hello67890".
ReplceValueAtPosition("5","")
The field value "1234567890" becomes "123467890".
ReplceValueAtPosition("@X.Index","@P.MyText")
This example will obtain the start position from the DCO variable called "Index"
on the current DCO field object. The replacement string will be obtained
from the variable "MyText" which would exist on the parent page object.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: SetAllFieldLabels
method.qi: Sets the label display variables from an INI file.

p.name: INIFileName
p.qi: The full path to the INI file containing the field labels.

p.name: AddMissingEntries
p.qi: True adds the missing entries into the INI file, False will not.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action is an automated way of updating fields with a user friendly display label at runtime.
To perform the update, it is required that the fields and their display labels are listed in an INI file.
Once set, the user label is displayed on verification panels instead of the field name.
The label is supported by Navigator, Datacap Desktop and Taskmaster Web, provided the panel in use
supports this feature.
The action will read scan through every document, page and field within the batch to set the "label"
variable on each field in the batch. This action might take some time in large batches. This is not the only
way that an application can set the label variable for fields. For environments that typically have
large batches, it would be more efficient to set the label variable
in the setup DCO, making it permanently set without having to use this action to read the labels over and over from a file at runtime
for every batch.
This action is not compatible with, nor is it necessary, on applications based on Flex technology.
The settings file needs to follow the following format:
[Verification Labels]
FieldName1=DisplayLabel
FieldName2=DisplayLabel
etc.
If AddMissingEntries is set to True, then any fields within the batch that do not exist in the INI file list is
added to the INI file. This may make it easier to go back and edit the INI file to configure these fields.
When the action updates the INI file, it requires that the user running the rules has full access to update
the specified INI file. If the user running the task is Rulerunner, then the Rulerunner user must have correct
permissions. If the user is running the rule through a client like Datacap Desktop, then that user must have correct
access permissions for the INI file.
An example INI file configuration:
[Verification Labels]
Vendor=Vendor
Vendor_Number=Vendor Number
Remittance_Zip=Postal code
Invoice_Number=Invoice Number
Invoice_Date=Invoice Date
PO_Number=PO Number
Shipping=Shipping
SetLabels("@APPPATH(settingsfile)")
method.lvl:
Any level, but will only process fields that are descendants of the object upon which you place the action, and the object itself (if it is a field object).
Typically, this action would be called at the batch level to ensure that all fields are set within the batch.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: SetFieldStatusMessage
method.qi: A message that appears in verify clients

p.name: Message
p.qi: The message to display.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Note: Some actions, such as validation actions, will automatically
set this variable. If this action is called, it will replace any
existing message with the new message. It is also recommended to
set the message back to @EMPTY prior to verification and then set the status only when needed.
The manner in which the message is displayed to the user is dependent on the verify client.
SetFieldStatusMessage("The value '+@F+' is invalid")
method.ret:
Always
False.
method.see: Refer to the top level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: SplitFieldValuePreserveStart
method.qi: Truncates a fields value starting at a specific string or character, keeping the beginning text in the field.
method.ap:
SplitAt
A character or a string of characters where the truncation will start.
CaseSensitive:
"True" indicates that the comparison should be case sensitive.
"False" will perform a case insensitive comparison. If the parameter is missing
or invalid, the parameter will default to "True".
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Splits a Field object's text value at the first instance of the character or string
specified as a parameter. The result is that the final string is truncated at
the location where the SplitAt parameter matches the field's text.
The action deletes all characters to the end of the string starting from the separating
character, as well as the separation character.
All text prior to the separating character remains.
The confidence values of the remaining characters is not changed by this action.
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart("c", "True")
If the current field object's value is "Description," this action truncates it to "Des".
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart("a", "False")
If the current field object's value is "ABCDEFG," the final result is "".
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart("g", "False")
If the current field object's value is "ABCDEFG," the final result is "ABCDEF".
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart("Dog", "False")
If the current field object's value is "I love cats and doggies." this action truncates it to "I love cats and ".
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart("@X.MyVariable", "True")
This works similar to the other examples however the text for the parameter is obtained
from the value of the DCO variable called "MyVariable" on the current object
that is attached to the rule.
method.ret:
True
if the separator character is found. Otherwise
False.
method.see:
SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd, TruncateFromStart, TruncateFromEnd.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd
method.qi: Truncates a fields value starting at a specific string or character, keeping the ending text in the field.
method.ap:
SplitAt
A character or a string of characters where the truncation will stop.
CaseSensitive:
"True" indicates that the comparison should be case sensitive.
"False" will perform a case insensitive comparison. If the parameter is missing
or invalid, the parameter will default to "True".
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Splits a Field object's text value at the first instance of the character or string
specified as a parameter. The result is that the final string will have the text removed
from the start of the value, up to and including
the location where the SplitAt parameter matches the field's text.
The action deletes all characters to the end of the string starting from the separating
character, as well as the separation character.
All text prior to the separating character remains.
The confidence values of the remaining characters is not changed by this action.
SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd("c", "True")
If the current field object's value is "Description," this action truncates it to "ription,".
SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd("a", "False")
If the current field object's value is "ABCDEFG," the final result is "BCDEFG".
SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd("g", "False")
If the current field object's value is "ABCDEFG," the final result is "".
SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd("Dog", "False")
If the current field object's value is "I love cats and doggies." this action truncates it to "gies.".
SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd("@X.MyVariable", "True")
This works similar to the other examples however the text for the parameter is obtained
from the value of the DCO variable called "MyVariable" on the current object
that is attached to the rule.
method.ret:
True
if the separator character is found. Otherwise
False.
method.see:
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart, TruncateFromStart, TruncateFromEnd.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: SplitTextIntoVariables
method.qi: Breaks a field or variable, using a specified character, into multiple DCO variables with each split segment.
method.ap:
TextToSplit:
Text that will be split into multiple DCO variables based on a specified split character.
NewVariableName:
The text will be split into new variables in the current DCO object
using this as the base variable name.
SplitCharacter:
The character that will be used as the splitting value in the source text.
This character will be removed from the final split text.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Splits text into multiple variables based on a split character. For each separate sequence of text,
a new variable will be created in the current DCO object, based on the root name provided
in the parameter "NewVariableName". Each new variable will be indexed by the suffix "_N", where
N is an integer starting at 0 up to the number of created variables minus 1.
The number of created variables is in the same variable with the suffix "_count".
SplitTextIntoVariables("Here Is;Some Text;To Split", "MySplitVar", ";")
This example will split the input text into 3 separate variables based on the semicolon
character.
These will be the variables created on the current DCO object:
MySplitVar_count = 3
MySplitVar_0 = "Here Is"
MySplitVar_1 = "Some Text"
MySplitVar_2 = "To Split"
SplitTextIntoVariables("@F", "MySplitVar", ":")
Assuming this is called on a field that contains the text "12345:678:9ABCD:EFG",
the field text will be split into 3 separate variables based on the colon
character.
These will be the variables created on the current DCO field object:
MySplitVar_count = 4
MySplitVar_0 = "12345"
MySplitVar_1 = "678"
MySplitVar_2 = "9ABCD"
MySplitVar_3 = "EFG"
SplitTextIntoVariables("@P.MySourceText", "MySplitVar", ":")
Similar to the previous example, this example will obtain the source
text from the page level DCO variable called "MySourceText", splitting
the value of that variable based on the colon
character.
method.ret:
False
if there is an error or if one of the parameters is invalid. Returns
true
if the text is successfully split. If the field is empty, the action still returns
true
and the count of variables created will be 0. No additional variables will be created.
If the split character is not found in the source string, only one variable will be created
which will contain the entire source string and the action will still return
true.
method.see: Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: SumFields
method.qi: Sums children of a DCO object that match the specified name.
method.ap:
TypeOrVariable:
The type of the field or the name of a variable that will be summed.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The action locates child fields that match the specified type or child objects that
contain variables of the same name as specified in the parameter.
If the name refers to a field, then the text value of the field
will be summed. If the parameter specifies a variable name, then every object that has a variable of that name
will be summed will have the value of that variable summed.
The sum of the values will be stored in a variable on the current DCO node. The variable name will be
"SumFields_" followed by the parameter type. If the parameter provided was "Lineitem", then all of the
items that matched "Lineitem" would be summed and stored in a variable named "SumFields_Lineitem".
The result of the sum can then be used by subsequent actions as needed.
The format of the numbers being added must be in the correct numeric format based on the current locale.
If there are decimal separators, the number must use the correct decimal separator for the locale.
If the value is plain text or is not in a number format that is valid for the current
locale, the value will not be added to the total.
SumFields("Detail")
This example will look for any fields called "Detail" that are children of the current object
and look to see if the children contain a variable called Detail. If the name refers to a type
for a field, then the text value of the field will be added to the total. If the name refers
to a variable of a child object, then the value of that variable will be added to the total sum.
Assuming the above action was called on a page and the page has 10 fields and 3 of those fields have a variable
called "Detail", then the values from the variable on each of the 3 fields will be added together. If the value
of the variable "Detail" is "10" on one field, and the variable "Detail" contains "4.50" on another field and
contains "6.25" on another field, they will be added for a total of "20.75". That total will be stored
on the current page object in a DCO variable called "SumFields_Detail".
rrSet("10", "@X\Field1.AddMe")
rrSet("4.50", "@X\Field4.AddMe")
rrSet("6.25", "@X\Field7.AddMe")
SumFields("AddMe")
This example further illustrates the above example. While it is not typical that
an application would hard code variable values simply to sum them as shown, the intent is to
illustrate how the SumFields actions works. This example assumes there are at least
these three child fields on the current object: "Field1", "Field4", "Field7".
The exact field names could of course be changed to something meaningful for
the application. This simply shows there are three fields with a variable, although
there could be more without the variable set. If the variable is not set, then
the field is simply ignored.
The SumFields action then looks for all child types called "AddMe" and looks for children
that have a variable called "AddMe". Again, the name could be changed to something
appropriate for the application. SumFields will add these three values and store
the result in a variable called "SumFields_AddMe".
method.lvl: The parent object that contains the child fields or variables that will be summed.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
Refer to the top level help for information regarding the use of locale in actions.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: SwitchMMDD
method.qi: Removes leading or trailing spaces from a field or variable.

p.name: Target
p.qi: A smart parameter that references a variable or field.

p.name: Separator
p.qi: The date separator.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action operates on a short date that has a format that starts MM/DD or DD/MM and swaps
the position of the month and day values.
The action operates on the string regardless of the date format of the current locale.
It does not perform any analysis on the date to determine if the two values should be
swapped, it simply swaps them.
SwitchMMDD("/")
In this example, the value "03/09/10" becomes "09/03/10".

method.name: TrimSpaces
method.qi: Removes leading or trailing spaces from a field or variable.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to trim.
method.h:
Deletes extra spaces at the beginning and end of the current Field object's captured text value.
Spaces that are not at the beginning or end of the field's text value will not be removed.
If acting on a field text value, the confidence of the remaining characters is not changed by this action.
TrimSpaces("@F")
Assuming this action is called on a field level object, the current text value
of the field will be trimmed. If the value is "456.11_ _ _ _" it will be
updated to "456.11".
TrimSpaces("@X.MyVariable")
This example will trim the spaces of the value for the
DCO variable called "MyVariable" on the current DCO object.
method.see:
DeleteSelectedCharacters
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: TruncateFromEnd
method.qi: Truncates a field or variable to the length specified, removing the text on the end.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to truncate.
Length:
The maximum length for the value. If the text is longer than this length, it will be shortened to the
specified length by removing the characters at the end of the text. If the starting length of the value
is equal to or less than the specified length,
the text will not be changed. The length must be a positive integer.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action adjusts a text string to a maximum size. If the value is larger than the maximum length,
the string will be adjusted to the specified maximum length by removing extra characters from
the end of the string. If the string is less than or equal to the maximum size, the text
will not be changed.
If acting on a field text value, the confidence of the remaining characters is not changed by this action.
TruncateFromEnd("@F","6")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, it will truncate the text value
of the field to a maximum length of 6 by removing extra characters from the end.
The value "EU0002240" would become "EU0002"
TruncateFromEnd("@F","1")
In this example the value "ABCDEFG" would become "A"
TruncateFromEnd("@P.MyVariable","10")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, it obtain the value from the
variable called "MyVariable" that exists on the parent page object. The string
will be truncated to a maximum length of 10. If "MyVariable" contains
the text "123456789012345", it will be truncated to "1234567890".
TruncateFromEnd("@P\Field2","10")
Assuming this action is called on a field object,
this action will adjust the length of the text value
of a sibling field called "Field2".
method.see:
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart, SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd, TruncateFromStart, IsTextLength.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

method.name: TruncateFromStart
method.qi: Truncates a field or variable to the length specified, removing the text on at the start.
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that resolves to a target DCO field or DCO variable to truncate.
Length:
The maximum length for the value. If the text is longer than this length, it will be shortened to the
specified length by removing the characters at the beginning of the text. If the starting length of the value
is equal to or less than the specified length,
the text will not be changed. The length must be a positive integer.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action adjusts a text string to a maximum size. If the value is larger than the maximum length,
the string will be adjusted to the specified maximum length by removing extra characters from
the start of the string. If the string is less than or equal to the maximum size, the text
will not be changed.
If acting on a field text value, the confidence of the remaining characters is not changed by this action.
TruncateFromStart("@F","6")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, it will truncate the text value
of the field to a maximum length of 6 by removing extra characters from the end.
The value "EU0002240" would become "002240"
TruncateFromStart("@F","1")
In this example the value "ABCDEFG" would become "G"
TruncateFromStart("@P.MyVariable","10")
Assuming this action is called on a field object, it obtain the value from the
variable called "MyVariable" that exists on the parent page object. The string
will be truncated to a maximum length of 10. If "MyVariable" contains
the text "123456789012345", it will be truncated to "6789012345".
TruncateFromStart("@P\Field2","10")
Assuming this action is called on a field object,
this action will adjust the length of the text value
of a sibling field called "Field2".
method.see:
SplitFieldValuePreserveStart, SplitFieldValuePreserveEnd, TruncateFromEnd, IsTextLength.
Refer to the top level help for more information regarding smart parameters.

com.qi: : Actions that increase or decrease character confidence based on two sets of field data that should be identical.
com.h:
Voting is a method of comparing recognition results from two calls of recognition, or data entry from two different
users, and determine if the data entered is identical or if there is a mismatch.
Voting is used with field data or field recognition, not full page recognition.
When comparing results from two different recognition engines, or recognition from the same engine
with different settings, the results are compared. If the characters are identical, then the read
is considered to be accurate and raises the character confidence to the highest level. If
the characters do not match, then the confidence is lowered to the minimum confidence.
This can help confirm text is correct without a user verification, however if text confidence
is voted down, it would then be flagged for a verification operator.
Manual data entry can be compared in what is typically performed as a double-blind
data entry. One user would enter verification data, then a second user would enter the validation
data. If the data entered matches, then the data is considered to be accurate and move
on to the next step. If not, the data would need to be re-entered by the second
verification operator for it to be accepted.
Multiple values of recognized text are stored in a field using a
mechanism called "Alternate Text". The procedure allows a single field to store
multiple independent text strings, with confidence values stored for each
of the strings in the field DCO.
The alternate text is accessed via indexes. By default, alternate text is not used
and any text recognized, or entered by a user, is stored in the field along with the confidence.
Indexes can be provided to store additional data along side the original data.
Typically, once the first data has been recognized or entered, it will
be moved from the primary field text index to an alternate index using
the action PropagateToAlternateText
Calling the action PropagateToAlternateText("1") will take the primary text
in the field and move it to another location within the field, giving it
an index value of "1". The field can then be recognized again, or
entered by a secondary verification operator, so the field will then
contain two text strings. The VoteField action will then compare
the two strings and change the confidence of the primary text
either up or down, depending on the characters that match or
do not match.
If necessary, multiple indexes can be used, meaning that
text can be moved to index 1, recognition can be performed again,
and that text can be stored in index 2, etc. Allowing storage of
several different versions of the text that is expected to be
identical and then can be tested to confirm if the text matches
or not.
If performing double blind user entry, not ever verification panel may support double
blind entry.
Smart Parameters
Parameters that use an "@" notation, such as "@X.xxxx", "@P.xxxx", "@STRING()", "@PILOT()", etc., are
known as "smart parameters". The data passed as a parameter to an action will be evaluated at runtime.
For example, "@X" is notation for accessing the current object. "@P" accesses the page object, which
could be the current object, or a parent object. Being evaluated at runtime, allows recognized data
or other batch specific data to be passed to actions or stored as metadata. A smart parameter such
as @DATE could be used to name export files based on the current date. Similar smart parameters
will retrieve the current batch ID, current batch directory, current operator ID, and more.
Smart parameters are a very powerful mechanism of getting data from other areas of the application and copying
it into a new location or passing it as a parameter to an action. It is recommended that the smart parameter
documentation is reviewed to understand the full capabilities available. The top-level help of the
ValidationAndTextAdjustments action library also has information about smart parameters. Some characters such
as +, \ and . also have special smart parameter meaning and may be interpreted as a smart parameter. This
can be controlled using smart parameter syntax.

method.name: ClearAlternateText
method.qi: Clears character and confidence values from the alternate text index specified by the parameter.
method.ap:
The alternate text index in the current field to clear the character and confidence values.
0 is the primary index, followed by 1, 2, etc. for storage of comparison text.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Clears character and confidence values from the Character Array position specified by the parameter.
When cleared, the confidence values are set to 10 (high confidence).
A field in the Data file can hold more than one representation of the field's value.
Values other than the current, visible value are accessed via an index number.
The primary field text value is at index 0, the next alternate value is at index 1. Each additional
value also has corresponding character confidences. Typically
only one alternate string is used for voting, however additional indexes can be
used as required.
Note:
Most actions only work with characters and confidence values
located in the first position of the Character Array (position 0).
The ClearAlternateText action can be used with User Application Web's Advanced Index task, for "Double Blind" data entry.
PropagateToAlternateText("1")
ClearAlternateText("0")
In this example, all characters at the primary index (0) of the Character Array will be copied to the second index (1).
The second action will then clear character and confidence values from the first index in the Character Array.
The field can then be recognized again and then call the voting action
or the batch can be routed to a second verification operator.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
PropagateToAlternateText
Refer to the top level help topic for this action library for more information about voting.

method.name: PropagateToAlternateText
method.qi: Copies the character and confidence values from the field's primary index to the index specified by the parameter.
method.ap:
The alternate text index in the current field to clear the character and confidence values.
0 is the primary index, followed by 1, 2, etc. for storage of comparison text.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Copies the character and confidence values from the primary index of the field text (index 0)
to the index specified by the parameter. (The character "node" of a page's Data file is an array
that can hold many recognized character values, and their corresponding confidence values.)
Note:
Rules will only work with characters and confidence values located in the
first position of the Character Array (index 0).
The PropagateToAlternateText action can be used with the User Application
Web's Advanced Index task, for "Double Blind" data entry.
PropagateToAltText("1")
ClearAlternateText("0")
All characters in the first index of the Character Array will be copied to the second index.
Then, the second action will clear the character and confidence values from the first index.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
ClearAlternateText
Refer to the top level help topic for this action library for more information about voting.

method.name: VoteField
method.qi: Checks to see if the data entered for by the first Data Entry operator or recognition, matches the second value.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Checks to see if the data entered for by the first Data Entry operator, or recognized text, matches the
data enter by the second Data Entry operator or the second text recognition.
The text in the primary index 0 will be compared to the text in the alternate index 1.
Failed (mismatched) values set the confidence for the invalid character to '1',
therefore flagging the field as Low Confidence. Positive matches set the
character's confidence to '10' (High Confidence).
When performing double blind verification, this action needs to run after the second Data Entry task has been completed.
This action is used for workflows using third pass data entry.
Character confidence typically uses a range of 1 to 10. Some areas of the application
may interpret this range to 0 to 9.
RecognizeFieldOCR_A()
PropagateToAlternateText("1")
ClearAlternateText("0")
RecognizeFieldOCR_S()
VoteField()
This example compares the results of two different recognition engines. First the field
is recognized using OCR/A. The recognized text is stored in the alternate
index "1" location. The primary text is cleared and recognition is performed again
using OCR/S. Lastly the VoteField action is used to compare the results
of the recognition.
If the text recognized by the first engine is "Hello Tom" and the text
of the second engine is "Hello Tim", then regardless of the original
confidence levels, the new confidence values of the text will be
10 for every character except the letter "i" in the primary
field location will have its confidence reduced to "1".
method.see: Refer to the top level help topic of this action library for more information on voting.

com.qi: : Work with zones and line items.
com.h:
The ZonesAndLineItems action library focuses on actions that manipulate fields, zones and lineitems.
A field is a location allocated in the DCO that tracks a text value and location on the image associated with the page.
A zone is the pixel location on the page image, that contains the coordinates for the text within
a field. For example, if the field contains a date, the zone coordinates identifies the location
on the image that holds the date value in a left, top, right, bottom format. It is common for
the words "field" and "zone" to be used interchangeably although there are these slight
differences in meaning.
Lineitems are special kinds of fields. If line items are used in an application,
they not necessarily appear on every page.
Lineitems are fields that are children of a field, creating a short tree structure.
Lineitems are typically used to represent a table on the page.
A typical lineitem structure example:
Details
- Lineitem
- - ItemID
- - ItemDesc
- - Qty
- - Price
- - LineTotal
Lineitems add an additional level of complexity to field manipulation, verification
and export. It is recommended to create lineitem fields only when necessary.
♕ Smart Parameters ♕
Action parameters can be provided with smart parameter specifications. The complete smart parameter
reference can be found in the top-level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library.

method.name: AdjustMergedCCOPositions
method.qi: : Adjusts positions in a merged CCO.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
AdjustMergedCCOPositions
is for use in applications using merged
CCOs. It normalizes zone position coordinates populated to the DCO when the data is
generated from a document using a merged CCO. The coordinates are adjusted relative to
the page and also sets the DCO ImageFile property to the name of the TIFF that the data was
found on.
Note: All files to be merged MUST have an associated CCO file.
Used in conjunction with action
MergeCCOsByType
from the
AutomaticDocumentFingerprinting
action library in a prior ruleset.
AdjustMergedCCOPositions()
method.ret:
False
if the current document does not consist of more than one source page, or if
a page to be merged did not have an associated CCO file created.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see: Action MergeCCOsByType in the AutomaticDocumentFingerprinting action library.

method.name: AdjustZoneBottomToImageBottom
method.qi: : Expands the zone to the bottom of the current image.

p.name: UseCCO
p.qi: True: Use the CCO boundaries, False: Use the current image boundaries.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Changes the bottom zone boundary of the current field to either the bottom of the associated
page image, or to the bottom of the CCO. This action is useful when there is a use case to extend
the bottom coordinates of the current field.
AdjustZoneBottomToImageBottom("True")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: AdjustZoneLeftToImageLeft
method.qi: : Expands the zone to the left of the current image.

p.name: UseCCO
p.qi: True: Use the CCO boundaries, False: Use the current image boundaries.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Changes the top zone boundary of the current field to either the left of the associated
page image, or to the left of the CCO. This action is useful when there is a use case to extend
the left coordinates of the current field to the edge of the page.
AdjustZoneLeftToImageLeft("True")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: AdjustZoneRightToImageRight
method.qi: : Expands the zone to the right of the current image.

p.name: UseCCO
p.qi: True: Use the CCO boundaries, False: Use the current image boundaries.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Changes the top zone boundary of the current field to either the right of the associated
page image, or to the right of the CCO. This action is useful when there is a use case to extend
the right coordinates of the current field to the edge of the page.
AdjustZoneRightToImageRight("True")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: AdjustZoneTopToImageTop
method.qi: : Expands the zone to the top of the current image.

p.name: UseCCO
p.qi: True: Use the CCO boundaries, False: Use the current image boundaries.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Changes the top zone boundary of the current field to either the top of the associated
page image, or to the top of the CCO. This action is useful when there is a use case to extend
the top coordinates of the current field.
AdjustZoneTopToImageTop("True")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: CalculateBlankInvoiceLineItemDetails
method.qi: : Calculates the value when either the Qty, Price or LineTotal lineitem is empty.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action is for use on the line item field where the fields quantity, price and line total exists on the line item,
as is typical for an invoice document. If one of the three fields is missing, the action will calculate the value of the missing field
using the values of the two fields with values.
This calculation is performed for all detail lines on the page.
To calculate the missing field, it is required that the line items
in the application are named exactly "Qty", "Price", and "LineTotal".
CalculateBlankInvoiceLineItemDetails()
method.lvl: Field level. Specifically, the lineitem field under the Details field.
method.ret: Always True.

method.name: CallPOLR
method.qi: : Pre-matches invoice line items with a previously processed PO.
method.ap:
DisplayPOLRPanel:
True = Display the POLR panel. False = Do not display the POLR panel.
This parameter must never be set to true within any task profile that is run unattended, such
as with Rulerunner. Typically, this value will be set to False.
ADOBDBType:
The ADOBDB constant number for the PO number field.
When using bind variables, the data type
of the PO Number is specified with this action. For example: 200 = varchar.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action is used to pre-match invoice line items with the PO prior to verify operator verification.
Additional action parameters must exist in the settings.ini file.
The record set for the PO is retrieved using the information in the settings.ini.
This calls the record set according to the DSN in the settings INI.
PODSN and POLookup indicate how to obtain the record set.
The record set is expected to be the line items for the PO for the current document and
is keyed off of the PO number. It then uses the POLR logic to perform the automatic matching.
The database connection is retrieved from Database\PODSN.
The SQL query is retrieved from Database\POLookup.
There is a special testing mode that occurs when the station name ends in "-Test". In this situation,
the values are retrieved from different locations in the settings.ini file.
The database connection is retrieved from Database\TestPODSN.
The SQL query is retrieved from Database\TestPOLookup.
The PODSN and TestPODSN support smart parameters to allow for secure connection strings.
The connection string can be encrypted in the application manager and can be referenced in the
INI file section using a smart parameter.
The POLookup and TestPOLookup values may also contain smart parameters.
The settings ini file must contain values for these keys:
[POLR]
Qty=
ItemID=
Price=
WriteUnusedPOLInes=
PriceTolerance=
SeparatorCharacter=
If the station name has a suffix of "-Test" then these keys must exist:
[Database]
TestPODSN=
TestPOLookup=
If the station name does not have a suffix of "-Test" then these keys must exist:
[Database]
PODSN=
POLookup=
CallPOLR("False", "200")
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: GenerateDetails
method.qi: : Creates the detail lineitem fields on the page.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action sets up a field in the APT application and puts a detail subfield on every page. This extra detail subfield
appears on all pages of a multi-page invoice, allowing every page to be viewed.
GenerateDetails()

method.name: InheritParentPosition
method.qi: : Provides the current field zone with the zone position of a parent object identified by the parameter.
method.ap:
Case-sensitive string value of the parent field name.
The current field is expected to be a child of another field and will inherit the position
of the parent field whose type or name exactly matches the one specified in the parameter.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Provides the current object bound to this action, a subfield of another field, of the Document Hierarchy with the zone
parameters of a parent object identified by the parameter.
InheritParentPosition("Details")
Details, in this example, is the name of a parent field object in the
Invoices application. If this action is called on the child LINEITEM field,
the action will provide this child object with the zone parameters of the parent.
The current field is then assigned the same position value of the Details field.
The Details field will be unchanged.

method.name: LoadCCOFromField
method.qi: : Forces the load of the CCO for this action library.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action loads the CCO associated with the parent page from a field object.
Using this action will force a refresh of the current page CCO in memory
prior to using another action in this library that uses the CCO.
Typically it is not necessary to call this action as any action within
this library that requires the CCO will load the CCO, when it is not
already loaded.
LoadCCOFromField()
SetDynamicDetailZones("Zone Bottom,Notes")
AdjustZoneBottomToImageBottom()
ScanDetails()

method.name: LearnLineItemZones
method.qi: : Adds new zones to the DCO.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action has the capability to learn new zones based on a variable setting.
A variable "PreVerify Pos" with a value of "0,0,0,0" indicates that there wasn't
previously a zone for the line item and will be added to the DCO.
The current page must contain a field called "Details" which contains the line items.
Legacy fingerprints are stored in the Setup DCO. The client or service running rules must
have sufficient rights to write updates to the application's setup. XML fingerprints
may provide better performance.
This action is not compatible with XML fingerprints. This action only learns the first line item.
LearnLineItemZones()

method.name: LearnLineItemZonesFingerprintXML
method.qi: : Adds new zones to the XML fingerprint.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action has the capability to learn new zones based on a variable setting.
A variable "PreVerify Pos" with a value of "0,0,0,0" indicates that there wasn't
previously a zone and will be added to the DCO.
This action is fingerprint XML compatible. This action only learns the first line item.
The current page must contain a field called "Details" which contains the line items.
This action needs to be followed by XMLWriteZones to write the zones to fingerprint XML file.
The service or client user ID running the rules must have rights to write to the fingerprint XML file location.
LearnLineItemZonesFingerprintXML()
XMLWriteZones()

method.name: LoadZonesFromFingerprint
method.qi: : Forces loading of a fingerprint and sets all of the zone positions baased on the fingerprint zones coordinates

p.name: FingerprintID
p.qi: The ID of the fingerprint to load.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Loads position information for each field in the calling object and children from the specified fingerprint. Pre-adjusts these
values based on offset information stored in an 'Image_Offset' variable from the current field or page.
Position information is based on the setup DCO position for the fingerprint ID passed as a parameter.
The offset value is applied to all child objects of a node where an 'Image_Offset' variable is found;
unless overwritten by a child node also having an Image_Offset value to apply.
This action does not support XML fingerprints.
LoadZonesFromFingerprint("1022");
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: MergeLineItemFieldToPageField
method.qi: : Merges line item values to a page variable
method.ap:
DetailFieldName:
The name of the field, a direct child of the page, that
contains the line items.
LineItemFieldName:
The name of the field, a grandchild of the DetailField, whose value
is to be concatenated in the field specified by PageFieldName.
Delimiter:
The delimiter character to be placed between each field value.
PageFieldName
The name of a field, a direct child of the page object, that will
hold the results.
Smart parameters are supported for all fields.
method.h:
This action concatenates all of the values of a subfield contained in
a detail section and place the values in a field on the current page.
This action can be useful to place all of the values from a line item field into
a page field which is then available using other export techniques.
MergeLineItemFieldToPageField("Details","Description",",","MyExportField")
method.lvl:
Must be on the page object that contains the detail section and the PageFieldName
holder of the concatenated values
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: MergePageFieldToDocumentVariable

method.name: MergePageFieldToDocumentVariable
method.qi: : Copies fields from multiple pages into a parent document variable.
method.ap:
PageFieldName:
The name of a field, a direct child of the page object, that will
have its value copied to a parent document variable.
Delimiter:
The delimiter character to be placed between each field value.
DocumentVariableName:
The name of the destination variable on the current document
where the field values are to be concatenated.
All parameters support smart parameters.
method.h:
This action will iterate through each page within the current document. For each page,
the value in the specified page field will be copied to the specified document variable.
If there are multiple pages, each value will be separated by the delimiter.
MergeLineItemFieldToPageField("Total",",","AllPageTotals")
method.lvl: Each page must be an immediate child of the document.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: MergeLineItemFieldToPageField

method.name: MergeZones
method.qi: : Merges the zone from calling field with zone of dco fields passed as smart parameters.
method.ap:
A comma separated set of smart parameters that specify target fields to merge together.
Each smart parameter must resolve to a field on the current page.
method.h:
Merges calling field's position with each passed dco position.
MergeZones("@P\5PAddTel,@P\5PAddZip,@P\2PatName")

method.name: PadZone
method.qi: : Pads the zone by the value passed. Number of CSV passed values varies padding value by vector.

p.name: Padding
p.qi: A comma separated list of 1 to 4 integers.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Pads the calling field's position with each value passed. Number of passed values varies the padding vector as follows:
1) Pads Left, Top, Right, and Bottom by this value (i.e. expand if positive)
2) Pads as X,Y (X: pad to Left and Right, Y: pad to Top and Bottom)
3) Pads as Left, Top, Right, and Bottom. (missing values will be treated as zero).
4) Pads as Left, Top, Right, and Bottom.
PadZone("15")
Pads 15 pixels to the Left, Right, Top and Bottom position.
PadZone("5,10")
Pads 5 pixels to the Left and Right position, and 10 to the Top and Bottom position.
PadZone("-5,0,12,25")
Pads -5 pixels to the Left (making the zone smaller), 0 to the Right, 12 to the Top and 25 to the Bottom position.
method.ret:
False
if the calling field does not have a valid non zero position.
False
if there are zero or more than four CSV parameters.
False
if the SmartParameter value returns as a non-numeric.
Otherwise,
True.

method.name: PopulateZonedField
method.qi: : Copies a section CCO page text to the current field based on the current field's zone coordinates.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action populates the current field value with the full-page recognition results
that fall within the field's zone boundaries.
The field must have coordinates set.
A CCO must exist for the page. A CCO can be created through a RecognizePage action
or created by CreateCCOFromLayout action, after a Recognize action has been performed.
The text at the location of the field's zone will be copied from the CCO to the field.
This action is very similar to the action SnapCCOtoDCO in the SharedRecognitionTools action library.
The difference is that SnapCCOToDCO populates every field on the page with the recognized text
within the CCO and PopulateZonedField will only populate the current field.
PopulateZonedField()
If the current field had a zone position of "46,72,85,81", this action will
copy the text, from the CCO for the current page,
that exists within those coordinates and place it into the
"text" property of the current field.
method.see: SnapCCOtoDCO, PopulateZoneLineItemField.

method.name: PopulateZonedLineItemField
method.qi: : Copies text from the CCO page text to lineitem fields based on the zone coordinates.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action populates the field value with the full-page recognition results
(in the CCO) that fall within a child field's zone boundaries of a LINEITEM parent field.
The field must have coordinates set.
A CCO must exist for the page. A CCO for the page can be created through a RecognizePage action
or created by CreateCCOFromLayout action, after a Recognize action has been performed.
The text at the location of the field's zone will be copied from the CCO to the field.
This action is very similar to the action PopulateZonedField.
The difference is that PopulateZonedField does not populate lineitem fields while
PopulateZonedLineItemField will only populate lineitem fields.
PopulateZonedLineItemField()
method.see: SnapCCOToDCO, PopulateZonedLineItemField.

method.name: PopulateZoneLineItemFieldDynamic
method.qi: : Populates line items.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action is like the PopulateZNLineItemField but it uses the CCO that was
loaded into memory by LoadCCOFromField, instead of the global CCO.
It populates the fingerprint’s Data file with the recognized value contained inside
the zone of a child Field object of a LINEITEM parent field. This action should
only be used with sub-fields of the LINEITEM field - ItemID, ItemDesc,
Quantity, Price in the Invoices application.
rrCompare("@P.ZoneRead", "FPXML")
PopulateZoneLineItemFieldDynamic()
method.ret:
True,
if there is no field position or if the data was found in a zone.
False,
if there is a zone defined but it is blank.

method.name: ReadZones
method.qi: : Sets the page zones coordinates based on the current fingerprint.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Based on the current page fingerprint, this action loads field
position information for each node in the calling object and it's children. It adjusts
these values based on offset information stored in an 'Image_Offset' variable at any node level.
Position information is based on the setup DCO position for the parent page's fingerprint ID.
The offset value is applied to all child objects of a node where an 'Image_Offset' variable is found;
unless overwritten by a child node also having an Image_Offset value to apply.
This action is not compatible with XML fingerprints. For XML fingerprints
use the action XMLReadZones in the AutomaticDocumentFingerprints action library.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: XMLReadZones in the AutomaticDocumentFingerprints action library.

method.name: ResetField
method.qi: : Clears a field's value and position information.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action deletes the selected Field object's captured value, and sets the field's Position
attribute to 0,0,0,0.
This action is intended to provide an easy mechanism to both reset the field position and
clear the text captured in the field. If the only the field's text needed to be cleared,
that can be accomplished using rrSet("EMPTY", "@X"). This would clear the text and retain
the field's zone location on the page.
If only the field's position needs to be reset,
this can be performed using rrSet("0,0,0,0", "@X.Position")
Note, however, that the action does not clear any Alt-Text values
associated with the bound Field object. Alternate text can be cleared
using the action ClearAlternateText in the VoteUsingComparativeText action library.
ResetField()
This action typically belongs to a follow-up Validate rule that deals with a
False
response to
an action such as IsDate() in the previous rule. If the field's value is not a date (in this example),
the
ResetField
action will remove the value that is there.
Note:
It will also set the
field's
Position
attribute to 0,0,0,0. This allows a click-n-key operation to select a new
location on the page containing the next text.
method.see: ClearAlternateText in the VoteUsingComparativeText action library.

method.name: ScanDetails
method.qi: : Creates the lineitem fields in the runtime DCO.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
The action estimates the number of lineitem rows to create and then
instantiates the Lineitem children fields for the current field
in the runtime DCO. This is similar to the "CreateFields" action,
but this action is specifically for lineitems.
The lineitem rows created are potential line but they may not exist on
the page. Follow-on Rulesets are required delete ineligible lineitems
based on the criteria of the application.
In the APT application, the
Clean
and
Filter
Rulesets
perform the post-step cleanup.
Example field structure:
Main_Page
- Details
- - Lineitem
- - - ItemID
- - - ItemDesc
- - - Qty
- - - Price
- - - LineTotal
- - - POLineNum
ScanDetails()
In this example, ScanDetails is used on a rule that is attached to the "Details" field.
method.see: ScanDetailsByLines, ScanDetailsByVerticalSpace.

method.name: ScanDetailsByLines
method.qi: : Creates the line items using the provided count to determine the number of lines in each row.

p.name: Count
p.qi: The number of lines in each line item.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The action estimates the number of lineitem rows to create and then
instantiates the Lineitem children fields for the current field
in the runtime DCO. This is similar to the "CreateFields" action,
but this action is specificaly for lineitems.
The difference between ScanDetailsByLines and ScanDetails is that
ScanDetails always assumes a lineitem contains only 1 row of text.
ScanDetailsByLines will use the provided number as the number of
rows of text within each lineitem.
The lineitem rows created are potential line but they may not exist on
the page. Follow-on Rulesets are required delete ineligible lineitems
based on the criteria of the application.
In the APT application, the
Clean
and
Filter
Rulesets
perform the post-step cleanup.
Example field structure:
Main_Page
- Details
- - Lineitem
- - - ItemID
- - - ItemDesc
- - - Qty
- - - Price
- - - LineTotal
- - - POLineNum
ScanDetailsByLines("2")
In this example, ScanDetailsByLines is used on a rule that is attached to the "Details" field.
method.see: ScanDetails, ScanDetailsByVerticalSpace.

method.name: ScanDetailsByVerticalSpace
method.qi: : Creates the line items using the provided pixel height to determine the number of lines in each row.

p.name: Count
p.qi: The Number of vertical pixels in each lineitem.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The action estimates the number of lineitem rows to create and then
instantiates the Lineitem children fields for the current field
in the runtime DCO. This is similar to the "CreateFields" action,
but this action is specificaly for lineitems.
The difference between ScanDetailsByVerticalSpace and ScanDetails is that
ScanDetails always assumes a lineitem contains only 1 row of text.
ScanDetailsByLines will use the provided number as the number of
pixels to determine the height of each lineitem.
The lineitem rows created are potential line but they may not exist on
the page. Follow-on Rulesets are required delete ineligible lineitems
based on the criteria of the application.
In the APT application, the
Clean
and
Filter
Rulesets
perform the post-step cleanup.
Example field structure:
Main_Page
- Details
- - Lineitem
- - - ItemID
- - - ItemDesc
- - - Qty
- - - Price
- - - LineTotal
- - - POLineNum
ScanDetailsByVerticalSpace("45")
In this example, ScanDetailsByVerticalSpace is used on a rule that is attached to the "Details" field.
method.ret:
True
if the bound
Field
object contains lines of data. Otherwise,
False.
method.see: ScanDetails, ScanDetailsByLines.

method.name: ScanLineItem
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action creates the lineitem child sub-fields, usually representing columns, for the current lineitem row field.
The page must have identified an associated fingerprint.
The child field positions are then obtained from the lineitem variables "Pos{ID}" where {ID} is the current fingerprint ID.
Fields are created and the zones set, but the text contents of the fields are not populated.
This action is not compatible with XML fingerprints. If using XML fingerprints, use ScanLineItemDynamic.
Main_Page
- Details
- - Lineitem
- - - ItemID
- - - ItemDesc
- - - Qty
- - - Price
- - - LineTotal
- - - POLineNum
ScanLineItem()
In this example, ScanLineItem is used on a rule that is attached to the "Lineitem" field.

method.name: ScanLineItemDynamic
method.qi: : Creates the child fields for the current field.

p.name: Fields
p.qi: A comma separated list of any fields that should be ignored.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
ScanLineItemDynamic is called on a field that contains child fields, and creates the
child fields. It then reads the "POS" positions from the parent object
to set the positions of each child field. Any child fields whose type
matches the value provided in the parameter will be skipped.
It is required for Find Details functionality. It saves the positions of the line and of the fields at the detail
level so all of the line items can be erased and recreated.
This action is for applications using lineitems and XML fingerprints. If using traditional fingerprints
that place fingerprint position information in the DCO, use the action ScanLineItem.
Main_Page
- Details
- - Lineitem
- - - ItemID
- - - ItemDesc
- - - Qty
- - - Price
- - - LineTotal
- - - POLineNum
rrCompare("@P.ZoneRead", "FPXML")
ScanLineItemDynamic("ZoneBottom,Notes")
In this example, ScanLineItemDynamic is used on a rule that is attached to the "Lineitem" field.
method.lvl: Field Level on a field that contains child fields.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: SetDynamicDetailZones
method.qi: : Builds the detail zones

p.name: Field
p.qi: The name of the bottom field.

method.ap: The parameter is the Zone Bottom field. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action takes the position of the line items and it builds the line coordinates from them
and then it sets the details zones from that top line to the bottom of the CCO.
LoadCCOFromField()
SetDynamicDetailZones("Zone Bottom,Notes")
AdjustZoneBottomToImageBottom()
ScanDetails()

method.name: SetFieldEndOfLineCustom
method.qi: : Sets the End of Line character that will be used to separate data from a zone with multiple lines of text.
method.ap:
The end of line separator character used to multiple lines in a single field.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets the end of line character that will be used to separate data from a zone
with multiple lines of text.
When a field is populated by an action in the ZonesAndLineItems action library
by copying the contents of the CCO to the field position, then the specified
character is used to separate lines when more than one line is placed
into a field's Text value.
If this action is not used, and SetFieldEndOfLineToCRLF is not used, the default separator character is a space.
SetFieldEndOfLineCustom("|")
This example sets the End of Line character to the ‘|’ (pipe) character.
A field with two lines of text will have the captured value separated
by this new character.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: SetFieldEndOfLineToCRLF

method.name: SetFieldEndOfLineToCRLF
method.qi: : Sets the End Of Line character that will be used to separate data from a zone with multiple lines of text.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Sets the End Of Line character that will be used to separate data
from a zone with multiple lines of text to the carriage return and
line feed characters: ASCII values 13 and 10.
When a field is populated by an action in the ZonesAndLineItems action library
by copying the contents of the CCO to the field position, then the specified
character is used to separate lines when more than one line is placed
into a field's Text value.
If this action is not used, and SetFieldEndOfLineCustom is not used,
the default separator character is a space.
SetFieldEndOfLineToCRLF()
This sets the End of Line character to the Carriage Return and Line
Feed characters. A field with two lines of text will have
the captured value separated by these characters.
method.ret: Always True
method.see: SetFieldEndOfLineCustom

af.name: FindFingerprint
af.g:
'Attempts to match the current page to a fingerprint and creates a new fingerprint if a match does not occur." ' 'Two comma-separated values (the second is optional):
' 1.A True / False value:
' True if a task is to create a new fingerprint and add it to the fingerprint directory when ' a match does not occur;
' False if the task is to proceed without creating a new fingerprint.

' 2.Optional:
The Page Type that is to be assigned to the newly-created fingerprint. If ' omitted, the current Page Type of the current page will be used.
' Smart parameters are supported. ' Page level only. FindFingerprint = False Writelog("Autodoc " & Version) If InitAutoDocGlobalObjects=False then Exit Function If (CurrentObj.ObjectType<>2) Then Exit Function 'must be a page If Not(FileMgr.FileExists(CurrentObj.ImageName)) Then WriteLog("FindFingerprint skipping. Image file doesn't exist") Exit Function End If StrParam=MetaWord(StrParam) writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "'") aStrParam = Split(StrParam, ",", -1, 1) If (UBound(aStrParam) > 1) Then WriteLog("FindFingerprint: Parameter is invalid.") : Exit Function strPageType = CurrentObj.Type strFingerprintCreation = Trim(aStrParam(0)) If (UBound(aStrParam) = 1) Then strPageType = Trim(aStrParam(1)) oFingerprint.m_bFingerprintCreation = False If (LCase(strFingerprintCreation)="false") Then oFingerprint.m_bFingerprintCreation = False If (LCase(strFingerprintCreation)="true") Then oFingerprint.m_bFingerprintCreation = True WriteLog("----- FindFingerprint of: "&CurrentObj.ImageName&" -----") 'RTC 179132 - Logic added to get the extension of a file and then calculate the length of extension to get the corresponding cco file name. Dim aPath Dim realExt aPath =Split(CurrentObj.ImageName,".") Dim l l=UBound(aPath) 'Get the last item of an array which will be the real extenstion of an image. realExt = aPath(l) 'Initially it was hardcoded to 3 considering image extension to be always 3 characters. 'Modified it with realExt variable which will work for any number of characters in extension. Dim strCCOFile strCCOFile = Left(CurrentObj.ImageName, Len(CurrentObj.ImageName)-Len(realExt))&"cco" WriteLog("strCCOFile :" +strCCOFile) If Not(FileMgr.FileExists(strCCOFile)) Then WriteLog("FindFingerprint skipping. CCO file doesn't exist") Exit Function End If Dim oCCO Set oCCO = CCOCreator.Load(strCCOFile ) oFingerprint.UpdateSearchArea oFingerprint.m_bBlackFingerprint = False oFingerprint.Process oCCO, CurrentObj, oFingerprint.m_ProblemValue, strPageType If oFingerprint.m_bFailRule = True Then FindFingerprint = False Else FindFingerprint = True End If WriteLog("FindFingerprint returns " & FindFingerprint)

af.name: CreateFingerprint
af.g:
' Creates a fingerprint for the current source page. The resulting fingerprint will
' consist of two files: the page's Image file (.tif) and its Processing file (.cco)."
CreateFingerprint = False
If InitAutoDocGlobalObjects=False then Exit Function
If (CurrentObj.ObjectType<>2) Then Exit Function 'must be a page
If Not(FileMgr.FileExists(CurrentObj.ImageName)) Then
WriteLog("CreateFingerprint skipping. Image file doesn't exist")
Exit Function
End If
WriteLog("----- CreateFingerprint for: "& CurrentObj.ImageName & " -----")
retn = oFingerprint.AddNewFingerprint(CurrentObj, CurrentObj.Type)
If retn = False Then
CreateFingerprint = False
Else
CreateFingerprint = True
End If
WriteLog("CreateFingerprint returns " & CreateFingerprint)

af.name: DeleteFingerprint
af.g:
'Deletes the Image file (.tif) and Processing file (.cco) of the current page's fingerprint from
'the application's fingerprint directory, and its record from the Rules database.
'A SetFingerprintDir action must precede this action."
DeleteFingerprint = True
If (CurrentObj.ObjectType<>2) Then
WriteLog("DeleteFingerprint invalid. This Action should be used on Page level Objects only")
Exit Function 'must be a page
End If
If Not(FileMgr.FileExists(CurrentObj.ImageName)) Then
WriteLog("DeleteFingerprint invalid. Image file doesn't exist")
Exit Function
End If
WriteLog("----- DeleteFingerprint for: "&CurrentObj.ImageName&" -----")
If InitAutoDocGlobalObjects=False then Exit Function
retn = oFingerprint.DeleteFingerprint(CurrentObj)
If retn <> True Then
'DeleteFingerprint = False
WriteLog("DeleteFingerprint failed, returning True")
Else
'DeleteFingerprint = True
WriteLog("DeleteFingerprint Action successful")
End If

af.name: SetFingerprint
af.g:
'Sets a newly created fingerprint's Fingerprint Class and Fingerprint Class ID values. " ' A two-part, comma-separated value consisting of:

' 1.The Fingerprint Class value. Smart parameters are supported. Alternatively, the name of the Field on this page that specifies the Fingerprint Class.
' 2.(optional) The Fingerprint ID value. Smart parameters are supported. Alternatively, the name of the Field on this page that specifies the Fingerprint ID.

SetFingerprint = False If InitAutoDocGlobalObjects=False then Exit Function 'StrParam is a CSV Value: ' (0) is the HostNameField ' (1) is the optional HostIDField ' Added support for smart parameters 'StrParam=MetaWord(StrParam) writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "'") Dim aStrParam, sHostName, sHostRefID, sTmp aStrParam = Split(StrParam, ",", 2, 1) sHostName = Trim(aStrParam(0)) If UBound(aStrParam) = 1 Then sHostRefID = Trim(aStrParam(1)) On Error Resume Next sTmp = MetaWord(sHostRefID) If (sTmp = "") Then 'Field Value Set oChild = CurrentObj.FindChild(Right(sHostRefID, Len(sHostRefID)-1)) If Not(oChild Is Nothing) Then sTmp = oChild.Text WriteLog("HostID from field") Set oChild = Nothing End If End If sHostRefID = sTmp sTmp = MetaWord(sHostName) If (sTmp = "") Then 'Field Value Set oChild = CurrentObj.FindChild(Right(sHostName, Len(sHostName)-1)) If Not(oChild Is Nothing) Then WriteLog("Hostname from field") sTmp = oChild.Text Set oChild = Nothing End If End If sHostName = sTmp If (sHostName = "" And sHostRefID = "") Then WriteLog("Host Name and Host ID are Empty.") : Exit Function sHostName = Replace(sHostName, "'", "''" ) sHostRefID = Replace(sHostRefID, "'", "''" ) if err.number <> 0 then Writelog("Setfingerprint err " & err.description) err.clear on error goto 0 SetFingerprint = oFingerprint.SetFingerprint(sHostName, sHostRefID, CurrentObj)

af.name: SetPageFingerprintID
af.g:
SetPageFingerprintID = False
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "'")
If (CurrentObj.ObjectType = 2) Then
CurrentObj.Variable("TemplateID") = StrParam
WriteLog("Setting TemplateID to: " & StrParam)
