method.name: CMISDoesFolderExist
method.qi: Tests that a folder exists on the CMIS server.
method.ap:
cmisDirectoryPath :
The folder and path to test for existence. Smart parameters are supported.
existenceResult :
If True the action will return True when the folder exists, otherwise False is returned.
If False the action will return false if the folder exists, otherwise True is returned.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
Tests that the provided directory path exists in the connected CMIS repository. This action can be configured
to return true if the folder exists or return true if the folder does not exist.
CMISDoesFolderExist("/MyFolder/AnotherFolder", True)
Returns true if "AnotherFolder" exists in the repository and returns false if it does not exist.
CMISDoesFolderExist("/MyFolder/AnotherFolder", False)
Returns false if "AnotherFolder" exists in the repository and returns true if the folder does not exist.
method.ret: existenceResult if True, then return True if folder exits. If false, return true if directory does not exist.

method.name: CMISSetVersion
method.qi: Sets the version type of the file that will be uploaded.
method.ap:
cmisVersion :
The version of the uploaded document. It must be one of the following: None, Major, Minor, CheckedOut.
If this action is not called prior to the file upload, the type of "None" will be used.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
Call this action prior to the CMISUploadFile action to set the version type of the uploaded file.
The support for versions is dependent on the target repository. Check your repository documentation
to determine which version types it supports via the CMIS interface. The supported types may also
vary based on the specific version configuration settings of your repository.
The use of this action is optional.
If this action is not called, then the type of "None" will be used for uploaded files.
CMISSetVersion("Major")
CMISUploadFile("C:\MyDir\MyFile.txt","MyFile.txt", "/MyCMISDir", "text/plain")
method.ret:
This action always returns
True.
If the type specified is invalid or if
a CMIS connection has not yet been established, then the type will default to "None".

method.name: CMISDoesFileExist
method.qi: Tests that a file exists on the CMIS server.
method.ap:
cmisFilePath :
The document and path to test for existence. Smart parameters are supported.
existenceResult :
If True the action will return True when the file exists, otherwise False is returned.
If False the action will return false if the file exists, otherwise True is returned.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
This action tests that the provided file exists in the connected CMIS repository. This action can be
configured to return true if the file exists or return true if the file does not exist.
CMISDoesFileExist("/MyFolder/MyDoc.txt", True)
Returns true if "MyDoc.txt" exists in the repository and returns false if it does not exist.
CMISDoesFileExist("/MyFolder/MyDoc.txt", False)
Returns false if "MyDoc.txt" exists in the repository and returns true if the folder does not exist.
method.ret: existenceResult if True, then return True if file exits. If false, return true if file does not exist.

method.name: CMISDeleteFolder
method.qi: Deletes a folder on the CMIS server.
method.ap:
cmisDirectoryPath :
The path of the folder to delete. Smart parameters are supported.
ignoreFailure :
Set to True to ignore any failure so the action will always return True.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
The folder must be empty for the delete to be successful.
Some, but not all, CMIS repositories have the notion of a "soft" delete where the
deletion is performed at a later time. You should assume that
once the object is deleted, that it is deleted forever. If an object is deleted,
it can only be restored if the repository provides a mechanism to restore the object.
A delete failure can be ignored by using the ignoreFailure parameter. This allows actions
to continue even if the delete should fail.
CMISDeleteFolder("/MyFolder/AnotherFolder", false)
This returns true if AnotherFolder is deleted, otherwise it returns false.
CMISDeleteFolder("/MyFolder/AnotherFolder", true)
This always returns true, even if the folder is not deleted.
method.ret:
If ignoreFailure is True, the action always returns true, even if the folder could not be deleted.
If ignoreFailure is False, the action will return true if the directory is deleted, otherwise false is returned.

method.name: CMISDeleteFile
method.qi: Deletes a file on the CMIS server.
method.ap:
cmisFilePath :
The file to delete on the CMIS server. Smart parameters are supported.
ignoreFailure :
Set to True to ignore any failure so the action will always return True.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
Deletes the specified file in the CMIS repository.
Some, but not all, repositories have the notion of a "soft" delete, which will perform the
final deletion at a later time. You should assume that
once the object is deleted, that it is deleted forever. If an object is deleted,
it can only be restored if the repository provides a mechanism to restore the object.
A delete failure can be ignored by using the ignoreFailure parameter. This allows actions
to continue even if the delete should fail.
CMISDeleteFile("/MyFolder/MyDoc.txt", false)
This returns true if MyDoc.txt is deleted, otherwise it returns false.
CMISDeleteFile("/MyFolder/MyDoc.txt", true)
This always returns true, even if the file could not be deleted.
method.ret:
if ignoreFailure is True, the action always returns true, even if the file could not be deleted.
If ignoreFailure is False, the action will return true if the file is deleted, otherwise false is returned.

method.name: CMISDownloadFile
method.qi: Download a file on the CMIS server to a local hard drive.
method.ap:
cmisFileToDownload :
The file, with the full path, to download from the CMIS repository.
fullFileNameTarget :
The path and file name for the downloaded file.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
Downloads a file from the CMIS repository to a local hard drive. The file in the repository is not changed.
If the target file exists, it will be overwritten.
CMISDownloadFile("/MyCMISDir/MyCMISFile.txt", "c:\MyLocalDir\MyLocalFile.txt")
Downloads a copy of the file MyCMISFile.txt and names it MyLocalFile.txt on the local system.
method.ret: Returns True, if the download is successful, otherwise False is returned.

method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
Creates a folder on the configured CMIS server. This action is identical to CMISCreateFolder with
the ability to specify a custom type. The standard type is cmis:folder. If your CMIS server
requires a different type, it can be specified in this action.
Note that objects created on the CMIS server may not be immediately accessible by the client.
For example, the indexing service on your CMIS server may run on a configured interval,
so your new object may not be available until the indexing service completes.
If you are having trouble accessing newly created objects, check the settings and documentation
of your CMIS server to determine when objects should become available.
CMISCreateFolderCustomType("/MyParent","MyNewFolder", "MyType")
Creates the folder "MyNewFolder" in the "MyParent" folder.
method.ret: Returns True if the folder is created, otherwise it returns false.

method.name: CMISRefreshClientCache
method.qi: Refreshes the client side cache.
method.ap:
milliseconds :
Refreshes the object local cache if it is older than the specified number of milliseconds.
A value of 0 will refresh immediately. A value of -1 will disable this refresh feature and the CMIS interface
will manage the cache itself. By default, this refresh is disabled.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
CMIS client side caching will first look into the session cache if an object already exists in the client cache.
If the desired object is found, that object will be used without contacting the repository.
It is possible that it may be a stale object.
This action will refresh the client side cache, if it is older than the time specified in the parameter
The value of 0 will refresh the cache immediately.
This action will affect all subsequent CMIS actions, refreshing each object as they are used.
Call this action with a value of -1 to disable this automatic refresh.
Typically this action does not need to be called.
It is provided in case a specific application requires a cache refresh.
If this action is not called, the CMIS interface will manage the cache as it sees fit.
Note that objects created on the CMIS server may not be immediately accessible by the client.
For example, the indexing service on your CMIS server may run on a configured interval,
so a new object may not be available until the indexing service completes.
This refresh setting will not affect components on the CMIS server such as the indexing service interval.
If you are having trouble accessing newly created objects, check the settings and documentation of
your CMIS server to determine when objects should become available.
CMISRefreshClientCache("1000")
Refreshes the client local cache if it is older than 1 second.
method.ret: Always true.

method.name: CMISLogDocumentTypes
method.qi: Logs the document types defined on the CMIS server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release.
It is recommended that you no longer use this action.
This action will query the CMIS server and log all of the server defined document types to
the RRS log, providing that logging is enabled.
This is a diagnostic action and is not intended for use in a production environment, nor is it
supported in a production environment. CMISLogin must be called prior to this action.
It may be useful for an developer to obtain this type information during application development and has no
intended use other than this limited diagnostic.
Be aware that depending on the number of types and attributes defined on the CMIS server, this action may be
slow and create a large log file.
CMISLogDocumentTypes()
method.ret: Always true.

net.qi: : IBM Datacap and IBM Automation Document Processing integration(Document Processing).
net.h:
The IBM Automation Document Processing project provides capabilities to automatically processmulti-pagePDF documentsassociated with a batch to categorizeand extract and validate data.
For example, a batch for a mortgage application might contain a multi-page PDF file containing the mortgage application form,
a PDF containing scanned pages of tax returns and a PDF containing the scanned imageof a photo ID.
These documents can be uploaded and processed together to provide context to the user correcting classification and validation errors.
Datacap Customers can take advantage of IBM Automation Document Processing by using this action library.
Datacap user can use Datacap to scan, import emails, import fax files, import file system files and send to IBM Automation Document Processing to process, fixup classification and separation and verify documents.
Using this action library Datacap user can scan and import documents, assemble batches, fixup, and upload to IBM Automation Document Processing.

method.name: DocumentProcessingConnectToFileNet

p.name: DocumentProcessingConnectionURL
p.qi: The URL to the IBM Automation Document Processing filenet server. Smart parameters are supported.

p.name: domainName
p.qi: Domain name created in filenet server.

p.name: objectStoreName
p.qi: Provides the name of the Object Store that you wish to store your documents in.

p.name: userName
p.qi: User name to login to IBM Automation Document Processing project.

p.name: userPassword
p.qi: Password to login to IBM Automation Document Processing project

method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters. All parameters are required.
method.h:
This action establishes a connection to the IBM Automation Document Processing project through Filenet API
DocumentProcessingConnectToFileNet only needs to be called once per task profile. It is typically called on a batch
level rule so it will run once per task and the settings will be used by subsequent Document Processing actions
within the task. This action will initiate a connection with the Document processing service and hence validating the credentials.
The parameters can be stored in the application settings using Datacap Application Manager in custom values and referenced using smart parameters.
If the password is stored in advanced values, it will be encrypted while saving and decrypted during action execution.
Note: the Document Processing service urls are configured using SSL and before calling this action, it must be ensured that the SSL certificate is valid and stored in the trust store.
DocumentProcessingConnectToFileNet("https://cpe.test.ibm.com/wsi/FNCEWS40MTOM/","testDomain","OS1","Testuser","password")

method.name: DocumentProcessingCreateBatch

p.name: projectID
p.qi: Project guid of the Document Processing project. Smart parameters are supported.

p.name: displayName
p.qi: A user defined string that represents a name for the batch. Smart parameters are supported.

p.name: batchType
p.qi: A user defined string that represents a type for the batch.

p.name: priority
p.qi: A user defined integer that represents the values high, medium and low. The status is only used as a filter to locate a batch.

p.name: batchGroup
p.qi: A user defined string that represents a group for the batch.

p.name: description
p.qi: A user defined string that represents description for the batch.

p.name: location
p.qi: A user defined string that represents a location for the batch.

method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters. Required parameters: displayName, batchType, batchGroup.
method.h:
This action creates a batch in the IBM Automation Document Processing project. A batch is defined as a set of documents or pages that are acquired together or need to be processed together.
When the action is successful, a unique batch id will be generated by the Document Processing service and returned to Datacap. This batch id is stored in the current DCO object as a variable named DocumentProcessingBatchID.
Additionally this batch id is also stored as an XtraBatchFieldValue named PB_DPBATCHID. So if you add a column in your engine DB with name PB_DPBATCHID, this batch id will also be stored in the DB for the particular Datacap batch.
DocumentProcessingConnectToFileNet("https://cpe.test.ibm.com/wsi/FNCEWS40MTOM/","testDomain","OS1","Testuser","password")
DocumentProcessingCreateBatch(@APPVAR(PROJ_ID), @BATCHID, "Test Batch Type", 2, "Test Batch Group", "This batch was created with Datacap", "Test location")

method.name: DocumentProcessingUploadBatch

p.name: projectID
p.qi: This field contain a GUID that represents the ID of the deployed project version in the CE server to be used for processing. Smart parameters are supported.

p.name: projectConfig
p.qi: This is a string property that contains a JSON formatted collection of configuration settings to be used for processing a document. Smart parameters are supported.

method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters. All parameters are required.
method.h:
This action uploads documents from Datacap batch to the IBM Automation Document Processing batch
If this action is called at Batch level, all the pages/documents in the batch with PDF page type will be considered for upload.
If this action is called at Document level, all the pages in the documents will be considerd for upload.
The batch id that was generated in action DocumentProcessingCreateBatch, will be used to upload the documents.
DocumentProcessingConnectToFileNet("https://cpe.test.ibm.com/wsi/FNCEWS40MTOM/","testDomain","OS1","Testuser","password")
DocumentProcessingCreateBatch(@APPVAR(PROJ_ID), @BATCHID, "Test Batch Type", 2, "Test Batch Group", "This batch was created with Datacap", "Test location")
DocumentProcessingUploadBatch()

method.name: DocumentProcessingConnectionRetry

p.name: RetryCount
p.qi: This must be an integer of 1 or greater and indicates how many times to retry a call to the IBM Automation Document Processing service, if an error occurs. If this action is not called, the retry count will default to 1.

p.name: RetryDelay
p.qi: This must be an integer of 0 or greater and indicates how many seconds to wait before retrying a failed call to the IBM Automation Document Processing service. If this action is not called, the retry delay will default to 3 seconds.

method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters.
method.h:
When communicating with the IBM Automation Document Processing service, actions will wait for the response. If no response is received within
a specific time frame, the communication will be retried. This action will customize the number of retries and the time to wait
between each communication attempt.
DocumentProcessingConnectionRetry(3,10)
This example sets the connection information and then adjusts the default retry values. The action will set the retry count value to
3 and retry delay to 10 seconds.
method.lvl: Any Level, but prior to calling other Document Processing actions.
method.ret:
True,
If parameters set properly else
False.

method.name: DocumentProcessingUpdateBatchStatus

p.name: projectID
p.qi: This field contain a GUID that represents the ID of the deployed project version in the CE server to be used for processing. Smart parameters are supported.

p.name: projectConfig
p.qi: This is a string property that contains a JSON formatted collection of configuration settings to be used for processing a document. Smart parameters are supported.

p.name: batchDisplayName
p.qi: This must be a string providing the display name of a Document Processing Batch that was previously created

method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters.
method.h:
This action can be used to retrieve the status of an ADP batch after it has has been uploaded. The status will be fetched from the ADP datastore and stored in a custom column PB_DPSTATUS in tmbatch table.
This column can then be viewed in JobMonitor along will all other attributes of the batch.
DocumentProcessingConnectToFileNet("https://cpe.test.ibm.com/wsi/FNCEWS40MTOM/","testDomain","OS1","Testuser","password")
DocumentProcessingUpdateBatchStatus(@APPVAR(PROJ_ID),@APPVAR(PROJ_CONFIG), @BATCHID)
method.ret:
True,
If parameters set properly else
False.

method.name: IBMCM_Logon
method.qi: Logs on to a IBM Content Manager server.

p.name: connectioninfo
p.qi: A comma-separated string consisting of three values: 1) the ID of the IBM Content Manager server 2) a valid Content Manager User ID 3) the user’s Password

method.ap:
A comma-separated string consisting of three values:
1) the ID of the IBM Content Manager server.
2) a valid Content Manager User ID.
3) the user’s Password.
Smart parameters are supported for each parameter.
method.h:
Performs the logon to the IBM Content Manager system. This action must be called prior to the
actions that communicate with the Content Manager repository. Connectivity, based on
the requirements of the IBM Content Manager server, needs to be
setup on the machine which is running the Datacap rules.
IBMCM_Logon("ibmcmserver,user1,password")
IBMCM_Logon("ibmcmserver,user1,+@APPVAR(values/adv/MyPassword)")
This example uses the smart parameter @APPVAR to obtain the password from the
advanced value section of the application manager. The custom value name is "MyPassword".
method.lvl: Any level. Usually used at the Batch level.
method.ret:
Action returns
True
if the log on succeeds;
False
if the log on is unsuccessful.
The log on will be unsuccessful if the action cannot find the specified server, or if the user ID or password is invalid.

method.name: IBMCM_Logoff
method.qi: Logs off from the IBM Content Manager server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Performs the logoff from the IBM Content Manager system. This action disconnects from the Content Manager datastore and destroys the reference to the datastore object.
IBMCM_Logon("ibmcmserver,user1,password")
IBMCM_Logoff()
method.ret:
Action returns
True
if the logoff succeeds;
False
if the logoff is unsuccessful.
The logoff will be unsuccessful if logon was not done and a datastore object does not exists.

method.name: IBMCM_CreateItem
method.qi: Creates a IBM CM document based on the item type.

p.name: itemtype
p.qi: Creates a IBM CM document based on the item type.

method.ap:
itemType is a string value of a valid IBM Content Manager Item Type – NOINDEX, for example.
A IBM Content Manger Item Type is equivalent to a Document Class (Index Class).
Smart parameters are supported, such as @BATCHID, @ID, @STATUS, @TYPE, @VALUE,
@JOBID, @JOBNAME, @OPERATOR, @STATION, @TASKID, @TASKNAME, etc. Please refer to
the smart parameter documentation for more information and usage.
method.h:
Creates a IBM Content Manger document based on the item type. This action needs to be called prior to the document
and page upload actions.
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will create an IBM Content Manager document based on the NOINDEX item type,
set the mime type of the uploaded document, then perform the upload.
IBMCM_CreateItem("@P.name")
This example will create an IBM Content Manager document based on the value contained inside the Smart Parameter @P.name at the page level.
Typically, there is one item for each processed document represented by a Document object of the Document Hierarchy,
or for a processed page represented by a Page object.

method.name: IBMCM_CreateChildItem
method.qi: Create a child component under the current document created using IBMCM_CreateItem

p.name: Child Item Information
p.qi: A comma-separated string consisting of two values: 1) childItemName: Create a child component. Creates a child component specified by the childItemName, under the defined object type (IBMCM_CreateItem). 2) count: The number of child component attribute values that will be set.

method.ap:
childItemName is a string value that contains the name of a valid child componet name of the item specified by IBMCM_CreateItem.
The count is the number of child component attributes values that will be set by IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue.
method.h:
This action needs to be called after IBMCM_CreateItem.
IBMCM_CreateItem("ABCInsPlc")
IBMCM_CreateChildItem("Automobiles,1")
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue("Automobiles,ABCVIN,vin123")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will create an IBM Content Manager Child Item based on the name Automobiles.

method.name: IBMCM_CreateFolder
method.qi: Creates a IBM Content Manger folder in the parent folder, based on the specified item type.

p.name: itemType
p.qi: The item type (classification) to create the IBM Content Manger folder. This parameter is required.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

p.name: hasParent
p.qi: If true then the new folder has a parent folder.

method.ap:
If hasParent is False, the new folder will be created without a parent folder and the action will ignore attribute and attributeValue.
If hasParent is true, then it is expected that this folder will be the child of an already existing
folder and that the attribute and attributeValue specify the parent.
If hasParent is true and both attribute and attributeValue are not provided then parent folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
If folder ID is used in the attributeValue parameter, leave the attribute parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported for the string type parameters.
method.ret:
True,
if the folder is successfully created. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Creates a folder in the IBM Content Manger repository. IBMCM_SetAttributeValue can be called following this action
to set attributes of the newly created folder.
Important: If the new folder is based on an item type classfication that contains attributes that are required, an application should use the IBMCM_CreateFolderEx action instead.
IBMCM_CreateFolder will create and save the folder immediately to the repository
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "", False)
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The new folder has no parent and will be placed in the root directory.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215", True)
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The folder will be placed inside the parent folder with ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
IBMCM_CreateFolder(@B.MyItemtye, @B.MyAttribute, @B.MyAttributeValue, True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,@BATCHID")
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType and
will be a child of the folder identified by values from
the batch level Smart Parameters @B.MyAttribute and @B.MyAttributeValue.
IBMCM_CreateFolder(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", False)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder1")
IBMCM_CreateFolder(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder2")
This example will create folder "MyFolder1" and folder "MyFolder2" based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType.
The folder "MyFolder1" folder has no parent. The parent of folder "MyFolder2" is folder "MyFolder1".

method.name: IBMCM_CreateFolderEx
method.qi: Creates a IBM Content Manger folder in the parent folder, based on the specified item type.

p.name: itemType
p.qi: The item type (classification) to create the IBM Content Manager folder. This parameter is required.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

p.name: hasParent
p.qi: If true then the new folder has a parent folder.

method.ap:
If hasParent is False, the new folder will be created without a parent folder and the action will ignore attribute and attributeValue.
If hasParent is true, then it is expected that this folder will be the child of an already existing
folder and that the attribute and attributeValue specify the parent.
If hasParent is true and both attribute and attributeValue are not provided then parent folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
If folder ID is used in the attributeValue parameter, leave the attribute parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported for the string type parameters.
Important: Use this action when the new folder is based on an item type classfication that contains attributes that are required.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx will create the folder in memory and the folder will be saved to the repository once the IBMCM_SaveFolder action has been called
method.ret:
True,
if the folder is successfully created. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Creates a folder in the IBM Content Manger repository. IBMCM_SetAttributeValue can be called following this action
to set attributes of the newly created folder.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx("NOINDEX", "", "", False)
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The new folder has no parent and will be placed in the root directory.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx("NOINDEX", "", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215", True)
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the NOINDEX item type.
The folder will be placed inside the parent folder with ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx(@B.MyItemtye, @B.MyAttribute, @B.MyAttributeValue, True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,@BATCHID")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create an IBM Content Manger folder based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType and
will be a child of the folder identified by values from
the batch level Smart Parameters @B.MyAttribute and @B.MyAttributeValue.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", False)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder1")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx(@B.MyItemtye, "", "", True)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,"MyFolder2")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
This example will create folder "MyFolder1" and folder "MyFolder2" based on the type identified by @B.MyItemType.
The folder "MyFolder1" folder has no parent. The parent of folder "MyFolder2" is folder "MyFolder1".

method.name: IBMCM_SaveFolder
method.qi: Saves folder data from memory to IBM Content Manager.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
IBMCM_SaveFolder is used to save folder creation data to IBM Content Manager that was produced by the call to the IBMCM_CreateFolderEx action.
IBMCM_CreateFolderEx("XYZ_ClaimFolder, "", "", False)
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("XYZ_ClaimNumber, 12345")
IBMCM_SaveFolder()
The sequence creates a folder, assigns that folder with an attribute value of 12345 to the XYZ_ClaimNumber attribute
method.ret:
True,
If the action successfully saves the folder
False
if the action is unable to save the folder.

method.name: IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder
method.qi: Set the destination folder for uploading image files to IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

method.ap:
If both parameters are not provided then destination folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
If folder ID is used in the second parameter, leave the first parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
True,
if the destination folder is successfully set. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Sets the upload destination folder in IBM Content Manger repository. To set the destination to a newly created
folder, first create the folder using IBMCM_CreateFolder and then call IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder
with empty ("") paramters.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder("Department", "Human Resource")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the folder with attribute Department="Human Resource" to upload images to it.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the folder with folder ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215 to upload images to it.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215", true)
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder("", "")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the most recently created folder to upload images to it.

method.name: IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx
method.qi: Set the destination folder for uploading image files to IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: itemType
p.qi: The item type.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or folder ID.

method.ap: If all parameters are not provided then destination folder will be set to the most recently created folder.
method.ret:
True,
if the destination folder is successfully set. Otherwise,
False.
The action fails if a folder with the specified attribute or ID is not found.
method.h:
Sets the upload destination folder in IBM Content Manger repository. To set the destination to a newly created
folder, first create the folder using IBMCM_CreateFolder and then call IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx
with empty ("") paramters.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx allows the application to specify an Attribute, Attribute value combination associated with a specific item type, whereas IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder only
allowed an application to specify only an Attribute and Attribute value combination.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx does not support specifying just an item ID, use IBMCM_SetDestinationFolder instead.
IBMCM_SetDestinationFolderEx("NOINDEX","SOURCE","Human Resource")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will set the destination folder to the folder with attribute Department="Human Resource" to upload images to it.

method.name: IBMCM_SetAttributeValue
method.qi: Sets the attribute value on an IBM Content Manager document or IBM Content Manager folder.

p.name: attributesvalues
p.qi: Sets the attribute value on an IBM Content Manager document or IBM Content Manager folder.

method.ap:
attributesvalues is a string value of two comma separated variables.
Name :
The name of the attribute to set.
Value :
The value of the attribute.
An IBM Content Manager Item Type is equivalent to a Document Class (Index Class).
Smart parameters are supported, such as @BATCHID, @ID, @STATUS, @TYPE, @VALUE,
@JOBID, @JOBNAME, @OPERATOR, @STATION, @TASKID, @TASKNAME, etc. Please refer to
the smart parameter documentation for more information and usage.
method.h:
Sets the attribute value on an IBM Content Manager document or folder. The specified attribute must already
be defined on the IBM Content Manager server. The attribute can be applied to a document or to a folder.
This action must follow a previous action that created or identified a folder or document.
This action can be called multiple times to set multiple attributes of the same document or folder.
After the last call to this action, you must call IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC, IBMCM_UploadDCO_Page, or IBMCM_Update actions
to persist the changes to the document item in the Content Manager server.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("MyFolderItemType")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Name,@BATCHID")
This example will create an IBM Content Manager folder and then set the "Name"
property of the folder to the ID of the current batch.
IBMCM_CreateItem("@B.name")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Author,@D.TheAuthor")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Date,@DATE")
Assuming this is running on the document level, this will create a new document using the batch
level value stored in the DCO variable "name" and set the "Author" attribute to the value stored
in the DCO document level variable named "TheAuthor", then it stores the current date in the
"Date" property.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "3F1234D")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("FirstName,Thomas")
This example will search the IBM Content Manager repository for an existing IBM Content Manager document with EmployeeID=3F1234D.
If the existing IBM Content Manager document is found then its attribute "FirstName" will be set to "Thomas".
To set a DATE attribute, make sure the date value is in one of the date formats accepted by IBM Content Manager.
The valid date formats include:
"yyyy-MM-dd"
"yyyy/MM/dd"
"MM-dd-yyyy"
"MM/dd/yyyy"
You can reformat a date field by calling Validations.IsFieldDateWithReformat on the current field.
Note that the smart parameter @DATE defaults to using the "MM/dd/yyyy" format and does not need to be reformatted.
IsFieldDateWithReformat("yyyy/MM/dd")

method.name: IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue
method.qi: Assigns a child attribute value for a child item. (child component attribute value)

p.name: Child Attribute Information
p.qi: A comma-separated string consisting of three values: 1) childItemName: Create a child component. Creates a child component specified by the childItemName, under the defined object type (IBMCM_CreateItem). 2) attributeName: The attribute name of the child 3) attributeValue: The attribute value

method.ap:
IBMCM_CreateChildItem must be called prior.
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue must be called the same number of times that is specified in IBMCM_CreateChildItem otherwise the child attributes will not be saved
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action needs to be called after IBMCM_CreateItem.
IBMCM_CreateItem("ABCInsPlc")
IBMCM_CreateChildItem("Automobiles,2")
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue("Automobiles,ABCVIN,vin123")
IBMCM_SetChildAttributeValue("Automobiles,ABCLicensePlate,carlic123")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This example will create an IBM Content Manager Child Item based on the name Automobiles and assigns two attributes

method.name: IBMCM_UploadDCO_Page
method.qi: Uploads Image files associated with the current Page object of the Document Hierarchy to IBM Content Manager.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Uploads the Image file associated with current Page object of the Document Hierarchy to the IBM Content Manager server.
Additionally, all attributes set using IBMCM_SetAttributeValue will also be persisted.
IBMCM_Logon("cmserver,adminPWD,adminUID")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("USERID, @OPERATOR")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_Page()
This sequence uploads Image files associated with the current Page object of the Document Hierarchy
to IBM Content Manager, and assigns the name of the object – the value of its Type property.
method.ret:
True,
If the action successfully sends the image to the server;
False
if the action is unable to save the image.

method.name: IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC
method.qi: Uploads the set of Images files associated with the current document object of the Document Hierarchy to the IBM Content Manager server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Uploads the Image file(s) associated with current Document object of the Document Hierarchy to IBM Content Manager server.
IBMCM_Logon("cmserver,adminPWD,adminUID")
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("USERID, @OPERATOR")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
This sequence uploads the set of Images files associated with the current document object
of the Document Hierarchy to the IBM Content Manager server.
Additionally, all attributes set using IBMCM_SetAttributeValue will also be persisted.

method.name: IBMCM_Update
method.qi: Updates the current document object to the IBM Content Manager server.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Updates the current document object and its attributes to IBM Content Manager server.
All attributes set using IBMCM_SetAttributeValue will be persisted into the latest version of the document item.
If the document item type has enabled versioning to 'always create new version', then a new version will be create with the changes.
The document item was checked out by the
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue
, and will be checked in by this action.
IBMCM_Logon("cmserver,adminPWD,adminUID")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("USERID, @OPERATOR")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("SOURCE, DATACAP")
IBMCM_Update()
method.lvl: Page level or the field level.

method.name: IBMCM_StoreItemIDinDCO
method.qi: Stores the Item ID of the most recently created folder or most recently uploaded IBM Content Manager item into a variable of the current object of the Document Hierarchy.

p.name: itemID
p.qi: Sets the attribute value on a CM document or folder.

method.h:
Stores the Item ID of the most recently created folder or most recently uploaded
IBM Content Manager document into a variable of the current object of the DCO Hierarchy.
If the variable does not exist, it will be created on the current DCO Hierarchy object.
It may be useful to store the item ID if the object needs to be referenced in following action,
such as setting the upload destination directory.
IBMCM_CreateFolder("NOINDEX", "", "", False)
IBMCM_StoreItemIDinDCO("ItemID")
The action above stores the ID of the new IBM Content Manger folder in a variable called “ItemID” in the current object of the DCO Hierarchy.
IBMCM_CreateItem("NOINDEX")
IBMCM_SetMimeType("image/tiff")
IBMCM_UploadDCO_DOC()
IBMCM_StoreItemIDinDCO("ItemID")
The action above stores the ID of the new IBM Content Manger document in a variable called “ItemID” in the current object of the DCO Hierarchy.
method.ret:
True,
if the Item ID is returned successfully, otherwise
False.

method.name: IBMCM_SearchItem
method.qi: Search for the existing item in IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: attribute
p.qi: The attribute name.

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: The unique attribute value or item ID.

method.ap:
Both attribute and attributeValue are required parameters.
If item ID is used in the second parameter, leave the first parameter empty ("").
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Searches for the existing item in IBM Content Manger repository that matches the specified attribute and value.
If an item is found, the current item will be set to it. Otherwise the current item will be set to NULL.
See
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems
action to specify whether to search for folder items only.
By default,
IBMCM_SearchItem
searches only folder items.
IBMCM_SearchItem is used to retrieve a existing IBM Content Manger item before calling other actions to update its attributes
or its content such as IBMCM_AddPages, IBMCM_DeletePages, IBMCM_ReplacePage, IBMCM_SetAttributeValue....
IBMCM_SearchItem("Department", "Human Resource")
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue("Department", "Operations")
This example will search for a folder item with attribute Department="Human Resource" and change to "Operations".
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems("False")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
This example will search for a folder item or a non-folder item with the item ID: A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems("True")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "@P.PageName")
This example will search only for a folder item with item ID derived from a predefined smart parameter, @P.PageName.
The
VScan.Scan
action populates
@P.PageName
to be the filename of the image file without the file extension.
For example, the image file A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.tif will have a PageName of "A1001001A17E08B00210C00000".
This smart parameter can be used to identify the CM8 item ID if the image file name conforms to the convention.

method.name: IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
method.qi: Search and download item content from IBM Content Manger repository.
method.ret:
False,
if any error occurred during parameter validation or searching or downloading.
Otherwise,
True
.
method.h:
Searches for items in IBM Content Manger repository that matches the specified search criteria from the
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria
action.
For each matching item found, if the corresponding ICMBase parts have content,
the content file will be written to the directory set from
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory
.
The output file name will be the CM8 item ID, and the file extension will be the same as the original file extension.
If the original file did not have a file extension, the default extension will be ".tif".
If the file already exists, it will be overwritten.
To limit the number of downloads for each IBMCM_SearchAndDownload action, you can set a limit with
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum
action. The default maximum is 1000.
To add sorting, call
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort
.
To update a download status attribute for the downloaded item, call
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute
action.
After
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
has downloaded the CM8 content files,
scan()
action can be called
to read the files from the same directory.
Important:
to prevent downloading duplicate item content, the task that calls IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownload action should not
be run in a multi-threaded configuration. Instead, use single-threaded tasks.
For information about configuring threads in Rulerunner, see Configuring Rulerunner to run tasks.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT",,,,)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("100")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort("True","Date","ASCENDING")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute("DCStatus")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
SetSourceDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
Scan()
This example will search and download up to 100 APT CM items' content to the directory, C:\datacap\APT\images\input.
The CM query syntax is "/APT [ICMPARTS AND (@DCStatus IS NULL OR @DCStatus=0)] SORTBY(@Date ASCENDING)".
Each item content will have the item ID as the file name. For example, A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.tif.
When the scan() action runs, it will see the populated image directory and process as usual.
method.see:
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute
Scan

method.name: IBMCM_AddPages
method.qi: Add new page(s) to the existing document in IBM Content Manger repository. The new page(s) will be appended to the existing page(s) in the IBM Content Manger document.

p.name: newPage
p.qi: The new page to add.

method.ap:
newPage is required when calling the action at document level.
If newPage = 0, all new pages in the runtime DCO will be added to the existing IBM Content Manger document.
If newPage > 0, only the new page specified by newPage is added.
method.h:
Need to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document from IBM Content Manger repository before calling this action to add new page(s) to it.
The IBMCM_SearchItem action can be used to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "A1001001A14B04B12546D00215")
IBMCM_AddPages(2)
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique ID=A1001001A14B04B12546D00215.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will add the second page (TM000002) in the runtime Document DCO to the existing IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_AddPages(0)
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will add all new pages in the runtime Document DCO to the existing IBM Content Manger document.

method.name: IBMCM_DeletePages
method.qi: Delete page(s) from an existing document in IBM Content Manger repository.

p.name: existingPage
p.qi: The existing page to be deleted. This parameter is required.

method.ap:
existingPage is required when calling the action at document level.
If existingPage = 0, all existing pages in the IBM Content Manger document will be deleted. Otherwise, only the existing page specified by existingPage will be deleted.
method.h:
Need to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document from IBM Content Manger repository before calling this action to delete page(s) from it.
The IBMCM_SearchItem action can be used to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document.
Important Notes:
Be careful with this destructive action. It should be used at the batch level to make sure it will be executed once per batch.
If you need to use it at the document or page level, make sure you set filters/conditions to avoid this action being called repeatly.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_DeletePages(2)
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will delete the second page from the IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_DeletePages(0)
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will delete all existing pages from the IBM Content Manger document.

method.name: IBMCM_ReplacePage
method.qi: Replace an existing page in the IBM Content Manger document with a new page in the runtime DCO hierarchy.

p.name: existingPage
p.qi: The existing page in IBM Content Manger document.

p.name: newPage
p.qi: The new page in runtime DCO hierarchy.

method.ap:
When calling at document level, both existingPage and newPage parameter are required.
When calling at page level, the newPage parameter is ignored.
method.h:
Need to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document from IBM Content Manger repository before calling this action.
The IBMCM_SearchItem action can be used to retrieve the existing IBM Content Manger document.
IBMCM_SearchItem("EmployeeID", "14B04B12")
IBMCM_ReplacePage(2,3)
This example will search the IBM Content Manger repository for the existing IBM Content Manger document with unique attribute EmployeeID=14B04B12.
If the existing IBM Content Manger document is found, it will replace the second page in the existing IBM Content Manger document with the third page (TM000003) in the runtime Document DCO.

This example will set mime type to "image/tiff".

method.name: IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems
method.qi: Prepares the IBMCM_SearchItem action whether to limit the searches to only folder items.

p.name: strParam
p.qi: True or False

method.ap:
A string or smart parameter value "True" or "False" whether the subsequent IBMCM_SearchItem actions
will limit the result to folder items. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
If "True", the subsequent IBMCM_SearchItem actions will only search for folder items.
If "False", the subsequent IBMCM_SearchItem actions will search for all items that match the search criteria.
If this action is not called or the parameter is not "True" or "False", the default value of "True" will be used, and IBMCM_SearchItem actions will only return folder items. This action should be called before IBMCM_SearchItem.
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems("False")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "A1001001A17E08B00210C00000")
This example will search for an item with item ID A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.
If an item is found, regardless of whether it is a folder item or not,
the current item will be set to it.
Otherwise if the item is not found,
the current item will be set to NULL.
IBMCM_SetSearchOnlyFolderItems("True")
IBMCM_SearchItem("", "@P.PageName")
This example will search only for a folder item.
If a folder item is found, the current item will be set to it.
Otherwise if the item is not found or the item is not a folder item,
the current item will be set to NULL.
This example also demonstrates the use of the predefined smart parameter @PageName.
The VScan.Scan action populates @P.PageName to be the filename of the image file without the file extension.
For example, the image file A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.tif will have a PageName of "A1001001A17E08B00210C00000". This smart parameter can be used to identify the CM8 item ID if the image file name conforms to the convention.

method.name: IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria
method.qi: Sets the search criteria for IBMCM_SearchAndDownload action.

p.name: itemType
p.qi: Name of the item type

p.name: attributeName
p.qi: Name of the attribute

p.name: comparisonOperator
p.qi: Comparison operator

p.name: attributeValue
p.qi: Comparison value of the attribute

p.name: dataType
p.qi: Data type of the attribute

method.ap:
Item type name
is mandatory. The search will be limited to the specified item type.
The rest of the parameters are optional. If they are not provided,
then the search will return all items from the specified item type.
If the
attribute name
is specified, the item attribute must exist in the IBM Content Manager repository schema.
If the
comparison operator
is not specified, but the attribute name and value are specified,
then the comparisonOperator defaults to the equal operator, "=". Supported comparison operators are:
"="," < "," < ="," > "," > =","!=","LIKE","NOT LIKE","IS NULL","IS NOT NULL","IN","NOT IN".
The
comparison value of the attribute
is mandatory if the
attribute name
is specified.
For "IS NULL" and "IS NOT NULL" operations, the attribute value and the data type are ignored.
For "LIKE" and "NOT LIKE" operations, the attribute value should include the wildcard character "%".
For "IN" and "NOT IN" operations, the attribute value should be enclosed in parentheses "()" and delimited by commas. See examples below.
The
data type of the attribute
is optional. Supported data types are: "STRING", "DATE", "NUMBER".
The default is "STRING".
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.ret:
False,
if parameters are not strings or parameter validations failed. Otherwise,
True.
Some parameter validations are done in this action, others are done in the IBMCM_SearchAndDownload() action.
method.h:
The parameters will be used in IBMCM_SearchAndDownload action to construct the IBM Content Manager query.
If this action is not called and the search criteria has not been set before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload(),
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload() will return False. This action should be called before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT",,,,)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("100")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
This example will search and download up to 100 APT CM items' content to the directory, C:\datacap\APT\images\input, with no sorting.
The CM query syntax is "/APT [ICMPARTS]". Each item content will have the item ID as the file name.
For example, A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.tif
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT", "APT_Flag","=","NA",)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort("False",,)
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
This example will search and download up to the default maximum number of APT CM items'
content that have not been processed by Datacap into the Smart Parameter VScan image directory.
The CM query syntax is "/APT[ICMPARTS AND @APT_Flag="NA"]". Each item content will have the item ID as the file name.
The file extension will be the same as the file extension of the original file.
For example, A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.jpg
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT", "Quantity",">","5", "NUMBER")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT", "DCStatus","IS NULL",,)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT", "DCStatus","LIKE","start%",)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT", "DCStatus","IN","("started","stopped")",)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT", "Date",">","2017-01-01","DATE")
These are usage examples of the supported data type and comparison operators.

method.name: IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory
method.qi: Sets the download directory for SearchAndDownload action.

p.name: path
p.qi: The directory where the downloaded files will reside

method.ap:
The parameter will be used as the download directory in
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
action.
The output directory is mandatory. You must verify that the directory is valid and has write permissions.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
True,
if parameter is a string. Otherwise,
False.
The directory will not be verified until the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
attempts to write to the directory.
method.h:
If this action is not called and the download directory has not been set before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload(),
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload() will return False. This action must be called before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload to set the output directory.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT",,,)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("100")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
This example will search and download up to 100 APT CM items' content to the directory, C:\datacap\APT\images\input.
The CM query syntax is "/APT [ICMPARTS] SORTBY(@ITEMID ASCENDING)". Each item content will have the item ID as the file name.
For example, A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.tif
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT", "APT_Flag","=","NA")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("@APPPATH(vscanimagedir)")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort("True","Date","ASCENDING")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
This example will search and download up to the default maximum number of APT CM items'
content that have not been processed by Datacap into the Smart Parameter VScan image directory.
The CM query syntax is "/APT[ICMPARTS AND @APT_Flag="NA"] SORTBY(@Date ASCENDING)". Each item content will have the item ID as the file name. The file extension will be the same as the file extension of the original file.
For example, A1001001A17E08B00210C00000.jpg

method.name: IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum
method.qi: Sets the maximum number of downloads for SearchAndDownload action.

p.name: strParm
p.qi: The maximum number of downloads

method.ap:
The strParm sets the maximum number of downloads in the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
action.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
If this action is not called and the download maximum has not been set before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload(),
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload() will use the default maximum, which is 1000. Specify a number less than 1 to have no maximum, and IBMCM_SearchAndDownload() will return all matching items.
This action should be called before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload to change the maximum download.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT",,,)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("100")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
This example will search and download up to 100 APT CM items' content to the directory, C:\datacap\APT\images\input.
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
Since this action was not called, the default maximum will be used. This example will search and download up to 1000 of content matching the IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria parameters.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("0")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
Since the maximum is zero, there will not be a limit to the search. This example will search and download all
content matching the IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria parameters.

method.name: IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort
method.qi: Sets the sortby and sort order for SearchAndDownload action.

p.name: doSort
p.qi: True or False to sort

p.name: sortBy
p.qi: Item attribute name to sort by

p.name: sortOrder
p.qi: Sort order ASCENDING or DESCENDING

method.ap:
The
doSort
parameter takes "True" or "False" and determines whether to sort the search results
during the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
action.
The
sortBy
parameter is the name of the item attribute to sort by. The item attribute must exist in the CM8 repository schema.
The
sortOrder
parameter takes "ASCENDING" or "DESCENDING" and determines the sort order of the sort by attribute.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
If this action is not called and the sort information has not been set before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload(),
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload() will not sort the returned results.
This action should be called before IBMCM_SearchAndDownload to change the sort information.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT","Date","IS NULL",)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("100")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadSort("True","Date","ASCENDING")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
This example will search and download up to 100 APT CM items' content to the directory, C:\datacap\APT\images\input, sorted by the "Date" attribute in ascending order.
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
Since this action was not called, no sorting will be done. This example will search and download
content matching the IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria parameters.

method.name: IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute
method.qi: Sets the status attribute to update after a successful SearchAndDownload action.

p.name: checkStatus
p.qi: True or False whehter to add checking for download status

p.name: attributeName
p.qi: The Datacap download status attribute name

method.ap:
The
checkStatus
parameter takes "True" or "False" and determines whether to check the download status
of an item during the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
action.
The
attribute
must exist and must be defined for the SearchAndDownload item type as a short integer,
with no default. The attribute name is case-sensitive and must be the same as defined in the CM8 System Administration Client.
The default behavior is
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute("False",).
Setting a status attribute is not required for the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
action.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.ret:
True,
if parameters are string. Otherwise,
False.
The attribute will not be verified until the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
attempts to update the status attribute value.
method.h:
The status attribute will be used two times during the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
action.
First, the search criteria will be appended to search for the attribute being 0 or NULL.
Second, when an item has been downloaded, the attribute will be updated to 1. Note that
if the document item type has enabled versioning to 'always create new version',
then a new version will be create with the changes.
Having a status attribute for the download is beneficial to avoid downloading duplicates with the
same search criteria between batches.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT",,,,)
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadMaximum("100")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadDirectory("C:\datacap\APT\images\input")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute("True", "DCStatus")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
In this example, the CM query syntax is "/APT [ICMPARTS AND (@DCStatus IS NULL OR @DCStatus=0)] ".
During each bach, 100 items will be downloaded and their attributes changed to @DCStatus=1.
Subsequent batches using the
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload
action will not return any items that have already been downloaded, since
the DCStatus is no longer null.
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT","Date"," < ","2017-01-01","DATE")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute("True","DCStatus")
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
In this example, the CM query syntax is "/APT [ICMPARTS AND @Date < "2017-01-01" AND (@DCStatus IS NULL OR @DCStatus=0)] ".
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadCriteria("APT","APT_Date"," < ","2017-01-01","DATE")
IBMCM_SetSearchAndDownloadStatusAttribute("False",)
IBMCM_SearchAndDownload()
In this example, the CM query syntax is "/APT [ICMPARTS AND @APT_Date < "2017-01-01"] ".
No checking is done whether the item has been downloaded by Datacap before. Unless you do want to be able to download items
that have been downloaded by Datacap before, we recommend that the application
call
IBMCM_SetAttributeValue()
to update the @APT_Date value to prevent the item from matching the criteria
next time.

af.name: SetPageType
af.g:
Dim PageObj
Dim sNode
Dim bNode
Dim sType
StrParam = MetaWord(Trim(StrParam))
SetPageType = False
Set PageObj = CurrentObj
While PageObj.ObjectType > 2
Set PageObj = PageObj.Parent
If PageObj.ObjectType = 0 Then
Writelog("No Page Object Found.")
Exit Function
End If
Wend
status = PageObj.Status
bNode = False
'Ensure Min Length requirement
If Len(Trim(StrParam))>0 Then
'replace dbl quotes with single
sNode = Replace(StrParam,Chrw(34),Chrw(39))
'Check If quoted value
If Left(Trim(sNode),1)=Chrw(39) And Right(Trim(sNode),1)=Chrw(39) Then
sNode = Trim(Replace(StrParam,Chrw(39),""))
'Check If self
If sNode = CurrentObj.Type Then
Writelog("Current Object is Search Type.")
If(Trim(CurrentObj.Text) <> "") Then
sType = CurrentObj.Text
bNode = True
Writelog("Node is CurrentObj. New Value is " & sType)
End If
End If
'Check If Child of Self
If Not(bNode) Then
Set iChild = CurrentObj.FindChild(sNode)
If Not(iChild Is Nothing) Then
Writelog("Child Object is Search Type.")
If(Trim(iChild.Text) <> "" ) Then
sType = iChild.Text
bNode = True
debuglog("Node is Property Object. New Value is " & sType)
End If
End If
End If
'Check If Variable of Self
If Not(bNode) Then
If CurrentObj.FindVariable(sNode) >= 0 Then
Writelog("Current Object Variable is Search Type.")
If(Trim(CurrentObj.Variable(sNode)) <> "" ) Then
sType = CurrentObj.Variable(sNode)
bNode = True
debuglog("Node is Property Object. New Value is " & sType)
End If
End If
End If
Else
'Assign PageType as StrParam
sType = StrParam
bNode = True
End If
End If
If(PageObj.ObjectType = 2) And bNode Then PageObj.Type = sType
PageObj.Status = CLng(status)
SetPageType = bNode

f.name: ChkLastDCOTypeEx
f.g:
Dim oParent
Dim nCurIndex
Dim nPrevIndex
Dim oPrevObj
Dim bIgnorePage
On Error Resume Next
ChkLastDCOTypeEx = FALSE
prevPageToMatch = Trim(prevPageToMatch)
ignoreTypes = Trim(ignoreTypes)
If (Not IsNumeric(chkObjLevel)) OR (CInt(chkObjLevel) < 0) OR (CInt(chkObjLevel) > 3) Then chkObjLevel = 0
chkObjLevel = CInt(chkObjLevel)
If CurrentObj.ObjectType = DCO_BATCH Then
Writelog("Calling Object is ROOT object for BATCH.")
Exit Function
End if
Set oParent = CurrentObj.Parent()
If oParent is Nothing then
Writelog("No Parent Object Returned.")
Exit Function
End if
strDCOType = oParent.Type
Writelog("Parent Type is: '" & strDCOtype & "'.")
nCurrIndex = oParent.FindChildIndex(CurrentObj.ID)
nPrevIndex = nCurrIndex - 1
Do While (nPrevIndex > -1)
bIgnorePage = False
Set oPrevObj = oParent.GetChild(nPrevIndex)
strDCOtype = oPrevObj.Type
If chkObjLevel <> 0 AND oPrevObj.ObjectType <> chkObjLevel Then
bIgnorePage = TRUE
ElseIf ignoreTypes <> "" Then
For Each ignoreType in Split(ignoreTypes, ",")
If strDCOtype = Trim(ignoreType) Then bIgnorePage = TRUE : Exit For
Next
End If
If Not bIgnorePage Then Writelog("Prev Obj Type is: '" & strDCOtype & "'.") : Exit Do
nPrevIndex = nPrevIndex - 1
Loop
If (strDCOType = prevPageToMatch) Then ChkLastDCOTypeEx = TRUE
WriteLog("DCO last type: " & strDCOType & "; Returning: " & ChkLastDCOTypeEx)
Set oParent = Nothing
Set oPrevObj = Nothing

Dim NameIndex

Writelog("Document Object Detected")

For i = 1 to nChildren
If oDocSetupNode.RuleObjectType(i-1)=3 then

'check if field already exists add second field type(?) << no just skip!
' NameIndex = 0

' NameIndex = NameIndex+1

oChildName=oChildNode.Name

f.name: AddDCONode
f.g:
'"Adds new Node (Document, Page or Field) to the Runtime DCO"
On Error Resume Next
AddDCONode=True
Dim oChild
ID=trim(ID)
ID=MetaWord(ID)
NameType=trim(NameType)
NameType=MetaWord(NameType)
ObjectType=trim(ObjectType)
ObjectType=MetaWord(ObjectType)
If ObjectType="" then ObjectType=3
bBadOT=False
If Not(Isnumeric(ObjectType)) then
bBadOT=True
Else
If (clng(ObjectType)<>3) or (clng(ObjectType)<>2) or (clng(ObjectType)<>1) then bBadOT=True
End if
If bBadOT=True then
Writelog("ObjectType Parameter must be a Numeric value of 1,2 or 3. Defaulting value to '3' (Field).")
ObjectType=3
Else
ObjectType=clng(ObjectType)
End if
Status=trim(Status)
Status=MetaWord(Status)
If Status="" then Status="0"
If Not(Isnumeric(Status)) then
Writelog("Status Parameter must be Numeric. Defaulting value to '0' (Zero).")
Status="0"
End if
Index=trim(Index)
Index=MetaWord(Index)
If Index="" then Index=-1
If Not(Isnumeric(Index)) then
Writelog("Index Parameter must be Numeric. Defaulting value to '-1'.")
Index=-1
Else
Index=clng(Index)
End if
If CurrentObj.FindChildIndex(ID)<0 then
If Index>clng(CurrentObj.NumOfChildren) then Index=-1
Set oChild = CurrentObj.AddChild(ObjectType, ID, Index)
If IsAlive(oChild) then
oChild.Type = NameType
oChild.Variable("STATUS")=Status
Else
AddDCONode=False
End if
Else
Writelog("A DCO Node with ID of " & ID & " exists. No action taken.")
End if
If len(CurrentObj.GetLastError())>0 then writelog("Log:" & CurrentObj.GetLastError())
If Err.number<>0 then AddDCONode=False

af.g:
Dim nNumOfChildren

Dim nVarCounter
Dim sVarname
On Error Resume Next
ClearDCO = False
nObjCounter = 0
nVarCounter = 0
'Clear/Remove all Fields & Characters
nNumOfChildren = CurrentObj.NumOfChildren
Writelog("Child Objects to Delete:'" & nNumOfChildren & "'")
For nIndex = nNumOfChildren to 1 Step -1
If CurrentObj.Deletechild(nIndex-1)=True then
nObjCounter = nObjCounter + 1
End if
Next 'nIndex
Writelog("Child Objects Deleted: '" & nObjCounter & "'")
'Clear/Remove all Variables
nNumOfVars = CurrentObj.NumOfVars
Writelog("Variables to Delete:'" & nNumOfVars & "'")

ClearDCO = True
Else
Writelog("Deleted Counts do not match Child + Variable count.")
End if
ErrorHandler("End Function ClearDCO")

af.name: ChkConfidence
af.g:
Dim aStrParam
Dim MinLevel
Dim LCStatus
Dim HCStatus
Dim bExit
Dim nChildren
Dim dNodeDict
Dim oSetupDCO
Dim oChild
Dim RegEx
Dim sReqConf
Dim i
On Error Resume Next
ChkConfidence=True
aStrParam = Split(StrParam & ",,",",")
MinLevel = trim(MetaWord(aStrParam(0)))
LCStatus = trim(MetaWord(aStrParam(1)))
writelog("Param: '" & MinLevel & "','" & LCStatus &"'")
If Not IsNumeric(MinLevel) then MinLevel=-1
If cint(MinLevel)<1 or cint(MinLevel)>10 then
Writelog("First Parameter 'MinLevel' must be a numeric value between 1 and 10.")
bExit = True
End if
If Not IsNumeric(LCStatus) and len(LCStatus)>0 then
Writelog("Second Parameter 'Low Confidence Status' must be numeric.")
bExit = True
End if
Writelog("Pages with status Failed (" & cstr(nFail) & ") will NOT be checked for low confidence fields.")
ChkStatus=""
For i = 2 to Ubound(aStrParam)
If len(Trim(aStrParam(i)))>0 And isNumeric(Trim(aStrParam(i))) Then
ChkStatus = ChkStatus & trim(aStrParam(i)) & ","
Writelog("Pages with status '" & aStrParam(i) & "' will be checked for low confidence fields.")
End if
Next 'i
If len(ChkStatus)=0 then
Writelog("Pages with status '" & cstr(nPass) & "' will be checked for low confidence fields.")
ChkStatus=nPass & ","
End if
If bExit = True then
ChkConfidence=False
Exit Function
End if
'Populate Dictionary object with list of Fields and ReqConf pattern value.
Set dNodeDict = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
Set oSetupDCO = DCO.SetupObject
Writelog("Reading Setup DCO confidence settings...")
For i = 1 to oSetupDCO.NumOfNodes(3)
Set oChild = oSetupDCO.GetNode(3,i-1)
If oChild is Nothing then
Writelog(Space(5) & "Child " & i & " returned as Nothing")
Else
If cstr(oChild.Variable("STATUS"))<>"-1" then
sReqConf = Trim(oChild.Variable("ReqConf"))
If IsNumeric(sReqConf) Then
Call dNodeDict.Add(oChild.Name,"[" & sReqConf-1 & "-9]*")
Writelog(Space(5) & "Child '" & ochild.Name & "' added to dictionary. ReqConf: [" & sReqConf & "-9].")
Else
Call dNodeDict.Add(oChild.Name,"[" & MinLevel-1 & "-9]*")
Writelog(Space(5) & "Child '" & ochild.Name & "' added to dictionary. ReqConf: [" & MinLevel & "-9].")
End if
End if
End if
Next 'i
Set oSetupDCO = Nothing
Set oChild = Nothing
Writelog("---------------------------------------------")
Set RegEx = CreateObject("VBScript.RegExp")
'Loop through DCO tree
ChkConfidence = EvalDCOConf(CurrentObj, LCStatus, ChkStatus, dNodeDict, RegEx)
Set dNodeDict = Nothing
Set RegEx = Nothing

af.name: SetFldConfidence
af.g:
Dim sFieldName 'String of the field name to change, (empty means current field.???)
Dim sNewConf 'Confidence Level 1 - 10. Sets all confidence characters to this value.
Dim aParam 'Split Input "field name" "Confidence"
Dim numChars 'Length of the value which implies the length of the confidence string.
On Error Resume Next
' If setting of the confidence fails, we will still return success, but log that the confidence
' was not adjusted.
SetFldConfidence = True
' A little trick to guarantee that there are two parameters by appending an extra blank parameter.
' Default the 2nd parameter to 10 if only a single parameter is passed in.
aParam = Split(StrParam & ",10",",")
' Pull out the 1st and 2nd parameters
sFieldName = trim(aParam(0))
sNewConf = trim(MetaWord(aParam(1)))
writelog("Param: '" & sFieldName & "','" & sNewConf &"'")
If (sFieldName = "") Then
WriteLog("Field Parameter is empty. Character confidence values were not changed.")
exit function
End If
' Validate that sNewConf is 1 or 2 characters
numChars = Len(sNewConf)
if ((NumChars <> 1) and (NumChars <> 2)) Then
WriteLog("Field Parameter length is wrong, must be value 1-10:" & sNewConf)
WriteLog("Character confidence values for field: " & sFieldName & " were not changed!")
exit function
End If
' Validate that cConfidence is between 1 and 10
if (not IsNumeric(sNewConf)) Then
WriteLog("Field Parameter must be a single digit:" & sNewConf)
WriteLog("Character confidence values for field: " & sFieldName & " were not changed!")
exit function
End If
iConfidence = CInt(sNewConf) - 1
if ((iConfidence < 0) or (iConfidence > 9)) Then
WriteLog("Field Parameter must be a 1-10:" & sNewConf)
WriteLog("Character confidence values for field: " & sFieldName & " were not changed!")
exit function
End If
Set oDcoObj = DCONav(sFieldName)
' Check that oDcoObj is not empty, Not Null and nothing
if (not IsAlive(oDcoObj)) then
WriteLog("Could not locate field:" & sFieldName & ". Character confidence values were not changed!")
oDcoObj = NULL
Exit Function
End If
WriteLog("Located Field: " & sFieldName & " containing value: " & oDcoObj.text)
WriteLog("Original Confidence: " & oDcoObj.ConfidenceString & ". New character confidence: " & iConfidence)
' Obtain the length of the field so we can set the confidence for each character.
numChars = len(CurrentObj.Text)
' Set new confidence value
oDcoObj.ConfidenceString = String(clng(numChars), trim(cStr(iConfidence)))
Call ErrorHandler("SetFldConfidence")
oDcoObj = NULL

f.name: IsDocumentCountMoreThan
f.g:
' count = comparison value Supports smart paramaters
' returnTrueIfMore - True returns true if more, false returns false if more.
on error resume next
IsDocumentCountMoreThan = false
count = MetaWord(count)
returnTrueIfMore = MetaWord(returnTrueIfMore)
writelog "Count = " & count & ". returnTrueIfMore = " & returnTrueIfMore
set oParent= currentobj
'write log "starting object " & currentobj.type
do while oParent.objecttype>0
writelog "parent was" & oparent.type
set oParent=oParent.parent
loop
writelog "ending object type " & oParent.type & oParent.numofchildren
docTotal = 0
for i=0 to oParent.numofchildren-1
if err.number > 0 then
writelog err.description
end if
if oParent.getchild(i).objecttype =1 then
docTotal =docTotal + 1
writelog "Doc ID" & oParent.getchild(i).ID
end if
i=i+1
next 'i
if cint(docTotal)>cint(count) then
IsDocumentCountMoreThan = true
end if
if (LCase(returnTrueIfMore) = "false") then
IsDocumentCountMoreThan = NOT(IsDocumentCountMoreThan)
end if
writelog "There are " & docTotal & " documents"
Call ErrorHandler("IsDocumentCountMoreThan")

af.name: RemoveDocumentStructure
af.qi: Removes the document hierarchy from the batch.
af.g:
Dim oDoc
RemoveDocumentStructure = TRUE
For i = 0 to DCO.NumOfChildren - 1 'loop through the objects that are children of the batch
if DCO.GetChild(i).ObjectType = 1 then 'found a document
Set oDoc = DCO.GetChild(i)
While oDoc.NumOfChildren > 0
Call oDoc.GetChild(0).MoveIn(DCO,-1)
Wend
end if
next 'i
'remove the documents
For i = DCO.NumOfChildren - 1 to 0 Step - 1
if DCO.GetChild(i).ObjectType = 1 then
Call DCO.DeleteChild(i)
end if
Next 'i
Writelog("Structure removed")

af.name: CountPagesToDocumentVar
af.qi: Counts the number of pages in the document.
af.g:
Dim i
Dim PageCount
CountPagesToDocumentVar = TRUE
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "'")
if CurrentObj.ObjectType <> 1 then
Writelog("Action must be on a document object. Exiting")
Exit Function
end if
PageCount = 0
For i = 0 to CurrentObj.NumOfChildren -1
if CurrentObj.GetChild(i).ObjectType = 2 then
PageCount = PageCount + 1
end if
next 'i
CurrentObj.Variable(StrParam) = cStr(PageCount)

f.name: JoinPreviousDocument
f.qi: Combines the previous document into the current document.
f.g:
Dim oCurrentDoc
Dim oPreviousDoc
Dim oPageToMove
JoinPreviousDocument = TRUE 'Actions must always return a TRUE or FALSE.
If CurrentObj.ObjectType <> 1 then
Writelog("This action goes on a DOCUMENT type object (the first page of the document you want to combine the previous document into")
Exit Function
End if
Set oCurrentDoc = CurrentObj
CurrentDocIndex = oCurrentDoc.Parent.FindChildIndex(oCurrentDoc.ID)
Writelog("CurrentDocIndex: " & cStr(CurrentDocIndex) )
if CurrentDocIndex = 0 then
Writelog("This is the first document in the batch, so there are no previous documents. Exiting")
Exit Function
end if
Set oPreviousDoc = oCurrentDoc.Parent.GetChild(CurrentDocIndex - 1)
if oPreviousDoc.Type <> DocTypeToCombine then
Writelog("The previous document was the wrong type to combine: " & oPreviousDoc.Type & ". Exiting.")
Exit Function
End if
For i = oPreviousDoc.NumOfChildren - 1 to 0 Step - 1
Set oPageToMove = oPreviousDoc.GetChild(i)
Writelog("Attempting to move: " & oPageToMove.ID)
If oPageToMove.MoveIn(oCurrentDoc,0) then
Writelog("Moved successfully")
else
writelog("Unable to move document")
end if
next 'i
'Delete oPreviousDocument if empty
Writelog("Moves done.")
if oPreviousDoc.NumOfChildren = 0 then
Call oPreviousDoc.Parent.DeleteChild(CurrentDocIndex - 1)
Writelog("Successfully moved page(s) and deleted document")
else
Writelog("Not all pages were moved. Did not delete document")
end if

f.name: IsFirstPageInBatch
f.qi: Checks to see if this is the first page in the batch
f.g:
Dim oFirst
Dim oPage
IsFirstPageInBatch = FALSE
If CurrentObj.ObjectType <> DCO_PAGE Then
WriteLog("IsFirstPageInBatch must be called at page level. Exiting.")
Exit Function
End If
For i = 0 To DCO.NumOfChildren-1
Set oFirst = DCO.GetChild(i)
If oFirst.ObjectType = DCO_DOCUMENT Then
WriteLog("Document type is found. Process further for pages.")
For j = 0 To oFirst.NumOfChildren-1 'Shallow search only
Set oPage = oFirst.GetChild(j)
If oPage.ObjectType = DCO_PAGE Then Set oFirst = oPage : Exit For
Next
End If
If oFirst.ObjectType = DCO_PAGE Then Exit For
Next
IsFirstPageInBatch = (CurrentObj.ID = oFirst.ID)

f.name: IsFirstDocumentInBatch
f.qi: Checks to see if this is the first document in the batch
f.g:
Dim oDoc
Set oDoc = CurrentObj
While oDoc.ObjectType > 1
Set oDoc = oDoc.Parent
Wend
if oDoc.ObjectType = 0 then
Writelog("No document object found. Exiting")
Exit Function
end if
if DCO.GetChild(0).ID = oDoc.ID then
IsFirstDocumentInBatch = TRUE
else
IsFirstDocumentInBatch = FALSE
end if

The action assigns the page status you enter to the page object of the Document Hierarchy. The current object can be the page or field. If the current object is a field object, it will set the page status for its parent page object.
A scan task might assign Other as the Page Type and 49 as the default Page Status for every successfully scanned image in the batch.
The sequence below is an example of a rule that converts Other pages to Invoices pages, and assigns a Page Status to each:
SetPageType(Invoice)
SetPageStatus(1)
This combination establishes the page as an Invoices page, and gives it a status of 1. This means that the page has not yet been validated and must be processed by a task which applies Validation rules (a Recognition or Verification task, for example).
