method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters.
method.h:
The action will use the previously supplied credentials to connect to the Business Automation Content Analytics, Content Analyzer, service through action
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration
.
This action can be called only on a document DCO node.
The page that is associated with the current DCO node will be submitted to the service for processing.
If the document does not have an associated file, then a document level multi-page TIF will be automatically created from the child pages.
The associated file can be any type supported by Content Analyzer such as PDF, TIF, PNG, or JPG documents.
This action is very similar to the ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest action. The associated document level file will be sent to Content Analyzer
for processing, identically to ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest. The associated file can be any type of file that is supported by
Content Analyzer, such as a PDF or mult-page TIF.
If a file is not associated with the document level object, then this action will automatically create a multi-page TIF
image from the child pages and associate the multi-page TIF with the current document object. When automatically creating
a multi-page TIF image from the child pages, it is required that all of the child pages are all single page TIF images.
The new multi-page TIF is the image that will be submitted to Content Analyzer for processing as a single document, populating
the page object data as specified by the action parameters.
Once the document has been submitted to Content Analyzer for processing, this action will update the AnalyzerRequestID variable
to be used by a subsequent call to ContentAnalzyerGetOutput. Action will not
wait for Content Analyzer to process the document and will return True if the request is successful.
The results of Content Analyzer processing are not ingested into the batch using this action, it simply submits documents for processing.
If desired, multiple submit actions can be called to provide multiple documents to Content Analyzer for processing and
once all of desired documents have been submitted, subsequent rules can call ContentAnalyzerGetOutput.
The action in turn returns the
AnalyzerID
which gets save as DCO variable
AnalyzerRequestID
in the current
object which can be used later by further actions.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequestCreateMultipage("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
This example will configure the actions to connect to Content Analyzer, and then submits a document for processing.
The two actions are shown together for illustration. Typically ContentAnalzyerConfiguration would be called once on a
batch level rule and then ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequestCreateMultipage will be associated with Document level or Page level objects and
will be called once for each document to submit.
In case if action is called at Document level, and page is not promoted as Document, in such case this action will merge
the tiff files associated to this document and will create one single file at Document level. A variable
MergedTiffFileName
will be added in the DCO xml within the Document containing the name of merge file.
The whole merged tiff file will be submitted to Content Analyzer server for processing similar to sending multipage tiff.
method.ret:
True,
action is successful. Otherwise,
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerGetOutput
method.ap: None.
method.h:
The action will use the previously supplied credentials to connect to the Business Automation Content Analytics, Content Analyzer, service through action
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration
and download the processing results from a previous ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest action.
If the previously submitted document has not completed processing, this action will wait up to the time specified as the RecogTimeout
in the ContentAnalyzerSetTimeout action for Content Analyzer to return the results. Once the results are available, the data returned
from Content Analyzer will be saved in the batch and associated with the current DCO node.
This action can be called on a document or page DCO node that was used with the action ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest which saved
the request information in the DCO variable
AnalyzerRequestID.
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput uses the saved ID as the key
to retrieve the data that was associated with the submitted document.
The parameters used on the previous call to ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest and the ontology used by Content Analyzer
will determine the type of content that is returned from Content Analyzer. The output files will be downloaded by this action and
saved in the batch.
New variables are created in the DCO containing the name of any associated files and data
returned by Content Analyzer.
Created Variables:
DocumentClass
This variable will store the DocumentClass returned by Content Analyzer.
AnalyzerJSON
The name of the raw JSON returned from Content Analyzer. The file is named based on the
ID of the current DCO node.
For example:
If the object ID is TM000001 then the JSON will be saved in a file named tm000001_BACA.json.
The file name is stored in the variable AnalyzerJSON.
AnalyzerPDF
If in the action ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest the parameter
CreatePDF
is passed as TRUE then this
action will save the pdf output in the variable
AnalyzerPDF.
For example:
If the object ID TM000001 then the returned PDF will be named tm000001_BACA.pdf
and the file name will be stored in the variable AnalyzerPDF.
AnalyzerUTF8
If in the action ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest the parameter
CreateTextFile
is
passed as TRUE then this action will save the utf8(text) output in the variable
AnalyzerUTF8.
For example:
If the object ID is TM000001 then the text will be saved in a file named tm000001_BACA.txt
and the file name will be stored in the variable AnalyzerUTF8.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput()
This example first calls ContentAnalyzerConfiguration to configure the connection to Content Analyzer.
ContentAnalzyerSubmitRequest sends the document to Content Analyzer for processing and stores the AnalyzerID in the variable AnalyzerRequestID.
The submit parameters state a PDF will be needed as output and Text file is not needed as it is set as false.
Please refer parameters section of this action for details of the other parameters.
Finally ContentAnalyzerGetOutput is called which will wait for processing to finish and obtain the results
from Content Analyzer. The action will save the returned json output file and the PDF. The variables will be updated such as the DocumentClass DCO variable.
Because the PDF output was also required as specified in the submit action so it will also save the PDF file as output.
The three actions are shown together for illustration. Typically ContentAnalzyerConfiguration would be called once on a
batch level rule.
method.ret:
True,
If able to download the files as per the configuration while submitting the request. Else
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerRetry

p.name: RetryCount
p.qi: This must be an integer of 1 or greater and indicates how many times to retry a call to the ContentAnalyzer service, if an error occurs. If this action is not called, the retry count will default to 1.

p.name: RetryDelay
p.qi: This must be an integer of 0 or greater and indicates how many seconds to wait before retrying a failed call to the Content Analyzer service. If this action is not called, the retry delay will default to 5 seconds.

method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters.
method.h:
When communicating with the Content Analyzer service, actions will wait for the response. If no response is received within
a specific time frame, the communication will be retried. This action will customize the number of retries and the time to wait
between each communication attempt.
If this action is not called, by default the call will be automatically retried once after a 5 second delay.
Call this action prior to using other ContentAnalyzer actions to configure how the subsequent actions will respond.
This action only needs to be called once per task to configure the subsequent actions within the task.
If Content Analyzer actions are called again in a subsequent task, then call this action again to configure
retry values for the task.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
ContentAnalyzerRetry(3,10)
This example sets the connection information and then adjusts the default retry values. The action will set the retry count value to
3 and retry delay to 10 seconds. If a subsequent call to ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest
fails to connect to the service, it will be tried 3 times with a delay of 10 seconds between each retry.
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
This call to ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest would occur on a Document or Page object while the two previous
actions would typically be run on a batch level object.
method.lvl: Any Level, but prior to calling other Content Analyzer actions.
method.ret:
True,
If parameters set properly else
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action will convert the JSON output file generated by Content Analyzer to a layout xml file. OCR results and key-value-pair results will be included in the layout file.
The layout file can be loaded into the Datacap CCO using the action LoadCCOFromLayout in the Shared Recognition Tools action library. Once the full page recognition
results are loaded into the CCO, the CCO can be used by other actions and other Datacap clients.
This action uses the JSON file name saved through the earlier action ContentAnalyzerGetOutput which was saved in DCO as the variable
AnalyzerJSON.
The new layout xml file will be created in the batch and its name will be saved in the DCO file. If a layout file is expected,
the previous call to ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest must have the
"FullPageRecognition"
parameter set to "True".
The layout files created will always be associated with a Page object.
If this action is called at on a Page level object, it is expected that the document is a one page document. The layout file will be created
for the current page and associated with the current Page object.
If the action is called on a Document level object, then the
processed document can be 1 or more pages. The layout files created will be associated with the child pages of the current Document level
object. It is expected that at least one child Page object exists for each page within the source document. When using a Document level
object, it is expected that previously an action from the Convert action library has been called on the Document level object to create
child Page objects and associated image files for each page. For example, if the Document object
has an associated document that contained two pages, then at least two child Page objects need to exist for the current
object. Two layout files will be created and associated with the two child pages. Refer to the top level help for the Content Analyzer actions
for more information.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
This action will use the provided credentails and url to connect to Content Analyzer service.
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
This action will be used to submit the request. It will store the AnalyzerID in the variable AnalyzerRequestID.
In order to call ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout action later,
"FullPageRecognition"
parameter must be set as true.
Please refer parameters section of this action for the details of other parameters.
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput()
This action will save the json output file and DocumentClass value in a DCO variable.
ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout()
This action will convert the json output file to a layout xml file. File name will be saved in the Layout variable in the associated DCO.
If the input document can be 1 or more pages, such as a multi-page pdf, then the first call the PromoteToDocument
action to convert the page object associated with the scanned file into a Document level object.
After that the actions ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest, ContentAnalyzerGetOutput and
ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout
should be called on the Document level object.
When used on a Document level object, the action ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout will associate the layout file with the child Page objects.
The child Page objects must exist before ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout is called. The Convert action library must be used prior to creating
the layout files. Call the appropriate conversion action for the document type. For example, if the document is a PDF, then
call PDFFREDocumentToImage to create a child Page object and associated TIF file for each page within the PDF. Depending on the
application's needs, the original input PDF could be converted or the PDF that was returned from Content Analyzer could be converted.
If the child Page objects do not exist prior to calling the create layout action, then the action will fail.
The following example shows the required steps. They are all shown together for illustration only. The actions will not
all be performed on the same DCO object.
PromotePageToDocument("Invoice","")
This action will change the input file into the Document level. Call this action on the original input Page object, typically
ingested as type "Other". Once the new document node is created, all of the child nodes can be deleted by
calling DeleteDCOChildWithStatus("75")
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
This action will use the provided credentails and url to connect to Content Analyzer service and is typically called on the batch object.
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","","True","","","","","False")
This action will be used to submit the request.It will store the AnalyzerID in the variable AnalyzerRequestID.
In order to call ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout action later,
"FullPageRecognition"
parameter must be set as true.
Please refer parameters section of this action for more details. This would be called on the Document or Page object
to submit to Content Analyzer.
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput()
This action will save the json output file and DocumentClass in dco variable. Call this action on the same object
as the submit.
PDFFREDocumentToImage("300","18","33","32",".bw.tif","col.tif","gray.tif","0","False","100")
This action will split a multi-page PDF document into single page TIF pages and create child Page objects. One child
will be created for each page.
ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout()
This action should be called on the Document level and it will convert the json output file to several layout xml
files based on the split child pages. The layout file name will be saved in the DCO variable called Layout.
method.ret:
True,
If able to convert the JSON file generated by Content Analyzer to a layout xml file. Else
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerCreateFieldsFromKVP
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action will create fields to a DCO file from the key-value pairs (KVP) results in the Content Analyzer JSON file. If a DCO file exists already,
fields based on the KVP will be added, if the DCO file does not exist, it will be created automatically and the name of this DCO file will be saved
in the task DCO variable called DATAFILE. The field name is created based on the Key or KeyClass name of the key-value pair. It will look for the KeyClass first.
If Content Analyzer returns a KeyClass, then the field name will be the same as the returned KeyClass. If a KeyClass is not returned, then the
field will be named the same as the returned Key.
If this action is called at on a Page level object, it is expected that the document is a one page document. The DCO file will be created
for the current page and associated with the current Page object.
If the action is called on a Document level object, then the
processed document can be 1 or more pages. The DCO files created will be associated with the child pages of the current Document level
object. It is expected that at least one child Page object exists for each page within the source document. When using a Document level
object, it is expected that previously an action from the Convert action library has been called on the Document level object to create
child Page objects and associated image files for each page. For example, if the Document object
has an associated document that contained two pages, then at least two child Page objects need to exist for the current
object. When running on a document object, the action will operate like it does for a single page, but across all pages within the document.
For each page attached to the current document object, this action will create a field for each key value pair returned from Content Analyzer
that associated with the page. Refer to the top level help for the Content Analyzer actions
for more information.
This action can only be called after ContentAnalyzerGetOutput() action.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
This action will use the provided credentails and url to connect to Content Analyzer service.
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
This action will be used to submit the request. It will store the AnalyzerID in the variable AnalyzerRequestID.
In order to call ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout action later,
"FullPageRecognition"
parameter must be set as true.
Please refer parameters section of this action for the details of other parameters.
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput()
This action will save the json output file and DocumentClass value in a DCO variable.
ContentAnalyzerCreateFieldsFromKVP()
This action will create a field based DCO file from Content Analyzer JSON file. File name will be saved in the DATAFILE variable in the associated DCO.
method.ret:
True,
If able to create fields to a DCO file from the key-value pairs (KVP) results in the Content Analyzer JSON file. Else
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerSetTimeout

p.name: RequestTimeout
p.qi: The number of seconds to wait for a Content Analyzer request. The default timeout is 30 seconds.

p.name: RecogTimeout
p.qi: The number of seconds to wait for Content Analyzer recognition and return the results. The default timeout is 1800 seconds.

method.ap: All parameters support Smart Parameters.
method.h:
Sets the number of seconds to wait before it is determined that a Content Analyzer request has not responded.
When the timeout is reached, the action processing the Content Analyzer request will fail. If retry is enabled, the failed request will be tried again.
The RequestTimeout is for the response from Content Analyzer APIs which are expected to be quick, such as login and submitting
a document for processing. If this action is not called, this timeout will default to 30 seconds. The RecogTimeout parameter is used to wait
for recognition results and
extraction processing on Content Analyzer which will take a longer time to finish and return the output. If this action
is not called, RecogTimeout will use a default value of 1800 seconds
(processing of a 1 page document on a basic Content Analyzer system may take around 10 seconds).
If ContentAnalyzerSetTimeout is not called, the default value of 30 and 1800 seconds are used.
In normal conditions, the default values are sufficient and does not need to be changed.
The value of RecogTimeout needs to be increased only if the document submitted to the Content Analyzer is very big
and the total number of documents submitted as the same time is very large.
The application developer to adjust the values as needed based on the expected load and response times.
If this action is called, it must be called before actions that communicate with the Content Analyzer service.
Once called, the settings will remain in effect for the remainder of the task profile. If Content Analyzer
actions are used in a follow on task profile, then this action will need be be called again to configure
the settings for the new task profile. Typically it will be called once on a batch level object.
ContentAnalyzerSetTimeout("15", "1800")
This action will set the timeout values for the ContentAnalyzer actions.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
This action will use the provided credentials and url to connect to Content Analyzer service.
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
This action will be used to submit the request. It will store the AnalyzerID in the variable AnalyzerRequestID.
In order to call ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout action later,
"FullPageRecognition"
parameter must be set as true.
Please refer parameters section of this action for more detail.
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput()
This action will save the json output file and DocumentClass in a DCO variable.
ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout()
This action will convert the json output file to a layout xml file. File name will be saved in the variable Layout in the DCO.
method.ret:
Always
True
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerFindExtractedText

p.name: Target
p.qi: The target DCO object where the value will be saved. If used on a field use '@F' to update the current field.

p.name: Scope
p.qi: First|Last|All - Populates the target using the match(es) using the specified key or keyclass. If First is specified the first match is used. If Last is specified the last match is used. If All is specified a sub field will be created for each matches. All is only supported when the target is detail field and is not supported for variable.

p.name: Key
p.qi: Name of the key to match. This key will be returned by Content Analyzer service.

p.name: KeyClass
p.qi: Name of the key class to match. KeyClass returned by Content Analyzer service for Key value pairs. First priority to the key class parameter.

method.ap:
The Key or Keyclass parameter must be provided, or both may be provided. If both the parameters are provided, the keyclass parameter will be used for the search first.
Key-value pairs returned by Content Analyzer will always have a "Key". Depending on the ontology definition, a "KeyClass" entry may or may not be returned by the service.
If the KeyClass is blank, then the action will look for the key-value pair specified in the Key parameter.
If both the Key and KeyClass are provided as parameters and if the KeyClass is not found in a key-value pair, the Key parameter will
be used for the search. If there is a match for the specified key, it will be able to populate the field correctly and return true.
All parameters support Smart Parameters.
method.h:
Populates a field or variable using a value populated in Layout xml file through the ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout action.
IMPORTANT : The Content Analyzer result will be returned by ContentAnalyzerGetOutput action in JSON format and stored in the batch in JSON. To transfer the data
to the layout file, the action ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout must be called prior to this action to find the extracted text.
When the layout file is generated, the key-value pairs will also be placed into the layout xml file.
The Layout xml file and Page xml file (Datafile) must exist before calling the ContentAnalyzerFindExtractedText action.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
This action will use the provided credentails and url to connect to Content Analyzer service. It is typically called on the batch object.
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
This action will be used to submit the request to Content Analyzer. The action will store the AnalyzerID in the variable AnalyzerRequestID.
In order to call ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout action later,
"FullPageRecognition"
parameter must be set as true.
Please refer parameters section of this action for more details.
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput()
This action will save the json output file and DocumentClass in dco variable.
ContentAnalyzerCreateLayout()
This action will convert the json output file to a layout xml file. File name will be saved in Layout in dco variable.
Example 1
ContentAnalyzerFindExtractedText("@P\Invoice_Date","First","","InvoiceDate")
This example assumes action is called at Page level, where the page field "Invoice_Date" is expected to
be populated with the value returned by Content Analyzer service corresponds to the key class "InvoiceDate".
The scope First denotes the first occurrence of this key will be searched and its value will be used.
Example 2
ContentAnalyzerFindExtractedText("@P\Airfare","Last","airfare","")
Because the key class is not provided to the action, the key "airfare" will be used to populate the value to the text property of child field "Airfare".
The scope Last denotes the last occurrence of this key will be searched and its value will be used.
Example 3
ContentAnalyzerFindExtractedText("@P\Airfare","First","airfare","Airfare")
Because this example provides both the key class and key, the search will be on keyclass Airfare
and if the keyclass "airfare" is not found in the key-value pari results then it will not populate the value to the child field "Airfare".
Example 4
ContentAnalyzerFindExtractedText("@P\DateDetail","All","Date")
This example will create a line item for each Key Date found in the document. The following document hierarchy is expected to be defined.
Field DateDetail
- Field LineItem
- - Field Date
method.ret:
True,
if able to populate the field correctly and if data is correctly available else
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerSetProxy
method.qi: Allows optional specification of proxy service settings.

p.name: hostname
p.qi: URL or IP address of proxy service.

p.name: proxyPort
p.qi: The proxy service connection port.

p.name: proxyUsername
p.qi: Username for the proxy server.

p.name: proxyPassword
p.qi: Password for the proxy server

method.ap:
All parameters support Smart Parameters.
The password can be encrypted by storing it in the Advanced section of the Custom tab in the Application Manager.
The URL and user name parameters can be stored in the General section of the Datacap Application Manager but they cannot be encrypted.
To retrieve the password that is stored in the Advanced section,
use a smart parameter for the action's password parameter similar to
@APPVAR(values/adv/ProxyPassword) where ProxyPassword is the variable name entered for the value in the Application Manager.
method.h:
Optionally sets the values to a proxy service that will be used to connect to the Content Analyzer API.
This action does not confirm that the connection to the proxy service is successful. Connection to the
proxy service will not occur until the other ContentAnalyzer actions that initiate a transaction with the service are called.
If this action is used, it must be called prior to the ContentAnalyzer actions. If this action is not
called, then no proxy service will be used.
This action only needs to be called once for a task profile. Once set, it will remain in effect until
the end of the task. If Content Analizer actions are used in subsquent tasks, then this action must be
called again to configure the proxy settings.
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
ContentAnalyzerSetProxy("theHostName", "80", "MyUser", "@APPVAR(values/adv/ProxyPassword)")
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
This example sets up the parameters to use a proxy and then call the SubmitRequest action to connect to Content Analyzer API to upload the document.
The parameter for the password is an example smart parameter that obtains the password
from an advanced value in the application service. The actions are shown together for illustration. Typically the configuration
and proxy would be set once using a Batch level rule while the submit is used on a Document or Page level rule.
method.ret:
True
if the proxy settings set correct else
False.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help for the Content Analyzer Actions for information on the features of this action
library and how to use it.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments

p.name: DeleteDocumentInAllCase
p.qi: True or False. Default value false. If true, the document is unconditionally deleted from the server. If false, the document will be deleted from the server, if the JSON is already downloaded from Content Analytics and is available in the batch directory.

p.name: AnalyzerRequestID
p.qi: Optional. The AnalyzerRequestID of a document to be deleted from server. If not provided the action will use the analyzer request ID of the page / document on which this action was previously called.

method.ap: All parameters support smart parameters.
method.h:
The action deletes the document or pages from the Content Analyzer server that were previously submitted for processing.
A flag is provided as a parameter in the action that allows the document to be deleted the conditionally based on success of the transaction.
This action is optional. By default document stays on Content Analyzer server for 24 hours. After 24 hours the documents are deleted by the Content Analyzer system.
This action can be used if it is desired to immediately delete documents from the server after they have been processed and downloaded to the batch.
The Analyzer Request ID can be optionally provided to this action. If the parameter is supplied, the document that is associated with the ID will
be deleted from the Content Analyzer server. The action will not validate whether the provided AnalyzerRequestID is valid. If the ID is not supplied,
then the ID associated for a previous request on the current DCO object will be used.
If Content Analyzer is still retaining the document for the provided AnalyzerRequestID then it will delete the related document.
Example 1:
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments("False","")
As per above set of action, ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments is called after ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest action through which document is submitted to Content Analyzer system.
The action ContentAnalyzerGetOutput() is not called thus output JSON not downloaded so action will return false. Document will not delete in this case from Content Analyzer system since the flag is set to False.
Example 2:
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","@APPVAR(values/gen/FunctionalID)","@APPVAR(values/adv/Password)","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
ContentAnalyzerGetOutput()
ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments("False","")
As per above set of action, ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments is called after ContentAnalyzerGetOutput() through which the corresponding JSON should have downloaded.
Since the flag is set to False , so the action will look for the existince of JSON variable in DCO xml and will then delete the documents from Content Analyzer System for the current page/document.
Example 3:
ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments("True","")
This action will delete the page/pages from Content Analyzer server irrespective of its status since the flag is set to True.
Example 4:
ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments("False","")
This action will delete the page/pages from Content Analyzer server only if its corresponding JSON downloaded in the batch directory.
Example 5:
ContentAnalyzerDeleteDocuments("True","69da91c0-dd1e-11e9-858c-97d87eb11b1f")
This action will delete the page/pages from Content Analyzer server for the provided Analyzer Request ID. To force deletion, set the first parameter to True as its corresponding JSON may or may not be available in batch directory.
method.ret:
True
if documents are deleted successfully from Content Analyzer server or if the analyzerID is provided explicitly and documents are not available in Content Analyzer server corresponding to the provided analyzerID.
False
if document cannot be deleted from Content Analyzer server or if the DeleteDocumentInAllCase parameter is provided as False and JSON is not available for the current page.

method.name: ContentAnalyzerUMSAuthorization

p.name: UMSHosturl
p.qi: UMS host url.

p.name: client_secret
p.qi: client password

p.name: UMSUsername
p.qi: Resource owner user name for whom the access token is being requested.

p.name: UMSPassword
p.qi: Resource owner password for whom the access token is being requested.

method.ap: All parameters support smart parameters.
method.h:
User Management Services (UMS) provide single sign-on (SSO) and Teams options, which provide users of multiple applications with a single sign-on experience and centrally administered teams.
ContentAnalyzerUMSAuthorization action checks for the user registration, if not registered it registers the user and then finally generates the access token.
UMSUsername and UMSPassword, are used directly to obtain an access_token. The custom application therefore initially needs to obtain credentials from the resource owner.
Upon the access token request, UMS SSO authenticates the client and validates the resource owner credentials before issuing an access token.
Generated access_token gets stored in xml file as a DCO variable
access_token
at Batch level.
Access_token generated will remain active for two hours only.
Action is allowed to be called at Batch level only.
To use UMS on Datacap Content Analyzer actions, ContentAnalyzerUMSAuthorization action should be called before ContentAnalyzerConfiguration.
If ContentAnalyzerUMSAuthorization action is configured and called, the other Content Analyzer actions of this library will assume to authorize through UMS only.
ContentAnalyzerUMSAuthorization("https://abc.usure.ibm.com/oidc/endpoint/ums","datacapaca","passw0rd","umsadmin","password")
ContentAnalyzerConfiguration("url","","","@APPVAR(values/adv/APIKey")
ContentAnalyzerSubmitRequest("True,"True","False","True","Invoice","True","","","","","False")
When using ContentAnalyzerUMSAuthorization to use UMS Authorization, the parameter functional id and password will be optional for the action ContentAnalyzerConfiguration.
method.ret:
True
if able to generate token successfully else
False

af.name: SetMailServer
af.g:
'Configures the mail server to use for sending mail."
' The IP or DNS address of the outgoing mail (SMTP) server.
SetMailServer = true
if (gOutlookInit) then
' When not set, these actions will always create an outlook email object.
Writelog("Warning, SetMailServer was called while the Outlook object is in use.")
End If
gMailServer=trim(MetaWord(StrParam))
Writelog("Setting for IP or DNS address of SMTP server is:" & gMailServer)

af.name: SetRecipients
af.g:
'Sets email recipients' address(es)."
'Email address(es) of recipient(s). You can either call this action multiple times to add multiple recipients,
'or you can enter multiple email addresses separated by commas.
On Error Resume Next
SetRecipients = true
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
if (Trim(CStr(StrParam)) = "") Then
WriteLog("Error: SetRecipients was called with no recipients")
SetRecipients = false
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetRecipients")
Exit Function
End if
if ( Not CheckExistingMailItem() ) Then
WriteLog("Error: SetRecipients could not create email object")
SetRecipients = false
Exit Function
end if
if(g_CDOSYS_NotPresent = TRUE) Then ' Using Outlook
g_MailItem.Recipients.Add StrParam
writelog("Setting Recipient for Outlook: " & StrParam)
if(ParseError("can not set Recipients for Outlook MailItem")) Then
WriteLog("Error: SetRecipients could not set outlook recipient")
SetRecipients = false
' and store that Initialization is fail
gOutlookInit = FALSE
gInitProcedurePassed = TRUE
Set g_theOutlook = Nothing
exit Function
end if
if Not g_MailItem.Recipients.ResolveAll Then
WriteLog("Unknown recipient: " + StrParam)
SetRecipients = false
Set g_theOutlook = Nothing
exit function
end if
else
writelog("Setting Recipient for CDOSYS: " & StrParam)
Dim Ub
Ub = Ubound(arRecipients,1)
Redim Preserve arRecipients(Ub + 1)
arRecipients(Ub + 1) = StrParam
end if
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetRecipients")

af.name: SetCarbonCopyRcpts

' You can enter multiple email addresses separated by commas.
On Error Resume Next
SetCarbonCopyRcpts = true
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
writelog("CC Recipients: '" & StrParam & "'")
if(Trim(CStr(StrParam)) = "") Then
writelog("Error: SetCarbonCopyRcpts was called with no recipients")
SetCarbonCopyRcpts = false

End If

writelog("Error: SetCarbonCopyRcpts CheckExistingMailItem failed")
SetCarbonCopyRcpts = false
Exit Function
end if
if(g_CDOSYS_NotPresent = TRUE) Then ' Using Outlook Object
g_MailItem.CC = StrParam
if(ParseError("can not sets SenderName for Outlook MailItem")) Then
writelog("Error: SetCarbonCopyRcpts could not set Outlook CC")
SetCarbonCopyRcpts = false
' and store that Initialization is fail
gOutlookInit = FALSE
gInitProcedurePassed = TRUE
Set g_theOutlook = Nothing
exit Function
end if
else ' Using CDOSYS Object
if(trim(MessageHeaders(cCarbonCopy)) <> "" ) Then
MessageHeaders(cCarbonCopy) = MessageHeaders(cCarbonCopy) & "," & StrParam
else
MessageHeaders(cCarbonCopy) = StrParam
end if
end if
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetCarbonCopyRcpts")

af.name: SetAttachment
af.g:
'Adds a file attachment to an email."
' The file’s path and name. Smart Parameters are supported.
Dim g_ExportName_email
On Error Resume Next
' this function sets attachment from g_ExportName_email, which is set up by the same function
g_ExportName_email = MetaWord(Trim(StrParamMW)) ' Smart Parameters are allowed. Process them if any are present.
Dim StrPath ' actual path to file; StrParam is file name
if(Trim(CStr(g_ExportName_email)) = "") Then
writelog(space(2) & "SetAttachment get empty PathName")
SetAttachment = false
exit function
End If
StrPath = Pilot.BatchDir & "\" & Trim(g_ExportName_email)
StrPath = Trim(g_ExportName_email)
if(FileMgr.FileExists(StrPath)) Then
if( Not CheckExistingMailItem() ) Then
writelog(space(2) & "SetAttachment CheckExistingMailItem failed")
SetAttachment = false
Exit Function
end if
if(g_CDOSYS_NotPresent = TRUE) Then ' Using Outlook email object
g_MailItem.Attachments.Add Trim(CStr(StrPath))
if(ParseError("can not add Attachments for Outlook MailItem")) Then
writelog(space(2) & "SetAttachment Cannot add outlook attachment")
SetAttachment = false
' and store that Initialization is fail
gOutlookInit = FALSE
gInitProcedurePassed = TRUE
Set g_theOutlook = Nothing
exit Function
end if
else ' Using CDOSYS
writelog(space(2) & "Setting CDOSYS attachment: " & strPath)
'call g_MailItem.AttachFile(Trim(CStr(StrPath)),g_ExportName_email )
call g_MailItem.AddAttachment(Trim(CStr(StrPath)),"","")
end if
else
writelog(space(2) & "SetAttachment get unexisting file:" & StrPath)
SetAttachment = false
exit function
end if
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetAttachment")
SetAttachment = true

af.name: SendEMail
af.g:
'Sends an email."
On Error Resume Next
if (Not IsObject(g_MailItem)) Then
WriteLog("Fatal Error: call SetRecipients() first")
SendEMail = false
gInitProcedurePassed = FALSE
exit function
End If
If(g_MailItem Is Nothing) Then
WriteLog("SendEmail Error: email object is not created, first call actions to set email parameters")
SendEMail = false
gInitProcedurePassed = FALSE
exit function
End If
if( Not CheckExistingMailItem() ) Then
WriteLog("SendEmail Error: CheckExistingMailItem failed")
SendEmail = false
gInitProcedurePassed = FALSE
Set g_MailItem = Nothing
Exit Function
end if
if(g_CDOSYS_NotPresent = TRUE) then ' Using Outlook Object
call SendEMailThroughOutlook()
WriteLog("Sent with Outlook")
else ' Using CDOSYS Object
call SendEMailThroughCDOSYS()
WriteLog("Sent with CDOSYS")
end if
' After Sending, reset everything to inital state to create a new e-mail for next calls to the actions
Set g_MailItem = Nothing
gCDOSYSinit = FALSE
gOutlookInit = FALSE
gInitProcedurePassed = FALSE
g_CDOSYS_NotPresent = TRUE
MessageHeaders(cSubject) = ""
MessageHeaders(cFrom) = ""
MessageHeaders(cBody) = ""
MessageHeaders(cImportance) = 1
MessageHeaders(cCarbonCopy) = ""
MessageHeaders(cBlindCarbonCopy) = ""
Redim Preserve arRecipients(0)
If Err.Number <> 0 Then
Call ErrorHandler("Function SendEMail")
SendEMail = FALSE
Else
SendEMail = TRUE
End If

The IP or DNS address of the outgoing mail (SMTP) server.
Smart parameters are supported.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the ms_login action in the Email.MSGraph action library.
Sets the address of the outgoing mail (SMTP) server. This may be the same mail server you configure in your mail program. The server must be accessible from the computer running the email actions. This action should be the first action in an email rule if the CDOSYS object is being used.
Use this action only if you are sending emails with CDOSYS. To use CDOSYS, this action must be called prior to any of the other email actions. If this action is not called prior to other email actions, these actions will use Outlook for sending emails.
You can use Email actions to direct a task to compose and send emails containing information and attachments. Email actions use the Windows CDOSYS library to send email via your preferred SMTP mail server. The CDOSYS object is included with Windows 2000 and above. Alternatively, Email actions can use the Outlook object but this is not recommended.
One of these two libraries (CDOSYS or Outlook) must be registered on the computer that runs rules employing email actions.
Outlook is primarily useful for demonstration purposes, as it is not suitable for unattended operation: it requires the Outlook user to be logged into the computer, and security prompts may be displayed for each message sent.

SetSender("paul@adomain.com")

af.name: BlankFields

StrParam = cint(StrParam)
For Cntr = 1 to StrParam
Call WriteExport(bInter, bDeBug, "")
Next
WriteLog(Space(5) & "Added " & cstr(StrParam) & " BlankFields to the Export.")

af.name: BlankLines
af.g:
Dim sFileContent
On Error Resume Next
Strparam=replace(Strparam,Chrw(32),"")
If Not IsNumeric(StrParam) or len(Trim(Strparam))=0 Then
Writelog("Parameter must be numeric. Defaulting to 1")
StrParam = 1
End if
StrParam = abs(StrParam)
If StrParam-cint(Strparam)>0 then
Writelog("Parameter must be an Integer. Parameter will be rounded to nearest integer.")
StrParam = cint(StrParam)
end if
If StrParam <= 0 then
Writelog("Parameter must be an Integer greater than Zero. Defaulting to 1")
StrParam = 1
End if
If Not IsObject(g_ExportFile) Then
Call OpenExportFile(bInter, bDebug)
End if
If Not IsObject(g_ExportFile) Then
Writelog("Unable to find open file.")
Exit Function
End if
WriteLog("Adding Blank LINE x " & StrParam)
If len(g_LastExportValue)>0 then
If NOT(right(g_LastExportValue,1)=Chrw(10) or right(g_LastExportValue,1)=Chrw(13)) then
StrParam=StrParam+1
end if
End if
g_LastExportValue=vbcrlf
Call g_ExportFile.WriteBlankLines(Cint(StrParam))
BlankLines = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function BlankLines")

af.name: ExportFieldValue
af.g:
Dim setupObj
Dim oFld
Dim nCount
Dim sValue
Dim VarId
Dim aObjID
Set oFld = Nothing
On Error Resume Next
ExportFieldValue= False
If len(trim(StrParam))=0 then
Writelog("This action requires a parameter.")
Exit function
End if
writelog("EXPORT FIELD " & Ucase(StrParam))
If IsObject(CurrentObj) Then
If CurrentObj.Objecttype<>2 then
Writelog("Action must be called from a DCO Page.")
Exit Function
End if
writelog(Space(5) & "Finding DCO Value:'" & StrParam & "'")
Set oFld = RReturnNamedComponent(StrParam)
If NOT(oFld is nothing) then
'Check for variable in sFindObjID argument. Flag is the Decimal '.' character (period).
aObjID = split(StrParam & ".",".")
VarID = trim(aObjID(1))
If Len(VarID)=0 then
sValue = CheckDICT(oFld)
Else
sValue = oFld.Variable(VarID)
End if
Writelog(Space(5) & "DCO Value is :'" & sValue & "' ")
If u_CheckNoExportStatus(oFld)=TRUE then
Call WriteExport(bInter, False, sValue)
End if
ExportFieldValue= True
Else
Writelog(Space(5) & "Object '" & StrParam & "' Not Found.")
ExportFieldValue = False
End if
Else
WriteLog(Space(5) & "There is No Current Object.")
ExportFieldValue= False
End If
WriteLog("END Export Field. Returns: " & ExportFieldValue)
Call ErrorHandler("Function ExportFieldValue")

af.name: GetDATE
af.g:
Dim dd,ddd,mm,yyyy,yy,y,m,d
Dim DateText
'Updates field with current Date value
'Strparam is the pattern to update the field with
'Value: '*' sets to default value
If len(trim(StrParam))=0 then
Writelog("Parameter is Empty. Exiting Action.")
GetDATE = False
Exit Function
End if
GetDATE = True
If InStr(StrParam,"*")>0 Then StrParam = "mm/dd/yyyy"
StrParam = LCase(StrParam)
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"c","y")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam," "," & Chrw(32) &")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"/"," & Chrw(47) &")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"& &","&")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"day","dd")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"month","mm")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"year","yyyy")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"julian","y")
WriteLog("DateStamp Strparam= '" & StrParam & "' ")
d = Day(Now)
dd = Right("0" & d,2)
yyyy = Year(Now)
yy = Right(yyyy,2)
m = Month(Now)
mm = Right("0" & m,2)
ccyy = yyyy
y = DatePart("y",Now)
DateText = Eval(Strparam)
Call WriteExport(bInter, bDeBug, DateText )
WriteLog("GetDATE returns true. Value: " & DateText)
Call ErrorHandler("Function GetDATE")

af.name: GetProfileString
af.g:
Dim aParams
Dim sHeader
Dim sSubSection
Dim sFileNameINI
Dim INIvalue
Writelog("GetProfileString Input: " & StrParam)
If len(Trim(StrParam))=0 then
Writelog("Parameter is Empty. Exiting Action.")
GetProfileString = False
Exit Function
End if
aParams = Split(StrParam & ",," , ",")
sHeader = aParams(0)
sSubSection = aParams(1)
sFileNameINI = aParams(2)
If FileMgr.FileExists(Pilot.BatchDir & "\" & sFileNameINI) Then
' Writelog("Getting section: " & sSubSection & " from file: " & Pilot.BatchDir & "\" & sFileNameINI)
INIvalue = Pilot.GetProfileString(sHeader, sSubSection,"",Pilot.BatchDir & "\" & sFileNameINI)
Call WriteExport(bInter, bDebug, INIvalue)
GetProfileString = True
Else
Writelog("Could not locate file: " & Pilot.BatchDir & "\" & sFileNameINI)
GetProfileString = False
End If
Call ErrorHandler("Function GetProfileString")

af.name: GetTime
af.g:
Dim mm,ss,hh,hhhh,m,s,h
Dim TimeText
GetTime = False
If len(trim(StrParam))=0 then
Writelog("Parameter is Empty. Exiting Action.")
Exit Function
End if
' Remove all valid parameters from input string.
' If sTest is empty at the end, then only valid input strings were passed in.
sTest = LCASE(StrParam)
sTest = Replace(sTest,"minute","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"second","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"hour","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"min","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"sec","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"hr","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"h","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"m","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"s","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,":","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"/","")
sTest = Replace(sTest," ","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"&","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"-","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"'","")
sTest = Replace(sTest,"*","")
If len(sTest)>0 then
Writelog("Invalid Parameter Characters '" & sTest & "' found. Exiting Action.")
Exit Function
end if
'Updates field with current Time value
'Strparam is the pattern to update the field with
'Value: '*' sets to default value
'WriteLog("Gettime Strparam= '" & StrParam & "' ")
If instr(StrParam,"*")>0 Then StrParam = "HH:MM:SS"
StrParam = LCase(StrParam)
StrParam = Replace(StrParam," "," & CHRW(32) &") 'NOTE CHRW is upper case so the 'hr' replace does not change chrw to chhw
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"/"," & CHRW(47) &")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,":"," & CHRW(58) &")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"-"," & CHRW(45) &")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"'"," & CHRW(39) &")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"& &","&")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"minute","mm")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"min","mm")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"second","ss")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"sec","ss")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"hr","hh")
StrParam = Replace(StrParam,"hour","hh")
WriteLog("TimeStamp Strparam= '" & StrParam & "' ")
m = Minute(Now)
s = Second(Now)
h = Hour(Now)
hhhh = hh
mm = Right("0" & m,2)
ss = Right("0" & s,2)
hh = Right("0" & h,2)
TimeText = Eval(StrParam)
If err.number=0 then GetTime = True
Call WriteExport(bInter, bDeBug, TimeText)
WriteLog("GetTime returns " & GetTime & ". Value: " & TimeText)
Call ErrorHandler("Function GetTime")

af.name: LineItem_AddElement
af.g:
Dim Lie, nLie
LineItem_AddElement = True
strParam = trim(strParam)
WriteLog(Space(2) & "Starting LineItem_AddElement")
For Lie = 0 to ubound(g_aLineItems)
if g_aLineItems(Lie) = strParam then
writelog(space(7) & "Element already exists in Line Item Element Array.")
exit Function
end if
Next 'Lie
WriteLog(space(5) & "Adding Element '" & strparam & "' to Line Item Element Array.")
nLie = ubound(g_aLineItems)
Redim Preserve g_aLineItems(nLie + 1)
g_aLineItems(nLie) = strParam
Call ErrorHandler("Function LineItem_AddElement")
WriteLog(space(2) & "LineItem_AddElement Finished TRUE. Added element " & nLie & " '" & strparam & "'.")

af.name: LineItem_BlankFields
af.g:
Dim Lie, nLie
LineItem_BlankFields = False
StrParam = Trim(Strparam)
WriteLog(Space(2) & "Starting LineItem_BlankFields")
If Not Isnumeric(StrParam) then
Writelog("Parameter must be NUMERIC")
Exit Function
End if
LineItem_BlankFields = TRUE
StrParam = cint(StrParam)
WriteLog(space(5) & "Adding '" & StrParam & "' blank field Elements to Line Item Element Array.")
For Cntr = 1 to StrParam
nLie = ubound(g_aLineItems)
Redim Preserve g_aLineItems(nLie + 1)
g_aLineItems(nLie) = ""
Next
Call ErrorHandler("Function LineItem_BlankFields")
WriteLog(space(2) & "LineItem_BlankFields Finished TRUE. Added element " & nLie & " '" & strparam & "'.")

af.name: LineItem_SmartParameter
af.g:
Dim nLie
LineItem_SmartParameter = True
WriteLog(Space(2) & "Starting LineItem_SmartParameter")
For Lie = 0 to ubound(g_aLineItems)
if g_aLineItems(Lie) = strParam then
writelog(space(7) & "Element already exists in Line Item Element Array.")
exit Function
end if
Next 'Lie
nLie = ubound(g_aLineItems)
Redim Preserve g_aLineItems(nLie + 1)
g_aLineItems(nLie) = StrParam
WriteLog(Space(5) & "Adding SmartParameter " & StrParam & " to Line Item Array at position " & nLie)
If not g_dictLISmartParam.Exists(nLie) then
call g_dictLISmartParam.Add(nLie,StrParam)
End if
Call ErrorHandler("Function LineItem_SmartParameter")
WriteLog(space(2) & "LineItem_SmartParameter Finished TRUE. Added element " & nLie & " '" & strparam & "'.")

af.name: LineItem_ClearElements
af.g:
Redim g_aLineItems(0)
Call g_dictLISmartParam.RemoveAll()
LineItem_ClearElements = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function LineItem_ClearElements")

af.name: LineItem_ExportElements
af.g:
LineItem_ExportElements = True
WriteLog(space(2) & "Starting LineItem_ExportElements")
Dim n
Dim LieObj
Dim oVal
For n = 0 to ubound(g_aLineItems)-1
WriteLog(space(5) & "Exporting element " & n & ": '" & g_aLineItems(n) & "'.")
If g_aLineItems(n)<>"" then
If g_dictLISmartParam.Exists(n) then
Writelog(Space(5) & "Finding Smart Parameter Value")
oVal = MetaWord(g_aLineItems(n))
Call WriteExport(bInter, bDebug, oVal)
WriteLog(space(7) & "Value '" & oVal & "'.")
Else
Set LieObj = CurrentObj.FindChild(g_aLineItems(n))
If not LieObj is Nothing then
Call WriteExport(bInter, bDebug, CheckDICT(LieObj))
WriteLog(space(7) & "Value '" & LieObj.text & "'.")
Else
WriteLog(space(7) & "Element is NOTHING")
End if
End if
Else
WriteLog(space(7) & "Exporting Blank field.")
Call WriteExport(bInter, bDebug,"")
End if
Next 'n
Call ErrorHandler("Function LineItem_ExportElements")
WriteLog(space(2) & "LineItem_ExportElements Returns TRUE")

af.name: NewLine
af.g:
g_bNewLine = True
newLine = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function NewLine")

af.name: SaveFilePathAsVariable
af.g:
sPath = g_ExportPath & "\" & g_ExportName & g_ExportExtn
WriteLog("Saveing Export File Path as Variable " & strparam & " Path: " & g_ExportPath & "\" & g_ExportName & g_ExportExtn)
CurrentObj.Variable(StrParam) = g_ExportPath & "\" & g_ExportName & g_ExportExtn
SaveFilePathAsVariable = True

af.name: SetCSV
af.g:
dim sSmartParam
'Added support for Smart Parameters
sSmartParam=MetaWord(strParam)
If sSmartParam<>"" Then
strParam=sSmartParam
Else
Writelog("No result from Smart Parameter parsing. Using original parameter '" & strparam & "'")
End if
StrParam = Trim(Ucase(StrParam))
If len(Trim(StrParam))=0 then
Writelog("Parameter is Empty. Exiting Action.")
SetCSV = False
Exit Function
End if
If StrParam = "TRUE" Or StrParam = "FALSE" or StrParam = "ON" or StrParam = "OFF" Then
g_CSVformat = strParam
Else
SetCSV = False
End If
SetCSV = True
WriteLog("Comma Separated file output is set to " & g_CSVformat)
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetCSV")

af.name: SetElementSeparator
af.g:
'Added support for Smart Parameters
sSmartParam=MetaWord(strParam)
If sSmartParam<>"" Then
StrParam=sSmartParam
Else
Writelog("No result from Smart Parameter parsing. Using original parameter '" & StrParam & "'")
End if
if ucase(trim(StrParam)) = "OFF" or ucase(trim(StrParam)) = "FALSE" then
g_ElementSeparator = Space(1)
g_CSVformat = "OFF"
else
if ucase(trim(StrParam)) = "ON" or ucase(trim(StrParam)) = "TRUE" then
StrParam = Space(1)
end if
g_ElementSeparator = StrParam
g_CSVformat = "OTHER"
end if
SetElementSeparator= True
WriteLog("Element Separator is '" & StrParam & "'.")
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetElementSeparator")

af.name: SetExportPath
af.g:
Dim sDriveName
Dim sSmartParam
WriteLog("SET EXPORT PATH")
SetExportPath = False
'Added support for Smart Parameters
sSmartParam=MetaWord(strParam)
If sSmartParam<>"" Then
strParam=sSmartParam
Else
Writelog("No result from Smart Parameter parsing. Using original parameter '" & strparam & "'")
End if
sDriveName = FileMgr.GetDriveName(strParam)
If Not FileMgr.DriveExists(sDriveName) Then
writelog(Space(5) & "SET EXPORT PATH FAILED. NO SUCH DRIVE : " & strParam)
SetExportPath = False
Exit Function
End If
If FileMgr.FolderExists(strParam) Then
writelog(Space(5) & "Folder Exists. Setting Export path to: " & strParam)
g_ExportPath = strParam
SetExportPath = True
Else
writelog(Space(5) & "Folder does Not Exist. Beginning MakePath Function.")
If MakePath(strParam) Then
SetExportPath = True
g_ExportPath = strParam
End If
End If
WriteLog("END Set Export Path")
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetExportPath")

af.name: SetExtensionName
af.g:
Dim i, nChar
On error resume Next
SetExtensionName=False
'Added support for Smart Parameters
sSmartParam=MetaWord(strParam)
If sSmartParam<>"" Then
strParam=sSmartParam
Else
Writelog("No result from Smart Parameter parsing. Using original parameter '" & strparam & "'")
End if
g_ExportExtn = Trim(StrParam)
If len(g_ExportExtn)>0 then
While left(g_ExportExtn,1)="."
g_ExportExtn = Right(g_ExportExtn,len(g_ExportExtn)-1)
Wend
End if
'Check for windows prohibited file name characters *<>[]"/|\:? and control characters '\p{C}'
sPattern = "\*\<\>\[\]\/\|\\:\?"""
If DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(g_ExportExtn,"[" & sPattern & "\p{C}]") then
Call writelog("Invalid Characters found in extension name '*<>[]""/|\:?' or control characters. Exiting function with Status FAILED.")
Exit Function
End if
Writelog("Setting Export File Extension Name to : " & g_ExportExtn)
g_ExportExtn = "." & g_ExportExtn
SetExtensionName = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetExtensionName")

af.name: SetFileName
af.g:
g_ExportName = ""
on error resume next
'Added support for Smart Parameters
sSmartParam=MetaWord(strParam)
If sSmartParam<>"" Then
g_ExportName=Trim(sSmartParam)
Else
Writelog("No result from Smart Parameter parsing. Using original parameter '" & strparam & "'")
If instr(strParam,",") > 0 or left(StrParam,1) = "@" or left(StrParam,1) = "#" then
Dim aStrParam
Dim n
aStrParam = Split(StrParam & ",",",")
For n = 0 to ubound(aStrParam) - 1
Dim sArg
sArg = ucase(trim(aStrParam(n)))
WriteLog("Processing Arg# " & n & ". Argument: " & sArg)
if len(sArg) = 0 then exit For
if left(sArg,1) = "@" then
Select Case sArg
Case "@BATCHID"
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & replace(Pilot.BatchID,".","")
WriteLog("Adding BatchID to Export File Name")
Case "@ID"
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & CurrentObj.ID
WriteLog("Adding Object ID to Export File Name")
Case "@STATUS"
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & CurrentObj.Status
WriteLog("Adding Object Status to Export File Name")
Case "@TYPE"
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & CurrentObj.Type
WriteLog("Adding Object Type to Export File Name")
Case "@DATE"
n = n + 1
sArg = Trim(aStrParam(n))
if len(sArg) = 0 then sArg= "mm/dd/yyyy"
If InStr(sArg,"*")>0 Then sArg= "mm/dd/yyyy"
sArg= LCase(sArg)
sArg= Replace(sArg,"c","y")
sArg= Replace(sArg," "," & Chrw(32) &")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"/"," & Chrw(47) &")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"& &","&")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"day","dd")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"month","mm")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"year","yyyy")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"julian","y")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"jjj","y")
WriteLog("Export filename DateStamp = '" & sArg & "' ")
d = Day(Now)
dd = Right("0" & d,2)
yyyy = Year(Now)
yy = Right(yyyy,2)
m = Month(Now)
mm = Right("0" & m,2)
ccyy = yyyy
y = DatePart("y",Now)
DateVal = Eval(sArg)
DateVal = Replace(DateVal ," ","")
DateVal = Replace(DateVal ,"/","")
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & DateVal
Case "@TIME"
n = n + 1
sArg = Trim(aStrParam(n))
if len(sArg) = 0 then sArg= "HH:MM:SS"
If Trim(sArg) = "*" Then sArg= "HH:MM:SS"
sArg= LCase(sArg)
sArg= Replace(sArg,"/"," & Chrw(47) &")
sArg= Replace(sArg," "," & Chrw(32) &")
sArg= Replace(sArg,":"," & Chrw(58) &")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"& &","&")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"min","mm")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"minute","mm")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"sec","ss")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"second","ss")
sArg= Replace(sArg,"hr","hh")
WriteLog("TimeStamp sArg= '" & sArg& "' ")
m = Minute(Now)
s = Second(Now)
h = Hour(Now)
hhhh = hh
mm = Right("0" & m,2)
ss = Right("0" & s,2)
hh = Right("0" & h,2)
TimeText = Eval(sArg)
TimeText = Replace(TimeText ,"/","")
TimeText = Replace(TimeText ," ","")
TimeText = Replace(TimeText ,":","")
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & TimeText
Case "@VALUE"
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & CheckDICT(CurrentObj)
WriteLog("Adding Object Text to Export File Name")
End Select
elseif left(sArg,1) = "#" then
Dim oObj
Set oObj = Nothing
Set oObj = CurrentObj.FindChild(replace(sArg,"#",""))
if not oObj is Nothing then
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & CheckDICT(oObj)
WriteLog("Adding Field Value '" & oObj.Text & "' to Export File Name")
end if
else
g_ExportName = g_ExportName & sArg
end if
Next 'n
else
g_ExportName = Trim(StrParam)
end if
End if
if len(trim(g_ExportName))=0 then
WriteLog("Export Name has no value. Setting to Default 'Export'")
g_ExportName = "Export"
end if
Writelog("Setting Export File Name to : " & g_ExportName)
SetFileName = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetFileName")

af.name: SetOMR_Separator
af.g:
g_OMRSepChar = StrParam
DCO.Variable("g_OMRSepChar")=StrParam
Writelog("OMR Separation Character is set to '" & StrParam & "' ")
SetOMR_Separator = True

af.name: Variable_ExportValue
af.g:
Dim sValue
Variable_ExportValue = False
If len(strParam)=0 then
Writelog("Parameter is Empty. Exiting.")
Exit Function
End if
WriteLog("EXPORT Variable: " & StrParam)
sValue = ""
If CurrentObj.FindVariable(Strparam)>0 then
sValue = CurrentObj.Variable(Strparam)

Else
Writelog("Variable Not Found.")

af.name: Variable_IsValue
af.g:
Dim aStrParam
Dim sVarName
Dim sMatchVal
Dim sCMD
Dim sFoundVal
On Error Resume Next
Variable_IsValue = False
WriteLog(space(2) & "Starting Function Variable_IsValue")
If len(strParam)=0 then
Writelog("Parameter is Empty. Exiting.")
Exit Function
End if
aStrParam = Split(strParam & "," ,",")
sVarName = trim(aStrParam(0))
sMatchVal = trim(aStrParam(1))
WriteLog(space(4) & "Find Variable: " & sVarName)
WriteLog(space(4) & " Match Value: " & sMatchVal)
If len(sVarName)=0 then
Writelog("Variable name is Empty. Exiting.")
Exit Function
End if
If len(sMatchVal)=0 then
Writelog("Match value is Empty. Exiting.")
Exit Function
End if
If CurrentObj.FindVariable(sVarName)<=0 then
Writelog("Variable does not Exist. Exiting.")
Exit Function
End if
sFoundVal = cstr(CurrentObj.Variable(sVarName))
WriteLog(space(4) & "Variable Value: " & sFoundVal)
if sFoundVal = sMatchVal then Variable_IsValue = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function Variable_IsValue")
WriteLog(space(2) & "Variable_IsValue returns " & Variable_IsValue)

af.name: SetFixedLength
af.g:

af.name: SetJustified

af.name: FixedLenLJ

af.name: FixedLenRJ

af.name: Filler
af.g:
'StrParams is a 2 part CSV of the length and optional character for export
'If no character is specified the last global Fill character setting is used.
Dim sFiller
Dim sChar
Dim aParams
Dim nLength
Dim tLength
On Error Resume Next
Writelog("Filler Input: " & StrParam)
Filler=False
aParams = Split(StrParam & ",",",")
nLength = Trim(aParams(0))
sChar = Trim(aParams(1))
If Not IsNumeric(nLength) Then
Writelog("Invalid Parameter '" & nLength & "'. Numeric value expected. Exiting Action.")
Exit function
Else
tLength = g_FixedLen
g_FixedLen = nLength
End if
Select Case len(sChar)
Case 0
sChar = g_SetFill
Case 1
'Value is ok. Continue Action.
Case Else
Writelog("Invalid Fill Character Parameter '" & sChar & "'. Single charcter expected. Exiting Action.")
Exit function
End Select
sFiller = String(nLength,sChar)
If Text(bInter, bDebug, sFiller) = False then Exit Function
Call ErrorHandler("Function Filler")
g_FixedLen = tLength
Filler = True

f.name: SetExportFileEncodingAsASCII
f.g:
On Error Resume Next
SetExportFileEncodingAsASCII=TRUE
Dim mStrParam
'Determines if a file uses ANSI or Unicode encoding.
mStrParam = MetaWord(ASCIIEncoding)
If mStrParam<>"" then ASCIIEncoding = mStrParam
if UCase(ASCIIEncoding) = "TRUE" Then
g_ExportFileEncoding = g_exportASCII
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "' Setting to Export file encoding to ASCII")
else
g_ExportFileEncoding = g_exportUNICODE
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "' Setting to Export file encoding to UNICODE")
end if
SetExportFileEncodingAsASCII = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function SetExportFileEncodingAsASCII")

af.name: AddRecord
af.g:
Dim sSQL
Dim sClm
AddRecord = False
Writelog("Add Record...")
Writelog("oConn.State = " & oConn.State)
On Error Resume Next
If oConn.State = 0 Then
Writelog("Connection is Closed. Trying to open...")
If Not ExportOpenConnection(bInteractive, bDebug, g_sDSN) Then
Writelog("Failed to open connection. Setting status to abort.")
bAbort = True
Exit Function
End If
End If
sClm = GetColumnNames
If Len(sClm) <> 0 Then
sSQL = "INSERT INTO " & g_sTableName & " (" & GetColumnNames() & ") VALUES (" & GetColumnValues() & ");"
'Modify sSQL if DB type is Oracle - rrunner.rrx 7.6.42 function
sSQL = ModifySQLByDBType(oConn,sSQL)
Writelog(sSQL)
On Error Resume Next
Call oConn.Execute(sSQL)
Writelog("Post Execute")
If DBErrTrap(oConn,"ADD Record")= False then
AddRecord = True
Else
Err.Clear
End if
dictFldColumn.RemoveAll()
Else

af.name: ExportCloseConnection

af.name: ExportFieldToColumn
af.g:
Dim sColumnName
Dim aStrParam

Dim sStyle
Dim sQuotChar
Dim sValue
On Error Resume Next
ExportFieldToColumn= False
aStrParam = Split(strParam & ",,",",")
sField = aStrParam(0)
sColumnName = Trim(astrParam(1))
sStyle = Trim(aStrParam(2))
sValue = ""
If sStyle = "1" Then
If CheckColumnName(sColumnName) = False Then
ExportFieldToColumn= False
Exit Function
End if
End If
If sStyle = "2" Then
sQuotChar = "" 'no quotes
Else
sQuotChar = "'"
End if
If IsAlive(CurrentObj) Then
Writelog(Space(5) & "Finding Value of Field:" & sField)
Set oFld = CurrentObj.FindChild(sField)
If Not(oFld Is Nothing) Then
sValue=CheckDict(oFld)
Writelog(Space(5) & "Field Value is :'" & sValue & "' ")
ExportFieldToColumn= True
Else
Writelog(Space(5) & "Field Object Not Found.")
Writelog(Space(5) & "Current Obj is " & CurrentObj.ID)
ExportFieldToColumn = False
End If
Else
Writelog(Space(5) & "There is No Current Object.")
ExportFieldToColumn= False
End If
If (sStyle="2") AND sValue = "" then
Call dictFldColumn.Add(sColumnName, "NULL")
Else
sValue = replace(sValue,"'","''")
Call dictFldColumn.Add(sColumnName, sQuotChar & sValue & sQuotChar)
End if

af.name: ExportOpenConnection
af.g:
' OpenConnection was replaced by ExportOpenConnection.
On error resume next
Dim i
Dim sError
Dim sSmartParam
oConn.Errors.Clear
ExportOpenConnection = True
'Added support for Smart Parameters
sSmartParam=MetaWord(strParam)
If sSmartParam<>"" and strParam<>sSmartParam Then
'attempt to decrypt value
bRes = [securecall]sSmartParam,strParam[/securecall]
If bRes=False Then Writelog("Value not Decrypted.")
Else
Writelog("No result from Smart Parameter parsing. Using the original parameter string.")
End if
strParam = FormatADOConn(strParam)
If oConn.State = 1 Then
Writelog("Connection is already Open, Function returns TRUE")
Exit Function
End If
oConn.Open(strParam)
Writelog("oConn.State = " & oConn.State)
If oConn.State = 1 Then ExportOpenConnection = True Else ExportOpenConnection = False : WriteLog(sError)
Writelog("ExportOpenConnection returns " & ExportOpenConnection )
Call ConnErrHandler("Function ExportOpenConnection")
Call ErrorHandler("Function ExportOpenConnection")

af.name: ExportSmartParamToColumn
af.g:
Dim sColumnName
Dim aStrParam
Dim sProperty
Dim sStyle
Dim sQuotChar
Dim sValue
On Error Resume Next
ExportSmartParamToColumn= False
aStrParam = Split(strParam & ",,",",")
sProperty = aStrParam(0)
sColumnName = Trim(astrParam(1))
sStyle = Trim(aStrParam(2))
If sStyle = "1" Then
If CheckColumnName(sColumnName) = False Then
ExportSmartParamToColumn = False
Exit Function
End if
End If
If sStyle = "2" OR sStyle = "4" Then
sQuotChar = "" 'no quotes
Else
sQuotChar = "'"
End if
ExportSmartParamToColumn= True
'If sStyle = "3" Then
'Do Nothing --> Null value flag
'End if
If IsObject(CurrentObj) Then
Writelog(Space(5) & "Finding Property Value")
If sStyle = "4" Then ' Current DATE/Time
WriteLog("Current Date/Time")
dtNow = Now()
If (IsDBOracleEx("")) then
FormattedDateStamp = Right("00" & Month(dtNow),2) & "-" & Right("00" & Day(dtNow),2) & "-" & Year(dtNow) ' mm-dd-yyyy
FormattedDateStamp = FormattedDateStamp & " " & Right("00" & Hour(dtNow),2) & ":" & Right("00" & Minute(dtNow),2) & ":" & Right("00" & Second(dtNow),2) ' hh:mm:ss
oVal = "to_date('" & FormattedDateStamp & "','mm-dd-yyyy HH24:MI:SS')"
' should include hhmmss YYYY/MM/DD HH24:MI:SS
Else
'NON-ORACLE VERSION:
if IsDBSQLEx("") or IsDBDB2Ex("") then
'SQL Server or DB2 date/time:
oVal = "'" & Year(Now) & "-" & Right("00" & Month(Now),2) & "-" & Right("00" & Day(Now),2) ' yyyy-MM-dd
oVal = oVal & " " & Right("00" & Hour(dtNow),2) & ":" & Right("00" & Minute(dtNow),2) & ":" & Right("00" & Second(dtNow),2) & "'" ' HH:mm:ss
else
'Access date/tome:
oVal = "'" & CStr(dtNow) & "'"
End If
End If
Else ' not date/time (style <> 4), regular Smart Param parsing
oVal = MetaWord(sProperty)
End If
If Not(oVal = "") Then
Writelog(Space(5) & "Found Value is :'" & oVal & "' ")
Else
Writelog(Space(5) & "Smart Parameter Value Not Found.")
End If
Else
Writelog(Space(5) & "There is No Current Object.")
ExportSmartParamToColumn= False
End If
If (sStyle="2" OR sStyle="3" OR sStyle="4") AND oVal = "" then
Call dictFldColumn.Add(sColumnName, "NULL")
Else
if (sStyle = "4") then
sValue = oVal
else
sValue = replace(oVal,"'","''")
end if
Call dictFldColumn.Add(sColumnName, sQuotChar & sValue & sQuotChar)
End if

SetTableName("Invoice")

This ExportDB rule applies to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy.
The actions open the database and direct the rule's attention to the Invoice table. The rule then sets up a record with three values - Vendor ID, Invoice Number and Total. Afterwards, the AddRecord action updates the table with new information.
Note: A return of False means the record may not have been successfully exported, and needs to be followed by a "failure check" rule that typically would call SetTaskStatus(0) (or the rrunner action rr_AbortBatch) to ensure that the batch aborts.
All, but generally used at the Page or Field level.

Closes an open connection to the previously opened Export database.
Usually, this action is placed in a RuleSet that is separate from the RuleSet that opens the connection and stores the data.
For example this action could be placed into a RuleSet called ExportDBClose, and attached to a batch level close event which executes after all data has been exported from the batch to the specified database.
ExportCloseConnection()
This action closes the previously opened connection to the Export database.
This action is usually part of a separate RuleSet that prevents the need to repeatedly open the connection to the Export database. (You can open the connection once in the first RuleSet, export data from all documents and pages in the batch, then close the connection once in the second RuleSet.)
All, but generally used as part of a separate RuleSet at the Batch level.

Three comma-separated values:
1. The name of the field whose value will be stored in the column.
2. The name of the database column that will hold the value.
3. Optional: Can be set to the numerical value of 1, 2, or 3. If this parameter is not specified, quotes will be placed around the value in the SQL query to update the table.
Setting the value to 1 causes this action to return False if the Table name is invalid; otherwise the error will not be discovered until the action that performs the DB insert call, such as an AddRecord action, is called. This value would typically only be used in a development environment as it will increase processing time.
Setting this value to 2 allows NULL column values and inserts no quotes around values (for numeric) in the SQL query to update the database.
Setting the value to 3 allows NULL and if the column value is not NULL, the column value will be surrounded in quotes in the SQL query to update the database.

Opens a connection to the database specified as the parameter.
A rule containing this action can apply to any object of the Document Hierarchy, but it is most often used at the batch level.
ExportOpenConnection("@APPVAR(values/dsn/exportdb:cs)")
Note: This action must come before any other ExportDB actions. This example uses smart parameters to obtain the connection string from the application service where the custom connection string key "exportdb" has been created in the "Custom Values" tab. It provides a single location for the connection string and security for passwords.
Note: If the action is establishing a connection with an Oracle database, or a SQL Server database using SQL Server Authentication, be sure to expand the DSN parameter by adding the correct Provider, user ID and Password. For example:
Oracle
ExportOpenConnection("PROVIDER=ODBCORACLE;DSN=1040Look;CATALOG=;DBNTA=;UID=Admin;PWD=Admin;")
SQL Server Authentication
ExportOpenConnection("PROVIDER=ODBCMSSQL;DSN=1040Look;CATALOG=;DBNTA=;UID=Admin;PWD=Admin;")
Note: Although the Oracle and SQL examples show the connection string, it is recommended that a smart parameter is used to obtain the connection string from the application service, as shown in the first example, to provide password security and application portability.

af.g:
Dim NodeID
Dim sAttID
Dim aStrparam
Dim sFindValue
Dim sNodeValue
On Error Resume Next
xml_SetAttribute=True
aStrParam = Split(StrParam & ",," & CurrentObj.Type,",")
NodeID = Trim(aStrParam(0))
sAttID = Trim(aStrParam(1))
sFindValue = Trim(aStrParam(2))
sNodeValue = MetaWord(sFindValue)
xml_SetAttributeValue=XMLExport.SetAttributeValue(NodeID,sAttID,sNodeValue)
Call ErrorHandler("Action xml_SetAttributeValue")

af.name: xml_CommitNode
af.g:
On Error Resume Next
xml_CommitNode=XMLExport.CommitChildren(metaword(Trim(StrParam)))
Call ErrorHandler("Action xml_CommitNode")

f.name: xml_SetFileEncodingAsASCII
f.g:
On Error Resume Next
xml_SetFileEncodingAsASCII=TRUE
Dim mStrParam
'Determines if a file uses ANSI or Unicode encoding.
mStrParam = MetaWord(ASCIIEncoding)
If mStrParam<>"" then ASCIIEncoding = mStrParam
if UCase(ASCIIEncoding) = "TRUE" Then
XMLExport.ExportFileEncoding = False
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "' Setting to Export file encoding to ASCII")
else
XMLExport.ExportFileEncoding = True
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "' Setting to Export file encoding to UNICODE")
end if
xml_SetFileEncodingAsASCII = True
Call ErrorHandler("Function xml_SetFileEncodingAsASCII")

This action commits all unsaved nodes and saves XML file to disk. You must use this action to complete the creation of the export XML file.
Nodes that were not committed using the xml_CommitNode action will be committed to the parent node when xml_SaveFile is called, and will appear subsequent to nodes previously committed using action xml_CommitNode.
xml_SaveFile()

The new NodeID followed by the parent NodeID creates a new Node in the Export XML file.
The first xml_NewNode action in a ruleset will create the root node of the XML file using the new child NodeID, the parent NodeID must be blank.
xml_SetExportPath("C:\ParentDir\APT")
xml_SetFileName("@BATCHID")

xml_SetAttributeValue("B,id,@BATCHID")
The example above starts an export XML file that is named the same as the current batch ID. It has a root node "B" whose "id" is assigned the batch ID. It is expected that additional rules will continue to build the XML structure. The last invoked action must call xml_SaveFile to save the export file to disk.

String value of the xml Tag. Smart parameters are supported.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the XMLCommitNode action in the ExportToXML action library.
Commits (closes) current xml node to it's parent node with the xml tag value of the parameter. Allowing a new node with the same tag to be created at the same hierarchical level in the output xml. xml_CommitNode("LineTotal")
Example commits (closes) the current xml node with a Tag LineTotal.
Remember: Use of this action can change the expected order of xml nodes as they appear in the final xml, since this action commits the current xml to the parent xml node when it is called. Sibling xml nodes that were not committed using this action are later committed to the parent node when the xml_SaveFile is called, so those xml nodes will appear after nodes previously committed using the xml_CommitNode action.
All.
Always True.
If set to "True", then Export files will be created with ASCII encoding. "False" creates files with UNICODE encoding and is the default.
Smart parameters are supported.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the XMLSetFileEncodingAsASCII action in the ExportToXML action library.
Determines if the Export file is created with ASCII or UNICODE encoding. A parameter value of "True" will create files with ASCII format. "False" will create files with UNICODE format.
NOTE: This action must be called before any actions that physically write to and create the Export file. If not called, then the file will be created with UNICODE encoding.
xml_SetFileEncodingAsASCII("True")
xml_CommitNode("LineTotal")
This example will create files in ASCII format.
xml_SetFileEncodingAsASCII("False")
xml_CommitNode("LineTotal")
This example will create the file in UNICODE format.
Any.
Always True.

af.name: Library_IS_Initialize
af.qi: Initializes a previously defined, active Image Services Library.

af.name: Library_DS_Initialize
af.qi: Initializes a previously defined, active Document Services Library.

af.name: Library_DMA_Initialize
af.qi: Initializes a previously-defined, active DMA Library.

af.name: Library_LogIn
af.qi: Logs into the initialized FileNet library using the User ID and Password parameter values.

af.name: SaveDocToFolder
af.qi: Places the committed FileNet document in an existing folder of the open FileNet library.

af.name: AddTIFImageToDocument
af.qi: Adds an Image file to the new FileNet document.

af.name: AddPDFImageToDocument
af.qi: Adds a PDF Image file to the new FileNet document.

af.name: AddFileToDocument
af.qi: Adds a file to the current FileNet document.

af.name: AddAllImagesToDocument
af.qi: Adds All Document Page object Images to IS Document object.

af.name: IndexProperty_ID_DateComponent
af.qi: Sets up a Date element of the FileNet task’s processing index.

af.name: IndexProperty_LeftJUSTIFY
af.qi: Left-justifies a value that is being assigned to a target property of the FileNet document.

af.name: IndexProperty_RightJUSTIFY
af.qi: Right-justifies a value that is being assigned to a target property of the FileNet document.

af.name: Upload
af.qi: Commits the Active FileNet Document to the FileNet Library.

af.name: FileNETDocID_SetValue
af.qi: Assigns the FileNet Document’s ID.

af.name: GetDocuments
af.qi: Logs the names of the documents in the FileNet collection.

af.name: GetTopFolders
af.qi: Lists existing top-level FileNet folders in the current task’s Log file.

af.name: CreateFolder
af.qi: Creates a top-level FileNet folder.

af.name: FileNetDB_ADOConnect
af.qi: Establishes an ActiveX Data Connection object (ADO connection) with FileNet.

af.name: Upload_SetDelay
af.qi: Controls the delay between upload retries.

af.name: Upload_SetNumAttempts
af.qi: Control the number of retries for the FileNet upload.
