This action creates a new page that is a subset of an existing page or a subset of merged pages. Using the actions SetVirtualPageStartPosition and SetVirtualPageEndPosition, a segment of text from within the current page can be duplicated into a unique page. This approach can be useful to separate out a desired area of text to allow subsequent actions to work solely on the desired area.
A layout file is required to use this action and the CCO must be loaded from the layout file using the CreateCcoFromLayout action. The recognition of the layout file and creation of the CCO for the page can be performed in the same ruleset or in an earlier ruleset. Multiple pages within the same document can be merged together, using the action MergeLayoutByType, to create a multi-page segment of text to extracted into a new page. For example, it is possible to merge together 3 pages of text and create a new page that starts with text from the bottom of page 1, all of the text in page 2 and text from the start of page 3. When creating the new page, all of the text must be contiguous.
It is possible to create multiple new page subsets from a single page or single merged page. To do this, use the Start and End actions to define the start and end of a page, create the new virtual page, then define new start and end points, create another new page, etc.
The new pages that are created are no different than any other page. Actions that work on a page object can be used on these pages, allowing processing on these new pages as needed. For example, these new pages could be combined into their own new document and then processed with additional searches or exported.
When the new page is created, the image for the current page is copied to the name for the new page object and the new page object is added to the application's runtime DCO. The new page ID and associated image and layout file will use the name of the existing page with an underscore added and an number that is incremented if CreateVirtualPage is called multiple times on the same page. For example, "TM000001_0". CreateCcoFromLayout can be called on the new page and have additional rules run on it as needed.

CreateCcoFromLayout()
WordFind("Hello")
SetVirtualPageStartPosition()
WordFindNext("Good bye")
GoUpLine("1")
GoLastWord()
SetVirtualPageEndPosition()
CreateVirtualPage("MyNewPageType")
This example recognizes a page, creating a layout file. The CCO is created from the layout file and then Locate actions are used to find the first word to include in the new page. The start of the new page's text segment is identified by calling SetVirtualPageStartPosition. The end of the text segment is located. In this example, the word "Good bye" indicates it is the end of the desired text. Because the word "Good bye" should not be included in the new page, the located word position is moved to the last word of the line above the word "Good bye". SetVirtualPageEndPosition then identifies this new position as the end of the new page segment. Finally, the action CreateVirtualPage is called to create the new page. After this action completes, the new page will exist in the document hierarchy and can be acted upon by subsequent rules and actions.
Page level.
Returns True if the new page is created. Returns False if there is an error or if the start and end points for the block are not set.

This action assigns zone coordinates to a field based on previously set start and end positions that were identified using locate actions. Using the actions SetVirtualPageStartPosition and SetVirtualPageEndPosition, a rectangular segment of text from within the current page can be identified at run time and set as a zoned area. This approach can be useful to set the zone position of a field that is not a fixed location but can be determined by searching the recognized text to find the top-left corner and bottom-right corner of the zone area.
A layout file is required to use this action and the CCO must be loaded from the layout file using the CreateCcoFromLayout action. The recognition of the layout file and creation of the CCO for the page can be performed in the same ruleset or in an earlier ruleset.
Once the zone is set, it can be used just like a zone created from a fingerprint. Subsequent actions can be used to process the zoned text.
A field with coordinates set based on the contents of the recognized page can have many uses. One less obvious use would be for table identification when the table boundary is not determined by grid lines or the engine is not properly determining the table area even if grid lines exist. In this scenario, use the locate actions to determine the top-left and bottom-right coordinates of the table with steps similar to the example below. This will find the table location based on the text that exists on the page. There would need to be expected text or positions to identify the table boundaries. After calling CreateVirtualZone, then the field can be identified with the variable y_TableZone as described in the help for the OCR/A Recognize action to provide table boundaries for better table identification by making a second call to the Recognize action.

This example recognizes a page, creating a layout file. The CCO is created from the layout file. The Locate actions are used to create the boundaries for the new zone.
The action WordFind starts at the top of the page and it finds the first occurrence of the word "Hello". The search is case sensitive. If the word case can change, then a keyfile with different cases for the word and the keyfile locate action can be used to create find the starting point of the zone.
SetVirtualPageStartPosition causes the locate actions to remember that this word is the start of the zone. If the start should be the line under the word "Hello", then the action GoBelowWord("1") could be added to move to the next line to exclude that line, before calling SetVirtualPageStartPosition.
Next the locate action WordFindNext starts at the current locate location to look for "Good Bye". If that word is found, the action GoUpLine("1") selects the line just above the word "Good Bye", so the word "Good Bye" will not be included within the zone. The action GoLastWord moves the locate position to the last word on the new line. The last call is to SetVirtualPageEndPosition to mark the ending point of the new zone.
Lastly the action CreateVirtualZone sets the position for the field called "MyField" off of the current object, which is typically a page. The field zone position is set and the text of the field is set to the text within the new boundary. Only the text within the boundary created by the start of the word idenditified by SetVirtualPageStartPosition and the end of the word identified by SetVirtualPageEndPosition will be included within the field zone. If the field "MyField" does not exist, the field will be created.
Page or Field level.

Using the actions SetVirtualPageStartPosition and SetVirtualPageEndPosition, a rectangular segment of text from within the current page can be identified at run time and set as a zoned area. This approach can be useful to set the zone position of a field that is not a fixed location but can be determined by searching the recognized text to find the top-left corner and bottom-right corner of the zone area.
This function is similar to CreateVirtualZone but has the added feature that it will expand the left and right coordinates of the zone area to contain all of the text within the top and bottom area. For example, a page may have some section of text that needs to be zoned, however it is not possible to create a start point and/or an end point that is at the correct position to capture all of the desired text. A paragraph of text is one kind of area that does not have even text allowing creation of a zone that captures all of the text to the left and right. As long as it is possible to correctly locate the top portion of the text to capture and the bottom portion of text to capture, then this action will select all of the text between those two points and create that area as a zone.
A layout file is required to use this action and the CCO must be loaded from the layout file using the CreateCcoFromLayout action. The recognition of the layout file and creation of the CCO for the page can be performed in the same ruleset or in an earlier ruleset.
Once the zone is set, it can be used just like a zone created from a fingerprint. Subsequent actions can be used to process the zoned text for the field.
A field with coordinates set based on the contents of the recognized page can have many uses. One less obvious use would be for table identification when the table boundary is not determined by grid lines or the engine is not properly determining the table area even if grid lines exist. In this scenario, use the locate actions to determine the top-left and bottom-right coordinates of the table with steps similar to the example below. This will find the table location based on the text that exists on the page. There would need to be expected text or positions to identify the table boundaries. After calling CreateVirtualZone, then the field can be identified with the variable y_TableZone as described in the help for the OCR/A Recognize action to provide table boundaries for better table identification by making a second call to the Recognize action.
RecognitionRuleset
- Recognize()
- SetMaxCharacterHeightAVG("0")
- SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM("0")
- CreateCcoFromLayout()
LocateRuleset
- WordFind("Hello")
- SetVirtualPageStartPosition()
- WordFindNext("Good bye")
- GoUpLine("1")
- SetVirtualPageEndPosition()
- CreateVirtualZoneFullWidth("MyField")
Sample Page Text
Text Text Text Text Text Text Text Text
Text Text Text Text Text Text Text
Hello
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Good Bye
Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2
Explanation
This example recognizes a page, creating a layout file. The CCO is created from the layout file. The Locate actions are used to create the boundaries for the new zone.
The action WordFind starts at the top of the page and it finds the first occurrence of the word "Hello". The search is case sensitive. If the word case can change, then a keyfile with different cases for the word and the keyfile locate action can be used to create find the starting point of the zone.
SetVirtualPageStartPosition causes the locate actions to remember that this word is the start of the zone. If the start should be the line under the word "Hello", then the action GoBelowWord("1") could be added to move to the next line to exclude that line, before calling SetVirtualPageStartPosition.
Next the locate action WordFindNext starts at the current locate location to look for "Good Bye". If that word is found, the action GoUpLine("1") selects the line just above the word "Good Bye", so the word "Good Bye" will not be included within the zone. The last call is to SetVirtualPageEndPosition to mark the ending point of the new zone.
Lastly the action CreateVirtualZoneFullWidth sets the position for the field called "MyField" off of the current object, which is typically a page. All of the text between the top of the word identified by SetVirtualPageStarPosition and the bottom of the word identified by SetVirtualPageEndPosition will be included in the zone. This zone area is automatically enlarged to capture the full text to the left and right. The field zone position is set and the text of the field is set to the text within the new boundary. If the field "MyField" does not exist, the field will be created.
Using the sample page text shown above, this example will capture the following as the field text:
Hello
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Page or Field level.
Returns True if the zone is set on the field. Returns False if there is an error or if the start and end points for the zone are not set.
SetVirtualPageStartPosition, SetVirtualPageEndPosition, CreateCcoFromLayout, MergeLayoutByType

net.qi: : Actions that dynamically find text on the page after recognition
net.h:
The LocateText action library contains sets of actions that find text on a page.
The text can be found dynamically at run time and then found text can be loaded
fields.
The Locate actions use an internal word pointer that allows consecutive actions to be performed
to achieve a final goal. Typically, it isn't the search word that is loaded into a field,
but words around the search word, which may or may not include the search word.
For example, the locate actions can find the word "Total" on a page and then capture the word
to the right of the word "Total", which is typically a numerical value, and then load
the value and position into the field. This allows the field to be set on a page without having
to define an exact location using a fingerprint.
More complex rules can be created to move around.
In the previous case of looking for the value next to the word total, rules can be constructed that
will test the word after "Total" to see if it is numerical, if not, then the rules can look to the
word before the word "Total" and see if that word is numerical.
Locate actions require that the page text is recognized and a CCO is created
for the page before using them. Some locate actions require both a CCO file and a Layout XML file
to have been created before the action is called. Refer to the recognition action libraries to see how to perform
recognition and create CCO files and Layout XML files.
The locate actions keep an internal pointer to the word or phrase that is found. This pointer can be moved
around by calling the appropriate locate actions. If you find a word and want to move to the next word, this
can be achieved by the action GoNextWord. If the desired location is under the found word, the action
GoBelowWord can be called.
Review the supported level for the action you are using. Many actions operate on a page or field
level object, and other actions operate only on a field. When a locate action operates on a field,
that field must have a parent page object.
Refer to the top-level help of the ApplicationObjects action library for an overview of the Datacap Object Hierarchy (DCO).
Refer to the top-level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library for the smart parameter reference documentation.
♕ Smart Parameters ♕
Action parameters allow smart parameter specifications. The complete smart parameter
reference can be found in the top-level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library.
♕ Upgrading From Legacy Locate Actions ♕
If your application is using the legacy "Locate" actions, the following lists the LocateText
actions that replace them.
A task must use only the "LocateText" actions or the legacy "Locate" actions.
Actions between the Location action library and the LocateText action library cannot be mixed
as the functionality is separate.

method.name: AdjustZoneBottomToLowerBound
method.qi: : Adjusts the field's bottom position based on the currently located word.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action adjusts the zone coordinates for the current field.
The bottom zone position of the field is changed to the bottom coordinate position
of the currently located word.
If the field coordinates are currently
above the selected word, this action would have the effect of
extending the bottom of the field to just below the selected word.
The other zone positions will not be adjusted.
Depending on the original coordinates and the location of the word
relative to the field, other sides of the zone may need to be adjusted
to completely include or exclude the currently located word.
This action requires that a locate action from this action library
has previously been used to locate text on the current page.
The current field must have zone coordinates loaded.
FindWordOnPage("Hello")
AdjustZoneBottomToLowerBound()
If the current zone position is 100,200,300,400, and the located word
is at position 1100,1200,1300,1400, then the final zone's location
will be 100,200,300,1400.
method.ret:
Returns
False,
if there is an error. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: The ZonesAndLineItems action library contains additional actions that can adjust the zone.

method.name: CreateVirtualPage
method.qi: : Creates a new page from a subset of the current page.

p.name: PageType
p.qi: The page type to assign the new page.

method.ap:
The new page type for the created page can be optionally provided as a parameter to this action.
The provided name is assigned
as the type for the new DCO page that is created by this action. If no parameter is provided, the new
page type will default to "Other".
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action creates a new page that is a subset of an existing page or a subset of merged pages.
Using the actions SetVirtualPageStartPosition and SetVirtualPageEndPosition, a segment of text from within
the current page can be duplicated into a unique page. This approach can be useful to separate out
a desired area of text to allow subsequent actions to work solely on the desired area.
For example, a locate can be used to identify the start of a sub-page, and then another locate
can mark the end of the section. That area of text from the page can then be created into
a unique page of its own.
A layout file is required to use this action and the CCO must be loaded from the layout file
using the CreateCcoFromLayout action. The recognition of the layout file and creation of the CCO
for the page can be performed in the same ruleset or in an earlier ruleset. Multiple
pages within the same document can be merged together, using the action MergeLayoutByType, to create
a multi-page segment of text to extracted into a new page. For example, it is possible
to merge 3 pages of text and create a new page that starts with text from the bottom
of page 1, all of the text in page 2 and text from the start of page 3.
When creating the new page, all of the text must be contiguous in the same page.
It is possible to create multiple new page subsets from a single page or single merged page.
To do this, use the Start and End actions to define the start and end of a page,
create the new virtual page, then define new start and end points, create another new page, etc.
The new pages that are created are no different than any other page. Actions that work on a page
object can be used on these pages, allowing processing on these new pages as needed. For example,
these new pages could be combined into their own new document and then processed with additional
searches or exported.
When the new page is created, the image for the current page is copied to the name for the new
page object and the new page object is added to the application's runtime DCO. The new
page ID and associated image and layout file will use the name of the existing page
with an underscore added and an number that is incremented if
CreateVirtualPage is called multiple times on the same page. For example, "TM000001_0".
CreateCcoFromLayout can be called on the new page and have additional rules run on it as needed.
Recognize()
CreateCcoFromLayout()
FindWordOnPage("Hello")
SetVirtualPageStartPosition()
FindWordOnPageNext("Good bye")
GoUpLine("1")
GoLastWord()
SetVirtualPageEndPosition()
CreateVirtualPage("MyNewPageType")
This example recognizes a page, creating a layout file. The CCO is created from the layout file
and then Locate actions are used to find the first word to include in the new page. The start of
the new page's text segment is identified by calling SetVirtualPageStartPosition.
The end of the text segment is located. In this example, the word "Good bye" indicates
it is the end of the desired text. Because the word "Good bye" should not be included
in the new page, the located word position is moved to the last word of the line
above the word "Good bye". SetVirtualPageEndPosition then identifies this new position as the
end of the new page segment. Finally, the action CreateVirtualPage is called to
create the new page. After this action completes, the new page will exist in the document
hierarchy and can be acted upon by subsequent rules and actions.
method.ret:
Returns
True
if the new page is created. Returns
False
if there is an error
or if the start and end points for the block are not set.
method.see: SetVirtualPageStartPosition, SetVirtualPageEndPosition, CreateCcoFromLayout, MergeLayoutByType

method.name: CreateVirtualZone
method.qi: : Creates a new field from a subset of the page.

p.name: FieldName
p.qi: The name of the new field.

method.ap:
The name of the field which will have its zone assigned based on the previously set virtual start and end positions.
If the field does not exist, it is created.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action assigns zone coordinates to a field based on previously set start and end positions
that were identified using locate actions.
Using the actions SetVirtualPageStartPosition and SetVirtualPageEndPosition, a rectangular segment of text from within
the current page can be identified at run time and set as a zoned area. This approach can be useful to
set the zone position of a field that is not a fixed location but can be determined by searching
the recognized text to find the top-left corner and bottom-right corner of the zone area.
A layout file is required to use this action and the CCO must be loaded from the layout file
using the CreateCcoFromLayout action. The recognition of the layout file and creation of the CCO
for the page can be performed in the same ruleset or in an earlier ruleset.
Once the zone is set, it can be used just like a zone created from a fingerprint.
Subsequent actions can be used to process the zoned text.
A field with coordinates set based on the contents of the recognized page can have many uses.
A less obvious use is for table identification when the table boundary is not
determined by grid lines or the engine is not properly determining the table area
even if grid lines exist. In this scenario, use the locate actions to determine the
top-left and bottom-right coordinates of the table with steps similar to the example below.
This will find the table location based on the text that exists on the page. There would need
to be expected text or positions to identify the table boundaries.
After calling CreateVirtualZone, then the field can be identified with the variable
y_TableZone as described in the help for the OCR/A Recognize action to provide
table boundaries for better table identification by making a second call to the Recognize action.
RecognitionRuleset
- Recognize()
- SetMaxCharacterHeightAVG("0")
- SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM("0")
- CreateCcoFromLayout()
LocateRuleset
- FindWordOnPage("Hello")
- SetVirtualPageStartPosition()
- FindWordOnPageNext("Good bye")
- GoUpLine("1")
- GoLastWord()
- SetVirtualPageEndPosition()
-
CreateVirtualZone("MyField")
This example recognizes a page, creating a layout file. The CCO is created from the layout file.
The Locate actions are used to create the boundaries for the new zone.
The action FindWordOnPage starts at the top of the page, and it finds the first
occurrence of the word "Hello". The search is case sensitive. If the word case can change,
then a keyfile with different cases for the word and the keyfile locate action can be used to create
find the starting point of the zone.
SetVirtualPageStartPosition causes the locate actions to remember that this word is the start of
the zone. If the start should be the line under the word "Hello", then the action GoBelowWord("1")
could be added to move to the next line to exclude that line, before calling SetVirtualPageStartPosition.
Next the locate action FindWordOnPageNext starts at the current locate location to look for "Good Bye".
If that word is found, the action GoUpLine("1") selects the line just above the word "Good Bye",
so the word "Good Bye" will not be included within the zone.
The action GoLastWord moves the locate position to the last word on the new line.
The last call is to SetVirtualPageEndPosition
to mark the ending point of the new zone.
Lastly the action CreateVirtualZone sets the position for the field called "MyField" as a child of
the current object, which is typically a page. The field zone position is set, and the text
of the field is set to the text within the new boundary. Only the text within the boundary
created by the start of the word identified by SetVirtualPageStartPosition and the end
of the word identified by SetVirtualPageEndPosition is included within the field zone.
If the field "MyField" does not exist, the field is created.
method.ret:
Returns
True
if the zone is set on the field. Returns
False
if there is an error
or if the start and end points for the zone are not set.
method.see: SetVirtualPageStartPosition, SetVirtualPageEndPosition, CreateCcoFromLayout, MergeLayoutByType

method.name: CreateVirtualZoneFullWidth
method.qi: : Creates a new field that spans the entire width of the page.

p.name: FieldName
p.qi: The name of the new field.

method.ap:
The name of the field which will have its zone assigned based on the previously set virtual start and end positions.
If the field does not exist, it is created.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action assigns zone coordinates to a field based on previously set start and end positions
that were identified using SetVirtualPageStartPosition and SetVirtualPageEndPosition actions
and will expand the selection to capture all of the text to the left and right of the area
between the located top and bottom coordinates.
Using the actions SetVirtualPageStartPosition and SetVirtualPageEndPosition, a rectangular segment of text from within
the current page can be identified at run time and set as a zoned area. This approach can be useful to
set the zone position of a field that is not a fixed location but can be determined by searching
the recognized text to find the top-left corner and bottom-right corner of the zone area.
This function is similar to CreateVirtualZone but has the added feature that it will
expand the left and right coordinates of the zone area to contain all of the text within
the top and bottom area. For example, a page may have some section of text that needs to
be zoned, however it is not possible to create a start point and/or an end point that is at the correct position
to capture all of the desired text. A paragraph of text is one kind of area that does not have even text
allowing creation of a zone that captures all of the text to the left and right. As long as it is possible
to correctly locate the top portion of the text to capture and the bottom portion of text to capture,
then this action will select all of the text between those two points and create that area as a zone.
A layout file is required to use this action and the CCO must be loaded from the layout file
using the CreateCcoFromLayout action. The recognition of the layout file and creation of the CCO
for the page can be performed in the same ruleset or in an earlier ruleset.
Once the zone is set, it can be used just like a zone created from a fingerprint.
Subsequent actions can be used to process the zoned text for the field.
A field with coordinates set based on the contents of the recognized page can have many uses.
One less obvious use would be for table identification when the table boundary is not
determined by grid lines, or the engine is not properly determining the table area
even if grid lines exist. In this scenario, use the locate actions to determine the
top-left and bottom-right coordinates of the table with steps similar to the example below.
This will find the table location based on the text that exists on the page. There would need
to be expected text or positions to identify the table boundaries.
After calling CreateVirtualZone, then the field can be identified with the variable
y_TableZone as described in the help for the OCR/A Recognize action to provide
table boundaries for better table identification by making a second call to the Recognize action.
RecognitionRuleset
- Recognize()
- SetMaxCharacterHeightAVG("0")
- SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM("0")
- CreateCcoFromLayout()
LocateRuleset
- FindWordOnPage("Hello")
- SetVirtualPageStartPosition()
- FindWordOnPageNext("Good bye")
- GoUpLine("1")
- SetVirtualPageEndPosition()
-
CreateVirtualZoneFullWidth("MyField")
Sample Page Text
Text Text Text Text Text Text Text Text
Text Text Text Text Text Text Text
Hello
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Good Bye
Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2 Text2
Explanation
This example recognizes a page, creating a layout file. The CCO is created from the layout file.
The Locate actions are used to create the boundaries for the new zone.
The action FindWordOnPage starts at the top of the page, and it finds the first
occurrence of the word "Hello". The search is case sensitive. If the word case can change,
then a keyfile with different cases for the word and the keyfile locate action can be used to create
find the starting point of the zone.
SetVirtualPageStartPosition causes the locate actions to remember that this word is the start of
the zone. If the start should be the line under the word "Hello", then the action GoBelowWord("1")
could be added to move to the next line to exclude that line, before calling SetVirtualPageStartPosition.
Next the locate action FindWordOnPageNext starts at the current locate location to look for "Good Bye".
If that word is found, the action GoUpLine("1") selects the line just above the word "Good Bye",
so the word "Good Bye" will not be included within the zone. The last call is to SetVirtualPageEndPosition
to mark the ending point of the new zone.
Lastly the action CreateVirtualZoneFullWidth sets the position for the field called "MyField" off of
the current object, which is typically a page. All of the text between the top of the word
identified by SetVirtualPageStarPosition and the bottom of the word identified by SetVirtualPageEndPosition
will be included in the zone. This zone area is automatically enlarged to capture the full text to the left and
right. The field zone position is set and the text
of the field is set to the text within the new boundary.
If the field "MyField" does not exist, the field will be created.
Using the sample page text shown above, this example captures the following as the field text:
Hello
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
Text1 Text1 Text1 Text1
method.ret:
Returns
True
if the zone is set on the field. Returns
False
if there is an error
or if the start and end points for the zone are not set.
method.see: SetVirtualPageStartPosition, SetVirtualPageEndPosition, CreateCcoFromLayout, MergeLayoutByType

method.name: FilterCurrentWord
method.qi: : Removes characters from the currently located word or phrase.

p.name: filter
p.qi: The characters to remove.

method.ap:
A string containing the character(s) to be removed.
This action removes every instance of the character or characters from the currently selected word or phrase.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Removes all instances of each character you enter as a parameter from the located word or phrase.
The action directly modifies the currently loaded CCO file. Although the change will remain active
while the locate actions are being used, it does not change the saved CCO file. Once the task completes,
the CCO changes are discarded.
This action can be used to remove characters from the selected word or phrase prior to performing
a comparison test or prior to loading the selected phrase into a field.
Note: The ValidationsAndTextAdjustments library has a variety of actions that can perform
character manipulation of text for "cleaning" and validation, once the text is loaded into a field.
It may be easier to first update the field, then use the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments actions
to adjust the text as needed.
FindWordOnPage("Date")
GoNextWord("1")
FilterCurrentWord("-")
UpdateField()
Assuming the page has this text: "Date 31-Dec-01", 31-Dec-01 becomes 31Dec01
FilterCurrentWord("1")
31-Dec-01 becomes 3-Dec-0
FilterCurrentWord("1-")
31-Dec-01 becomes 3Dec0
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: FindWordOnPage, UpdateField

method.name: FindDatabaseListInZone
method.qi: : Searches the current zone for text obtained from a database query.

p.name: SQL
p.qi: The SQL query to obtain the search text.

method.ap:
An SQL statement whose result returns a word or phrase, or a list of word or phrases.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action issues an SQL query against a database, returning a list
of words or phrases that will be located within the current field. The search is performed
from the first word within the zone. Initially, the first listed word or phrase
is searched for on the page. If there is no match, it will search for the next word or
phrase returned from the database. This continues until a match is found or none of the returned words
are contained on the page. The location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
The search is case sensitive.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries. The action will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindDatabaseListInZone("Select LastName from Providers")
This example will obtain a list of last names from a provider table and find the first
matching occurrence within the page. If found, then that location will be used
by subsequent locate actions.
method.see: FindDatabaseListInZoneNext, FindDatabaseListOnPage

method.name: FindDatabaseListInZoneNext
method.qi: : Starting from the current locate position, searches the current zone for text obtained from a database query.

p.name: SQL
p.qi: The SQL query to obtain the search text.

method.ap:
An SQL statement whose result returns a word or phrase, or a list of word or phrases.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action issues an SQL query against the lookup database, returning a list
of words or phrases that will be located on the current field. Starting from the
location of a previously found word, the search is performed.
Initially, the first listed word or phrase from the SQL query
is searched for on the page. If there is no match, it will search for the next word or
phrase returned from the database. This continues until a match is found or none of the returned words
are contained on the page. The location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
The search is case sensitive.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries, i.e. will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindWordInZone("Hello")
FindDatabaseListInZoneNext("Select LastName from Providers")
This example will first locate the word, "Hello" in the current field. Once found, it will then
obtain a list of last names from a provider table and find the first
matching occurrence in the field that occurs after the word "Hello".
method.see: FindDatabaseListInZone, FindDatabaseListOnPage, FindWordOnPage

method.ap:
An SQL statement whose result returns a word or phrase, or a list of words or phrases.

method.h:
This action issues an SQL query against a database, returning a list
of words or phrases that will be located on the current page. The search is performed
from the first word of the current page. Initially, the first listed word or phrase
is searched for on the page. If there is no match, it will search for the next word or
phrase returned from the database. This continues until a match is found or none of the returned words

To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for

BatchOpenRule
-
DatabaseOpenConnectionForLocate(@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs))
FieldLevel Rule
-
FindDatabaseListOnPage("Select LastName from Providers")
- GoNextWord("1")
- UpdateField()
BatchCloseRule
- DatabaseCloseConnectionForLocate()
The example is a common paradigm for managing the database connection.
The database connection is created in the batch open event of the ruleset.
The example shows that the application's "Lookup" database is opened.
This database connection is preconfigured in the Application Manager.
Page level and field level rules will use actions that perform database queries.
FindDatabaseListOnPage obtains a list of last names from a provider table and
searches the page for the first matching occurrence on the page.
The current field is then updated with the match that was found on the current page.
Lastly, the database connection is closed on the batch close event.

DatabaseOpenConnectionForLocate,
DatabaseCloseConnectionForLocate,

FindWordOnPage("Supplier")
DatabaseOpenConnectionForLocate(@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs))

method.name: FindKeyListWordInZone
method.qi: : Searches within a field from a list of search terms.

p.name: FileName
p.qi: The name of the key file.

method.ap:
The name of the Keyword text file. The file will contain a list of words or phrases,
separated by new lines, that will be used for matching.
The file name can be provided in one of two ways:
1. A full path name of the file, including the ".key" extension.
2. The file name only, with no extension specified. The application will look in
the process directory and the file must have a ".key" extension.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Opens the Keyword file you specify as a parameter, then checks the
words or phrases in the current field of the source page's .cco file against the keywords
in the key file list to find a match. The location of the
found word or phrase that matches an entry in the keyword file
will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Matching is case sensitive.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindKeyListWordInZone("Line_Items")
This action searches the current bound zone for the
first keyword in the Keyword file (Line_Items.key).
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching for the next word in Line_Items.key, from the beginning
of the current bound zone, repeating this search pattern until
a match is found, or until there are no more keywords.
method.ret:
True
if at least one word in the current bound zone matches any
word or pattern in the Keyword file. Otherwise,
False.
method.see: FindKeyListWordInZoneNext, FindKeyWordInZoneLast, SetDynamicKeyList

method.name: FindKeyListWordInZoneLast
method.qi: : Searches the current zone for the last word that matches a list of terms.

p.name: FileName
p.qi: The name of the file containing search terms.

method.ap:
The name of the Keyword text file. The file will contain a list of words or phrases,
which is separated by new lines, and will be used for matching.
The file name can be provided in one of two ways:
1. A full path name of the file, including the ".key" extension.
2. The file name only, with no extension specified. The application will look in
the process directory and the file must have a ".key" extension.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Opens the Keyword file you specify as a parameter, then checks the
words or phrases in the current bound zone against the keywords in the list to find a match.
The location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Word matching is case sensitive.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries, i.e. will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindKeyListWordInZoneLast("ClaimsData")
This action searches the field for the
last instance of a match with the first keyword in the Keyword file (ClaimsData.key).
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching using the next word in ClaimsData.key, matching the last occurrence
of the word, repeating this search pattern until a match is found,
or until there are no more keywords.
method.ret:
True
if at least one word in the current zone matches any word or pattern in the Keyword file.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: SetAggregateKeyList, SetDynamicKeyList, FindKeyListWordInZone, FindKeyListWordOnPage

method.name: FindKeyListWordInZoneNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found word, searches the text in a field for a list of words.

p.name: FileName
p.qi: The name of the file containing the search terms.

method.ap:
The name of the Keyword text file. The file will contain a list of words or phrases,
separated by new lines, that will be used for matching.
The file name can be provided in one of two ways:
1. A full path name of the file, including the ".key" extension.
2. The file name only, with no extension specified. The application will look in
the process directory and the file must have a ".key" extension.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Opens the Keyword file, then checks the
words or phrases in the current field against the keywords in the list to find a match.
The search starts from the last word that had been found using an action such as
FindKeyListInWordInZone or FindKeyListInWordInZoneNext. The location of the
found word or phrase that matches an entry in the keyword file
will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Matching is case sensitive.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries, i.e. will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindKeyListWordInZone("Inventory")
FindKeyListWordInZoneNext("Parts")
This action searches the current field, starting from the first word of the zone, for the
first occurrence of a word or phrase in the Keyword file "Inventory.key". If a match is found,
the application will then look for a word from within the Keyword file "Parts.key",
starting from the previously found word from the FindKeyListWordInZone action and using the
first word or phrase in the "Parts.key" file.
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of the new word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching using the next word in "Parts.key", starting again from the
location of previously found word in the zone, repeating this search pattern until a match is found,
or until there are no more keywords in the file.

method.name: FindKeyListWordOnPage
method.qi: : Searches the current page for a word from a list.

p.name: FileName
p.qi: The name of the file containing search terms.

method.ap:
The name of the Keyword text file. The file will contain a list of words or phrases,
separated by new lines, that will be used for matching.
The file name is provided in one of two ways:
1. A full path name of the file, including the ".key" extension.
2. The file name only, with no extension specified. The application searches in
the process directory and the file must have a ".key" extension.
Smart parameters are supported
method.h:
Opens the specified file containing the search keywords, then checks the
words or phrases on the current page against the keywords in the list to find a match.
The location of the found word or phrase that matches an entry in the keyword file
will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Matching is case sensitive.
The search always starts from the beginning of the page, regardless of previous locate actions
that have been called. If the action is called on a field,
it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition reads "wi11", a match still occurs.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
By default, the action will search the entire page for the first word, then the entire page
for the next word, etc., until a match is found or all words in the keyfile have been exhausted.
The action SetAggregateKeyList can be called before this action to change the search behavior
so all words in the file will be searched for on the page, at the same time, providing
a faster search pattern.
FindKeyListWordOnPage("InvNum")
This action searches the current page, from first word on the page,
for the first keyword in the Invoices Number Keyword file (InvNum.key).
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching for the next word in InvNum.key, starting from first word
of the current page, repeating this search pattern until a match is found,
or until there are no more keywords. Once a word is found, that found location
can be acted upon by subsequent locate actions.
method.ret:
True
if at least one word on the page matches any word or pattern in the Keyword file.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: SetDynamicKeyList, SetAggregateKeyList, FindKeyWordOnPageNext

method.name: FindKeyListWordOnPageNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found word, continue searching the page from a list of terms.

p.name: FileName

method.ap:
The name of the Keyword text file. The file will contain a list of words or phrases,

method.name: FindRegularExpressionInBlock
method.qi: : Search a block of text for a word that matches a regular expression.

p.name: expression
p.qi: The regular expression to word match in the block structure.

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find on the current page.
The parameter is expected to be a Regular Expression.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The action locates the first occurrence of a word or phrase on the current page where the input search term
is specified as a regular expression, respecting the currently selected block of the document layout.
The search is started from the first word within the currently selected block.
Upon creation of the document layout the entire page is set as the currently selected block, making the
initial search area the entire page. Once the regular expression has been matched, the location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Additionally, the found word will become the currently selected word and the block region of that word
becomes the currently selected block area within the document block layout.
Subsequent "block" actions will act upon the currently selected block, allowing the area of interest
to be changed to control the area of the page that is the target of subsequent actions.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
It is very important to be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlock()
GoNextWord("1")
IsDate()
UpdateField()
FindRegularExpressionInBlock will look for the first occurrence of a word or phrase that matches the regular expression.
If a match is found, the next action will change the currently selected block from the found word to
the entire line that contains the word, then move to the right of the word.
If it is a date format, UpdateField will place the value into the current field.
method.see: FindKeyListWordInZoneNext.

method.name: FindRegularExpressionInBlockNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found position in a block, search for a word that matches a regular expression.

p.name: expression
p.qi: The regular expression to word match in the block structure.

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find in the current field. The parameter is expected to be
a Regular Expression. The search is case sensitive.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action utilizes the document block layout created by the Document Analytics actions.
Starting from the location of a previously found word or phrase, this action locates the first
occurrence of a word or phrase in the currently selected block where the input search term
is specified as a regular expression. Once the regular expression has been matched, the location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Additionally, the found word will become the currently selected word and the block region of that word
becomes the currently selected block area within the document block layout.
Subsequent "block" actions will act upon the currently selected block, allowing the area of interest
to be changed to control the area of the page that is the target of subsequent actions.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
It is very important to be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("ItemID")
SelectParentBlock()
GoParentBlockNext()
FindRegularExpressionInBlockNext("Description")
GoNextWord("1")
UpdateField()
In this sequence, the first action looks for "ItemID" starting from the beginning of
the currently selected block. If the search succeeded, the selected block is changed to the
containing line, then changed to the following line.
FindRegularExpressionInBlockNext looks for the first occurrence of "Description" within the line that
follows "ItemID", selects the word that follows "Description" and updates the current field.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionInBlock

method.name: FindRegularExpressionInZone
method.qi: : Search for a word in the current field that matches a regular expression.

p.name: expression
p.qi: The regular expression to match in the zone.

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find in the current field. The parameter is expected to be
a Regular Expression.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Locates the first occurrence of a word or phrase in the current field where the input
search term is specified as a regular expression.
The search is started from the first word of the current field. Only text within the current
field coordinates is searched.
The location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
FindRegularExpressionInZone("Da.e")
GoNextWord("1")
IsDate()
UpdateField()
FindRegularExpressionInZone searches for the first occurrence of a word or phrase that matches
the regular expression. If a match is found, it will continue processing by moving
one word right of the result of FindRegularExpressionInZone and act on that word.
If it the next word is a date format, UpdateField will place the value into the current field
and change the zone's coordinates to the new word.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionInZoneNext, FindRegularExpressionOnPage, FindWordOnPage.

p.name: expression

is specified as a regular expression.

Only the text within the field coordinates is searched.
The location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
FindRegularExpressionInZoneLast("Da.e")
GoNextWord("1")
IsDate()
UpdateField()
FindRegularExpressionInZoneLast search for the last occurrence of a word that matches the regular expression.

method.name: FindRegularExpressionInZoneNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found word, search the field for a word that matches the regular expression.

p.name: expression
p.qi: The regular expression to find on the page

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find in the current field. The parameter is expected to be
a Regular Expression.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from the location of a previously found word or phrase, this action locates the first
occurrence of a word or phrase in the current field that matches the regular expression.
The search is started from the location of a previously found word or phrase in the current
field. The search will be within the current field's coordinates.
The location of the found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be
used by subsequent actions.
FindWordInZone("ItemID")
FindRegularExpresionInZoneNext(".otal")
In this sequence, the first action looks for "ItemID" with the current field's coordinates.
If a match is found, FindRegularExpressionInZoneNext starts from the found word
looking for the first occurrence that matches the regular expression within the zone.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionInZone, FindRegularExpressionInZoneLast, FindWordInZone

method.name: FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZone
method.qi: : Search the current field for a word that matches a regular expression.

p.name: FileName
p.qi: The name of the file containing the search terms.

method.ap:
The name of the Keyword text file. The file will contain a list of words or phrases,
separated by new lines, that will be used for matching.
The file name can be provided in one of two ways:
1. A full path name of the file, including the ".key" extension.
2. The file name only, with no extension specified. The application will look in
the process directory and the file must have a ".key" extension.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Opens the Keyword file, then checks the
words or phrases on the current page against the keywords in the list to find a match. The
entries in the keyword file are expected to be regular expressions.
To perform the action, the search first looks for the first word or phrase in the keyword
file. If the word or phrase is found in the current field zone, the search stops. If no match is found,
the next line from the keyword file is read and again the current field zone is searched. This
process continues until a match is found or all of the lines in the keyword file have
been read. The location of the
found word or phrase that matches an entry in the keyword file
will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Word matching is case sensitive.
The search pattern can be changed to search for all of the words at once using the action SetAggregateKeyList.
FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZone("InvoiceNum")
This action searches the current page, from the first word of the current field, for the
first keyword in the Keyword file (InvoiceNum.key).
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching for the next word in InvoiceNum.key, starting from first word
of the current field, repeating this search pattern until a match is found,
or until there are no more keywords.
method.ret:
True
if at least one word on the page matches any word or pattern in the Keyword file.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionKeyListOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage, SetAggregateKeyList

p.name: FileName
p.qi: The name of the file containing the search terms.

Opens the Keyword file you specify as a parameter, then checks the
words or phrases in the current field against the keywords in the list to find a match. The
entries in the keyword file are expected to be regular expressions.
To perform the action, the search first looks for the last occurrence of the first word
or phrase in the keyword file. If the word is found on the page,
the search stops at the last occurrence of the word. If no match is found,
the next line from the keyword file is read and again the entire field is searched. This
process continues until a match is found or all of the lines in the keyword file have
been read.
The location of the last occurrence of a
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Word matching is case sensitive.

FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneLast("InvoiceNum")
This action searches the current page, from the first word of the current page, for the

If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching for the last occurrence of the next word in InvoiceNum.key,
starting from top of the current page, repeating this search pattern until a match is found,
or until there are no more keywords.
method.ret:
True
if at least one word in the field matches any word or pattern in the Keyword file.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZone, FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneNext, SetAggregateKeyList, SetDynamicKeyList

method.name: FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found word, searches the field for a word that matches a regular expression.

p.name: FileName
p.qi: The name of file containing search terms.

method.ap:
The name of the Keyword text file. The file will contain a list of words or phrases,
separated by new lines, that will be used for matching.
The file name can be provided in one of two ways:
1. A full path name of the file, including the ".key" extension.

method.h:
Opens the Keyword file you specify as a parameter, starting from the location of
a previous find, this action checks the words or phrases
in the current field against the keywords in the list to find a match. The
entries in the keyword file are expected to be regular expressions.
To perform the action, the search first looks for the first word or phrase in the keyword
file. Starting from the location of the last find, if the word is found, the search stops. If no match is found,
the next line from the keyword file is read and again the search starts from the result of
a previous find. This
process continues until a match is found or all of the lines in the keyword file have
been read. The location of the
found word or phrase that matches an entry in the keyword file
will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
Word matching is case sensitive.
FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZone("InvoiceNum")
FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneNext("InvoiceNum")
This action searches within the current zone,
for the first keyword in the Keyword file (InvoiceNum.key).
Next, starting from the word that was matched in the InvoiceNum.key file,
FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneNext continues searching, looking for a match from
the file InvoiceNum.key.
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching for the next word in Tax.key,
repeating this search pattern until a match is found,
or until there are no more keywords. Although this example shows FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneNext
using the same keyword file, a different keyword file may be used in the second search.
method.ret:
True
if at least one word in the field, that follows the result of a previous find,
matches any word or pattern in the Keyword file.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZone, FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneNext, FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneLast

method.name: FindRegularExpressionOnPage
method.qi: : Searches the page to find a word that matches a regular expression.

p.name: expression
p.qi: The regular expression to find on the page.

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find on the current page. The parameter is expected to be
a Regular Expression.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Locates the first occurrence of a word or phrase on the current page that matches
the regular expression provided in the action parameter.
The search is always started from the first word on the current page, regardless of previous searches performed. The location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
If the action is called on a field, it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
FindRegularExpressionOnPage("Da.e")
GoNextWord("1")
IsDate()
UpdateField()
This example assumes the rules are running on a field object.
FindRegularExpressionOnPage will look for the first occurrence of a word or phrase that matches the regular expression.
If a match is found, it continues processing by moving one word to the right of the match.
The next word is then checked to see if it matches a date format.
If it does match a date, then UpdateField will place the
value into the current field and update the field coordinates to match that of the found word.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionOnPageNext, FindRegularExpressionOnPageLast, FindRegularExpressionInZone, FindWordOnPage

method.qi: : Searches the page to find the last word that matches a regular expression.

p.name: expression

a Regular Expression.

method.h:
Locates the last occurrence of a word or phrase on the current page where the input search term
is specified as a regular expression.
The search is started from the first word of the current page.
The location of the
found word or phrase will be remembered so the result can be used by subsequent actions.
If the action is called on a field, it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
FindRegularExpressionOnPageLast("Da.e")
GoNextWord("1")
IsDate()
UpdateField()
This example assumes the rule is running on a page object.
FindRegularExpressionOnPageLast will look for the last occurrence of a word that matches the regular expression.
If it match is found, it will continue processing by moving one word right to the result
of FindRegularExpressionOnPageLast and act on that word. In this example, if it is a date format,
UpdateField will place the value into the current field.
method.see: FindRegularExpressionOnPage, FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, SetAggregateKeyList, SetDynamicKeyList

method.name: FindRegularExpressionOnPageNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found word, searches the page for a regular expression.

p.name: expression
p.qi: The regular expression to find on the page.

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find on the current page. The parameter is expected to be
a Regular Expression.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from the location of a previously found word or phrase, this action locates the first
occurrence of a word or phrase on the current page that matches the regular expression.
The search is started from the location of a previously found word or phrase. The
location of the newly found word or phrase will now be remembered so the result can be used
by subsequent actions.
If the action is called on a field, it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
FindWordOnPage("Item")
FindRegularExpressionOnPageNext(".otal")
In this sequence, the first action looks for the word "Item". If the search
succeeded, FindRegularExpressionOnPageNext starts searching after the found word
for the first occurrence that matches the specified regular expression. Subsequent
