method.name: FindTaxValue
method.qi: : Attempts to locate the numeric value for the Tax_Value field.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Attempts to locate the value for the Tax_Value field within line items.
The action finds the last occurance of the word in the "Tax_Type" field.
Next, the action will look on the page to the right and under the keyword until it locates
a word that is numeric. If it finds a numeric word to the right, or under the keyword,
it assumes that is the tax value and sets that found word to the Tax_Value
line item field.
This action is for APT and not intended for general use.
FindTaxValue("@P\")
method.lvl: Field level. The Tax_Value lineitem field in APT.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: FindWordInZone
method.qi: : Searches the current field for a word.

p.name: TextToFind
p.qi: Text to find on within a zone. Smart parameters are supported.

method.ap:
The word or phrase to find within the zone's boundary.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The current field will be searched to find the word or phrase. The location of the first
word or phrase that matches the parameter will be remembered so it can be
utilized by subsequent actions. Matching is case sensitive. Case sensitivity can be changed using the action SetFindCaseSensitivity.
The searching is performed within the boundary of the field's zone. If a match does not exist within the zone's coordinates,
a match will not be found.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries, i.e. will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindWordInZone("Sub Total")
GoNextWord("1")
IsCurrency()
UpdateField()
In this example, the FindWordInZone action looks for the first occurrence of
"Sub Total" within the current field, always starting at the first word of the zone.
If the phrase "Sub Total" is found, the subsequent actions will operate based
on the location of the found phrase. GoNextWord will move the internal position to
the next word, then it is tested to see if it is a currency. If it matches,
then the zones position is change to just the area for the found word.
method.see: FindWordInZoneNext, FindWordInZoneLast, FindWordOnPage

method.name: FindWordInZoneLast
method.qi: : Searches the current field for the last occurrence of a word.

p.name: TextToFind
p.qi: The text to find within the zone.

method.ap:
The word or phrase to locate within the current zone.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The current field will be searched to find the word or phrase. The location of the last
occurrence of the word or phrase that matches the parameter will be remembered so it can be
utilized by subsequent actions.
Word matching is case sensitive.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries, i.e. will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
The search will be restricted to the boundaries of the current zone.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindWordInZoneLast("Total")
GoNextWord("1")
IsCurrency()
This sequence attempts to find the last occurrence of "Total" in the current zone.
It then locates and validates a Currency amount for the Total field, assuming
the currency amount is to the right of the word "Total".
method.see: FindWordInZone, FindWordOnPage, SetFindCaseSensitivity

method.name: FindWordInZoneNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found word, searches a word in a field.

p.name: TextToFind
p.qi: The word or phrase to find.

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find in the current field, following a previously found word or phrase.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The current field will be searched to find the word or phrase, starting from the
remembered location of a previous find. The new location of the first
word or phrase in the field that matches the parameter will now be remembered so it can be
utilized by subsequent actions.
Matching is case sensitive.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindWordInZone(ItemID)
FindWordInZoneNext(Desc)
In this example, the FindWordInZone action looks for the first occurrence of
"ItemID" within the current field, always starting at the first word of the zone.
If the phrase "ItemID" is found, the word "Desc" will be looked for in the
current field, starting after the location of "ItemID". If "Desc" is found,
any subsequent actions will operate based
on the location of that found phrase.
method.see: FindWordInZone, FindWordInZoneLast, SetFindCaseSensitivity

method.name: FindWordOnPage
method.qi: : Searches the page for a word or phrase.

p.name: TextToFind
p.qi: Text to find on the page.

method.ap:
The word or phrase to find on the page.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The current page is searched to find the whole word or phrase. The location of the first
word or phrase that matches the parameter will be remembered so it can be
utilized by subsequent actions. Matching is case sensitive. Case sensitivity can be changed using the action SetFindCaseSensitivity.
Search starts from the top of the page, and searches down. The starting location is always the first word
regardless of previous locate searches that may have been performed.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries, i.e. will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
If the action is called on a field, it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindWordOnPage("Sales Tax")
GoNextWord("1")
IsCurrency()
UpdateField
In this example, it is assumed the rule is running on a field.
The FindWordOnPage action looks for the first occurrence of
"Sales Tax" within the current page, always starting at the first word of the page.
If the phrase "Sales Tax" is found, the location of the match will be remembered
and any subsequent LocateText actions will operate based
on the location of the found phrase. Here, the position is moved to the next
word on the page by the action GoNextWord. That new word is tested to see if
it is of a currency format. If it is a currency format, then the current field
is updated with the found word. The field's zone coordinates are updated
with the coordinates for the found word.
method.see: SetFindCaseSensitivity, FindWordOnPageNext, FindWordOnPageLast, FindKeyListWordOnPage

method.name: FindWordOnPageLast
method.qi: : Searches the page for the last occurrence of a word or phrase.

p.name: TextToFind
p.qi: The word to find on the page.

method.ap:
A word or phrase to find on the page.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The current page will be searched to find the last occurrence of a word or phrase.
Once found, the location of the last
word or phrase that matches the parameter will be remembered so it can be
utilized by subsequent actions.
This action will only match values with whole word boundaries, i.e. will not search for
parts of a word or characters within words.
If the action is called on a field, it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindWordOnPageLast("Total")
GoNextWord("1")
IsCurrency()
UpdateField()
This example assumes it is called on a field object.
This sequence finds the last instance of "Total" on the current page;
moves right one word; and checks to be sure that the word has a Currency value.
If the value is a currency format, it will update the field to contain the word
and the field's coordinates will be set to the word.
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindWordOnPageNext, FindWordInZone

method.name: FindWordOnPageNext
method.qi: : Starting from the last found word, searches the page for a word or phrase.

p.name: TextToFind
p.qi: The text to find on the page. Smart parameters are supported.

method.ap:
The word or phrase to find on the page.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The current page will be searched to find the word or phrase, starting from the location
remembered from the last search, such as from FindWordOnPage.
The search will be performed starting at the current location until a match is found, then the location of
the first word or phrase that matches the parameter, that follows from the last location, will now be remembered so it can be
utilized by subsequent actions.
Matching is case sensitive. Case sensitivity can be changed using the action SetFindCaseSensitivity.
If the action is called on a field, it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
To improve matching,
this action automatically adjusts the search criteria to allow for
common character substitutions. For example, if the list includes
"will" and the recognition read "wi11", a match will still occur.
Common substitutions include characters: B8, Z2, S5, oO0 and iItl1.
FindWordOnPage("Total")
FindWordOnPageNext("Total")
FindWordOnPageNext("Total")
GoNexttWord("1")
IsCurrency()
UpdateField
In this sequence, it is assumed that the rule is run on a field object.
The Locate rule locates the third instance of
the word "Total" in the current page. Once the third total is found,
the location moves to the next word. That new word is then tested to see
if it is a currency format. If so, then the field is updated with the text
and position of that word. Note that although this example shows
the same word being used in each search, there is no requirement for the words
to be the same, it is just an illustration.
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindWordOnPageLast, FindWordInZone

method.name: GetSelectedBlockType
method.qi: : Stores the block type name of the currently selected block in a variable in a field.

p.name: target
p.qi: The location to store the block type name.

method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter that defines the target variable to
store the type of the currently selected block.
method.h:
GetSelectedBlockType obtains the type of the currently selected block and stores it in the
DCO location indicated by the target parameter.
Important:
It is very important to be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure that is identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
The name of the block type is decided by the recognition engine and could change in future releases.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
GetSelectedBlockType("@X.SelectedBlock")
Finds the block that contains the matching expression and then stores
the name of the currently selected block in a variable called "SelectedBlock"
on the current DCO object. If the variable does not exist, it is created.
In this example, the name of the stored block is "Word" because
the currently selected block is the found word block.
method.ret:
True
if the type was successfully stored, otherwise
False.
method.see: IsSelectedBlockType

method.name: GoAboveWord
method.qi: : Selects a word above the last found word.

p.name: lines
p.qi: Word Movement Count.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the number of lines to move up. If the parameter is invalid, the value will default to 1.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from a word or phrase found by a previous Locate action, the location position is moved to a
word directly above it by the number of lines indicated by the input parameter.
Subsequent Locate actions can then perform additional operations on this located word.
Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action operates on the recognized
text for the current page.
Prior to calling this action, a Locate action must be used to set the starting word.
FindWordOnPage("Total")
GoAboveWord("1")
GoNextWord("1")
UpdateField()
This sequence finds the word which is the
Tax field's entered value ("29.78") when a fingerprint has these fields and values:
Tax
29.78
Total
234.70
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage, GoBelowWord, GoNextWord, GoPreviousWord

method.name: GoBelowWord
method.qi: : Selects the word below the last found word.

p.name: lines
p.qi: Word Movement Count.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the number of lines to move down.
If the parameter is invalid, the value will default to 1
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from a word or phrase found by a previous Locate action, the location position is moved
to a word directly below it by the number of lines indicated by the input parameter.
Subsequent Locate actions can then perform additional operations on this located word.
Regardless of being called at the page or field level,
this action operates on the recognized text for the current page.
Prior to calling this action, a Locate action must be used to set the starting word.
FindWordOnPage("Tax")
GoBelowWord("1")
GoNextWord("1")
UpdateField()
This sequence finds the word which is the Total field's
entered value ("234.70") when a fingerprint has these fields:
Tax
29.78
Total
234.70
method.see: GoAboveWord, FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage

method.name: GoDownLine
method.qi: : Moves to the line below the last found word.

p.name: lines
p.qi: Line movement count.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the number of lines to move down below the current line.
If the parameter is in valid, the value will default to 1.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from the current locate position, the location position is moved down by the number of lines indicated
in the input parameter and is moved to the first word of that line.
Prior to calling this action, a Locate action must be used to set the starting word.
FindKeyListWordOnPage("Invoice")
GoDownLine("1")
GoNextWord("1")
UpdateField()
This example assumes the rule is run a field object and this
is the page text:
INVOICE
Number: 10034
The sequence uses the word list in the "Invoice.key" file to
find a matching word on the page. Assuming the key list file has an entry "INVOICE",
the word is found. GoDownLine moves the position to the word "Number:".
GoNextWord then moves to word "10034" and UpdateField sets the field's value to "10034"
and sets the field's coordinates to the position of the word "10034"
method.see: GoUpLine, FindWord, FindKeyListWordOnPage

method.name: GoFirstLine
method.qi: : Selects the first word on the first line of the page.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Starting from the current position, the location position is moved to the first line of the current zone,
or to the first line on the page if a zone is not present. Subsequent Locate actions can then perform
additional operations from this position. Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action
operates on the recognized text for the current page.
GoFirstLine()
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage

method.name: GoFirstWord
method.qi: : Selects the first word on the line of the last found word.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Starting from a word or phrase found by a previous Locate action, the location position is moved to the first word
on the current line.
Subsequent Locate actions can then perform additional operations
on this located word. Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action operates on the
recognized text for the current page.
FindWordOnPage("Tax")
GoFirstWord()
The example first finds the word "Tax" on the page. It then selects the first word
on the same line that contains the found word "Tax". Subsequent Locate actions can
then take further action on the new position.
method.see: GoNextWord, FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage

method.name: GoLastLine
method.qi: : Selects the last line and word on the page.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Starting from the current position, the location position is moved to the last line and word of the current zone,
or to the last line and word on the page if a zone is not present. Subsequent Locate actions can then perform
additional operations from this position. Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action
operates on the recognized text for the current page.
GoLastLine()
method.ret:
False
if the source page's CCO file is not available, or
if it is empty. Otherwise,
True.
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage

method.name: GoLastWord
method.qi: : Selects the last word on the line of the last found word.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Starting from a word or phrase found by a previous Locate action, the location position is moved to the last word
on the current line. If the page's CCO does not have a line position, the action
defaults to the last word on the first line of the current zone, or on the first line of
the current page if a zone is not present. Subsequent Locate actions can then perform additional operations
on this located word. Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action operates on the
recognized text for the current page.
FindWordOnPage("Tax")
GoLastWord()
This example finds the first occurrence of the word "Tax" on the page, it then moves
the internal postition to the last word on the same line as "Tax".
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage

method.name: GoNextWord
method.qi: : Moves to a word on the same line that follows the last found word.

p.name: words
p.qi: Word movement count.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the number of words, that follow the currently selected word,
to position the internal located word position. If the parameter is invalid, the value will default to 1.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from a word or phrase found by a previous Locate action, the selected word location position is moved to the next word on the
current line by the number of words indicated by the input parameter. Subsequent Locate actions can then
perform additional operations on this new located word position.
Regardless of being called at the page or field level,
this action operates on the recognized text for the current page.
The internal location position is moved to the next word based on the reading order of the text.
The movement will be perceived as a right directional
movement on left-to-right text. The movement will be perceived as a left directional movement on right-to-left text.
Note: If the action is added with an empty or non-numeric parameter, the action will default the argument to '1'.
Prior to calling this action, a Locate action must be used to set the starting word.
FindWordOnPage("Tax")
GoNexttWord("1")
GoBelowWord("1")
UpdateField()
This example assumes the rule is called on a field object.
The locate action FindWordOnPage will search the entire page, from top to bottom,
looking for the word "Tax". Once found, the internal word pointer will move to the next
word, then to the word below the word. The field associated with this ruleset will have
it's zone coordinates updated with the position of the current word.
Given this scenario where the page has a table with columns such as Tax and Total similar to this:
Tax
Total
344.76
13,774.00
The actions above will locate the amount 13,774.00 and set the field zone to that word.
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, GoPreviousWord

method.name: GoPreviousWord
method.qi: : Finds a word on the same line before the last found word.

p.name: words
p.qi: Word movement count.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the number of words, that proceed the currently selected word,
to position the internal located word position. If the parameter is invalid, the value will default to 1.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from a word or phrase found by a previous Locate action, the current location position is moved to the previous words on the
current line by the number of words indicated by the input parameter. Subsequent Locate actions can then
perform additional operations on this new located word position.
If the action is called on a field, it will search the entire page regardless of the field's coordinates.
The internal location position is moved to the previous word based on the reading order of the text.
The movement will be perceived as a left directional
movement on left-to-right text. The movement will be perceived as a right directional movement on right-to-left text.
Note: If the action is added with an empty or non-numeric parameter, the action will default the argument to '1'.
Prior to calling this action, a Locate action must be used to set the starting word.
FindWordOnPage("Total")
GoPreviousWord("1")
GoBelowWord("1")
UpdateField()
The example assumes the rule is running on a field object.
The locate action FindWordOnPage will search the entire page, from top to bottom,
looking for the word "Total". Once found, the action GoPReviousWord changes the internal word pointer to the previous
word, then to the word below the word. The field associated with this ruleset will have
it's zone coordinates updated with the position of the current word.
Given this scenario where the page has a table with columns such as Tax and Total similar to this:
Tax Total
344.76 13,774.00
The actions above will locate the Tax amount 344.76 and set the field zone to that word.
method.see: GoNextWord, FindWordOnPage, FindWordInZone, FindKeyListWordOnPage

method.name: GoSiblingBlockNext
method.qi: : Selects the next sibling block from the last found block.

p.name: count
p.qi: Block movement count.

method.ap:
count:
The number of sibling blocks to move. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action utilizes the document block layout created by the Document Analytics actions.
The currently selected block in the document layout is changed to the next sibling block at
the same level in the structure. The number of siblings moved is determined by the input
parameter.
When a sibling block is selected, the currently selected block becomes the sibling block
and the currently selected word is changed to the first
word in the new block and that word may be in a nested block.
Any "next" type searches will start from the location
of this selected word.
For example, if the currently selected block is a line and the parameter is two, then the currently
selected block will move down two lines in the structure and the currently selected block
will be the sibling line and the selected word will be the first word in the new line.
If there is no sibling at that location,
then the current block is not changed, and the action returns false.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlockType("Block")
GoSiblingBlockNext("2")
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Qty")
This example finds the matching text for the regular expression "Da.e", then select the parent
block of type "Block". It then moves down two blocks of type "Block". At this point, the
currently selected block is a type block and the currently selected word is the first
word in that block. Then another search is performed within that new block for "Qty".
If Qty does not exist within the bounds of that new block, the action will return false.
method.ret:
True
if the sibling is found at the location specified from the currently selected block.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: GoSiblingBlockPrevious

method.name: GoSiblingBlockPrevious
method.qi: : Selects the previous sibling block from the last found block.

p.name: count
p.qi: Block movement count.

method.ap:
count:
The number of sibling blocks to move. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
The currently selected block in the document layout is changed to the previous sibling block at
the same level in the structure. The number of siblings moved is determined by the input
parameter.
When a sibling block is selected, the currently select block becomes the sibling block
and the currently selected word is changed to the first
word in the new block and that word may be in a nested block.
Any "next" type searches will start from the location
of this selected word.
For example, if the currently selected block is a line and the parameter is two, then the currently
selected block will move up two lines in the structure. If there is no sibling at that location,
then the current block is not changed, and the action returns false.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
Be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlockType("Block")
GoSiblingBlockPrevious("2")
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Qty")
This example finds the matching text for the regular expression "Da.e", then select the parent
block of type "Block". It then moves up two blocks of type "Block". At this point, the
currently selected block is a type block and the currently selected word is the first
word in that block. Then another search is performed within that new block for "Qty".
If Qty does not exist within the bounds of that new block, the action will return false.
method.ret:
True
if the sibling is found at the location specified from the currently selected block.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: GoSiblingBlockNext

method.name: GoUpLine
method.qi: : Selects the first word on a line above the last found word.

p.name: lines
p.qi: Line movement count.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the number of lines to move up above the current line.
If the parameter is invalid, the value will default to 1.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Starting from the current position, the location position is moved up by the number of lines indicated
in the input parameter and is moved to the first word of that line.
Prior to calling this action, a Locate action must be used to set the starting word.
FindKeyListOnPage("Invoice")
GoUpLine("1")
GoNextWord("1")
UpdateField()
This example assumes the rule is run on a field object and the page text contains:
Date: 2/13/03
INVOICE
This sequence first opens the key word file "Invoice.key" and searches the page for all of the
words within the file, locating the word "INVOICE".
It then moves up one line and to the next word, selecting "2/13/03".
The current word is then updated with the word and the coordinates of the field are
updated to the word's position.
method.see: GoDownLine, FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage

method.name: GroupNextWords
method.qi: : Expands the locate selection to include multiple words that follow the current word.

p.name: value
p.qi: Maximum separating width.

method.ap:
A numeric value indicating the maximum character width separating words to group that follow the current word.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Groups words that follow currently located word, if the target words are separated
by a character width equal to or less than the specified average character width.
The action only changes the internal size of the currently selected word being manipulated with the locate actions.
For example, if a word was located, this action is called and groups two words that follow the currently located word,
then all 3 words will be considered a single entity when performing subsequent actions, such as UpdateField.
All grouped words all become part of the current location. This means that if
an action to test the found value is called, or if UpdateField is called,
the entire grouped value is used.
When called on a field object, this action still operates on the entire page text.
The grouping of words is performed on the current line for words that appear after the current word based on the reading order of the text.
The movement will be perceived as a right directional
movement on left-to-right text. The movement will be perceived as a left directional movement on right-to-left text.
FindWordOnPage("US")
GroupNextWords("2")
If a line contains these words:
Found
20 000 US Treasury
bills.
the GroupPreviousWords action will merge "US" with "Treasury" to produce the selected word:
"US Treasury"
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: GroupWords, GroupPreviousWords

method.name: GroupPreviousWords
method.qi: : Expands the locate selection to include words prior to the last found word.

p.name: value
p.qi: Maximum separating width.

method.ap:
A numeric value indicating the maximum character width separating words to group that precede the current word.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action groups words that appear before the located word if the target words are
separated by a character width equal to or less than the specified character width.
This does not change the text on the page, and does not remove any characters or spaces.
The action only changes the internal size of the currently selected word being manipulated with the locate actions.
For example, if a word was located, this action is called and groups two words that precede the currently located word,
then all 3 words will be considered a single entity when performing subsequent actions, such as UpdateField.
When called on a field object, this action still operates on the entire page text.
The grouping of words is performed on the current line for words that appear before the current word based on the reading order of the text.
The movement will be perceived as a left directional
movement on left-to-right text. The movement will be perceived as a right directional movement on right-to-left text.
FindWordOnPage("000")
GroupPreviousWords("2")
If a line contains these words:
Found
20 000 US Treasury
bills.
the GroupWordsLeft action will merge "20" with "000" to produce the newly selected word:
"20 000"
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: GroupWords, GroupNextWords

method.name: GroupWords
method.qi: : Expands the located word selection to include words both before and after the last found word.

p.name: value
p.qi: Maximum separating width.

method.ap:
The maximum character width separating words to the right and left of the current word.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action groups words to the left and right of a located word, that are on the same line, if the target words are
themselves separated by a character width equal to or less than the average character
width you specify as a parameter.
All of the grouped words become part of the current location. This means that if
an action to test the found value is called, or if UpdateField is called,
the entire grouped value is used.
When called on a field object, this action still operates on the entire page text.
FindWordOnPage("Treasury")
GroupWords("1.5")
If a line contains these words:
20 000 U S Treasury 7 33
the
GroupWords
action will merge "20" with "000"; "U" with "S" and "7" with "33" to produce:
20 000 U S Treasury 7 33
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: GroupPreviousWords, GroupNextWords

method.name: IsAlpha
method.qi: : Returns true if the selected word has the amount of alphabetic characters indicated by the percentage.

p.name: Percentage
p.qi: An integer between 0 and 100, inclusive.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the minimum percentage of characters that must be alphabetic in the currently located word or phrase.
If no value is provided, the percentage defaults to 100; all characters must be alphabetic.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Using the current location of a previously located word or phrase, this action determines if the characters
are alphabetic. By testing the type of characters recognized in the current word or phrase, it is possible
for an application to determine it has located the type of data that is required, and then take
subsequent actions based on the result of the test. Regardless of being called at the page or
field level, this action operates on the recognized text for the current page.
FindKey(Name)
GoNextWord("1")
IsAlpha("100")
If the found word only contains alphabetic characters, then IsAlpha will return True and the next action will run.
If not, then the action will return False and the next function will run.
If the located word's recognized value is: ABC1
IsAlpha("75")
returns True
IsAlpha("80")
returns False
method.see: IsCurrency, IsDate, IsNumeric

method.name: IsCurrency
method.qi: : Returns true if the selected word matches currency values.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Using the current location of a previously located word or phrase, this action determines if the characters are in a valid
currency format and are a valid currency value. By testing the type of characters recognized in the current word or phrase,
it is possible for an application to determine it has located the type of data that is required, and then perform
subsequent actions based on the result of the test. Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this
action operates on the recognized text for the current page, ignoring the position of the current zone.
Note: This action is not dynamic locale aware and uses a simple regex and separator character test.
It does not confirm that the currency format matches the current locale format.
If the recognized value of the word or phrase is: 12.00
IsCurrency()
returns TRUE
If the recognized value of the word or phrase is: 12,00
IsCurrency()
returns TRUE
If the recognized value of the word or phrase is: 1200
IsCurrency()
returns FALSE
If the recognized value of the word or phrase is: 1,200.00
IsCurrency()
returns TRUE

method.name: IsDate
method.qi: : Returns true if the selected word matches a date format specified by the current locale.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Using the current location of a previously located word or phrase, this action determines if the characters
are in a valid date format and are a valid date. By testing the type of characters recognized in
the current word or phrase, it is possible for an application to determine it has located the type of data
that is required, and then take subsequent actions based on the result of the test. Regardless of
being called at the page or field level, this action operates on the recognized text for the current
page.
Note: This action is dynamic locale aware and will use the format allowed by the current locale.
If the located word's recognized value is: 01/01/2003
IsDate()
returns TRUE
If the located word's recognized value is: January 01,2003
IsDate()
returns TRUE
If the located word's recognized value is: 13/13/2003
IsDate()
returns FALSE
method.see: IsAlpha, IsCurrency, IsNumeric, FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpresionOnPage, UpdateField

Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action operates on the currently located word.
The action allows the rules to take different paths depending on the length of the located word.
If the recognized value of the located word or phrase is: ANYTHING

method.name: IsNumeric
method.qi: : Returns true if the selected word contains the amount of numeric characters indicated by the percentage.

p.name: Percent
p.qi: An integer between 0 and 100, inclusive.

method.ap:
An integer indicating the minimum percentage of characters that must be numeric in the current located word position.
If no parameter is specified, the value defaults to 100 percent; all characters must be numeric.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Using the current location of a previously located word or phrase, this action determines if the
characters are numeric. By testing the type of characters contained in the currently located word or phrase.
Using this action, it allows an application to determine it has located the type of data that is
required, and then perform subsequent actions based on the result of the test. This action
does not consider the decimal symbol, digit grouping symbol or a currency symbol to be
numeric. Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action operates on
the recognized text for the current page. If called on a field, it does not require
that the located text is contained within the field zone.
FindWordOnPage("Total")
GoNextWord("1")
IsNumeric("100")
Assuming the current page has the following text on a line: "Total $24.97",
the action IsNumeric will return False because it is not 100% numeric.
If the current page has this text: "Total 2497", then IsNumeric will return True.
If the located word's recognized value is: "#755"
IsNumeric("75")
returns TRUE
IsNumeric("80")
returns FALSE

method.name: IsSelectedBlockType
method.qi: : Returns true if the currently selected block type matches the name provided.

p.name: type
p.qi: The expected block type.

method.ap:
Type:
The name of the expected block type.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action utilizes the document block layout created by the Document Analytics actions.
IsSelectedBlockType compares the provided block type to the type of the currently selected block.
Important:
Be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlock()
IsSelectedBlockType("Line")
This example finds a word, selects the parent of the word and then confirms that the parent is of type "Line".
method.see: GetSelectedBlockType

method.name: IsValue
method.qi: : Returns true if the selected word matches the provided text.

p.name: match
p.qi: The word or phrase to validate against the current locate position.

method.ap:
The value to be compared to the object's recognized value.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Using the current location of a previously located word or phrase, this action determines if the
value matches the value of the input parameter. The locate found word consists of the
match that was previously located. If words have been grouped to the found item,
then this comparison will include those words as well.
The comparison is case insensitive, and the
comparison must match the entire located string, including grouped words.
By testing the value recognized in the
current word or phrase, it is possible for an application to determine it has located the data
that is required, and then perform subsequent actions based on the result of the test.
Regardless of being called at the page or field level, this action operates on the
recognized text for the entire page. It is not constrained by a field's coordinates.
Note: Match test is not case sensitive and does not include leading and trailing spaces.
FindWordOnPage("Houston")
GoNextWord("2")
IsValue("77770")
This example assumes the page has the following words on the same line: "Houston TX 77770".
FindWordOnPage always starts searching from the top of the page, regardless of the field zones.
First the first occurrence of the word "Houston" is found, then the location is moved over
two words and "777770" is selected as the located word.
IsValue then tests the current word to see if it matches the expected word, "77770".
If the word matches, then the next action is run. If it does not match,
then the first action of the next function is run. In this example, the word
does match "77770", which will then run the next action.
One common use case is to call "UpdateField" after a sequence of actions that locates
an expected word. UpdateField will load the current field with the results of the locate.
FindWordOnPage("Houston")
IsValue("Houston TX")
This example assumes the page has the following words on the same line: "Houston TX 77770".
First the first occurrence of the word "Houston" is found.
IsValue then tests the current word to see if it matches the expected word, "Houston TX".
In this example, the word will not match because only the word "Houston" was found by FindWordOnPage.
IsValue returns False and the first action of the next function will run.
method.see: IsValueInField, FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, RegExFind, UpdateField

method.name: IsValueRegularExpression
method.qi: : Returns true if the selected word matches the provided regular expression.

p.name: expression
p.qi: The regular expression to validate against the current locate position.

method.ap:
A Regular Expression that will be used for comparison with the recognized value of the word or phrase.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Using the current location of a previously located word or phrase, this action determines if the regular
expression provided in the input parameter finds a match in the value. By testing the value recognized
in the current word or phrase, it is possible for an application to determine it has located the data that is
required, and then take subsequent actions based on the result of the test. Regardless of being called
at the page or field level, this action operates on the recognized text for the current page.
FindWordOnPage("Houston")
GoNextWord("2")
IsValueRegularExpression(@STRING(\A...\d\d\d\d\d))
This example starts from the top of the page, and searches for the word "Houston", then
it moves over two words. The word two over from "Houston" is then tested to see if it
matches the regular expression. If it matches, then the action returns true
and the next action will run, if one exists. If it does not match, then the first
action in the next function will run, if one exists.

method.name: LocatePositionRestore
method.qi: : Resets the last located word and block to the previous saved position.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
LocatePositionRestore returns the internal locate word pointer to the word position it was on when
LocatePositionSave was called.
Using LocatePositionSave and LocatePositionRestore together
provides an efficient way to reset the position to a located word, when the subsequent locate actions
have moved the pointer to a located word.
For example, when rules need to look for text in multiple directions based
on a found word, these actions efficiently reset the internal locate
pointer to a saved position instead of performing the original locate action a second time,
which can require more processing time.
Key List Right 1 Function
+ FindKeyList("InvNum")
+ LocatePositionSave()
+ GoNextWord("1")
+ IsNumeric("60")
+ UpdateField()
Key List Down 1 Function
+
LocatePositionRestore()
+ GoBelowWord("1")
+ IsNumeric("60")
+ UpdateField()
This example shows two functions. The first performs a locate, saves the location, moves to the right and tests the word.
If the word does not match the IsNumeric criteria, then control falls to the next function which restores
the saved locate position to the word found in the previous "FindKeyList" action and then
looks in a different direction for a numeric value. Alternatively, the second function could have called
FindKeyList again, but the action to restore the last position is much more efficient.
method.see: LocatePositionSave

method.name: LocatePositionSave
method.qi: Creates a restore point for the currently located word or phrase and block.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
LocatePositionSave creates a restore point for the current word position of the locate pointer.
After calling additional locate actions that change the word location of locate pointer,
the previously saved position can be restored using the LocatePositionRestore action.
Using LocatePositionSave and LocatePositionRestore together
provides an efficient way to reset the position to a located word, when the subsequent locate actions
have moved the pointer to a located word.
For example, when rules need to look for text in multiple directions based
on a found word, these actions efficiently reset the internal locate
pointer to a saved position instead of performing the original locate action a second time,
which can require more processing time.
Only one restore point is supported, meaning you can store a point, then restore it. If you save a second
position, it will overwrite the previously saved position.
Key List Right 1 Function
+ FindKeyList("InvNum")
+
LocatePositionSave()
+ GoNextWord("1")
+ IsNumeric("60")
+ UpdateField()
Key List Down 1 Function
+ LocatePositionRestore()
+ GoBelowWord("1")
+ IsNumeric("60")
+ UpdateField()
This example shows two functions. The first performs a locate, saves the location, moves to the right and tests the word.
If the word does not match the IsNumeric criteria, then control falls to the next function which restores
the saved locate position to the word found in the previous "FindKeyList" action and then
looks in a different direction for a numeric value. Alternatively, the second function could have called
FindKeyList again, but the action to restore the last position is much more efficient.
method.see: LocatePositionRestore

method.name: RedactByRegularExpression
method.qi: : Redacts every word on the page that matches a regular expression.
method.ap:
RegularExpression:
The expression to search for on the page.
VariableBase:
A variable prefix to create in the runtime DCO to track each redaction.
All parameters support smart parameters.
method.h:
This action uses a regular expression to locate words on the page. All of the words that match
the regular expression are redacted. Each redacted location is tracked by a variable
placed into the parent document node in the runtime DCO.
This action must be called on a field that has a parent page and the page must have
a parent document. The field is used as a "working" location for the action. The zoned coordinates
for the field do not affect how this action runs. However, the action will change the zone
coordinate location of the field as it runs. It is best to use a field that is otherwise
unused in the application. Additionally, by setting the field's status to "-1", the field
will be ignored by verify panels.
The VariableBase parameter specifies a variable name to used to track the history of redacted words. For each redaction,
a variable of the form "VariableBaseN", where N is an incrementing number,
is created in the runtime DCO with the page ID and the coordinates of the redacted
word. For example, if the VariableBase parameter was "Hello", the variables created would be named: "Hello1", "Hello2",
"Hello3", etc. for each redaction. An example value of the variable value: "TM000001,159,1085,242,1115".
A CCO file must exist for the current page. The CCO must be created by a recognition action and contain the full page text.
As would be expected, this action operates on the recognized text. If text is recognized incorrectly and does not match
the regular expression, it will not be redacted. Consider using regular expressions that account for typical recognition
problems such as incorrect casing or substitution characters such as "0Oo" and "1l".
This action does not create a backup of the current page image prior to performing the redaction. If it is
desired to keep a copy of the original image, it could be performed with the CopyFile action in the
fileIO action library. For example CopyFile("@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+.tif", "@PILOT(BATCHDIR)+\+@ID+BeforeRedaction.tif")
RedactByRegularExpression("[Hh]istory", "Location")
This example will redact all areas on the page where the word "History" or "history" exists.
The redactions are tracked in the runtime DCO in a variable called Location0, Location1, etc.
An example of the DCO XML at the document level:
˂V n="Location1"˃ TM000005,771,1523,874,1559˂/V˃
˂V n="Location2"˃ TM000005,779,1602,882,1638˂/V˃
˂V n="Location3"˃ TM000005,778,1840,881,1875˂/V˃
method.ret:
Always
TRUE.

method.name: RemoveCharactersOutsideFieldZone
method.qi: : Removes characters that are not completely within the zone area.

p.name: RemoveNoPosition
p.qi: True: Remove characters with no position. False (default): Keep characters with no position.

p.name: TrimField
p.qi: True (default): Remove leading and trailing whitespace. False: Keep whitespace characters.

p.name: UsePageCCO
p.qi: True (default): Use full page recognition to check for word boundaries. False: Use character positions only.

method.ap: Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
RemoveCharactersOutsideFieldZone ensures that all of the words are completely within the zone. Any characters or words
that are only partially within the zone are removed from the field.
The action requires the field to contain text but it does not require a locate to be performed.
If the parameter UsePageCCO is false, the action strictly operates on the characters of the field. Every character must
be completely within the zoned area. If any part of the character is outside the zoned area, it is removed.
For example, when a field is recognized, text may be included if the top of the zone touches words, even though they may not
be fully within the zone. This action removes these characters from the field that are not completely within the zone.
Words that were truncated on the left or the right of the zone remain in the partial text within the field.
For example, if the word "Telephone" was along the left edge of a zone and only the letters "hone" were in the zone area,
then the characters "hone" remain in the field as the characters are completely within the zone boundaries.
If the parameter UsePageCCO is true, the action takes an extra step to remove truncated words.
For example, if the word is "Telephone" and because of the field boundary only the word "hone" is within
the field, the CCO is checked to determine if "hone" is a truncated word. Because the full word is "Telephone"
and the whole word is not completely in the field, the orphan text "hone" is removed from the field. This feature
requires full page recognition to have been performed and that the page CCO file exists with the text recognition.
If the CCO does not exist, this step is not performed.
Sometimes characters within a field have no "left, top, right, bottom" position, such as a carriage return character.
When parameter "RemoveNoPosition" is set to "True", characters with no position are removed. If set to "False",
the characters without positions remain within the field. The default value for this parameter is "False".
It is possible that a field may have leading or trailing white space and new line characters. When the parameter
TrimField is True, any leading or trailing white space is removed from the field text.
RecognizeFieldOCRPL()
RemoveCharatersOutsideFieldZone("False", "True", "True")
In this example, RemoveCharactersOutsideFieldZone is used to ensure that only text that is
not completely within the field zoned area is removed from the field text.
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: SelectParentBlock
method.qi: : Selects the parent block of the currently selected block.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action utilizes the document block layout created by the Document Analytics actions.
The currently selected block, which denotes an area on the page, is changed to the containing block.
This will effectively make the new area of interest larger than the previous area.
For example, if the currently selected block is a word, when SelectParentBlock is called, the
selected word remains the same, but the area of interest is changed to the parent block,
which would be the entire line. Subsequent actions that act on the current block
will now respect the line as the area of interest on the page.
Calling SelectParentBlock again would move the selected block to the parent of the line.
The block selected will depend on the layout of the page. One typical scenario is that the
selected block will now be a paragraph that contains multiple lines, including the word that
was previously found. Any block actions, such as additional searches, will be performed
within the boundaries of this newly selected paragraph block.
While the block nesting layout typically follows the same pattern, the layout of blocks
will depend on the layout of text on the page. For predictable results, the application
rules may need to work on expected layouts based on the page types supported by
the application.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
It is very important to be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlock()
SelectParentBlock()
UpdateFieldWithBlock()
This example assumes the rule is run on a field object.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock searches for the first occurrence of a word or phrase that matches the regular expression.
If a match is found, the next action will change the currently selected block from the found word to
the entire line that contains the word. SelectParentBlock is then called again to change
the selected block to the parent of the current line,
then the current field zone is updated to contain the entire set of lines contained in the current block
and the field value is set to all of the text within the current block.
method.see: SelectParentBlockType, SelectParentBlockOuterType

method.name: SelectParentBlockOuterType
method.qi: : Selects the outer block that matches the provided block type.

p.name: type
p.qi: The block type to select.

method.ap:
type:
The type of the outer most parent block to select.
method.h:
This action utilizes the document block layout created by the Document Analytics actions.
The action selects the outer most parent of the current block of the type that is specified. If the currently selected block
has multiple parent blocks of the same type, then the parent farthest from the current block would be
selected.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
It is very important to be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlockOuterType("Block")
In this example the selected block will be the one of type "Block" that is the
farthest parent to the block containing the found word.
The following is the list of block types: Document, Page, Title, Block,
Table, Row, Cell, Paragraph, Header and Footer.
Assuming the page contained this nested block layout:
[Page]
- [Block]
- - [Block]
- - - [Line]
- - - - [Word] "Date" [/Word]
- - - [/Line]
- - [/Block]
- [/Block]
[/Page]
The "word" block would be found, then the selected block would be the "Block" that is the first child to the "Page" block.
method.see: SelectParentBlock, SelectParentBlockType

method.name: SelectParentBlockType
method.qi: : Selects the nearest parent block type that matches the provided name.

p.name: type
p.qi: The block type to select.

method.ap:
selectType:
The type of the parent block to select.
method.h:
This action utilizes the document block layout created by the Document Analytics actions.
The action selects the parent of the current block of the type that is specified. If the currently selected block
has multiple parent blocks of the same type, then the parent nearest to the current block would be
selected.
If the current block is of the specified type, then the action will return true and the selected block
will remain at the current block. When starting a new search after performing previous searches, it may be useful to
call this action with type "Page" to reset the selected block to the page block so the entire
page block area can be searched again using the "block" actions.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
It is very important to be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
block structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlockType("Block")
In this example the selected block will be the one of type "Block" that is the
nearest parent to the block containing the found word.
The following is the list of typical block types: Document, Page, Title, Block
Table, Row, Cell, Paragraph, Header and Footer.
Assuming the page contained this nested block layout:
[Page]
- [Block]
- - [Block]
- - - [Line]
- - - - [Word] "Date" [/Word]
- - - [/Line]
- - [/Block]
- [/Block]
[/Page]
The "word" block would be found, then the selected block would be the "Block" that is the parent to the "Line" block.
SelectParentBlockType("Page")
Specifying "Page" will select the page block as the currently selected block.
When a previous locate has been performed, reselecting the "Page" block will
reset the block to the page node so the next action that searches within the
selected block will search the entire page. Use this if you perform
multiple, unique, block locates on a single page.
method.ret:
True
the specified parent block is found and selected.
If the current block is of the specified type, then true will be returned.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: SelectParentBlock, SelectParentBlockOuterType

method.name: SetAggregateKeyList
method.qi: : Controls searching of all 'List' searching, allowing for all words to be found in one pass.

p.name: AggregateSearchWords
p.qi: A boolean indicating key list search words should be aggregated together.

method.ap:
Toggles Key list searches to merge all words or phrases in the list into a single query.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Use of this action changes the search behavior for all 'List' type key word search actions.
The default search behavior is to search each keyword in the list sequentially. In this mode,
the page will be searched for the first word in the list, then the page is searched for the next
word in the list, etc.
Calling this action with the
parameter set to TRUE changes the search behavior to check for all the keywords in a single
aggregate keyword search. This causes the search to make one pass through the page, searching for
all of the words. The one pass approach offers a speed improvement over the default mode
as the action looks for all of the list words as it moves down the page.
To change back to the default behavior, use this action with the FALSE parameter.
SetAggregateKeyList(True)
FindKeyListOnPage("InvNum")
This action searches the current page, from the first word to the last word of the current page, for the
first occurrence of all keywords in the Invoices Number keyword file (InvNum.key).
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions;
if not, the action continues searching for the next word in InvNum.key, starting from first word
of the current page, repeating this search pattern until a match is found,
or until there are no more keywords.
method.ret:
Always
True
.
method.see: FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPageNext, FindKeyListWordInZone, FindRegularExpressionKeyListOnPage, SetDynamicKeyList

method.ap:
KeyFileName:
A name for the virtual key file that references the provided search terms.
KeyWordXX:
Up to 25 search terms can be specified for this virtual key file. These are the terms that will
be used for the search when a "KeyList" action is provided the KeyFileName.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Adds a list of keywords or phrases that can be used for matching with a "KeyList" action.
The list of words works the same as a key list file. The difference is that the words
are provided at runtime, allowing for a dynamically created key list file.
This action complements the List search actions that can load a Keyword text file which
contains a list of words or phrases, separated by new lines, that will be used for matching.
AddKeyList adds a list of up to 25 words or phrases without having to read or edit a file.
Note: You can not redefine or overwrite an existing key list.
SetDynamicKeyList("InvNum","Invoice Number","Inv. Num.","Invoice #:")
SetAggregateKeyList("True")
FindKeyListWordOnPage("InvNum")
This action searches the current page, from first word to the last word of the current page, for the
first occurrence of all keywords in the Invoices Number Keyword list "InvNum".
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions.
If not successful, the action continues searching for the next keyword in the InvNum list, starting from first word
of the current page, repeating this search pattern until a match is found, or until there are no more keywords.
method.ret:
False
if no keywords or phrases are entered, otherwise
True
.
method.see:
FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordInZone, FindKeyListWordOnPageNext, FindKeyListWordInZoneNext, FindRegularExpressionKeyListOnPage,
FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZone, FindRegularExpressionKeyListOnPageNext, FindRegularExpressionKeyListInZoneNext, FindKeyListWordOnPageLast,
SetAggregateKeyList

method.name: SetFindCaseSensitivity
method.qi: : Controls the case sensitivity of the 'Find' actions, except for those using regular expressions or key lists.

p.name: CaseInsensitive
p.qi: A boolean that enables and disables case sensitivity.

method.ap:
True:
Searches ignore the word case.
False:
Searches are case sensitive.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Use of this action changes the search behavior for all 'Find' type key word search actions.
Default behavior is a case sensitive search. This action with the parameter set to TRUE changes
the keyword search behavior to be case insensitive.
To change back to the default behavior, use this action with the FALSE parameter.
SetFindCaseSensitivity("True")
FindWordOnPage("InvNum")
This action searches the current page, from first word to the last word of the current page, for the
first occurrence of the word "InvNum" regardless of the character case on the current page.
If successful, the search stops and remembers the location of that word for subsequent actions.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
FindWordInZone, FindWordInZoneNext, FindWordOnPage, FindWordOnPageNext, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPageNext, FindKeyListWordOnPageLast,
FindDatabaseListOnPage, FindDatabaseListInZone, FindKeyListWordInZone, FindKeyListWordInZoneLast, FindRegularExpressionKeyListOnPage, FindREgularExpressionKeyListInZone,
SetDynamicKeyList

method.name: SetVirtualPageEndPosition
method.qi: : The last found word or phrase is set as the end of a virtual page or zone.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Use this action after performing Locate commands that identify the last word
of a new virtual page. This action requires that the page has an associated
layout file and that the CCO has been populated using the CreateCcoFromLayout action.
This action is expected to be used with CreateVirtualPage to build a new page using
a subset of text from the current page. See the help for CreateVirtualPage for
more details.
The start and end positions must be on the same page.
Recognize()
CreateCcoFromLayout()
FindWordOnPage("Hello")
SetVirtualPageStartPosition()
FindWordOnPageNext("Good bye")
GoUpLine("1")
GoLastWord()
SetVirtualPageEndPosition()
CreateVirtualPage("MyNewPageType")
method.ret:
True
if the action is successful.
False
if an error occurs.
method.see: SetVirtualPageStartPosition, CreateVirtualPage, CreateCcoFromLayout

This action is expected to be used with CreateVirtualPage to build a new page using

The start and end positions must be on the same page.
Recognize()
CreateCcoFromLayout()
FindWordOnPage("Hello")
SetVirtualPageStartPosition()
FindWordOnPageNext("Good bye")
GoUpLine("1")

SetVirtualPageEndPosition()

method.name: UpdateField
method.qi: : Updates the current field with the text and position of the last found word or phrase.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Updates the current field with the word, or group of words, found by a previous Locate action.
The field's coordinates are also updated with position of the word or word group.
Locate actions must be used to identify a word or phrase prior to calling this action.
The field's value can then be used by subsequent tasks that perform operations on field
objects such as validation panels, validation actions and export actions.
FindKeyListOnPage("Date")
GoNextWord("1")
IsDate()
UpdateField()
The first action in the sequence uses the words listed in the key file, Date.key", to find
a matching word or phrase on the current page.
The GoNextWord action moves the found location to the next word on the page text.
This is expected to be a date, such as 12/31/2032. IsDate then checks the format of the
word to confirm it matches an acceptable date format.
The concluding UpdateField action takes place only if the others are successful.
It adds the found text, such as "12/31/2032", to the field's text value and
sets the field's coordinates to the location of the word.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage

method.name: UpdateFieldWithBlock
method.qi: : Updates the current field with the contents and position of the currently selected block.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
UpdateFieldWithBlock updates the current DCO object's field zone coordinates with
the coordinates of the currently selected block. The text of the field will be set
with the contents of the text bound by the currently selected block in the document layout.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
It is important to know that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlock()
SelectParentBlock()
UpdateFieldWithBlock()
FindRegularExpressionInBlock searches for the first occurrence of a word or phrase that matches the regular expression.
The location of the word using an "InBlock" action means that the current block selected is the word itself.
If target field is expected to only contain the single word, then UpdateFieldWithBlock could be used
to set the field zone to the field. This example captures a larger text area by calling SelectParentBlock.
The first is to select the line containing the word.
SelectParentBlock is then called again to change
the selected block to the parent of the current line, likely a paragraph.
Then the current field zone is updated to contain the entire set of lines contained in the current block
and the field value is set to all of the text within the current block.
method.see: SelectParentBlock, SelectParentBlockType

method.name: UpdateFieldWithBlockWithSiblings
method.qi: : Updates a field with the contents of a block and its sibling blocks.

p.name: count
p.qi: The number of siblings to include.

method.ap: An integer that specifies the number of sibling blocks to group into the field.
method.h:
This action utilizes the document block layout created by the Document Analytics actions.
UpdateFieldWithBlock will update the current DCO object's field zone coordinates with
the coordinates of the currently selected block. The text of the field will be set
with the contents of the text bound by the currently selected block and the number of sibling blocks
as specified in the parameter.
The parameter indicates the number of sibling blocks to include in the zone. A value of 0
will operate the same as UpdateFieldWithBlock. A value of 1 will also include the next sibling block
in the zone. A value of 2 will include the next 2 sibling blocks, etc. A negative number will include
the previous sibling blocks.
The sibling blocks are defined by the document layout structure identified by the recognition engine.
A sibling is a block that has the same parent block as the current block. Siblings with different parent blocks
will not be included in the grouping.
Note:
This action requires that a layout XML file has been created from full page recognition and that the page CCO
has been created from the layout file using the CreateCCOFromLayout action in SharedRecognitionTools.
Important:
It is very important to be aware that the block logic is subject to the block structure identified by the
recognition engine. For a given page, it is likely that the block structure identified by one recognition engine
will be different from another recognition engine. If two similar looking pages are provided to the same
recognition engine, it is possible for there to be significantly different block structures identified for the
text on the page. It is also possible that when a specific engine is upgraded to a new version, the way in which
it detects blocks on the page can change, requiring the application logic to change with the upgrade.
When using the "block" oriented locate commands, perform sufficient testing confirm that the
blocks structure is operating reliably enough for the needs of the application.
When upgrading versions of Datacap, the block action rules may need to change, if the engine has changed
the detected block structure.
FindRegularExpressionInBlock("Da.e")
SelectParentBlock()
SelectParentBlock()
UpdateFieldWithBlockWithSiblings("1")
FindRegularExpressionInBlock searches for the first occurrence of a word or phrase that matches the regular expression.
The location of the word using an "InBlock" action means that the current block selected is the word itself.
If target field is expected to only contain the single word, then UpdateFieldWithBlock could be used
to set the field zone to the field. This example captures a larger text area so it calls select parent block.
The first is to select the line containing the word.
SelectParentBlock is then called again to change
the selected block to the parent of the current line, likely a paragraph.
UpdateFieldWithBlockWithSiblings is called to add the current set of lines to the field along
with the next set of sibling lines, likely the next paragraph, if there is a sibling.
method.see: SelectParentBlock, SelectParentBlockType

method.name: UpdateTargetField
method.qi: : Works like UpdateField but also allows specification of the field to update.

p.name: target
p.qi: A smart parameter specification for the field to update.

method.ap:
The smart parameter specification for the target field's name that will
be updated with the word, or group of words, from the last locate operation.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action is similar to UpdateField; the difference is that it does not require this
action to be run on the field being updated. For example, locate actions can be run on
a page and then the page can use this action to update a specific field. It is also
possible for a field to update a sibling field.
The action updates the specified target field with the identified word, or phrase,
found by the last locate action and update the coordinates of the field with the position.
Locate actions must be used to identify a word or phrase prior to calling this action.
Assuming this action is called on a field object, this
updates a sibling field called 'Preparer_Name':
UpdateTargetField("..\Preparer_Name")
Assuming this action is called on a page object, this
example updates a child field called "Preparer_Name":
UpdateTargetField("@X\Preparer_Name")
method.ret:
False
an error occurs, otherwise,
True.
method.see:
FindWordOnPage, FindKeyListWordOnPage, FindRegularExpressionOnPage, UpdateField
Refer to the top-level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library for the smart parameter reference documentation.

af.name: OpenConnection
af.g:
' The Data Source Name or Connection String.

' ' If the action is establishing a connection with an Oracle database, ' or a SQL Server database using SQL Authentication, be sure to expand the DSN parameter ' by adding the correct Provider, user ID and Password.

' A smart parameters are supported to prevent plain text credentials in the application rules. On error resume next Dim i Dim sError Dim sSmartParam oConn.Errors.Clear OpenConnection = True 'Added support for Smart Parameters sSmartParam=MetaWord(strParam) If sSmartParam<>"" and strParam<>sSmartParam Then 'attempt to decrypt value bRes = [securecall]sSmartParam,strParam[/securecall] If bRes=False Then Writelog("Value not decrypted.") Else Writelog("No result from Smart Parameter parsing. Using the original parameter string.") End if strParam = FormatADOConn(strParam) If oConn.State = 1 Then Writelog("Connection is already Open, Function returns TRUE") Exit Function End If oConn.CursorLocation=3 oConn.Open(strParam) Writelog("oConn.State = " & oConn.State) If oConn.State = 1 Then OpenConnection = True Else OpenConnection = False : WriteLog(sError) Writelog("OpenConnection returns " & OpenConnection ) Call ConnErrHandler("Function OpenConnection") Call ErrorHandler("Function OpenConnection")
