Dim i, sError CloseConnection = True Writelog("Close Connection...") Writelog("oConn.State = " & oConn.State) Call CloseDB() If oConn.State = 1 Then CloseConnection = True Else Writelog(sError) Writelog("CloseConnection returns " & CloseConnection ) Call ConnErrHandler("Function CloseConnection") Call ErrorHandler("Function CloseConnection")

af.name: PopulateWithResult
af.g:
' 1. A number <var>n</var> indicating which value in a record retrieved by an
' earlier <scr>ExecuteSQL</scr> action is to be assigned to the current
' Field object (and added to the Data file of the current page.)
'
' "1" refers to the first column in a recordset, "2" refers to the second column, etc.
'
' 2. True or False. True causes the action to fail if the action
' returns a recordset with multiple lines. False permits the action to accept a recordset with multiple
' lines but to use values in the first record of the recordset.
On Error Resume Next
aStrParam = Split(StrParam & ",," , ",")
bMultiReturnFail = True
aStrParam(0)=Trim(aStrParam(0))
aStrParam(1)=Trim(aStrParam(1))
If Ucase(aStrParam(1)) = "FALSE" Then
bMultiReturnFail = False
End If
PopulateWithResult = False
Writelog("Beginning Populate With Results")
If Not(IsNumeric(aStrParam(0))) Then aStrParam(0)=1
aStrParam(0) = CLng(aStrParam(0))
'Note: g_aResults is a two dimensional array of results from a prior lookup
If IsArray(g_aResults) Then
Writelog("Array Found")
writelog((UBound(g_aResults,2)+1) & " Columns in DB Array.")
If (aStrParam(0) > UBound(g_aResults,2)+1) Or (aStrParam(0)<1) Then
Writelog("Queried Column Value '" & aStrParam(0) & "' is an invalid number. Setting to '1'.")
aStrParam(0) = 1
End If
If bMultiReturnFail = True And UBound(g_aResults,1) >= 1 Then
Writelog("Multiple Rows returned")
Else
Writelog("Populating Current Field with Result #" & aStrParam(0) & " : '" & g_aResults(0,aStrParam(0)-1) & "' ")
CurrentObj.Text = CStr(g_aResults(0,aStrParam(0)-1))
PopulateWithResult = True
End If
End If
Writelog("PopulateWithResult returns " & PopulateWithResult)
Call ConnErrHandler("Function PopulateWithResult")
Call ErrorHandler("Function PopulateWithResult")

af.name: ExecuteSQL
af.g:
' section 1 : SELECT * FROM [Names] WHERE Zip=%s AND State='%s';
' section 2 : ZipCode, State (Sibling DCO field names, Values are 10951 and NY)
' Constructs SQL of: SELECT * FROM [Names] WHERE Zip=10951 AND State='NY';
' Result is saved as the calling field value.
' Suppress Result saved to field by having a field name of '-1' in fields list
On Error Resume Next
Dim bSuppressResult
bSuppressResult = (InStr(FieldList,"-1") > 0)
ExecuteSQL = ExecuteSQLEx(sStringIn, Not bSuppressResult, "")

f.name: ExecuteSQLEx
f.g:
' section 1 : SELECT * FROM [Names] WHERE Zip=%s AND State='%s';
' section 2 : ZipCode, State (Sibling DCO field names, Values are 10951 and NY)
' Constructs SQL of: SELECT * FROM [Names] WHERE Zip=10951 AND State='NY';
Dim oRS
Dim sSQL
Dim Index
Dim nSubst
Dim Tmpstr
Dim Counter
Dim FieldVal
Dim FieldList
Dim FieldArray
Dim RowCount
Dim bSuppressResult
Dim nStart
On Error Resume Next
ExecuteSQLEx = False
'Check for Connection Errors
writelog("Checking connection...")
If Not isobject(oConn) Or oConn is Nothing then
writelog("No DB Connection Object. Aborting Task.")
nTaskStatus = RetAbort
Exit Function
End if
If oConn.State =0 then
Writelog("DB Connection is Closed.")
Exit Function
End if
sStringIn = Trim(sStringIn)
g_aResults = ""
Index = InStrRev(sStringIn, Chr(34))
If Index > 1 Then
sSQL = Left(sStringIn,index-1)
FieldList = Mid(sStringIn,(index+2),Len(sStringIn))
Else
sSQL = sStringIn
FieldList = ""
End If
Writelog("Parameter : " & sStringIn)
Writelog(" Index : " & index)
Writelog(" Raw SQL : " & sSql)
Writelog("FieldList : " & FieldList)
Call ErrorHandler("Pre-Substitute")
FieldArray = Split(FieldList & ",",",")
nSubst = InStr(sSQL,"%s")
Counter = 0
bSuppressResult = (Not sPopulate)
If bSuppressResult Then Writelog("Suppressing Result to DCO.Text is ON")
While nSubst > 0
writelog("FieldName:" & FieldArray(Counter))
FormatLen = 0
If nSubst+2<len(sSQL) Then
ch = Mid(sSQL,nSubst+2,1)
C = ASC(ch)
If(C >= 48 And C <= 57) then
FormatLen = cInt(ch)
End If
End if
If FieldArray(Counter)<>"-1" Then
FieldVal=ReturnNamedValue(FieldArray(Counter))
Writelog("FieldVal: '" & FieldVal & "' ")
FieldVal = replace(FieldVal,"'","''")
If FormatLen = 0 Then
sSQL = Mid(sSQL,1,nSubst-1) & FieldVal & Mid(sSQL,nSubst+2,Len(sSQL))
Else
sSQL = Mid(sSQL,1,nSubst-1) & Mid(FieldVal,1,FormatLen) & Mid(sSQL,nSubst+3,Len(sSQL))
End if
nSubst = InStr(sSQL,"%s")
End If
Counter = Counter+1
Wend
'Remove leading spaces and quote char
If len(sSQL)>1 Then
While left(sSQL,1)=CHR(34)
sSQL = Right(sSQL,len(sSQL)-1)
sSQL = Trim(sSQL)
If len(sSQL)<=1 then
Writelog("SQL Expression '" & sSQL & "' is less than 1 character long. Exiting Function.")
Exit Function
End if
wend
End if
Call ErrorHandler("Post Substitute")
sSQL = ModifySQLByDBType(oConn,sSQL)
Writelog("Constructed SQL :" & sSQL)
ExecuteSQLEx = True
If InStr(Ucase(sSQL), "SELECT")=1 or InStr(Ucase(sSQL), "EXEC")=1 Then
Set oRS = oConn.Execute(sSQL)
If IsAlive(oRS) then
If oRS.State=0 Then
writelog("RecordSet returned Closed.")
Elseif oRS.EOF Or oRS.BOF Then
ExecuteSQLEx = False
writelog("RecordSet Returns EOF or BOF. Exiting Function.")
Call ConnErrHandler("EOF or BOF")
Exit Function
Else
Tmpstr = oRS.GetString
Writelog("Query Return String: " & Tmpstr)
If (Len(Tmpstr) <> 0) AND (Not bSuppressResult) Then
If sTarget <> "" Then
Call rrSet("@STRING(" & Left(tmpstr, Len(tmpstr)-1) & ")", sTarget)
Else
CurrentObj.Text = Left(tmpstr, Len(tmpstr)-1)
End If
End If
RowCount = 0
oRS.MoveFirst
While Not oRS.EOF
RowCount = RowCount + 1
oRS.MoveNext()
Wend
Writelog(Space(3) & (RowCount) & " Row(s) containing " & oRS.Fields.Count & " fields found.")
ReDim g_aResults(RowCount-1,oRS.Fields.Count-1)
oRS.MoveFirst
For Row = 0 To RowCount-1
fldStr = ""
For Fld = 0 To oRS.Fields.Count-1
if IsNull(oRS.Fields(Fld).Value) Then
g_aResults(Row,Fld) = ""
fldStr = fldStr & "["& "" & "] "
else
g_aResults(Row,Fld) = CStr(oRS.Fields(Fld).Value)
fldStr = fldStr & "["& oRS.Fields(Fld).Value & "] "
end if
Next 'Fld
Writelog("RowSet: " & fldStr)
oRS.MoveNext
Next 'Row
End if
Set oRS = Nothing
End if 'IsAlive(oRS)
Else
Call oConn.Execute(sSQL)
End if
If oConn.Errors.Count=0 Then
ExecuteSQLEx = True
Writelog("SUCCESS: SQL Statement executed properly")
Else
ExecuteSQLEx = False
Writelog("ERROR:The SQL statement DID NOT execute properly")
End If
Call ConnErrHandler("ExecuteSQLEx")
Call ErrorHandler("ExecuteSQLEx")

f.name: SmartSQL
f.g:
' 1.The SQL expression you want to execute. Smart parameters are supported within the expression.
' 2.True/False value to enable or suppress populating value of any record returned from the SQL expression.
On Error Resume Next Dim bSuppressResult bSuppressResult = False If InStr(sPopulate,"0")>0 or ucase(sPopulate)="NO" or ucase(sPopulate)="FALSE" Then bSuppressResult = True SmartSQL = SmartSQLEx(sStringIn, Not bSuppressResult, "")

f.name: SmartSQLEx
f.g:
Dim oRS
Dim sSQL
Dim bSuppressResult
Dim nStart
Dim sValue
Dim Row
Dim RowCount
Dim Tmpstr
Dim fldstr
Dim bError
On Error Resume Next
SmartSQLEx = False
'oConn.Errors
writelog("Checking connection...")
If Not isobject(oConn) Or oConn is Nothing then
writelog("No DB Connection Object. Aborting Task.")
nTaskStatus = RetAbort
Exit Function
End if
If oConn.State =0 then
Writelog("DB Connection is Closed.")
Exit Function
End if
sStringIn = Trim(sStringIn)
g_aResults = ""
Call ErrorHandler("Pre Smart Parameter Parsing")
bSuppressResult = (Not sPopulate)
If bSuppressResult Then Writelog("Suppressing Result to DCO Text property is ON")
'Convert Smart Parameters
sValue = MetaWord(sStringIn)
If Len(sValue)=0 then
Writelog("No smart parameter return value.")
sSQL=sStringIn
Else
sSQL=sValue
End if
Call ErrorHandler("Post Smart Parameter Parsing")
sSQL = ModifySQLByDBType(oConn,sSQL)
Writelog("Constructed SQL :" & sSQL)
SmartSQLEx = True
If InStr(Ucase(sSQL), "SELECT")=1 or InStr(Ucase(sSQL), "EXEC")=1 Then
Set oRS = oConn.Execute(sSQL)
If IsAlive(oRS) then
If oRS.State=0 Then
writelog("RecordSet returned Closed.")
ElseIf oRS.EOF Or oRS.BOF Then
SmartSQLEx = False
writelog("RecordSet Returns EOF or BOF. Exiting Function.")
Call ConnErrHandler("EOF or BOF")
Exit Function
Else
Tmpstr = oRS.GetString
Writelog("Query Return String: " & Tmpstr)
If (Len(Tmpstr) <> 0) AND (Not bSuppressResult) Then
If sTarget <> "" Then
Call rrSet("@STRING(" & Left(tmpstr, Len(tmpstr)-1) & ")", sTarget)
Else
CurrentObj.Text = Left(tmpstr, Len(tmpstr)-1)
End If
End If
RowCount = 0
oRS.MoveFirst
While Not oRS.EOF
RowCount = RowCount + 1
oRS.MoveNext()
Wend
Writelog(Space(3) & (RowCount) & " Row(s) containing " & oRS.Fields.Count & " fields found.")
ReDim g_aResults(RowCount-1,oRS.Fields.Count-1)
oRS.MoveFirst
For Row = 0 To RowCount-1
fldStr = ""
For Fld = 0 To oRS.Fields.Count-1
if IsNull(oRS.Fields(Fld).Value) Then
g_aResults(Row,Fld) = ""
fldStr = fldStr & "["& "" & "] "
else
g_aResults(Row,Fld) = CStr(oRS.Fields(Fld).Value)
fldStr = fldStr & "["& oRS.Fields(Fld).Value & "] "
end if
Next 'Fld
Writelog("RowSet: " & fldStr)
oRS.MoveNext
Next 'Row
If IsObject(LogWindow) Then ValueUp.Text = GetFieldValue
End if
Set oRS = Nothing
End if 'IsAlive(oRS)
Else
Call oConn.Execute(sSQL)
End if
'Trap Warnings Here
bError = DBErrTrap(oConn,"SmartSQLEx")
'DBErrTrap returns True on valid error, false on warnings. Clears all errors.
If bError=False Then
SmartSQLEx = True
Writelog("SUCCESS: SQL Statement executed properly")
Else
SmartSQLEx = False
Writelog("ERROR:The SQL statement DID NOT execute properly")
End If
Call ErrorHandler("SmartSQLEx")

af.name: ClearLookupResults
af.g:
' This action clears the stored results returned from a previous Lookup action such as PopulateWithResult.
On Error Resume Next
ClearLookupResults=True
Writelog("Clearing Lookup Results.")
g_aResults = ""

rrx.help:
'************************************************************ ' help.xml for Lookup '************************************************************
Uses a data source name or connection string to open a connection to a Lookup database.
The Database Connection String, using an OLEDB or ODBC database provider. If the action is establishing a connection with DB2, Oracle database, or SQL Server database, you must specify the user ID and Password. Some database providers support integrated authentication, which use the credentials of the running process.
Smart parameters are supported and recommended to prevent plain text credentials in the application rules.
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Use action OpenLookupConnection in the LookupDatabase action library.
This action uses the Connection String you provide as the parameter to open a connection to your LookUp database.
OpenConnection("@APPVAR(*/fingerprintconn:cs)")
This example opens the fingerprint database and obtains the connection information from the Application Service. It is recomended to use the applicaiton service so passwords are kept hidden.
Access:
OpenConnection("Provider=MSACCESS;DSN=C:\Datacap\1040EZ\1040ezLook.mdb;UID=;PWD=;")
Oracle:
OpenConnection("Provider=OraOLEDB.Oracle.1;Password=mypassword;Persist Security Info=True;User ID=myuserid;Data Source=TM2")
SQL Server (Standard Authentication):

net.qi: : Actions to perform queries for the Lookup database.
net.h:
The LookupDatabase action library provides a set of actions that allows an application
to perform queries to the lookup database. The results from the lookup can be placed
into the fields of a document being processed or can be stored in a variable to
be acted upon by a subsequent action.
A typical use scenario is to first open a connection to the database. Then actions associated
with pages and fields will perform queries against the database as required.
Once complete, the action CloseLookupConnection will be called to close the database connection.

method.name: ClearLookupResults
method.qi: Clears the results from a previous call to QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action clears the stored results returned from a previous QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget action.
It does not remove values that have been stored in fields or variables, it only removes
the previously returned recordset that is retained in memory for use by the action PopulateWithResult.
Once the task completes, the recordset is removed. If required by a subsequent task, the query must
be run again to create the in memory recordset.
OpenLookupConnection("@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)")
QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget("SELECT NAME, ADDRESS FROM Vendor;", "False", "")
PopulateWithResult("1")
ClearLookupResults()
Here, ClearLookupResults() clears the stored results of the Vendor Name and Address.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget

method.name: CloseLookupConnection
method.qi: Closes a previously opened connection to the database.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
Closes an open connection to your Lookup database.
Usually, this action is placed in a RuleSet that is separate from the RuleSet that opens
the connection and stores the data or in a batch close event, after all calls to the
LookupDatabase actions have been completed.
For example, a Ruleset called LookupDBClose is run at the Batch level after all data has been
exported from the batch to the specified database. The Ruleset must be run within the
same task profile.
CloseLookupConnection()
This action closes the previously opened connection to the Lookup database.
This action is usually part of a separate Ruleset that prevents the
need to repeatedly open the connection to the database. (You can
open the connection once in the first Ruleset, use the database from all
documents and pages in the batch, then close the connection once in the second Ruleset.)
method.lvl: All, but generally used as part of a separate RuleSet at the Batch level.
method.ret:
Always
True,
even if the connection is already closed.

method.name: OpenLookupConnection
method.qi: Connects to the specified database to allow subsequent actions to perform queries.

p.name: Connection
p.qi: Smart parameters are supported.

method.ap:
Uses a data source name or connection string to open a connection to a Lookup database.
The Database Connection String, using an OLEDB or ODBC database provider.
If the action is establishing a connection with DB2, Oracle database, or SQL Server database,
you must specify the user ID and Password. Some database providers support integrated authentication,
which use the credentials of the running process.
Smart parameters are supported, allowing the connection string to be stored in the application manager
to prevent plain text credentials in the application rules.
method.h:
This action uses the provided Connection to open a connection to the application's LookUp database.
OpenLookupConnection("@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)")
This example opens the lookup database and obtains the connection information from the Application Service.
It is recommended to use the application service, so passwords are kept hidden.
The following examples show the raw connection strings for clarity. It is best to obtain these from the application manager.
Access:
OpenLookupConnection("Provider=MSACCESS;DSN=C:\Datacap\1040EZ\1040ezLook.mdb;UID=;PWD=;")
Note, the Access database is not supported for concurrent or production use.
Oracle:
OpenLookupConnection("Provider=OraOLEDB.Oracle.1;Password=mypassword;Persist Security Info=True;User ID=myuserid;Data Source=TM2")
Oracle (The Oracle Net Configuration Assistance Data Source):
OpenLookupConnection("Provider=OraOLEDB.Oracle;Data Source=ORCL;Persist Security Info=True;User ID=myUserid;Password=myPassword;)
SQL Server (Standard Authentication):
OpenLookupConnection("Provider=SQLOLEDB;Data Source=SQLServerName;Initial Catalog=myDatabase;User ID=myUserid;Password=myPassword;")
SQL Server (Integrated Authentication):
OpenLookupConnection("Provider=SQLOLEDB;Data Source=SQLServerName;Initial Catalog=myDatabase;Integrated Security=SSPI;")
SQL Server (Microsoft SQL Server Database Application Manager Configuration):
OpenLookupConnection("Provider=SQLOLEDB;Server=9.9.9.9;Database=SQLLookupDb;UID=myUserid;PWD=myPassword;Persist Security Info=True;)
DB2:
OpenLookupConnection("Provider=IBMDADB2;Hostname=1.22.333.444;Port=50000;Data Source=DB2;Database=myDatabase;User ID=myUserid;Password=myPassword;")

method.name: PopulateWithResult
method.qi: Exracts column values returned from a previous call to QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget.

p.name: ColumnNumber
p.qi: Smart parameters are supported.

p.name: AllowSingleRecordOnly
p.qi: Smart parameters are supported.

method.ap:
ColumnNumber:
A number indicating which value in a record retrieved by an
earlier QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget action is to be assigned to the current
Field object.
"1" refers to the first column in the first row of a returned recordset, "2" refers to the second column of the first row, and so on.
AllowSingleRecordOnly:
True or False. True causes the action to fail if the action
returns a recordset with multiple lines. False permits the action to accept a returned recordset with multiple
lines but will still only use values in the first record of the recordset.
method.h:
Populates a Field object with a database value retrieved by
a previous call to the QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget action.
This action allows multiple rules to populate multiple Field objects with data from a
single database record. A previous call to QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget retrieves a recordset
and subsequent calls to PopulateWithResult will then use the results.
(Field #1)
OpenLookupConnection("@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)")
QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget(""Select * From Vendor Where VendorID = %s;",VendorID", "True", "")
PopulateWithResult("1","FALSE")
(Field #2)
PopulateWithResult("2","FALSE")
In the example, the QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget
action of the RuleSet applied to Field #1
retrieves the recordset (if it exists). The PopulateWithResult action places
the value of the first record's first column into the field where the rule has been applied.
The PopulateWithResult
action of a rule applied to Field #2 populates the field with
the value of the first record's second column.
False
means that the action can accept a recordset with multiple records but will
extract value(s) from the first record only.
(Batch Level Close)
CloseLookupDatabase()
QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget("SELECT * FROM Taxpayer WHERE SSN='+@P\TaxpayerSSN+';", "False", "")
PopulateWithResult("2", "True")
When called on a field, this example performs a query using data from the field TaxpayerSSN to find the value "Taxpayer" in the
database. PopulateWithResult then places the value "Taxpayer" that is returned from the database
query and populates the Text value of the current field.
method.ret:
True
if the second parameter is "True" and a previous QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget action finds
a recordset with only one record.
True
if the second parameter is "False" and a previous QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget
action finds a recordset with one or more records.
Otherwise,
False.
method.see: QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget

method.name: QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget
method.qi: Sends a custom SQL query to the database.

p.name: SQL
p.qi: The SQL to execute.

p.name: Populate
p.qi: Populate value into target True/False.

p.name: Target
p.qi: Saved result location.

method.ap:
SQL
- The SQL expression you want to execute. Smart parameters are supported within the expression.
Populate
- True or False value to enable or suppress populating value of any record returned from the SQL expression.
Target
- Smart Parameter destination for value population, leave this blank to update the current object's Text property.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
Executes the SQL statement and populates a target location with the result and saves the set of returned data
that can be further processed using the PopulateWithResult action to extract data from
the returned record set.
When creating an SQL query for an application, it is often helpful to first workout the desired SQL statement by testing
the final SQL query against the database. The approach allows interactive adjustment of the SQL until the desired response
is received from the database. Once the correct SQL query is created, place the query into the action parameter. Smart parameters
can be used to place runtime values, such as OCR field text, into the query.
This sequence opens a connection to the database. Next, it inserts values
into the CompanyCode and Type columns of the Vendor table:
OpenLookupConnection("@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)")
QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget("INSERT INTO Vendor (CompanyCode,Type) VALUES ('+@X.CompanyCode+','New')", "False", "")
Here, dbVendorID is a numeric field while dbVendorname is the calling text field:
OpenLookupConnection("@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)")
QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget("SELECT CompanyCode FROM Vendor WHERE dbVendorID =+@P\VendorID+ AND dbVendorName = '+@F+';", "True", "@F.MyLookupResult")
QueryDatabaseAndUpdateTarget("SELECT * FROM Taxpayer WHERE SSN='+@P\TaxpayerSSN+';", "False", "")
PopulateWithResult("2", "True")
When called on a field, this example performs a query using data from the field TaxpayerSSN to find the value "Taxpayer" in the
database. PopulateWithResult then places the value "Taxpayer" value returned from the database
query and populates the Text value of the current field.
method.ret:
True
if the SQL statement executes successfully, select statements must also
return a value.
False
if the SQL statement does not execute successfully.
If the database connection does not exist, the action will return false and set the batch to abort.

method.name: ValidateVendor
method.qi: Validates the Vendor, Vendor_Number and Remittance_Zip.

p.name: Connection
p.qi: The connection to the lookup database.

p.name: SQL
p.qi: The query to test that the vendor information exists in the database.

p.name: ADOType
p.qi: The ADO data type.

method.ap:
Connection:
Optional. The connection setting for the lookup database.
When the connection is provided the action will connect to the database, perform the query and disconnect from the database.
Any previous connection will be closed.
If the connection is not provided, the action will use the connection from a previous call to OpenLookupDatabase and
the connection will remain open until CloseLookupDatabase is called.
SQL:
The SQL query to execute against the opened database to determine if the the vendor
information is valid or invalid.
ADOType:
The ADO data type for the database transaction.
If not provided, the action defaults to "202", which typically works for most installations.
Typical Values:
WChar = 130
VarChar = 200
LongVarChar = 201
VarWChar = 202
LongVarWChar = 203
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters. This allows any of the parameters, such as the connection,
to be encrypted in the application manager and obtained at runtime.
method.h:
Checks to see if the current vendor, vendor number and zip code exist on the same record in the lookup database.
The fields that are validated are: Vendor, Vendor_Number and Remittance_Zip. The application page must have fields with these exact names.
The vendor name in the Vendor field must exactly match the name listed in the database. At runtime, the question marks within
the query are replaced with the values from the required fields.
The validation action is typically used to confirm the vendor information is correct by creating rules to
pass validation when ValidateVendor returns true and fail validation when ValidateVendor returns false.
SetIsOverrideable("False")
ValidateVendor("@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)", "Select Count (VendorName) from VendorTable where VendorName = ? AND VendorID = ? AND VendorZip = ?", "202")
In this example, the database connection is retrieved from the application manger using the parameter "@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)". Because
the connection string was provided, the ValidateVendor action will connect to the database, run the query and then disconnect from the database.
If a connection to the Lookup database already exists from a call to OpenLookupConnection, the first parameter can be blank.
The query runs using the values from the required fields, Vendor, Vendor_Number and Remittance_Zip, to determine if the record exists in the database
that exactly matches the values in the field.
The example shows the typical SQL query that is used to perform the database query with the question marks replaced at run time with the respective
field values. The SQL statement must be provided and can be adjusted as needed for differences in vendor database table names,
column names and SQL differences that can exist between different database vendors. The overall form must remain the same.
ValidateVendor("@APPVAR(*/lookupdb:cs)", "SELECT COUNT(TP_VendorName) FROM VENDORTABLE WHERE TP_VendorName = ? AND TP_VendorID = ? AND TP_VendorZip = ?;", "")
In this example, the database SQL SELECT statement has been adjusted for a DB2 database and the database table was created with slightly different column names.
Although the columns are named slightly differently compared to the typical names, so the query was adjusted to specify the correct column names within the table
as implemented.
method.ret:
False,
if the connection cannot be opened or if the settings file cannot be found.
False,
if any of these fields do not exist on the current page: Vendor, Vendor_Number or Remittance_Zip.
False,
if the exact vendor information cannot be found in the database.
Otherwise,
True,
if the values of the Vendor, Vendor_Number and Remittance_Zip
were found in the same record in the database.

af.name: MatchPattern
af.g:
Dim l_HBitMap
Dim nL, nT, nR, nB
Dim mL, mT, mR, mB
Dim nX, nY, nC
Dim vAnchor, nBH, nSub
Dim aAnchor, aMetric
Dim nTID
Dim sTIDFileName
Dim aResult
Dim nWidth, nHeight, nResolution, nResult
Dim nConf
Dim oSA
Dim g_oPM
Dim oCurPage
On Error Resume Next
MatchPattern = False
If CurrentObj.ObjectType<>3 then
Writelog("Action must be called from a DCO field.")
Exit Function
End if
Set oCurPage = CurrentObj
While oCurPage.ObjectType<>2 AND oCurPage.ObjectType>1
Set oCurPage = oCurPage.Parent()
Wend
nTID = oCurPage.Variable("TemplateID")
'vANCHOR is the Position of the AREA on the Permanent Fingerprint to Match to.
'vMETRIC is the area to search beyond the center of the source area: vANCHOR. Pattern is (Horizonal,Vertical)
If len(CurrentObj.Variable("ANCHOR"))>0 then
vANCHOR = CurrentObj.Variable("ANCHOR")
Writelog("'ANCHOR' variable found. ANCHOR ZONE='" & vANCHOR & "' ")
Elseif len(CurrentObj.Variable("Pos" & nTID))>0 then
vANCHOR = CurrentObj.Variable("Pos" & nTID)
Writelog("'Pos" & nTID & "' variable found. ANCHOR ZONE='" & vANCHOR & "' ")
Else
vANCHOR = CurrentObj.Variable("Position")
Writelog("'Position' variable found. ANCHOR ZONE='" & vANCHOR & "' ")
End if
vMETRIC=""
If CurrentObj.FindVariable("METRIC")>0 then
vMETRIC = CurrentObj.Variable("METRIC")
Writelog("Run Time METRIC variable found. METRIC='" & vMETRIC & "'")
Elseif CurrentObj.Variable("METRIC")<>"" then
vMETRIC = CurrentObj.Variable("METRIC")
Writelog("Setup XML METRIC variable found. METRIC='" & vMETRIC & "'")
Else
vMETRIC = "500,500"
Writelog("Default Metric used. METRIC='" & vMETRIC & "'")
End if
aAnchor=Split(vAnchor, ",")
For i=0 To UBound(aAnchor)
If IsNumeric(aAnchor(i)) then
aAnchor(i)=CLng(aAnchor(i))
Else
writelog("Invalid Anchor Position info. A non-numeric value was found.")
Exit Function
End if
Next
'Set PATTERN AREA
nL = aAnchor(0)
nT = aAnchor(1)
nR = aAnchor(2)
nB = aAnchor(3)
aMetric = Split(vMetric, ",")
For i=0 To UBound(aMetric )
If IsNumeric(aMetric (i)) then
aMetric(i)=CLng(aMetric (i))
Else
writelog("Invalid METRIC Position information. A non-numeric value was found.")
Exit Function
End if
Next
pm_GetLock() ' Get Pattern Match object lock
'Calculate Search Area based on METRIC, Note: must be recalculated using image area to reflect image bounds
mL = aAnchor(0)-aMetric(0)
If mL<0 then mL = Clng(0)
mT = aAnchor(1)-aMetric(1)
if mT<0 then mT = Clng(0)
mR = aAnchor(2)+aMetric(0)
mB = aAnchor(3)+aMetric(1)
Writelog("Anchor: " & vAnchor & ", Metric: " & vMETRIC & ", ml: " & mL & ", mt: " & mT & ", mr: " & mR & ", mb: " & mB & ", Parent: " & oCurPage.ID)
If len(nTID)>0 and IsNumeric(nTID) then
Writelog("Requesting templateID : '" & nTID & "' ")
aResult = GetDataArray("SELECT tp_ImagePath FROM Template WHERE tp_TemplateID =" & nTID & "; ")
Else
Writelog("Requesting template with status : '" & chr(39) & "<Global>" & chr(39) & "' ")
aResult = GetDataArray("SELECT tp_ImagePath FROM Template WHERE tp_Status =" & chr(39) & "<Global>" & chr(39) & "; ")
End if
If isArray(aResult) then
sTIDFileName = g_DCI.FileName
sTIDFileName = aResult(0,0)
Writelog("Anchor Image: '" & sTIDFileName & "' ")
Else
Writelog("No Anchor Image Path found.")
pm_ReleaseLock() ' Release Pattern Match lock
Exit Function
End if
g_DCI.FileName = sTIDFileName
g_DCI.Invert
lHBitMap = g_DCI.GetHBITMAP
If g_dictAnchors.Exists(sTIDFileName & vAnchor) then
Set g_oPM = g_dictAnchors.Item(sTIDFileName & vAnchor)
Else
Set g_oPM = CreateObject("Datacap.PatternMatch")
Writelog("Created patternmatch")
MatchPattern = g_oPM.CreateAnchor(nL,nT,nR,nB,lHBitMap)
Set g_dictAnchors(sTIDFileName & vAnchor) = g_oPM
End if
g_DCI.FileName = oCurPage.ImageName
Writelog("Search Image: '" & g_DCI.FileName & "' ")
ImageCtrl.filename = g_DCI.FileName
Call g_DCI.Invert
lHBitMap = g_DCI.GetHBITMAP
nResult = g_DCI.GetImageInfo(nWidth, nHeight, nResolution)
If clng(mR) > clng(nWidth) then mR = clng(nWidth)
If clng(mB) > clng(nHeight) then mB = clng(nHeight)
Writelog("Search Area: " & mL & "," & mT & "," & mR & "," & mB)
MatchPattern = g_oPM.SearchForAnchor(mL, mT, mR, mB, lHBitMap)', nBH, nSub ,nX, nY, nC)
Set oSA = g_oPM.StatUP
Writelog("X:" & oSA.X & ", Y:" & oSA.Y & " diff:" & oSA.Diff & " white:" & oSA.White & " black:" & oSA.Black & " w_diff:" & oSA.w_diff & " w_white:" & oSA.w_White & " w_black:" & oSA.w_black)
'nRectIndex = ImageCtrl.DrawRect(nL,nT,nR,nB,3,RGB(0,0,255),RGB(255,0,0),"")
'nRectIndex = ImageCtrl.DrawRect(oSA.X ,oSA.Y ,oSA.X + (nR-nL),oSA.Y + (nB-nT),3,RGB(255,0,0),RGB(255,0,0),"")
nConf = g_oPM.Confidence
writelog("Match Confidence: " & nConf)
g_DCI.FileName = ""
if clng(nConf)<clng(g_MatchConf) then
Writelog("Confidence too low - match requires conf " & clng(g_MatchConf))
MatchPattern = False
Set oSA = Nothing
pm_ReleaseLock() ' Release Pattern Match lock
If CurrentObj.Variable("Req"&nTID) = "1" Or CurrentObj.Variable("Required") = "1" Then
CurrentObj.Variable("STATUS") = 1
End If
Exit Function
End if
'Calculate Offset for found Pattern
Dim xOffset, yOffset
xOffset = abs(clng(aAnchor(0)) - clng(mL+oSA.X))
yOffset = abs(clng(aAnchor(1)) - clng(mT+oSA.Y))
If clng(aAnchor(0))>clng(mL+oSA.X) then xOffset = (xOffset * -1)
If clng(aAnchor(1))>clng(mT+oSA.Y) then yOffset = (yOffset * -1)
Writelog("Calculated offset is: (" & xOffset & "," & yOffset & ")")
CurrentObj.Variable("Image_Offset") = xOffset & "," & yOffset
CurrentObj.Variable("Zone_Offset") = xOffset & "," & yOffset
CurrentObj.Variable("Position") = CStr(nL+xOffset) & "," & CStr(nT+yOffset) & "," & CStr(nR+xOffset) & "," & CStr(nB+yOffset)
Set oSA = Nothing
pm_ReleaseLock() ' Release Pattern Match lock

af.name: pat_RegisterZones
af.g:
Dim oPg
pat_RegisterZones = False
counter = 0
xScale = 1
yScale = 1
xOff = 0
yOff = 0
set oPg = CurrentObj
if (CurrentObj.ObjectType <> 2) then Exit Function ' must be a page
If (oPg.NumOfChildren <= 0) Then
WriteLog("No fields in current page, RegisterPageAnchors fails")
Exit Function
End If
pm_GetLock() ' Get pattern match object lock
sName = ""
sName = oPg.Variable("TemplateID") ' needed to find expected positions?
if (sName = "") then
sPosName = "Position"
else
sPosName = "Pos" & sName
End If
' make a list of all found anchors
For i = 0 To oPg.NumOfChildren -1
Set oAnc = oPg.GetChild(i)
If Not oAnc Is Nothing Then
If oAnc.Variable("PatternMatch") = "1" Then
AnchorsFound = False
WriteLog("Anchor " & oAnc.Type & " found. Looking for offset...")
Set oSetupNode = oAnc.SetupNode()
' get expected loc
sExp = oSetupNode.Variable(sPosName)
If (len(sExp) <= 1) Then sExp = oSetupNode.Variable("Position")
If (len(sExp) > 1) then
WriteLog("Expected " & sExp)
arExp = split(sExp, ",", -1, 1)
WriteLog("Image_Offset " & oAnc.Variable("Image_Offset"))
sOff = oAnc.Variable("Image_Offset")
If Len(sOff) < 1 Then
WriteLog("Zone_Offset " & oAnc.Variable("Zone_Offset"))
sOff = oAnc.Variable("Zone_Offset")
End If
' Anchor was found, we can tell because offset was set
If Len(sOff) >= 1 Then
arOff = split(sOff, ",", -1, 1)
sExp = CStr(CInt((CInt(arExp(0)) + CInt(arExp(2)) + .5)/2.)) & "," & CStr(CInt((CInt(arExp(1)) + CInt(arExp(3)) + .5)/2.))
Redim Preserve arAnchors(2, counter+1)
sFnd = CStr(CInt(arOff(0) + (CInt(arExp(0)) + CInt(arExp(2)) + .5)/2.)) & "," & CStr(CInt(arOff(1) + (CInt(arExp(1)) + CInt(arExp(3)) + .5)/2.))
arAnchors(0, counter) = CStr(sExp)
arAnchors(1, counter) = CStr(sFnd)
counter = counter + 1
End If ' found an anchor that is set on this image
End If ' found an anchor that has an expected location POSnnnn for this fingerprint
End If ' found a pattern match (anchor) field
End If ' found a field in this runtime DCO
Next ' i ' loop through fields in this runtime DCO
If counter = 3 Then
' special case for 3 FOUND anchors - calculate linear scale and offset X & Y
' use found anchor pair with biggest X difference, and pair with biggest Y difference
'Writelog("Linear anchor calculate")
xMax = 0
yMax = 0
' match up all anchor pairs to find the most distant pair in X and Y axes
For i = 0 To counter-1
For j = 0 To counter-1
If i <> j Then
arAnchExp1 = split(arAnchors(0, i), ",")
arAnchFnd1 = split(arAnchors(1, i), ",")
arAnchExp2 = split(arAnchors(0, j), ",")
arAnchFnd2 = split(arAnchors(1, j), ",")
xdiff = ABS(arAnchFnd1(0)-arAnchFnd2(0))
ydiff = ABS(arAnchFnd1(1)-arAnchFnd2(1))
if xdiff > xMax then
xMax = xdiff
denom = ABS(arAnchExp1(0)-arAnchExp2(0))
If denom < 1 Then denom = 1
xScale = xdiff / denom
end if
if ydiff > yMax then
yMax = ydiff
denom = ABS(arAnchExp1(1)-arAnchExp2(1))
If denom < 1 Then denom = 1
yScale = ydiff / denom
end if
End If
Next ' j
Next ' i
'WriteLog("X scale " + CStr(xScale) + " span " + CStr(xMax))
'WriteLog("Y scale " + CStr(yScale) + " span " + CStr(yMax))
' we have found the X and Y scale, now calculate offset
' negative of average distance from expected to found
For i = 0 To counter-1
arAnchExp1 = split(arAnchors(0, i), ",")
arAnchExp1(0) = arAnchExp1(0)*xScale
arAnchFnd1 = split(arAnchors(1, i), ",")
arAnchExp1(1) = arAnchExp1(1)*yScale
xOff = xOff + (arAnchFnd1(0)-arAnchExp1(0))
yOff = yOff + (arAnchFnd1(1)-arAnchExp1(1))
Next ' i
If counter > 0 Then
xOff = xOff / counter
yOff = yOff / counter
End If
Writelog("Linear scale ("+ CStr(xScale) + ","+ CStr(yScale) +") offset ("+ CStr(xOff) +","+ CStr(yOff) +")")
End If
' now adjust all the fields using the found anchors
If counter > 0 Then
WriteLog("Register using " & counter & " anchors")
temp = AZoneChildren(CurrentObj, sPosName)
pat_RegisterZones = temp
Else
WriteLog("No anchors set on this page")
pat_RegisterZones = True ' this is OK, not an error
End If
pm_ReleaseLock() ' Release Pattern Match lock

af.g:

af.name: pat_RecogMatch_Id
af.g:
Dim sTID
Dim DCOsetup
Dim ChildNode
Dim i,j
Dim nTID
Dim aResult
Dim lHBitMap
Dim oSA
Dim iCCOobj
Dim oCCOCreator
Dim bMatch
Dim aAnchor
On error resume next
pat_RecogMatch_Id = False
bMatch = False
If CurrentObj.ObjectType<>2 then
Writelog("Current DCO is not a Page.")
Exit Function
End if
WriteLog("Current Page Type = " & cstr(CurrentObj.Type))
pm_GetLock() ' Get Pattern Match object lock
Set oSA = Nothing
Set oCCOCreator = CreateObject("CCO._CCOCreator")
Set iCCOobj = Nothing
'Check if Dictionary is already loaded
If g_dictRMID.Count = 0 then
'Read Setup DCO and a Create Dictionary of CCO Recognition Match Objects
Set DCOsetup = DCO.SetupObject
If DCOsetup is Nothing then
pm_ReleaseLock() ' Release Pattern Match lock
Writelog("DCOSetup is empty. Cannot check for fields with PatternMatch")
Exit Function
End if
Set ChildNode = Nothing
For i = 1 to DCOsetup.NumOfNodes(3) ' Getting the SETUP DCO. Not sure why the value is (3)
Set ChildNode = DCOsetup.GetNode(3,i-1)
If Not(ChildNode is Nothing) Then
If ChildNode.Variable("PatternMatch")="1" Then ' Look to see if the field has a variable called "PatternMatch" set to 1. This means we want to get the IDs from it.
WriteLog("Found PatternMatch=1 on name: " & cstr(ChildNode.name)) ' Use Name on setup fields
For j = 0 to ChildNode.NumOfVariables
If left(ChildNode.VariableName(j) & Space(3),3)="Pos" And isnumeric(replace(ChildNode.VariableName(j),"Pos","")) then
nTID = trim(replace(ChildNode.VariableName(j),"Pos",""))
If isNumeric(nTID) and len(nTID)>=1 then
'Add to Dictionary
If Not(g_dictRMID.Exists(nTID)) then
Set g_dictRMID(nTID) = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary")
End if
Set dictZone = g_dictRMID(nTID)
If Not(dictZone.Exists(ChildNode.Variable("Pos" & nTID))) then
Call dictZone.Add(ChildNode.Variable("Pos" & nTID),cstr(""))
End if
Set g_dictRMID(nTID) = dictZone
End if
End if
Next 'j
End if
Set ChildNode = Nothing
End if
Next 'i
Set DCOsetup = Nothing
On Error Resume Next
WriteLog("dictRMID count = " & cstr(g_dictRMID.Count))
If g_dictRMID.Count <> 0 then
'Load All Template records based on Key Values
aKeys = g_dictRMID.Keys
sKeys = join(aKeys,",") ' This is the list of template IDs that we want to get.
WriteLog("Attempting to load fingerprints of ID: " & cstr(sKeys))
sSQL = "SELECT tp_TemplateID, tp_CCOPath FROM Template WHERE tp_TemplateID IN (" & sKeys & "); "
aResult = GetDataArray(sSQL)
If isArray(aResult) then
WriteLog("Number of FPs found in DB: " & cstr(ubound(aResult,1) + 1) )
For k = 0 to ubound(aResult,1)
Writelog("#" & aResult(k,0) & ", path:'" & aResult(k,1) & "' ")
'Ensure CCO file exists
If FileMgr.FileExists(aResult(k,1)) Then
'Load CCO file as Object into dictionary
Set iCCOobj = oCCOCreator.Load(aResult(k,1))
If g_dictRMID.Exists(cstr(aResult(k,0))) then
If Not(iCCOobj is Nothing) then
Set dictZone = g_dictRMID.item(cstr(aResult(k,0)))
For Each zoneKey in dictZone.Keys
aAnchor = pm_SplitNumber(zoneKey)
'***Find Recognition Text for FingerPrint CCO Area....
AnchorText=Trim(rm_ZoneText(aAnchor,iCCOObj))
If len(AnchorText)>0 Then
Writelog(Space(5) & "FPZone:'" & zoneKey & "' TXTZone:'" & Join(aAnchor,",") & "' Value:'" & AnchorText & "'")
Call dictZone.Remove(zoneKey)
Call dictZone.Add(Join(aAnchor,","),cstr(AnchorText))
Else
dictZone(zoneKey)=cstr(AnchorText)
End if
Next 'zoneKey
Else
Writelog("CCO file did not load!")
Call g_dictRMID.Remove(cstr(aResult(k,0)))
End if
End if
Set iCCOobj = Nothing
Else
Writelog("File '" & aResult(k,1) & " not found. CCO File Missing while loading Patterns. Skipping it.")
If g_dictRMID.Exists(cstr(aResult(k,0))) then g_dictRMID.Remove(cstr(aResult(k,0)))
End if
Next 'k
Else
Writelog("No results retrieved from Template Table Lookup.")
set oCCOCreator = Nothing
pm_ReleaseLock() ' Release Pattern Match lock
Exit Function
End if
End if
End if
set oCCOCreator = Nothing
aStrParam = g_dictRMID.Keys
pat_RecogMatch_Id = rm_Match(aStrParam)
pm_ReleaseLock() ' Release Pattern Match lock

None.
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that this action is no longer used. Use the replacement action MatchPattern in the PatternMatchImage action library.
Searches on the current image in a zone associated with the current field for a match to the pattern specified for this field in a fingerprint. This pattern match between the fingerprint and the current image allows adjustment of field zones so they will align with the current image.
One to three anchor fields can be defined for a page. Two or three anchor fields will allow for better alignment than 1 anchor field. Anchor fields are identified by creating a DCO variable "PatternMatch" on the field and assigning it the value "1".
The zoned area from the original fingerprint is matched against a larger zone in the current image. The action will attempt to find the pattern within the zone from the fingerprint on the current image to determine if the current image is shifted compared to the original fingerprint. The search area is controlled by the METRIC variable. METRIC=200,100 means search from 200 pixels to the left and right, and 100 pixels above and below the expected location. If METRIC is not specified in the field object, the default is 500 pixels horizontal and vertical. There should be a balance between the search area and the amount of difference expected in production images. Smaller search areas will reduce the chance of matching an incorrect area of the image, however if the image is shifted beyond the search area, the match will not be found.
The fingerprint is determined by the current image's Fingerprint ID, or the Global Fingerprint ID if the current image is not identified.
MatchPattern may be called on any anchor field and if matched an offset variable will be saved for that field. If called prior to ReadZones then ReadZones will use the offset for that field when setting its position. Other fields will be unaffected.
If the field is matched to the fingerprint with a confidence equal to or greater than the required confidence, the position of the field is set to the found location. If the field is not matched, the function returns false. If not found and the field's Required variable is nonzero, the field status is set to 1 (Error or Validation failed).
This action operates on black and white images. Both the fingerprint and current page image must be black and white. Grayscale or color images will cause the action to fail. The fingerprint image must have the same resolution (DPI) as the current page image.
The geometric shape contained in the Anchor field should be bold and well defined with clear edges, with crisp black and white markings, producing a distinct shape. The shape should be thick and compact, not composed of long thin lines. To avoid false positive matches, the shape should not match other shapes or black areas that may exist nearby within the same image. If using multiple anchors, the best locations are typically near the corners of the image.
SetMatchConfidence("5")
MatchPattern()
This example would be configured so it is associated with each anchor field on the page. The anchor fields are the fields that have a zone on an image location that is a unique pixel pattern and the field has the variable "PatternMatch" defined with the value "1". First the required confidence level is set, then MatchPattern will compare the fingerprint image with the page image, looking for the zoned area on the fingerprint on the current page image. If found, then the offset value is saved and this offset value will be used by a subsequent call to pat_RegisterZones in a following ruleset.
Field level.
False if:
- The Anchor position returned is not Numeric.
- No image is found.
- The accuracy of the match is below the set Confidence Value.
- An Anchor match does not occur.
Otherwise, True.

None.
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that this action is no longer used. Use the replacement action PatternMatchIdentify in the PatternMatchImage action library.
PatternMatch_Identify identifies a page's type and fingerprint using geometric pattern matching. The locations of unique patterns are configured as Anchor Fields for each fingerprint in the Document Hierarchy. One or more Anchor fields can be used to match geometric shapes on a fingerprint to the current image. If one or more Anchor fields on the current page match a fingerprint, at or above the configured confidence level, the page is identified with that fingerprint. The action does not require all defined anchors to match - the first match is used.
The action loads all Anchor field patterns from the fingerprint library, then searches on the current image for each of the patterns in the associated zones. The search area for each zone is increased by the dimensions specified in the page METRIC variable. If METRIC is not specified, the default is 500 pixels horizontal and vertical.
When this action finds a match, it sets the matching Fingerprint ID and Page Type. It will also create page-level fields and update the Anchor fields with Anchor-specific pattern offset values in a field-level Image_Offset variable. The offset can be used subsequent to matching a fingerprint. The pat_RegisterZones action can be used to align the zones in the fingerprint to the current image, providing more accurately positioned text in each field.
This action requires the current page image to be bitonal (black and white), grayscale or color images will cause the action to fail. The fingerprint image must have the same resolution (DPI) as the current page image. The geometric shape contained in each Anchor field should be bold and well defined with clear edges, with crisp black and white markings, producing a distinct shape. The shape should be thick and compact, not composed of long thin lines. To avoid false positive matches, the shape should not match other shapes or black areas that may exist nearby within the same image.

pat_RegisterZones registers and adjusts the positions of all fields on the current page, based on the previously matched positions of the page's designated Anchor field(s). Anchor fields are determined by the Anchor Field setting in Datacap Studio, for each field.
Prior to calling pat_RegisterZones, usually in a different task or ruleset, one of the PatternMatch actions that performs Anchor matching must be called. Then, when the pat_RegisterZones action is called, the expected positions of the Anchor fields on the image (taking into account the Fingerprint classification) are compared with the recognized positions of the fields identified as an Anchor field. The action ReadZones must be called prior to pat_RegisterZones. If any required Anchors are not matched, an operator may be required to update the Anchor position in a verify or fixup task.
All matched or manually adjusted Anchor positions are used for adjustment, Anchors that are not matched are ignored.
If one Anchor is found, the field positions are all shifted by the same amount.
If two or more Anchors are found, the field positions are shifted by different amounts, depending on their distance from each Anchor. This process is called Interpolation.
The expected positions of the Anchor fields on the image (taking into account the Fingerprint classification) are compared with the recognized positions of those Anchor fields - or the Anchor positions set manually by a Fixup task's operator. This action will adjust the zone coordinates for all of the fields on the page that have loaded coordinate positions but it will not adjust the position of anchor fields.
ReadZones()
pat_RegisterZones()
RecognizePageFieldsOCR_S()
This example assumes that between 1 to 3 anchor fields have been configured for the page. The action MatchPattern must have been called for each of the anchor fields prior to this example. Once those steps are completed, this example will call ReadZones to load the coordinate positions for each field. pat_RegisterZones then uses the previously defined anchor fields to determine the correction offset and then adjusts each of the zones on the page to align the field to the image for the page.
Page only.
True if the ruleset with this action is bound to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy, and if the action can find all designated Anchor fields. Otherwise, False.
None.
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that this action is no longer used. Use the replacement action ReleasePageAnchors in the PatternMatchImage action library.
This action can be optionally called to release the small amount of Anchor memory that was allocated by the action pat_RegisterZones. If pat_ReleasePageAnchors is not called, the memory will be released at the end of the batch or the next time pat_RegisterZones is called.
pat_ReleasePageAnchors()
Page only. Always True.
None.
This action will be removed in a future release. It is recommended that this action is no longer used. There is no direct replacement for this action. Configure your application to use one of Datacap's page identification techniques.
pat_RecogMatch_Id identifies the page by matching text from any fingerprint Anchor field with the corresponding text on the current page. Fuzzy matching is used. Full-page OCR or ICR must be performed prior to calling this action.
If any Anchor field text in the current page matches the zonal text of any fingerprint, the page is identified by that fingerprint (first match). The Type of the current page is set to the fingerprint page type if a match is found. Full page OCR or ICR must be performed on both the fingerprints and the current image prior to calling this action. Text to be matched is extracted from each fingerprint's Anchor field, which should be defined tightly around the text in the fingerprint. The search area in the current image is the fingerprint-specific field zone in the Document Hierarchy, extended by any associated METRIC variable.
Page identification using pat_RecogMatch_ID (text matching) is mutually exclusive with identification using graphical pattern matching actions (PatternMatch_Identify, etc.). Anchor fields in the Document Hierarchy should be selected carefully so that false positive text matches do not occur.
The anchor fields must directly off of the page object. The anchor fields must be identified in the setup DCO by the variable "PatternMatch" and it must have the value of "1". The action will not check every fingerprint in the application. Only fingerprints with zones associated with these identified fields will be checked. This function does not support FPXML fingerprints.
pat_RecogMatch_Id()
Page only.
True if the ruleset is bound to a Page, and a fingerprint matching the text of at least one Anchor field is found. Otherwise, and in case of any errors, False. In addition, the page variable TemplateID is set to the matching Fingerprint ID.

net.qi: : Actions that use page 'anchors' to adjust zones.
net.h:
The PatternMatchImage action library contains actions that evaluate the original fingerprint
image and can compare it to the current page image. The actions have a requirement that
the fingerprint and current page be black and white images with a 1 bit color depth.
The current page must have the same resolution, dots-per-inch, as the fingerprint used for matching.
The scaling must be the identical as well. For example, if a fingerprint is an 8.5"x11" page
at 300 dpi, then the image dimensions would be 2550x3300 pixels. The scanned image must be the same.
Images must also be isotropic, meaning that the x DPI is identical to the y DPI. Fax images are usually
non-isotropic and must be first adjusted before fingerprinting and pattern matching. Non-isotropic
images can be corrected using the action EqualizeUnbalancedImage in the ImageUtilities action library.
Defining Anchors
An anchor is a mark on a page, typically a form, that is expected in a consistent spot for every
page of the page type. The mark works best when it is in the corner of a page. One to three anchors can be defined for a page.
The geometric shape contained in the anchor field should be bold and well defined with clear edges,
with crisp black and white markings, producing a distinct shape. The shape should be thick and compact,
not composed of long thin lines. To avoid false positive matches,
the shape should not match other shapes or black areas that may exist nearby within the same image.
If using multiple anchors, the best locations are typically near the corners of the image.
Form printed text is generally not suitable for use as an anchor.
An anchor field is identified by setting the variable "PatternMatch" to a value of "1".
This variable is typically added and configured in the SetupDCO from within Datacap Studio.
An anchor field should not be used for any other purpose other than identifying the anchor
mark on the page.
Aligning Zones With Anchors
When one or two anchors are used on a page, all pages must be of the same scale. This means
that the anchor alignment will compensate for the image needing x and y adjustment to properly
align with the original fingerprint, but it does not allow for images that have been scaled
larger or smaller. If images are scaled larger or smaller, then the images must first be
resized so they have the same scaling. For example, when scanning pages, a page may be positioned
slightly differently in the scanner, but the scaling of the text and objects on the page is the same.
Only the amount of boarder along the sides of the page have been changed. Additionally, all pages
should be deskewed before calling MatchPattern and RegisterZones.
When three anchors are used on a page, in addition to determining the x and y adjustment, RegisterZones
will also attempt to correct small amounts of scaling on the page, meaning that if the page has been scaled
slightly larger or smaller, the registration will attempt to compensate for a small amount of scaling when adjusting the zones.
Scaling adjustment only supports images that have a linear scale difference across the page. This means
that if the page is reduced by 4%, then that scaling factor must be consistent across the entire page. The action
cannot compensate for scaling that changes across the page such as the top of the page is 4% scaled and the bottom
of the page is 6% scaled.
The larger the scaling difference becomes, compared to the fingerprint,
the less likely the anchor will be correctly found due to the scaling
difference. Scaled pages will also reduce the confidence of the found anchor, if the correct location is found.
Anchor Alignment Guidelines
A field that has been designated as an anchor field must identify an object on the page that
is expected to exist on every page of the same type, such as a printed form.
The area of the anchor should include a crisp and distinct geometric shape, such as a square,
with crisp edges, has white space around it, and does not match any nearby area of the page.
When a page properly scaled page is not aligning to a fingerprint, it is likely due to the anchors not being found correctly.
There are several reasons why anchors may not be found:
The METRIC is too big.
The METRIC is too small.
The anchor zone may need adjustment.
The anchor is being confused with other markings on the page.
The page scale is too different.
The page has scan issues such as too light, too speckled, or too dark.
If the original fingerprint and the current source page are clean, sharp, and closely scaled,
then it is likely that the anchor zone or METRIC may need adjustment. By default, the METRIC is
500 pixels by 500 pixels, which is a fairly large area. A good metric is one that is large enough for typical
scanning alignment problems, but does not go beyond that value.
If the METRIC value appears to be appropriate, then try adjusting the area of the zone itself.
Ideally the zone should only contain the target shape along with whitespace around the object.
It should be large enough to identify the object on the page without matching other black
areas on the page.
If the action is finding the correct location, but does not have a high confidence, then lowering
the confidence can resolve the problem. The action log for MatchPattern will indicate if
an anchor match is found, but it did not have a high enough confidence. Of course, if the match found is
with an incorrect marking on the page, it will also have low confidence and will cause adjusted alignments
to be incorrect.

method.name: MatchPattern
method.qi: : Locate the field's anchor position on the page and calculate an offset compared to the fingerprint.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
MatchPattern searches on the current image in a zone associated with the current field
for a match to the pattern specified for this field in a fingerprint.
This pattern match between the fingerprint and the current image allows adjustment of
field zones so they will align with the current image.
The current field must be an anchor field.
One to three anchor fields can be defined for a page. Two or three anchor fields will allow for
better alignment than 1 anchor field. Anchor fields are identified by creating a DCO variable
"PatternMatch"
on the field and assigning it the value "1".
The zoned area from the original fingerprint is matched against a larger
zone in the current image. The action will attempt to find the pattern within
the anchor zone from the fingerprint on the current image to determine if the current image
is shifted compared to the original fingerprint.
The search area is controlled by the METRIC variable.
METRIC=200,100 means search from 200 pixels to the left and right, and 100 pixels
above and below the expected location. If METRIC is not specified in the field object, the default is 500
pixels horizontal and vertical. There should be a balance between the search area and the
amount of difference expected in production images. Smaller search areas will reduce the chance
of matching an incorrect area of the image, however if the image is shifted beyond the
search area, the match will not be found. A metric that is too large, increases
the chance of an incorrect anchor match.
The fingerprint is determined by the current image's Fingerprint ID, or the
Global Fingerprint ID if the current image is not identified.
MatchPattern is to be called on each anchor field and if matched an offset variable will
be saved for that field. If called prior to ReadZones then ReadZones will
use the offset for that field when setting its position.
Other fields will be unaffected.
If the field is matched to the fingerprint with a confidence equal to or greater than the required confidence,
the position of the field is set to the found location.
If the field is not matched, the function returns false.
If not found and the field's "Required" variable is nonzero, the field status is set to 1 to indicate an error or that validation failed.
This action operates on black and white images. Both the fingerprint and current page
image must be black and white. Grayscale or color images will cause the action to fail.
The fingerprint image must have the same resolution (DPI) as the current page image.
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for guidance on defining and using anchors.
SetMatchConfidence("5")
MatchPattern()
This example would be configured so it is associated with each anchor field on the page.
The anchor fields are the fields that have a zone on an image location that is a
unique pixel pattern and the field has the variable "PatternMatch" defined with the value "1".
First the required confidence level is set, then MatchPattern will compare the fingerprint
image with the page image, looking for the zoned area on the fingerprint on the current
page image. If found, then the offset value is saved and this offset value will be
used by a subsequent call to RegisterZones in a following ruleset.
method.lvl: Field level, defined as an anchor field.
method.ret:
False
if:
- The Anchor position returned is not Numeric.
- No image is found.
- The accuracy of the match is below the set Confidence Value.
- An Anchor match does not occur.
Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
RegisterZones
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general guidance, and image requirements,
for using anchors to align a page with the original fingerprint.

method.name: PatternMatchFingerprint
method.qi: : Uses anchor matching to identify a page from a specified list of fingerprints.
method.ap:
A comma-separated list of one or more Fingerprint ID's.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
PatternMatchFingerprint identifies a page's type and fingerprint using geometric pattern matching.
The locations of unique patterns are configured as Anchor Fields for each fingerprint in the Document Hierarchy.
One or more Anchor fields can be used to match geometric shapes on a fingerprint to the current image.
If one or more Anchor fields on the current page match a fingerprint, at or above the configured confidence level,
the page is identified with that fingerprint. The action does not require all defined anchors to match. If not, the first match is used.
The action loads all Anchor field patterns from the specified fingerprints, then searches on the
current image for each of the patterns in the associated zones. The search area for each zone is increased
by the dimensions specified in the page METRIC variable. If METRIC is not specified, the default is 500 pixels horizontal and vertical.
When this action finds a match, it sets the matching Fingerprint ID and Page Type. It will also create
page-level fields and update the Anchor fields with Anchor-specific pattern offset values in a field-level
Image_Offset variable. The offset can be used subsequent to matching a fingerprint. The pat_RegisterZones
action can be used to align the zones in the fingerprint to the current image, providing more accurately
positioned text in each field.
This action requires the current page image to be bitonal (black and white), grayscale or color
images will cause the action to fail. The fingerprint image must have the same resolution (DPI) as
the current page image. The geometric shape contained in each Anchor field should be bold and well
defined with clear edges, with crisp black and white markings, producing a distinct shape.
The shape should be thick and compact, not composed of long thin lines. To avoid false positive matches,
the shape should not match other shapes or black areas that may exist nearby within the same image.
PatternMatchFingerprint(1024,1034,1035,1036)
This example compares the current page to the four fingerprints specified by their IDs.
method.ret:
False
if the rule containing this action was not applied to a Page object of
the Document Hierarchy; if a parameter is invalid; if a match does not occur;
or if one or more of the specified fingerprints do not exist. Otherwise,
True.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general guidance, and image requirements,
for using anchors to align a page with the original fingerprint.

method.name: PatternMatchIdentify
method.qi: : Identifies a page using image pattern matching.
method.ap: None.
method.h:
PatternMatchIdentify identifies a page's type and fingerprint using geometric pattern matching.
The locations of unique patterns are configured as Anchor Fields for each fingerprint in the Document Hierarchy.
One or more Anchor fields can be used to match geometric shapes on a fingerprint to the current image.
If one or more Anchor fields on the current page match a fingerprint, at or above the configured confidence level,
the page is identified with that fingerprint. The action does not require all defined anchors to match - the first match is used.
The action loads all Anchor field patterns from the fingerprint library, then searches on the current image
for each of the patterns in the associated zones. The search area for each zone is increased by the dimensions
specified in the page METRIC variable. If METRIC is not specified, the default is 500 pixels horizontal and vertical.
When this action finds a match, it sets the matching Fingerprint ID and Page Type. It will also create page-level
fields and update the Anchor fields with Anchor-specific pattern offset values in a field-level Image_Offset variable.
The offset can be used subsequent to matching a fingerprint. The pat_RegisterZones action can be used to align the
zones in the fingerprint to the current image, providing more accurately positioned text in each field.
This action requires the current page image to be bitonal (black and white), grayscale or color images will
cause the action to fail. The fingerprint image must have the same resolution (DPI) as the current page image.
The geometric shape contained in each Anchor field should be bold and well defined with clear edges, with
crisp black and white markings, producing a distinct shape. The shape should be thick and compact, not
composed of long thin lines. To avoid false positive matches, the shape should not match other shapes or black areas that may exist nearby within the same image.
PatternMatchIdentify()
method.ret: False, if the rule containing this action was not applied to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy; if a pattern match is not found; or if fingerprints do not exist. Otherwise, True.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general guidance, and image requirements,
for using anchors to align a page with the original fingerprint.

method.name: PatternMatchPageType
method.qi: : Identifies a page, restricted by the page type.
method.ap:
PageTypeList:
One or more Page Types defined in the Document Hierarchy.
If multiple types are specified, each type must be separated with a comma.
Smart Parameters are supported.
method.h:
PatternMatchPageType identifies a page's type and fingerprint using geometric pattern matching.
The locations of unique patterns are configured as Anchor Fields for each fingerprint in the Document Hierarchy.
One or more Anchor fields can be used to match geometric shapes on a fingerprint to the current image.
If one or more Anchor fields on the current page match a fingerprint, at or above the configured confidence level,
the page is identified with that fingerprint. The action does not require all defined anchors to match - the first match is used.
The action loads all Anchor field patterns from fingerprints with the specified page types, then searches on the current
image for each of the patterns in the associated zones. The search area for each zone is increased by the dimensions
specified in the page METRIC variable. If METRIC is not specified, the default is 500 pixels horizontal and vertical.
When this action finds a match, it sets the matching Fingerprint ID and Page Type. It will also create page-level fields
and update the Anchor fields with Anchor-specific pattern offset values in a field-level Image_Offset variable.
The offset can be used subsequent to matching a fingerprint. The RegisterZones action can be used to align the
zones in the fingerprint to the current image, providing more accurately positioned text in each field.
This action requires the current page image to be bitonal (black and white). Grayscale or color images
are not supported by this action. The fingerprint image must have the same resolution (DPI) as the current page image.
The geometric shape contained in each Anchor field should be bold and well defined with clear edges, with
crisp black and white markings, producing a distinct shape. The shape should be thick and compact, not
composed of long thin lines. To avoid false positive matches, the shape should not match other shapes
or black areas that may exist nearby within the same image. The shape should be a solid shape. Alphabetic
characters are not suitable anchors.
PatternMatchPageType("Invoice")
This action looks for a match among the inventory of fingerprints that have a
page type of "Invoice".
method.ret: False, if the rule containing this action was not applied to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy; if a pattern match is not found; or if fingerprints do not exist. Otherwise, True.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general guidance, and image requirements,
for using anchors to align a page with the original fingerprint.

method.name: RegisterZones
method.qi: : Registers and adjusts the positions of all fields on the current source page, based on the positions of the page's designated Anchor field(s).
method.ap: None.
method.h:
RegisterZones registers and adjusts the positions of all fields on the current page,
based on the previously matched positions of the page's designated Anchor field(s).
Anchor fields are determined by the Anchor Field setting in field's SetupDCO set using Datacap Studio, for each anchor field.
Prior to calling RegisterZones, usually in a different task or ruleset,
MatchPattern action must be called on each anchor field to identify the matching anchor position.
Then, when the RegisterZones action is called, the expected positions of the Anchor fields on the image
(taking into account the Fingerprint classification) are compared with the recognized
positions of the fields identified as an Anchor field.
The pages field zones must be set prior to calling RegisterZones.
Typically this is accomplished using action ReadZones to load the zone positions for the fields.
If any required Anchors are not matched, an operator may be required to update the Anchor position in a verify or fixup task.
If a field does not have loaded zone coordinates, it will be skipped.
All matched Anchor positions are used for adjustment, Anchors that are not matched are ignored.
If one Anchor is found, the field positions are all shifted by the same amount.
If two or more Anchors are found, the field positions are shifted by different amounts,
depending on their distance from each Anchor. This process is called Interpolation.
The expected positions of the Anchor fields on the image (taking into
account the Fingerprint classification) are compared with the recognized positions
of those Anchor fields - or the Anchor positions set manually by a Fixup task's operator.
RegisterZones adjusts the zone coordinates for all of the fields on the page that have
loaded coordinate positions but it will not adjust the position of anchor fields.
When debugging anchor alignment problems, it can be helpful to view the field
positions in the Test tab of Datacap Studio. While the field positions are updated on the page,
the anchor field positions are not updated.
To aid debugging alignment problems, RegisterZones can be configured to adjust anchor zones
when adjusting field positions.
By setting the variable "PMAdjustAnchor" to "1" on each anchor field, the zone coordinates
for the anchor field will be adjusted along with all of the other fields on the page.
This step can be useful to see if the adjusted values match the expected anchor position.
If the anchor position is not aligning with the anchor, then it is likely that the correct
anchor position is not being located during the MatchPattern action for one or more of the
anchors on the page. The anchor zone or METRIC may need adjustment to allow for
better matching. See the top-level help of this action library for more guidance.
ReadZones()
RegisterZones()
RecognizePageFieldsOCR_S()
This example assumes that between 1 to 3 anchor fields have been configured for the page.
The action MatchPattern must have been called for each of the anchor fields prior to this
example. Once those steps are completed, this example will call ReadZones to load
the coordinate positions for each field. RegisterZones then uses the previously
defined anchor fields to determine the correction offset and then adjusts each of
the zones on the page to align the field to the image for the page.
method.ret:
True
if the ruleset with this action is bound to a Page object of the Document Hierarchy,
and if the action can process all designated Anchor fields. Otherwise,
False.
method.see:
MatchPattern
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general guidance, and image requirements,
for using anchors to align a page with the original fingerprint.

method.name: ReleasePageAnchors
method.qi: : An action that can be called at the end of a batch to release information about the identity and location of a page's Anchor field(s).
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action can be optionally called to release the small amount of Anchor memory that
was allocated by the action RegisterZones. If ReleasePageAnchors is not called,
the memory will be released at the end of the batch or the next time RegisterZones is called.
ReleasePageAnchors()
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general guidance, and image requirements,
for using anchors to align a page with the original fingerprint.

method.name: SetMatchConfidence
method.qi: : Sets the confidence threshold for pattern matching.
method.ap:
The value of the minimum allowable confidence threshold.
The value must be between 0 (lowest confidence) and 9 (highest confidence).
Higher values require fewer differences between the compared areas to return a positive match value.
If this action is not called, then the minimum confidence defaults to 9.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Sets the confidence threshold for pattern matching.
SetMatchConfidence("5")
MatchPattern()
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for general guidance, and image requirements,
for using anchors to align a page with the original fingerprint.

af.name: PIC_FormatFields
af.g:
PIC_FormatFields = False
On Error Resume Next
oPictureStringFormater.m_bFilter = False
PIC_FormatFields = oPictureStringFormater.Process(CurrentObj)
oPictureStringFormater.CatchError("")

af.name: PIC_FilterFields
af.g:
PIC_FilterFields = False
On Error Resume Next
oPictureStringFormater.m_bFilter = True ' Replace low confidence with a space.
PIC_FilterFields = oPictureStringFormater.Process(CurrentObj)
oPictureStringFormater.CatchError("")

af.name: PIC_ValidateField
af.g:
Dim bReturn
Dim oSetupNode
Dim nSetupStatus
Dim bHiddenField
Dim sMsg
PIC_ValidateField = True
On Error Resume Next
If CurrentObj.ObjectType<>3 then
Writelog("Object must be of Type Field. Exiting.")
PIC_ValidateField = False
End if
bHiddenField=False
oPictureStringFormater.m_bFilter = False
bReturn = oPictureStringFormater.Validate(CurrentObj)
If bReturn = False Then
sMsg = RRState.LoadString("picture","CharOutOfScope","Field '{0}' value of '{1}' does not match the picture string format '{2}'.")
sMsg = replace(sMsg,"{0}",CurrentObj.ID)
sMsg = replace(sMsg,"{1}",CurrentObj.Text)
sMsg = replace(sMsg,"{2}",CurrentObj.Variable("PictureString"))
DCOMessage(sMsg)
End If
Set oSetupNode = CurrentObj.SetupNode
If oSetupNode is nothing then
Writelog("Unable to get setupNode for field " & CurrentObj.ID)
Else
If Trim(cstr(oSetupNode.Variable("STATUS")))="-1" then bHiddenField=True
End if
If Trim(cstr(CurrentObj.STATUS))="-1" then bHiddenField=True
If bHiddenField=False then PIC_ValidateField = bReturn

af.name: PIC_SetPictureCharacter
af.g:
On Error Resume Next
Dim PicCharNum
PIC_SetPictureCharacter = FALSE
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "'")
PicCharNum = Left(StrParam,1)
if Len(StrParam) < 3 then
WriteLog("SetPicChar parameter must be a single digit numeric followed by a comma, followed by the allowable characters")
Exit Function
end if
if Not IsNumeric(PicCharNum) then 'first character must be a digit
WriteLog("SetPicChar parameter must be a single digit numeric followed by a comma, followed by the allowable characters")
Exit Function
end if
if mid(StrParam,2,1) <> "," then
WriteLog("SetPicChar parameter must be a single digit numeric followed by a comma, followed by the allowable characters")
Exit Function
end if
CustomPicCharAr(PicCharNum) = Right(StrParam,Len(StrParam) - 2)
WriteLog("Picture Character " & cStr(PicCharNum) & " is set to: " & CustomPicCharAr(PicCharNum))
PIC_SetPictureCharacter = TRUE

af.name: PIC_ApplyPictureString
af.g:
Dim PicRepeatChar
Dim i
Dim CharaterSet
On Error Resume Next
PIC_ApplyPictureString = FALSE
if CurrentObj.ObjectType <> 3 then
Writelog("Action is for use on a field object only. Exiting")
Exit Function
end if
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "'")
if Len(StrParam) > len(CurrentObj.Text) then
WriteLog("Picture String is longer than the detected field value.")
Exit Function
End if
PicRepeatChar = Right(StrParam,1)
While len(StrParam) < len(CurrentObj.Text)
StrParam = StrParam & PicRepeatChar
wend
Writelog("Applying Picture String: " & StrParam & " to: " & CurrentObj.Text)
For i = 1 to Len(CurrentObj.Text)
Writelog("Checking " & mid(CurrentObj.Text,i,1) & " against picture character " & mid(StrParam,i,1) )
if Not oPictureStringFormater.IsCharValid(cStr(mid(CurrentObj.Text,i,1)), cStr(mid(StrParam,i,1))) then
'didn't find the current character in the characterset
Writelog("Picture Validation failed at character position " & cStr(i))
Exit Function
end if
next 'i
PIC_ApplyPictureString = TRUE

af.name: PIC_ReplaceBlankField
af.g:
Dim TrimValue ' The current field value with spaces trimmed at front and end.
Dim numChars ' Number of characters in the new field, if changed.
On Error Resume Next
PIC_ReplaceBlankField = False
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
call Writelog("PIC_ReplaceBlankField Input: " & strParam)
If (strParam = "") Then
Call Writelog("PIC_ReplaceBlankField requires a parameter. Exiting.")
Call ErrorHandler("PIC_ReplaceBlankField")
Exit Function
End if
If (CurrentObj.ObjectType <> 3) Then
Call Writelog("PIC_ReplaceBlankField Object must be of Type Field. Exiting.")
Call ErrorHandler("PIC_ReplaceBlankField")
Exit Function
End if
PIC_ReplaceBlankField = True
TrimValue = trim(CurrentObj.Text)
If (TrimValue = "") Then
Call Writelog("Replacing empty field " & CurrentObj.Text & " with: " & strParam)
CurrentObj.Text = strParam
numChars = len(strParam)
CurrentObj.ConfidenceString = String(clng(numChars), "1") ' Set new confidence value to low
Else
Call Writelog("Field is not empty: " & CurrentObj.Text)
End if
Call ErrorHandler("PIC_ReplaceBlankField")
