method.name: IsBlankPage
method.ap:
MaximumWords:
A numeric value indicating the maximum number of words in the Fingerprint file (.cco) of a
"blank" source page. "50", for example, tells the action that if a CCO file has 50 words or less,
its page is
blank.
. The value must be a positive integer.
IsBlank:
"True" or "False" indicating if the action should return true if the page is blank or return false
if the page is blank.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action counts the number of "words" in the CCO file of the current page and returns true if
the count is less than or equal to the number entered as the parameter.
A CCO file must exist prior to calling this action.
The CCO file must contain results of recognition to work properly.
The file can be created by recogntion actions such as RecognizePageOCR_S, or RecognizePageOCR_A.
For fingerprints only, a CCO file can be created by the action
AnalyzeImage, which will not contain any recognized words, it will only
contain geometry information about the image for fingerprint matching. Because of this,
a CCO created by AnalyzeImage is not suitable for using IsBlankPage.
Recognition actions like RecognizePageOCR_A may interpret non-character data as characters,
such as blobs, specs and logos, increasing the word count.
It can be helpful to use image enhancement to clean up a page
to remove scan artifacts to prevent them from being recognized as words or letters on
a blank page. Adjusting the IsBlankPage action to allow a small number of words
will allow the action to distinguish between blank pages
with some noise vs. a page that should be considered non-blank.
RecognizePageOCR_A()
IsBlankPage(15)
SetPageType(Separator)
This sequence uses RecognizePageOCR_A to create a CCO file, then checks to see
if the file contains less than 15 words. If so, the
IsBlankPage(15)
action
returns True. The final action, SetPageType, establishes the page as a Separator page
by setting the page type to the current DCO page object.
method.ret:
False
if the action parameter is invalid or if the action is unable to locate the Image file for the
current page or its CCO file. It also returns
False,
if the number of "words" in the CCO
is greater than the value passed as a parameter.
If the "IsBlank" parameter is "True", returns
True
if the number of "words"
in the CCO is less than or equal to the value of the parameter, otherwise it will return False.
If the "IsBlank" parameter is "False", returns
False
if the number of "words"
in the CCO is less than or equal to the value of the parameter, otherwise it will return True.
method.see:

A similar action, IdentifyBlankPagesBySize, in the AutomaticDocumentFingerprinting action library checks the size of
a file, and if the size is smaller than the provided size, it is considered to be blank.

method.name: CreateCcoFromLayout
method.h:
Creates a CCO file after recognition or document conversion is performed when the recognition result is a layout XML file.
The CCO is needed for the locate actions, for click ‘n’ key during verification and other Datacap operations.
Calling this action will convert the results in the layout XML into
a CCO so it can be utilized in other subsequent actions and Datacap clients.
CreateCcoFromLayout requires a previously created layout file (for example: tm000001_layout.xml) that was created by the Recognize() action.
Refer to the action you are using to perform recognition
to see if that action creates a layout file or if the action automatically creates a CCO.
The recognition action, such as RecognizePageOCR_A, creates a CCO directly then calling this action separately is not required
because RecognizePage directly creates a CCO file. Refer to the action help to determine if CCO normalization must be called
separately or if it is automatically performed by the RecognizePage action.
Some Datacap actions may require a CCO and a layout file.
See the DocumentAnalytics help introduction for information on the layout XML file.
Recognize()
CreateCcoFromLayout()
NormalizeCCO()
The layout file is created by the Recognize action. Then CreateCcoFromLayout creates the CCO based on the
recognition results. NormalizeCCO then normalizes the CCO to get it ready for use by other Datacap clients
and actions.
method.ret:
Always
True.
method.see: Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about this action library.

method.name: SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM

p.name: MaxHeightTMM
p.qi: The new maximum height for calculations.

method.ap:
An
Integer
specifying a maximum height of characters to permit in the CCO, in 1/10 mm units. Default is 64, or approximately 1/4 inch (50 pixels at 200 DPI).
The value of zero (0) turns off this functionality.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
When the action NormalizeCCO is run, it organizes the recognition results, determining which text belongs on the same line.
During its calculations, it will filter out characters that are larger than a specific size and these characters will not
be included in the final CCO that is created. The characters that are filtered out are typically logos or other large text
that is usually not needed for document verification and processing. Having large text can cause lines to be
created in an unexpected way. For example, text from two different lines may appear in the same line, or the text from the
same line may be split into multiple lines. That is why the action tries to remove large text that is likely not needed.
If large text is missing within the CCO then it is likely that the text was removed because it was too large.
This can be confirmed by enabling action logging and reviewing the text of the NormalizeCCO action to see if it states
large characters were removed.
By adjusting the character height, it is possible to control the size of the characters that should be removed, so large text can
be maintained within the final CCO.
SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM(75)
NormalizeCCO()
This example shows how the adjustment can be made prior to calling NormalizeCCO.
SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM(75)

method.name: SetMaxCharacterHeightAVG

p.name: AVG
p.qi: The new average for calculations.

method.ap:
One or two digit
Integer
value sets the percent maximum height of characters over the average to permit in the CCO.
Off by default. Parameter of zero (0) or less turns off this functionality.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
When the action NormalizeCCO is run, it organizes the recognition results, determining which text belongs on the same line.
During its calculations, it will filter out characters that are larger than a specific size and these characters will not
be included in the final CCO that is created. The characters that are filtered out are typically logos or other large text
that is usually not needed for document verification and processing. Having large text can cause lines to be
created in an unexpected way. For example, text from two different lines may appear in the same line, or the text from the
same line may be split into multiple lines. That is why the action tries to remove large text that is likely not needed.
If large text is missing within the CCO then it is likely that the text was removed because it was too large.
This can be confirmed by enabling action logging and reviewing the text of the NormalizeCCO action to see if it states
large characters were removed.
By adjusting the average character height, it is possible to control the size of the characters that should be removed, so large text can
be maintained within the final CCO.
SetMaxCharacterHeightAVG(15)
NormalizeCCO()
This example shows how the adjustment can be made prior to calling NormalizeCCO.
SetMaxCharacterHeightAVG(15)
RecognizePageOCR_A()
This example shows how to specify the adjustment prior to calling an action that automatically performs the
NormalizeCCO operation.
method.ret:
True,
if the input value is an integer, otherwise
false.

method.name: NormalizeCCO
method.h:
This action sorts the words and lines in a Fingerprint file (.cco) created by a recognition engine.
The CCO file contains the recognized text and is used for click-n-key during validation,
pattern match actions, locate actions, snapping full page recognized text to fields,
and used by other components of Datacap that operate
on recognized text. It takes the text as recognized by a recognition engine and
organizes it into lines. For example, if this action is not called,
text that appears separated on the left and right side of a page, but would visually
be considered the same line, may not be considered on the same line, causing actions
like the Locate actions to operate in ways that may not be anticipated.
The action is automatically called by some full-page recognition
actions like OCR/A. This action should always be called before using
Locate
actions or the
pat_RecogMatch_ID
action to
find recognized text on a page.
In this context, the fingerprint is calculated for a particular image in a batch, as opposed to
the Fingerprint database, which contains fingerprints for various page types and layout variations
that have been defined for a particular application.
There are two types of Fingerprint files. One type is based on the image geometry. The second
type is based on recognized text. The
AnalyzeImage
action creates a geometric
fingerprint containing lines and "words" based only on the black pixels in the image. Full-page
recognition actions (
RecognizePageOCR_S, RecognizePageICR_C, RecognizePageOCR_A
etc.) create a
fingerprint based on the results of recognition, i.e. both geometry and text of the
recognized characters, words and lines.
In recognition-based fingerprints, the order of lines and words may appear to be arbitrary,
especially if the page contains images, tables, stamps, or blocks of text with varying font sizes.
This can cause unpredictable results from
Locate
actions that navigate geometrically.
The word-matching and phrase-matching action
pat_RecogMatch_ID
also requires
well-ordered text to work reliably.
The
NormalizeCCO
action re-orders the words of text in a Recognition-based fingerprint into
lines and words in "standard" reading order, from top to bottom and left to right.
LineHeightOverlapPercent parameter
is percentage of a line that two words must be offset to be considered as separate lines.
By default LineHeightOverlapPercent is set to 50 percent.
This variable can be used if the offset between two word in different lines, seems to be less than the default value which is 50.
It may be necessary to test multiple values on a wide variety of pages to get a value that works well
for all of your documents.
Some recognition actions, such as RecognizePageOCR_S, do not automatically call NormalizeCCO so this action
will need to be explicitly called in rules after recognition to normalize the CCO for subsequent actions that
use the CCO results.
Conversely, it may be possible that for specific applications, it may be better to leave the recognition
as it is returned from the engine. If this is the case, then for actions that automatically perform
NormalizeCCO, such as RecognizePageOCR_A, the application must first call the action CCONormalization_OFF()
to prevent the recognition action from automatically performing the normalization.
Because the action MergeCCOs_ByType removes page numbers, NormalizeCCO should not be called
after the action MergeCCOs_ByType is used.
rrSet (35,@P.LineHeightOverlapPercent)
In the example, if two words are vertically offset by more than 35% of the height of the words, then they are considered to be on separate lines.
Lower values are more likely to split words into separate lines. Higher values are more likely to merge words into a single line.
LineHeightOverlapPercent variable
should be set before NormalizeCCO().
rrSet (35,@P.LineHeightOverlapPercent)
RecognizePageOCR_A
IMPORTANT NOTE: By default NormalizeCCO
discards any "words" or blocks
containing characters taller than 1/4 inch, or the height set by SetMaxCharacterHeightTMM().
If large words are missing from the page, this may be the reason and can be confirmed by reviewing the action
log to see if large text is being removed. This is done as large text, such as company logos, are typically
not needed and can cause text alignment problems when the CCO is normalized.
NOTE:
If the
AnalyzeImage
action is called before full-page recognition,
the recognized text is placed into the geometry created by
AnalyzeImage.
This hybrid
Fingerprint file is not always suitable for
cco2cco.
To force creation of a pure
recognition-based fingerprint, call
SetFingerprintRecogPriority(True)
before full-page recognition. This guarantees that any existing geometric fingerprint will be ignored,
and it applies to
OCR_S
and
ICR_C
only.
NOTE:
The full page recognition actions, RecognizePageXXX from the
ICR_C
and
RecognizeOCRA
libraries call NormalizeCCO() automatically unless the action
CCONormalization_OFF (from the
Recog_Shared
library) is called prior to recognition. The full page recognition from the
OCR_SR
library, however, requires that
NormalizeCCO() to be called manually post recognition.
If using the OCR/A or OCR/SR action "Recognize", then first use the action CreateCcoFromLayout to load the CCO after recognition has been performed.
If only field level recognition is performed, then the CCO and CCO normalization does not apply.
SetFingerprintRecogPriority("True")
RecognizePageOCR_S()
NormalizeCCO()
pat_RecogMatch_ID()

method.name: SnapCCOtoDCO
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action transfers the recognition results of the current page's CCO file to the
appropriate
Field
objects of the Document Hierarchy (DCO). Note that the action only
transfers the text to child fields.
This action is useful by taking the results of full page recognition results contained within
the page CCO file and mapping the results
into DCO fields based on the zone position of the field. The effect is
similar to performing field level recognition on each of the fields.
A CCO must exist for the page. The CCO can be created by calling a RecongizePage action
or by calling a Recognize action and then using CreateCCOFromLayout to generate the CCO
for the page. The fields must
have the zone locations loaded, just as is required for field level recognition.
SnapCCOToDCO will only clear / update field text when all of the following conditions are met:
- Field is not an OMR field (i.e. var RecogType=4).
- Field has positions assigned.
- Field does not have the variable "v_skipsnap" set to 1.
- Field has data mapping to the CCO (at least one character).
- Fixes issue that would affect processing of reserved fields (i.e. fields that are used for anchor finding followed by snapping of data).
The action PopulateZonedField in the ZonesAndLineItems action library is very similar to this action. The difference
is that PopulateZonedField updates a single field.
RecognizePageOCR_A()
SnapCCOtoDCO()
method.ret:
False
if a ruleset with this action is not bound to a
Page
object or
Field
object of the Document Hierarchy. Otherwise,
True.

To have an effect, this action must be called prior to SnapCCOtoDCO.
The adjustment is set to off by Default.

method.name: SetFingerprintRecognitionPriority
method.ap:
True:
If a CCO already exists prior to recognition, it is replaced with a brand new one with
recognition results.
False:
If SetFingerprintRecognitionPriority is not called (or is set to false) and a CCO already
exists prior to recognition, the recognition results will be added to that CCO.
method.h:
This action sets the option that controls whether a full-page recognition action is to create
a CCO file for the current page. When the option is On, processing is faster because the call
to the
AnalyzeImage
action is eliminated.
The difference between creating a CCO from scratch with recognition results and adding the recognition
results to the existing CCO created by AnalyzeImage is that in the "adding" case,
the recognized characters are put into the CCO in a manner that uses a different fingerprinting technique.
Note:
Be sure to place this action before a full-page recognition action.
SetFingerprintRecognitionPriority(True)
method.ret:
Always
True.

method.name: SnapDCOtoCCO
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action transfers the recognition results assigned to
Field
objects of the
Document Hierarchy(DCO) to the current page's CCO file.
If zonal recognition is used instead of full-page recognition, the action will populate
the current page's CCO file with the results of zonal recognition from each of the fields.
When a new CCO is created,
the CCO will only contain the text from the field recognition. There can be use cases
where it is preferable to only have field text in the CCO, ignoring all other text on the page
that was not within a field zone. Because the field position text is in the CCO, when the Verify
task runs, a user can use the ClickNKey option to populate fields in a verification panel
as can be done with full page recognition.
After calling SnapDCOtoCCO, the action NormalizeCCO should be called to ensure that
the text is properly located in the CCO.

method.name: PercentBlackPixels

p.name: Percentage
p.qi: The percentage of black pixels

p.name: MinMax
p.qi: Indicates if the percentage should be evaluated as a minimum or maximum

method.ap:
Percentage:
The parameter must be a numerical value that indicates the percentage to be tested.
Either a minimum percentage or a maximum percentage.
MinMax:
Indicates if the percentage should be considered a minimum value or a maximum value.
A value of "Min" or "Minimum" indicates the percentage is a minimum value.
A value of "Max" or "Maximum" indicates the percentage is a maximum value.
If not provided, the value will default to "Minimum".
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
The action evaluates the image for the current object and determines the percentage of black pixels.
If the current object is a page, then the entire page image will be evaluated. If the current object
is a field, then the area defined for the field will be evaluated. If the object is a field,
then the field's zone coordinates must be loaded.
The action will evaluate the percentage and compare it to the provided percentage parameter.
If the percentage is expected to be a minimum, then the action will return true if the
percentage of black is greater than the provided percentage value. If the
percentage is expected to be a maximum, then the action will return true if the
actual percentage is less than the maximum percentage provided.
The action will create the DCO variable "NumberBlackPixels" with the value
of the number of black pixels in the image.
The action will create the DCO variable "PercentPixels" indicating the
actual percentage of black pixels in the area.
It is required that the associated page image must be a 1 bit image.
PercentBlackPixels("4.54", "Min")
This action will return true if the percentage of black pixels is greater than or equal to 4.54%.
PercentBlackPixels("4.54", "Max")
This action will return true if the percentage of black pixels is less than or equal to 4.54%.
method.ret:
If the percentage is expected to be a minimum, then the action will return
true
if the
percentage of black is greater than the provided percentage value. If the
percentage is expected to be a maximum, then the action will return
true
if the
actual percentage is less than the maximum percentage provided.
If an error is encountered, the action will return
false.
method.see:
DetermineOMRThreshold
Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about this action library.

method.name: DetermineOMRThreshold
method.ap:
Floating Point
or
Integer
values that specify the count of black
pixels in OMR boxes:
1.
Threshold:
the percentage of pixels in the zone - the field zone not the printed box
that should be considered "checked", i.e. the lightest box that is not just noise, but should
be considered a check mark.
2.
Background:
the percentage of pixels in the zone that might be due to scanner noise
and/or the border of the printed box. This value also controls the range on either side of the
Threshold value that is “low confidence”.
Please note: The action also accepts parameters that are fractional percentages which are needed
to detect marks in very large zones.
The parameters should be experimentally adjusted on real-world scanned forms.
First, determine the Threshold value that correctly identifies a light mark as “checked”, and
correctly identifies noisy zones as “unchecked”.
Second, adjust the Background parameter’s value to achieve an acceptable confidence interval.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action performs OMR, Optical Mark Recognition, checkbox detection by counting black pixels within each OMR box area in a
Field with one or more OMR boxes. This action can be used to perform OMR detection on a page
that has drop-out boxes which leave just the mark and it can be used on black forms that
where the bounding box has not been removed. The input parameters can be adjusted to allow
OMR detection for both scenarios.
Text Boxes
The action sets the text value of the field to a string of 0's and 1's
(one digit per OMR box); and assigns a Confidence String to the string of digits: '4' for Low Confidence up to '9' for High Confidence.
Density String and Confidence Value
The action also creates a "DensityString"
variable for the Character String, indicating percentage-filled, from ASCII 48 ('0') through 148.
For each possible OMR box, there will be a character. The character's ASCII value minus 48 is the percentage-filled.
If the Density String=0X, the first OMR field was blank, and the second was 40% filled. The ASCII value for X is 88. 88 minus 48 = 40.
For each OMR mark a DCO variable named OMRXPct, where X is the numerical index of the OMR mark, is created
and set with the percentage of the field that is black. This is provided in case this information is also useful for the application.
MultiPunch and Confidence Values
If the MultiPunch setting is set to 1 and multiple OMR's were filled beyond the threshold,
the one that was filled the most will be marked and set to Low Confidence.
If the percentage-filled is below the second parameter, the OMR box will not be selected and the confidence will be high.
If the percentage-filled is between the two parameters, the OMR box will not be selected and the confidence will be low.
If the percentage-filled is above the first parameter and below double the first parameter minus the second parameter,
the OMR box will be selected and the confidence will be low.
If the percentage-filled is above double the first parameter minus the second parameter,
the OMR box will be selected and the confidence will be high.
Note: The
DetermineOMRThreshold
action works best on dropout boxes, but with an appropriate background value can work effectively with
mark bounding boxes that are visible in the scanned image.
If you are using small visible mark bounding boxes on your image, it is best to zone the area by surrounding the entire
visible box with room for alignment movement, then factor out the black from the box using the parameters.
If you attempt to zone inside the borders of a visible box, you can get a false positive if the page
does not align exactly because with poor alignment, part of the bounding box may be unexpectedly in the area
that should be clear, causing a false positive.
The page image must be a 1 bit black and white image. If the image is not 1 bit, the action C2BW_Convert in
the ColorToBW library can be used to convert the image to a black and white 1 bit image.
When converting a color image to black and white, it is best to disable dithering of shaded areas.
This action requires the target field to be an OMR field with subfields for each OMR mark.
The field must be defined as an OMR field by having the DCO variable "RecogType" defined with a value of "4".
DetermineOMRThreshold("10","5")
For a small to medium size zone, “10% filled” may be considered a deliberate mark. Anything below 5% (Background) is definitely
not
a mark. Anything above 15% (Threshold + (Threshold – Background)) is a high confidence mark.
This would work with a non-dropout OMR field where the box’s printed outline takes up less than 5% of the zone area. It would also work for dropout forms.
DetermineOMRThreshold("2","0")
This is for a signature line, or a large zone where the percentage-filled is usually much lower than for a small zone. This assumes very little background or noise.

method.h:

PopulateZnLineItemField()
DetermineLineItemOMRThreshold("10","5")
For a small to medium size zone, “10% filled” may be considered a deliberate mark. Anything below 5% (Background) is definitely
not
a mark. Anything above 15% (Threshold + (Threshold – Background)) is a high confidence mark.
This would work with a non-dropout OMR field where the box’s printed outline takes up less than 5% of the zone area. It would also work for dropout forms.

method.name: CCONormalizationOff
method.ap: None.
method.h:
A full-page recognition action such as
RecognizePageOCR_A
automatically call the
NormalizeCCO
action after recognition is complete to properly format the recognized text within
the new CCO.
Normalization is needed for features such as the Locate actions and for Click-n-key. There may be circumstances where
automatic normalization should be skipped.
To by-pass this procedure, place
CCONormalizationOff
right before a recognition action
that automatically calls NormalizeCCO.
CCONormalizationOff()
RecognizePageOCR_A()

method.name: CopyPageTextToTarget
method.ap:
Target:
A smart parameter expression that resolves to a field or variable.
MaxLines:
A number that specifies the number of lines to write from the current page.
A 0 value will include all lines from the page. Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This action will copy the recognized text in a page to a field or variable. The text is copied
without any formatting information, only line breaks.
Recognition must have been previously performed on the page and a Datacap CCO must
exist for the page.
Actions such as "RecognizePage..." perform recognition resulting in the creation of
a page CCO. The action "CreateCCOFromLayout" will create a CCO from a layout file,
which is created by a "Recognize" action. See these actions in other action
libraries for more information on their operation.
After successfully completing, this action will also create a DCO variable on the current
page called
"PageLineCount"
. This variable holds the number of lines written from the page.
Be aware that it is possible for text that appears on the same line on the document
to be split into multiple lines. This will usually occur if there is text of different sizes,
the baseline of the text is not close enough, or if there is a skew to the page. This situation
is unavoidable on some documents.
When page text is copied to a variable or field, no position or confidence information is retained.
Only the text itself is copied and any other attributes are discarded. If the destination
is a field, the field location properties are not updated with the coordinates of the text.
Important:
Use this action with caution as it may put a substantial amount of data within the DCO.
The issue could be compounded by using this action on every page within a batch.
A large DCO may not perform well. This issue can be improved
by storing the text in a field or a field variable instead of a page variable.
Regardless of where the page text is stored in the DCO,
it is recommended to delete the text from the DCO when it is no longer needed
limit the growth of the DCO. The added text can be removed
by using an rrSet action to remove the text. For example: rrSet("@EMPTY", "@X.MySavedText"), where the variable "MySavedText"
would be replaced by the location where the page text has been copied. This action will empty
the variable or field, removing the text from the DCO.
RecognizePageOCR_A()
CopyPageTextToTarget("@X.PageText", "0")
˂Additional actions that use the text>
rrSet("@EMPTY", "@X.PageText")
The action, RecognizePageOCR_A, recognizes the text on the current page
and creates a CCO for the page, which contains the recognition results for use
by follow on actions.
The CopyPageToTarget
action places the recognized page text into a variable called "PageText" on the current page
as plain text.
The action CopyPageTetToTarget also creates a variable called "PageLineCount" that has the number of lines
copied from the page.
Next, any number of actions can use the PageText variable as needed. Once the work is done,
the page text is deleted from the DCO using the rrSet action.
RecognizePageOCR_A()
CopyPageTextToTarget("@X\Field1", "4")
This example performs full page recognition and then copies the first 4 lines
of page text to a child field called "Field1".
It also creates a variable on the current page object called "PageLineCount" that has the number of lines
copied from the page.

RecognizePageOCR_A, RecognizePageOCR_S, and Recognize.

method.name: CreateTextFile
method.ap: None.
method.h:
This action creates a UTF-8 encoded Text file (.txt) for the current page; adds the page's recognized values to the file;
and places the file in the current batch, in the current batch directory.
The Text file generated by this action is handy for debugging purposes - to
see what recognition is placing into the page's Fingerprint file(.cco) file.
The text file is a dump of the CCO and the intended use is only for debugging.
The action must
follow a full-page recognition action such as
RecognizePageOCR_S
, in a rule applied
to a
Page
object of the Document Hierarchy.
Some actions may need the action NormalizeCCO to be called after recognition to
standardize the text positions in the CCO. This action does not add padding spaces
to exactly match the formatting of the original page.
RecognizePageOCR_S()
CreateTextFile()
SetProblemValue(0.7)
SetSearchArea(0.5)
FindFingerprint(True)
After the full-page recognition action (
RecognizePageOCR_S
), the
CreateTextFile()
action places the recognized values into a Text file that it has set up for the page, and
adds the file to the current batch, in the application's
Batches
directory.
The text file that is created has the same filename as the image, but is assigned a .txt
filename extension.

method.name: SetFullPageRecognitionArea

p.name: Area
p.qi: A percentage indicating the amount of the page to recognize.

p.name: StartPosition
p.qi: A percentage indicating how far down the page to start.

method.ap:
Area:
A decimal value indicating the percent of the page to be recognized in response to this action.
For example: "0.1" designates the first 10% of the page, while "1.0" calls for recognition
of the entire page. If this action is not called, 100% of the page will be recognized.
StartPosition:
A decimal value indicating the percentage of the page to skip
when recognizing a portion of the page. A value of "0.0" indicates that none
of the page should be skipped so recognition will start at the top of the page.
A value of "0.5" will start recognizing the page from half way down from the
top of the page. The page will then be recognized for the percentage specified
by the "Area" parameter. If this action is not called, full page recognition
always starts from the top of the page.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
This optional action sets the area of the current page that will be the target of
recognition procedures when full-page recognition action is called. This action is helpful
if it is known that a page's values will always be in a particular location or if
it is useful to recognize only a portion of the page. Like field level recognition, recognizing
a portion of the page is faster then recognizing the entire page.
The Area and StartPosition parameters control the location of the page to recognize. The
StartPosition parameter indicates the percentage down on the page to start recognition while the Area
parameter controls how much to recognize below the start position. The sum of the Area and StartPosition
percentages can be less than 100%, but they cannot exceed 100%.
Only specific actions utilize this setting. The OCR/A action RecognizePageOCR_A and the
OCR/S action RecognizePageOCR_S will use this setting, if this action is used.
Note that this action can cause recognition to include a slice of lines
at the top or bottom of the recognition area. In this kind of situation, it is likely
that the lines that are only partially included within the recognition area
will not be recognized correctly.
SetFullPageRecognitionArea("0.5", "0.0")
RecognizePageOCR_S()
This example recognizes the top half of the page using the OCR/S engine.
SetFullPageRecognitionArea(".2", "0.15")
ReconizePageOCR_A()
This example recognizes 20% of the page. The recognition will start
15% down from the top of the page, effectively performing recognition
on the page starting from 15% from the top, down to 35% from the top of the page.
method.see:
RecognizePageOCR_S, RecognizePageOCR_A
Refer to the top-level help topic for more information about this action library.

af.name: SplitBatch
af.g:
'Splits documents or pages in the batch into sub-batches, according to the value of the smart parameter you enter. ' If a page is part of a document, it goes along with all other pages in that parent document. For more information, ' see the Parameters and Details sections below. " 'A smart parameter that determines the sub-batch for each document or page.

' Important: The action evaluates each document and loose page in the batch. ' An unbound page is any page not inside a document. ' The set of smart parameter values found during the evaluation are grouped into "buckets":

' 1. Identical values go into the same bucket.

' 2. If there are multiple buckets, all pages/documents that share the same value will ' split to the same child batch.

' 3. There can be only one child batch for each unique bucket value.

' ' Child batches are named like the parent batch, but with a suffix such as .01, .02, etc.

' For example you might use for splitting:

' @D.Inbox. If there is an Inbox variable in each document, this will split documents by ' the value of the Inbox. Important! Any document or loose page ' that does not have this value set will remain in the parent batch. On Error Resume Next Dim nPages Dim CurrentPage Dim retn Dim retSplit Dim sBucketValue Dim oPage Dim i Dim nIndex Dim bReturn Pilot.ChildrenQuantity = 0 sBucketName = StrParam SplitBatch = False retSplit = True If CurrentObj.ObjectType <> DCO_BATCH Then Writelog("SplitBatch action must be bound at the batch level. Failed.") Exit Function End If 'Force write DCO Data files If Instr(lcase(Pilot.dcofile),lcase(Pilot.BatchDir))<=0 Then sPageFile = Pilot.BatchDir + "\" + Pilot.dcofile Else sPageFile = Pilot.dcofile End if bReturn=DCO.Write(sPageFile) If bReturn=False then Call Writelog("ERROR Writing File: '" & Pilot.dcofile & "'. Aborting Batch.") Call Writelog("DCO Last Error:'" & DCO.GetLastError() & "'.") Call AbortBatch() End if WriteLog("SplitBatch on value: '" & StrParam & "'") sStatID = dco.Variable("ScanStation") sScanUser = dco.Variable("ScanUser") If CurrentObj.Variable("SplitBatchRetryCount") = "" Then retryCount = 3 'default max number of retries Else retryCount = CInt(CurrentObj.Variable("SplitBatchRetryCount")) End If If CurrentObj.Variable("SplitBatchRetrySleep") = "" Then retrySleepSecs = 1 'default retry sleep 1 second Else retrySleepSecs = CInt(CurrentObj.Variable("SplitBatchRetrySleep")) if (retrySleepSecs > 59) Then retrySleepSecs = 59 End If Writelog("SplitBatchRetryCount: " & retryCount &", SplitBatchRetrySleep: " & retrySleepSecs) On Error Goto 0 nPages = CurrentObj.NumOfChildren() Call WriteLog("SplitBatch processing " + CStr(CurrentObj.NumOfChildren())+" pages or docs") If nPages = 0 Then ' abort the batch Exit Function End If Set dictBuckets = CreateObject("Scripting.Dictionary") For CurrentPage = 0 To nPages - 1 ' Call WriteLog("SplitBatch evaluate # " + CStr(CurrentPage+1)) Set oPage = CurrentObj.GetChild(CurrentPage) If oPage.ObjectType = DCO_PAGE or oPage.ObjectType = DCO_DOCUMENT Then If sBucketName = "" then ' for testing - when no parameter just use pageID sBucketValue = oPage.ID Else On Error Resume Next Set oSaveCurrentObj = CurrentObj Set CurrentObj = oPage If IsAlive(g_DCSmart) then g_DCSmart.SetRRCurrentDCO(CurrentObj) sBucketValue = CStr(MetaWord(sBucketName)) Call WriteLog("Page or document value: " & sBucketValue) Set CurrentObj = oSaveCurrentObj If IsAlive(g_DCSmart) then g_DCSmart.SetRRCurrentDCO(CurrentObj) On Error Goto 0 End if if sBucketValue <> "" then if Not dictBuckets.Exists(sBucketValue) then dictBuckets.Add sBucketValue, sBucketValue End If End If Else 'Call WriteLog("Process unknown object - failed") 'Set dictBuckets = Nothing 'bAbort = True 'nTaskStatus = RetAbort 'Exit Function End If Next ' next page in batch ' Was maximum of 99 sub-batches now with new object 'oDCBase36' and AlphaDecimal names (01 to ZZ) allows 1295 sub-batches if dictBuckets.Count > 1295 Then WriteLog("More than 1295 values in " & sBucketName & ", SplitBatch failed") Set dictBuckets = Nothing bAbort = True nTaskStatus = RetAbort Exit Function End If If dictBuckets.Count > 0 Then ' we will split N batches Pilot.ChildrenQuantity = dictBuckets.Count ' this must be done before setting any of the conditions aBuckets = dictBuckets.Keys For i = 0 to dictBuckets.Count-1 WriteLog ("SplitBatch process subbatch " & CStr(i) & " " & aBuckets(i)) retSplit = SplitChildBatch(CurrentObj, aBuckets(i), i) ' split a subbatch for each bucket if retSplit <> True then Set dictBuckets = Nothing bAbort = True nTaskStatus = RetAbort WriteLog("SplitBatch failed") Exit Function End If Next ' next i ' clear out all pages/docs that were split from the page file For nIndex = CurrentObj.NumOfChildren-1 to 0 Step -1 Set oPage = CurrentObj.GetChild(nIndex) if sBucketName = "" then ' for testing - when no parameter just use pageID sBucketValue = oPage.ID else On Error Resume Next Set oSaveCurrentObj = CurrentObj Set CurrentObj = oPage If IsAlive(g_DCSmart) then g_DCSmart.SetRRCurrentDCO(CurrentObj) sBucketValue = CStr(MetaWord(sBucketName)) Call WriteLog("Page or document value: " & sBucketValue) Set CurrentObj = oSaveCurrentObj If IsAlive(g_DCSmart) then g_DCSmart.SetRRCurrentDCO(CurrentObj) On Error Goto 0 End if if sBucketValue <> "" then ' delete any page or doc that has a bucket value - e.g. is split CurrentObj.Deletechild(nIndex) End If Next 'nIndex End If Set dictBuckets = Nothing If retSplit = True Then SplitBatch = True End If

'************************************************************************ ' Batch Split Actions ' ' Licensed Materials - Property of IBM ' “Restricted Materials of IBM” ' 5725-C15 5725-C69 ' ' © Copyright IBM Corp. 1994, 2020 All Rights Reserved ' ' US Government Users Restricted Rights - Use, duplication or ' disclosure restricted by GSA ADP Schedule Contract with ' IBM Corp. ' '************************************************************************
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the Newly SplitBatch action in the SplitBatch action library.
A smart parameter pointing to a Document or Page variable that determines if the Document or Page is to be split to a Child Batch.
Important: The action evaluates all documents and pages (including unbound* pages) in the batch.
The values of the smart parameter variable found during the document and page evaluation are grouped into "buckets":
1. Pages/documents that contain the variable and the variable values are identical go into the same bucket.
2. If there are multiple buckets, all pages/documents that share the same value will split to the same child batch.
3. There can be only one child batch for each unique bucket value.
Child batches have the same name as the parent batch, but include an additional two character alpha-decimal suffix such as .01, .02, .0A, ..., up to .ZZ. This hexadecimal numbering for child batches is required by Taskmaster Server. Taskmaster Server creates the batch and queue entries for the child batches after the task is finished, when the split condition is processed. There is a maximum of 1295 child batches.
Example:
@D.Inbox. If there is an Inbox variable in each document, this will split documents by the value of the Inbox variable.
Important: Any document or unbound* page that does not have this Inbox variable value, will remain in the parent batch.
*An unbound page is any page not inside a document.
This action will process all of the documents and "unbound" pages that are in the batch and attempt to split the identified documents and pages into child batches. The action will look in the documents or unbound pages for the variable specified in the a parameter, group the objects that have a matching value, and split each group into a unique child batch.
Only documents and unbound pages will be processed. Pages that are already placed within in a document structure will not be processed individually, the pages will be as part of their document, not as a separate page.
Additional considerations:
There is only one "job routing condition" raised by this action: it is the first one in the task's list of conditions.
The task's Task Setup/Task Settings screen must be configured as Job Router, and a single condition defined (by convention, call it Split).
1. Any and all child batches will be routed via this single condition.
2. If the application wants to treat the individual buckets differently, then the first step in the workflow after splitting can check the same smart parameter value and branch or re-route the child batch using that value.
3. All the structure and variables, etc. that were in the parent batch docs/pages are retained in the child batches.
4. In addition, new variables ParentBatch and ParentBatchDir are added.
5. The action can only be used once per Parent Batch.
6. The maximum number of child batches is 1295.
7. The page count and document count in child batches is not accurate after splitting. It is updated and will be accurate once the next task completes. SplitBatchRetryCount This variable can be used to set the retry count for splitbatch.
SplitBatchRetrySleep This variable can be set sleeping time between the retries. If not set default value will be 1 second.
SplitBatch(@D.Inbox)
Batch level only.
False if an error occurs like a file could not be created, etc., and the batch will be set to abort. Otherwise True.
If the specified variable is not found in any documents or unbound pages, meaning there is nothing to split, the action is still considered to be successful and will return true.
Each child batch split off will generate a condition, which should be configured for Split in the workflow.
Any page or document with a blank value for the splitting value will remain in the original "parent" batch.

af.name: TifMerge_SetFileName
af.g:
'Sets the name of the multi-Image file (.tif) to be created by TifMerge." 'String value of the file name to be assigned to the multi-page file. Smart parameters are supported.
' This action sets the name of the multi-Image file (.tif) to be created by the TifMerge actions. ' The file’s name can be text, or a combination of text and the value of a variable your enter as a parameter. ' The action automatically adds the “.tif” extension to the file.

g_TifMergeName = "" on error resume next Dim sSmartReturn sSmartReturn = MetaWord(Trim(StrParam)) if Trim(sSmartReturn)<>"" then g_TifMergeName=sSmartReturn if len(trim(g_TifMergeName))=0 then WriteLog("TifMerge Name has no value. Setting to Default name 'TifMerge'") g_TifMergeName = "TifMerge" end if Writelog("Setting TifMerge File Name to : " & g_TifMergeName) TifMerge_SetFileName = True Call ErrorHandler("Function TifMerge_SetFileName")

af.name: TifMerge_SetFilePath
af.g:
'Sets the path for the multi-Image file."
'String value for the output path of the multi-Image TIF file. Smart parameters are supported.
On Error Resume Next
Dim sDriveName
Dim sSmartReturn
WriteLog("SET FILE PATH")
TifMerge_SetPath = False
sSmartReturn = MetaWord(Trim(strParam))
if Trim(sSmartReturn)<>"" then strParam=sSmartReturn
sDriveName = FileMgr.GetDriveName(strParam)
If Not FileMgr.DriveExists(sDriveName) Then
writelog(Space(5) & "SET TifMerge_SetFilePath FAILED. NO SUCH DRIVE : " & strParam)
TifMerge_SetFilePath = False
Exit Function
End If
If FileMgr.FolderExists(strParam) Then
writelog(Space(5) & "Folder Exists. Setting Export path to: " & strParam)
g_TifMergePath = strParam
TifMerge_SetFilePath = True
Else
writelog(Space(5) & "NO SUCH PATH : " & strParam & " Building New Path.")
TifMerge_SetFilePath = TifMerge_MakePath(strParam)
g_TifMergePath = strParam
End If
writelog("Path set to " & g_TifMergePath)
WriteLog("END TifMerge_SetFilePath")
Call ErrorHandler("Function TifMerge_SetFilePath")

af.name: TifMerge_MergeImages
af.g:
'Merges the images associated with the object of the Document Hierarchy to which the action’s ruleset applies into a single, multi-Image file." 'String value indicating either:

' 1. "All" if the multi-Image file is to contain images of all pages without regard to Page Type.

' 2. The Page Type(s) of the images to be included (comma-separated list, if the parameter includes more than one Page Type.)

' Smart parameters are supported. On Error Resume Next Dim sSmartReturn sSmartReturn = MetaWord(Trim(sPageType)) if Trim(sSmartReturn)="" then sSmartReturn=sPageType If trim(ucase(sSmartReturn)) = "ALL" or trim(ucase(sSmartReturn)) = "" then sSmartReturn = "*" TifMerge_MergeImages = tm_TifMerge_MergeImages(CurrentObj, sSmartReturn) Call ErrorHandler("Function TifMerge_MergeImages")

af.name: TifMerge_MyImage
af.g:
'Adds each single image to the multi-Image file."None. ' Adds the current page image to the multi-Image TIF file. Actions that proceed the TifMerge_MyImage action ' allow you to specify under which conditions an image is to be added to the multi-Image file.

' A rule with this action can only be applied to a Page object. The output image file name ' and destination path must have been previously set using TifMerge_SetFileName and TifMerge_SetFilePath. Dim sMergeFile Dim StrParam Dim bRes TifMerge_MyImage = False sMergeFile = g_TifMergePath & "\" & g_TifMergeName & ".tif" If CurrentObj.ObjectType = DCO_PAGE Then StrParam = CurrentObj.ImageName ' Get the filename for the current page. If Not FileMgr.FileExists(StrParam) Then Writelog("File " & StrParam & " not Found. Skipping Image") Elseif StrParam = sMergeFile then Writelog("Image File is Merge to File. Image not Merged!") Else g_TifMergeFile.filename = StrParam bRes=g_TifMergeFile.save(sMergeFile) If bRes=False then writelog(StrParam & " ** Merge Failed: " & g_TifMergeFile.GetLastError) Else writelog(StrParam & " Merged.") TifMerge_MyImage = True End if End If Else Writelog("Calling Obj is not a Page object. No Image uploaded.") TifMerge_MyImage = False End If

f.name: TifMerge_PreserveCompression
f.g:
'Determines the output compression type for merged images." ' TRUE : Preserves the original compression type of the source image.
' FALSE : Uses G4 compression for black and white images. JEPG is used for color images. On Error Resume Next TifMerge_PreserveCompression = true If (UCase(PreserveCompression)="TRUE") Then g_PreserveCompression = true Else g_PreserveCompression = false End If

f.name: TifMerge_CheckStatus
f.g:
'Acceptable Statuses: CSV of status values to accept. Blank indicates no statuses will be checked.
'Disregard Statuses: CSV of status values to disregard. Blank indicates no statuses will be checked.
On Error Resume Next
TifMerge_CheckStatus = true
g_AcceptablePageStatuses=""
g_DisregardPageStatuses=""
g_AcceptableDocStatuses=""
g_DisregardDocStatuses=""

DisregardPageStatuses = replace(DisregardPageStatuses,Space(1),"")
AcceptableDocStatuses = replace(AcceptableDocStatuses,Space(1),"")
DisregardDocStatuses = replace(DisregardDocStatuses,Space(1),"")
g_AcceptablePageStatuses=AcceptablePageStatuses
g_DisregardPageStatuses=DisregardPageStatuses
g_AcceptableDocStatuses=AcceptableDocStatuses
g_DisregardDocStatuses=DisregardDocStatuses

af.name: TM524
af.g:
' Makes changes to the Page file for the current batch so that it is backward-compatible ' with older tasks that are not rules-based, tasks such as Recog2K, or ExportTX." 'This action alters the task's Page file for the current batch so that it is 'backward-compatible with non-rules-based tasks, such as Recog2K, or ExportTX.

' These tasks expect certain batch-, document-, and page-level variables that are not ' used in the rules-based environment. After the action is run, old-style tasks will ' proceed as if the batch was run entirely with that type of task.

If DCO.FindVariable("ED")= -1 then DCO.Variable("ED")= "0" End If If DCO.FindVariable("AD")= -1 then DCO.Variable("AD")= "0" End If If DCO.FindVariable("EP")= -1 then DCO.Variable("EP")= "0" End If If DCO.FindVariable("AP")= -1 then DCO.Variable("AP")= "0" End If g_TM524_nIndex = 0 TM524 = GetChildren(CurrentObj) Writelog("Total fields Indexed: " & g_TM524_nIndex)

af.name: TM4DocIdFormat
af.g:
'Formats all Document ID's with a Taskmaster 4 layout style." 'This action formats all Document ID's with a Taskmaster 4layout style.

' Note: Rules that employ this action must be part of a RuleSet that is bound ' to the Document Hierarchy's Batch object. TM4DocIdFormat = False If CurrentObj.ObjectType <> 0 then Writelog("Action Must be Bound at the Batch level. Exiting Function.") Exit Function End If Dim nSize Dim rChild Dim i Dim cIndex Dim sOrigID Dim sNewID On Error Resume Next nSize = CurrentObj.NumOfChildren() Debuglog("Found " & cstr(nSize) & " children to Process.") cIndex = 1 Writelog("Starting w/ " & CurrentObj.ID) For i=0 To nSize-1 Set rChild=CurrentObj.GetChild(i) if Not(rChild is Nothing) then Debuglog("Child is Type '" & rChild.ObjectType & "' ") If rChild.ObjectType = 1 Then sOrigID = rChild.ID sNewID = Pilot.BatchID & "." & Right("00" & cstr(cIndex),2) rChild.ID = sNewID Writelog("Renaming Document '" & sOrigID & "' to '" & sNewID & "' ") cIndex = cIndex + 1 End If End if Next 'i Call ErrorHandler("TM4DocIdFormat") TM4DocIdFormat = True

af.name: IsFieldPercentNumeric
af.g:
'A number (0-100) indicating the percentage that results in a condition. The
'default percentage is 100. The value must be numeric, without the percent sign.
On Error Resume Next
Dim Value, TrueCount, FalseCount, TFRatio, Lval, sCharacter, locale
locale = DetermineLocale() 'From rrunner.rrx
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
If IsNull(StrParam) Then StrParam = 100
If Not DCGlobalCurrency.IsNumeric(StrParam,locale) Then StrParam = 100
StrParam = cint(StrParam)
WriteLog("IsFieldPercentNumeric percentage parameter set to " & StrParam & " percent.")
IsFieldPercentNumeric = False
TrueCount = 0
FalseCount = 0
Value = Trim(GetFieldValue())
ValueLen = len(Value)
' \p{N} or \p{Number}: any kind of numeric character in any script.
' \p{Nd} or \p{Decimal_Digit_Number}: a digit zero through nine in any script except ideographic scripts.
' \p{Nl} or \p{Letter_Number}: a number that looks like a letter, such as a Roman numeral.
' \p{No} or \p{Other_Number}: a superscript or subscript digit, or a number that is not a digit 0..9 (excluding numbers from ideographic scripts).
For Cx = 1 To Len(value)
sCharacter=Mid(value,Cx,1)
If DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(sCharacter,"\p{N}") Then
TrueCount = TrueCount + 1
Elseif DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(sCharacter,"\p{Mn}") Then
ValueLen = ValueLen - 1
Else
FalseCount = FalseCount + 1
End If
Next 'Cx
TFRatio = (StrParam/100)*ValueLen
If TrueCount >= TFRatio and ValueLen>0 Then IsFieldPercentNumeric = True
If ValueLen <= 0 Then ValueLen = 1
WriteLog(Space(3) & "Value is " & (TrueCount/ValueLen)*100 & "% Numeric")
WriteLog("IsFieldPercentNumeric returns " & IsFieldPercentNumeric )
If IsFieldPercentNumeric = False Then
sReturn = RRState.LoadString("validations","IsFieldPercentNumeric_01","Field '{0}' value '{1}' contains less than the expected {2} percent of numeric characters.")
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{0}",CurrentObj.ID)
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{1}",CurrentObj.Text)
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{2}",StrParam)
DCOMessage(sReturn)
End If

af.name: IsFieldPercentAlpha
af.g:
' A number (0-100) indicating the percentage necessary to return a condition. The value must be numeric, without the percent sign.
On Error Resume Next
Dim Value, TrueCount, FalseCount, TFRatio, Cx, Lval, locale
locale = DetermineLocale() 'From rrunner.rrx
IsFieldPercentAlpha = False
' StrParam is a value between 0 and 100
' This action determines the percentage of numbers required to return True
' Defaults to 100%
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
If IsNull(StrParam) Then StrParam = 100
If Not DCGlobalCurrency.IsNumeric(StrParam, locale) Then StrParam = 100
StrParam = cint(StrParam)
Writelog("IsFieldPercentAlpha percentage parameter set to " & StrParam & " percent.")
TrueCount = 0
FalseCount = 0
Value = Trim(GetFieldValue())
ValueLen = len(Value)
' \p{L} or \p{Letter}: any kind of letter from any language.
' \p{Ll} or \p{Lowercase_Letter}: a lowercase letter that has an uppercase variant.
' \p{Lu} or \p{Uppercase_Letter}: an uppercase letter that has a lowercase variant.
' \p{Lt} or \p{Titlecase_Letter}: a letter that appears at the start of a word when only the first letter of the word is capitalized.
' \p{L&} or \p{Letter&}: a letter that exists in lowercase and uppercase variants (combination of Ll, Lu and Lt).
' \p{Lm} or \p{Modifier_Letter}: a special character that is used like a letter.
' \p{Lo} or \p{Other_Letter}: a letter or ideograph that does not have lowercase and uppercase variants.
' \p{Mn} : a non spacing mark - used with non composite character sets.
For Cx = 1 To Len(value)
sCharacter=Mid(value,Cx,1)
If DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(sCharacter,"\p{L}") Then
TrueCount = TrueCount + 1
Elseif DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(sCharacter,"\p{Mn}") Then
ValueLen = ValueLen - 1
Else
FalseCount = FalseCount + 1
End If
Next 'Cx
TFRatio = (StrParam/100)*ValueLen
If TrueCount >= TFRatio and ValueLen>0 Then IsFieldPercentAlpha = True
If ValueLen <= 0 Then ValueLen = 1
WriteLog(Space(3) & "Value is " & (TrueCount/ValueLen)*100 & "% Alphabetic")
WriteLog("IsFieldPercentAlpha returns " & IsFieldPercentAlpha)
If IsFieldPercentAlpha = False Then
sReturn = RRState.LoadString("validation","IsFieldPercentAlpha_01","Field '{0}' value '{1}' contains less than the expected {2} percent of Alphabetic characters.")
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{0}",CurrentObj.ID)
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{1}",CurrentObj.Text)
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{2}",StrParam)
DCOMessage(sReturn)
End If
'Call ErrorHandler("Function IsAlpha")

af.name: IsFieldDate
af.g:
' Checks that the captured value of the field represented by the bound Field
' object has an acceptable Date format.
' This action will accept any valid date from 01/01/0001 through 12/31/9999.
Dim value
Dim locale
On Error Resume Next
IsFieldDate = True
value = Trim(GetFieldValue())
locale = DetermineLocale() 'From rrunner.rrx
If Not DCGlobalDates.IsDate(value,locale) Then
IsFieldDate = False
sReturn = RRState.LoadString("validations","InvalidDate_01","Field '{0}' date value of '{1}' is not a valid date or recognized date format.")
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{0}",CurrentObj.ID)
sReturn = replace(sReturn,"{1}",CurrentObj.Text)
DCOMessage(sReturn)
End if
Writelog(DCGlobalDates.GetLog)
WriteLog("IsFieldDate returns " & IsFieldDate)

af.name: IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter
af.g:
' The name of the Field object of the Document Hierarchy to be compared with the
' current field's Date value.
' Checks that the Date value in the current field represented by the bound Field
' object of the Document Hierarchy is greater than or equal to the Date value in the
' field specified as the parameter.
Dim oDcoObj
Dim sDateFrom
Dim sDateThru
Dim locale
On error Resume Next
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter=True
'Added support for smart parameters
StrParam=MetaWord(StrParam)
writelog("Param: '" & StrParam & "'")
Set oDcoObj = ReturnNamedComponent(trim(StrParam))
If oDcoObj is nothing then
Writelog("Compare to Field '" & StrParam & "' not found.")
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter=False
Exit Function
End if
sDateFrom = Trim(GetFieldValue())
sDateFrom = DCGlobalDates.ReplaceIndicWithWesternDigits(sDateFrom)
locale = DetermineLocale() 'From rrunner.rrx
If Not DCGlobalDates.IsDate(sDateFrom,locale) Then
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter = False
sMessage = RRState.Loadstring("validations","InvalidDate_01","Field '{0}' date value of '{1}' is not a valid date or recognised date format.")
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{0}",CurrentObj.ID)
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{1}",sDateFrom)
DCOMessage(sMessage)
Writelog(sMessage)
End if
sDateThru = Trim(oDcoObj.Text)
sDateThru = DCGlobalDates.ReplaceIndicWithWesternDigits(sDateThru)
If Not DCGlobalDates.IsDate(sDateThru,locale) Then
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter = False
sMessage = RRState.Loadstring("validations","InvalidDate_01","Field '{0}' date value of '{1}' is not a valid date or recognised date format.")
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{0}",oDcoObj.ID)
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{1}",sDateThru)
DCOMessage(sMessage)
Writelog(sMessage)
End if
If IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter=False Then
Set oDcoObj = Nothing
Exit Function
End if
Select Case DCGlobalDates.CompareDate(sDateFrom,sDateThru,locale)
Case "-1"
IsFieldDateEqualOrAfter = False
sMessage = RRState.Loadstring("validations","IsDateEqualorAfter_01","Field '{0}' date of '{1}' must be after or the same date as Field '{2}' date of '{3}'.")
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{0}",CurrentObj.ID)
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{1}",sDateFrom)
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{2}",oDcoObj.ID)
sMessage = replace(sMessage,"{3}",sDateThru)
DCOMessage(sMessage)
Writelog(sMessage)
Case "1","0"
sMessage = "From date is greater than or equal to through date"
Writelog(sMessage)
Case else
Writelog("unknown result")
End Select

af.g:
' The name of the Field object of the Document Hierarchy to be compared with
' the current field's Date value.
' Checks that the date in the current field represented by the bound Field object of the
' Document Hierarchy is less than or equal to the Date value in the field specified as the parameter.
Dim oDcoObj
