af.name: IsPatternInField
af.g:
Dim sValue
Dim Match
Dim Matches
Dim bFound
Dim bIgnoreCase
' String value of the Regular Expression. The expression can include any Regular Expression characters.
' Uses VBScript Regular Expression Pattern entered as parameter to search for a matching pattern in
' current object's Text value.
On Error Resume Next
IsPatternInField = False
bFound = False
bIgnoreCase = True
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
sValue= Replace(GetFieldValue,"~"," ")
Writelog("Looking for value '" & strParam & "' in string: '" & sValue & "'")
' Use dcglobal dotNet regex engine:
If DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(sValue, StrParam, bIgnoreCase) Then
sDCGlobalLog = DCGlobalStrings.GetLog()
WriteLog(sDCGlobalLog)
bFound = True
End if
If bFound = True Then
IsPatternInField = True
Else
sMessage = RRState.LoadString("validations","IsPatternInField_01","Field '{0}' value of '{1}' does not contain the pattern '{2}'.")
sMessage = Replace(sMessage,"{0}",CurrentObj.ID)
sMessage = Replace(sMessage,"{1}",sValue)
sMessage = Replace(sMessage,"{2}",StrParam)
DCOMessage(sMessage)
Debuglog(sMessage)
End If
WriteLog("IsPatternInField returns " & IsPatternInField)

af.name: ConvertFieldToCurrency
af.g:
'Formats a field's text value as a currency value. The following steps are performed on the field:
'
' 1. Removes existing currency symbols.Off
' 2. Replaces negative value characters such as parenthesis, 'NEG', 'CR' and trailing hyphen
' with a leading hyphen.
' 3. If a decimal exists, its position is not changed.
' 4. If a decimal does not exist and the field contains 2 or more characters, a decimal is inserted
' before the last two characters in the field.
' 5. If a decimal does not exist and the field contains less than 2 characters, no decimal is inserted.
Dim sValue
Dim cObj
Dim nLen
Dim nChar
Dim RegEx
Dim Matches
Dim Match
Dim m
Dim Index
On Error Resume Next
Dim sLocalNum
Dim sDecimal
Dim sGroup
Dim locale
locale = DetermineLocale() 'From rrunner.rrx
sDecimal = DCGlobalCurrency.CurrencyDecimalSeparator(locale)
sGroup = DCGlobalCurrency.CurrencyGroupSeparator(locale)
sSymbol = DCGlobalCurrency.CurrencySymbol(locale)
sDecimalDigits = DCGlobalCurrency.CurrencyDecimalDigits(locale)
ConvertFieldToCurrency = False
Writelog("Start value: '" & currentobj.text & "'")
'Remove all currency symbols
sResult = DCGlobalStrings.RemoveReplace("[\s\p{Sc}_]*",cint(0),"",cint(0), CurrentObj)
'Check for Negative Currency values
If DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(CurrentObj.Text,"\(\d\d+\)|\d\d+CR|\d\d+NEG|\d\d+-") then
'If we found Negative currency indicator(s), remove the symbols and then replace with a leading hyphen character
sResult = DCGlobalStrings.RemoveReplace("[\(\)-]|CR|NEG",cint(0),"",cint(0), CurrentObj)
'Check to see if the value is already Negative
If instr(CurrentObj.text,"-")<>1 then
Set cObj = CurrentObj.AddChild(4,"",CurrentObj.NumOfchildren-Len(Currentobj.Text))
nChar = cObj.AddValue(CLng(45), CLng(10))
bRes = cObj.SetPosition(clng(0),clng(0),clng(0),clng(0))
End if
End if
'Numeric Check - look at a copy of the field value
If DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(CurrentObj.Text,"[^\p{N}\.,-']") then
ConvertFieldToCurrency = False
Writelog("Value must be numeric to format as currency. Exiting Action.")
Exit Function
End if
Writelog("Current locale decimal separator character is { " & sDecimal & " }")
'Add Decimal Character - preserve confidence of existing values
'Assumes two position decimal if no decimal symbols are found
If Not DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(CurrentObj.Text,"[\.,\u066b]") and (len(CurrentObj.Text)>2) then
Set cObj = CurrentObj.AddChild(4,"",len(CurrentObj.Text)-2)
nChar = cObj.AddValue(CLng(ASCW(sDecimal)), CLng(10))
bRes = cObj.SetPosition(clng(0),clng(0),clng(0),clng(0))
End if
If Not DCGlobalStrings.RegExIsMatch(CurrentObj.Text,"[^\p{N}\.,-'\u066b]") then
If len(CurrentObj.Text)>=2 then
ConvertFieldToCurrency = True
end if
Else
Writelog("Non currency character in value")
End if
writelog("Formatted value: '" & currentobj.text & "'")
Set cObj = Nothing

af.name: IsFieldHidden
af.g:
' Note: This action returns True if the calling field is 'Hidden'...if the corresponding object of the Document Hierarchy has a variable STATUS equal to -1.
Dim oSetupNode
Dim oNodeValue
On Error Resume Next
IsFieldHidden=False
If CurrentObj.ObjectType<>3 then

Else

af.name: IsSupportedImageFile
af.g:
' A Boolean that determines the type of test to perform.
'
' True: Tests the validity of the image by checking the file extension and attempting to load the image.
' False: Only a file extension check is performed to determine if it is a supported file.
Dim oDCImage
On Error Resume Next
IsSupportedImageFile = FALSE
If CurrentObj.ObjectType<>2 then
Writelog("Action must be called on a DCO page. Exiting Action.")
Exit Function
End if
'Added support for smart parameters
StrParamInput=MetaWord(StrParamInput)
writelog("Param: '" & StrParamInput & "'")
strParam = UCase(Trim(strParamInput))
If (trim(strParam) = "") then
Writelog("Parameter missing. A parameter of True or False is required.")
Exit Function
End if
If ((strParam <> "TRUE") and (strParam <> "FALSE")) then
Writelog("A parameter of True or False is required. Parameter is: " & strParam)
Exit Function
End if
If CurrentObj.ImageName <> "" Then
If CBool(strParam) = TRUE Then
Set oDCImage = createObject("DCIMAGE.DcimageCtrl.1")
oDCImage.FileName = CurrentObj.ImageName
If Err.Number <> 0 Then
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is not supported."
Err.Clear
Else
If oDCImage.Filename = "" Then
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is not supported."
Else
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is supported."
IsSupportedImageFile = TRUE
End If
End If
Set oDCImage = Nothing
Else
sFileName = UCase(CurrentObj.ImageName)
If InStr(sFileName,".TIF") > 0 Then
IsSupportedImageFile = TRUE
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is supported."
ElseIf InStr(sFileName,".TIFF") > 0 Then
IsSupportedImageFile = TRUE
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is supported."
ElseIf InStr(sFileName,".JPG") > 0 Then
IsSupportedImageFile = TRUE
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is supported."
ElseIf InStr(sFileName,".JPEG") > 0 Then
IsSupportedImageFile = TRUE
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is supported."
Else
Writelog "Image file '" & CurrentObj.ImageName & "' is not supported."
End If
End If
Else
Writelog "The current page does not have an image associated with it."
End If

af.name: ReplaceValueAtPosition
af.g:
' Two-part comma-separated value:
' 1. The position that contains the value to be replaced.
' 2. The replacement string; this parameter defaults to "" indicating a deletion.
' This action replaces the value at a specific position with a string replacement value, or a deletion.
Dim locale
On Error Resume Next
ReplaceValueAtPosition = False
locale = DetermineLocale() 'From rrunner.rrx

nStartIndex = MetaWord(aStrParam(0))
ReplaceWithString = MetaWord(aStrParam(1))

Writelog("Start value:'" & CurrentObj.Text & "' Replace character index:'" & sFind & "'")

FindString=Mid(CurrentObj.Text,nStartIndex,1)
ReplaceValueAtPosition = u_ModifyText(FindString,nStartIndex,1,ReplaceWithString)
Else
Writelog("Replace position is outside of field length.")
End if
WriteLog("End value:'" & CurrentObj.Text & "'")

f.name: FormatNumberToLocale
f.g:
On Error Resume Next
FormatNumberToLocale = False
Dim StartValue
Dim EndValue
Dim locale
Dim sLogVal
locale = DetermineLocale() ' in rrunner
Writelog("Start Field value:" & CurrentObj.text)
EndValue = DCGlobalCurrency.NormalizeNumber(CurrentObj,locale)
sLogVal=DCGlobalCurrency.GetLog
Writelog(sLogVal)
Writelog("End value:" & CurrentObj.text)
If Err.number=0 then
FormatNumberToLocale = True
Else
Err.Clear
End if

This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the IsFieldCurrency action in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
Determines if the Field's captured value meets the current locale's currency format, including the number of decimal places, decimal and digit separator characters and any present currency indicators. The locale formats are the standard currency symbol, digit grouping symbol and decimal symbols as defined in windows for a specific locale.
A currency symbol is not required for the validation to pass. If a currency symbol is present, then the currency symbol provided must be correct for the current locale or the validation will fail. Similarly, digit grouping symbols are not required, but if they are present, they must also be the correct symbol for the current locale.
If the currency has a decimal value, then the decimal symbol must be the correct symbol. For example, if validating U.S. currency, and the currency has a decimal value such as 123.56, then the decimal separator must be the correct separator for the country. Some countries do not allow decimal values in their currency, and if a decimal value is present, it will fail validation.
If the field appears to have a valid currency but it is not passing the validation, confirm that the locale used by the field is correct for the currency type. For example, if the field has a Japanese currency, then the locale must be set to Japan. This can either be in effect for the whole application, such as the machine's locale, or it can be in effect based on the setting of the hr_locale DCO variable.
When validating Japanese currency, in addition to using the defined locale's currency format, it is also allowed to specify negative values using the △ symbol instead of a minus symbol. Additionally, in place of a Yen symbol ¥ at the start of a currency, the word 円 is allowed at the end of the currency value.
Example 1:
IsFieldCurrency()
$1,200 returns False
$1,200.00 returns True
Example 2:
rrSet("ja-JP","@X.hr_locale")
IsFieldCurrency()
This example first sets the locale for the field to Japan prior to validating the currency. If hr_locale was already set at a higher DCO node level, such as page, document or batch, then it is not necessary to set it again at the field level.
Field level.

This Action has been marked for Deprecation and will removed in a future release. It has been replaced with Action CalculateFields.
Equation: The equation that is the basis for the calculation.
You can use a Field object's name or numeric values with any arithmetic operator (+,-,*,/,^). To use a Field object's name, surround the field name with single quotation marks ('). An empty value is treated as a "0".
DecimalDigits: The number of decimal places to limit the logical comparison. If left blank, or invalid, the number will default to the value for the current locale.
PreserveStatus: Can be "True" or "False" to indicate if he status of all associated fields if the calculation fails should be updated based on success or failure of the operation. If not provided, or invalid, the value will default to False.
Smart parameters are supported.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the CalculateFields action in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
Calculates the equation entered as a parameter and compares the result to the current Field object's captured value.
Note: If the result does not match the equation's result, dependant fields (fields involved in the equation) will receive a Failed status and will appear pink in the applicable field of the Data Entry panel.
If the results of a previously failed CalculateFields call are corrected by a user, such that the calculation no longer returns false, dependant fields that were set to status Failed by the CalculateFields action will be updated to status Pass.
It is likely that dependant fields could have their statuses updated via other rules and actions, so it is important when configuring your application to properly stage, and sequence your validations action logic to work in tandem with the CalculateFields action.
CalculateFields("@STRING('SubTotal' + 'Shipping' + 'Tax' = 'Total')", "2", "False")
This example sums the "SubTotal", "Shipping" and "Tax" fields and checks to see if the total of the three fields equals the value in the "Total" field. If they are not the same, then the status will be changed to "1" for each of the fields.
CalculateFields("('SubTotal' +@CHR(43)+ 'Shipping' +@CHR(43)+ 'Tax') - '0.05' = 'Total'", "2", "False")
This example is similar to the above example, but also includes a hard coded value within the equation. The smart parameter @CHR(43) evaluates to a plus sign. Because the parameter is supports smart parameters, the + will be interpreted as a smart parameter and change the input string. This technique will resolve to a + in the final equation like this:
('SubTotal' + 'Shipping' + 'Tax') - '0.05' = 'Total'
To check for a 'tolerance' use two actions in sequence like this:
CalculateFields("@STRING(('Wages' + 'Interest' + 'Unemployment')>=('Gross'- '.05'))", "2", "False")
CalculateFields("@STRING(('Wages' + 'Interest' + 'Unemployment')<=('Gross'+ '.05'))", "2", "False")
The example will calculate fields twice and allow the range of values. If both tests pass, then they will both return True. If either test fails, the action will return false and set the status of the field to "1" indicating there is a problem with the field.
CalculateFields("'SubTotal' +@CHR(43)+ 'Shipping' +@CHR(43)+ 'Tax')", "0", "False")
This example will sum the values of the "SubTotal", "Shipping" and "Tax" fields and store the result in the text value of the current field, or if called on a page object, the value will be stored in a variable called "CalculateFields".
Page and Field level.

False if the expression evaluates to False or the expression is not valid (eg. a field's value is not numeric).

This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the CheckSubFields action in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
Validates an instance of a parent Field object by confirming the presence (or absence) of captured values for one or more of its child fields. (In the Invoices application, as an example, child fields of the LINEITEM parent include: ItemID, ItemDesc, Quantity, Price and LineTotal.)
Invalid parent Field objects are deleted if they do not meet this criteria.
This action usually runs in its own RuleSet (for example, in a Filter RuleSet) and would be applied to the DETAILS Field object (parent object to the LINEITEM field) in the Invoices example. Example 1: The captured values for a LINEITEM field are:
ItemID = 12345
ItemDesc =
Price = 12.00
LineTotal =
The action's parameter contains this expression:
CheckSubFields("('ItemID' OR 'ItemDesc') AND ('Price' OR 'LineTotal')")
In this example the action returns True and the current LINEITEM object is Valid.
Example 2: The captured values for the LINEITEM field are:
ItemID = 12345
ItemDesc = Thank you for your order
Price =
LineTotal =
The action's parameter contains this expression:
CheckSubFields("('ItemID' OR 'ItemDesc') AND ('Price' OR 'LineTotal')")
In this example the action's equation returns is False and the current LINEITEM object is Invalid. The field and the values of its child fields are deleted from the Data file.
Example 3: The captured values for the LINEITEM field are:
ItemID = 12345
LineTotal = gonetolunch
The action's parameter contains this expression:
CheckSubFields("('ItemID') AND ('LineTotal')")
In this case, the action returns True and validates the LINEITEM field - despite the presence of a nonsense entry in the LineTotal child field!

This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the DeleteDCOParent action in the ApplicationObjects action library.
Deletes the parent of the Document Hierarchy object to which a rule with this action is bound. DeleteParentObj()
Document, Page, and Field.
False if a parent or grandparent object cannot be found, or if the deletion of the parent object fails. Otherwise, True.
String value of the Regular Expression. The expression can include any Regular Expression characters. Smart parameters are supported.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the expanded IsRegularExpressionPatternInValue action in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
Uses VBScript Regular Expression Pattern entered as parameter to search for a matching pattern in current object's Text value.
Note: If you are using an input boundary, ^, it must be followed by a space and then the remainder of the search string.
IsPatternInField("[\^\b\s\n\r]*Inv[oO0][iItl1]ce[\b\s]*")
IsPatternInField("@STRING([\^\b\s\n\r]*Inv[oO0][iItl1]ce[\b\s]*)")
This example searches for the word “Invoice” in the current field. To allow for recognition errors, the search allows for common recognition substitutions in “o” and “i” by matching “Invoice”, “InvOice”, “Inv0ice”, “Inv01ce”, “Involce”, etc. The search will also ignore any text placed before or after the word. Encapsulating the parameter with @STRING is recommended when the value is not a Smart Parameter.
All, but generally at the Field level.
True if the pattern is found within the field. Otherwise, False.
None.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the ConvertFieldToCurrency action in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
Formats a field's text value as a currency value. The following steps are performed on the field:
1. Removes existing currency symbols.
2. Replaces negative value characters such as parenthesis, 'NEG', 'CR' and trailing hyphen with a leading hyphen.
3. If a decimal exists, its position is not changed.
4. If a decimal does not exist and the field contains 2 or more characters, a decimal is inserted before the last two characters in the field.
5. If a decimal does not exist and the field contains less than 2 characters, no decimal is inserted.
ConvertFieldToCurrency()
A value of 1 remains 1
A value of 12 becomes .12
A value of 105 becomes 1.05
A value of 104.009 remains 104.009
All levels, but generally applied at the Field level.
True if the text value is numeric and greater than one character. Otherwise, False.
None.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead use the rrCompare action in Rrunner to test the object's STATUS variable.
Note: This action returns True if the calling field is 'Hidden'...if the corresponding Fieldobject of the Document Hierarchy has a variable STATUS equal to -1.
IsFieldHidden()

True if the Fieldobject's STATUS = -1; Otherwise False.
A Boolean that determines the type of test to perform.
True: Tests the validity of the image by checking the file extension and attempting to load the image.
False: Only a file extension check is performed to determine if it is a supported file.
Smart parameters are supported.
This action tests a file to determine if the file format is supported. The extension is checked to determine if it denotes a supported image type. If True is passed as a parameter, it also attempts to load the file into the Image view control.
Using False as a parameter will greatly improve the speed of this action. A parameter of True will slow down the processing, especially if the images are very large, but it will add an extra confirmation that the file is not corrupted and confirm that any subformat of the file type, such as compression type, is also supported.
IsSupportedImageFile()

True, if parameter is valid, the action is called at the page level and the page's IMAGEFILE variable (set at scan time by the scan tasks) points to a file whose format is supported (can be displayed) by the Image view control. Otherwise False.
Two-part comma-separated value:
1. The position that contains the value to be replaced.
2. The replacement string; this parameter defaults to "" indicating a deletion.
Smart parameters are supported.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the ReplaceValueAtPosition action in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
This action replaces the value at a specific position with a string replacement value, or a deletion.
ReplaceValueAtPosition("3,/")
Field level.
True if the character replacement is successful. Otherwise, False.
*** This Action Is Deprecated ***
This action has been deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in a future release. It is recommended that you no longer use this action. Instead, use the FormatNumerToLocale action in the ValidationsAndTextAdjustments action library.
This action evaluates the current field value for known number patterns and if a known pattern is detected, updates the decimal and digit separators characters (if present) to match that of the current locale, for use when processing fields with number types formatted incorrectly for the current locale. ie USA vs European.
Known patterns are industry standard digits with or without 3 digit group separators, and 1-2 digits following a decimal separator.
Distinct Analyzed groups:
1) Numerals with decimal point Group Separators using comma, apostrope or space characters. Decimal Separator using decimal character.
2) Numerals with decimal comma Group Separator using decimal, apostrope or space characters. Decimal Separator using comma character.
3) Numerals with Arabic/Persian characters Group Separator using Arabic/Persian character. Decimal Separator using Arabic/Persian character.
Note: Numerals with lakhs layout and decimal mark (pattern of n,nn,nn,nnn.dd) are not supported.
a) Given a US number 1,234.56 to be formatted to UK.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 1.234,56
b) Given a US number 1234.5 to be formatted to UK.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 1234,5
c) Given a US number 1,234.567 to be formatted to UK.
FormatNumberToLocale()
Format will remain 1,234.567 since 3 digits following the decimal are not supported.
d) Given a US number 12345678.90 to be formatted to UK.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 12345678.90
e) Given a UK number 1.234.567,89 to be formatted to US.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 1,234,567.89
f) Given a UK number 0,5 to be formatted to US.
FormatNumberToLocale()
New format will be 0.5
Field level.
True if no errors are encountered. Otherwise, False.

af.name: SetImageType
af.g:
' String value of the file's identifying extension. If you are listing multiple types, separate
' each one with a comma.
'
' It is not necessary to include a period before each extension. The parameters are not case-sensitive.
StrParam = MetaWord(StrParam)
StrParam=Replace(StrParam,".","")
StrParam=Replace(StrParam,Chr(32),"")
SetImageType = False
sExtn = Trim(StrParam) ' LCase(Trim(StrParam))
'Remove period from extension
sExtn = Replace(sExtn,".","")
If LCase(sExtn)<>"tiff" and LCase(sExtn)<>"tif" and LCase(sExtn)<>"jpg" and LCase(sExtn)<>"jpeg"then
'If the input is not a single file type of tiff, tif or jpg, then disable fast mode.
oOut.SetDoNotOpenInputFiles(True)
Writelog("special or multiple extensions were provided : setting Fast Mode to TRUE.")
ElseIf gReinitVScanUponRescan Then
oOut.SetDoNotOpenInputFiles(False)
End if
oIn.SetImageExtension(StrParam)
oOut.SetImageExtension(StrParam)
SetImageType = True
Call ErrorHandler("SetImageType")

af.name: SetMultiPageTiff
af.g:
'Permits the use of multipage source image files.
oOut.SetMultiPageTiff(True)
SetMultiPageTiff = true
Call ErrorHandler("SetMultiPageTiff")

af.name: SetFastMode
af.g:
' Increases speed by preventing the Scan action from opening the files it is scanning.

' ' This action is provided as backwards compatibility to older applications where this action was ' required to properly enable fast mode for PDF files. SetImageType will automatically enable ' fast mode, if it is called with a PDF extension. oOut.SetDoNotOpenInputFiles(True) SetFastMode = true Call ErrorHandler("SetFastMode")

af.name: SearchInSubdirectory
af.g:
' Looks for source files in sub-directories of the directory you designated with a
' SetSourceDirectory action.
oIn.SearchInSubDirectory(True)
SearchInSubdirectory = true
Call ErrorHandler("SearchInSubdirectory")

af.name: SetSourceDirectory
af.g:
'
' String value of the directory's name and path. Instead, you can use a Smart Parameter such
' as @Path to establish the Source Directory's name and path.
Dim StrParam
Dim oFolder
On Error Resume Next
SetSourceDirectory = False
StrParam = MetaWord(SmartParam)
If len(Trim(StrParam))=0 Then StrParam=SmartParam
Writelog("looking for:" & StrParam)
If trim(StrParam)="" Then
Writelog("Error: Folder '" & StrParam & "' does not exist.")
SetSourceDirectory = False
End if
If FileMgr.FolderExists(StrParam)=False Then
WriteLog("Error: Folder '" & StrParam & "' does not exist")
nTaskStatus = RetAbort
Exit Function
End if
'Check existing directory and insert DRIVER LETTER: required for Mail Object
Set oFolder = FileMgr.GetFolder(StrParam)
StrParam = oFolder.Path
Set oFolder = Nothing
oIn.SetSourceDir(StrParam)
Err.Clear
oOutLook.SetSourceDir(StrParam)
If err.number <> 0 Then
WriteLog("Fatal error: Outlook is not running")
SetSourceDirectory = FALSE
Else
SourceDir = StrParam
SetSourceDirectory = TRUE
End If

af.name: SetMaxImageFiles
af.g:
' An optional string value specifying the maximum number of files. Smart parameter accepted.
'
' If you do not enter a value, the task will scan all images in the target folder - and
' this action will return True.
Dim StrParam
Dim strTrimParam ' Input with leading / trailing space removed
Dim lParmValue ' Value as a long
On Error Resume Next
StrParam=MetaWord(SmartParam)
If len(Trim(StrParam))=0 Then StrParam=SmartParam
strTrimParam = Trim(StrParam)
'Always return success. If the parameter value is not a valid integer, then we will just
'log the problem and use the default value. Let's set that up as the default condition.
SetMaxImageFiles = True
oOut.SetMaxImageFiles(MaxImageFiles)
if len(strTrimParam) = 0 Then
' In this one case where no parameter is present, we will use the largest size.
WriteLog("SetMaxImageFiles: No parameter, using largest value: 32767")
oOut.SetMaxImageFiles(32767)
Exit function
end if
' CInt will cause an error if the value is a number that is bigger than an int.
' We will validate it is a positive integer.
if (Not IsNumeric(strTrimParam)) Then
WriteLog("SetMaxImageFiles: Parameter: " & strTrimParam & " is not a number, using default value: " & MaxImageFiles)
exit function
end if
' We have some kind of number. It can be an int or a long.
if (Len(strTrimParam) > 5) then
WriteLog("SetMaxImageFiles: Parameter: " & strTrimParam & " is too big, using default value: " & MaxImageFiles)
exit function
end if
' Might or might not be an int, but it must be a long by now.
lParmValue = CLng(strTrimParam) ' Set value to a long to prevent overflow
if ((lParmValue > 32767) or (lParmValue < 1)) Then
' bigger than signed int or 0 or negative
WriteLog("SetMaxImageFiles: Parameter: " & strTrimParam & " is too big or 0, using default value: " & MaxImageFiles)
exit function
end if
' We have a valid, positive integer.
oOut.SetMaxImageFiles( CInt(strTrimParam) ) ' Note, CInt rounds and uses system numeric settings
Call ErrorHandler("SetMaxImageFiles")

af.name: DeleteImageFile
af.g:
'A housekeeping action that deletes the current source image file. A Scan action
'must follow this action.
On Error Resume Next
Call oIn.ResetFileOption(FILE_DELETE,"")
DeleteImageFile = True
Call ErrorHandler("DeleteImageFile")

af.name: CopyFile
af.g:
' 1. The String value of the name of the target file system folder.
' 2. Optional. The file extension you wish to use for each file. If you provide an extension, it must ' not be preceded by a period. The action defaults to "tif" if this parameter is blank.
' Smart parameters are supported. Dim aParam Dim StrParam On Error Resume Next StrParam = MetaWord(trim(StrParamSP)) writelog("Input after processing smart parameters: '" & StrParam & "'") aParam = Split(StrParam,",") If uBound(aParam) = 1 Then call oIn.ResetFileOption(FILE_COPY, StrParam) CopyFile = true Else call oIn.ResetFileOption(FILE_COPY, StrParam & ",tif") CopyFile = true End if Call ErrorHandler("CopyFile")

af.name: Scan
af.g:
' Scans a set of waiting Image files, according to the parameters set by earlier actions.

' This is usually the last action in a vScan rule. On Error Resume Next Scan = False If gReinitVScanUponRescan Then Writelog "gReinitVScanUponRescan = True" If cInt(CurrentObj.ObjectType) <> 0 Then writelog("The Scan action is required to run at the Batch level. Returning False.") Exit Function End If If (Not FileMgr.FolderExists(SourceDir)) Then If len(trim(SourceDir))=0 then writelog("Source Directory is not setup correctly, an empty path exists for this value. Exiting.") Else writelog("Source Directory '" & SourceDir & "' not Found. Exiting.") End if Scan = False Exit function End if If IsAlive(oOutLook) then oOutLook.SaveAttachmentsAndDeleteMail() nImages = Ubound(oIn.GetArray()) If nImages = 32767 Then writelog("Maximum reached. Found " & nImages & " or more image files in Source folder:'" & SourceDir & "'.") Else writelog("Found " & nImages & " image files in Source folder:'" & SourceDir & "' for the batch.") End if nMaxImageFiles = oOut.GetMaxImageFiles() 'Get image files If cInt(nImages)<>cInt(0) Then If bDocumentStructurePresents=TRUE then 'Set the Expected Pages variable DCO.Variable("EP") = cStr(nMaxImageFiles) End if 'Process Image Files For i = 1 to min(nImages,oOut.GetMaxImageFiles) 'nImages sUnderProcessFile = oIn.GetFile(i) Select Case cStr(oOut.Perform(sUnderProcessFile)) Case cStr(PerformPageOk) 'we will release files at the end 'oIn.ReleaseFile(sUnderProcessFile) Case cStr(PerformPageAbort) 'oIn.ReleaseFile(sUnderProcessFile) writelog("Files not released - File Processing Aborting.") nTaskStatus = RetAbort Scan = false Exit function Case cStr(PerformPageFinish) 'we did not process oIn.ReleaseFile(sUnderProcessFile) nTaskStatus = RetFinished Exit for Case Else 'oIn.ReleaseFile(sUnderProcessFile) writelog("Files not released - Unexpected result from File Processing.") Scan = False Exit function End Select Next 'i If nTaskStatus = RetFinished Then writelog("Releasing files...") For i = 1 to min(nImages,oOut.GetMaxImageFiles) 'nImages sUnderProcessFile = oIn.GetFile(i) oIn.ReleaseFile(sUnderProcessFile) Next Writelog("Files Released.") End if Pilot.ExpectedPages = cStr(nImages) nTaskStatus = RetFinished Else nTaskStatus = RetPending End if Scan = True Call ErrorHandler("Scan")

af.name: AddDocument
af.g:
' Places all scanned pages into a single, batch-wide document. ' This action must be called before the Scan action.

' ' The action also adds ED (Expected Documents), AD (Actual Documents), EP (Expected Pages) ' and AP (Actual Pages) properties to a task's Page file (.xml).

' ' This action allows a VScan task to create a batch that has all the same ' characteristics of a batch that is created using a standard scan task such as kScan or iScan. ' It is not required to call this action. Use this action if your application relies on a ' document structure on import. On Error Resume Next AddDocument = False If cInt(CurrentObj.ObjectType) <> 0 Then writelog("The AddDocument action is required to run at the Batch level. Returning False.") Exit Function End If Set oSetupObject = DCO.SetupObject writelog("Checking Setup DCO for a document structure...") nDocs = oSetupObject.NumOfNodes(1) If (nDocs >= 1 ) Then ' we suppose there is just one document Writelog("Found '" & cstr(nDocs) & "' document structures in current setup DCO.") If DCO.NumOfChildren = 0 Then Set oDoc = DCO.AddChild(1,Pilot.BatchID & ".01" ,-1) oDoc.Type = "" 'oDoc.Type=oSetupObject.GetNode(1,0).Name DCO.Variable("ED") = cStr(nDocs) DCO.Variable("AD") = "0" DCO.Variable("EP") = "0" DCO.Variable("AP") = "0" Else Set oDoc = DCO.GetChild(0) End if bDocumentStructurePresents = True AddDocument = True Else Writelog("No document structures found in current setup DCO. No Document structure will be created.") bDocumentStructurePresents = false AddDocument = false End If Set oSetupObject = Nothing

af.name: SetSortOrder
af.g:
' Two comma-separated String values:
'
' 1. Designation of the images' sorting field: ImageName=1, Type=2, DateCreated=3,
' DateLastAccessed=4, DateLastModified=5, or Size=6.
' 2. Optional: ASC or 1 (Ascending), DESC or 2 (Descending). If you do not include this
' parameter, the action defaults to ASC (1).
Dim bValid
Dim arParam
On Error Resume Next
SetSortOrder = false
strParam=trim(strParam)
If len(strParam)=0 then
writelog("Expecting 1 or 2 parameter values. None found.")
Exit function
End if
arParam = split(strParam,",")
if Ubound(arParam) > 1 Then
writelog("Wrong number of parameters, should be 1 or 2")
exit function
end if
arParam(0)=Trim(cStr(arParam(0)))
Select Case Ucase(arParam(0))
Case "NAME","1"
gSortType = "Name"
Case "TYPE","2"
gSortType = "Type"
Case "DATECREATED","3"
gSortType = "DateCreated"
Case "DATELASTACCESSED","4"
gSortType = "DateLastAccessed"
Case "DATELASTMODIFIED","5"
gSortType = "DateLastModified"
Case "SIZE","6"
gSortType = "Size"
Case Else
writelog ("first argument has to be one of the names: Name,Type,DateCreated,DateLastAccessed,DateLastModified,Size")
Exit function
End Select
' Default to assending sort order.
gSortOrder = "ASC"
If uBound(arParam)=1 Then
arParam(1)=Trim(cStr(arParam(1)))
Select Case uCase(arParam(1))
Case "DESC","2"
gSortOrder = "DESC"
writelog("sort order is DESC")
Case Else
writelog("sort order is ASC")
end Select
end if
SetSortOrder = true

af.name: MoveImageFileToDirectory
af.g:
'The full path to the target location of the Image file. Smart parameters are supported.
'
' A housekeeping action that moves the current Image file to a location you specify. The source
' image file will be removed from the input directory and moved to the specified directory.
' This action is typically used when it is desired to place images into a specific
' location for archiving. A copy of the image will still be placed into the batch directory.
'
' If the target directory already contains a file of the same name, it will give a unique name to the new file.
'
' This action must precede the Scan action. If MoveImageFileToDirectory is used and the Scan action
' is never subsequently called, the file move will not be performed.
Dim StrParam
On Error Resume Next
StrParam=Metaword(SmartParam)
If len(Trim(StrParam))=0 Then StrParam=SmartParam
If trim(StrParam)<>"" Then
If ( Not FileMgr.FolderExists(StrParam) ) Then
WriteLog("Fatal error: Folder " & StrParam & " does not exist")
nTaskStatus = RetAbort
MoveImageFileToDirectory = False
Else
' check existing directory
' AND insert DRIVER LETTER : it is needed for Mail Object
Dim folder
Set folder = FileMgr.GetFolder(StrParam)
StrParam = folder.Path
Set Folder = Nothing
call oIn.ResetFileOption(FILE_MOVE, StrParam)
MoveImageFileToDirectory = True
End if
Else
WriteLog("MoveImageFileToDirectory: Parameter is not correct.")
nTaskStatus = RetAbort
MoveImageFileToDirectory = False
End if
Call ErrorHandler("MoveImageFileToDirectory")

net.h:
The watsonx.ai actions allow a Datacap application to submit questions, via an AI prompt, to the watsonx.ai service.
The result from the prompt is saved in a Datacap field or DCO variable. The application can then store or act on
the response from the AI model. The actions can provide page data to the model and have the model
return desired information. One could use these actions to ask the model to classify the page based
on the page text. Another use could be to ask the model to find metadata or key-value pairs in the page data.
While these are common steps within a Datacap application, the actions are also intended to be open, allowing an application developer to customize
the prompt to any appropriate prompt where a model can be useful in processing of page data.
These actions allow connectivity to the IBM watsonx.ai service. These actions are not intended for any other service provider.
Responses from Large Language Models (LLMs) can vary greatly based on the
question and provided context. It may take some experimentation to create prompts
that return data in a consistent manner.
watsonx.ai Account Information:
It is required to have a watsonx.ai account to use the watsonx.ai actions. At the time of publishing, a
watsonx.ai account can be created at this address: http://watsonx.ai
For the Datacap watsonx.ai actions to submit requests, the target account will need to be properly configured
with a workspace and an API Key must be generated. The API Key is used to authenticate the Datacap
actions with your watsonx.ai account.
The watsonx.ai URLs, models and configuration information are separate from the Datacap product.
Refer to the watsonx.ai documentation for steps to setup an account and to configure the required
workspace and API Key. It will also be critical to keep current on the watsonx.ai URLs and models
as these can be deprecated and changed over time. Updating your application prior to a change
from the service is required to keep your Datacap watsonx.ai actions to continue functioning
as required.
Refer to the watsonx.ai website for all documentation regarding account setup,
available models, pricing, and deprecation schedules.
Important Model Considerations:
Any model, the default model or a user specified model, can eventually be deprecated or
removed by the service provider. This change is out of the hands of the Datacap product.
It is extremely important to keep up with any notices from the service provider about
an upcoming model deprecation or removal.
When changing to a new model, comprehensive testing is required to ensure that the
model performs well enough to be processed by the Datacap actions and that the results
are acceptable for the application.
It is recommended to review the service documentation as to the purpose of the
selected model. Models that are targeted to responding to programmatic requests
will generally work better in a "zero-shot" approach than a "chat" model, which typically uses a back-and-forth
approach to refine an answer.
Important Prompt Considerations:
There are two aspects to getting good results, the first is the model selected and the second is
the prompt. One large language model may work well with a specific prompt while another model will
respond poorly to the same prompt. Some of the actions in this library allow for
any prompt while others have restrictions on the prompt and on the required response from the model.
Review the help text for the actions to determine if the action fits the required use case. Perform sufficient
testing to ensure the model is returning results in the format required by the action and the results
are acceptable for the application. It is up to the application to handle situations where the
model does not return any results or the model returns inaccurate results.
The models available are at the discretion of the watson.ai service. The way the models return
results, and the contents of the results, are beyond the control of the Datacap product.
Action Summary:
AskAFreeFormQuestion:
Allows any prompt text and stores the result in a single location.
AskAQuestionUsingPageText:
Allows a custom question and builds it into a prompt with page text.
AskForKVPsAndCreateFieldsUsingPageText:
Asks the LLM for the keys it finds on page text and creates fields with those keys.
AskForPageValuesUsingKeys:
Allows specification of specific keys to obtain and asks the LLM to find those keys in the page text.
The results are stored in pre-defined fields where the corresponding key is specified.
SetAccessTokenURL:
Sets the token API endpoint.
SetAPIKey:
The unique API key for the target watsonx.ai account. The API Key must be configured with the key for the target account.
SetDecodingMethod:
Allows configuration of "greedy" or "sample".
SetEndpointURL:
The prompt API endpoint.
SetMaximumNewTokens:
The maximum tokens to return.
SetModel:
The model that will evaluate the prompt.
SetProjectID:
The watson.ai project ID. Required to be configured with the watsonx.ai project ID.
SetTemperature:
Controls the variation in a sample.
SetTimeLimit:
The maximum time allowed for the transaction.
The action
AskForPageValuesUsingKeys
is a good candidate to retrieve values of keys from a page of text.
It allows fields to be found on a page without using the traditional Datacap method of setting up
a fingerprint that defines the location of all fields on a page.
To do this, page fields are created at setup time in the usual way for Datacap, and then tagged with the expected name of the
key to find on the page. While there is no predetermined list of keys for a document type, testing has shown
that a model will generally understand expected keys for a document type. For example, on an Invoice document,
the LLM will understand that "Invoice Number" is a key-value pair that typically exists. AskForPageValuesUsingKeys
will then fill all of the fields with the values returned from the model. Classification
would be performed before using AskForPageValuesUsingKeys, so the correct key names are requested for the page type. Page classification
could be performed with standard Datacap techniques or could be performed by using the "AskFreeFormQuestion" action,
submitting the document text to the model and asking it to classify the document, then assigning the page type
based on the model response.
How To Use The Actions:
The application must first configure the service parameters using the "Set" actions. Once configured,
the "Ask" actions can be used to submit query prompts and obtain results for use within a Datacap application.
The actions that must be called are the following:
· SetProjectID
· SetAPIKey
· SetMaximumNewTokens
Additional "Set" actions can be called, if needed to change the default values.
The "set" actions can be performed in any order, as long as they are configured before calling an "Ask"
action. It is allowed to call a set action again to change parameters during processing. For example,
a specific model may be set using SetModel and then an "Ask" action called, then SetModel could be called
again, providing a different model name and then calling another "Ask" action.
Typically it is necessary to call SetMaximumNewTokens to increase the allowed tokens to the value
allowed by the model.
Issues With Results:
The nature of models can cause returned results to change or sometimes be unpredictable. These issues are beyond
the scope of the action. If the action is not returning results in the correct format, then try changing the keys
that are being requested for the page or a different model.
When models are updated by the model provider, the change may cause different results or no results.
Always fully test before using updated models in production. If a model is changed while in production, it can cause results
to be returned in unexpected ways. Changes by the service are independent of the Datacap product.
Model updates occur as determined by the service provider and are beyond the control of the Datacap product.
It is up to the implementer using these actions to monitor model changes and fully test as needed.
If the results are truncated due to exceeding the maximum allowed tokens,
increase the maximum token limit to that supported by the model. It is possible for the token limit
to reach the maximum allowed by the model when generating results for a single page of text.
In this situation, the prompt would need to be changed to have the LLM return fewer results.
Page Text Format:
When page text is included with the prompt sent to the model, it is included as plain text by default.
If the page has a table or structured information, the model usually responds better when the
page text is sent in HTML format. This allows the model to better understand the relationships
of the text. It can often help the model provide better answers. If the HTML option is enabled
in the action, a layout file must exist in addition to the CCO file. The "Recognize()" actions
in the recognition libraries create a layout file containing the page results.
A CCO can then be created from the layout file by calling the action CreateCcoFromLayout in the
SharedRecognitionTools action library.
It is suggested to use
a recognition engine that does the best at detecting the tables on the document.
Table detection quality varies between recognition engines.
Tip: The prompt sent to the model can be found in the log, when SetEnhancedLogging is enabled.
When developing a prompt, it is suggested to copy the basic prompt, with the page text,
from the log and place it into the watsonx.ai prompt lab interactive prompt. Using the prompt lab, prompts can
be quickly tweaked and tested. Be sure to delete the answer before trying a changed prompt.
Once you have a prompt that is responding as desired, that new prompt can be used in the action
instead of the default prompt.
Custom Prompts Using Text Files
The "Ask" actions allow the prompt to be customized and provided as a parameter to the action. While it
is possible to construct the prompt as a long input parameter, this can be difficult to create and
maintain. An alternative approach is to create a text file with the custom prompt. The text file can
contain the custom prompt, plus any replacement parameters supported by the action.
To input a text file as the custom prompt, first create the prompt text in a plain text file.
It can be helpful to use an interactive prompt to help create prompt text that provides desired results.
Replacement parameters, such as "{{PAGETEXT}}" and "{{LLMKEYS}}", can also be placed into the prompt text file.
The text file must be placed in a location accessible by the rules engine. A good location would be
within the application directories. If needed, multiple text files can be created.
The file IO action, "ReadFile", will read a plain text file into a DCO variable. The contents of this
variable can then be passed to the "Ask" questions. This method allows for a clear way of creating
prompt text, providing easy maintenance.
Placing the prompt text into a DCO variable will increase the size of the DCO. This text will be in addition
to all of the information about the batch and pages that also exist in the DCO. A large DCO does not perform
as well as a small DCO. It is highly recommended to remove the prompt text from the DCO after the action
has completed by setting the variable to "@EMPTY".
Example:
ReadFile("C:\MyApplication\PromptText1.txt","@P.MyPrompt")
AskAQuestionUsingPageText("@P.MyPrompt", "@P\InvoiceNum", "")
rrSet("@EMPTY", "@P.MyPrompt")
The above example reads the custom prompt from a text file, passes it to an "Ask" question,
then removes the prompt text from the DCO.
Token Use:
When response is returned, it uses "tokens" from the server. The amount of tokens used by the
request are listed in the log file.
Bad Request Error:
The most common type of error is a "Bad Request". The error will usually appear when working to get the actions
setup with the correct URLs, keys, etc. It is a very generic error that means something is wrong with the
request made to the endpoint. If you are receiving this error, confirm that specified URLs are correct.
Likewise, the API key and model names must be correct as well.
If the model specified does not exist on the service, or it has been spelled wrong, it will typically
cause a "Bad Request" error and the response may not specifically state the model name is invalid.
Model names can change over time, including the default model name provided by these actions.
Check the log for the exact model name being provided to the endpoint and confirm the model name
exactly matches the expected model name by the endpoint.
Prompt Engineering:
By default, each of the "Ask" actions will create a prompt to the model. The built-in prompt may not
satisfy all possible use cases. This is not necessarily a defect in the model, but simply how the model
interpreted the question and what it believes to be the best answer to the prompt.
Common problems with the answer:
· The required data is not returned.
· The required data is returned but contains extra text that is not relevant.
The results of a prompt are dependent on these things:
· The prompt or question.
· The data from the page and the format of the data.
· The selected model to process the prompt.
The crafting of an appropriate prompt is called Prompt Engineering. Slight changes to the wording of
a prompt can create notable differences in the response. Prompt Engineering is an interesting aspect
of the AI world. The Datacap actions uses a "zero-shot" approach to prompting. This means that the action
has one chance to ask the question and get the correct answer. The prompt must be crafted in a way to provide
enough information and direction to the model so it returns the desired answer on the very first try.
Each of the "Ask" actions allows a custom prompt to be provided. The custom prompt will override the built-in
prompt. The actions also allow the custom prompt to contain a special tag which is replaced with the
page text when the action submits the prompt to the model. The custom prompt can control every aspect
of the prompt and the location of the page text within the page.
One approach to crafting a custom prompt is to use the interactive prompt page in the watsonx.ai system.
When the actions have the extended logging enabled, the prompt is placed into the log file.
An application developer can copy the prompt text from the log as a starting point and paste it into the
freeform section of the watsonx.ai prompt GUI. From there, the text can be easily tweaked and run interactively
to immediately see how a particular model responds. This interactive approach allows quick testing of different
wording and different models to determine which works the best for a use case. Once a good prompt has
bee created, it can be added to the action as a custom prompt. Refer to the help for the action for
more information for how to include page data within the custom prompt.

method.name: AskAFreeFormQuestion
method.qi: : Send a custom prompt to the LLM allowing full control over the prompt text.

p.name: Question
p.qi: The question to ask the model.

p.name: Target
p.qi: A smart parameter expression that identifies the target field or DCO variable.

p.name: Format
p.qi: Specifies the format of the page text that is sent to the model.

method.ap:
Question:
The text that is provided as the LLM prompt text.
See the top-level text to learn how to read the prompt from a text file.
Target:
The location to place text returned from the LLM. It can reference a field or a variable.
The parameter is expected to be provided in the form of a smart parameter.
Format:
If the Question parameter contains the tag to embed the page text, this parameter identifies the format of the text sent to the model.
0: The page text is provided as plain text. If not specified, this is the default format.
1: The page text is automatically provided to watsonx.ai in HTML format, if a layout file exists along with the CCO.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action allows for a complete, user constructed, query to be provided to the LLM,
allowing any text to be submitted as-is. Using this action, the user can create
a custom prompt for the LLM. The action allows a single request to be
made with results stored in a single location.
The query can be built using custom "canned" text along with text obtained from
other locations within the application using smart parameters.
If the prompt requires full page text to be embedded within the prompt,
specify "{{PAGETEXT}}" in the parameter text. This identifier will
be replaced with the page text. To use this parameter,
the action must be called at the page level, recognition must have
previously been performed and a CCO created for the page.
If the format parameter specifies a text format other than plain text, such as HTML,
it is required that a layout file and the CCO exist for the current page.
The layout file is used to create the page representation provided to the model
and the CCO is used to locate the response text on the page. Use the action
CreateCCOFromLayout to create the CCO file from the layout file and the action
NormalizeCCO to adjust the text within the CCO, prior to calling this action.
If the returned text exactly matches text on the page, and if the target
is a field, then the field is updated with the coordinates of the found text.
Important:
Line breaks are very important in a prompt to help the model correctly interpret the request.
Line breaks in the correct place can create a very different response from the LLM.
The examples illustrate simplified calls without line breaks in the parameter.
If you have trouble adding line breaks in Datacap Studio, the smart parameter
@CHR() can be used to input specific characters, such as a carriage return and line feed,
by specifying the numeric value of the desired character.
Future updates to the model could change the response from a model.
When the model is updated perform sufficient testing to confirm that answers are still returned as expected or adjust the actions
to accommodate any changes. Updates to the model are beyond the scope of the Datacap product.
AskAFreeFormQuestion("What is the average temperature in the United States?", "@X.TheAnswer", "")
This asks the question "What is the average temperature in the United States?"
and stores the returned result in a variable called "TheAnswer" on the current object.
AskAFreeFormQuestion("What is the invoice number of this document? Provide only the invoice number without any explanation. Do not provide extra text that says something like "The invoice number is".+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+ [Document]+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+{{PAGETEXT}}+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+[End]+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)++@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)", "@X\InvoiceNum", "")
This example must be called on a page object and a CCO must exist for the page.
AskAFreeFormQuestion submits the question "What is the invoice number in the provided text?" with the {{PAGETEXT}} location replaced with
the text from the page. The smart parameter @CHR() is used to add carriage returns and line feeds into the string, which is important for
a successful prompt. The result is stored in a child field called "InvoiceNum"
AskAFreeFormQuestion("Using the provided input text, what is the document type? The answer must be one of the following: Invoice, Utility Bill, Passport, Unknown.+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+ [Input]+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+{{PAGETEXT}}+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+[End]+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)", "@X.LLMType", "")
rrSet("@EMPTY", "@X.PageText")
This example must be called on a page object with a CCO created.
AskAFreeFormQuestion submits the question to have the model classify the document and includes
the text from the page. The result is stored in a child field called "LLMType".
By providing specific answer terms, this will help guide the model to return a fixed set
of answers that can be later tested with an action such as rrCompare. It is up to the model
to decide exactly what to return.
Follow on actions
could then use this value to set the page type of the page.
Some models may return additional "helpful" text
even when only specific terms are expected. For example, a model may return "The document type is Invoice" instead
of the single term "Invoice". Specifying the allowed types usually resolves that issue, but it is dependent on the LLM.
It is up to the application to handle unexpected or inaccurate results.
ReadFile("C:\MyApplication\PromptText1.txt","@P.MyPrompt")
AskAFreeFormQuestion("@P.MyPrompt", "@P\InvoiceNum", "1")
rrSet("@EMPTY", "@P.MyPrompt")
The above example reads the custom prompt from a text file, passes it to the action,
then removes the prompt text from the DCO.
method.see:
Refer to the top-level help of this action library for information regarding this action library.
Refer to the top-level help of the RuleRunnerLogic action library for the smart parameter reference guide.
CopyPageTextToTarget in the SharedRecognitionTools action library and rrSet in the RuleRunnerLogic action library.

method.name: AskAQuestionUsingPageText
method.qi: : A simplified action that automatically adds the current page text into the prompt.

p.name: Question
p.qi: The question to ask the model.

p.name: Target
p.qi: A smart parameter expression that identifies the target field or DCO variable.

p.name: Format
p.qi: Specifies the format of the page text that is sent to the model.

method.ap:
Question:
The text that is used for searching.
See the top-level text to learn how to read the prompt from a text file.
Smart parameters are supported.
Target:
The location to place text returned from the query to Watson.
It is expected to be provided in the form of a smart parameter.
Format:
Identifies the format of the text sent to the model.
0: The page text is provided as plain text. If not specified, this is the default format.
1: The page text is automatically provided to watsonx.ai in HTML format, if a layout file exists along with the CCO.
Smart parameters are supported.
method.h:
Submits the question to the model using a pre-determined prompt layout and automatically provides
the text for the current page within the prompt. The action allows a single request to be
made with results stored in a single location.
The question placed within the prompt could be used to locate single
values from within the page text or have the model evaluate the page text for operations, such as classification.
The response will depend on the question, the input text and the ability of the model to formulate
the desired answer. It is highly recommended that sufficient testing be performed
to confirm the answers are acceptable.
Recognition must have been performed on the page and a CCO must have been created
prior to calling this action.
If the format parameter specifies a text format other than plain text, such as HTML,
it is required that a layout file and the CCO exist for the current page.
The layout file is used to create the page representation provided to the model
and the CCO is used to locate the response text on the page. Use the action
CreateCCOFromLayout to create the CCO file from the layout file and the action
NormalizeCCO to adjust the text within the CCO, prior to calling this action.
If the returned text exactly matches text on the page, and if the target
is a field, then the field is updated with the coordinates of the found text.
Important:
Future updates could change the returned results. This applies to both updates
in the model as well as updates to Datacap.
When the model is updated or applying Datacap updates,
perform sufficient testing to confirm that answers are still returned as expected or adjust the actions
to accommodate any changes. Updates to the model are beyond the scope of the Datacap product.
Some models may return additional "helpful" text
even when only specific terms are expected. For example, "The document type is Invoice" instead
of the single term "Invoice".
It is up to the application to handle unexpected or inaccurate results.
AskAQuestionUsingPageText("What is the invoice number? Return the single value only.", "@P\InvoiceNum", "")
This asks the question "What is the invoice number?" using the data from the current page
and the result is populated in the child field called "InvoiceNum".
The following example shows how the action, and the model, can be use to perform page classification using the recognized text.
This approach allows pages to be classified without using other traditional Datacap techniques, such as fingerprinting.
After image Recognition is performed on each page, the LLM is asked to classify the page. Follow-on actions
then use the model's response to set the appropriate page type. As is usual, the application will still
need to handle instances where a document is not properly classified.
Function Watsonx Classify
-
AskAQuestionUsingPageText("Classify the text in this document. The page classification must be one of the following classification types: "Invoice", "Bill of Lading", "Bank Statement", "Utility Bill", "Unknown". Only respond with the exact answer. Do not return explanation text.", "@P.LLMType", "0")
- GoToNextFunction()
Function Test For Invoice
- IsValueInText(@P.LLMType, "Invoice", "False")
- SetPageType("Invoice")
Function Test For BOL
- IsValueInText(@P.LLMType, "Bill of Lading", "False")
- SetPageType("BillofLading")
Function Test For Bank Statement
- IsValueInText(@P.LLMType, "Bank Statement", "False")
- SetPageType("BankStatement")
Function Test For Utility
- IsValueInText(@P.LLMType, "Utility Bill", "False")
- SetPageType("Utility")
The above rules show one way to configure them in Datacap Studio to ask the classification question to the model, including the recognized page text,
and places the answer in a page variable called "LLMType". The question can be adjusted with other document types or other application specific information
that will help guide the model to one of the desired answers. It is important for the model to return a answer that is as concise and accurate
as possible. One reason for specifying a list of valid documents types is to avoid free-form variations in
answers from the model such as "Invoice" vs. "Invoice Document", or other permutations that mean the same thing but can prevent the classification logic from working as expected.
ReadFile("C:\MyApplication\PromptText1.txt","@P.MyPrompt")
AskAQuestionUsingPageText("@P.MyPrompt", "@P\InvoiceNum", "1")
rrSet("@EMPTY", "@P.MyPrompt")
The above example reads the custom prompt from a text file, passes it to the action,
then removes the prompt text from the DCO.

method.name: AskForPageValuesUsingKeys
method.qi: : Queries the LLM based on tagged page fields (keys), filling each field with the result (value).

p.name: Question
p.qi: A custom question with identifiers for page text and key placement.

p.name: Format
p.qi: Specifies the format of the page text that is sent to the model.

method.ap:
Question:
Allows the preconfigured prompt to be replaced with a custom prompt.
Testing with the prompt that is automatically created by this action has shown acceptable
results. It is possible that specific user documents or scenarios may require a different prompt.
If a custom prompt is specified, it must also specify where to place the page text and the
requested key values.
If this parameter is blank, the action will use the built-in prompt to generate the results.
A typical scenario would start by using the built-in prompt and then providing a custom
prompt when the response is not meeting the needs of the application.
See the top-level text to learn how to read the prompt from a text file.
Format:
Identifies the format of the text sent to the model.
0: The page text is provided as plain text. If not specified, this is the default format.
1: The page text is automatically provided to watsonx.ai in HTML format, if a layout file exists along with the CCO.
Smart parameters are supported for all parameters.
method.h:
This action uses a key-value-pair approach to query a model with page text, finds the values of the requested keys from the page, and
fills multiple fields with the results in a single step.
The action will dynamically create an LLM prompt using the page text and data from specially configured
fields on the current page. The action will use the LLM to dynamically find the values of all of the configured fields.
For example, with an invoice, fields can be configured to hold values such as the invoice number, invoice date,
invoice total, etc. This action will ask the model to find these fields on the page text, and then
automatically populate the associated fields with the values from the text. The text is located using
the plain text and does not require fingerprints to be configured that properly identify the location
of the text on the page. This action is a good candidate to find values on a page without
needing the traditional Datacap setup of a fingerprint that identifies the location of the fields
on the page, simplifying the setup of an application.
A pre-defined list of expected key names to request from an LLM does not exit. A model generally does a good job of
understanding the expected keys of a document type, such as an "Invoice Number" for an invoice document
and other similar terms for specific documents.
Many types of documents share common terms as well, such as dates, names, addresses, line items, etc.
When configuring the keys to find on a page, use typical terms for the type of document being processed.
It is expected that the page type is already known prior to calling this action. For example, if an application
processes invoices and utility bills, then the invoice pages would be configured to have fields configured with key terms expected
on an invoice page and the utility page fields is configured with the keys terms expected on a utility bill.
The classification would be performed using the traditional classification techniques provided by Datacap.
An alternative approach could use the action AskAQuestionUsingPageText to ask a model to classify the page
and then using the action SetPageType to set the type prior to calling Create Documents, and prior
to calling this action on the identified pages.
Recognition must have been performed on the page prior to calling this action and
the page CCO must exist.
If the format parameter specifies a text format other than plain text, such as HTML,
it is required that a layout file and the CCO exist for the current page.
The layout file is used to create the page representation provided to the model
and the CCO is used to locate the response text on the page. Use the action
CreateCCOFromLayout to create the CCO file from the layout file and the action
NormalizeCCO to adjust the text within the CCO, prior to calling this action.
Prior to calling this action, at least one field on the page needs to be configured for use
with this action. The field must contain a variable called "LLMKey". The value of this variable must be
the text that is used to identify the target property for the field. For example,
the page may have a field called "InvoiceNum". The intent is for this field to be populated with the
invoice number from the page data. Setting the LLMKey value to "Invoice Number", will cause the request
for the "Invoice Number" to be included in the prompt and direct the
LLM to find the invoice number on the page. When the invoice number is returned, the value returned by the
LLM is placed into the field.
It is recommended to use the default model as testing has shown that it is fairly consistent in the
returned JSON format. If the model does not return the expected format, the data will not be
populated into the fields. The LLM must return the data in a JSON format with key-value pairs: {"Key1":"Value1", etc.}.
If the exact returned value can be found within the page text,
then the field is updated with the coordinates of the found text. If the exact text
occurs multiple times, then the coordinates may not be for the actual value referenced
by the LLM.
Multiple fields can be configured with the "LLMKey" variable prior to calling this action.
All of the fields on the page that contain the variable LLMKey is gathered and used
in the query to the LLM and then is populated with the responses from the LLM.
If the LLM changes the name of the key in the returned answer, the data for that key
will not be populated into the field. For example, if the variable "LLMKey" is set to "Invoice Number"
and the LLM decides to return the key as "The Invoice Number", then a match will not be found, and the
field will not be populated.
If the LLM does not return valid JSON, none of the fields is populated with results.
All of the LLMKey values on the page must be unique.
There is no definitive list of keys that are supported by a model or how it will determine the value
for the key. Models tend to use a "common sense" approach. One way to start is to use normally
expected terms to extract text from the page. Testing will help determine what terms work
best for the processed documents.
When developing an application using this action, it may be best to configure fields
one at a time and then running this action to test it. This will confirm that the LLM responds as expected
to the value provided in the LLMKey variable. If you first setup multiple keys and then try to use
the action, the LLM may not return some results or may not return any results, and it is harder
to determine if the LLM has a problem with one or more of the specified values to find within the document.
Another approach is to use an interactive prompt through a browser to determine the best key values
to extract the desired data. Be aware that the action is a zero-shot prompt which means that the
answer is determined by a single prompt, not using a history of prompts.
It is recommended that the default model is used for this action. The default values
will obtain the proper JSON response from the LLM. If the values are changed, it must be assured
that the LLM will only return valid key-value pairs in the expected JSON format. If the LLM does not return
valid JSON in the expected format, then the action will not be able to parse the results and create the fields.
If a custom question is provided, or if the model is changed, it is required that the results returned
from the LLM are key-value pairs in JSON format, otherwise this action will not function properly.
The results returned are determined by the model selected. The quality of the results are dependent on
several factors such as the quality of the recognition, the layout of the document, the relationship between
the keys and the values and the model selected. It is the responsibility of the model to locate the values
that correspond to the provided keys. If values are not found or are incorrect, it is dependent on the
model and beyond the control of the Datacap product.
Because a large number of tokens can be returned from the LLM, it is recommended to increase the number of tokens
by calling the action SetMaximumNewTokens(). If the LLM generates more tokens than the limit, the generated JSON will be
truncated and invalid and no results will be returned from this action. The maximum supported tokens varies from
model to model. Set the value to the maximum value supported by the model to reduce the chance of data truncation.
If the model returns a list of answers for a field, subfields are automatically created for those values.
If the model has not been set, the action will use the model "ibm/granite-3-8b-instruct" by default.
If the model is changed, the configured model must respond as expected to the prompt created
by this action or no data will be extracted.
The model must also respond with an answer in JSON, using the following
format:
{
"Key1": "Value1",
"Key2": "Value2",
"Key3": "Value3",
"Line Items": [
. . {
. . . "LItem1": "Value1",
. . . "LItem2": "Value2",
. . }
]
}
The response must be valid JSON in the proper format and
the returned keys must exactly match the value provided in the LLMKey variable on each field
for results to be populated.
Setup Steps For Using This Action:
1. Setup the fields for a page as desired. The field names can be anything that
makes sense for the application. The field names themselves will not affect the operation of this action.
For example, if the page type is an Invoice, setup fields for the invoice number, date, etc.
2. For each field that should have text located by the LLM, set the variable "LLMKey"
on the field object with a term that the LLM will understand and can extract.
The most efficient way to statically configure the values is to create the variable for the term in the setup DCO using Datacap Studio,
but the variable can also be set runtime using the rrSet action. For example: rrSet("Invoice Number", "@P\InvoiceNum.LLMKey")
3. Call the action AskForPageValuesUsingKeys.
Optionally Saving Returned JSON:
The JSON response from the model can be saved in a file within the batch.
To enable this feature, set the DCO variable "SaveLLMjson" on the page node
where this action is called. Setting the variable will enable the saving
of the JSON in a file and the value of the variable is used to name
the saved file. The file is saved using the following format:
˂ID>˂value>.json. For example, if the variable set to "-extract" and the current
page ID is "TM000001", then the file name will be TM000001-extract.json.
The variable SaveLLMjson can be configured in the setup DCO or can be set
at runtime using the action rrSet.
Table Line Items:
Testing has shown that typically a model responds to the key "Line Items" by returning the line items
it finds on the page. To setup a field to be a line item field, on the field set the variable "LLMKey"
to the value "Line Items". When this action runs, it will request that the LLM find the values for
the key. Line items will typically be returned as a list of items, with each row in its own list.
For example, if the field is named "MyLineItems" and the model returns the line item list,
this action will then create an entry under the field "MyLineItems" for each returned item/row
in the list. Each of these entries are sequentially numbered. Under each of these sub-fields,
the items in the list will be added by creating a new sub-field that matches the key name and the
value of the field will be the corresponding value that was returned by the model.
Be aware that DCO rules do now allow siblings to have the same name. Similarly, none
of the parents of a node may share the same name as the child node.
Providing A Custom Question Prompt:
The action provides a "built-in" prompt that is simple yet has given good results in testing.
If the prompt needs to be changed, a custom prompt can be created. The prompt needs to include the
following special identifiers:
"{{PAGETEXT}}" : Identifies where to place the page text.
"{{LLMKEYS}}" : Identifies where to place the keys to request as identified in each field.
The prompt that is sent to the model is also placed into the log for debugging.
New lines are very important for a prompt to operate correctly. New lines can be inserted
using the @CHR() smart parameter. See the example below that shows how to specify a custom
prompt and how to use the @CHR() smart parameter.
An example DCO configuration for an Invoice page: ˂P id="TM000001"˃
˂F type="InvoiceNum">
- - ˂V n="TYPE"˃Field˂/V˃
- - ˂V n="STATUS"˃0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="Position"˃0,0,0,0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="LLMKey"˃Invoice Number˂/V˃
˂/F˃
˂F type="BillToName"˃
- - ˂V n="TYPE"˃Field˂/V˃
- - ˂V n="STATUS"˃0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="Position"˃0,0,0,0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="LLMKey"˃Bill To Name˂/V˃
˂/F˃
˂F type="BillToAddress"˃
- - ˂V n="TYPE"˃Field˂/V˃
- - ˂V n="STATUS"˃0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="Position"˃0,0,0,0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="LLMKey"˃Bill To Address˂/V˃
˂/F˃
˂F type="Date"˃
- - ˂V n="TYPE"˃Field˂/V˃
- - ˂V n="STATUS"˃0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="Position"˃0,0,0,0˂/V>
- - ˂V n="LLMKey"˃Invoice Date˂/V˃
˂/F˃
An example of calling the action:
SetMaximumNewTokens("4096")
AskForPageValuesUsingKeys("", "1")
The action will query the LLM to find the values based on the LLMKey. Looking at the example fields above,
the action will ask for the values of the following keys: "Invoice Number", "Bill To Name", "Bill To Address" and "Invoice Date".
The returned results will automatically be populated
into the fields based on the keys requested.
If the returned value exactly matches text on the page, the coordinates for the field will be set based on the text.
If the exact same text occurs multiple times on a page, then the location of the field may not match the text coordinates
for the correct page location. The model might reformat some data, such as dates, so it may not exactly match the value on the page.
AskForPageValuesUsingKeys("˂|system|˃+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+You are a cautious assistant. You carefully follow instructions. You are helpful and harmless and you follow ethical guidelines and promote positive behavior.+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+˂|user|˃
+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+[Document]+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+{{PAGETEXT}}+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+[End]+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+The
following is a list of keys to find within the document. Please find only these keys and do not return any additional
keys.+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+{{LLMKEYS}}+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+Return the key value pairs in JSON format. Return only JSON in the following format.
Do not include additional keys. Do not include additional text before or after the JSON.+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+˂| assistant |˃+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)", "1")
This example shows how a custom prompt can be provided. It includes the {{PAGETEXT}} and {{LLMKEYS}} identifiers. It also uses the smart parameters "+@CHR(13)+@CHR(10)+"
to insert a carriage return and line feed into the string. If the prompt does not cause the model to return json in the expected format, the results
will not be processed. The page text format specified is HTML, which will provide the page to watsonx.ai in HTML format and can return better results on documents with tables.
ReadFile("C:\MyApplication\PromptText1.txt","@P.MyPrompt")
AskForPageValuesUsingKeys("@P.MyPrompt", "1")
rrSet("@EMPTY", "@P.MyPrompt")
The above example reads the custom prompt from a text file, passes it to the action,
then removes the prompt text from the DCO.
